# Sri Rasika-mangala

*"The Auspicious Song of Rasika"*

*A poem by Gopijana-vallabha Dasa (Bengali, 17th century). Four vibhagas, sixty-four laharis*

*Translated from the Bengali into English*

---

## Translator's Note

The *Sri Rasika-mangala* is a Bengali poem on the life of Rasikananda (Rasika-Murari, 1590–1652), the disciple of Shyamananda who, together with his guru, turned Utkala — Orissa, Mallabhum and the forest country of Jharikhanda — to Krishna. Its author, Gopijana-vallabha Dasa, is the son of Rasamaya of Dharenda, one of the first Shyamanandis; as a child he himself played one of the eight sakhis at the great Rasa-yatra in Gopivallabhapura (Pashchima, lahari 2) and describes much as an eyewitness. According to the colophon the poem was begun on Vasanta-panchami of the ninth regnal year ("anka") of the Gajapati Balabhadra and finished two years and eight months later (by the editors' reckoning, 1658–1660), that is, some six to eight years after Rasikananda's departure.

**What the book contains.** The poem is divided into four parts — the Purva (eastern), Dakshina (southern), Pashchima (western) and Uttara (northern) vibhagas — of sixteen laharis ("waves") each. The Purva-vibhaga contains the vandana of the associates of Shyamananda and Rasikananda, Shyamananda's birth and youth, his initiation by Hridayananda at Ambika and his pilgrimage; Rasika's birth at Rohini (Dipavali of 1512 Shaka), his childhood, studies and marriage, his vision of Krishna in the forest and his meeting with Shyamananda at Ghatshila. The Dakshina-vibhaga tells of Rasika's initiation, his stay in Vraja, the founding of Gopivallabhapura, the conversion of Dharenda, of Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja and of Uddanda Raya, and gives long teachings on bhakti and on the jiva. The Pashchima-vibhaga describes the Rasa-yatra at Gopivallabhapura, the deliverance of the maddened elephant at Banapur, the submission of the governor Ahmad Beg and of the Gajapati, Shyamananda's departure (1552 Shaka) and the festival of separation with a list of all the branches of the Shyamanandis. The Uttara-vibhaga tells of the community's annual festivals, the troubles in Shyamananda's family, the journey to Nilachala and Jagannatha's chariot moving at Rasika's touch, and finally Rasikananda's departure — his entering the Deity of Kshirachora Gopinatha at Remuna. Much of this — names, dates, the customs of the community — is known only from the *Rasika-mangala*.

**Source.** The translation follows the edition of Sripat Gopivallabhapura (ed. Gopala-Govindananda Deva Gosvami, 2nd ed., 455 Chaitanyabda = 1941), from the scan; for the Purva and Dakshina vibhagas the edition of Kishori Dasa Babaji (Halisahar, 1997), set from the same edition, was also consulted, and its variant readings are noted. **Only the text of the poem** is translated; the editors' prefaces and notes have not been used.

**How the translation was made.** The couplets (payar and tripadi) are translated one by one, keeping the division into lines; words supplied for sense are in square brackets; the Sanskrit mangala-shlokas at the beginning of a lahari are marked "S1", "S2"… The couplet numbers are those of the edition (separately in each lahari); the titles of the laharis follow the poem's colophons. The italic summary at the head of each lahari is the translator's. Doubtful readings are discussed in the notes; questions for a specialist in Bengali are collected separately.

**The author and Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching.** Gopijana-vallabha writes as a devotee of his gurus and of their house, and his praise at times goes beyond theological precision: he calls Shyamananda "Mahaprabhu" and "Prabhu" and speaks of him as Srimati Radhika Herself, descending age after age; of Rasika his characters say "a second Narayana," "a partial incarnation," "Ishvara." The translation renders these words exactly, softening nothing, and in the notes briefly states the Gaudiya Vaishnava position according to Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati: the Lord is Krishna Himself, who appeared as Sri Chaitanya; Shyamananda is His eternal servant and the servant of Radha, the disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya; Rasikananda is a great devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord. The birth and departure of such mahatmas are not subject to karma: Rasikananda's departure at Remuna is a disappearance, an entering into the lila of the Deity, not a merging (sayujya). Likewise marked are the places where the author, as the genre requires, narrates Krishna-lila (the rasa-lila, the gopis' separation): the gopis' prema is not mundane love (kama) but the pure desire to give joy to Krishna. With these reservations the *Rasika-mangala* is a priceless witness to the life of Utkala and Bengal in the 17th century and to the faith and customs of a community that grew from Sri Chaitanya's preaching.

# Purva-vibhaga

*The Eastern Part*

## Lahari 1. Obeisances to the Vaishnavas

*Mangala-shlokas to Shyamananda, Rasikananda and the Gosvamis; a song of obeisance to the guru Shyamananda and his wives, to Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates, to the holy places, to Shyamananda's disciples and Rasikananda's companions; the author's humility and the fruit of hearing the Rasika-mangala*

*Glory to Sri Sri Radha and Govinda!*
*Sri Sri Rasika-mangala.*
*Purva-vibhaga.*
*The first lahari.*
*Glory to Sri Sri Rasikananda-deva!*

**S1.** *How many, how many Puranas and Itihasas are there not in the world! Yet in them*
*nowhere did Krishna Himself write anything, except in the Gita-govinda.*
*Likewise among devotees nowhere is a mark in the form of a dot inscribed by one's own hand —*
*only for Sri Shyamananda did Srimati Radhika Herself joyfully make [it].*[^101-1],[^101-2],[^101-3]

**S2.** *A treasury of deep bliss, an ocean of grace, a treasury of the beauty of the three worlds,*
*a treasury and abode of the nectar of the rasa of full prema, a treasury of the Lakshmi of good fortune,*
*the one great treasury of the afflicted, a treasury of tenderness,*[^101-4] *a treasury of the pastimes of compassion —*
*all glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of mercy, whose mind is filled with sweetness!*

**S3.** *Bestower of deep bliss, exalter of rasa, a mine of the bhava of Sri Krishna,*
*giver of peace to the heart, destroyer of darkness, bringer of good to the host of devotees,*
*cutter of sorrow, prolonger of happiness, maker of the wealth of compassion,*
*deliverer of the lowly — to Prabhu Rasikananda, [like] the sun, I bow.*

**S4.** *O Sri Sanatana Prabhu, ocean of compassion!*
*O Rupa, whose merciful glance is the only [refuge] of the wretched!*
*O pair of Bhattas! O wise Raghunatha Dasa!*
*O Sri Jiva! Quickly show mercy to me, whose mind is dull.*[^101-5]

**S5.** *I worship the two lotus feet of Sri Shyamananda-deva,*
*by meditating on which people attain prema-bhakti for Hari.*

**S6.** *I worship the two feet of Rasikendra — the highest good,*
*the support of the essence of all sweetness, the highest festival.*[^101-6]

**S7.** *His face is the moon, his speech nectar, Bharati is in his throat;*
*his beauty is Lakshmi, his sweet smile is lovely — a row of kunda flowers;*
*his teeth are pearls, his pair of eyes a pair of bees, his arms two lotus stalks:*
*may people serve this Sri Murari like a chintamani gem.*[^101-7]

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^101-8]
*Ghosha: "Rama, glory [to You]! Govinda, Rama, glory [to You]!"*

**1.** *Song.* I worship the feet of Sri Guru — Shyamananda-raya,
by whose mercy attachment to Krishna arose.

**2.** By his mercy comes release from the bonds of worldly existence;
by his mercy all people became full of bhakti.

**3.** Such is Shyamananda: by the touch of his feet
the people of the three worlds float in the rasa of prema-bhakti.

**4.** To poor, lowly, miserable people he showed great mercy;
out of compassion he won over the three worlds.

**5.** The moon of the cowherd clan, shining forth in Utkala,[^101-9]
he destroyed the darkness of sin by giving prema-bhakti.

**6.** Prabhu is an ocean of bliss, a sea of mercy;
surpassing the three worlds, the beauty of his body is charming.

**7.** Prabhu is a sea of prema, an ocean of nectar;
fortunate in every way, a treasury of tens of millions and hundreds of thousands.

**8.** He dispels the torment of the three worlds;
at his compassionate words everyone's heart melts.

**9.** The crest-jewel of all sweetness is Shyamananda;
age after age he performs pastimes, having descended [into the world].[^101-10]

**10.** Be merciful to me, Prabhu, son of Durika:[^101-11]
I shall describe the glory of your dear devotee.

**11.** Then I worship the wives of the guru — the three Thakuranis,[^101-12]
by whose mercy I know prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**12.** Prema for Krishna embodied, bhakti itself —
she is praised in the world as a disciple of Hridayananda.[^101-13]

**13.** Show your favour, wife of Shyamananda,
so that with my mouth I may proclaim the glory of Rasika.

**14.** I worship Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Svayam Bhagavan,
who gave prema-bhakti to all living beings.

**15.** Descending age after age, the son of Shachi,
destroying the wicked, protects the saintly.

**16.** Seeing the dreadful [age of] Kali, full of compassion for the living beings,
He took birth in Navadvipa, bringing His associates and companions with Him.

**17.** Sri Chaitanya-raya, to whom the destitute are dear as life,
on whom Brahma, Shiva and Purandara meditate —

**18.** be merciful to me, son of Jagannatha:
I shall describe something of the Rasika-mangala.

**19.** Then I worshipped Nityananda-Balarama,
whose incomparable beauty surpasses tens of millions of Kamadevas.

**20.** The poor, the lowly — every single person, down to the chandalas —
by giving them bhakti for Krishna He delivered the three worlds.

**21.** Bowing down, I worship Shachi and Jagannatha;
I worship Hadai Pandita and Padmavati.

**22.** I worship Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, the two Thakuranis;
I worship Vasudha and Jahnava, the wives of the elder brother.[^101-14]

**23.** With devotion I worship Advaita Acharya,
by whose mercy bhakti for Chaitanya arises.

**24.** With joy I have now worshipped Sita Thakurani,
bhakti itself in the descent of Sri Chaitanya.

**25.** I worship Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita;
I worship all the household of Sita Thakurani.

**26.** I worship Virabhadra-raya, radiant in body,[^101-15]
whose manifestation is famed throughout the earth.

**27.** Together with their households I worship all the companions,
so that Rasika's glory may shine forth in my heart.

**28.** With joy I worshipped Ramai and Sundarananda,
whose greatness is manifest on earth.

**29.** I worship Gauridasa Thakura — Subala-raya;
everyone sings of him as dear to Nityananda.

**30.** The whole world calls him an intimate friend (priya-narma-sakha);
in his line the Vaishnava Shyamananda appeared.[^101-16]

**31.** If that Prabhu grants [me] his mercy,
then I shall spread the Rasika-mangala.

**32.** With respect I worship Uddharana Datta;
I worship Premeshvara, a follower of Chaitanya.[^101-17]

**33.** With humble entreaty I worship Murari Thakura;
with devotion I worshipped Kamalakara.

**34.** I worship the two, Purushottama and Manohara;
I worshipped the feet of Kaliya Krishnadasa.[^101-18]

**35.** I worshipped the eight Giris, most dear to Chaitanya;
I worshipped the eight Puris, the elders of all.

**36.** I worshipped the eight Bharatis, great mahajanas,
who had Vishvambhara accept sannyasa.[^101-19]

**37.** I worship the eight boys, followers of Chaitanya;
I worship the sixty-four mahantas, all the companions.[^101-20]

**38.** With great joy I worship the guru's line;
I worship Balarama, Bada Thakura, Haridasa.[^101-21]

**39.** I worship Govinda Gosvami, Thakura Mahesha;
especially I worship Durlabha Thakurani.[^101-22]

**40.** I worship Hridayananda, who brought light to the line;[^101-23]
I worshipped the feet of all [his] servants and all the household.

**41.** Together with their associates and companions I worship [them], the abode of all virtues;
I worship all the Vaishnavas, bowing down [to them].

**42.** I worship all the brahmanas, the best of all sannyasis;
I worship the seven seas, the earth with all that moves and does not move.

**43.** Among these I joyfully worshipped the holy places,
by hearing of which bhakti for Krishna becomes manifest.

**44.** I worship Sri Vrindavana, Madana-gopala,
Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Sri Banka-vihara.[^101-24]

**45.** I worship Radha-vallabha, the graceful Thakura;[^101-25]
I worship Kalindi-Yamuna, all of Vraja-pura.

**46.** I worship Gokula, Mathura, Sri Keshava-raya,
by hearing of whom all sins are destroyed.[^101-26]

**47.** I worship Yadava-raya, the lord of Gokula;
I worshipped Gopala-raya, the holder of Govardhana.

**48.** Then I worshipped Dvaraka and Ranchhor-raya:[^101-27]
that abode of Krishna is greater than Vaikuntha.

**49.** I worship Badarikashrama and Nara-Narayana;
I worship the Gandaki, the Gomati, Naimisharanya.

**50.** I worship Prabhasa, Pushkara, the tirtha of the Godavari;
I worship the Narmada, the Sarasvati, the Sindhu, the Kaveri.

**51.** I worshipped Ayodhya and Kurukshetra, holy abodes;
I worship Setubandha and every place where Hari [resides].

**52.** I worshipped Hastinapura, the home of the Pandavas,
where Sri Krishna stays for the sake of His devotees.

**53.** I worship Kanchi and Avantika, most holy places:
age after age the seven cities are the abodes of Hari.[^101-28]

**54.** I worship Sri Purushottama, the lord of Nilachala,[^101-29]
Gaya, the Ganga, Varanasi, Prayaga and the rest.

**55.** I worship the Bhagirathi and Navadvipa, the great place,
the abode of Sri Chaitanyachandra Mahaprabhu.

**56.** I worship Gangasagara, famed throughout the world;
I worship holy Navadvipa and Tamralipta.[^101-30]

**57.** I worshipped the three places — heaven, earth and the netherworld;
among them I worshipped all the holy abodes.

**58.** Be merciful to me, all of you — I bow down [to you] —
so that I may expound the Rasika-mangala.

**59.** Briefly I shall speak of two or four of the elders;
by Rasika's mercy I worship the feet of them all.

**60.** I worship Gopiramana, the adhikari [of the service] of Chaitanya;
I worship Sri Rama Thakura, possessed of every virtue.[^101-31]

**61.** I worshipped the two, Krishnananda and Dvarika;
I worship Achyuta and Bhavani, dear to Krishna.[^101-32]

**62.** I worship Prasada Thakura and Balaramadasa,
who lived together with Shyamananda's younger brother.[^101-33]

**63.** Manohara, full of bhava, renounced, devoted to Krishna;
I worship the feet of Kishora the teacher.

**64.** I worship Sri Tulasidasa, the guru of sankirtana,
who from his birth lived together with Rasika.[^101-34]

**65.** At the festival of sankirtana he receives the first worship:
Rasika honours him with cloth and ornaments.

**66.** When Rasika cannot manage to water Tulasi,
he offers [the water] at the feet of Tulasi[dasa] and drinks it with a joyful heart.[^101-35]

**67.** I worship all the elders, holding their feet,
so that I may sing Rasika's praise at every moment.

**68.** I worship the feet of all the Vaishnavas of Shyamananda;
[I name] ten or twenty of the chief ones — this is a brief account.

**69.** Do not hold against me any fault of order:
in the course of the book I shall tell of everything.

**70.** I worship Yadavendradasa, the elder [brother] of Nityananda;[^101-36]
I worship Sri Kishora and Sri Balakadasa.

**71.** Vaishnavadasa, Gopinathadasa, Manohara;
I worship Damodara-prabhu, the servant of Krishna.[^101-37]

**72.** His voice choked with prema, his eyes filled with tears,
in the bliss of Krishna he weeps constantly night and day.

**73.** Damodara knows nothing but Krishna;
he made very many disciples who took the one sole shelter.

**74.** His union with Rasika is undivided;
to such a Damodara, a jewel among men, I bow.

**75.** With joy I worshipped the brahmana Govindadasa;
I worshipped Gopala, Balabhadra, Haridasa.[^101-38]

**76.** I worshipped Govinda, the mahajana of Vrindavana;
I worship the feet of Shyamasundara and Uddhava.

**77.** I worship the two, Shyamadasa and Jagannatha;
I worship the feet of Kaviraja Balabhadra.

**78.** With devotion I worship Chintamanidasa;
I worship Sri Radhavallabhadasa, pure of mind.

**79.** Anantadasa, Raghunathadasa of Mathura;
I worship the brahmana Padmanabha and Gangadharadasa.

**80.** I worship Sri Radhamohana, the brahmana Shirikara;[^101-39]
with respect I worship merciful Kanudasa.

**81.** With reverence I worshipped Govindadasa and Bhudhara;
I worship Radhacharana and Purushottama, the best of brahmanas.

**82.** I worship Ananta, Radhavallabha, Radhadhara,
Gokula, Krishna-smarana, the brahmana Damodara.[^101-40]

**83.** I worship Sri Shyamaranginidasa, the best of sadhus;
I worship Sri Shyamatarangi, a brahmana, the best of sadhus.

**84.** Abhaya, Ramagovinda — I worshipped them all;
Ananda, Mathurashyama, pure in body.

**85.** I worship Madhuvanadasa, a companion of Krishna;
each one of them has hundreds and hundreds of disciples, very many.

**86.** I worship Sri Anandananda, a worthy brahmana;
I worshipped the descendants of Divakara, kind of heart.[^101-41]

**87.** With great joy I worship Sri Mathuradasa of the gopas;
with joy I worshipped Mathuradasa of Gauda.[^101-42]

**88.** Jagannathadasa, Radhavallabha, Bhudhara,
Ramadasa, Sri Chaitanyadasa, the best of brahmanas —

**89.** their feet I worship, rejoicing;
I worship Sri Krishnadasa and Gopaladasa.

**90.** I worship Mukunda-bhupati, a servant of Shyamananda,
whose poetic gift is manifest in all four directions.[^101-43]

**91.** I worship Sri Keshava Shiromani, greatly steadfast;
I worship Sachuda Sri Jagannatha, full of sattva.[^101-44]

**92.** With joy I worshipped Bhrigu and Sri Purushottama;
I worshipped Bhudeva and Sri Chaitanyadasa.

**93.** I worship the vaidya Sri Gopaladasa, the fortunate;
I worship the brahmanas Shyama, Rasika, Govinda.

**94.** Madana-mohanadasa, the brahmana Gadadhara;
I worship the brahmana Balabhadra and Vamshi, the best of brahmanas.

**95.** I worship the brahmana Purushottama, greatly fortunate,
for whom Prabhu Shyamananda is caste, wealth and life.

**96.** I worship the brahmana Damodara, a servant of Shyamananda,
whose true abode is at Shyamananda's holy feet.

**97.** With all his family he gave himself over to Shyamananda;
he knows nothing but guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

**98.** I worship Sri Mathuradasa, a great mahajana:
all [his] wealth and people he surrendered to Shyamananda.

**99.** A dear disciple of Shyamananda, prema-bhakti embodied —
for him Prabhu Shyamananda is family, character and caste.

**100.** The brahmana Haridasa, Vanamali, the best of brahmanas,
Radhakrishna, Dharambara, the vaishya Narayana;

**101.** I worshipped Gauranga, Purushottama, Madhava;
I worship the brahmana Gopala, Manohara, Bhudeva.

**102.** I worship Govinda Bhattacharya, who lives in Vanga:
in Vanga he made [the glory of] Shyamananda manifest.[^101-45]

**103.** I worship Sri Kishoradasa and Kanudasa,
Sri Mathuradasa of the gopas, Rasamayadasa.[^101-46]

**104.** I worship Sri Gaurangadasa and Manoharadasa;
I worship all the Shyamanandis, wherever each one lives.

**105.** I worship Nilambaradasa and Sri Ananta-raya;
then I worshipped the worthy Sanatana.

**106.** With joy I worshipped Thakura Vishnudasa,
who constantly delights [in the company of] Rasika.

**107.** Then I worshipped Shyamadasi Thakurani,
Rasika's wife, prema-bhakti embodied.[^101-47]

**108.** A disciple of Shyamananda, devoted to her husband, mother of the world;
from her birth her service to Govinda has been known to the world.

**109.** Then I worship Sri Devaki, Rasika's daughter,
a disciple of Shyamananda: the eldest sister, she is [our] mother.

**110.** I worship Radhananda Thakura, Rasika's son,
a dear disciple of Shyamananda, endowed with every virtue.[^101-48]

**111.** Absorbed in Krishna, his heart is enchanted by the rasa of prema;
the streams from his eyes drench his whole body.

**112.** He is full of all the shastras, a great scholar,
skilled in music, known to the world.

**113.** I worshipped Sri Krishna Bhanja-deva, the maharaja,
who with firm faith serves and worships Shyamananda's feet.[^101-49]

**114.** A dear disciple of Shyamananda, the moon that illumines his line,
in whose land is the bliss of great festivals of service to Krishna.

**115.** A king wholly devoted [to Krishna], known to the world,
dedicated to Hari-nama, always practising [it].

**116.** In his heart dwell the sixty-four limbs of bhakti;[^101-50]
everyone proclaims him devoted to the brahmanas.

**117.** Is it Parikshit, Ambarisha, Sanaka and his brothers
who took birth in the form of bhakti for Krishna? He has won renown.[^101-51]

**118.** By the strength of his piety the best of kings, mighty and formidable:
hostile kings come and become servants at his feet.

**119.** Such a king, a devotee of Krishna — be merciful to me:
I shall sing Rasika's glory, sitting steadfast.

**120.** With devotion I worship Krishnanandadasa,
who has no other refuge than Shyamananda.

**121.** I worship the chaste Vrindavati, Rasika's daughter,
humble and patient, whom the world praises.

**122.** With joy I worshipped Krishnagati, pure of mind,
Rasika's middle son, renowned in the world.

**123.** Mad with prema for Krishna, he does not know day from night;
such is Krishnagati, whose life's treasure is Krishna.

**124.** Rasika's youngest son is Radhakrishnadasa,
dear to Shyamananda; [Krishna] is manifest in his pure heart.[^101-52]

**125.** Rasika's son, filled with the bliss of prema,
kind to all living beings — I worship those feet.

**126.** Prasada, Gopala, Govinda, Ramadasa,
Madhava, Kishora, Radhamohana — those servants;

**127.** and I worshipped the feet of Purushottamadasa;
the gopa Ankura — both are servants of Sri Shyamananda.[^101-53]

**128.** Krishnadasa Dariya, Radhavallabhadasa —
the servants among the Shyamanandis cannot be counted.[^101-54]

**129.** I worship Jagannatha, the servant of Achyuta's son;[^101-55]
I worship Ananta, Sridhara and Kashinatha.

**130.** Then I worshipped Nilambara Shirikara,
Kapileshvara, Gangadasa — all the companions.

**131.** I worship Sri Shyamagopala, a great mahajana;
I worshipped the two, Chintamani and Vihari.

**132.** Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Shyama, Manohara,
Gopinatha, Vaidyanatha — all the companions.

**133.** The Shyamanandis are numberless — how many names shall I take?
One by one I bow down to them all.

**134.** Be merciful to me, all of you, accept me:
I shall proclaim something of Rasika's glory.

**135.** Rolling at his feet, I worship my father Rasamaya;
then I worshipped my mother, devoted to her husband.

**136.** Husband and wife, both, and five sons —
all took shelter at Rasika's feet.[^101-56]

**137.** I worshipped my paternal uncle, Vamshi Mathuradasa,
who is renowned among the first Shyamanandis.[^101-57]

**138.** I worship with devotion all the elders,
pure of mind, in my mother's line and my father's line.

**139.** In the line of the gopas we all were born;
Shyamananda's two feet are [our] family, character and caste.

**140.** Gopijana-vallabha, Haricharanadasa,
Madhava, Rasikananda, Kishoradasa —

**141.** the five brothers, sons of Sri Rasamaya,
whose caste, wealth and life is Achyuta's son.[^101-58]

**142.** Vallabha's son is the renowned Radhavallabha,
whose mother and father is Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of devotees].[^101-59]

**143.** Together with their families they are Rasika's servants;
they constantly abide with Rasika.

**144.** As once upon the Pandavas and other poor, suffering people
Krishna kept His watchful gaze without cease,[^101-60]

**145.** [so,] by the power of the feet of Rasika, the devotee of Krishna,
no sorrow touches [them] or their families.

**146.** Apart from Rasikendra they know nothing of all this —
puja, meditation, austerity, japa, the eightfold sadhana.[^101-61]

**147.** With their whole being they serve Rasika;
regarding them as servants, he protects them all.

**148.** As Krishna, the friend of the poor, is a shelter and a shield,
so still more is [His] devotee a shelter, [like] one's own brother.[^101-62]

**149.** Thus the whole [of our] family abides at Rasika's feet
constantly — be it night, be it day.

**150.** Rasika's paternal uncle, Tulasi Thakura,
every year urgently commands [me]:[^101-63]

**151.** "Seeing the prema for Krishna throughout the land of Utkala,
describe Rasika's glory!"

**152.** Prabhu is embarrassed on hearing his own virtues —
fearing that embarrassment, I did not make [it] known.[^101-64]

**153.** At that time Rasika-shekhara of Berhapal,
laughing playfully, answered everyone:[^101-65]

**154.** "There will be a Shyamanandi who is so fortunate —
[who it is,] all the Shyamanandis devoted to Krishna decide.[^101-66]

**155.** So that all people may sing of this whole community,
it is good if someone describes [it] thus."

**156.** Having received that encouragement, I took the command upon my head,
quickly honouring Rasika's feet, [placing them] upon my head.

**157.** Remembering the lotus feet of Sri Krishna,
I shall describe something of Rasika's glory.

**158.** Gopijana-vallabha, a servant of Sri Shyamananda,
has dared to make something known.

**159.** The glory of a devotee is a boundless, fathomless ocean:
Brahma, Shiva, Indra and the others cannot find its limit.

**160.** The greatness of a devotee is many times greater than Krishna['s]:
[Krishna] constantly goes about [after His devotees] in hope of the dust of their feet.[^101-67]

**161.** Such is Rasika-Murari, most dear to Krishna:
even with ten million mouths I could not tell his virtues.

**162.** I am utterly poor and lowly, wretched, in a sorry plight;
whatever is spoken — it is Rasika, the lord of [my] life, who speaks it.

**163.** Who can tell of the boundless ocean of [his] pastimes?
Whatever appears to me by Shyamananda's mercy,

**164.** I, relying on his command, shall make known —
something of Rasika-deva's holy glory.

**165.** Without intelligence, without learning, I am of wicked mind;
what could I know of Rasika-deva's holy glory?

**166.** All the Shyamanandis devoted to Krishna commanded me
to proclaim Rasika-deva's glory.

**167.** Being a tiny person, I am very bold:
show favour, all of you, that [my] heart's wish may be fulfilled.

**168.** I shall describe something — a description of [his] nature —
as the son of Achyuta, like a magician, makes [me] dance.[^101-68]

**169.** Do not mind any faults in the order [of the narrative];
may sadhus and learned people listen with affection.

**170.** I shall tell something — the Rasika-mangala;
in the three worlds fortunate people will hear [it].

**171.** Devotees of Sri Krishna, each abiding in his own place,
hear the Sri Rasika-mangala day and night.

**172.** To hear it is a joy to the ears, to sing it is full of rasa;
merely by hearing it, one easily crosses [the ocean of] worldly existence.

**173.** To destroy the terrible darkness of Kali, the impenetrable gloom,
[he] appeared in the form of a devotee.[^101-69]

**174.** As by hearing Krishna's qualities one crosses [the ocean of] worldly existence,
so merely by hearing a devotee's qualities one overcomes the three times.

**175.** Whoever even once hears this with his ears,
in that very moment millions upon millions of great sins are destroyed.

**176.** Release from all bonds and prema-bhakti come [to one]
who hears the holy praise — the Rasika-mangala.

**177.** To the poor [it gives] wealth, to the childless a son;
hearing the Rasika-mangala takes away grief and sorrow.

**178.** Supreme, exclusive bhakti arises at once [in one]
who reads [it] with love.

**179.** All living beings suffer from the bite of Time —
recite, all of you, the mantra — the Rasika-mangala!

**180.** Whoever reads or hears [it] is not devoured by the wheel of Time;
at once the noose of the bondage of worldly existence is destroyed.

**181.** Effortlessly [he gains] wife, sons and every strength,
wealth, people, prema-bhakti, the highest good.

**182.** Let no one disregard [it], saying, "It is composed in the common tongue" —
a venomous snake never at any time gives up its poison.[^101-70]

**183.** Listen attentively, all of you, leaving other talk;
having heard, destroy the pain of the bondage of worldly existence.

**184.** Especially for the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas [this] is life:
Rasikendra-chudamani is their caste, life and wealth.

**185.** Those who hear his qualities with faith
attain Rasika's feet without delay.

**186.** In Patala the Nagas hear [it];
in heaven the devas hear, on earth the sadhus.[^101-71]

**187.** Sing with your own mouths the qualities of Krishna's devotee:
the four Vedas sing that Bhagavan is subject to His devotees.[^101-72]

**188.** O you most wise, all of you, do not impute any faults [to me];
setting aside [thought of] all faults, listen with joy.[^101-73]

**189.** Women, men and others, be they children or old people —
whoever hears [it] with whatever desire,

**190.** merely by hearing, the desire is completely fulfilled:
wealth, grain, sons, grandsons, fame, a home full of prosperity.

**191.** Release from all bonds [and] prema-bhakti come
merely by hearing the praise of Rasika.

**192.** The Purva-vibhaga is supremely full of rasa:
having heard it, all living beings, cross over [the age of] Kali.

**193.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**194.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the first lahari, called "Obeisances to the Vaishnavas".*

[^101-1]: The mangala-shlokas at the beginning of the lahari are numbered separately in the edition (॥ 1 ॥–॥ 7 ॥), and from the song (after the raga and the ghosha, at the word "গীত") the numbering starts again from 1 and runs to the end of the lahari. To keep the numbers distinct, the shlokas are labelled S1–S7; the numbers 1, 2… are the edition's.

[^101-2]: According to tradition, Krishna Himself wrote a line into Jayadeva's Gita-govinda (in the 10th canto) when the poet hesitated to write it. The "mark in the form of a dot" (bindu) is apparently the tilaka mark on Shyamananda's forehead: tradition says Sri Radha Herself placed it, and the distinctive tilaka of his followers is connected with this (cf. BR 15 on Radha's anklet). The line can also be read differently — "only Sri Shyamananda, [being] Srimati Radhika Herself, joyfully made [it]" — the author's exaltation of Shyamananda. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, not Radhika Herself.

[^101-3]: So in the 1941 edition: "জয়মকৃতমুদা" (*jayam akṛta mudā*); the 1997 edition reads "স্বয়ম কৃতমুদা" (*svayam akṛta mudā*, "Herself joyfully made"), which fits the sense; translated by the latter reading.

[^101-4]: "A treasury of tenderness" — *drava-nidhiḥ* (literally "a treasury of melting", i.e. of a heart melting with compassion); the reading is confirmed by the 1941 edition, the sense is conjectural.

[^101-5]: The pair of Bhattas are Raghunatha Bhatta and Gopala Bhatta; together with Sanatana, Rupa, Raghunatha Dasa and Jiva they are the six Gosvamis of Vrindavana.

[^101-6]: Rasikendra ("the king of rasikas") is Rasikananda.

[^101-7]: The shloka has a double meaning: Murari is a name of Krishna ("the enemy of Mura") and also Rasika-Murari, i.e. Rasikananda. Bharati is Sarasvati, the goddess of speech. A chintamani is a wish-fulfilling gem.

[^101-8]: Raga Karuna-shri. The ghosha is the refrain repeated when the song is sung; the following laharis begin in the same way.

[^101-9]: Shyamananda was born at Dharenda (Utkala) in a family of gopas (sadgopas, an agricultural caste); hence "the moon of the cowherd clan".

[^101-10]: "Having descended" — *avatīrṇa*: the author speaks of Shyamananda as descending age after age. This is the author's exalted praise; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching it is the Lord who descends age after age (cf. 15), while Shyamananda is His eternal associate and servant.

[^101-11]: Durika is Shyamananda's mother.

[^101-12]: The three Thakuranis are Shyamananda's three wives.

[^101-13]: Hridayananda is Hridaya Chaitanya of Ambika (Kalna), Shyamananda's guru.

[^101-14]: Lakshmi (Lakshmipriya) and Vishnupriya are the wives of Sri Chaitanya; Vasudha and Jahnava are the wives of Nityananda, the Lord's "elder brother".

[^101-15]: Virabhadra (Virachandra; so in the 1997 edition) is Nityananda's son.

[^101-16]: In Krishna's pastimes Gauridasa Pandita is the cowherd boy Subala, Krishna's intimate friend (priya-narma-sakha). "Line" here means spiritual succession: Gauridasa is the guru of Hridaya Chaitanya, and he of Shyamananda.

[^101-17]: So in the edition (*premeśvara*). Possibly Parameshvara (Dasa), an associate of Nityananda, is meant; not identified.

[^101-18]: Many of those named in 28–39 — Sundarananda, Gauridasa, Uddharana Datta, Kamalakara (Pippalai), Purushottama, Kala (Kaliya) Krishnadasa, Mahesha (Pandita) — are traditionally counted among the twelve gopalas, the associates of Nityananda. Murari Thakura and Manohara are not identified here.

[^101-19]: Giri, Puri and Bharati are branches of the sannyasa order. Sri Chaitanya (Vishvambhara) received sannyasa from Keshava Bharati (CC, Adi 17; CB, Madhya 28).

[^101-20]: The "eight boys" are not identified. The sixty-four mahantas are the traditional list of Sri Chaitanya's associates.

[^101-21]: The line is unclear: "বলরাম বড় ঠাকুর বন্দো হরিদাসে" (*balarāma baṛa ṭhākura bando haridāse*) — it may also be understood as "Balarama [and] the elder Thakura Haridasa". The persons are not identified.

[^101-22]: Thakura Mahesha is apparently Mahesha Pandita, an associate of Nityananda. Govinda Gosvami and Durlabha Thakurani are not identified.

[^101-23]: So in the 1941 edition: "হৃদয়ানন্দন" (*hṛdayānandana*, possibly "son of Hridaya"); the 1997 edition reads "হৃদয়ানন্দ". Understood as Hridayananda, i.e. Hridaya Chaitanya (cf. 12), who "brought light" to Gauridasa's line.

[^101-24]: Madana-gopala, Govinda and Gopinatha are the Deities of Vrindavana served by the Gosvamis. Banka-vihara (*baṅka-behāra*, "the curved sporting One") is apparently the Deity Banke-bihari in Vrindavana.

[^101-25]: Radha-vallabha is a Deity in Vrindavana. "Graceful" — *cikaniyā* ("smooth, graceful, charming").

[^101-26]: Keshava-raya (Keshavadeva) is the Deity of Krishna in Mathura. Gopala-raya, "the holder of Govardhana", is apparently the Gopala found by Madhavendra Puri on Govardhana Hill (CC, Madhya 4). Yadava-raya, "the lord of Gokula", is not identified.

[^101-27]: Ranchhor-raya ("he who left the battlefield") is Krishna as the Deity of Dvaraka (also worshipped at Dakor, Gujarat).

[^101-28]: The seven cities (sapta-puri) are traditionally Ayodhya, Mathura, Maya (Haridvar), Kashi, Kanchi, Avanti (Avantika) and Dvaraka.

[^101-29]: Purushottama is Puri; its lord is Jagannatha.

[^101-30]: Tamralipta is the old name of Tamluk in southern Bengal, near the border of Utkala.

[^101-31]: Adhikari — "owner; one entrusted with the service". Gopiramana and Rama Thakura are not identified.

[^101-32]: Krishnananda and Dvarika are apparently Shyamananda's parents: according to tradition his father was named Krishna (Mandala) and his mother Durika (cf. 10); the edition's variant reading here is "দুরিকা" (*durikā*). Achyuta and Bhavani are Rasikananda's parents (cf. BR 15).

[^101-33]: "Who lived together with Shyamananda's younger brother" — *śyāmānandānuja saṅge yā̃dera nivāsa*; the line can be understood otherwise, and its sense is not quite clear. Prasada Thakura and Balaramadasa are not identified.

[^101-34]: Tulasidasa is possibly the same as Tulasi Thakura, Rasikananda's paternal uncle (150).

[^101-35]: A play on words: Tulasi is the sacred plant and also Tulasidasa's name. When he cannot water Tulasi, Rasika bathes Tulasidasa's feet with the water and drinks it.

[^101-36]: Literally "the elder of Nityananda" (*nityānanda-jyeṣṭha*): which Nityananda is meant (apparently one of the Shyamanandis, not the Lord) and in what sense "elder" is unclear. The edition's variant reading: "জ্যেষ্ঠ নেত্রানন্দ" — "the elder, Netrananda".

[^101-37]: Damodara is apparently the former yogi whom Shyamananda made his disciple (BR 15, 55–58).

[^101-38]: From here on (75–132) the author lists disciples of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; most of them are not identified. BR 15 (63–65) names among Shyamananda's disciples Radhananda, Purushottama, Manohara, Chintamani, Balabhadra, Jagadishvara, Uddhava, Akrura, Madhuvana, Govinda, Jagannatha, Gadadhara, Anandananda, Radhamohana. Where a word may be either a name or an epithet (e.g. Bhudhara, Bhudeva, Ananda), it is rendered as a name.

[^101-39]: Shirikara (শিরীকর, *śirīkara*; also 130) is apparently a surname, possibly an Odia form of shrikarana (the scribal caste). Taken as a surname.

[^101-40]: "Krishna-smarana" (*kṛṣṇa-smaraṇa*, "remembrance of Krishna") is taken as a name; it may be an epithet of Gokula: "Gokula, who remembers Krishna".

[^101-41]: Divakara is not identified.

[^101-42]: "Of the gopas" — *gopa*: of the gopa caste (like Shyamananda, see 5); "of Gauda" — *gauṛīyā*, a Bengali.

[^101-43]: Bhupati — "king, lord of the earth"; possibly part of the name. The person is not identified.

[^101-44]: So in the 1941 edition: "সচূড়" (*sacūṛa*, "with a topknot, with a crest") and "সত্ত্বশীল" (*sattva-śīla*); the first word is taken as a byname. Keshava Shiromani and Jagannatha are not identified.

[^101-45]: Vanga — eastern Bengal.

[^101-46]: Rasamayadasa is apparently Rasamaya, the author's father (cf. 135, 141).

[^101-47]: Shyamadasi is Rasikananda's wife; in BR 15 (30) she is called Ichchha. Shyamadasi is apparently her initiated name, received from Shyamananda (cf. 108).

[^101-48]: Radhananda is Rasikananda's eldest son (cf. 122, the middle son, and 124, the youngest); a Radhananda is also named in BR 15 (63) among Shyamananda's disciples.

[^101-49]: Krishna Bhanja is apparently a raja of Mayurbhanj (northern Utkala) of the Bhanja dynasty; the person is not identified. Vaidyanatha (132) is possibly Vaidyanatha Bhanja, according to tradition a disciple of Rasikananda; not established.

[^101-50]: The sixty-four limbs (angas) of bhakti are listed in Rupa Gosvami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2) and in CC, Madhya 22.

[^101-51]: Parikshit, Ambarisha, and the four Kumaras (Sanaka and his brothers) are great devotees of the Srimad-Bhagavatam. In the second line the 1997 edition reads "কৃষ্ণ ভক্ত রূপে" ("in the form of a devotee of Krishna").

[^101-52]: "[Krishna] is manifest in his pure heart" — *śuddha hṛdaye prakāśa*; the subject is not named; possibly "[bhakti] is manifest…" or "he is renowned [as] pure of heart".

[^101-53]: So in the 1941 edition: "গোপ অঙ্কুর দোঁহে" (*gopa aṅkura dõhe*, "the gopa Ankura — both"); the 1997 edition has "দেহে". Understood thus: Purushottamadasa and Ankura of the gopa caste — both servants of Shyamananda.

[^101-54]: Dariya (দাড়িয়া, *dāṛiyā*) is possibly a byname ("the bearded one") or a village name; not identified.

[^101-55]: Achyuta's son is Rasikananda (cf. 141). The line can also be read as "I worship Achyuta's son [and] the servant Jagannatha".

[^101-56]: Rasamaya is the author's father, a disciple of Rasikananda; the author does not name his mother. The five sons are listed in 140.

[^101-57]: The first word of the second line reads in the 1941 edition approximately as "আদ্য" (*ādya*, "first, original"), possibly "আত্ম"; the 1997 edition has "অন্য" ("other"): "renowned among the other Shyamanandis". Translated by the reading *ādya*; the reading is unclear. It is also unclear whether this is one person (Vamshi Mathuradasa) or two (Vamshi and Mathuradasa).

[^101-58]: Gopijana-vallabha is the author himself. Rasikananda here is one of his brothers, not the hero of the poem. "Kishoradasa" — *kiśorera dāsa*, literally "the servant of Kishora", taken as a name. Achyuta's son is Rasikananda (cf. 129).

[^101-59]: Vallabha is apparently the author himself (Gopijana-vallabha), and Radhavallabha his son. "Crest-jewel" — *cūṛāmaṇi*: "Rasikendra-chudamani" is an epithet of Rasikananda.

[^101-60]: Cf. Kunti's prayers on how Krishna protected the Pandavas in their calamities (SB 1.8).

[^101-61]: "They" are the author's family (cf. 140–145). Ashtanga-sadhana is eightfold yoga.

[^101-62]: "A shelter and a shield" — *śaraṇa pañjara* (*pañjara*, "cage, enclosure"), i.e. secure protection. "One's own brother" — *sodara*, literally "born of the same womb".

[^101-63]: Tulasi Thakura is apparently the same Tulasidasa, the "guru of sankirtana", whom Rasika honoured from birth (64–66; cf. note 34).

[^101-64]: Prabhu is apparently Rasikananda.

[^101-65]: Berhapal (বেঢ়াপাল, *beṛhāpāla*) is unidentified. Rasika-shekhara ("crest-jewel of rasikas") is taken as the name of a resident of Berhapal; the author also calls Rasikananda himself by this name (lahari 2, 4). The second line can also be understood as "…and all laughingly answered".

[^101-66]: So in the 1941 edition: "কাষ্ণ´" (the superscript mark is a displaced reph), taken as *kārṣṇa* ("devotees of Krishna"); likewise in 166. The 1997 edition reads "কাঞ্চ'", and in a quotation in that edition's preface "কার্য" ("affairs").

[^101-67]: Cf. SB 11.14.16: the Lord follows His desireless devotee in order to be purified by the dust of his feet. Thus the Lord Himself exalts His devotees.

[^101-68]: So in the 1941 edition: "স্বভাব বর্ণনা" (*svabhāva varṇanā*); the 1997 edition reads "স্বভাষ" ("in one's own language") or "ভাব". "Like a magician" — *kuhake* (*kuhaka*, a conjurer, magician). The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda.

[^101-69]: The subject is not named: apparently Rasikananda, whom the author speaks of as appearing "in the form of a devotee" (cf. note 10); it can also be understood of Sri Chaitanya — the Lord who came in the form of a devotee. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord.

[^101-70]: "Composed in the common tongue" — *bhāṣā-bandha*: in Bengali, not in Sanskrit. The point of the comparison: the power [of the narrative] does not depend on its language, just as a snake is venomous at all times.

[^101-71]: "On earth" — in the 1941 edition *mañce* (মঞ্চে), taken as *martye* ("in the world of men"); the 1997 edition reads "মর্তে".

[^101-72]: So in the 1941 edition: "গাও" (*gāo*, "sing"); it can also be understood as "[Krishna] with His own mouth sings the qualities of His devotee".

[^101-73]: The 1941 edition reads "না হইবে" ("there will not be"); the 1997 edition reads "না লইবে" ("do not impute"); translated by the latter reading.


## Lahari 2. Pilgrimage to the Holy Places

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda and an outline of what will be told; Shyamananda's birth in Dandeshvara to Krishna Mandala and Durika, his detachment and departure from home; his meeting with Hridayananda in Ambika and the name "Shyamananda"; Shyamananda's pilgrimage to the holy places, his return to Vraja and his life there in the company of Jiva Gosvami*

*The second lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^102-1]
*Ghosha: "It remains to proclaim the qualities of the moon Gauranga."*

**1.** *Song.* Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the abode of all virtues,
expert in all virtues, the life of those who have nothing!

**2.** Be merciful, Mahaprabhu — I humbly entreat —
that the glory of your virtues may appear in [my] heart.[^102-2]

**3.** How Prabhu came to the earth —
of that I shall tell; listen eagerly.

**4.** Let everyone say what he wishes — I have no fear of it:
the lord of my life is Rasika-shekhara.

**5.** I cannot live without singing his virtues:
Rasika-Murari has driven Vallabha mad.[^102-3]

**6.** I shall proclaim Rasika-deva's glory;
may good people and the learned not impute faults to me.

**7.** If one covers the moon with one's hand, it cannot be hidden:
it shows its own signs by itself.

**8.** Who has ever heard of such prema-bhakti?
[Such] has not been and will not be on the earth.

**9.** The lord of Rasika's life is the renowned Shyamananda;
through devotion to Shyamananda he became a giver of bhakti.

**10.** The Lord abides and sports in the heart of the devotee;
age after age, bestowing bhakti, He delivers the world.[^102-4]

**11.** All the people of Utkala were firmly set in sin —
[and] Shyamananda took birth in the form of Krishna's beloved.[^102-5]

**12.** His dearest devotee, the moon Rasikendra,
Shyamananda brought along with him to deliver living beings.

**13.** How the two of them subdued Utkala —
something of those stories I shall tell:

**14.** how the two were born, each in his own place;
how in detachment they wandered to the holy places;

**15.** how the two met and came together
[and] in many delightful ways gave prema-bhakti in Utkala;

**16.** how they delivered chandalas and others;
how the two became renowned in Utkala —

**17.** of all these wondrous [deeds] I shall make something known;
may the wise and learned not impute faults to me.

**18.** Now hear the secret of Shyamananda's birth,
the supreme object of worship of the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas.

**19.** Of his birth, of how he took renunciation, of his pilgrimage
I shall briefly tell something.

**20.** In the clan of the gopas [there was] Sri Krishna Mandala Mahashaya;
leaving Gauda, he made his home in Utkala.

**21.** A village called Dandeshvara is a very holy place;
in that village the Mahashaya settled.[^102-6]

**22.** His wife, devoted to her husband, was called Durika —
peaceful, self-controlled, forbearing, a mother of the world.

**23.** Husband and wife — both were known for their reverence for brahmanas,
devoted to every dharma, very pure of heart.

**24.** From her womb Shyamananda-raya was born;
for some time he lived in his own home.

**25.** Marriage and other enjoyments, various gifts —
thus he spent some time.

**26.** His heart was ever full of detachment out of love for Krishna;
the tears from his eyes drenched his whole body.

**27.** Absorbed in the rasa of Krishna, Prabhu does not know himself;
day and night he weeps unceasingly, calling "Krishna!"

**28.** The happiness of attachment to home he regards as equal to poison:
nothing pleases him but Krishna alone.

**29.** Prabhu tries to go away [from home],
but no one lets him go — all his kinsmen.

**30.** Then Prabhu explained everything to them all:
"Out of love for Krishna I shall go wandering.

**31.** I shall see Vrajapuri, Krishna's own abode;
when I remember it, my life will not stay in me.

**32.** Say nothing to me; listen, all of you:
I shall certainly go on pilgrimage to the holy places.

**33.** I shall certainly go round [the whole] earth."
Hearing this, his kinsmen were greatly afraid.

**34.** His kinsmen resort to various means:
in many ways they tried to keep [him].

**35.** Ocean waves are not held back by a dam of sand:
who has the power to break such detachment?

**36.** Prabhu's younger brother was Balarama Mahashaya,
peaceful, self-controlled, very pure of heart.[^102-7]

**37.** To him [Prabhu] handed over all household affairs,
and himself, taking renunciation, went out.

**38.** For some time Balarama remained at home;
out of love for Shyamananda his life would not stay in him.

**39.** After some days Balarama
set out on pilgrimage to the holy places in search of Shyamananda.

**40.** First of all Mahaprabhu Shyamananda-raya,
having gone to Ambuya, sees Sri Chaitanya-raya.[^102-8]

**41.** On seeing Nityananda he was filled with supreme bliss;
then he had the darshan of Sri Hridayananda.

**42.** Prostrate on the ground like a stick, he offers prayers;
the devotees report [to Hridayananda]: "[A] certain vairagi [has come].

**43.** He is very beautiful to look at, his form is divine;
offering praises, he keeps prostrating again and again."

**44.** Hearing [this], Hridayananda was overjoyed
and ordered: "Bring the vairagi quickly."

**45.** Seeing [him], Hridayananda rejoiced in his mind:
"This is the one who will make bhakti for Krishna manifest."

**46.** The Mahashaya asked: "Whose servant are you?
What is [your] name, for what purpose have you appeared here?"

**47.** He replied: "My name is Duhkhi Krishnadasa;
birth after birth I am your very own servant."

**48.** Hearing [this], Hridayananda Prabhu rejoiced;
giving instruction, he gave [him] the name Shyamananda.[^102-9]

**49.** [Hridayananda] commanded Shyamananda: "Listen, [and act] quickly:
make Vaishnavas of every house in Utkala, one after another.

**50.** By your mercy [one person] will become equal to you:
such a person has appeared in Utkala.[^102-10]

**51.** Taking him with you, give prema to all living beings;
Chaitanya's command is the sixteen names of "Hare Krishna."[^102-11]

**52.** Preach Chaitanya's prema-bhakti,
deliver all the living beings of Utkala."

**53.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda-raya was abashed:
"Everything comes true, Prabhu, by your mercy.

**54.** Be merciful to me, Prabhu, son of Subala:[^102-12]
in my heart I have a desire — to wander on pilgrimage to the holy places."

**55.** Having stayed there some days, he took his leave
[and] set out on pilgrimage to the holy places — Shyamananda-raya.

**56.** Listen, all, to Shyamananda's pilgrimage to the holy places,
by hearing which one obtains the treasure of love for Krishna.

**57.** First he went to Vakreshvara [and] Vaidyanatha;
to Gaya [and] Kashi, the abode of Shiva, he went quickly.[^102-13]

**58.** In [the month of] Magha — at Prayaga, [where] the Ganga flows south;
then, quickly reaching Mathura, he himself stayed there.[^102-14]

**59.** He saw the resting place on the Yamuna, Govardhana;
he sees Madana-gopala, Govinda, Vrindavana.[^102-15]

**60.** Wandering from kunja to kunja, he sees all the temples;
Gokula [and] the twelve forests — he saw them all.[^102-16]

**61.** Endowed with great renunciation, full of love for Krishna —
the servants [who were] with him cannot keep up with him.

**62.** Having stayed there some days, in his own play
he goes in whatever direction he wishes.

**63.** Joyfully seeing Hastina, the city of the Pandavas,
Prabhu very quickly reached Dvaraka.

**64.** Seeing Ranchhor-raya, [he was filled with] great bliss;
Shyamananda stayed some days in Dvaraka.[^102-17]

**65.** [His] renunciation is very severe; [he has] no awareness of the body;
he goes in whatever direction he wishes.

**66.** He knows neither north nor south, east nor west:
wherever the mind leads, there he goes.

**67.** All his companions search [for him] and roam from land to land;
after a day or two someone finds a trace of him.

**68.** Then he went to Sindhupura, to Kapila's place;
he came to Matsya-tirtha, Shiva-kanchi, Vishnu-kanchi.[^102-18]

**69.** Kurukshetra, Prithudaka, Bindu-sarovara —
Prabhu goes quickly to see Prabhasa.[^102-19]

**70.** With joy in his heart he roams, [heeding] neither day nor night;
in whatever direction he hears of a tirtha, that way he goes.

**71.** He takes no care to go round [the places] in order:
by his own will, as his heart pleases, he wanders.

**72.** He came to Tritakupayana-tirtha, Vishala;
he went to Brahma-tirtha, Chandra-tirtha, Pratisrota.[^102-20]

**73.** Having seen Prachi-Sarasvati, Naimisharanya,
Prabhu came to the city of Ayodhya and stayed [there].

**74.** The kingdom of Guhaka, [king] of the chandalas, the Sarayu, the Kaushiki;
he went to the hermitage of Paulastya, to the Gomati, the Gandaki.[^102-21]

**75.** Bathing in the sixteen tirthas on Mount Mahendra;
to Haridvara, the birth[place] of the Ganga, he came quickly.[^102-22]

**76.** He went to Badarikashrama and saw Narayana;
joyfully Prabhu sees the hermitage of Vyasa.

**77.** Incessantly he remembers the name of Krishna;
his cloth is soaked by the streams of tears from his eyes.

**78.** From there, after some days, wandering and wandering,
Prabhu came quickly to the Pampa, the Bhagirathi.

**79.** Afterwards Prabhu came to Sapta-Godavari,
to Dhenu-tirtha, to Shri-parvata, to the city of the Dravidas.

**80.** He went to the Lord of Mount Venkata, to Kamakoshthi-puri,
Kanchi, Haridvara, [to] southern Madhupuri.[^102-23]

**81.** He crossed the Kritamala, the Tamraparni, the Yamuna;
[visited] Mount Malaya, [and] Agastya's sacrificial ground.

**82.** He went to the abode of Chaidya, to the city of Kalinga;
he went to the southern ocean, to Sri Anantapura.[^102-24]

**83.** Wandering and wandering, at the lake of Pancha-apsaras
Prabhu spends his time with joy in his heart.

**84.** [The place] called Gokarna, Kulanaka, Trigartaka,
Durveshana, Arya, Nirvindhya, the abode of the Payoshni.

**85.** He went to the Reva, to the city of Mahishmati, to Malla-tirtha;
[visited] Shurparaka, Pratichiri, came to Setubandha.[^102-25]

**86.** In whatever direction the mind leads, in that direction he goes —
wherever he hears there is a holy place.

**87.** Whatever direction Prabhu goes, he asks no one;
what comes first, what comes after — he pays no heed to this.

**88.** Going to Dhenu-tirtha, he hears of the abduction of maya-Sita;
Avanti, Jiyada-Narasimha, the Godavari.[^102-26]

**89.** Devapuri, Trimalla, to the city of Kurmanatha —
in this way he keeps roaming, seeing tirtha after tirtha.[^102-27]

**90.** In supreme bliss Prabhu went to Nilachala:
arriving, he stayed in the city of Purushottama.

**91.** Seeing Krishna and Balarama — the lords of his life —
[he had] gooseflesh all over his body, tears flowing incessantly.

**92.** Seeing Jagabandhu, [he was filled with] great bliss and elation;
seeing [His] moonlike face, he fulfilled his desire.[^102-28]

**93.** Joyfully seeing all the places day and night,
conversing with all the mahantas,

**94.** having stayed [there] some days, he went to Gangasagara;
coming from there, he touched [the place of] his birth.[^102-29]

**95.** Then Prabhu went again to Mathura;
he stayed [there] many days in his own play.

**96.** Awaiting the appearance of [his] servant,
Prabhu incessantly wanders and sees Vrajapura.[^102-30]

**97.** Wandering from kunja to kunja, he sees all the places;
his voice choked with prema, tears, gooseflesh — incessantly.

**98.** Saying, "When will I attain Krishna, the lord of my life?"
in Vrindavana, at the place of the rasa[-lila], he rolls on the ground.

**99.** In renunciation, with a joyful mind, beside himself within,
he converses with all of Krishna's companions.

**100.** Jiva Gosani, Thakura Haripriya-dasa —
with all of them he constantly spent his time.[^102-31]

**101.** Absorbed in Krishna, he weeps incessantly,
reads the scriptures on bhakti and hears [them].

**102.** At every moment he delights in prema-bhakti —
thus Prabhu lived in Vrajapura.

**103.** The song Rasika-mangala is sweet to hear;
hearing it, all living beings, cross over [the age of] Kali.

**104.** Whoever hears of Shyamananda's pilgrimage to the holy places
is at once freed from all sins.

**105.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the second lahari, called "Pilgrimage to the Holy Places".*

[^102-1]: Raga Karuna-shri — as in lahari 1 (note 8). The ghosha (refrain) is rendered approximately: "গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদের গুণ রহিল ঘোষিতে" (*gaurāṅga-cā̃dera guṇa rahila ghoṣite*), literally "the qualities of the moon Gauranga remained to be proclaimed".

[^102-2]: Mahaprabhu here is apparently Shyamananda (cf. 40: "Mahaprabhu Shyamananda-raya"); it may also be an address to Sri Chaitanya (cf. the ghosha). In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition Mahaprabhu is Sri Chaitanya; the author thus exalts Shyamananda (cf. lahari 1, note 2).

[^102-3]: Rasika-shekhara ("crest-jewel of rasikas", 4) and Rasika-Murari are Rasikananda. Vallabha is the author himself, Gopijana-vallabha.

[^102-4]: Prabhu is here taken as the Lord; from the context the line may also refer to Shyamananda, whom the author exalts as descending age after age (cf. lahari 1, 9 and note 10).

[^102-5]: Literally "in the form of Krishna's beloved" (*kṛṣṇa-priyā-rūpe*; *priyā* is feminine), i.e. apparently Sri Radha; it can also be understood as "as one dear to Krishna". According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, not Radhika Herself (see lahari 1, note 2).

[^102-6]: Krishna Mandala and Durika are Shyamananda's parents (cf. lahari 1, 10 and 61). Dandeshvara is Shyamananda's native village in Utkala; in BR 15 (20) it is "the village of Dandeshvara-Dharenda".

[^102-7]: Balarama is Shyamananda's younger brother (cf. lahari 1, 62).

[^102-8]: Ambuya (আম্বুয়া, *āmbuyā*) is Ambika (Kalna) and its surroundings. There Gauridasa Pandita, and after him Hridaya Chaitanya, served the Deities of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda (cf. BR 15, 93–95); "sees Sri Chaitanya-raya" and "on seeing Nityananda" (41) refer to the darshan of these Deities. Hridayananda (41) is Hridaya Chaitanya, Shyamananda's guru (cf. lahari 1, note 13). On "Mahaprabhu" see note 2.

[^102-9]: Duhkhi Krishnadasa is Shyamananda's former name. Here the name "Shyamananda" is given to him by Hridayananda at initiation ("giving instruction" — *upadeśa kari*); according to BR 15 (106) and tradition, this name became known in Vrindavana when he found Sri Radha's anklet.

[^102-10]: "Has appeared" — *sannidhāna*. Apparently this refers to Rasikananda, Shyamananda's future disciple (his birth is told in lahari 3).

[^102-11]: The maha-mantra of sixteen names: "Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare / Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare".

[^102-12]: Prabhu here is Hridayananda. "Son of Subala" — the spiritual descendant of Gauridasa Pandita, who in Krishna's pastimes is the cowherd boy Subala (see lahari 1, note 16); Gauridasa is Hridayananda's guru.

[^102-13]: Vakreshvara is a holy place of Shiva in Birbhum (West Bengal). Vaidyanatha is the shrine of Shiva at Deoghar (Jharkhand). Kashi is Varanasi; "the abode of Shiva" may also refer to all three places named.

[^102-14]: Magha is the month (January–February) of the Magha Mela at Prayaga. "The Ganga flows south" (*dakṣiṇa-vāhinī*) — so in the edition (and in the 1997 edition); the sense is approximate.

[^102-15]: The resting place is apparently Vishrama Ghat on the Yamuna in Mathura. Madana-gopala and Govinda are Deities of Vrindavana (cf. lahari 1, note 24).

[^102-16]: The twelve forests of Vraja.

[^102-17]: Hastina is Hastinapura. Ranchhor-raya is the Deity of Krishna in Dvaraka (see lahari 1, note 27).

[^102-18]: Sindhupura, "Kapila's place" — apparently Kapila's ashrama where the Ganga meets the ocean (Gangasagara); the 1997 edition reads "Siddhapura". Matsya-tirtha is mentioned in Sri Chaitanya's southern journey (CC, Madhya 9). Shiva-kanchi and Vishnu-kanchi are the two parts of Kanchipuram.

[^102-19]: The list of tirthas in 69–89 largely follows Balarama's pilgrimage (SB 10.78–79) and Sri Chaitanya's southern journey (CC, Madhya 9), but without geographical order — as the author himself says (71, 87). Names are given as in the edition (the 1997 edition agrees); some are corrupt.

[^102-20]: Tritakupayana is apparently the Tritakupa of SB 10.79.11. Chandra-tirtha is Chakra-tirtha in the SB. "Pratisrota" apparently comes from SB 10.78.18, where Balarama went "upstream" (*prati-srotam*) along the Sarasvati; here it is taken as a place name.

[^102-21]: Guhaka is Guha, king of the Nishadas (a hunting tribe) in the Ramayana, Rama's friend. The hermitage of Paulastya — in SB 10.79.10, the hermitage of Pulaha.

[^102-22]: "In the sixteen tirthas" — *ṣoṛaśa-tīrthete*; it may also be the name of a single tirtha. Mount Mahendra — SB 10.79.11. Haridvara is where the Ganga comes down onto the plains.

[^102-23]: Shri-parvata is Shri-shaila; the Lord of Mount Venkata is the Deity of Venkateshvara at Tirupati; Kamakoshthi-puri — CC, Madhya 9; Kanchi is Kanchipuram; southern Madhupuri is Madurai, "southern Mathura". "Haridvara" (*haridvārāya*) here is apparently a corruption of the words *sarid-varām* ("the best of rivers", said of the Kaveri) in SB 10.79.14. Dhenu-tirtha (79, 88) has not been identified.

[^102-24]: Kritamala, Tamraparni, Mount Malaya, Agastya — SB 10.79.16–17 and CC, Madhya 9; the Yamuna here is as in the edition. Chaidya is Shishupala, king of Chedi; read as in the 1997 edition ("চৈদ্যের"), the conjunct being unclear in the 1941 edition. Sri Anantapura is apparently the shrine of Ananta Padmanabha (Trivandrum; CC, Madhya 9).

[^102-25]: Pancha-apsaras, Gokarna, Arya, Shurparaka, Payoshni, Nirvindhya, Reva, Mahishmati — SB 10.79.18–21. Kulanaka, Trigartaka (in the SB, Kerala and Trigarta?), Durveshana, Malla-tirtha (in the SB, Manu-tirtha?) and Pratichiri have not been identified and are apparently corrupt. Setubandha is Rameshvaram.

[^102-26]: According to CC, Madhya 9, Sri Chaitanya heard the account of the Kurma Purana about Ravana's abduction of maya-Sita (the illusory Sita) at Rameshvaram; the author places it at Dhenu-tirtha. Avanti is Ujjain; Jiyada-Narasimha is the Deity of Nrisimha at Simhachalam (CC, Madhya 8).

[^102-27]: Kurmanatha is Kurma-kshetra, a place of Sri Chaitanya's southern journey (CC, Madhya 7). Devapuri and Trimalla have not been identified.

[^102-28]: Nilachala, the city of Purushottama, is Puri. Krishna and Balarama are Jagannatha and Baladeva; Jagabandhu ("friend of the world") is Jagannatha.

[^102-29]: His birthplace is Dandeshvara (Dharenda); see note 6.

[^102-30]: "The appearance of the servant" — *bhṛtyera prakāśa*: apparently the appearance of Rasikananda, his future disciple (cf. 50); the sense is approximate.

[^102-31]: Jiva Gosani is Jiva Gosvami, under whom, according to BR 15, Shyamananda studied the books on bhakti in Vrindavana (cf. 101). Thakura Haripriya-dasa has not been identified; the 1997 edition reads "Thakura Haripriya" (*ṭhākura haripriyā*). It could also be taken as an epithet of Jiva: "Thakura, servant of Haripriya (Radha)", but "with all of them" points to several persons.


## Lahari 3. Description of the Glory of Rohini

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; the sinfulness of Utkala and the devotees' prayers to Krishna for the deliverance of living beings; Rohini in Mallabhumi, Rasikananda's native village, its beauty and wealth; Achyuta, Rasikananda's father, and his marriage to Bhavani*

*The third lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^103-1]
*Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!*
*O Murari, O Murari, O Murari!*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the abode of all virtues!
Be merciful, so that I may sing the glory of your name.

**2.** Listen, listen, everyone, to the Rasika-mangala:
I shall describe the glory of Rasika-deva.

**3.** Who can comprehend [his] supremely wonderful pastimes?
Briefly I shall proclaim only a little.

**4.** I shall make known the book in four vibhagas;
listen, all, attentively and joyfully.[^103-2]

**5.** For what reason Sri Chaitanya, sending [His] servant,
delivered Utkala by bestowing prema-bhakti —

**6.** of all that I shall tell something in detail;
learned and good people, do not find fault with me.

**7.** In Utkala all the people are firmly set on sin:
they do not take the name of Hari, do not hear of Hari's glory.

**8.** They constantly commit exceedingly wicked deeds,
endlessly revile brahmanas and Vaishnavas.

**9.** Drunk on wine, they do violence
to sannyasis bearing the danda, to Vaishnavas and brahmanas.

**10.** Out of greed for wealth they do violence to sadhus;
this is how they behave in the forest lands.

**11.** Whether king or subjects — all are wicked-minded;
[so are] all the castes, as many as dwell in the land of Utkala.

**12.** All of them, bereft of sense, kill living beings;
vying with one another, everyone slaughters and roasts goats.[^103-3]

**13.** As many mahatas and others as there are among them —
all are engaged in various kinds of ignorance; it cannot be told.[^103-4]

**14.** Merely out of greed for paltry goods they do violence to living beings,
they kill hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas, Vaishnavas and sadhus.

**15.** All the goods they bring by doing violence to sadhus
[they spend:] they eat meat, [drink] wine, and give to harlots.

**16.** Setting up [their own objects of worship], they perform various pujas;
they do not hear topics of Hari, do not hear kirtana.

**17.** Hearing sankirtana, all run to beat [the singers]:
"Because of the noise of these [people], Lakshmi leaves the land!"

**18.** Seeing a Vaishnava, they say, "These are thieves!" —
and, driving [them] out of the village, keep [them] in the far wilderness.

**19.** Thus I cannot tell all [their] various sins:
the land of Utkala was seized by great sin.

**20.** Such servants of Krishna as there were among them
at every moment prayed to [His] lotus feet:

**21.** "Prabhu, give good sense to all these living beings;
destroying all sins, give [them] devotion to Krishna."

**22.** Thus all the devotees of Krishna, day and night,
for the sake of the living beings prayed at Krishna's feet:

**23.** "Prabhu, send [Your] servant and deliver [them]:
this burden of the living beings' suffering is unbearable.

**24.** Prabhu, protect these suffering living beings;
bestowing prema-bhakti, preserve them all."

**25.** The Lord, affectionate to His devotees, at the word of the devotees
caused His dear devotee to be born as the son of Achyuta.[^103-5]

**26.** I shall tell of this in detail — listen, everyone —
how Rasika was born in the land of Utkala.

**27.** In Utkala there is [a region] called Mallabhumi;
in it is the incomparable village of Rohini,

**28.** a village equal to Cuttack — all people know this —
on the bank of the Suvarnarekha, a most holy place.[^103-6]

**29.** Near the village is a river called the Dolanga;
[its] water is like the water of the Ganga, a true well of sweetness.[^103-7]

**30.** Near Rohini is the great holy place of Barajit,
where Sita, Rama and Lakshmana rested.[^103-8]

**31.** [There is] Rameshvara of the twelve lingas, the excellent Shambhu;
the moon of the Raghu dynasty worshipped [him] abundantly.[^103-9]

**32.** [There] the stream of the Suvarnarekha flows northward;
millions of people come there to take its water.[^103-10]

**33.** Such a holy river and holy places [lie] on all sides;
all around Rohini people live by hundreds of thousands.

**34.** The place is beautiful to see, most delightful:
dense forests, groves of mango and jackfruit.

**35.** Taba, jamir, lemons, shatakara, kamala,
naranga, pomegranates — on every tree in clusters.[^103-11]

**36.** Many pandava trees, beautiful to see,
splendid, splendid banana groves, enchanting.[^103-12]

**37.** All kinds of flowers shine on all sides;
all the gods are enchanted, craving the six tastes.[^103-13]

**38.** Splendid, splendid betel, splendid, splendid rice;
much grain grows, and the place is enchanting.

**39.** Such a place, a well of sweetness, is beautiful to see:
there are very many ponds, embankments and fields.

**40.** There is a capital, a fort, beautiful to see;
around the fort lies the town of Rauni.[^103-14]

**41.** Hundreds upon hundreds of Deities and brahmanas dwell there;
[there is] Vedic learning, [and according to] the smriti-shastras, sandhya and tarpana.[^103-15]

**42.** All joyfully devote themselves to study;
the sound of the Vedas [rises] on all sides incessantly.

**43.** Sannyasis bearing the danda stay there at all times;
all the brahmanas who know the Vedas serve [them].

**44.** The navashakha castes live there, townspeople;
all carry on trade; there is no sorrow or grief.[^103-16]

**45.** The high platforms are very handsome, the houses splendid, splendid;
at the doors are tulasi-manchas, beautiful to see.[^103-17]

**46.** Whatever each one's livelihood, all buy and sell;
hundreds of thousands, thousands, hundreds — who can count them?

**47.** The townspeople live in royal splendour;
only one wealth is lacking — krishna-prema-bhakti.

**48.** All the other castes live at a distance;
no one is unhappy, all pass their time in joy.

**49.** I cannot describe the glory of Rauni at all:
is it Navadvipa, Mathura, or the city of the Raghu dynasty?

**50.** As the abode of Sri Krishna is Vaikuntha-dhama,
so the place where a devotee lives is equal to it.

**51.** Wherever devotees abide age after age,
all those places become equal to Vaikuntha.

**52.** Have no doubt at all about this in your minds:
the Vedas and Puranas speak of these signs.

**53.** Therefore I bow to Rauni:
blessed is that place of Rasikachandra's birth.

**54.** The lord of that land is Achyuta Mahashaya,
peaceful, self-controlled, forbearing, most kind-hearted.

**55.** It is known that he was born in a noble family of karanas;
round about live his kinsmen and all his servants.[^103-18]

**56.** Everyone's way of life is like royal splendour:
all have very large houses and walls.

**57.** Among them Achyuta's house is outstanding:
its supremely beautiful assembly hall is famous to all.

**58.** He knows nothing but service to the brahmanas;
all praise him, calling him a brahmana.

**59.** All know him as a benefactor of others;
Achyuta's glory cannot be told at all.

**60.** That Mahashaya is devoted to the name of Hari,
tender with compassion toward all beings, humble with all.

**61.** Birth after birth he performed much austerity;
for that reason Rasikendra was born [to him] as his son.

**62.** I shall tell something of all this in detail;
listen, listen attentively, all you people of Krishna.[^103-19]

**63.** Thus that Achyuta lived there;
he had several wives and many sons.[^103-20]

**64.** In Cuttack lived one named Haladhara;
because of the oppression of the Yavanas he left his home.[^103-21]

**65.** That Mahashaya was a pure, noble karana;
[asking,] "Rauni, Rauni?" he came there.

**66.** Hearing Achyuta's name, he went to that land;
arriving, he stayed in the house of Gopi Mandala.[^103-22]

**67.** Husband and wife, the two of them, and one daughter —
fortunate in beauty and virtues, most lovely in form.

**68.** The name of that mother of the world was Bhavani;
by her austerities she became the mother of Rasika.

**69.** One day Achyuta, most fortunate,
went to the house of Gopi Mandala.

**70.** Seeing that fortunate girl, Achyuta
inquires of Mandala about her:

**71.** "From where has this worthy man come?
Make an effort that this girl be given to me."

**72.** Then Gopi disclosed to the mother and father:
"Give your daughter to the Pattanayaka."[^103-23]

**73.** Hearing this, the mother and father were overjoyed;
briefly they told Mandala everything:

**74.** "Giving my daughter, I take his shelter.
There is only one thing I humbly submit:

**75.** through the oppression of the Yavanas I am bereft of my estate and without property;
I shall give him the girl alone.[^103-24]

**76.** Whatever shame and trouble there is in this, the burden is yours;
afterwards do not hold any fault against me."

**77.** Hearing such humility from the girl's father, [Gopi said:]
"The burden of this matter is mine, be assured."

**78.** Gopa told Achyuta everything in detail;
hearing it, [Achyuta] diligently sends messengers.[^103-25]

**79.** From kingdom after kingdom he had all the provisions brought;
no one can transgress Achyuta's command.

**80.** Fixing an excellent hour, he performed the wedding;
telling cannot convey the splendour of the wedding.

**81.** As at the wedding of a great king or of the gods,
such joy was there in the assembly of Rauni.

**82.** Music, the roar of dundubhis of many kinds;
hundreds of thousands upon hundreds of thousands of chandrodayas, deutis and torches.[^103-26]

**83.** Seeing the wedding, all the people were in an ocean of joy;
taking the bride, the Mahashaya came home.

**84.** Who can tell all that joy and happiness?
Briefly I have proclaimed a little.

**85.** Now I shall make known the birth of Rasika;
hearing it, the devotees will rejoice at heart.

**86.** The Rasika-mangala is a most excellent secret,
the supreme object of worship for the people of Krishna, [the followers] of Shyamananda.[^103-27]

**87.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the third lahari, called "Description of the Glory of Rohini," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^103-1]: Raga Kaushika. The two italic lines after the raga are the refrain; the word "ghosha" does not appear here in the edition (cf. lahari 2, note 1). Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari ("enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna, which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari, i.e. Rasikananda (cf. lahari 1, note 7).

[^103-2]: "The book in four vibhagas" — *caturtha-vibhāga puṁthi*, i.e. the whole Rasika-mangala (Purva, Dakshina, Pashchima, Uttara).

[^103-3]: The reading in the 1941 edition is clear: "বাদাবাদি বোদাপোড় কাটে" (*bādābādi bodā-poṛa kāṭe*); the sense is conjectural: Oriya *boda*, "he-goat"; *poṛa*, "to roast"; *bādābādi*, "vying with one another".

[^103-4]: Mahatas (*mahata*) are apparently village headmen and landholders (cf. *mahato*, *mahanti*); it may also be understood as "the notables".

[^103-5]: The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda; Achyuta is his father (cf. BR 15).

[^103-6]: Mallabhumi is the region to which BR 15 also assigns Rasikananda's native village (BR 15: "In Mallabhumi there is a village named Rayani"). Rohini is Rasikananda's native village on the Suvarnarekha (today in Jhargram district); in BR 15 it is called Rayani, and later in this lahari Rauni. Cuttack was the capital of Utkala under the Gajapatis.

[^103-7]: The Dolanga is a river near Rohini (cf. BR 15: "the Dolanga river"). "Well of sweetness" — *rasa-kūpa*; possibly a local name (cf. "the place Rasakupa" later in this lahari).

[^103-8]: Barajit (*bārājita*) — in BR 15 "Barayita" (*bārāyita*); local tradition connects it with the wanderings of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana. Its location has not been identified.

[^103-9]: "The twelve lingas" (*duyādaśa liṅga*) — apparently the twelve jyotirlingas of Shiva, among which Rameshvara is counted; here it is Shiva Rameshvara near Barajit, worshipped by Rama, "the moon of the Raghu dynasty" (cf. 30; BR 15: "In Barayita Rama, son of Dasharatha, installed the Shiva named Rameshvara").

[^103-10]: A river's northward course (*uttara-vāhinī*) is considered especially holy; cf. BR 15: "There the Suvarnarekha flows northward."

[^103-11]: The names of the citrus fruits are given as in the edition: taba (*ṭābā*, a large lemon), jamir (*jāmira*, a kind of citron), shatakara (*śatakarā*, unidentified), kamala (*kamalā*, mandarin), naranga (*nāreṅga*, orange). "In clusters" — *jhārā jhārā*.

[^103-12]: "Pandava" (*pāṇḍava-vṛkṣa*) — the reading in the 1941 edition is clear; which tree is meant has not been identified.

[^103-13]: "The six tastes" — *ṣaḍ-rasa* (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, astringent); the 1941 edition has "যড়রস," the same word in an older letter form (so also the 1997 ed.: "ষড়রস").

[^103-14]: Rauni (*rauni*) is the same village of Rohini (cf. note 6); in BR 15, Rayani.

[^103-15]: "Deities and brahmanas" — *devatā brāhmaṇa*; it may also be understood as "brahmanas [honoured as] gods." Sandhya is the daily prayer at dawn, noon and dusk; tarpana is the offering of water to the ancestors and the gods.

[^103-16]: Navashakha ("nine branches") — a group of clean Shudra castes of Bengal and neighbouring lands: artisans and traders.

[^103-17]: Platforms (*piṇḍā*) — high earthen verandas along the houses. A tulasi-mancha is a raised stand with a Tulasi plant in front of a Vaishnava's house.

[^103-18]: Karanas — the caste of scribes and officials in Utkala (corresponding to the Kayasthas of Bengal); Achyuta belonged to it, as did Haladhara below (65).

[^103-19]: "People of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana*, i.e. Vaishnavas.

[^103-20]: "Several" — literally "two or four" (*dui cāri*). Rasikananda's mother is Bhavani (68); the author says nothing here about Achyuta's other wives and sons.

[^103-21]: Haladhara is Bhavani's father (67–68). Cuttack — see note 6. The Yavanas here are apparently the Muslim rulers who took possession of Utkala after the fall of the Gajapatis (1568).

[^103-22]: Gopi Mandala (*gopī-maṇḍala*) — a resident of Rohini with whom Haladhara stayed; Mandala is a family title (usually of a village headman). Below he is called simply Mandala (70, 73), Gopi (72, 77) and Gopa (78).

[^103-23]: Pattanayaka (*paṭṭanāyaka*) — an honorific title of the karanas of Utkala; here, Achyuta.

[^103-24]: "The girl alone" (*kanyā-mātra*), i.e. without a dowry. "Bereft of my estate" — *rājya-hṛta*.

[^103-25]: "Gopa" — so in the 1941 edition; the 1997 ed. has "Gopi." Apparently the same Gopi Mandala.

[^103-26]: The dundubhi is a large kettledrum. Chandrodaya (*candrodaya*, "moonrise") — apparently a kind of festive lamp or firework; deuti (*deuṭi*) — a lamp on a stand.

[^103-27]: "[The followers] of Shyamananda" — *śyāmānandī*, the Shyamanandis, i.e. Shyamananda's line; "people of Krishna" — see note 19. "The supreme object of worship" — *parama upāsya*.


## Lahari 4. Description of the Pastime of Rasika's Birth

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; the devotees' prayers for Utkala and Rasika's descent; Bhavani's wondrous pregnancy, conjectures and blessings; the birth of Rasikananda on the night of Dipavali in Shaka 1512, the position of the planets and the beauty of the infant; gifts and rites, the women's blessings; the infant weeps on hearing Krishna's name; the rejoicing of the Vaishnavas in Achyuta's house*

*The fourth lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^104-1]
*Ghosha: "O Hari, this time be merciful to me:*
*I hope to obtain the shade of Your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the abode of all virtues!
Glory, glory [to him who is] the dear life of Rasika-shekhara![^104-2]

**2.** Thus in that land Achyuta Mahashaya
lives in royal splendour, fearing no one.

**3.** Constantly with his beloved Bhavani
he passes his time at home in manifold delights.

**4.** Here all the devotees at the lotus feet [of the Lord]
incessantly pray for the deliverance of Utkala:

**5.** "Prabhu, send a devotee and deliver [them]:
this burden of the living beings' suffering is unbearable."

**6.** At the devotees' word Prabhu became merciful:
He sent His own devotee Rasika to earth.

**7.** All Rasika's dear associates, his companions,
took birth in fitting places in Utkala.[^104-3]

**8.** Hear all this in detail with joy —
how he was born to deliver the living beings.

**9.** At that time, on an auspicious day with every good sign,
Achyuta came together with Bhavani.

**10.** Spending that night together in their chamber,
in joy in Krishna, in manifold rasas, they stayed awake all night.[^104-4]

**11.** At that very time [he] took his rest in the womb:
by the good fortune of Utkala the abode of virtues appeared.

**12.** Husband and wife, the two of them, and all the household
count the months — one, two.

**13.** Day by day that faithful wife grows more radiant:
bearing Rasika in her womb, she became the mother of the world.

**14.** Seeing this, all the household were astonished:
"From where has Bhavani gained such beauty?"

**15.** The family members say to one another:
"Bhavani's beauty and splendour cannot be described.

**16.** Is it Brahma, is it Shambhu, is it Narayana,
is it Vyasa, Shukadeva, Narada and others,

**17.** is it Parikshit, is it King Janaka —
what great soul has taken birth in the womb?"
