**18.** Such various conjectures the household make;
the extraordinary pregnancy cannot be described.

**19.** All the neighbours whisper together:
"Bhavani has taken on a form that enchants the world."

**20.** From mouth to mouth everyone hears —
subjects, kinsmen, Vaishnavas, brahmanas.

**21.** Hearing of the glory of the pregnancy, all the townspeople
came to see with joyful hearts.

**22.** Seeing the pregnancy, all are amazed:
"What mahapurusha has appeared here?"

**23.** All the devotees of Krishna, hearing this, are in an ocean of joy:
"This person will deliver everyone."

**24.** All the astrologer brahmanas give their blessings:
"From this womb will come a chakravarti, a king of the earth."

**25.** Hearing everyone's blessings, Achyuta,
seeing the form of the expectant mother, was struck with wonder.

**26.** Reflecting, Achyuta rejoiced at heart:
"A great mahapurusha is within this womb."

**27.** Thus ten months were counted;
the great month of Kartika arrived.

**28.** The new moon of the Dipa-yatra came;
people come from land after land to see it.[^104-5]

**29.** That day there was service to the Deity (Thakura) in Achyuta's house
and [in the houses of] all the other officials in the town of Rauni.

**30.** Many Vaishnavas and brahmanas came there;
on all four sides the name of Hari resounds again and again.

**31.** Hundreds upon hundreds of lamps burn, torches, deutis,
chandrodayas of many kinds, festive patis.[^104-6]

**32.** Darkness went far away, [all became] brilliantly radiant;
all those places became brighter than day.

**33.** At that time the mother of Sri Rasika-deva
herself lets everyone know of her labour pains.

**34.** Hearing this, Achyuta called all the brahmanas
and set in place excellent astrologers and dandatamis.[^104-7]

**35.** All the brahmanas who know the Vedas recite the Vedas;
on all sides the name of Hari and sankirtana are heard.

**36.** At this time came Rasika's arrival on earth;
the record is the Shaka year 1512,

**37.** the eighteenth day of Tula, the new moon of the dark fortnight:
the new moon waning, the pratipad setting in.[^104-8]

**38.** The bright pratipad, a Sunday, an auspicious moment,
the third watch of the night, the deepest darkness.[^104-9]

**39.** The Sun in Svati, in Tula; the Moon in Vishakha, in Tula;
and Mars in Uttara-phalguni, in Kanya.[^104-10]

**40.** Mercury in Svati, in Tula; Jupiter in Svati, in Tula;
Venus in Hasta, in Kanya: all the benefic planets were gathered.

**41.** Saturn in Ardra, in Mithuna: a most auspicious moment;
Rahu in Pushya, in Karkata: supremely excellent.

**42.** Ketu in Uttara-ashadha: everything excellent;
the lagna Kanya: at an auspicious moment he took birth.

**43.** That mahashaya was endowed with every auspicious mark:
all the signs [on him] were as of a chakravarti king.

**44.** Such a mahapurusha — Rasika mahashaya —
rose to destroy the blinding darkness of Utkala.

**45.** All the devotees of Krishna are in an ocean of joy;
knowing of a devotee's birth, the earth is in boundless joy.

**46.** In heaven the gods pour down a rain of flowers:
"He it is who will uphold all dharma."

**47.** Thus all give their blessings —
Vaishnavas, brahmanas, sannyasis and sadhus.

**48.** On all four sides the Vedas resound without pause:
here the *Bharata*, the *Gita*, there the Puranas,

**49.** here the *Ramayana*, there the study of the Vedas;
only they do not know what a treasure sankirtana is.[^104-11]

**50.** So that Utkala would take up the dharma of sankirtana,
Rasikendra-chandra took birth on earth.

**51.** Cries of "Hari!", the sound of conches and many instruments resound;
at the festival of Dipavali there is joy in the whole kingdom.

**52.** The world of the gods and the world of men, joined together,
[rejoice] in joy in Krishna in Achyuta's house in manifold ways.

**53.** At this time Rasika took birth;
everyone raises the hulahuli and cries of victory.[^104-12]

**54.** Come down upon the ground, he cries as all newborns cry;
by the radiance of his body the house shone bright.

**55.** Having given birth, the lady looks at her son's face:
the beautiful moon-like face lights up the darkness.

**56.** Curling locks of hair, a beautiful head;
long cheeks and nose — most charming.

**57.** The pair of brows is like the bow of Kama;
the beauty of the two eyes surpasses lotus petals.

**58.** The two ears, finely shaped, adorn their proper places;[^104-13]
seeing that beauty, everyone is enchanted.

**59.** The two lips look most tender:
their redness surpasses the bimba fruit.

**60.** Shoulders like an elephant's, very handsome; the neck most beautiful;
the cheeks and the roots of the arms captivate the eye.

**61.** The beauty of the long arms is like a lotus stalk;
on the reddish hands like young shoots, the nails [are like] a garland of kunda flowers.

**62.** Seeing his chest, the three worlds are enchanted;
a beautiful belly, a deep and lovely navel.

**63.** Beautiful upon it are the three folds — the beauty of millions of lions;
the knees and shanks — seeing them, the rama-kadali [is envious].[^104-14]

**64.** Seeing the marks on the lotus feet, [all] are amazed;
by the radiance of the moon-like nails darkness is dispelled.

**65.** The dark (shyamala) beautiful body, supremely beautiful —
seeing [it], the lady at once fell into a swoon.

**66.** Rising again, she looked at the moon-like face:
at that sight the misery of the bondage of birth was destroyed.

**67.** Seeing her son's beauty, she thinks within herself:
"Is this a king, a chakravarti, or [one of] the gods?

**68.** Such beauty in an infant I have never seen."
Seeing that beauty, millions upon millions of eyes are enchanted.

**69.** The whole account is told in full to Achyuta;
the townspeople tell [the news] to one another.

**70.** Hearing it, Achyuta cannot contain his joy;
he hurried to see his son.

**71.** Having cut the cord and taken the son in her arms,
the midwife (dhai) brought the son and shows him to Achyuta.

**72.** Seeing his son, Achyuta, most fortunate,
[gives] in charity sesame, rice, cloth, gold and cows.

**73.** He called all the brahmanas who know the Vedas
and gave [to them] as befitted his means.

**74.** Giving the Vaishnavas and brahmanas all that was needed,
he satisfied [them], honouring [them] with humility.

**75.** Satisfied, all give their blessings:
"May your son live long!

**76.** This son of yours is a devotee dear to Krishna;
he has taken birth to deliver Utkala.

**77.** He will preach prema-bhakti for Krishna to all" —
so say to one another all the learned devotees.

**78.** Then, when the Vaishnavas and brahmanas had been satisfied,
the women take the son and perform the customs of the family.

**79.** Seeing the son, everyone was immersed in joy;
again and again they pass him from lap to lap.

**80.** The townspeople say: "Bhavani is fortunate:
by the fruit of austerities this son was born from her womb."

**81.** All the elders of the family say: "The rise of the family
this man will bring about — so it seems to us.

**82.** He it is who will look after us all;
because of him everyone will live happily.

**83.** Achyuta's son is endowed with every auspicious mark;
may Krishna always protect this boy!"

**84.** Thus all give their blessings;
in joy the women raise the hulahuli.

**85.** All joyfully cry, "Jaya, jaya!"
Many days passed in this joy.

**86.** The day of the auspicious rite arrived;
messengers were quickly sent to bring all that was needed.

**87.** A great many brahmanas who know the Vedas came,
all the kinsmen, and women in throngs.

**88.** Young women adorned with splendid clothes and ornaments,
brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras and all the other castes —

**89.** all came to see Achyuta's son;
cries of "Hari!" and the hulahuli sound again and again.

**90.** All the observances prescribed by the rules
the women, gathering together, performed according to family custom.

**91.** Installing Shashthi in the chamber of the sixth day (chhati-ghara),
all worshipped with many kinds of offerings.[^104-15]

**92.** The whole family, bowing, ask for a blessing:
"May my [dear] son of Achyuta live long!"

**93.** Then the lady Bhavani, taking her son on her lap,
having completed all the auspicious rites, at once sat down.

**94.** Taking in their hands turmeric, rice, durva grass and akshata [grains],
the women, blessing him, place [them] on his head.

**95.** One says: "Mahesha, Parvati, grant a boon:
may this boy live eight hundred years!"

**96.** Another says: "By Shashthi's mercy may [this] son live!"
In many ways the throngs of women give their blessings.

**97.** Yet another says: "Protect [him], Krishna Bhagavan!
Markandeya! Grant him long life!"[^104-16]

**98.** As soon as he heard the name of Krishna, on his mother's lap
he, in tears and with his hair standing on end, began to cry.

**99.** At whatever woman utters the name of Krishna
he gazes with eyes full of tears.

**100.** Hearing him cry, his mother gives him the breast,
[but] nothing pleases him [when] he hears the name of Krishna.

**101.** As once Prahlada [while still] in his mother's womb
heard the name of Krishna that came from Narada's lips,[^104-17]

**102.** so [too], when the mother of Rasikendra carried [him] in her womb,
Dayaladasi told the mother about Krishna.[^104-18]

**103.** Dwelling in the womb, Rasikendra heard [it];
[and now] Achyuta's son is overwhelmed with joy in Krishna.

**104.** Come down upon the ground, he is absorbed in contemplation of the Lord (bhagavata-dhyana);
guru, Krishna and the sadhus are Rasika's wealth and life.

**105.** Keep no doubt at all about this in your mind:
an associate of Krishna has taken birth to deliver the living beings.

**106.** Thus the women cried "Jaya!";
[it was time] for all to take leave and go home.

**107.** Then Bhavani, honouring everyone,
put sindura on [their] heads and kajal on [their] eyes.

**108.** To all she gave splendid fragrant garlands,
adorning [their] bodies with kunkuma and sandal.

**109.** Preparing all kinds of dishes cooked in ghee,
she feeds the women with sweets.

**110.** Then she gave everyone camphor and betel;
taking leave, all went each to her own home.

**111.** On the way all talk together about Rasika:
"This boy is by no means [an ordinary] human being."

**112.** Seeing the boy's beauty, all are enchanted:
seeing his lotus face, the moon is put to shame.

**113.** "The sweetness of that beauty cannot be told;
has not an associate of Krishna been born here?"

**114.** Thus conjecturing in many ways, the young women
went home, leaving their hearts with Rasika.

**115.** Hearing of the auspicious rite, all the brahmanas came;
[Achyuta] gave many gifts and fed [them] with sweets.

**116.** He gave camphor and betel, adorning [their] bodies,
and satisfied the twice-born, giving dakshina and the rest.

**117.** The dust of the twice-born's feet was placed on Rasika's head;
in joy the twice-born give their blessings.

**118.** Having taken leave of the twice-born, the mahashaya
brings all the Vaishnavas there [were] in the town.

**119.** Calling "Hari!", they all came in a throng —
with murali, rabab, venu, shinga, beta and vishana.[^104-19]

**120.** Bowing to all, [Achyuta] seats [them] on their seats;
with pleasure he feeds everyone with sweets.

**121.** The devotees of Krishna began to sing the name of Krishna —
there was no way to keep Achyuta's son on anyone's lap.[^104-20]

**122.** He cries as he hears the song of Krishna's qualities;
the midwife, taking [him] in her arms, brought [him] to that place.

**123.** Hearing the name of Krishna, seeing the Vaishnavas feasting,
the [beautiful] moon-faced one, in joy, has his hair standing on end.

**124.** All the devotees, seeing [this], are in an ocean of joy:
"This boy will deliver Utkala."

**125.** Having thus pleased everyone,
the midwife entered the house with the boy.

**126.** All the kinsmen joyfully took their meal;
Achyuta's courtyard became the world of Vaikuntha.

**127.** From that day all people come and go;
the world of the gods and the world of men met in one place.

**128.** From that day his wealth became abundant:
the eight siddhis, the nine treasures (nidhis), [he was] endowed with all virtues.[^104-21]

**129.** Constantly they accompany Rasika:
they all appeared in Achyuta's house.

**130.** Thus day by day [this] became manifest;
seeing [it], all the people exult with joy.

**131.** [This is] the composition in the Purva-vibhaga on the birth;
hear the Rasika-mangala, all good people.

**132.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourth lahari, called "Description of the Pastime of Rasika's Birth".*

[^104-1]: Raga Karuna-shri — as in lahari 1 (note 8) and lahari 2 (note 1). The ghosha is the refrain. There are no mangala-shlokas at the beginning of this lahari: after the heading, raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥.

[^104-2]: Rasika-shekhara ("crown of rasikas") is Rasikananda (cf. lahari 2, note 3). The compound *rasika-śekhara-priya-prāṇa* may also be understood as "[he] whose dear life is Rasika-shekhara."

[^104-3]: "Companions" — *sāṅgopāṅga*, literally "with [all] limbs and minor limbs," i.e. Rasikananda's associates and helpers in his future service.

[^104-4]: "Chamber" — *vāsara* (the bridal chamber). "In joy in Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-sukhe*; a variant noted in the edition, and the 1997 ed., have *krīḍā-sukhe*, "in the joy of play."

[^104-5]: Kartika is the month of October–November. The new moon of the Dipa-yatra (*dīpa-yātrā*) is the new moon of Kartika, the festival of lamps (Dipavali, Dipanvita).

[^104-6]: Deuti and chandrodaya — see lahari 3, note 26. Pati (*paṭī*) — the reading in the 1941 edition is clear; apparently festive cloths or canopies.

[^104-7]: Dandatami (*daṇḍatāmī*) — the reading in the 1941 edition is clear; apparently those who count the dandas (divisions of the day of 24 minutes) with a copper water-bowl (*tāmrī*), so as to fix the exact hour of birth for the horoscope; possibly also "tantrikas."

[^104-8]: Shaka 1512 is 1590 CE. Tula is the solar month corresponding to Kartika. That is, Rasikananda was born in the last night of the dark fortnight of Kartika, the night of Dipavali, as the new moon gave way to the first day of the bright fortnight (pratipad); the description of the date continues in 38.

[^104-9]: The date from 36–37 continues. The bright pratipad is the first day of the bright fortnight of Kartika (the day after Dipavali, on which Govardhana-puja, Annakuta, is celebrated). The third watch (*prahara*) of the night is roughly from midnight to three o'clock (the night from sunset is divided into four praharas).

[^104-10]: 39–42 give the positions of the planets at the birth: the nakshatra (lunar mansion) and the sign (rashi). Tula is Libra, Kanya Virgo, Mithuna Gemini; Karkata is Cancer (Bengali *kāṁkaṛā*, "crab," in the text). The lagna is the ascendant. Ketu's sign is not named (Uttara-ashadha falls in Dhanu and Makara). "Gathered" — *melā*, literally "an assembly."

[^104-11]: The author speaks of his own region — northern Utkala (cf. lahari 3: Mallabhumi, Rohini), where, as he says, the Vedas, the epics and the Puranas were known, but not sankirtana. In Puri the sankirtana of Sri Chaitanya had resounded half a century earlier (CC, Madhya and Antya); according to BR 15, it was Shyamananda and Rasikananda who spread it in Utkala and Medinipur.

[^104-12]: Hulahuli (*hulahulī*, also ulu-dhvani) is the auspicious trilling cry of Bengali and Oriya women at a birth, a wedding or a puja.

[^104-13]: "Finely shaped" — *suśaṅka*; the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the 1997 ed. has *gaṭhita*; apparently "well-formed" (possibly from *śaṅkha*, "conch," a figure for the ear).

[^104-14]: Traditional marks of beauty (cf. the signs of a mahapurusha): shoulders like an elephant's; trivali, the three folds on the belly; "the beauty of lions," a waist slender as a lion's; rama-kadali, a variety of banana whose smooth trunk is a poetic figure for rounded legs.

[^104-15]: "The auspicious rite" (86) is apparently the rite of the sixth day after birth (*chaṭī*, *ṣaṣṭhī*), when the goddess Shashthi, protectress of children and mothers, is worshipped. "Chamber of the sixth day" — *chaṭī ghara*; the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the sense conjectural (apparently the lying-in room where the rite is performed); the 1997 ed. has *chaṭā*.

[^104-16]: Markandeya is the sage famed for his long life (Bhag. 12.8–10). The line may also be understood as "grant him Markandeya's span of life"; the exclamation mark follows the edition.

[^104-17]: Prahlada heard Narada's instructions while in his mother's womb (Bhag. 7.7). "That came from the lips" — *mukha-cyute*; a variant noted in the edition reads *mukhāśrite*, "that dwelt on the lips."

[^104-18]: Dayaladasi (*dayāla-dāsī*) — apparently a name (it could also be understood as "a kind maidservant"). In lahari 5 she is called "Dayaladasi Thakurani," a devotee of Chaitanya living in that region at her own temple; she whispered the holy name into the infant's ear, and later Rasikananda recalls that he heard the name from her in childhood.

[^104-19]: Murali and venu are flutes; the rabab is a stringed instrument; the shinga (*śiṅgā*) is a curved horn; the vishana (*viṣāṇa*) is a horn. "Beta" — *beta-viṣāṇa*, the reading in the 1941 edition is clear; possibly a reed (*vetra*) pipe or a horn with a cane; unclear.

[^104-20]: "The devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana*; read in the 1941 edition (a superscript repha over *ṣṇa*). That is, hearing the kirtana, the infant strains out of everyone's arms.

[^104-21]: The eight siddhis (*aṣṭa-siddhi*) are the mystic perfections of the yogis (anima, laghima, etc.; Bhag. 11.15); the nine nidhis (*nava-nidhi*) are the nine treasures of Kubera, an emblem of inexhaustible wealth. Here they stand for the prosperity that came to the house with Rasika's birth: pure devotees do not seek siddhis (Bhag. 11.14.14). "His" (*tā̃ra*) apparently refers to Achyuta (cf. 129).


## Lahari 5. The Name-Giving

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; the name-giving rite: the astrologers, the horoscope and the name Rasika, and, at Achyuta's request, Murari; Rasika's infant play and ornaments; hearing songs about Krishna the infant weeps, and the household, suspecting the evil eye, calls in exorcists; the blessings of the brahmanas*

*The fifth lahari.*

*Raga Shri — panchali metre.*[^105-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda! Glory to the moon Rasikendra!
Glory, glory [to him whose] glory is fathomless!
Be so merciful to me that your virtues may arise [in me] —
[that I may] compose [a song of] Rasika's fair fame.

**2.** Thus day by day he grew very strong —
the time for the name-giving came.
Bringing brahmana astrologers, Rasika's father and mother
at an auspicious moment give [him] a name.[^105-2]

**3.** All the astrologers, gathering, draw their chalk lines at an auspicious moment,
marking out on the ground the houses [of the horoscope].[^105-3]
Brahmanas versed in the Vedas ceaselessly intone [mantras];
some sing the Sama[-veda].

**4.** Vina, venu, various instruments; the sound of rabab and murali,
mridanga, mandira, karatalas;
dhol, dhak and all the rest — all sound wildly;
all the goyalas (cowherds) dance with delight.[^105-4]

**5.** Thus in various merriments, all in great joy,
they spend days and nights in dancing and singing.
The brahmanas perform homa according to the Vedic rule,
as if having taken counsel [together].[^105-5]

**6.** The women, with cries of victory, all the various family customs —
they performed them all.
Bhavani, having bathed, put on divine garments,
having bowed to the elders.

**7.** Having finished the boy's bath, having performed all the auspicious rites,
she sat down, taking the son on her lap.
Manuscripts of the Gita and the Bhagavatam the brahmanas and sannyasis read there;
there are discourses on the Bharata and the Puranas.

**8.** Placing the son in the middle, all sat on the four sides,
pronouncing Vedic mantras.
Endowed with all auspicious signs, the horoscope is most wondrous:
everyone is amazed.[^105-6]

**9.** Rashi — Vishakha, Tula; the principal name — Sri Rasika:
[this] they quickly wrote in the birth record.
The brahmana astrologers, having calculated, glad at heart,
say: "The horoscope is the most excellent of all."[^105-7]

**10.** The brahmanas versed in the Vedas again and again
all bless Achyuta:
"O, your son is the treasure of life of the world:
he will give prema-bhakti even to the chandalas.

**11.** His signs cannot be told even with a hundred mouths:
fathomless, boundless [is his] glory.
To prema-bhakti, to sankirtana he will lead all people;
its limit cannot be told."

**12.** Thus the brahmanas, having praised that son,
began to leave for their own places.
Achyuta, joining his palms, says: "Listen, O best of the twice-born,
I make one request.

**13.** The principal name is Sri Rasika, as the birth horoscope attests;
it will be known in the world.
[But] in my heart [there is] a wish — fulfil my hope:
let all people call [him] Murari.

**14.** Incomparable in all the shastras is the name Sri Murari Dasa:
let the whole world call [him] so."
The brahmanas, hearing [these] words and accepting this name as true,
went each to his own home.[^105-8]

**15.** The name Rasika-Murari was established:
[such was] the auspicious moment written by the Creator.
Taking the boy on her lap, joyfully within the house
[the mother] converses with everyone.

**16.** Everyone, according to the rules and in due order, he honoured with worship and obeisances,
and according to his means [rewarded and] took leave of them.
Seeing his son's face, he knows no sorrow at all:
the Mahashaya floats in joy.

**17.** Thus after some days, heaving himself on knees and chest,
he plays on the bed.
Day by day he moves about the house on his knees:
Rasika-shekhara crawls on all fours.

**18.** Wherever he finds some object, he breaks it and throws it right there;
he mixes curd, milk and ghee in one place.
Breaking the pots, to his heart's content he eats some and smears himself with some;
neither snake nor fire does he fear in the least.

**19.** Thorns, stones and the like — he regards them all alike;
enemy and friend he does not distinguish.
Night and day, at play, he roams the house and courtyard;
of good and bad he knows nothing.

**20.** Dust and mud he gleefully smears over his body —
[on him] they shine like aguru and sandal.
How sweet that smile! His lovely face defeats the moon;
those two eyes are very long.

**21.** At his waist a belt of little bells is fitting, on his neck fine pearls shine,
on his hands golden bracelets glitter;
on both arms two armlets, made of gold;
on his chest an ornament — a tiger's claw.[^105-9]

**22.** On his feet, jewelled anklets: their beauty cannot be told;
you look — as if [you saw] the form of Gopala.
On his head a lovely garland; with it he looks so tender:
that majesty cannot be told.

**23.** Thus crawling, now rising, now falling,
he constantly roams the courtyard.
Father and mother, seeing his face, cannot contain the joy in their chests;
shaking off the dust, they take him in their arms and carry him away.

**24.** Washing his body with scented water,
the mother gives him milk to drink.
Joyfully she sits on the swing, taking her son on her lap,
thinking [it is time] for sleep.

**25.** The fair fame and deeds of Krishna that fortunate [mother] sings,
saying: "So that [my] child may fall asleep."
Hearing Krishna's name, Rasika cannot contain himself:
he started up, crying aloud.

**26.** Sweat, trembling, a faltering voice, the hairs on all his limbs standing on end;
from his eyes streams of tears flow.
Sobbing, he weeps in the bliss of prema [at the song] of Krishna's fame:
where has his sleep gone![^105-10]

**27.** Hearing her son cry, the grieved mother
gives him the breast again and again.
More and more she sings, so that her son may sleep —
hearing the song, [he] weeps twice as hard.

**28.** Whatever means she tries to break that weeping —
plaintively [she sings] Krishna's name.[^105-11]
The fortunate [mother] summoned a few young women
and told them all: "Sing!"

**29.** A few women, gathering, sing with zest —
lovely and charming to hear.[^105-12]
Lamenting loudly, Rasika-Murari weeps:
his whole body is drenched through with streams [of tears].

**30.** [He is full of] longing under the weight of prema; when love for Krishna overflows,
he constantly floats in that rasa of prema.
As soon as he hears Krishna's name, [his] body is all full of prema for Krishna;
hearing Krishna's qualities, [he] exults.

**31.** All take [him] from his mother's lap, each in his own way,
yet Achyuta's son still weeps.
All say, guessing: "We know what this is:
some wicked person has cast the evil eye on him at some time."

**32.** Someone ties a protective charm on his head; with various mantras, in various ways,
all the ojhas (exorcists) began to sweep [the evil] off him.[^105-13]
Hearing the weeping, the mother — the poor soul's heart breaks with anxiety —
vows various pujas to the gods.

**33.** All those who are singing — [they sing] streams of Sri Krishna's fair fame:
by whose word, then, will the weeping stop?
In prema at moments he becomes stunned (stambha), meditating on Krishna's qualities;
with humility and shyness he looks at everyone.

**34.** Then, after a while, the tired women fell silent —
and then Prabhu stops weeping.
[Showing] his own childlike nature, restraining all [the feelings of] bhava,
he sucks the breast on his mother's lap.

**35.** The mother, joyful, thinking her son calmed,
treats the brahmanas to sweets.
The host of the twice-born blesses: "May the son remain free from obstacles:
this boy is under Krishna's shelter."

**36.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends, people of Krishna —
the account of Rasika's childhood.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^105-14]

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifth lahari, called "The Name-Giving".*

[^105-1]: Raga Shri (*śrī*) is one of the six principal ragas. "Panchali metre" (*pāñcālī-chanda*) here is the tripadi: each line has three parts (two short rhyming ones and a long one); the edition sets each stanza in four lines, and so it is translated. No ghosha (refrain) is given. The stanzas are numbered as in the edition (1–36).

[^105-2]: The name-giving (*nāma-karaṇa*) is one of the purificatory rites (samskaras) of childhood. Astrologers — *daivajña*; the 1941 edition has the misprint "দোইবজ্ঞ" (below, in 9, "দৈবজ্ঞ").

[^105-3]: "Astrologers" — *khaṛikāra*, lit. "those who work with chalk": the horoscope was calculated by drawing the squares of the "houses" in chalk (*khaṛi*) on the ground or on a board. For the line "marking out on the ground the houses" the edition gives in a footnote the variant "installing the auspicious pot" (*śubha ghaṭa kariyā sthāpana*).

[^105-4]: The vina is a stringed instrument; venu, rabab, murali — see lahari 4, note 19; the mandira are small cymbals; the dhol and dhak are large drums. Goyalas (*goyāla*) are cowherds, milkmen; the rejoicing recalls Nanda's festival at Krishna's birth (Bhag. 10.5).

[^105-5]: "As if having taken counsel [together]" — *kāro yena kariyā yukati*; the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the sense conjectural (lit. "as if having consulted someone").

[^105-6]: "Horoscope" — *koṭī*; so in the 1941 edition (and in the 1997 ed.), understood as *koṣṭhī*, "horoscope" (cf. 9, 13); "millions [of signs]" is also possible.

[^105-7]: The rashi is the sign of the Moon at birth: the Moon in Vishakha, in Tula (Libra), as in lahari 4, 39. "Principal name" (*mūla nāma*) — the name according to the birth sign; in one system names for the sign Tula begin with the syllable "ra" — hence "Rasika." Birth record — *jāta-patra*.

[^105-8]: Murari ("the enemy of [the demon] Mura") is a name of Krishna; "Murari Dasa" means "servant of Murari." Hence the double name Rasika-Murari, by which Rasikananda is also known in BR 15. In 15 the 1941 edition has the misprint "মুবারি" for "মুরারি".

[^105-9]: A tiger's claw (*vyāghra-nakha*) set in gold is a traditional amulet for children; in Vaishnava poetry the infant Krishna wears one too. "Belt of little bells" — *kiṅkiṇī*; "armlets" — *tāṛ*.

[^105-10]: "Sobbing" — *usaśī usaśī*; the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the word is not found in dictionaries and is understood from the context (an onomatopoeia for sobbing).

[^105-11]: The line is understood tentatively: *karuṇā kariyā kṛṣṇa-nāma*, lit. "having made Krishna's name plaintively," i.e. the mother, trying to stop the crying, herself sings Krishna's name, which only makes the crying worse (cf. 27). "Entreating [by] Krishna" is also possible.

[^105-12]: "Lovely" — *suśaṅka*, as in lahari 4, 58 (note 13 there); the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the sense from the context.

[^105-13]: The evil eye (lit. "a wicked person saw") is the folk explanation of an infant's crying. Protective charm — *rakṣā*, a protective thread or amulet. An ojha (*ojhā*) is a village exorcist-healer; "sweep off" — *jhāṛite*: to drive out the evil with mantras, brushing the patient with a twig or the edge of a cloth. The author shows that the household does not understand the ecstatic symptoms of prema in the infant.

[^105-14]: The author's signature is given by the common formula; here it is in the tripadi metre and reads slightly differently: "Making the holy feet of Shyamananda an ornament on his head, the son of Rasamaya sings."


## Lahari 6. Description of the Childhood Pastimes

*A verse in glory of Prabhu Murari and a song in glory of Shyamananda; the infant Rasika crawls about the courtyard and carries out everyone's requests; the rite of the first feeding with rice — among the objects laid out he chooses the Bhagavatam; games and kirtana with the children, ecstasy at the name of Krishna; honouring Tulasi, the ashvattha, the Vaishnavas and the brahmanas, cleaning the holy places; the townspeople's love for Achyuta's son*

*The sixth lahari.*

**S1.** *When the elephant of Kali has grown furious on the earth — him who makes known the meaning of the Vedas,*
*who is devoted to attentive meditation on the pair of lotus feet of Sri Vishnu,*
*who by the study of the shastras and reflection [on them] has become the rising of the root of bliss for the worlds —*
*O fools, worship him on earth, the glorious Prabhu Murari!*[^106-1]

*Raga Suhi.*[^106-2]
*Ghosha: "What shall I say of the beauty of Gopala's moon-like face?*
*It captivates the hearts of all the women of Vraja."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the abode of all virtues!
Glory, glory [to him who is] the dear life of Rasikachandra!

**2.** Glory, glory to all the associates with their followers,
by hearing of whom one quickly attains Krishna!

**3.** Thus day by day Achyuta's son
crawls on all fours about the courtyard.

**4.** Now he rises, now he falls, now he rolls;
everyone lifts [him] up, crying: "Ah, ah!"

**5.** He constantly roams the courtyard at play;
all the things lying on the ground he handles as he goes.

**6.** "Bring the shoes, child, the wooden sandals!" says someone;
"The jug, the cup, the broom!" say others.[^106-3]

**7.** Joyfully toddling, Prabhu brings [the thing] and puts it on someone's lap;
no one's words does he disregard.

**8.** Prabhu carries out everyone's words:
rising and falling, he does [it] — he never disobeys.

**9.** Seeing [this], all the people are in an ocean of joy;
again and again they pass him from arms to arms.

**10.** Thus the time of the annaprashana came;
the townspeople informed Achyuta [of it].[^106-4]

**11.** Hearing this, he respectfully sends out messengers:
"From [all the] lands bring all kinds of provisions quickly!"

**12.** Summoning learned brahmanas who knew the Vedas,
he has the Vedas and [sacred] learning recited on all sides.

**13.** Inviting them, he called together his kinsfolk,
throngs upon throngs of women, and his dear ones and friends.

**14.** Respectfully greeting everyone, Achyuta says:
"Give your permission: [my] son will undergo the annaprashana."

**15.** Hearing this, all the panditas say: "Good, good!
Arrange the homa, the auspicious rites and the rest, set up the ghata — everything [as is fitting]."[^106-5]

**16.** They adorned the house with colourful cloths;
chamaras and pendants hang down — most beautiful.

**17.** Grinding rice into powder, all the young women
decorated the place of the meal in many different ways.[^106-6]

**18.** In its midst they placed in due order
grain, cow dung and the like, a conch, silver and gold,

**19.** a stylus, palm leaves, paper, a reed pen —
and they placed the book of the Srimad-Bhagavatam.[^106-7]

**20.** Having completed all the auspicious rites, they adorned
Rasika-shekhara's whole body with ornaments.

**21.** Dusted with sandal, kunkuma and musk,
his beautiful face is enchanting, surpassing the autumn moon.

**22.** On his lovely forehead shines a fine [line] of gorochana;[^106-8]
seeing that beauty, everyone is enchanted.

**23.** Thus, taking the boy on her lap, the mother
[and] Rasika's father joyfully went and sat down.

**24.** All the kinsfolk and brahmanas sit on all sides;
the brahmanas on their part began the Vedic mantras and the homa.[^106-9]

**25.** Music and the roar of the dundubhi sound without pause;
the women cry "Jaya, jaya!" and raise the hulahuli.

**26.** Adorning the middle of that room,
they set out kshira, pithas and pakkanna.

**27.** Seating Rasika on a pindi,
the young women say to him again and again:[^106-10]

**28.** "Listen, listen, child, Rasika-shekhara:
whatever pleases you, bring that first, quickly!"

**29.** Hearing everyone's words, he looked around;
seeing the Srimad-Bhagavatam, [his] eyes [filled] with tears.

**30.** Drawing the book with both hands, he brings it
and clasps it firmly to his heart.

**31.** Holding the Bhagavatam to his breast, he began to weep:
sweat, trembling, tears and hair standing on end appeared.

**32.** Absorbed in Krishna, in the rasa of prema, he weeps;
all the men and women see a wonder.

**33.** Some say: "This boy is no human being:
surely a dear devotee of Sri Krishna has been born."

**34.** Some say: "He will deliver all living beings."
Others say: "[He has] descended (avatara) to uphold dharma."[^106-11]

**35.** Some say: "Achyuta is supremely fortunate."
Each praises [him] as it comes to his mind.

**36.** Thus having respectfully performed the annaprashana,
[Achyuta] promptly bade the brahmanas farewell.

**37.** Then that same day, gathering all the kinsfolk,
he feeds [them] with all kinds of [dishes] of the six tastes.[^106-12]

**38.** The young women, with great respect,
the lady herself, sitting [with them], feeds.

**39.** Having fed them, she gave [them] camphor and betel,
[put] sandal and kunkuma on their bodies and sindur on their heads.

**40.** All the women, taking the son on their laps
and praising Bhavani, took their leave and went.

**41.** Thus after some days the son of Achyuta
incessantly roams about the whole village.

**42.** With ten or twenty children of the same age
he incessantly plays many games in many ways.

**43.** One day all the children, clapping their hands,
hold sankirtana, and he moves in their midst, dancing.

**44.** [Seeing] the children's play, the townspeople —
[all] among them who were devotees of Krishna —

**45.** seeing the children's kirtana, [were] in an ocean of joy:
"Such understanding in a child we have never seen!"

**46.** Together with the children all sing Krishna's name;
saying, "Dance, child!", all clap their hands.

**47.** As soon as he heard Krishna's name, he lost consciousness:
his voice choked, tears on his beautiful moonlike face.

**48.** With the hair standing on end all over his body, he fell to the ground;
rolling [on the ground], he began to weep loudly.

**49.** Hearing [this], all the people came there;
with still greater joy they sing of Krishna's qualities.

**50.** Some cry "Hari!" again and again;
hearing [it], the son of Achyuta dances with joy.

**51.** From whosesoever mouth he hears Krishna's name,
with the dust of that person's feet he adorns [his] body.

**52.** Seeing the child's deeds, people are amazed;
all say: "This boy is no human being."

**53.** The boy's feelings cannot be described at all:
hearing Krishna's name, [he displays] the eight sattvika [bhavas].[^106-13]

**54.** Saying this, all lift [him] to their breasts;
snatching [him] from one another, they take [him] again and again.

**55.** All the men and women say to Achyuta:
"What can be told of your son is beyond telling.

**56.** What understanding has an infant [to know] whom they call Krishna?
[Yet] as soon as he hears [of] Krishna, tears [flow] and his hair stands on end.

**57.** Whoever utters 'Krishna, Krishna' —
with the dust of that person's feet he adorns himself.

**58.** [He] who wept on hearing Krishna's name —
this boy is no human being, we tell [you] plainly."

**59.** Hearing everyone's words, Achyuta says:
"May [my] son live, receiving the dust of the feet of you all!"

**60.** For his son's sake he humbly entreats everyone:
"All of you, bless this boy!"

**61.** Taking the boy in his arms, he came home.
In this way every day [Rasika] wanders about the village.

**62.** With him are ten or twenty boys of the same age,
and five or seven devotees of Krishna stay around [him].

**63.** From childhood he keeps all dharma:
[he honours] the ashvattha, Tulasi, the dhatri, Vaishnavas and brahmanas.[^106-14]

**64.** Day by day his understanding is ever more kindled;
apart from establishing dharma he knows nothing [else].

**65.** Not for a moment does he stay quietly at home:
in the joy of Krishna he wanders from village to village.

**66.** All know [him] as the son of the ruler of the land;[^106-15]
moreover, that enchanting form enchants everyone's heart.

**67.** Affectionately, vying with one another,
all carry Achyuta's son off to their own homes.

**68.** Seeing [his] moonlike face, they feel as if they had found millions of jewels;
clasping [him] to their breasts, they carry [him] off — great happiness in their hearts.

**69.** Bringing him home, setting out an excellent seat,
they seat the son of Achyuta on it.

**70.** Laddus, sandesh, cream from milk, fine sugar,
many offerings — ripe [fruits], water [sweet as] nectar —[^106-16]

**71.** all bring and give to Rasika;
seeing those offerings, he is glad at heart.

**72.** He takes all those things to Tulasi
and, in his own play, offers [them] to Krishna.

**73.** Circling Tulasi, he dances and claps his hands;
with the children — sankirtana, with many merry games.

**74.** Incessantly he passes his time in this joy;
seeing [it], the townspeople marvel.

**75.** After a moment, taking all those things himself,
he goes and gives the first portion to the brahmanas and Vaishnavas.

**76.** All respectfully accept [it], holding out their hands;
regarding [it] as prasada, they praise the boy:

**77.** "This boy's character cannot be described;
it seems [this] son will establish dharma."

**78.** Then he gives the offerings to all the children,
and afterwards takes a little [of it] himself.

**79.** In this way he wanders about the village day and night;
the joy of all the people cannot be contained.

**80.** Wherever [there is] a place of Krishna, wherever a sadhu dwells —
joyfully visiting them all, [he] wanders day and night.

**81.** A temple of Krishna or a devotee's dwelling,
the ashvattha, Tulasi, the dhatri, [the abodes of] brahmanas, holy places —

**82.** if he sees that these places are unclean,
he goes there with the children.

**83.** Quickly bringing clay, cow dung and water,
he cleanses the place thoroughly.

**84.** With his own hands he smears all those places:
in a moment they shine like Vaikuntha.[^106-17]

**85.** In this way, on the roads, at the ghats, in village after village,
he goes about constantly, cleansing the holy places.

**86.** Thus in his childhood the son of Achyuta
leads all people to keep dharma.

**87.** Seeing this deed of the child, [people] are in an ocean of shame;
from the very next day all [themselves] keep things clean.

**88.** Bringing soft grass with his own hands,
he serves the cows, giving [them] grass and water.

**89.** If on the road he sees a Vaishnava [or] a brahmana,
with the greatest respect he bows to [his] feet.

**90.** Joining his palms, with humility,
he greets everyone, smiling slightly.

**91.** How sweet [his] smile, [how] light [his] words!
In joy all the people take [him] in their arms.

**92.** All say: "Ah, little one, [may] your misfortunes [fall on us]![^106-18]
Where did you learn all these ways?

**93.** How did you learn thus to keep dharma —
to bow to Vaishnavas, sannyasis and brahmanas,

**94.** to clean the places of the gods and the Tulasi platforms?[^106-19]
Where, child, did you learn all these deeds?"

**95.** Thus in many ways the townspeople,
questioning [him], take [him] in their arms again and again.

**96.** Hundreds upon hundreds of kisses they give [him] on the face;
no one has a mind to set [him] down on the ground.

**97.** In their arms they carry [him] to Achyuta's house,
all snatching [him] from one another again and again.

**98.** All joyfully say to Achyuta:
"This son of yours is surely no human being.

**99.** Seeing his signs, [we] are amazed:
as soon as he hears Krishna's name, [tears] pour in a hundred streams."

**100.** Hearing Krishna's name, with eyes full of tears,
he came [and found himself] on Achyuta's lap.

**101.** Taking Rasika-shekhara on his lap and brushing off the dust,
[Achyuta] promptly has [him] bathed, fed and so on.

**102.** Thus day by day, growing older,
the son of Achyuta performs various pastimes.

**103.** The Rasika-mangala is very sweet to hear:
joyfully hearing [this] fair glory, cross over [the age of] Kali.

**104.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the sixth lahari, called "Description of the Childhood Pastimes," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^106-1]: The verse is unnumbered in the edition (after it come the raga, the ghosha and the song beginning with ॥১॥); it is marked S1, like the mangala-shlokas of lahari 1 (lahari 1, note 1). "The elephant of Kali" — *kali-vāraṇa*; *vāraṇa* means both "elephant" and "warding off, restraining," so "[who appeared] on earth to restrain the blazing [age of] Kali" is also possible. Prabhu Murari is Rasikananda (Rasika-Murari, lahari 5, 13–15). The source of the verse is not identified — apparently the author's own composition.

[^106-2]: Raga Suhi (*suhī*, also Suhai) — a raga frequently found in Vaishnava padas; cf. BR 15 ("raga Suhai").

[^106-3]: "Shoes" — *pāṇḍoi*, "wooden sandals" — *kaṭhāu*: the meanings follow the edition's glosses (*jutā*, "footwear"; *khaṛama*, "wooden sandals"). That is, the household playfully gives the infant errands.

[^106-4]: Annaprashana (*anna-prāśana*, "eating of rice") — the samskara of a child's first feeding with rice (usually in the sixth to eighth month of life).

[^106-5]: Homa — a fire sacrifice. Ghata (*ghaṭa*) — a water-pot (mangala-ghata) set up at the beginning of a rite as an auspicious seat of the deities.

[^106-6]: That is, they drew auspicious designs (alpana) in rice paste on the spot where the child would be fed.

[^106-7]: 18–19 and 27–30 describe a custom of the annaprashana: grain, earth or cow dung, a conch, silver and gold, writing materials and a book are laid out before the child; what he takes first is considered a sign of his future (wealth, learning, piety). A stylus (*lekhanī*) is for writing on palm leaves; a *kalam* is a reed pen.

[^106-8]: Gorochana — a bright yellow pigment used for auspicious marks on the forehead.

[^106-9]: "On their part" — *dvija-bhāge*; the reading in the 1941 edition is clear; it may also be understood as "in the part [of the assembly] where the brahmanas [sat]."

[^106-10]: Kshira — thickened milk; pitha — rice cakes; pakkanna — dishes fried in ghee. Pindi (*piṁṛā*) — a low wooden seat.

[^106-11]: So the townspeople say. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding Rasikananda is not an avatara of the Lord but an eternal associate and dear devotee (cf. 33 and lahari 4, 105: "an associate of Krishna has been born for the deliverance of living beings"); *avatāra* here is in the broad sense of "one who has descended [into the world]."

[^106-12]: The couplet number is defectively printed in the 1941 edition (it looks like "৩০"); by sequence it is 37. "The six tastes" — see lahari 3, note 13.

[^106-13]: The eight sattvika bhavas (*aṣṭa-sāttvika*) — involuntary bodily manifestations of love for Krishna: stupefaction, perspiration, hair standing on end, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of complexion, tears and fainting (*Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu* 2.3). Cf. 31, 47–48.

[^106-14]: Ashvattha — the sacred fig (pipal); dhatri — the amalaki (emblic myrobalan). Together with Tulasi they are honoured by watering, circumambulation and obeisances.

[^106-15]: "The son of the ruler of the land" — *rājya-adhipati-suta*; cf. lahari 4, 2: Achyuta "lives in royal splendour."

[^106-16]: Laddus and sandesh are sweets; "cream" — *sara*, the skin of boiled milk. "Ripe [fruits], water [sweet as] nectar" — *supakka amṛta pāni*; it may also be understood as "well-cooked [food], nectarean water."

[^106-17]: Smearing the floor and courtyard with a mixture of clay, cow dung and water is the traditional way of purifying a place.

[^106-18]: "[May] your misfortunes [fall on us]" — *nichāni tomāra*: an affectionate exclamation; *nichāni* is the custom of "warding off" misfortune from a loved one by taking it upon oneself.

[^106-19]: "The Tulasi platforms" — *tulasī cauṛā*; corrected in the edition's list of errata to *caurā*: a raised platform for the Tulasi plant (cf. lahari 3, note 17: tulasi-mancha).


## Lahari 7. Description of the Childhood Pastimes

*The ear-piercing ceremony: Rasika faints on hearing the musicians sing of Krishna; Dayaladasi Thakurani comes to see the child, foretells his service in Utkala and gives him the name of Hari in his ear; the boy chants a hundred thousand names daily; with the children he enacts Krishna's pastimes after the Bhagavata*

*The seventh lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^107-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the lord of Rasika's life!
Be merciful, so that I may sing your glory and renown.[^107-2]

**2.** Day by day the joyful Rasika-shekhara
wanders from house to house, playing as he pleases.

**3.** At that time the hour for the karnavedha came;
the townspeople informed Achyuta [of it].[^107-3]

**4.** Having calculated an auspicious day and an auspicious moment,
[Achyuta] set up the mangala-ghata in the middle.

**5.** The brahmanas, rejoicing, perform the homa;
quickly they summoned that excellent barber.

**6.** Having bathed the son and dressed [him] handsomely,
they seated [him] on a seat, placing a laddu in [his] hand.

**7.** Music and the thunder of the dundubhi sound without pause;
two muhuriyas sing of Krishna's virtues.[^107-4]

**8.** ("Listen, friend, to what lies deep in my heart:
Shyama-nagara comes to my mind day and night.")[^107-5]

**9.** This pada the two [play] on the shanai;
hearing [it], Achyuta's son became motionless.[^107-6]

**10.** The eight sattvika-[bhavas] arose in his body:
the hairs stood on end all over his body, streams of tears flow from his eyes.

**11.** Sitting on the pindi, he lost consciousness;
hearing the shanai, Prabhu fell to the ground.[^107-7]

**12.** By degrees his mind [came] into a state of madness with Krishna-prema;
not understanding [the cause], [people] say, "What did he see, and when?"[^107-8]

**13.** Sobbing and sobbing, he weeps in distress,
saying, "When will I attain Krishna, the Lord of my life?"

**14.** He does not open his eyes, the weeping does not cease;
seeing [this], all the townspeople were frightened.

**15.** Running, everyone came there;
the relatives tend [him] in various ways.

**16.** In great fear the brahmanas do not perform the homa;
the musicians do not play at all.

**17.** [The players of] the shanai fell silent, seeing the boy;
everyone, stunned, comes and looks.

**18.** As soon as he no longer heard the sound of the shanai,
Achyuta's son sat up in his ordinary state.

**19.** Everyone raised cries of "Hari!" and "Jaya!";
joyfully the barber sits down to pierce the ears.

**20.** With care he pierced the beautiful, shapely ears;[^107-9]
[and the boy,] saying "Krishna," eats the laddu again and again.

**21.** The homa, the yajna and the auspicious rites were performed in due order;
the brahmanas utter the sound of the Vedas.

**22.** At that time Dayaladasi Thakurani —
all praise [her] as a devoted servant of Chaitanya —[^107-10]

**23.** having set up a temple, lives in this land;
Achyuta serves [her] at all times.

**24.** At that time, hearing of Rasika's appearance,
the mother came joyfully to see [him].[^107-11]

**25.** Having quickly blessed Achyuta,
she went into the chambers and saw the son.

**26.** Seeing Rasika's beauty, she became unconscious;
all the women, sprinkling water on her face, lift [her] up.

**27.** Everyone says, "To begin with she is old, and on top of that she came in the heat of the sun —
that is why she fainted and fell to the ground."

**28.** People make fun [of her] one to another;
rising, that mother tells the reason for her fainting:

**29.** "You do not know the glory of this child:
I saw as it were the form of Gopala.[^107-12]

**30.** Seeing [his] enchanting beauty, I lost consciousness.
This son is not [merely] a child: he is the life of the world.

**31.** He will deliver all living beings;
he will preach prema-bhakti in Utkala.

**32.** He will uphold all dharma:
service to the ashvattha, Tulasi, Vaishnavas [and] brahmanas.

**33.** He will show mercy to the poor and lowly;
by his signs [one sees that he is] the protector of the surrendered.

**34.** His glory cannot be told at all:
this great soul is Krishna's own associate.

**35.** Achyuta's son is endowed with every auspicious sign;
no one will transgress his word.

**36.** Seeing [his] dark, beautiful, enchanting body,
I know for certain: he is a servant of Krishna.

**37.** This great soul will be a knower of all the shastras;
this son will be deeply steadfast in all dharma.

**38.** He will preach the sixty-four limbs of bhakti;
he has descended (avatara) to deliver all beings.[^107-13]

**39.** I do not know how to tell of his endless virtues.
By great merit Bhavani obtained this son."

**40.** That mother is the eldest of the clan, the mother of the world:
she herself knows past, future and present.[^107-14]

**41.** In detail she told everything to Achyuta:
"This son is the moon that lights up the family."

**42.** Hearing all those words, humbly
Achyuta, bowing down, speaks to her:

**43.** "Bless [him], mother, that the son may live!
Birth after birth this boy is the servant of you all."

**44.** Hearing [this], the mother joyfully gives her blessing:
"Krishna, protect, Krishna, protect this boy!"

**45.** Hearing Krishna's name, he became joyful;
clasping that mother by the neck, he began to weep.

**46.** Joyfully taking the son on her lap, Dayaladasi
mercifully let [him] hear the name in his ear.[^107-15]

**47.** She gave the name "Hare Krishna" in Achyuta's presence
and openly told all about it:

**48.** "The true meaning of the mantra that I spoke into the boy's ear
a certain person will tell [him].

**49.** That great soul is his own lord of life;
the two will deliver living beings — this I say for certain.[^107-16]

**50.** Together they will deliver Utkala,
preaching prema-bhakti by Chaitanya's order.

**51.** They will distribute the wealth of Krishna-prema from house to house;
they will deliver all beings, [even] the chandalas.

**52.** Do not neglect him, thinking him a child:
this great soul is a dear devotee of Sri Krishna."

**53.** Having told everything in detail, she asked leave to go;
Achyuta [and] Bhavani gave [her] many gifts.

**54.** All took the dust of her feet on their heads;
following [her] some distance, they bade [her] farewell.

**55.** Thus, taking Rasika-shekhara in their arms,
the two came home, joyful at heart.

**56.** Day by day — a most wondrous account! —
Achyuta's son performs pastimes of Krishna-prema.

**57.** Whatever human childhood games there are —
those he does not touch: [all he] does is full of Krishna's pastimes.

**58.** Some days, spreading an asana, he sits in meditation
and remembers the Hare Krishna maha-mantra.

**59.** For two or three praharas he meditates on Krishna:[^107-17]
the hairs stand on end all over his body, tears flow unceasingly.

**60.** Seeing [this], his mother says, "Listen, my darling:
milk, laddu, cream, sugar — wish for something!"

**61.** [But] Prabhu does not hear anyone's words
until the count of a hundred thousand names is complete.[^107-18]

**62.** From that day he chants a hundred thousand names;
on his neck is a Tulasi necklace, beautiful beyond compare.

**63.** Seeing [this], all the people say to Achyuta:
"Surely Krishna's mercy has come upon this son.

**64.** In such a little one such understanding has appeared:
he has begun to chant Krishna's name unceasingly!"

**65.** He cares nothing for eating, resting or sleep;
[his] body, overwhelmed with Krishna-prema, shines.

**66.** Thus all the people praise the son;
day by day he enacts all the pastimes of Krishna there are.

**67.** Taking along children of the same age,
he plays those games in which there is talk of Krishna.

**68.** With his own hands he dresses the children;
he himself costumes [them] according to the pastime.[^107-19]

**69.** Some become the Earth in the form of a cow,
someone becomes Brahma — they go and lay [their plight] before him.[^107-20]

**70.** Someone becomes Narayana in the Ocean of Milk;
some [become] the demigods and with Brahma [offer] their plea.

**71.** Someone [becomes] Vasudeva, someone Devaki,
someone Kamsa, someone keeps [them] in prison.

**72.** Some are Nanda [and] Yashoda, others gopis [and] cowherds,
some become the cows, some the little ones.[^107-21]

**73.** Someone becomes Nanda's son, someone Putana:
he sucks her breast, tormenting her.

**74.** Someone becomes the cart and the rest, someone Trinavarta;
day by day he does [the pastimes] thus in various ways.

**75.** As [he] dresses the children, such is their appearance;
seeing the children's costumes, [he] sheds streams of tears.

**76.** Day by day they all play this pastime as a game;
seeing [it], Achyuta's child is immersed in bliss.[^107-22]

**77.** Apart from the Bhagavata he knows nothing else;
lying on the ground, he meditates on the Bhagavata.

**78.** In childhood he knows no other game:
he constantly plays the games of Krishna and Balarama.

**79.** All the boys take on those forms;
Rasika plays this game day and night.

**80.** Seeing [this], all the people are amazed:
"This son of Achyuta is not human."

**81.** Not with a child's understanding does he [enact] Krishna's pastimes:
he plays all the games in the order of the Bhagavata.

**82.** One day they stage the name-giving:
one is Garga, another Nanda, others the cowherd men.

**83.** One day some boy eats earth;
[his] mouth is opened, and someone sees within it the whole play.[^107-23]

**84.** One day, tying [someone] to a mortar,
[he] drags [it] between [the trees] and breaks the yamala-arjunas.

**85.** One day some child was finely dressed,[^107-24]
[and] someone kills the demon Vatsasura.

**86.** One day, making some child Bakasura,
[someone] slays [him] in fun; Rasika-Murari watches.

**87.** One day, dressing [someone] as Aghasura,
someone kills [him] in play; [Rasika] himself watches.

**88.** One day some [become] calves, [others] boys,
and someone, becoming Brahma, steals [them] and carries [them] off.

**89.** Someone becomes Krishna [and] creates calves and boys;
[someone], becoming Brahma, offers prayers in many ways.

**90.** One day [someone] takes the form of Dhenukasura;
having killed him, the child goes about dancing.

**91.** One day [they enact] with delight the subduing of Kaliya;
someone, [as] the wives of the naga, offers prayers together with the children.

**92.** One day [someone] puts out the forest fire;
someone kills the demon Pralamba.

**93.** One day they again put out the forest fire;
one day all together describe nature.[^107-25]

**94.** One day the child describes autumn;
one day he tells the glory of the Venu-gita.

**95.** One day, setting up Katyayani,
all the children together steal the clothes.

**96.** One day someone dresses as the wives of the sacrificing brahmanas;
all together they ask for food and accept [it].

**97.** One day they put a stop to the worship of Indra;
one day in play they lift Govardhana.[^107-26]

**98.** One day Indra, taking Surabhi with him,
offers prayers in many words, calling [Krishna] "Govinda."

**99.** On the day the child played the Holder of Govardhana,
Rasika-Murari, seeing [it], fainted.

**100.** His whole body overwhelmed, he rolls on the ground;
every day, seeing [these] pastimes, he weeps aloud.

**101.** Seeing the boy's understanding, the pandits praise [him]:
"This great soul is a dear devotee of Sri Krishna.

**102.** We [ourselves] know nothing of the truth of the Bhagavata,
[yet he], a child, plays [it] in exactly that form!"

**103.** Thus every day [people] praise the child;
thus the child, dressing [the children], plays constantly.[^107-27]

**104.** Day and night he knows nothing but the Bhagavata;
taking up childhood games, he spends nights and days.

**105.** One day someone, [as] Nanda, observes Ekadashi;
[another], becoming Varuna, seizes [him] and takes [him] away.[^107-28]

**106.** Someone, becoming Krishna, rescues him and brings him back.
One day, forming a circle at the place of the rasa —

**107.** some as gopis, some as Krishna: dressing up the children,
giving [them] exactly that appearance, taking all along —

**108.** someone at the foot of the wish-fulfilling tree imitates the sound of the flute with his singing;
hearing that sound, all the gopis set out.[^107-29]

**109.** Meeting Krishna, they sport, [dancing] the rasa;
someone disappears — [and he] is searched for again and again.

**110.** Seeing that Krishna has disappeared, Murari [enters such a state] —
those eight sattvika bhavas I am unable to describe.

**111.** Again the child-gopis, having found Krishna,
joyfully dance the rasa in Vrindavana.

**112.** One day someone delivers Sudarshana;
one day they sing the "Gopi-gita."[^107-30]

**113.** One day someone becomes the demon Arishta,
someone slays him — in great joy.[^107-31]

**114.** One day someone takes the form of Keshi,
and another child makes an end of him.

**115.** One day some boy becomes Akrura
and at Kamsa's command goes to fetch Krishna.

**116.** Some, becoming Akrura, offer prayers;
together with Krishna [they] enter Mathura.

**117.** One day a child, in fun, becomes the washerman;
slaying him, [Krishna] hands out the garments on all sides.

**118.** Someone becomes the garland-maker, [calling himself] Sudama;
dressing all the children, he puts flower garlands on their necks.

**119.** Someone becomes Kubja with a box of scents;
some child, taking her scents, makes her well.

**120.** Some child, taking up the bow, breaks [it];
some child slays the elephant Kuvalaya.

**121.** On some days [they] slay Chanura and Mushtika;
one day the children slay Kamsa.

**122.** Thus day and night, without pause, plays
Rasika-shekhara — the Sri Bhagavata embodied.[^107-32]

**123.** Listen, listen to the Rasika-mangala, all people:
Rasika's plays [follow] the order of the Bhagavata.

**124.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the seventh lahari, called "Description of the Childhood Pastimes," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^107-1]: Raga Narayani-gauda (*nārāyaṇī gauṛā*) — so in the 1941 edition. The ghosha is the refrain. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of this lahari (unlike lahari 6): after the heading, the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥.

[^107-2]: "Lord of life" — *prāṇa-pati*. "Your" — *tuyā* (a Brajabuli form): the address is to Shyamananda. "Glory and renown" — *yaśaḥ-kīrtti*.

[^107-3]: Karnavedha (*karṇa-vedha*) — the samskara of piercing a child's ears. Couplet 3 is built like the opening of the account of the annaprashana in lahari 6, 10; the rite itself is described further on (4–21).

[^107-4]: The dundubhi is a large kettledrum. Muhuriya (*muhuriyā*) — according to the edition's gloss, a *shanaidar*, a player of the shanai (sanai), a wind instrument like an oboe (see 9, 11, 17–18).

[^107-5]: Lines of the pada played by the musicians (9) — printed in the edition in parentheses but with the number ॥ 8 ॥. They are the words of a gopi (Radha) to a friend; Shyama-nagara ("Shyama the lover") is Krishna. "Listen, friend" — *śuna lo sajani*. The source of the pada has not been identified.

[^107-6]: "Became motionless" — *aceṣṭa*; according to the edition's gloss, "lost consciousness"; the edition also notes a variant *āviṣṭa*, "became absorbed [in ecstasy]" (so too in the 1997 edition).

[^107-7]: The pindi (*piṁṛā*) is a low wooden seat (cf. lahari 6, note 10). Prabhu — here Rasika (so also in lahari 6, 7–8).

[^107-8]: The sense of the second line is unclear: *nā jāniyā bale kibā dekhila kakhane*. It may also be understood as "without knowing [it], [he] speaks of what [he once] saw," i.e., the boy, hearing the song about Shyama, seems to recall something seen before.

[^107-9]: "Shapely" — *susañca*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; the word is unclear and the translation conjectural; cf. the infant's "finely shaped" (*suśaṅka*) ears in lahari 4, 58, note 13.

[^107-10]: Dayaladasi — see lahari 4, note 18 (she told Rasika's mother about Krishna during her pregnancy). Thakurani is a respectful title of a Vaishnava woman. She has not been identified in other sources.

[^107-11]: "The mother" — *mātā*: a respectful way of referring to an elderly Vaishnava woman (Dayaladasi), not Rasika's mother; so also in 28, 40, 42–45.

[^107-12]: "The form of Gopala" — *gopāla-pratimā*; *pratimā* means both "form, likeness" and "Deity (murti)": "as it were the Deity of Gopala." Gopala is Krishna as a child, the little cowherd.

[^107-13]: The sixty-four limbs (*aṅga*) of bhakti are listed in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2 and in the CC, Madhya 22. On the word "avatara" applied to Rasikananda see lahari 6, note 11: in the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding he is an eternal associate and dear devotee (cf. 34, 36, 52), not an avatara of the Lord.

[^107-14]: "Eldest of the clan" — *kula-vṛddha*; "mother of the world" — *jagata-jananī*: an honorific; knowledge of past, present and future is ascribed to her as a saintly Vaishnavi.

[^107-15]: That is, she whispered the holy name into his ear. This is not diksha: Rasikananda later receives diksha from Shyamananda (BR 15); Dayaladasi herself says that the meaning of the mantra will be revealed to him by another — his "lord of life" (48–49).

[^107-16]: "Lord of life" — *prāṇa-pati*: Shyamananda, Rasikananda's future guru (cf. 7, 1: "Shyamananda, the lord of Rasika's life"). "The two" (*doṁhe*) — Shyamananda and Rasikananda; cf. lahari 2, 13 on how "the two" won over Utkala.

[^107-17]: A prahara is a quarter of the day or night, about three hours.

[^107-18]: "A hundred thousand names" (*lakṣa-nāma*, cf. 62) — the vow to chant a lakh of holy names daily (about 64 rounds of the maha-mantra on beads of 108); cf. Haridasa Thakura, who chanted three lakhs of names (CC, Adi 10; Antya 3).

[^107-19]: "Dresses" — *kāchani karena*; *kāchani* — according to the edition's gloss, "dress, attire"; cf. 75, 85, 87, 103 (*kāchaya*, *kāchiyā*).

[^107-20]: 69–106 follow the order of the tenth canto of the Bhagavata (cf. 81): 69–71 — the Earth in the form of a cow, Brahma and the demigods at the Ocean of Milk, Vasudeva, Devaki and Kamsa (10.1–3); 72 — Nanda's festival (10.5); 73 — Putana (10.6); 74 — Shakatasura and Trinavarta (10.7); 82–83 — the name-giving by Garga and the universe in Krishna's mouth (10.8); 84 — Krishna bound to the mortar and the yamala-arjunas (10.9–10); 85–86 — Vatsasura and Bakasura (10.11); 87 — Aghasura (10.12); 88–89 — Brahma steals the calves and boys, Krishna becomes them, Brahma's prayers (10.13–14); 90 — Dhenukasura (10.15); 91 — Kaliya and the prayers of the naga's wives (10.16); 92–93 — the forest fire and Pralamba (10.17–19); 93–94 — the rains and autumn, the Venu-gita (10.20–21); 95 — the Katyayani vow and the stealing of the clothes (10.22); 96 — the wives of the brahmanas (10.23); 97 — Govardhana (10.24–25); 98 — Indra and Surabhi, "Govinda" (10.27); 105–106 — Nanda carried off by Varuna's servant after Ekadashi (10.28); 106 — the rasa (10.29 ff.).

[^107-21]: "Cowherds" — *gopāla*, the cowherd boys. "Little ones" — *chāoyāla*, "child, young one"; next to the cows it may also mean "calves."

[^107-22]: "Achyuta's child" — *acyutera bālā*; *bālā* here means "child," as in 83 (*kona bālā*, "some boy"); it could also be understood as "Achyuta's wife" (Bhavani).

[^107-23]: "Within it" — *garbhe*, lit. "in the womb, inside." According to the Bhagavata (10.8), Yashoda, opening Krishna's mouth, saw the whole universe in it; "the whole play" — *saba khelā*; possibly "the whole [universe as] play."

[^107-24]: "Finely" — *susāra*, glossed in the edition as *sundara*. Perhaps the one who is to play Krishna is dressed up.

[^107-25]: "Nature" — *svabhāva*: apparently the description of the rainy season and of Vrindavana's nature, which in the Bhagavata (10.20) precedes the description of autumn (94).

[^107-26]: "Put a stop to" — *bhañjana karaye*, lit. "break": Krishna persuaded Nanda and the cowherds to give up the sacrifice to Indra and honour Govardhana instead (Bhag. 10.24).

[^107-27]: "Dressing [the children]" — *kāche* is taken as the verb "dresses" (cf. the edition's glosses on 75, 85); it could also be understood as "plays near, together with the children."

[^107-28]: In the Bhagavata (10.28) Nanda, having observed Ekadashi, entered the waters of the Yamuna before dawn and was led away by a servant of Varuna; Krishna went to Varuna and brought his father back.

[^107-29]: 107–111 — the rasa-lila (Bhag. 10.29–33; cf. note 20): the call of the flute, the rasa dance, Krishna's disappearance, the search and His return. "Imitates the sound of the flute with his singing" — *vaṁśī-dhvani gāna*: the boy playing Krishna imitates the flute with his voice. The eight sattvika bhavas (110) — see lahari 6, note 13.

[^107-30]: Sudarshana — the vidyadhara who by a curse had become a serpent and was delivered by the touch of Krishna's foot (Bhag. 10.34); the editor of the edition in his note identifies him with Shankhachuda, who is slain in the same chapter. "Gopi-gita" ("the song of the gopis") is the name of Bhag. 10.31; by the order of the narrative (after 10.34) the gopis' song in their daytime separation from Krishna (10.35, the "Yugala-gita") may also be meant.

[^107-31]: 113–121 — Bhag. 10.36–44: Arishtasura, Keshi, Akrura sent by Kamsa and his prayers (10.39–40), Kamsa's washerman, Sudama the garland-maker, Kubja, the broken bow, the elephant Kuvalayapida, the wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika, Kamsa. "Box" — *peṛī*, a basket or box; "makes her well" — *bhāla kare*, lit. "makes good": Krishna straightened the hunchbacked Kubja.

[^107-32]: "The Sri Bhagavata embodied" — *śrī-bhāgavata-murati*: his whole play is the Bhagavata in living forms. Rasika-shekhara ("crown of the rasikas") is Rasikananda (lahari 4, note 2). 123 — cf. 81 (*bhāgavata-anukrame*, "in the order of the Bhagavata").


## Lahari 8. Hearing the Srimad-Bhagavatam

*A shloka on the superiority of bhakti over liberation and a song in glory of Shyamananda; the boy Rasika plays Bhagavata pastimes with the children day and night and forgets to eat; at his request Achyuta invites a learned brahmana to recite the Bhagavata, and Rasika, sitting on his father's lap, hears in order of Krishna's deeds in Mathura and Dvaraka, and faints at the account of the gopis' separation; he shapes a Deity and worships Him, holds sankirtana with the children and plays at pilgrimage; people call him Krishna's companion and bless him*

*The eighth lahari.*

**S1.** *Those whose understanding is formed by the study of the Vedas and reflection [on them] praise liberation as supreme,*
*but they, with an understanding made certain by guru and shastra, know nothing.*
*In my view bhakti is greater; and therefore, O fool,*
*lead your mind to him — Murari-deva Rasikananda, the shelter of peace.*[^108-1]

*Raga Varadi.*[^108-2]
*Ghosha: "O king of the Yadus! O beautiful one, darling, ah!"*

**1.** *Song.* Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the son of Durika!
Glory, glory to the treasure of Rasika-deva's life![^108-3]

**2.** Thus day by day he grows cleverer;
day and night he plays [the pastimes] in the order of the Bhagavata.

**3.** Putting aside [all care for] bed, food and sleep — everything,
he gathers the children and plays with eagerness.

**4.** Nothing pleases him but the Bhagavata.
Achyuta, taking [him] on his lap, asks again and again:

**5.** "You eat nothing, child — you play all the time,
gathering ten or twenty children around you.

**6.** You eat no rice, drink no water — you play without pause.
From tomorrow sit at home and play every day."

**7.** Hearing his father's words, he answers very softly —
the words barely leave his lips, [such is] the sweetness of his speech:

**8.** "Then I will not play [, running] all over the town,
if you will listen to the Bhagavata with reverence.

**9.** Sit still and listen to the narrations of the Bhagavata —
then I will by no means go out to play."[^108-4]

**10.** Hearing his son's words, [Achyuta] rejoiced in his heart:
"Good, good! So I have decided."

**11.** With care he invited a teacher —
the best of brahmanas, a bhattacharya, an ornament of Mimamsa.[^108-5]

**12.** Achyuta speaks these words to the teacher:
"My son wishes to hear the Sri Bhagavata.

**13.** Every day recite [to him this book], full of Krishna's pastimes."
Saying "good," the venerable [teacher] began [to read] the manuscript.

**14.** Sitting on his father's lap, Prabhu hears
[how Krishna] in childhood played eagerly with the children.[^108-6]

**15.** All this he heard with delight for some days;
the pastimes of the slaying of Kamsa and others he hears one after another.

**16.** Now one day he hears with love [how]
[Krishna] made Ugrasena king in Mathura.[^108-7]

**17.** One day he hears with delight of the schooling:
[how Krishna], bringing back his teacher's son, gave [him] to him.

**18.** One day he hears how Uddhava goes to Vraja,
[and] of the gopis' hurt pride [voiced] under the pretext [of speaking to] the bee.[^108-8]

**19.** Hearing of the gopis' separation, Rasika
falls senseless from his father's lap.

**20.** The hairs stand on end all over his body, streams [of tears] flow from both eyes;
seeing [this], Achyuta remembers Sri Krishna.

**21.** Lifting [him], alarmed, he wiped [his] face,
saying, "Krishna, protect this child!"

**22.** Thus every day on Achyuta's lap
he listens with love and great eagerness.

**23.** One day he hears of the meeting in Kubja's house,
one day — of how [Krishna] went to Akrura's house.

**24.** One day he hears how Akrura entered Hastina
to learn about [His] own servants, the Pandavas.

**25.** One day — [how] Kamsa's two wives, Asti and Prapti,
went to their father Jarasandha and complained [to him].[^108-9]

**26.** One day he hears of Jarasandha in [all his] might:
[how he] besieges Mathura in a terrible battle.

**27.** Again and again, seventeen times he fights,
[and] the king of Magadha goes away defeated.

**28.** One day he hears how [Krishna], leaving Madhupuri,
settled in Dvaraka with His kinsmen and friends.

**29.** One day he hears the story of Kalayavana:
[how he], breaking Muchukunda's sleep, was turned to ashes.

**30.** One day he hears Muchukunda's prayers;
of the burning of the mountain [and] the flight of the two brothers.[^108-10]

**31.** One day he hears of the abduction of Rukmini:
[how she], sending a brahmana to Dvaraka, summons Narayana;

**32.** [how He], binding Rukmi and shaving [his head],
fought a great battle with all the kings.

**33.** One day he hears of the abduction of Pradyumna
and of the deliverance of Pradyumna, who slew Shambara.

**34.** One day he hears of the theft of the Syamantaka jewel:
[how Krishna] fought with Jambavan,

**35.** [how He], because of a slander, brought the Syamantaka jewel
and married Jambavati Thakurani.

**36.** One day he hears of the marriage to Satyabhama:
Krishna slew Shatadhanva in battle.

**37.** One day he hears of the journey to Indraprastha
to see His servants, the Pandavas.

**38.** One day he hears of the marriage to Kalindi,
of the marriage to Nagnajiti and how [He] bound the seven bulls.

**39.** One day he hears of the slaying of Narakasura:
[Krishna] took his sixteen thousand one hundred maidens [as wives].[^108-11]

**40.** One day he hears of the taking of the parijata:
[Krishna] defeated the lord of the gods in battle.

**41.** One day he hears of Rukmini's bewilderment:
[how she], her voice choked with prema, offers prayers.[^108-12]

**42.** One day — of the number of the sons of the eight queens;
one day he hears of Aniruddha's marriage.

**43.** One day he hears of Pradyumna's marriage
and of how the king of Kalinga's teeth were knocked out.

**44.** One day he hears of the slaying of Rukmi,
of the abduction of Usha, of that unceasing battle with Bana.[^108-13]

**45.** One day he hears of the deliverance of King Nriga;
[of how] Balarama, coming to Vraja, sees His friends,

**46.** drags the Yamuna with His plough;
one day he hears of the slaying of Pundarika.[^108-14]

**47.** One day — [how] Sudarshana burns Varanasi;
[how] the fire, [driven] by the splendour of the disc, rushed to seek shelter.[^108-15]

**48.** [How] Shyama-kumara was bound in the land of Hastina —
for that reason Balarama went [there].[^108-16]

**49.** One day he hears how [Balarama] drags Hastina;
[how] Narada [comes] to Dvaraka to see Krishna.

**50.** In every palace Narada sees Bhagavan
and in supreme bliss offers prayers unceasingly.

**51.** One day he hears [how] Jarasandha
put ninety-six thousand kings in fetters.[^108-17]

**52.** Their messenger comes and tells Krishna [of it];
[and] again Narada comes to Dvaraka.

**53.** One day, [taking] Uddhava's counsel,
Krishna enters Hastina, to the Pandavas.

**54.** One day he hears of the slaying of Jarasandha:
[Krishna] freed the kings from captivity.

**55.** One day he hears the account of the Rajasuya sacrifice,
one day — the news of the slaying of Shishupala.

**56.** One day he hears of Duryodhana's humiliation,
one day he hears with great delight of the slaying of Shalva.

**57.** One day he hears of the slaying of Dantavakra,
one day — of Balarama's pilgrimage to the holy places;

**58.** one day he hears of [His] coming to Naimisharanya:
Balarama slays Suta the Pauranika.[^108-18]

**59.** [How He] visited all the holy places there are on earth.
Constantly he hears how Sudama's poverty was removed.[^108-19]

**60.** One day he hears [how] at the time of a solar eclipse
the king of the Yadus went to Kurukshetra,

**61.** met with Nanda and the other cowherds;
[how] Draupadi questions the eight queens.

**62.** One day — the prayers of Vasudeva and Devaki;
of the abduction of Subhadra he hears with undivided attention.

**63.** One day he hears of the journey to the land of Videha;
one day he hears [how] the four Vedas offer prayers.[^108-20]

**64.** One day — of the cause of the sages' dispute;
one day he hears of Bhrigu's coming to Dvaraka:

**65.** [how] Krishna, [receiving] a kick, bears [on His chest the mark of] Shrivatsa —
[this] Rasika hears with joy and attention.[^108-21]

**66.** One day he hears of Arjuna's vow:
[how Krishna] keeps [him] from entering the fire and restores the children.

**67.** One day he hears the count of the sons.
Thus he hears the Bhagavata unceasingly.[^108-22]

**68.** Day after day he hears the twelve cantos of the Bhagavata
[and] all the glory of Krishna that there is in the Puranas.

**69.** He hears those shastras in which [is told] the glory of Krishna,
and, hearing, he weeps, filled with tender feeling.

**70.** One day, bringing clay at an auspicious moment,
with his own hands he makes a Sri-murti (Deity).[^108-23]

**71.** Installing [Him], he dresses [Him] in various ways;
incense, lamps, naivedya — the sixteen articles of worship.

**72.** One day, taking the children, [he holds] sankirtana:
some sing, some play [instruments], some dance.

**73.** One day, taking up renunciation in childish play,
out of love for Krishna he goes off to wander to the holy places.

**74.** The children bring him back from far away;
day and night he plays this game with the children.

**75.** Apart from Krishna he knows nothing else even for a moment:
those plays, those qualities — hearing [of them], meditation [on them].

**76.** Without pause his eyes are wet with tears;
Krishna is [his] life, Krishna his wealth, Krishna his kin.

**77.** Seeing all these signs in Rasika in his childhood,
the men and women are amazed.

**78.** All say: "This boy is Krishna's companion;
day and night his body shines with absorption in Krishna.

**79.** Because of him the father listens to the Bhagavata;
apart from the Bhagavata he knows nothing, day or night.[^108-24]

**80.** O Krishna, always protect this boy!
This great soul will deliver all living beings."

**81.** Thus all the people bless [him] —
brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras — all who see [him].

**82.** All who see the beauty of [his] holy moon-like face,
forgetting themselves, gaze [at him] intently.

**83.** A gentle, gentle smile, tender, soft speech —
hearing [it], all living beings are enchanted.

**84.** Thus in the mood of childhood Rasika-shekhara
without pause enacts Krishna's pastimes with the children.

**85.** I am unable to tell [of it] in detail;
briefly I have described this [nature of his].

**86.** The narrative of the Purva-vibhaga is supremely full of rasa;
hearing the Rasika-mangala, cross over the age of Kali.[^108-25]

**87.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the eighth lahari, called "Hearing the Srimad-Bhagavatam," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^108-1]: The shloka is unnumbered in the edition (after it come the raga, the ghosha and the song with ॥ 1 ॥); it is marked S1, like the mangala-shlokas of lahari 1 (note 1) and 6 (note 1). The metre is shardula-vikridita. Second line: *guru-śāstra-niścita-dhiyā* — "with an understanding made certain by guru and shastra," i.e. for all their learning. Murari-deva Rasikananda is Rasikananda (Rasika-Murari, lahari 5, 13–15).
