According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, liberation (mukti) is inferior to bhakti: the pure devotee does not accept even liberation without service to the Lord (Bhag. 3.29.13; Bhag. 1.1.2 and CC, Adi 1: the desire for moksha is a "cheating" rejected by the Bhagavata). The source of the shloka has not been identified — apparently the author's own composition.

[^108-2]: Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*) — a raga frequent in Vaishnava padas. The ghosha (refrain) reads in the 1941 edition: *yadurājā nārere sundara yādumaṇi āhāre*. *Yādumaṇi* is an endearment, "darling, treasure" (said to a child), echoing "Yadu"; *āhā re* is an exclamation; the sense of *nāre re* (possibly a mere sung filler) is unclear.

[^108-3]: "Song" — *gīta*, the edition's marker before ॥ 1 ॥, as in lahari 1. Durika is Shyamananda's mother (lahari 1, note 11). Rasika-deva is Rasikananda.

[^108-4]: 8–9: "listen" (*śuna*) is addressed to the father: the boy asks that his father hear the Bhagavata [with him]; then (11–14) Achyuta invites a reciter, and Rasika listens sitting on his father's lap.

[^108-5]: "Ornament of Mimamsa" — *mīmāṁsā-maṇḍana*: an expert in Mimamsa (the school of Vedic exegesis); possibly also an honorific title or the teacher's name. In the edition's list of errata the reading "মীমাংম" is corrected to "মীমাংসা". Bhattacharya is a title of a learned brahmana.

[^108-6]: Prabhu is Rasika (lower case for him, as is the rule in this translation). The second line is elliptical; it is understood as the account of Krishna's childhood play (Bhag., Canto 10, up to ch. 44); "Kamsa and others" in 15 — Bhag. 10.36–44 (cf. lahari 7, 113–121).

[^108-7]: From 16 to 67 the list follows the order of the second half of the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavata (10.45–90); only some episodes and divergences are noted below. 17 — the schooling with Sandipani Muni and the return of his son (10.45).

[^108-8]: Bhag. 10.46–47: the "Bhramara-gita" — the gopis address a bee (*bhramara*), seeing it as Krishna's messenger. "Hurt pride" — *abhimāna*, the wounded feeling of a lover.

[^108-9]: Asti and Prapti — Kamsa's wives, daughters of Jarasandha (Bhag. 10.50; so also the edition's gloss). "Complained" — *gohārī karila* (the edition's gloss: "complaint"). 26 — *māhātme*, probably = *māhātmye*, "in [his] greatness, might."

[^108-10]: Bhag. 10.52: Jarasandha set fire to Mount Pravarshana, where Krishna and Balarama had taken refuge; They leapt down and went away to Dvaraka. "Flight" — so in the text (*palāyana*); the Bhagavata (10.52) says that the brothers fled only feigning fear.

[^108-11]: The sixteen thousand one hundred princesses whom Naraka held captive (Bhag. 10.59). *Kanyā naila* — "took the maidens."

[^108-12]: "Rukmini's bewilderment" — *rukmiṇīra mohana*: Krishna jokingly suggested that Rukmini choose another husband, and she fainted; then come her prayers (Bhag. 10.60).

[^108-13]: The 1941 edition reads *rukmiṇīra saṁhāra*, "the slaying of Rukmini"; the edition's list of errata corrects this word — by sense "Rukmi": Rukmini's brother, slain by Balarama at Aniruddha's wedding (Bhag. 10.61). Usha and Bana — Bhag. 10.62–63.

[^108-14]: Pundarika (*puṇḍarīka*) — in the Bhagavata, Paundraka, the false Vasudeva (10.66).

[^108-15]: Bhag. 10.66: the fiery demon (kritya) sent from Varanasi against Dvaraka fled back, pursued by Sudarshana, and burned those who had raised it; Sudarshana burned Varanasi.

[^108-16]: *Śyāma-kumāra* — so in the 1941 edition; by sense Samba, Jambavati's son, whom the Kauravas bound in Hastinapura for carrying off Duryodhana's daughter; Balarama dragged the city with His plough (Bhag. 10.68; cf. 49).

[^108-17]: According to the Bhagavata (10.70), twenty thousand eight hundred kings; the author has *chiyānabbai sahasra*, "ninety-six thousand."

[^108-18]: Bhag. 10.78: Balarama slew Romaharshana Suta, who had not risen before Him in the assembly of sages at Naimisharanya.

[^108-19]: Sudama — the poor brahmana, Krishna's childhood friend (Bhag. 10.80–81); not to be confused with Sudama the garland-maker (lahari 7, 118).

[^108-20]: 60–63: Bhag. 10.82–87: the meeting at Kurukshetra, Draupadi's questions to the queens, the prayers of Vasudeva and Devaki, the abduction of Subhadra, the visit to Mithila (the land of Videha), the prayers of the personified Vedas (the "Shruti-gita," 10.87).

[^108-21]: Bhag. 10.89: the sages disputed which of the three deities is greatest; Bhrigu, testing them, kicked Vishnu on the chest — in the Bhagavata this happens in Vaikuntha, in the author's account in Dvaraka. The author identifies the mark of Bhrigu's foot on the Lord's chest with the Shrivatsa.

[^108-22]: 66: Bhag. 10.89: Arjuna vowed to protect the children of a brahmana of Dvaraka and, having failed, wished to enter the fire; Krishna restrained him and brought the children back from the abode of Maha-Vishnu. 67: "the count of the sons" — Krishna's descendants (10.90).

[^108-23]: Sri-murti — the form of the Lord for worship, the Deity. The sixteen articles of worship (*ṣoḍaśa-upacāra*) — the full order of puja: offering of a seat, water, garments, scents, a lamp, food (naivedya) and so on.

[^108-24]: Cf. 8–14: at his son's request Achyuta invited a reciter and listens to the Bhagavata together with him. The second line refers to the boy.

[^108-25]: "Cross over the age of Kali" — *tara kali-kāla*: by hearing this book, overcome [the miseries of] the Kali age. Cf. the call to listen at the close of lahari 7 (123).


## Lahari 9. Description of the Delights of Learning

*A shloka in glory of Rasikananda and a song; the rite of beginning to write, performed by the astrologer Vasudeva; Rasika quickly masters the letters and the phalas, then studies grammar and the shastras with five teachers in the places where his father, the adhikari of Mallabhumi, takes him along, and surpasses all in exposition; Jagannatha Mishra reads the Bhagavata with him and, amazed at his explanations, weeps and blesses him; study with Haridasa Dube, their discussions of prema-bhakti and Dube's praise of the boy; the fruits of hearing*

*The ninth lahari.*

**S1.** *What [use] is thinking of the chintamani? What [use] are the praisers of the tree of the gods?*
*Or service of the gods, austerity, or attachment to meditation and the like?*
*There is not only suffering there: [there] the mind is again and again gripped by great fear.*
*Lead your mind to Rasikananda, manifest before our eyes for the welfare of the worlds.*[^109-1]

*Raga Sangada.*[^109-2]
*Ghosha: "In Nanda's house the crown-jewel of the gods*
*sports in the guise of a boy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Krishna's qualities! I bow to the holy feet.
Glory, glory to the son of Achyuta, the treasure of [my] life![^109-3]

**2.** Thus day by day Rasika-shekhara
hears without pause of Krishna's qualities, of Krishna's pastimes.

**3.** After some time Achyuta considers in his mind
placing the chalk in Rasika's hand according to the rite.

**4.** Quickly summoning all the brahmana astrologers,
he fixed an auspicious day according to the shastras.

**5.** Setting up the auspicious pot, he worships Sarasvati —
that wise astrologer named Vasudeva.

**6.** He placed the chalk in [his] hand, saying "Sri Krishna!" —
and Prabhu sat down to study, full of joy.

**7.** With his beautiful hand, [tender as] a young shoot, he took the chalk,
wrote "siddhir astu" and prostrated himself.[^109-4]

**8.** Quickly bowing at the feet of his teacher,
he then offered obeisance to the brahmanas.

**9.** Bowing at the feet of his father and mother,
Rasika then bowed to all his elders.

**10.** With joyful hearts all bless [him]:
"May Krishna make you like Brihaspati!"[^109-5]

**11.** Setting up an excellent school,
Vasudeva teaches the son of Achyuta.

**12.** He learns every letter as soon as he sees it;
the teacher joyfully teaches [him], [wholly] absorbed [in it].

**13.** Prabhu recites all the phalas in a sweet voice —
hearing [it] is as if nectar were sprinkled into the ears.[^109-6]

**14.** One longs to hear the sweetness of those words;
when he speaks, [the words] come from his sweet mouth in a childish half-lisp.

**15.** Hearing the nectar of those words, a stone melts.
Thus, as if at play, he studies with the children.

**16.** All the phalas he learned in a few days
and with a joyful heart began to spell out words.

**17.** After some time, having mastered the letters,
he resolved in his mind to study grammar.

**18.** He told his father of [his] wish to learn;
[the father] brought a teacher — Mimamsa-mandana.

**19.** Fixing an auspicious day, he took a manuscript in hand;
Mimamsa-mandana teaches Rasika-shekhara.[^109-7]

**20.** Hearing only once from the teacher's mouth,
Rasika quickly explains the roots and sutras.

**21.** Seeing the son's explanations, [all] are amazed.
The bhattacharya says: "This boy is no human being.

**22.** What we learn after studying a year or two —
all those explanations I hear from this mouth.

**23.** Truly this great soul is Krishna's associate;
he will crush the Shaivas, the Shaktas and the pashandas."[^109-8]

**24.** For some days he studied with him;
then the vaidya Balabhadrasena taught [him].

**25.** For some days he studied with Balabhadra —
he was highly accomplished in the science of grammar.

**26.** [He studied] for some time with Anukula Chakravarti,
and at last learned something with Kavichandra.

**27.** For some time with Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti
he studied with eagerness.

**28.** Alone, with five teachers, great men,
Sri Rasika studies, honouring [them].[^109-9]

**29.** Hearing once, he explains the roots and sutras,
poetry, drama, grammar, commentaries and glosses.

**30.** The son himself explains, himself refutes —
and no one is able to re-establish [what was refuted].

**31.** Hundreds of students study with all [these teachers];
when Rasika refutes, no one can re-establish.

**32.** By the mercy of Krishna, the Lord of Sarasvati,
Rasika himself establishes [the point] again.[^109-10]

**33.** The exposition [follows] the proper order, without a single fault;
hearing [it], that teacher is supremely pleased.

**34.** The students, hearing the exposition of the sutras, are astonished:
"How has a child come to such understanding of the shastras?

**35.** We have studied for so long, with all our strength —
[yet] no one could answer the child's refutation.

**36.** And he himself has re-established the roots and sutras.
This is no child — this is a person endowed with all virtues."

**37.** Thus all are amazed,
[while] the son of Achyuta studies with his teachers.

**38.** Achyuta is the adhikari in the land of Mallabhumi;
on royal business he travels from region to region.[^109-11]

**39.** Taking with him the son dearer than life,
wherever he goes, there he takes Rasika.

**40.** Choosing a dwelling in one place or another,
he stays there for many days.

**41.** In whatever place whatever teacher lives,
in that place, with him, [go on] the delights of learning.

**42.** Therefore with five teachers, in different places,
he studies day and night with diligence.

**43.** Absorbed in learning, Prabhu knows neither day nor night;
he became a knower of the six shastras, keen of understanding.

**44.** His heart is ever enchanted by prema for Krishna;
for the deliverance of living beings he studies with diligence.

**45.** In debate the opponents [are]: tarka, sankhya, sankhyayana,
mimamsa, [the teaching of] Patanjali and all the other [subjects of] study.[^109-12]

**46.** To crush their pride,
he quickly studied all the shastras and the essence of the Vedas.

**47.** He became a great pandita, equal to Brihaspati —
he by whose touch the earth rejoiced.

**48.** Having thus studied all the shastras,
he wished to study the Bhagavata.

**49.** The teacher Jagannatha Mishra, the fortunate,
set the Bhagavata Purana in song metre.[^109-13]

**50.** Fixing an auspicious moment, [Rasika] began his study;
the son of Achyuta studies with love.

**51.** Day by day he studies [it], beginning with the first canto;
hearing once from the teacher's mouth, he explains.

**52.** He explains the commentaries and glosses in accordance with Svami;
he explains in various ways — who will grasp [this] truth?[^109-14]

**53.** A single shloka he explains in so many ways:
the mood, the nature, the meaning of the words, the intent of Vyasa.

**54.** Joining prema with the conclusions of Vedanta,
he explains bhakti like Shuka embodied.[^109-15]

**55.** His voice choked with prema, he explains;
the hair stands on end all over his body, tears flow from his holy eyes.

**56.** Hearing that explanation, dry wood melts;
he explains as one who experiences prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**57.** Hearing the exposition of the Bhagavata, the teacher is amazed;
in joy he embraces [him] again and again.

**58.** Mishra says: "Blessed is the father, blessed is that mother!
Has Vyasa or Shukadeva himself been born?

**59.** Through the boy's exposition knowledge has come to me."
Pressing Rasika to his chest, he began to weep.

**60.** The eight sattvika [bhavas] arose in Mishra;
he says: "This great person is a dear devotee of Krishna.[^109-16]

**61.** By seeing him I shall surely attain Krishna;
by his touch prema-bhakti awakens.

**62.** By seeing him [one] is freed from all sins."
Saying these words, all cry: "Glory, glory!"

**63.** "Hearing his words, the ears are soothed;
this person will deliver the whole world.

**64.** We have studied the Bhagavata for so long —
[yet] never knew anything of the truth of the Bhagavata.

**65.** Hearing from this boy's mouth, I have gained knowledge;
whatever Rasika explains — that is the truth.[^109-17]

**66.** To make known to the world the deep meaning of the Bhagavata,
Krishna's servant has been born as the son of Achyuta."[^109-18]

**67.** Having said this, Jagannatha Mishra Mahashaya
gives [him] his blessing with joy in his heart.

**68.** After studying with him for some time,
Prabhu then studied with Hari Dube.[^109-19]

**69.** The fortunate Hari Dube, Krishna's servant,
without pause explains prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**70.** Hearing [him], Prabhu rejoices; with kindly words
they constantly expound prema-bhakti to each other.

**71.** He found great happiness with Hari Dube;
without pause, together with him, [he was engaged] in research among manuscripts.[^109-20]

**72.** Hearing Sri Rasika's explanations, Hari Dube
in joy [shows] horripilation and tears — in the mood of prema for Krishna.

**73.** He regards Rasika as dearer than his own self;
without pause the two sit discussing the shastras.

**74.** The two know nothing of eating, resting or sleep;
at every moment they expound prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**75.** The most steadfast and learned Haridasa Dube,
hearing from the boy's mouth, experiences Krishna.

**76.** In joy he takes Rasika on his lap and embraces him:
"May [all I have] be offered up for [your] face, son of Achyuta![^109-21]

**77.** Blessed, blessed is that land, blessed is that mother!
Has Brihaspati himself come and been born?

**78.** Or Vyasa, Shuka, Narada and the other gods,
or Aja, Bhava, Purandara, Narayana?[^109-22]

**79.** Such intelligence in a child [I] have never seen;
to the greatness of [his] learning Brihaspati and Shuka are witnesses.[^109-23]

**80.** [He] knows Vedanta, siddhanta, the meanings of words, the six shastras,
the eighteen Puranas, the Sri Bhagavata, the Gita.[^109-24]

**81.** The great ocean of the nectar of the rasa of prema-bhakti for Krishna
he expounds [so that it appears] embodied — such is the fame [of him].[^109-25]

**82.** Different people give a single shloka different meanings;
the child refuted the explanations of them all.

**83.** However Rasika explains [it] — that is the true evidence;
of this Vyasa, Shuka, Narada and others are the warrant.

**84.** By our good fortune [this] boy has come into the world;
this great-minded one will deliver all living beings."

**85.** Past, future [and] present Dube knows.
Blessing [Rasika], he proclaims [his] glory before everyone.

**86.** Thus, in love for Krishna, [went on] the delights of learning;
[Rasika] lived constantly in Dube's company.

**87.** Whoever hears of these delights of learning
[gains] prema-bhakti for Krishna [and] release from bondage.[^109-26]

**88.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all you devotees of Krishna:
soon you will attain the Sri feet of Rasika.[^109-27]

**89.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the ninth lahari, called "Description of the Delights of Learning," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^109-1]: The shloka is unnumbered in the edition (after it come the raga, the ghosha and the couplets from ॥ 1 ॥); it is marked S1, like the mangala-shlokas of lahari 1 (note 1), 6 and 8 (notes 1). The metre is shardula-vikridita. The chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem; "the tree of the gods" — *sura-kṣauṇīruha*, the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpa-vriksha) of the heavenly world. "Great fear" — *guru-bhaya*; the edition's shlokartha takes it as fear of the cycle of worldly existence (*saṁsṛti*). "Manifest before our eyes" — *pratyakṣam*. The thought is the same as in the mangala-shloka of lahari 8: not worldly boons, austerity or meditation, but devotion to a pure Vaishnava leads to bhakti (cf. lahari 8, note 1). The source is not established — apparently the author's own composition.

[^109-2]: Raga Sangada (*sāṅgaṛā*) — so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; we have not found this raga in other collections of padas. The ghosha (refrain) is *nandera mandire deva-śiromaṇi vihare bālaka-veśe*. Unlike lahari 8, there is no "song" (*gīta*) mark before ॥ 1 ॥.

[^109-3]: "Glory to Krishna's qualities" — *jaya jaya kṛṣṇa-guṇa* — so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; in the opening couplets of laharis 6, 8 and 10 Shyamananda's name stands here. "I bow to the holy feet" — *banda śrīcaraṇa*; "bow [all of you]" is also possible; whose feet is not said. The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda.

[^109-4]: 3–7 — the rite of beginning instruction (*hāte khaṛi*, lit. "[giving] chalk into the hand"): on an auspicious day fixed by astrologers (*daivajña*), an auspicious pot (*maṅgala-ghaṭa*) is set up, Sarasvati, the goddess of learning, is worshipped, and the child writes letters in chalk for the first time. "Siddhir astu" ("may there be success") are the customary first words written by a pupil. Vasudeva, the astrologer and Rasika's first teacher, is not mentioned in other sources.

[^109-5]: Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, the model of learning.

[^109-6]: Phalas (*phalā*) are the special (subscript) forms of consonants in Bengali script (*ya-phalā, ra-phalā*, etc.), which a child learns after the letters. "Spell out words" (16) — *bānāite*: to join letters into words, to learn spelling.

[^109-7]: Mimamsa-mandana (*mīmāṁsā-maṇḍana*, "ornament of mimamsa") — cf. lahari 8, 11 and note 5, where the learned brahmana who read the Bhagavata to Rasika is so called; here (apparently the same) teacher of grammar is so called — probably his honorific title or name; in 21 he is called the bhattacharya. "Roots and sutras" (*dhātu sūtra*) — the verbal roots and rules (sutras) of Sanskrit grammar.

[^109-8]: The Shaivas, the Shaktas (worshippers of Shiva and of Shakti-Durga) and the pashandas — opponents of Vaishnava bhakti. According to BR 15, Shyamananda and Rasikananda converted many pashandas in Utkala.

[^109-9]: 24–28: the five teachers are Mimamsa-mandana, the vaidya (of the physician caste) Balabhadrasena, Anukula Chakravarti, Kavichandra ("moon of poets," apparently a title) and Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti; BR 15 does not name them (it says only: "from his early years he was versed in all the shastras"). "Alone" (28, *ekā*) — apparently Rasika studied with them by himself, without fellow pupils. "With eagerness" (27) — *kariyā ārati*.

[^109-10]: 30–36: "to refute" (*khaṇḍana*) and "to re-establish, to affirm" (*sthāpana*) are moves in scholarly debate: Rasika himself refutes an explanation and himself re-establishes it. The Lord of Sarasvati is Krishna (Sarasvati is the goddess of speech and learning).

[^109-11]: Mallabhumi — lahari 3, note 6; there too (54) Achyuta is called the lord of the region. Adhikari (*adhikārī*) — a steward, an official.

[^109-12]: The six shastras (43, *ṣaḍ-śāstra*) are the six philosophical systems (darshanas). 45: tarka (nyaya, logic), sankhya, mimamsa, the [yoga] of Patanjali; *sāṅkhyāyana* — so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; probably Shankhayana (a Vedic school named after the rishi Shankhayana), but possibly just an echo of "sankhya"; the reading is unclear.

[^109-13]: Jagannatha Mishra is Rasika's teacher — not to be confused with Jagannatha Mishra, the father of Sri Chaitanya. "Set in song metre" — *gīta-chande bāndhilena*: apparently he composed a rendering of the Bhagavata in the vernacular. Cf. the Oriya Bhagavata of Jagannatha Dasa (16th c.); any connection with it is not established.

[^109-14]: Svami is Shridhara Svami, author of the commentary *Bhavartha-dipika* on the Bhagavata. Sri Chaitanya honoured this commentary and said that one who does not accept Svami should be counted as unfaithful, like a harlot (CC, Antya 7).

[^109-15]: Shuka is Shukadeva Gosvami, the speaker of the Bhagavata. "Joining prema with the conclusions of Vedanta": according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the Bhagavata is the natural commentary on the *Vedanta-sutra*, and its highest conclusion is prema (CC, Madhya 25).

[^109-16]: The eight sattvika bhavas — lahari 6, note 13; cf. 55 and 72.

[^109-17]: "Knowledge" — *giyāna* = *jñāna* (so also the edition's gloss). "The truth" — *pramāṇa*, "proof, the measure of truth."

[^109-18]: "Krishna's servant" — *kṛṣṇera kiṅkara*: Mishra sees in Rasika a devotee sent by Krishna (cf. 23, 60).

[^109-19]: Hari Dube is Haridasa Dube (75); Dube (Dvivedi) is a brahmana surname common in North India. He is not mentioned in other sources.

[^109-20]: "Research among manuscripts" — *puṅthi anveṣaṇe*: perhaps searching for and collating manuscripts, or simply the study of books.

[^109-21]: "May it be offered up for your face" — *nichāni mukhera yāu*: nichhani is the custom of waving a gift (or oneself) around a beloved's face to ward off misfortune; that is, "let all that is mine be sacrificed for you."

[^109-22]: Aja is Brahma, Bhava is Shiva, Purandara is Indra. The comparisons in Dube's praise are rapturous hyperbole; the author himself calls Rasika Krishna's servant (66) and His associate (23). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a pure devotee, an associate of Shyamananda, and not Narayana Himself.

[^109-23]: 79–84 continue Haridasa Dube's speech (76–78, note 21); the quotation closes in 84. Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, the model of learning; Shuka is Shukadeva (note 15).

[^109-24]: Siddhanta — the established conclusions of a teaching; "the meanings of words" — *śabdārtha* (grammar and lexicon); the six shastras are the six philosophical systems (note 12).

[^109-25]: "The great ocean of the nectar of the rasa of prema-bhakti" — *rasāmṛta-mahodadhi*; possibly an echo of the title of Rupa Gosvami's *Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu* ("The Ocean of the Nectar of the Rasa of Bhakti"). The second line is elliptical: *mūrttimanta bākhānaya ye āche prasiddhi* — "he expounds [it] embodied, as is well known"; "he expounds all that is renowned" is also possible.

[^109-26]: "Release from bondage" — *bandhana-mocana*, release from the bonds of material existence. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, liberation comes to the devotee of itself, as a by-product of bhakti, and is inferior to it (cf. lahari 8, note 1). The edition notes a variant reading of the first line, close in meaning.

[^109-27]: "The devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana*; read in the 1941 edition (a superscript repha), note 66; lahari 3, note 19).


## Lahari 10. Description of the Pastimes of Adolescence

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; reading the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavata with Hari Dube, Rasika hears that Krishna did not return to Vraja and, weeping like the gopis in separation, wanders the forests for seven days without food or water; Achyuta and the townspeople find him and carry him home; Dube, citing Rupa's Bhagavatamrita, explains to him that Krishna returned to Vraja and never leaves it, and Rasika comes back to himself; Achyuta entrusts his son to Dube; Rasika becomes a master of all the shastras, composes songs and shlokas, and his detachment grows; Achyuta looks for a bride for him; Balabhadra Dasa, the ruler of Hijli, and his daughter Ichchha-dei; Achyuta frees Balabhadra, detained by the subadar in Medinipur over arrears, and Balabhadra, seeing Rasika, offers him his daughter in marriage*

*The tenth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^110-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the son of Durika!
Glory to the son of Bhavani, Rasikendra-chandra![^110-2]

**2.** Thus together with Dube, [immersed] in the rasa of the Bhagavata,
he reads the Tenth [Canto] with love and with special [care].

**3.** One day he reads the Tenth [Canto] with Hari Dube —
[of how] the wives of Vraja, in separation, [pine] with love for Krishna.[^110-3]

**4.** Krishna went to Mathura and did not come back to Vraja —
hearing [this], Rasika fell senseless to the ground.

**5.** Hearing with his own ears that Krishna did not come back to Vraja,
[he thinks]: "How did the gopis keep their lives?

**6.** Parted from Krishna, the lord of [their] lives, how did they survive?" —
saying this again and again, he began to weep.

**7.** Sobbing and sobbing, he weeps and rolls on the ground;
the eight sattvika-[bhavas] arose in him.[^110-4]

**8.** Down [his] Sri moonlike face flow hundreds and hundreds of streams;
torrents of tears pour from his eyes without cease.

**9.** All over his body the hairs stand on end, his voice falters, [he is drowning in tears]:
"Krishna, lord of my life, to what land have You gone?"

**10.** He weeps, distraught with love for Krishna;
hearing the weeping, all the people came.

**11.** Everyone says: "Why is [this] best of children weeping,
whose father is the lord of the realm in Mallabhumi?[^110-5]

**12.** What thing does [he] not obtain, what task is beyond [him]?
Perhaps some wicked person has done [him] harm?"

**13.** What is in his heart, no one knows;
different mouths say different things without end.

**14.** Prabhu does not bathe, does not eat,
does not ponder his books — he weeps incessantly.

**15.** Prabhu does not stay at home; he is always [as if] mad;
everyone laments, [but] they do not know the truth [of it].

**16.** Day and night, wandering and wandering, he roams from forest to forest;
alone, weeping, he roams in the dense thicket.

**17.** In the forest he has no fear of tigers or bears;
in love for Krishna he has no awareness of the outer [world] and wanders all the time.

**18.** Coming into a terrible forest, he falls face down;
rolling and rolling [on the ground], he weeps and sighs heavily:

**19.** "O lord of life, why have You become so cruel?
For what fault did You leave the unfortunate gopis, and where have You gone?[^110-6]

**20.** For Your sake they gave up husbands, sons and homes;
leaving such beloveds, where have You gone, O best of the Yadus?

**21.** Family, good conduct, shame, fear — they know nothing of these;
like a shadow they always go about with You.

**22.** In hunger — food, in thirst — water the gopis did not take;
You left them all and went, leaving them without shelter.[^110-7]

**23.** Day and night they see You, lying [awake] and in dreams.
How did the cowherd boys and the cows survive?

**24.** How did Nanda and the grieving Yashoda survive?
Without You, how did they keep their lives?

**25.** The bank of the Yamuna weeps, remembering You;
the trees and creepers, the deer and the birds cannot steady their hearts.[^110-8]

**26.** How could You become so heartless, leaving them all?" —
remembering and remembering, he weeps, rolling on the ground.

**27.** Thus [his] absorption lasted seven days;
Achyuta's son gave up food and water.[^110-9]

**28.** He wandered from forest to forest, not knowing day from night;
meanwhile the townspeople go about searching [for him] on all sides.

**29.** Achyuta came home from the royal court
and heard that his son had gone into the forest.

**30.** "Where has [my] boy gone?" — saying this, he fell to the ground;
everyone rushed quickly to lift him up.

**31.** Getting up, he weeps, calling and calling:
"Into which forest has [my] son gone? Go and search!"

**32.** Hundreds and hundreds of people went at Achyuta's command;
in distress they all rush to search.

**33.** Together with Achyuta they went, weeping and weeping;
from forest to forest they all search with anxious hearts.

**34.** [They] saw Rasika rolling on the ground;
the radiance of [his] body was lighting up the forest.

**35.** [His] form, surpassing Kandarpa, captivates the heart;
his Sri moonlike face is beautiful to see.[^110-10]

**36.** His curling locks of hair lie spread on the ground.
Seeing his son, Achyuta [feels his] heart break.

**37.** "Alas, alas, my son!" — saying this, he lifted [him] and took him in his arms;
Prabhu does not open his eyes; tears flow.

**38.** Gladdened, they all came home,
[carrying] the beautiful Rasika on their chests.

**39.** At home they all saw the son's face:
on his Sri moonlike face — streams [of tears], his eyes closed.

**40.** Whatever they do, the weeping does not cease;
seeing [this], all the townspeople were amazed.

**41.** Some say: "[It is] because of the glance of an evil person";
some say: "A strong wind has overcome the son."[^110-11]

**42.** Thus different people [propose] different remedies;
whatever anyone says, that they do again and again.

**43.** By no means does the child say a word;
he does not look, does not eat, his head hung low.

**44.** Prabhu weeps incessantly, distraught;
seeing all this, Achyuta can barely hold on to life.

**45.** Humbly he speaks to Hari Dube:
"My son has given up food — how will he live?"

**46.** Dube says: "Do not worry at all in your mind:
he is intoxicated with feeling for Krishna and is aware of nothing [else].

**47.** This son of yours is a great soul;
this child will deliver the whole world."

**48.** Then Hari Dube speaks to Rasika,
speaking with care what accords with the shastras:

**49.** "Gathering together the words of all the shastras,
Rupa composed the book Bhagavatamrita.

**50.** In it he established [that] the separation [lasted] three months:
the great Krishna came to Vraja again.

**51.** Krishna never leaves Vraja —
this essential truth of the shastras no one knows.[^110-12]

**52.** He to whom Krishna in His mercy gives prema-bhakti
gives this explanation — the evidence of the shastras.

**53.** This is the meaning hidden in the Vedas; the devotees of Krishna know it;
[only] one who has taken exclusive refuge knows this secret."[^110-13]

**54.** [Rasika] heard from Dube's mouth that Krishna came to Vraja:
[he] told Rasika the essence of all the shastras.

**55.** Hearing Dube's words, filled with joy,
the lord of [our] life rose, [exclaiming]: "Sri Krishna!"[^110-14]

**56.** Dube told all this in private;
hearing those words, [Rasika] was rid of the turmoil of his mind.

**57.** Joyfully and humbly Achyuta says:
"Dube Mahashaya has made [my] son well.

**58.** I cannot repay you this debt:
today you have given Murari to me."[^110-15]

**59.** Joyfully Achyuta pays his respects to Dube:
[offering him] a bath, worship [and] feeding him sweet dishes,

**60.** giving [him] many clothes and much wealth, he humbly said:
"Mahashaya, do not leave Rasika even for a moment.

**61.** Having given the boy to you, I am free of care:
you will look after the child, [and] I have no fear."

**62.** Bowing to him, [Achyuta] took his son on his lap,
and they joyfully bathed, ate and so on.

**63.** Seeing [his] moonlike face, the fortunate Achyuta
goes about day and night [with him], holding Rasika as [his] wealth and life.

**64.** Thus, in various joys, [Rasika] lives in his own home;
day by day he became a great scholar.

**65.** The best of children became endowed with all virtues;
no one is able to answer [him] face to face.

**66.** Rasikendra-chandra is expert in all the shastras;
the host of pandits cannot establish [their own] conclusions [before him].

**67.** All the things people long to hear —
hearing [them] in that nectarean speech, they forget themselves.

**68.** Alone he examines all the shastras;
stunned, [people] by hundreds and hundreds listen without cease.

**69.** All the great scholars listen to Rasika's expositions;
no one has the power to refute [them].

**70.** Hearing the sweet explanations from that sweet mouth,
all living beings then float in bliss.

**71.** Thus day and night in the delights of learning
Rasika-chandra engages in his own home.[^110-16]

**72.** [He is] utterly detached; [his] mind does not stay at home;
from forest to forest he wanders constantly in solitude.[^110-17]

**73.** With love for Krishna [his] body is always overwhelmed;
from childhood he constantly composes songs.

**74.** In childhood he composes shlokas with love;
no one in the world can find fault [with them].

**75.** On some days, sitting alone in solitude,
he weeps incessantly with love for Krishna.

**76.** Thus in childhood bhava arises in him;
day by day his love for Krishna, full of rasa, grows.

**77.** Such is Prabhu's conduct in childhood and early boyhood:
constantly absorbed in Krishna, he weeps.[^110-18]

**78.** Sometimes he reads books, sitting in solitude;
sometimes he performs worship, absorbed in meditation.

**79.** Sometimes he composes songs in various languages;
sometimes he composes shlokas with various poetic meanings.[^110-19]

**80.** Sometimes [he holds] discussions of the shastras with everyone.
Thus [a good] while passed in childhood and early boyhood.

**81.** Adolescence, youth, maturity, old age and so on —
[through these] I shall describe a little of the nature of Rasika-Murari.

**82.** On entering adolescence, [his] form captivates the heart;
[his] beauty, surpassing Kandarpa, is lovely to see.

**83.** [His] body is always [as if] maddened by detachment;
in love for Krishna he wanders the forests without cease.

**84.** Household affairs and dealings do not please him at all;
Achyuta understood in his heart that detachment had arisen in him.

**85.** Thinking to himself of [his] marriage,
[Achyuta] carefully looks for a suitable family to ally with.[^110-20]

**86.** At that time the ruler of the land of Hijli,
Sadashiva's brother, bearing the name Balabhadra,[^110-21]

**87.** — his paternal uncle, Vibhishana Mahapatra,
always serves there in the royal retinue —

**88.** was the lord of a domain and very wealthy besides:
in the land of Hijli there was no one so fortunate.

**89.** Of valuables of many kinds — gems, diamonds, pearls, corals,
cloths surpassing gold, money — beyond counting.[^110-22]

**90.** His cows cannot be counted, his grain is beyond measure;
seeing [his] wealth, [even] the maharaja is amazed.

**91.** Thus Balabhadra Dasa lives there;
he dwells [in splendour] in the land of Hijli.

**92.** He has a daughter, most fortunate;
she is the darling of Lakshmi, very beautiful.[^110-23]

**93.** Endowed with all auspicious marks, supremely lovely;
in beauty and virtues there is no equal to her in the world.

**94.** The beauty of [her] lotus face cannot be described at all;
should Manasija see that form, [even] he is bewildered.

**95.** The beauty of every limb is most enchanting;
her gait, slow as a royal she-elephant's, is exceedingly lovely.

**96.** On all her limbs are ornaments — divine adornments;
apart from patanet silk she wears nothing else.[^110-24]

**97.** Her body is most tender, her speech soft and soft;
there is no comparison to give [for her] — [even] Ananga [is fit only] as a nichhani offering [for her].[^110-25]

**98.** Her name is renowned as Ichchha-dei Thakurani;
the Creator fashioned a girl equal to Rasika.[^110-26]

**99.** Balabhadra's daughter is endowed with every virtue;
from childhood she serves Krishna — she who [will be] devoted to her husband.

**100.** Taking along girls of her own age,
she installs a Deity of Krishna and worships [Him] with many delights.[^110-27]

**101.** At the end of the worship, bowing down, she begs a boon:
"Give me such a husband — one equal to Krishna.

**102.** Birth after birth I [will be] his maidservant always —
this is my plea at Your feet, O Lord."

**103.** Such is the renowned daughter of Balabhadra.
The account of her wedding — listen attentively.

**104.** At the order of the king of that country, Balabhadra
goes, taking the revenue and various goods.[^110-28]

**105.** In Medinipur, to the Padishah's subadar,
he came for an audience with the revenue and goods.

**106.** A lakh of rupees in arrears stands against the land of Hijli:
as soon as [the subadar] saw him, he had him taken into custody.

**107.** Balabhadra's messenger, in distress, quickly
tells everything in detail to Achyuta:

**108.** "Giving some money, [he] came for an audience with the subadar;
at the audience [the subadar] took [him] into custody because of the arrears."[^110-29]

**109.** Hearing all this, Achyuta quickly,
astonished, met with the subadar.

**110.** The subadar cannot break Achyuta's word:
once he stands [before him], he forgives tens of millions of faults.[^110-30]

**111.** He spoke to the subadar about Balabhadra's case:
"I will pay this money — release him altogether."

**112.** Hearing Achyuta's words, [the subadar] released [him] at once;
taking Balabhadra along, [Achyuta] went home.

**113.** Hand in hand the two go, [enjoying] many conversations,
and then arrived at Achyuta's abode.

**114.** He was honoured in many ways:
[served] sweet dishes to eat, [given] fine clothes to wear.

**115.** Seated on a seat, he chews betel with camphor.
At that moment Rasika comes to that place.

**116.** His curling locks of hair are tied up gracefully;
his cheeks are long, his face surpasses the full moon.

**117.** A finely shaped nose shines [between] those two eyes;
pearls glitter and shine in both ears.[^110-31]

**118.** Surpassing lightning, [gleams] the row of teeth [like] pomegranate seeds;
on his Shri face is a gentle, gentle smile — [how much] radiance!

**119.** His voice surpasses the kokila, at his beautifully red lips;
steeped in nectar are [his] half-spoken (lisping) words.

**120.** A double gold kanthi on his neck;
a coral and pearl necklace sways upon his chest.[^110-32]

**121.** On arms reaching to the knees bracelets shine;
lovely is his belly, his navel deep and radiant.

**122.** On his waist, [slimmer than] a lion's, fine cloth shines;
his two thighs appear [like] emerald pillars.

**123.** His tender feet are lovely to see;
the row of his nails glitters, enchanting.

**124.** His two lotus feet are red, redder than red dye;
with a book in hand he walks like the best of dancers.[^110-33]

**125.** A cloth, folded double, on his shoulder;
his gait slow as a lordly elephant's, his bearing beautiful.

**126.** Achyuta's son, intoxicated with love for Krishna,
went to Balabhadra and came [before him].

**127.** Seeing Rasika's form, [Balabhadra] was struck with wonder;
gazing [at him], Balabhadra fell into an ocean [of amazement].[^110-34]

**128.** Losing consciousness, he falls upon the ground;
his attendants lifted him and sprinkled water.

**129.** Coming to his senses, Balabhadra says to everyone:
"This boy is not human; he is equal to Narayana.

**130.** Nowhere in the world have I seen such a form;
a very great person — Narayana is [my] witness!"[^110-35]

**131.** "Whose son is this jewel among men?"
Everyone says, "This is Achyuta's son."

**132.** Hearing [these] wonderful words, Balabhadra Dasa
disclosed something to Achyuta:

**133.** "Listen, sir: if you consent,
I will give my daughter to your son.

**134.** A very beautiful girl, named Ichchha-dei;
in beauty and virtues she has no comparison in the world.

**135.** Your son is worthy to be that girl's husband;
she is a girl worthy of him: this is Providence's arrangement.

**136.** Seeing your son, I lost my senses:
this jewel among men is equal to Narayana.

**137.** Giving [my] daughter, I have entered your shelter;
your son is the treasure of the life of the world."

**138.** Hearing all of Balabhadra's words, Achyuta
said, "Good," and felt great joy.

**139.** Taking leave of the ruler right then,
Achyuta, coming home, showed [him] honour.[^110-36]

**140.** I will tell in detail of Rasika's wedding,
and compose some description of [his] nature.

**141.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all you devotees of Krishna:
Rasikendra is the lord of [our] life, the life of all.[^110-37]

**142.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the tenth lahari, called "Description of the Pastimes of Adolescence," in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala.*

[^110-1]: In the 1941 edition the raga is *nārānī gauṛā* (1997 ed.: *nārāṇī gauṛā*), apparently the same as *nārāyaṇī gauṛā* in lahari 7 (note 1); the ghosha (refrain) there is also the same. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of this lahari: after the heading, the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥.

[^110-2]: Durika is Shyamananda's mother (lahari 1, note 11), Bhavani is Rasikananda's mother (lahari 3). Rasikendra-chandra ("the moon among the kings of rasikas") is Rasikananda.

[^110-3]: "Reads with Hari Dube" — *paṛena haridube*; "Hari Dube reads [to him]" is also possible. Hari Dube (Haridasa Dube) is Rasika's teacher spoken of in lahari 9 (note 19). The second line is elliptical; it refers to the gopis' separation from Krishna after His departure for Mathura (Bhag. 10.39, 10.46–47).

[^110-4]: "Sobbing" — *uśasi uśasi*. The eight sattvika bhavas — see lahari 6, note 13.

[^110-5]: Mallabhumi is the region of Rasikananda's native village (lahari 3, note 6). "The lord of the realm" — *rājyera īśvara*: so the townspeople call Achyuta; in lahari 9 (38) he is called the *adhikārī* (ruler, administrator) in Mallabhumi.

[^110-6]: The number ॥ 19 ॥ is missing in the edition (the couplet stands between ॥ 18 ॥ and ॥ 20 ॥); it has been restored. In 19–26 Rasika speaks in the words of the gopis, addressing Krishna.

[^110-7]: "In hunger", "in thirst" — *bhokhe*, *śose*.

[^110-8]: "Cannot steady their hearts" — *buka nāhi bāndhe*, literally "do not bind their breasts".

[^110-9]: "Absorption" — *āveśa*: absorption in a mood (here, in the gopis' separation from Krishna). "Son" — *bālā*, "boy".

[^110-10]: Kandarpa is the god of love (Kamadeva). "Moonlike face" — the 1941 edition has the misprint *candra-bandana* for *candra-vadana* (cf. 8, 39).

[^110-11]: "Because of the glance of an evil person" — *duṣṭa loka darśana-kāraṇe*, i.e. the evil eye. "A strong wind" — *vāyu prabala*: in popular and Ayurvedic notions, a disorder of the "wind" (vata) in the body, a cause of madness, or possession by a spirit.

[^110-12]: 49–51: the "Bhagavatamrita" is Rupa Gosvami's *Laghu-bhagavatamrita*, which establishes on the evidence of the Puranas that Krishna returned to Vraja and eternally abides there. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Krishna in His original form never leaves Vrindavana (CC, Antya 1); it is His expansion Vasudeva who goes to Mathura and Dvaraka, while the pastimes in Vraja are eternal. The term of separation, "three months" (*trimāsi viraha*), is as the author has it. "The great Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa mahāśaya*.

[^110-13]: "The devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana*; read in the 1941 edition (a superscript repha). (cf. lahari 1, note 66; lahari 3, note 19). "Taken exclusive refuge" — *ananya-śaraṇa*.

[^110-14]: "The lord of [our] life" — *prāṇanātha*: so the author calls Rasika (cf. 1: "Rasikendra-chandra").

[^110-15]: Murari is Rasika-Murari, i.e. Rasikananda. "Made well" (57) — *bhāla karilena*, literally "did good".

[^110-16]: "The delights of learning" — *vidyāra vilāsa*, as in lahari 9 (41, 86–87; its title is "Description of the Delights of Learning").

[^110-17]: "In solitude" — *nigame*; from the context (cf. 75, 78), in a secluded place.

[^110-18]: Childhood (*bālya*, up to 5 years) and early boyhood (*paugaṇḍa*, 5–10 years); then (81) adolescence (*kaiśora*, 10–15 years), youth (*yauvana*), maturity (*prauṛha*) and old age (*jarā*). "Absorbed in Krishna" — *kṛṣṇāveśe*.

[^110-19]: "Composes songs" — *gīta kare* (cf. 73); "sings" is also possible. "In various languages" — *nānā bhāṣā-mate*.

[^110-20]: "A suitable family to ally with" — *yathāyogya bandhu*: a family with which to become related by marriage. Next (86 ff.) comes Balabhadra Dasa, the ruler of Hijli, and his daughter Ichchha-dei.

[^110-21]: Hijli (*hijalī maṇḍala*) is a coastal tract in the south-east of Medinipur, near the mouth of the Hooghly; *adhikārī* means a ruler or administrator (as Achyuta in Mallabhumi, lahari 9, 38). Sadashiva is Balabhadra's brother; in lahari 11, after Balabhadra's passing, he gives Balabhadra's daughter in marriage to Rasika. 86–88 form one sentence; 87 is a parenthesis about Balabhadra's uncle. Vibhishana Mahapatra is not mentioned in other sources; *mahāpātra* is a title of high officials in Utkala. "Serves in the royal retinue" — *rāja-paricchade*; possibly also "in royal attire."

[^110-22]: "Valuables" — *pāṇidravya*, literally "hand-goods"; apparently movable valuables. "Beyond counting" — *asaṅkhyalā*. The maharaja (90) is not named — perhaps the king mentioned in 104.

[^110-23]: "The darling of Lakshmi" — *lakṣmīra preyasī*: Lakshmi is the goddess of fortune and beauty, the consort of Narayana. "No equal" (93) — *nāhika paṭāntarī* (cf. 134). Manasija (94, "born of the mind") and Ananga (97, "the bodiless") are names of the god of love, Kandarpa (note 10).

[^110-24]: Patanet (*pāṭanet*) — a fine silk cloth.

[^110-25]: "As a nichhani offering" — *nichāni*: in the nichhani custom a gift is waved around a beloved's face to ward off misfortune (lahari 9, note 21); that is, even the god of love is fit only to be offered up for her beauty.

[^110-26]: Ichchha-dei (*icchādei*; the 1997 edition has *icchādevī*) — Rasikananda's future wife; in BR 15 (30) she is called Ichchha, in lahari 1 (107) Shyamadasi Thakurani (lahari 1, note 47). Thakurani is a respectful address to a lady.

[^110-27]: "A Deity of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-mūrti*. The girl's prayer (101–102) is addressed to Krishna; "O Lord" — *prabhu*. Cf. the gopis' worship of Katyayani to obtain Krishna as their husband (Bhag. 10.22).

[^110-28]: 104–106: "revenue" — *kaṛakaṛi*, as the editor explains it (*khājanā*, land tax). The king "of that country" is not named. The Padishah is the Mughal emperor; "subadar" — *subā*, here the Padishah's governor or revenue officer in Medinipur. A lakh is one hundred thousand; "rupees" — *ṭākā*. "Had him taken into custody" — *bandī karilā*.

[^110-29]: "In distress" — *ārata*, which the editor explains as *ārta*, "afflicted, alarmed." 108 gives the messenger's words; the subjects are omitted.

[^110-30]: "Once he stands [before him]" — *haile se ubhā*; *ubhā* means "standing" (the editor's gloss), that is, once Achyuta appears in person. Possibly also "if he himself stands up [for someone]." "Money" (111) — *taṅkā*.

[^110-31]: 116–125 describe Rasika's form in the traditional order "from head to foot" (*nakha-śikha*; cf. descriptions of Krishna). "Finely shaped" — *susañca*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; the meaning is unclear, translated from context. "Half-spoken words" (119) — *ādha ādha bola*, lisping, like a child's.

[^110-32]: Kanthi — a necklace fitting closely around the neck; "double" — *dosari*, of two strands. "Coral" — *pahalā*, which the editor explains as coral (*prabāla*, *palā-kā̃ṭhi*). "Fine cloth" (122) — *jhinabāsa*, explained by the editor as *sūkṣma-basana*.

[^110-33]: "Red dye" — *alakā*; apparently *alakta*, the red lac used to colour the feet. "The best of dancers" — *naṭavara*, an epithet of Krishna. "Bearing" (125) — *balani*, explained by the editor as *bhaṅgi*.

[^110-34]: "Came [before him]" (126) — *upasana*, i.e. *upasanna*, "having approached." "Fell into an ocean" — *paṛilā pāthāra*: was overwhelmed, lost his footing.

[^110-35]: 129–130 (cf. 136): Balabhadra's rapturous praise; see lahari 9, note 22: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a pure devotee and associate of Shyamananda, not Narayana Himself.

[^110-36]: The reading is clear (*nṛpa-sthāne bidāi kariyā tatakṣaṇe / gṛhe āsi' acyuta karila sanamāne*), but the sense is not: "the ruler" (*nṛpa*) is apparently Balabhadra; perhaps Achyuta sent him off with honours (gifts) according to custom. Cf. lahari 11, 2–3, where Achyuta tells his kin of the proposal.

[^110-37]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana* (note 13). Rasikendra is Rasikananda (notes 2, 14). "Description of [his] nature" (140) — *svabhāva varṇanā*; cf. 81.


## Lahari 11. Description of the Wedding Preparations

*A song in glory of Achyuta's son; Achyuta announces Balabhadra's proposal to his kin, and all prepare gifts and clean the house; Balabhadra announces to his own kin that Ichchha-dei will be Rasika's wife, and praises the bridegroom; Balabhadra's sudden passing; his brother Sadashiva, true to the given word, fixes the auspicious time with astrologers, prepares the feast, adorns the house and sends men to fetch the bridegroom; Achyuta summons his kin, and they gather*

*The eleventh lahari.*

*Raga Varadi — panchali metre.*[^111-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Krishna's qualities! To him who is full of all virtues —
glory, glory to Achyuta's son!
Treasure of the life of all, you have delivered all people —
of [your] glory I will compose [a song] a little.[^111-2]

**2.** Hearing Balabhadra's words, Achyuta, having weighed them in his mind,
spoke to everyone:
"Balabhadra Mahashaya has spoken with full certainty
about Rasika's wedding:

**3.** he has a daughter — in beauty and virtues [like] the Mother of the world;
he has given me his word [about her].
Seeing Rasika's form, he felt great happiness:
'I will surely give [him] my daughter.'[^111-3]

**4.** Listen, all you kinsmen: give your hearts to the wedding work,
prepare all the provisions.
The ruler of Hijli, the noble-minded Balabhadra,
who has wealth of lakhs and lakhs —

**5.** with such a man, by the Creator's arrangement,
a kinship has unexpectedly come about.
Prepare the provisions well, so that [our] dignity is upheld;
all of you together, make the effort."[^111-4]

**6.** Receiving Achyuta's order, all went to their places
and quickly prepared all the provisions.
What wonder in the gifts of him whose son is Rasika:
clothes and ornaments of every kind!

**7.** All the gifts and offerings, all the supplies they made ready —
of various kinds, of every sort;
the whole household cleans the house and doors,
[and] all four walls shone bright.

**8.** Then Balabhadra says, "Listen, listen, all you kinsmen,
I tell you all this news:
for Ichchha-dei, as is fitting, the bridegroom is Achyuta's son;
the Creator arranged this [match].[^111-5]

**9.** A most handsome bridegroom, enchanting in the three worlds —
is he Aja, Bhava or Narayana,
or Indra [and] the gods, or yogis such as Narada?
Seeing [this] boy, [one would say]: he is equal to Narayana.[^111-6]

**10.** Endowed with every virtue, there is none to compare [him] with;
boundless is the glory of his beauty.
Hearing the words of his Shri mouth, Brihaspati falls silent —
[he] is peerless in all the worlds.

**11.** By the good fortune of our line, or by the power of austerities,
[the Creator] has arranged such a bridegroom [for us].
Blessed, blessed is Ichchha-dei, born of a portion of Lakshmi,
whose husband is equal to Narayana!"

**12.** Calling his kinsmen, he tells them the true news:
Ichchha-dei [is the bride] of Achyuta's son.
At that time the most fortunate Balabhadra
suddenly breathed his last.[^111-7]

**13.** Then, after some days, Sadashiva, [true to] that word,
holding that promise as binding,
calling brahmana astrologers and reckoning all the auspicious times,
[resolved]: "I will give the daughter to Rasika."[^111-8]

**14.** Sadashiva, telling everyone all about it,
gave orders: "Take charge of the provisions:
curd, milk, ghee and the like, gur, guya, rice and the like;
bring cloths of many kinds.

**15.** Supplies of sweets and ghee — prepare them in great variety:
pitha, laru, bananas of every sort."
Royal dishes as gifts they prepared in many kinds,
in due order, according to their means.[^111-9]

**16.** They made the house and courtyard bright, laid jhunti-alipana,
drew mandalas in various forms.
Pictures of many kinds on the walls the bands of young women painted;
they adorned [all] with canopies of patanet silk.[^111-10]

**17.** Sadashiva Mahashaya says very humbly,
having reckoned the auspicious moment (lagna),
to two or four of his own people [and] two or four brahmanas:
"Bring the bridegroom," he says again and again.

**18.** "The bridegroom, Achyuta's son — go and bring him quickly,
having fixed the auspicious moment.
Go there with haste, bring Rasika here,
so that he enters [here] at that [appointed] time.[^111-11]

**19.** At Achyuta's place, all of you, speak humbly,
[asking him] to send his son:
'Having given our daughter to your son, we have taken shelter in you at heart' —
tell [him] the whole account."

**20.** Receiving Sadashiva's order, all went there
and told Achyuta [the whole] account.
Hearing all this, [Achyuta] attended to all
his kinsmen, wherever they were.[^111-12]

**21.** To all they gave gur and guya — to every house,
as custom prescribes.
They invited all — each and every person —
to Rasika's wedding.[^111-13]

**22.** Hearing [this], all the kinsfolk set out in haste
to celebrate Rasika's wedding.
Hearing, all came joyfully with [their] families,
having fitted out horses and litters in various ways.[^111-14]

**23.** Listen, listen, devotees of Krishna: the description of Rasika's wedding
I have composed as is fitting.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^111-15]

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eleventh lahari, called "Description of the Wedding Preparations".*

[^111-1]: Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; cf. lahari 8, note 2). "Panchali metre" (*pāñcālī chanda*) is tripadi; each stanza is set in four lines in the edition and translated likewise (cf. lahari 5, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition.

[^111-2]: "Glory to Krishna's qualities" — *jaya jaya kṛṣṇaguṇa*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition, as at the beginning of lahari 9 (note 3 there); possibly also "glory [to him who has] Krishna's qualities, full of all virtues." The address "you have delivered all people" (*uddhārile sarvajana*) is to Achyuta's son, Rasikananda.

[^111-3]: "The Mother of the world" — *jaganmātā*, an epithet of Lakshmi (or Durga); here, praise of the girl's beauty. "Has given me his word" — *bākyadatta kaila*: has promised to give his daughter in marriage (*vāg-dāna*, betrothal by word). 2–3 are Achyuta's words reporting Balabhadra's speech; Achyuta's speech runs to 5.

[^111-4]: "Kinship" — *bandhupaṇa*, relationship by marriage. "So that [our] dignity is upheld" — *mahatādi rahe yāte*, literally "so that greatness and the like remain." On Hijli and Balabhadra see lahari 10, note 21.

[^111-5]: "As is fitting" — *anukrama*, literally "in order, correspondingly"; the sense of the line is unclear and is translated from context. In 8–11 Balabhadra speaks to his own kin in Hijli.

[^111-6]: Aja is Brahma, Bhava is Shiva; Narada is the divine sage; Brihaspati (10) is the preceptor of the gods, a model of eloquence; "falls silent" — *tuni*, explained by the editor as *mauna*. The comparisons with Narayana (9, 11) and "a portion of Lakshmi" (11) are Balabhadra's rapturous praise (cf. lahari 9, note 22; lahari 10, note 35): according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a pure devotee and associate of Shyamananda, not Narayana Himself.

[^111-7]: "Breathed his last" — *prāṇatyāga*, literally "the giving up of the life-breath."

[^111-8]: Sadashiva is Balabhadra's brother (lahari 10, 86). "Holding as binding" — *pramāṇa kariyā*. "Astrologers" — *doibajña*, i.e. *daivajña*.

[^111-9]: Gur is unrefined cane sugar; guya (*guyā*) is areca nut; by custom gur and guya are sent to relatives with a wedding invitation (cf. 21). Pitha are rice cakes, laru are sweet balls. "Royal dishes" — *rājabhoga*.

[^111-10]: "Jhunti-alipana" — *jhũṭi ālipanā*: designs in rice paste on the floor and in the courtyard (in Utkala, *jhoṭi*, *jhuṭi*). "Mandalas" — *maṇḍalī*, circular designs. "On the walls" — *kā̃the*. Patanet is a fine silk cloth (lahari 10, note 24); "canopies" — *candrātapa*.

[^111-11]: The lagna is the auspicious moment reckoned by the astrologers; the bridegroom must arrive by it. "Two or four" (17) — *dui cāri*, i.e. a few.

[^111-12]: The second half of the stanza is elliptical: *śuniyā e saba kathā, bandhuvarga yathā yathā, sabākāre karila yatana* — apparently Achyuta summoned all his kin; cf. 21: the invitation sent to the kin with gur and guya.

[^111-13]: Gur and guya (*guṛa guyā*) — unrefined sugar and areca nut, which by custom are sent to relatives together with a wedding invitation (note 9). "As custom prescribes" — *yathāvidhi āchaye pramāṇa*.

[^111-14]: "With [their] families" — *sakuṭumbe*. "Litters" — *dolā*.

[^111-15]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana* (lahari 10, note 13). "The description of the wedding" — *vibhā varṇana*; the 1997 edition has *vibhā āyojana*, "the wedding preparations" (cf. the title of the lahari). The author's signature (the second half of the stanza) is given in the standard formula; in the tripadi metre it runs: "Making the holy feet of Shyamananda the ornament on his head, the son of Rasamaya sings" (cf. lahari 5, note 14).


## Lahari 12. Description of the Wedding

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; Rasika's wedding procession, with brahmanas, kinsfolk, gifts and music, goes to Hijli, and on the way all marvel at the bridegroom's beauty; Sadashiva receives the guests, adorns the house and the wedding pavilion and lights countless lamps; Rasika is dressed as a bridegroom and goes in procession to the pavilion, where the brahmanas bless him; the adorning of the bride Ichchha-dei, the wedding rite and the dowry; the return home, Achyuta's joy and the feasting of the kinsfolk*

*The twelfth lahari.*

*Raga Suhi.*[^112-1]
*Ghosha: "What shall I say of the beauty of Gopala's moon-like face?*
*It captivates the hearts of all the women of Vraja."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the friend of the afflicted!
Glory, glory to Rasikananda, the ocean of mercy!

**2.** At that time, by Achyuta's order, the kinsfolk —
all set out, taking Rasika with them.

**3.** Having reckoned an auspicious day and an auspicious moment,
Achyuta's son set out to be married.

**4.** Brahmanas versed in the Vedas they all took along;
the astrologer, the barber, the washerman and others go with [them].[^112-2]

**5.** All the kinsfolk, mounted on horses and in litters —
near ones, friends, bhattacharyas, mahatas and others.[^112-3]

**6.** With them, hundreds upon hundreds of loads with various gifts:
fried dishes, sweets, laddus — of many kinds.[^112-4]

**7.** Cloths of many sorts, ornaments of many kinds;
with them music and dundubhis of many kinds.

**8.** Dhol, dhak, pahara, mridanga, karatalas,
upanga, muraja, dampha — delightful music.

**9.** Tamaka, dogiri, gijighosha in abundance;
madal, murali, banshi, beautiful shanais.

**10.** Muchanga, karatalas, venu — instruments [sounding] in many ways;
at the sound of the music the earth quakes and trembles.[^112-5]

**11.** Having decked out palanquins in many ways,
Rasikendra set out to be married.[^112-6]

**12.** In royal attire all the companions go,
again and again [raising] the thunder of music and dundubhis.

**13.** Hearing, hundreds upon hundreds of people go to see;
seeing the moon-like face, all forget themselves.

**14.** Hearing [his] sweet words, all are enchanted;
no one has the heart to go away.

**15.** All say: "In what village did this man live?
Seeing all [his] marks, [he] is equal to Narayana.[^112-7]

**16.** In a human being we have never seen such a form;
once one sees [this] sweet form, the eyes cannot slip away."

**17.** Thus all go along the road praising [him];
seeing Rasika's form, all are enchanted.

**18.** At that time [the procession] entered the neighbourhood of Hijli;
a messenger went and quickly told Sadashiva.[^112-8]

**19.** Hearing [this], Sadashiva summoned the kinsfolk
and sent them all to fetch the bridegroom.

**20.** Going some distance, all saw Rasika;
seeing Rasika's form, they are charmed at heart.

**21.** All say: "Ichchha-devi is most fortunate:
the bridegroom in beauty and virtues is as if equal to Vishnu."[^112-9]

**22.** Praising [him], they quickly came, bringing the bridegroom;
all entered the town of Hijli.

**23.** Hearing of the greatness of Sri Rasika's beauty,
all run to see — there is no limit to it.

**24.** Seeing [his] sweet form, [people] forget themselves;
all the people praise Balabhadra:

**25.** "Blessed is Balabhadra, blessed is your daughter:
by great austerities [she] has obtained Achyuta's son!"[^112-10]

**26.** Seeing Rasika, all are in an ocean of bliss;
no one even thinks of going away.

**27.** At that time Sadashiva, delighted,
gave all of them lodging, bringing [them] to a fine house.

**28.** Preparing all the provisions as prescribed,
he sent [them] with hundreds of porters.

**29.** Calling astrologer brahmanas, [he] fixed the auspicious lagna
and adorned the house like a city of the gods.[^112-11]

**30.** Making the house, courtyard and pavilion beautiful,
they decked [them] with patanet of many colours.[^112-12]

**31.** Diamonds, sapphires, corals, pearls hang from it in tassels;
and hundreds upon hundreds of chamaras sway [in the air].[^112-13]

**32.** Flags, arches and the like shine on all sides;
they adorned the house on all sides with various paintings.

**33.** Golden pitchers shine on the verandas;
the place, like Vaikuntha, is beautiful to see.[^112-14]

**34.** Setting up a pitcher in the middle of the pavilion,
the brahmanas versed in the Vedas sat on the four sides.

**35.** Hundreds upon hundreds of kinsmen sat on all sides;
the notables sat right beside them.[^112-15]

**36.** On spreads of Bhot blankets, coloured carpets and mats
[the guests] sat in great assemblies.[^112-16]

**37.** Of lamps and torches there is no counting;
millions upon millions of blazing chandrodayas burn there.

**38.** Of lamps, lanterns and rockets there is no number;
millions upon millions of chandrabanas, millions of bhumichampas.

**39.** Kanakachampas and others shine in so many ways;
in the markets, on the roads, in the courtyards they burn in rows.[^112-17]

**40.** All around the pavilion there burn, beyond counting,
trees of white wax, most brilliant.

**41.** For four praharas those trees burn;
night became day in all those places.

**42.** Thus hundreds upon hundreds of wax trees burn;
they made [everything] brighter than day.[^112-18]

**43.** The supreme beauty [that met] the eye cannot be described:
pavilion, house and courtyard are arrayed with flowers.

**44.** Stringing various fragrant flowers into garlands,
on all sides — moon-garlands, flowers hanging in tassels.[^112-19]

**45.** With flowers they adorned the pavilion and the courtyard;
[all] surpassed ten million moons — it became [like] moonlight.

**46.** The extraordinary beauty cannot be told;
it seems as if Vaikuntha had risen.

**47.** Quickly adorning the place of the wedding,
everywhere they perform the family customs as prescribed.

**48.** All those festivities cannot be told even with a hundred mouths;
in brief I have given some account of the wedding.

**49.** At that time, fixing the lagna at the auspicious moment,
Sadashiva, taking all the kinsfolk with him,

**50.** having completed the proper rites — the adhivasa and the rest,
as many as there are according to the Vedas — came quickly.[^112-20]

**51.** Beside the wedding pavilion Sadashiva Dasa,
with all his kin, [is] in joy and jubilation.

**52.** All the kinsfolk sat in their places;
all accepted betel with camphor.

**53.** At that time the astrologer quickly announces:
"The lagna is most auspicious [now] to bring the bridegroom."[^112-21]

**54.** Hearing [this], Sadashiva, greatly delighted,
ordered everyone: "Go and bring the bridegroom."

**55.** Hearing, the whole kin, rejoicing,
taking music, dundubhis and the rest with them,

**56.** all came to where Rasika [was]
and said: "In the auspicious lagna, please set out."

**57.** Hearing, the companions quickly dressed [him]
and put various ornaments on every limb.[^112-22]

**58.** On the long cheeks they applied kunkuma and sandal;
in the midst of it, a dot of phagu, most beautiful.

**59.** The finely curling hair, which conquers the town-ladies, they tie up;
they adorn it with a fragrant garland of flowers.[^112-23]

**60.** With care they tie a turban of tansuk;
on it they fastened a crown, a golden ornament.[^112-24]

**61.** Diamonds, sapphires, corals, pearls — in the middle of the crown;
rubies, little mirrors — the radiance sparkles and glitters.

**62.** Various fragrant flowers are arranged in rows;
seeing the crown, all people are enchanted.

**63.** That captivating crown they placed on [his] head;
the beauty of [his] Sri moon-like face has no comparison.

**64.** Millions upon millions of moons are given as nichhani for that face;
by beauty, virtues and words he enchanted all living beings.[^112-25]

**65.** The jewelled pendants of the crown swing at the sides;
in the rays of the jewels the face shines like the moon.

**66.** In the eyes, lines of kajal, beautiful to see;
the two eyes are more restless than the wagtail.[^112-26]

**67.** The nose, surpassing the sesame flower, is beautiful to see;
the teeth surpass [pomegranate seeds], the lips are of a lovely red.

**68.** On them the colour of betel, most captivating;
a face with a gentle, gentle smile, a beautiful glance.

**69.** The brows are shaped surpassing Kama's bow;
the fine hairs on them shine like bees.[^112-27]

**70.** In both ears shine strings of gold and pearls;
on them shine various gems, [like] bright lightning.

**71.** On the neck, [mighty as] an elephant's shoulder, shines a double golden necklace;
on the chest shines a pendant, most captivating.[^112-28]

**72.** Various precious stones, gems and pearls, strung in rows,
encircle the pendant on the chest, shining beautifully.

**73.** On the arms reaching to the knees — keyuras and bracelets;
the arms, like lotus stalks, are most beautiful.[^112-29]

**74.** On both arms — armlets studded with various gems;
[his] body makes the ornaments shine.

**75.** The deep, lovely navel graces the belly;
the line of fine hairs and the three folds shine upon it.

**76.** On the slender waist shines fine cloth;
they wrapped [him] in a silk shawl — a yellow cloth.[^112-30]

**77.** At the waist they tied a silk garment tightly;
those hips and the pair of thighs enchant the three worlds.

**78.** On the very tender feet shines the row of nails;
the lines of red lac on them shine in various ways.[^112-31]

**79.** Seeing that form, the people of the world are enchanted in mind;
a silk cloth encircling the body shines on the left shoulder.

**80.** On the dark, beautiful body — kunkuma and sandal;
by the radiance of [his] body the three worlds were lit up.

**81.** On the feet — finely painted wooden sandals, captivating to see;
Rasika-shekhara was arrayed in a bridegroom's attire.[^112-32]

**82.** Holding a karajagya in his hand, with the gait of a king of elephants,
Rasikendra set out to be married.[^112-33]

**83.** Quickly seating himself in a palanquin at [his] lodging,
all in royal attire go slowly, slowly.

**84.** At the thunder of music and dundubhis the ground trembles;
with chandrodayas and torches the night is bright.

**85.** In one place — various instruments of various kinds;
in another place they recite poetry again and again.

**86.** In one place the brahmanas chant the Vedas;
in another — the "Bharata," the Puranas, the "Ramayana."[^112-34]

**87.** Somewhere there is sankirtana, and cries of "Hari!" resound;
somewhere the sound of shinga and vishana horns is heard.[^112-35]

**88.** Somewhere cowherds twirl their staffs;
somewhere women dance to various instruments.[^112-36]

**89.** Somewhere [they perform] raut-sharana in various ways;
somewhere they set horses galloping, herd after herd.[^112-37]

**90.** Somewhere all the people watch various amusements;
somewhere wrestlers wrestle in various ways.

**91.** Somewhere shield-bearers clash with one another;
the young men all jostle in the crowd.[^112-38]

**92.** Musicians from various kingdoms came at [his] order;
with music [playing] in rivalry the earth surged.[^112-39]

**93.** As many people as live in the town of Hijli —
rulers and subjects — all came to see the wedding.

**94.** In the markets, on the roads, in the courtyards, on the roofs of houses —
the people are beyond counting; it is very crowded.[^112-40]

**95.** Drop a mustard seed — it would never fall to the ground;
all say, "We have never seen such a wedding!"[^112-41]

**96.** With various festivities [they] arrived at the wedding pavilion;
in various ways chandrodayas light it up.

**97.** Surrounding the pavilion sit brahmanas versed in the Vedas;
all perform homa and yajna with care.

**98.** At this time Rasikendra, from the palanquin,
in beautifully painted wooden sandals stepped down onto the ground.[^112-42]

**99.** Standing beneath the pavilion, Rasikendra
joyfully bowed to the twice-born.

**100.** All the twice-born gave [him] their blessing:
"Bestowing devotion to Krishna, deliver the three worlds!"

**101.** Seeing Rasika's form, all were filled with bliss —
the rulers and the subjects and the host of twice-born;

**102.** children and old men and throngs upon throngs of women —
seeing Rasika's form, all [were] amazed.

**103.** All say, "Where has this man been living?
We see that by all [his] marks [he] is equal to Narayana."[^112-43]

**104.** How [lovely] that dark body, the soft, soft smile!
Tens of millions of moons offer themselves in ransom for this face.[^112-44]

**105.** How [lovely] the curve of these brows, the dance of the eyes!
How [lovely] that sweet smile that colours the lips!

**106.** The arms reaching to the knees — how [lovely] their swaying!
By the radiance of [his] body the earth was enchanted.

**107.** Such a form of the best of dancers we have never seen;
to see that form hundreds of eyes come running.

**108.** Blessed, fortunate is Balabhadra's daughter:
as the fruit of many austerities she has obtained such a husband.

**109.** Thus all the people, seeing Rasika,
like bees, surrounded [him] by the hundreds.[^112-45]

**110.** Seeing [his] Shri moon-like face, they gladden their eyes;
all those places came to surpass Vaikuntha.

**111.** Seeing [him], all the people are amazed;
all say, "What avatara is this man?"

**112.** Around the pavilion all sit on four sides:
kinsmen, close ones [and] Sadashiva Dasa.

**113.** Beside them sat all the twice-born;
setting up the auspicious pot, they perform the puja in due order.[^112-46]

**114.** Homa, yajna, service — all according to the injunctions;
[they keep] the family customs, whichever are known for each.[^112-47]

**115.** Swiftly performing one after another according to the rules,
after the varana of the bridegroom they seat the bridegroom on [his place] in the pavilion.[^112-48]

**116.** On a coloured mat — a bed of a coloured blanket;
over it they spread a covering of fine cloth.[^112-49]

**117.** On it sat the bridegroom Rasika-shekhara;
on all four sides — cries of "Jaya!" and loud music.

**118.** The women [raise] hulahuli; the conches sound again and again;
amid the roar of the music and the dundubhis nothing can be heard.

**119.** Hundreds of shahnai players perform the auspicious wedding songs;
cries of "Hari!", the sound of the Vedas — a mighty din.[^112-50]

**120.** The priest, gladly taking the book in hand,
performs one after another the Vedic injunctions and the family customs.[^112-51]

**121.** The Vedic injunctions, the family customs, homa, yajna and the rest;
setting up the auspicious pot, [they perform] the puja according to the injunctions.

**122.** The brahmanas ordered that the bride be brought;
hearing [this], the close ones rose and went to the inner apartments.[^112-52]

**123.** They said, "Quickly dress the bride!
Rasika is seated in the pavilion — he will not suffer delay."[^112-53]

**124.** Hearing [this], the women began to dress [her];
they anointed the body of the golden-complexioned [girl] with kunkuma and sandalwood.[^112-54]

**125.** On her head, at the parting, a braid beautifully adorned with jewels;
seeing the moon of [her] face, the full moon was put to shame.

**126.** The line of musk tilaka on her forehead
glitters, surpassing the new moon.

**127.** Her brows are lovely, surpassing Kama's bow;
on them — curls that attract swarms of bees.[^112-55]

**128.** The "chakshu-rakhi" placed in her eyes flashes like lightning;
in her nose, [like] a sesame flower, a pearl glitters.[^112-56]

**129.** The beauty of her two lips surpasses the bandhuli;
her row of teeth — kunda buds, its gleam [like] a creeper of lightning.[^112-57]

**130.** Surpassing [gold] of tenfold purity, golden earrings shine in her ears;
on her chin a dot of musk, on her neck ornaments.[^112-58]

**131.** On her neck various jewels blaze — diamonds, corals, pearls;
on her breast a necklace sways, its radiance shimmering.

**132.** On her arms golden taras, on her wrists golden bangles,
armlets, golden bracelets, golden rings.[^112-59]

**133.** Her breasts, [like] pitchers, are lovely; the line of fine hair — [a row of] bees;
slender-waisted, on her waist three folds shine.

**134.** On her, a yellow garment and a precious veil;
her knees and shanks are lovely, shapely to behold.[^112-60]

**135.** On her feet golden anklets, golden pashulis;
in the nails of her feet a hundred thousand moons glitter.[^112-61]

**136.** Dressing her in various ways, [adorning her] with various flower garlands,
her friends arrayed Balabhadra's daughter.[^112-62]

**137.** Descended as a portion of Lakshmi, Ichchha of the pata line —
therefore birth after birth [she is] Rasika's beloved.[^112-63]

**138.** Having thus dressed the bride, the close ones
brought [her] to the place in the pavilion and performed the varana.[^112-64]

**139.** Taking [her] on their laps, the elders quickly sat down;
the twice-born [perform] homa and yajna according to the Vedic injunctions.

**140.** Performing one after another the Vedic injunctions and the family customs,
they then joyfully gave the bride to Rasika.

**141.** Joining their hands and so on, they seated [her] beside [him];
it seemed as if [they were] Lakshmi and Narayana — the portion and [He who] possesses the portions.[^112-65]

**142.** To behold [it] was supreme beauty, most enchanting;
seeing [their] form, all the people rejoiced at heart.

**143.** Divine food, clothes and the like, loads of jewels
he gave as dowry — of very many kinds.[^112-66]

**144.** Thus, having celebrated the wedding with many joys,
having stayed there some days, having asked leave to depart,

**145.** having performed there the ashtamangala and the rest with many joys,
at an auspicious moment Rasika departed for home.[^112-67]

**146.** Rasika-shekhara came to his own house;
unceasingly [his] body is overwhelmed with love for Krishna.

**147.** In the bliss of Krishna [tears] flow from his eyes in a hundred streams;
unceasingly he chants the name of Hari in seclusion.[^112-68]

**148.** Seeing Rasika-chandra's face
[and] seeing the bride, Achyuta rejoiced greatly.

**149.** Greeting the kinsmen, the mahashaya
fed them all with dishes of six tastes.[^112-69]

**150.** Keeping them all some days, he bade [them] farewell;
to all he gave food, clothes, ornaments.

**151.** Such is the joy of Rasika's wedding;
whoever hears [it] with faith, the bonds of worldly existence fall away.

**152.** Listen to "Rasika-mangala", all you friends:
Achyuta's son is the friend of all, hard to attain.[^112-70]

**153.** Listen to the nectar of his lilas, leaving other talk:
the one who hears, Krishna delivers without fail.

**154.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^112-71]

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the twelfth lahari, called "Description of the Wedding".*

[^112-1]: The raga in the 1941 edition is *śuhī*, apparently the same as *suhī* (Suhi) in lahari 6 (note 2); there too is the same ghosha (refrain), whose translation is repeated here. Gopala ("the little cowherd") is Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of this lahari: after the heading, the raga and the ghosha, the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥.

[^112-2]: "To be married" (3; cf. 11, 82) — *vibhā haite*. The astrologer (*daivajña*) fixes the auspicious moment of the rite; the barber and the washerman (*nāpita*, *rajaka*) by custom take part in the wedding rites.

[^112-3]: "Litters" — *dolā*. Bhattacharyas are learned brahmanas; mahatas (*mahata*) are respected men, headmen (in Utkala and Medinipur also a hereditary title). "Near ones, friends" — *iṣṭa mitra*.

[^112-4]: "Loads" — *bhāra*: a load on a carrying pole borne by a porter (*bhārī*, 28). "Fried dishes" — *pakvānna*, food cooked in ghee; laddus are sweet balls.

[^112-5]: 8–10 are a list of instruments. The dundubhi is a large kettledrum (lahari 3, note 26); the dhol and dhak are large drums; the mridanga and muraja are clay drums; karatalas (*karatāla*, *karttāla*) are hand cymbals; the dampha is a frame drum; the madal is a double-headed drum of Utkala and Medinipur; murali, banshi and venu are flutes; the shanai (*sāhāni*) is a wind instrument like an oboe (lahari 7, note 4); the upanga (*upāṅga*) is a wind instrument known from descriptions of kirtana; the muchanga (*mucaṅga*) is apparently a jew's harp. Pahara (*pahaṛā*), tamaka (*ṭamaka*), dogiri (*dogiṛī*), gijighosha (*gijīghoṣa*): the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, but the instruments cannot be identified with certainty (apparently various drums). "Delightful music" — *saṅgīta rasāla*.

[^112-6]: "Palanquins" — *sukupāla*, which the edition's gloss explains as *pālkī*, palanquin (also 83, 98).

[^112-7]: "Marks" — *lakṣaṇa*: bodily signs by which a great personality is recognised (cf. 73: arms reaching to the knees). On the rapturous comparisons of Rasika with Narayana and Vishnu (15, 21) see lahari 10, note 35: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a pure devotee and associate of Shyamananda, not Narayana Himself.

[^112-8]: "A messenger went and quickly told Sadashiva" — *sadāśiva dūta giyā kahila satvare*; possibly also "Sadashiva's messenger went and told [him]." Sadashiva is Balabhadra's brother (lahari 10, note 21), who after Balabhadra's passing gives his daughter in marriage to Rasika (lahari 11).
