[^112-9]: Ichchha-devi (*icchādevī*) is Ichchha-dei, Balabhadra's daughter (lahari 10, note 26; lahari 11, 8–12).

[^112-10]: By this time Balabhadra had already departed from this world (lahari 11, 12); the people praise him and address him (25) — so in the author. "By great austerities" — *bahu tapasyāya*, literally "by many austerities" (cf. lahari 10, 99–102: from childhood the girl prayed to Krishna for such a husband).

[^112-11]: The lagna is the auspicious time of a rite, reckoned by the rising sign. "Adorned" — *maṇḍalī karila*: decked out, painted with patterns (cf. 45, 47).

[^112-12]: Patanet (*pāṭaneta*) — a fine silk cloth (lahari 10, note 24).

[^112-13]: "Sapphires" — *līlā*: so in the 1941 edition (also in 61, and in the 1997 edition), apparently for *nīlā*, "sapphire." "In tassels" — *jhārā*. Chamaras are yak-tail whisks.

[^112-14]: "Verandas" — *piṛā*, which the edition's gloss explains as *bārāndā*. Vaikuntha is the spiritual abode of Narayana.

[^112-15]: "Notables" — *mahājana*: eminent, respected men (also "merchants, moneylenders").

[^112-16]: "Bhot blankets" — *bhoṭa kambala*, woollen blankets from Bhot (Tibet, Bhutan). "Mats" — *masinā*, which the edition's gloss explains as *machalanda mādura*, a fine mat (masland). "In great assemblies" — *baṛa baṛa jamā*: *jamā* (Persian) means "gathering, assembly"; possibly "men of rank"; the meaning is unclear.

[^112-17]: 37–39: the deuti is a lamp on a stand; the chandrodaya, by the edition's gloss, is "a particular kind of lamp" (lahari 3, note 26); haui (*hāui*) are rockets; the chandrabana, by the edition's gloss, is "a particular kind of firework"; bhumichampa and kanakachampa (*bhūmicampā*, *kanakacāmpā*) are apparently ground fireworks that scatter sparks resembling champaka flowers. "In rows" — *pā̃ti pā̃ti*, glossed by the edition as *sāri sāri*.

[^112-18]: 40–42: "trees of white wax," "wax trees" (*momera vṛkṣa*, *mombṛkṣa*) — apparently tree-shaped candelabra holding white wax candles. A prahara is a watch of about three hours.

[^112-19]: "Into garlands" — *kerā kerā*: the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the meaning conjectural ("in bunches, in clusters"). "Moon-garlands" — *cā̃da-mālā*, apparently round wreaths of flowers.

[^112-20]: The adhivasa is a preliminary rite on the eve or on the day of the wedding (anointing and blessing of the bride and bridegroom).

[^112-21]: "The astrologer" — in the 1941 edition *doibajña*, a variant spelling of *daivajña* (as in lahari 5, note 2; cf. 29). "To bring the bridegroom" — to the bride in the wedding pavilion.

[^112-22]: "Put on" — *khũjilena*: so in the 1941 edition (and in the 1997 edition), literally "searched"; apparently for *guṃjilena*, "inserted, fastened." Possibly also "chose various ornaments for every limb."

[^112-23]: "Which conquers the town-ladies" — *nāgarī dalana*, literally "crushing the nagaris (town-ladies, beloveds)"; the sense is conjectural.

[^112-24]: Tansuk (*tanasuka*, cf. Persian *tansukh*) — a fine cloth (muslin); the edition's gloss has *cūṛā*, "crest, crown [of the turban]." "Turban" — *pāga*.

[^112-25]: "Given as nichhani" — *nichāni*: the nichhani custom (lahari 9, note 21; lahari 10, note 25).

[^112-26]: Kajal is the collyrium used to line the eyes. The wagtail (*khañjana*) is in Indian poetry a standard comparison for lively, restless eyes; the sesame flower (67), for a beautiful nose.

[^112-27]: Kama is the god of love (Kandarpa). "Like bees" — *ali paramāṇa*, literally "of the measure of bees": the dark hairs of the brows are compared to rows of bees.

[^112-28]: "An elephant's shoulder" — *gaja-skandha*: mighty shoulders and neck are a sign of a great man. "Double necklace" — *dosarī*, of two strands (cf. lahari 10, note 32); "pendant" — *padaka*.

[^112-29]: Arms "reaching to the knees" (*ājānulambita*) are a sign of a great personality. Keyuras are bracelets worn on the upper arm; "armlets" (74) — *bājubandha*; "studded" — *jhā̃pā*.

[^112-30]: "Fine cloth" — *jhinabāsa* (lahari 10, note 32); "shawl" — *pāchaṛi*, a wrap, a covering cloth.

[^112-31]: "Red lac" — *alakā*, i.e. *alakta* (cf. lahari 10, note 33).

[^112-32]: "Wooden sandals" — *kaṭhā̃u*, which the edition's gloss explains as *khaṛama* (cf. lahari 6, note 3). "Finely painted" — *suraṅga*, "beautifully coloured." Rasika-shekhara ("the crown of rasikas") is Rasikananda.

[^112-33]: "Karajagya" — *karajāgya*: the reading in the 1941 edition is clear, the meaning has not been established; apparently an object that the bridegroom by custom holds in his hand (in the 1997 edition the line is illegible). The gait of a king of elephants is stately and slow.

[^112-34]: The "Bharata" is the Mahabharata.

[^112-35]: Sankirtana — congregational singing of the holy names. Shinga and vishana are horns (lahari 4, note 19).

[^112-36]: "Twirl their staffs" — *laguṛī phirāya*: the cowherds (*gopa*) display their skill with the staff.

[^112-37]: Raut-sharana (*rāuta śaraṇa*) — according to the edition's gloss, "songs or praises of a particular caste"; the rautas (*rāuta*) of Utkala and Medinipur are a caste of horsemen and soldiers. "Set galloping" — *dhābāyena*; "herd after herd" — *yūthe yūthe*.

[^112-38]: "Shield-bearers" — *ḍhāli*, men with shields who give display fights (*melāmeli*, "clash with one another"). "Young men" — *bayesiyā*, "those of the same age"; "jostle" — *pelāpeli*.

[^112-39]: "In rivalry" — *bādābādi*, "competing, outdoing one another".

[^112-40]: "Beyond counting" — *samuccaya nāhi*, lit. "there is no reckoning"; "crowded" — *gahala*, "thronged, a press of people".

[^112-41]: A mustard seed that cannot fall to the ground is a common figure for a dense crowd.

[^112-42]: The palanquin (*sukupāla*) and the wooden sandals (*suraṅga kaṭhā̃u*) — notes 6 and 32.

[^112-43]: Cf. 15 and note 7: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a pure devotee, a companion of Shyamananda, not Narayana Himself; so also the rapturous question "what avatara" in 111.

[^112-44]: "Offer themselves in ransom" — *nichāni*: the nichhani rite (note 25).

[^112-45]: "Surrounded [him] by the hundreds" — *beṛi śata pure*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; *pure* may be understood as "fill" or as "from hundreds of villages"; the rendering is tentative.

[^112-46]: The auspicious pot (*maṅgala-ghaṭa*) — a water-filled pitcher set up for the rite (cf. 34); also 121.

[^112-47]: "Yajna" — the 1941 edition has *sajña*, a misprint for *yajña* (so in the 1997 edition). "Service" — *paricaryā*. "Family customs" — *kulācāra*.

[^112-48]: "After the varana" — *bariyā*: varana is the rite of honourably receiving the bridegroom (gifts, washing of the feet, etc.), after which he is led to his place; cf. 138.

[^112-49]: "Mat" — *masinā* (note 16). "Fine cloth" — *jhinapatri*, according to the edition's gloss, "fine cloth" (cf. *jhinabāsa*, note 30).

[^112-50]: Hulahuli — the women's auspicious cry (lahari 4, note 12). "Shahnai players" — *sāhaniyā*, apparently players of the shahnai (*sāhāni*, note 5); the verb is *gāya*, "sing". "Auspicious wedding songs" — *vibhāra maṅgala*. "A mighty din" — *ghana utarola*.

[^112-51]: The priest — *purohita*, the family priest conducting the rite; "the book" — *pũthi*, the manuscript of the ritual manual.

[^112-52]: "The brahmanas ordered" — *vipragaṇe ājñā dila*. "Inner apartments" — *antaḥpura*, the women's quarters of the house.

[^112-53]: "Delay" — *biyāja*.

[^112-54]: "Golden-complexioned [girl]" — *gaurāṅgī*, "of golden (fair) body", said of the bride; the 1997 edition has *gaurāṅgī āge*.

[^112-55]: "Curls" — *alakāvalī*, ringlets above the brows; "that attract swarms of bees" — *alikula-lobhā*.

[^112-56]: "Chakshu-rakhi" — *cakṣu rākhi*: so in the 1941 edition (enlarged) and in the 1997 edition; apparently kajal (collyrium), lit. "guardian of the eyes"; possibly also "placing [kajal] in the eyes, [they] flash like lightning". The reading is unclear. The sesame flower is a figure for a beautiful nose (note 26).

[^112-57]: Bandhuli (*bandhuli*, Skt. *bandhūka*) — according to the edition's gloss, the "chauddaghari" flower and the [red] telakucha fruit; a red flower to which lips are compared. Kunda — white jasmine. "Creeper of lightning" — *vidyullatā*.

[^112-58]: "[Gold] of tenfold purity" — *daśabāṇa*: *bāṇa*, *bāṇī* is a measure of the purity of gold; the rendering is tentative. "Golden earrings" — *svarṇakāpa*, according to the edition's gloss, "an ear ornament".

[^112-59]: Taras (*tāṛa*) — bracelets worn on the upper arm; "armlets" — *bājubandha* (note 29); "bracelets" — *bālā*; "rings" — *mudarī*, according to the edition's gloss, "ring".

[^112-60]: "Veil" — *uṛayāni*, an upper wrap or veil. "Shapely" — *suṭhāni*.

[^112-61]: Pashulis (*pāśuli*) — foot ornaments, apparently toe-rings.

[^112-62]: "Her friends" — *sakhāgaṇe*, lit. "friends"; read in the 1941 edition.

[^112-63]: "Of the pata line" — *pāṭa vaṃśī*: so in the 1941 edition (enlarged) and in the 1997 edition; the meaning is unclear: possibly "of the chief (noble) line" (*pāṭa* — "throne, chief seat") or the name of a family. Ichchha-dei, Rasikananda's wife, is called "Ichchha" in the "Bhakti-ratnakara" as well (taranga 15). That she is a portion of Lakshmi and Rasika's eternal beloved birth after birth is the author's view, as is the comparison of the couple with Lakshmi and Narayana (141); cf. note 43.

[^112-64]: "Varana" — *baraṇa*: here the rite of honourably receiving the bride in the pavilion (cf. 115).

[^112-65]: "Gave the bride" (140) — *kanyā samarpila*, the kanyadana. "Joining their hands" — *hāta joṛa*, the rite of joining the hands of bride and bridegroom. "The portion and [He who] possesses the portions" — *aṃśī aṃśe*: Lakshmi is Narayana's energy and Narayana the source; a rapturous comparison by the onlookers, cf. notes 43, 63.

[^112-66]: "He" — apparently Sadashiva, who gives the bride away in place of his departed brother. "Dowry" — *yautuka*. "Loads" — *bhāra*, lit. "burdens".

[^112-67]: Ashtamangala (*aṣṭa-maṅgala*) — the wedding rite of the eighth day, after which the couple returns to the bridegroom's house. "Departed" — *bije karila*, the honorific "was pleased to set out".

[^112-68]: "In seclusion" — *nigame*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition (also lahari 13, 3, 10); the meaning is taken from the context.

[^112-69]: The mahashaya — here Achyuta. Six tastes — lahari 3, note 13.

[^112-70]: "The friend of all, hard to attain" — *sabāra durlabha bandhu*; possibly also "the rare friend of all".

[^112-71]: The author's signature is rendered by the standard formula; here the verb is *kautuke racilā*, "joyfully (with delight) composed".


## Lahari 13. Description of the Mood of Renunciation

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; after the wedding Rasika lives at home, relishing the "Bhagavata" in the company of devotees; in seclusion he chants the name of Hari, weeps, rolls on the ground and calls on Krishna as his only refuge; his family search for him in the forests and bring him home; he regards his home as poison and wishes to leave, taking renunciation; Achyuta urges him to stay, and Rasika replies that only Krishna, His name, His lilas, Vrindavana and devotion are real, and calls on his father to worship Krishna*

*The thirteenth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi — panchali metre.*[^113-1]

**1.** Glory to Shyamananda, the joy of all [the world]!
Be merciful to me,
so that "Rasika-mangala", a wave of bliss,
I may sing day after day.[^113-2]

**2.** Having celebrated the wedding and so on, Rasika-Murari
lives at home, [passing the time] in various ways.
In the taste of the "Bhagavata" he always delights
in the company of rasikas.[^113-3]

**3.** On some days, sitting in seclusion,
he constantly chants the name of Hari.
The tears from his eyes flow in a hundred streams;
he is aware of neither night nor day.[^113-4]

**4.** Saying "Krishna, Krishna!", rolling on the ground,
he weeps in agitation:
"Krishna is the Lord of my life; I have no other refuge";
his loosened hair he does not tie up.[^113-5]

**5.** In the rapture of feeling, with a faltering voice,
[he repeats] "Krishna, Krishna" again and again.
Over his whole body the hairs stand on end; the eight sattvika [bhavas]
arise as he remembers Krishna.[^113-6]

**6.** In a loud voice he speaks, humbly:
"Krishna is the treasure of my life.
Krishna is my mother, Krishna is my father,
Krishna is [my] caste and life.

**7.** Krishna is my Destroyer, Krishna is my Creator,
Krishna is my Maintainer.
Krishna is son and wealth; Krishna is friend;
Krishna is my Protector.[^113-7]

**8.** Apart from Krishna I have no one else;
I have offered [my] life to Him."
Saying such words, greatly distraught,
he cries aloud, "Krishna!"

**9.** With eyes full [of tears] he weeps incessantly,
remembering Krishna's qualities.
At meals and in sleep he knows nothing else,
meditating on Krishna's name.

**10.** He does not stay at home, he eats nothing,
he sits in seclusion all the time.
The household search [for him] incessantly,
roaming from forest to forest.

**11.** Wandering and wandering, the one sent sees a wonder:
Rasika rolling on the ground.
Lifting [him], taking him on his lap, [he] wipes with his cloth
[his] body, grey with dust.[^113-8]

**12.** Taking him home, bathing him,
[they feed him] dishes of six tastes and so on.
Thus day after day he plays in the forests,
wandering about, searching especially [hard].[^113-9]

**13.** Day after day Achyuta's son
performs lilas in various ways.
On nothing but Krishna does he fix his meditation;
he regards worldly life as false.[^113-10]

**14.** His own home he regards as poison,
[and so] his wife, children, kinsmen.
Abandoning everything, taking renunciation,
he wishes again and again to leave.[^113-11]

**15.** Learning [of this], Achyuta speaks, explaining everything:
"Listen, Rasika, my child!
Stay at home — I will give you everything,
whatever you want, whatever you wish."[^113-12]

**16.** Hearing his father's words, Rasika says:
"Listen, father, to [my] words.
All the wealth of worldly life I see to be false;
truth is in Krishna: [this is what is] certain.[^113-13]

**17.** True is the treasure — Krishna; true are Krishna's people;
true are Krishna's lilas;
true is Vrindavana, true are the gopis,
true is the son of Nanda.[^113-14]

**18.** True is sankirtana, true is the name of Krishna,
true is the guru, [true is] devotion to Krishna.
Listen, my father: this is the essence of the Vedas —
let everyone turn their mind to Krishna.

**19.** Worship Krishna, father — this is the view of the shastras;
Krishna is the life of all.
Brahma and the others, Narada, Shiva, Shuka, Indra
know no one but Krishna."[^113-15]

**20.** Hearing these words, all the people
think in their minds: "Krishna is the truth."
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^113-16]

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the thirteenth lahari, called "Description of the Mood of Renunciation".*

[^113-1]: Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*) — panchali metre (*pāñcālī chanda*), i.e. tripadi, as in lahari 11 (note 1); each stanza is set in four lines in the edition and translated likewise. There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title of the lahari follows the colophon: "iti śrīrasika-maṅgala pūrva-vibhāge vairāgya-bhāva-varṇana-nāma trayodaśa-laharī sampūrṇa" (*vairāgya-bhāva-varṇana*).

[^113-2]: "The joy of all [the world]" — *akhila ānanda*. "A wave of bliss" — *ānanda-kallola*.

[^113-3]: Rasika-Murari is Rasikananda. "In the taste of the 'Bhagavata'" — *bhāgavata-rase*: so in the 1941 edition; the 1997 edition has *bhāgavata raṅge*, "in the delight of the 'Bhagavata'". "Rasikas" — *rasika-jana*, connoisseurs of rasa, devotees able to relish it.

[^113-4]: "In seclusion" — *nigame* (also 10): the meaning is taken from the context (lahari 12, note 68). "He is aware of neither night nor day" — *niśi diśi nāhi jāna*.

[^113-5]: "Rolling on the ground" — *bhūme gaṛi buli*. "Loosened" — *luṭhila*, according to the edition's gloss, "loose, dishevelled".

[^113-6]: "With a faltering voice" — *gada gada bhāṣe*. "The hairs stand on end" — *pulaka*. The eight sattvika bhavas (*aṣṭa sāttvika*) — lahari 6, note 13.

[^113-7]: "Destroyer, Creator, Maintainer" — *hartā*, *kartā*, *pālayitā*: the three functions of dissolution, creation and maintenance; that is, Krishna is everything to him. "Friend" — *bandhu-jita*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; possibly for *bandhu-hita*, "friend and benefactor"; the meaning of *jita* is unclear. "Protector" — *rakṣitā*.

[^113-8]: "The one sent" — *dūta*, a servant sent out to search. "With his cloth" — *nicole*, with his upper garment or wrap.

[^113-9]: Six tastes — lahari 3, note 13. "Plays in the forests" — *khele bane bane*; "wandering about, searching especially [hard]" — *cāhiyā bule viśeṣe*, apparently searching for Krishna; the rendering is tentative.

[^113-10]: "Son" — *bālā*, lit. "boy". "Does he fix his meditation" — *kare dhiyāna*, "meditates".

[^113-11]: "Home" — *sadana*, according to the edition's gloss, "house". "His wife, children, kinsmen" — *dārā-suta-bandhu-gaṇa*, a set expression for family ties (Rasika has no children yet). "Renunciation" — *vairāgya* (cf. the title of the lahari).

[^113-12]: "My child" — *bāchā*, an affectionate address to a son. "Whatever you wish" — *tomāra icchā*.

[^113-13]: "The wealth of worldly life" — *saṃsāra vaibhava*. "Truth is in Krishna: [this is what is] certain" — *satya kṛṣṇe paramāṇa*; *paramāṇa* (= *pramāṇa*) means "proof, measure"; possibly also "truth is proven [only] in Krishna".

[^113-14]: "Krishna's people" — *kṛṣṇa-jana*, His devotees. "The son of Nanda" — *nandera bālā*, lit. "Nanda's boy", that is, Krishna.

[^113-15]: Shuka is Shukadeva Gosvami, the narrator of the Bhagavata; Narada is the divine sage. "Know no one but Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa bine nāhi jāna*; the author uses *jāna* ("knows") the same way in 3 (note 4). Possibly also *jān* (Persian "life"): "without Krishna [they] have no life" (cf. the rhyme *prāṇa*, "life", in the first line).

[^113-16]: The author's signature (the second half of the stanza) is given in the common formula; here it is in tripadi metre and reads differently: "Shyamananda's feet are all the wealth of the son of Rasamaya" (*śyāmānanda-pada, sakala sampada, rasamayera nandane*); cf. lahari 5, note 14; lahari 11, note 15.


## Lahari 14. The Vision of Sri Krishna and the Hearing of His Command

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; absorbed in love for Krishna, Rasika wanders through Achyuta's domains, settles with his family at Ghantashila and reads the Bhagavata in the Jagannatha pavilion; in the forests on the Suvarnarekha, where the Pandavas once rested, he reads the Bhagavata, sings the name and feeds the Vaishnavas; as he sits in meditation at dusk, Krishna appears to him and declares that his teacher will be Shyamananda, in whose form His beloved has taken birth; Krishna vanishes, and Rasika weeps in separation until morning; the household find him in the forest and bring him home; Rasika, heedless of the joys of home, longs for Krishna and Shyamananda; the author promises to tell how Shyamananda came from Vraja to Utkala, and speaks of his own service to both since childhood*

*The fourteenth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^114-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the friend of all,
the benefactor of all people, the ocean of mercy!

**2.** Be merciful to me, Prabhu, son of Durika:
I shall describe a little of Rasika's glory.[^114-2]

**3.** How [his] meeting with Shyamananda came about —
of that I shall tell something in detail;

**4.** how [Shyamananda] was united with Rasika,
and how both, giving instruction, delivered living beings.

**5.** At that time Rasikendra, absorbed in Krishna,
freely, in the bliss of Krishna, wanders from land to land.[^114-3]

**6.** Achyuta had houses in various places;
in each of those places he stays for many days.

**7.** There is a most holy place called Ghantashila;
there he settled together with his family.[^114-4]

**8.** There stands the incomparable Jagannatha pavilion;
sitting there, he reads the Bhagavata without pause.[^114-5]

**9.** Rasika-shekhara is intoxicated with the rasa of the Bhagavata;
his whole body is drenched with the tears of [his] eyes.

**10.** On the bank of the Suvarnarekha is a most wondrous place:
very dense groves, wonderfully formed.

**11.** Formerly the Pandavas and others rested there;
[that it is] so holy a place — there is proof of it.[^114-6]

**12.** Seeing all these places, Rasika-shekhara
roams the forest alone, with love [for them].

**13.** In one place — [he reads] the Bhagavata, in another — [chants] the name,
in another he performs sankirtana without pause.

**14.** In one place, joyfully holding a meal in the forest,
Rasika feeds the Vaishnavas there.[^114-7]

**15.** At that time to the place where the Pandavas and others [once] were
Rasikendra went.

**16.** A most enchanting place, beautiful to behold:
dense forest, river, water, fragrance.

**17.** Rasikendra, taking his seat in that place,
sat in meditation, [chanting] the name of Hari, with closed eyes.

**18.** Now sweat, now trembling, now tears flow;
his heart is in great longing from separation from Krishna.

**19.** At that time a certain foremost of great personalities
appeared before Rasika.

**20.** A dark, beautiful, most enchanting body;
with the radiance of [His] limbs He lights up the forest.

**21.** Bent in three places, graceful; the flute adorns [His] lips;
curling locks [and] crown glitter.

**22.** His peacock feather is beautiful to behold;
armlets, anklets, little bells; He wears yellow garments.[^114-8]

**23.** On His neck sway various jewels and the Kaustubha gem;
in His ears are earrings; in His nose a pearl sparkles.

**24.** His ankle-bells are most beautiful to behold;
[His] unhurried, languid gait surpasses [that of] an elephant.[^114-9]

**25.** At the hour [when] the cows [return], Krishna came to that place
and gave darshana to His servant Rasika.[^114-10]

**26.** Standing before him, He speaks profound words;
the speech [seems to] melt on His lips, it delights the ear:

**27.** "Hear these words, Rasika-mahashaya:
your teacher [will be] Shyamananda-raya.

**28.** My beloved has taken birth in the form of Shyamananda;
bestowing prema-bhakti, he will deliver all people.[^114-11]

**29.** Serving him, you will attain My feet;
in your heart I shall sport constantly."

**30.** Hearing these words with his ears, Rasika-Murari
came out of his meditation and looked with tear-filled eyes.

**31.** Before him he saw Krishna, the Lord of [his] life,
whose enchanting form surpasses millions upon millions of Kamas.

**32.** Seeing [Him], Rasika fell joyfully at [His] feet;
placing his head on [His] holy feet, [he is] in deep bliss.

**33.** Right there Sri Krishna vanished;
rising, [Rasika] looked — there is no one in that place.

**34.** "O Krishna, where have You gone, my life?" —
[and] Rasika fell face down on that spot.[^114-12]

**35.** Fallen on the ground, he weeps, sobbing, sobbing;
streams of tears flow ceaselessly from his eyes.[^114-13]

**36.** His body grey with dust, he rolls on the ground;
his body is overwhelmed by the waves [of tears] from his eyes.

**37.** In a choked voice he speaks sweet words:
"Leaving me, where have You gone, Krishna, treasure of my life?

**38.** As the fruit of some merit I was granted the sight of You;
and now, Krishna, You have abandoned me and left me alone.

**39.** I saw Your form with these sinful eyes;
and now, leaving [me] without support, You have vanished.[^114-14]

**40.** How shall I pass my days without seeing You?" —
remembering, remembering, he weeps without end.

**41.** However much he lamented in his mood [of love] for Krishna —
what power have I to tell of those expressions [of feeling]?

**42.** Nothing can be told of that longing;
hearing of that love (anuraga), [even] a stone would melt.[^114-15]

**43.** Rasika weeps in love for Krishna, unaware of the outer world;
he lies right there, and morning came.

**44.** Meanwhile all the household go searching:
they search from village to village, look from forest to forest.

**45.** Looking [everywhere], they search in Panduya, at that place
where the Pandavas and others rested.[^114-16]

**46.** A most fearsome forest, very remote,
on the bank of the Suvarnarekha, adorned with hills.[^114-17]

**47.** Tigers, bears, elephants, lions, rhinoceroses — in [those] parts;
all [these] creatures live there by hundreds of thousands.

**48.** In the ecstasy of prema Prabhu [Rasika] is aware of nothing;
by Krishna's power none [of them] is anywhere near.

**49.** At that time all the people, searching in haste,
came and saw Rasika-shekhara there:

**50.** he lies on the ground, his eyes full of tears,
his curling locks scattered, his hairs ceaselessly standing on end.[^114-18]

**51.** Seeing [this], all the people, distraught,
lifted Rasika, seated him and brought him to his senses.

**52.** All wiped [his] holy face with fine cloth,
brushed [the dust] off his whole body and carefully tied up his hair.

**53.** Taking him by the hands, all raised [him]
and slowly, slowly came home.

**54.** The form that Rasika had seen with his own eyes
lives on unceasingly in [his] heart.

**55.** Having heard the command [that] his teacher is Shyamananda, [he thinks]:
"When shall I see that moon-like face?"

**56.** To no one does he speak of the thoughts of his heart;
ceaselessly he worships Shyamananda.

**57.** His heart is always in longing, intent on Krishna;
neither worldly affairs nor the joys of home please him at all.

**58.** His kinsfolk constantly surround him;
at times he sits with his [young] wife.[^114-19]

**59.** Various goods, various garments, various ornaments
they place before Rasika again and again.

**60.** He casts no glance at any of the heaps of goods;
Krishna [and] Shyamananda are always within his mind.

**61.** Worship of Krishna, meditation on Krishna, remembrance of Krishna;
Krishna is the truth, and all else — false aims.

**62.** Night and day he sees the three worlds full of Krishna;
in Rasika's eyes there is no hunger, no thirst, no sleep.

**63.** Having seen Krishna, [he was filled with] a most firm anuraga;
day and night, sitting, he weeps, thinking of that form.

**64.** Rasika gives no thought to books and does not stay at home;
in the ocean of separation from Krishna he roams the forest.

**65.** The secret thoughts of his heart he tells no one;
apart from that form, nothing [else] appears [to him].[^114-20]

**66.** Thus, when for many days he had been thinking and thinking,
Shyamananda, won over by [his] devotion, came in haste.

**67.** How he, leaving Vraja, came to Utkala —
of that I shall tell something.

**68.** What do I know of the inner meaning of these accounts?
[I tell them only] by the mercy of Shyamananda and Rasika.

**69.** Serving the two prabhus from childhood,
[I pass on] what was related without guile;

**70.** all the lilas of the two that I saw from childhood —
all of this I shall proclaim in brief.[^114-21]

**71.** Let no one hold against me any faults in the order [of the narrative]:
it is Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of rasikas], who makes me speak.

**72.** Listen to "Rasika-mangala", all you devotees of Krishna:
merely by hearing [it] one obtains the treasure of love for Krishna.[^114-22]

**73.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Vision of Sri Krishna and the Hearing of His Command".*

[^114-1]: In the 1941 edition the raga is *nārānī gauṛā* (1997 ed.: *nārāṇī gauṛā*), as in lahari 10 (note 1), that is, the *nārāyaṇī gauṛā* of lahari 7; the ghosha (refrain) is the same as in laharis 7 and 10, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of the lahari: after the heading, the raga and the ghosha, the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "śrīkṛṣṇa-darśana o tad-ādeśa-śravaṇa-nāma caturdaśa-laharī".

[^114-2]: The son of Durika is Shyamananda (Durika is his mother; lahari 1, note 11; lahari 10, note 2); "Prabhu" here is Shyamananda.

[^114-3]: "Absorbed in Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera āveśe*. "Freely" — *icchāmaya*, lit. "following [his own] will".

[^114-4]: Ghantashila (*ghaṇṭaśilā*; Ghantashila in BR 15) is apparently present-day Ghatshila on the Suvarnarekha (Jharkhand); cf. BR 15, 30–31: Rasikananda lived for some time at Ghantashila, where the Pandavas rested on the bank of the Suvarnarekha. "Settled" — *viśrāma karilā*, lit. "stayed, rested". Achyuta's houses in various places (6) were apparently on his estates: Achyuta is a man of rank who lives "in royal splendour" (lahari 4, 2).

[^114-5]: The Jagannatha pavilion (*jagannātha-maṇḍapa*) is apparently a mandapa (a roofed hall for gatherings and readings) attached to a shrine of Jagannatha.

[^114-6]: The Pandavas are the five sons of Pandu, the heroes of the Mahabharata; according to local tradition, they lived in the forests on the Suvarnarekha during their exile (cf. BR 15, 31). "There is proof of it" — *āchaye pramāṇa*.

[^114-7]: "A meal in the forest" — *banabhuji*, according to the edition's gloss *banabhojana*. "Feeds the Vaishnavas" — *vaiṣṇava-bhojana karaye*.

[^114-8]: "Peacock feather" — *mayūra-candrikā*, lit. "the moon-like eye of a peacock feather". "Armlets" — *tāṛ* (lahari 5, note 9); "anklets" — *khāṛu*; "little bells" — *kṣudraghuṇṭi*, according to the edition's gloss *ghuṅur*, *kiṅkiṇī* (bells worn on the waist or ankles). Kaustubha (23) is the jewel on Krishna's chest.

[^114-9]: "Ankle-bells" — *nūpura*. "Unhurried, languid" — *madana-manthara*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition, lit. "slow with love (Madana)"; possibly for *mada-manthara*, "slow as one intoxicated", the usual epithet of an elephant's gait.

[^114-10]: "At the hour [when] the cows [return]" — *godhūli*, lit. "cow-dust": dusk, when the herds come home from the pastures. Darshana is the sight of a saint or of the Deity.

[^114-11]: "My beloved" — *preyasī* (feminine), that is, apparently, Sri Radha: in this way the author exalts Shyamananda (cf. lahari 1, note 2; lahari 2, note 5). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, and not Radhika Herself. In BR 15 (32–39) Rasikananda at Ghantashila hears a voice from the sky saying that here he will become Shyamananda's disciple, and then Shyamananda himself appears to him in a dream; there is no appearance of Krishna there.

[^114-12]: "Face down" — *mukha māṛi*, lit. "pressing his face [to the ground]".

[^114-13]: "Sobbing" — *usasi usasi*, as in lahari 5 (note 10).

[^114-14]: "Without support" — *nirimākhi*, according to the edition's gloss *nirāśraya*, "without shelter".

[^114-15]: "Expressions [of feeling]" (41) — *anubhāva*, the outward signs of an inner emotion (bhava). "Longing" — *ārati* (= *ārti*), "yearning, anguish". Anuraga is deep, ever-increasing attachment to Krishna.

[^114-16]: "In Panduya" — *pāṇḍuyā*: clear in the 1941 edition (1997 ed.: *pāṇḍayā*); apparently the name of a locality associated with the Pandavas; another interpretation is possible (e.g. a corruption of a verb meaning "having found").

[^114-17]: "Very remote" — *nirgama-vidita*: clear in the 1941 edition (and in the 1997 edition); the meaning is unclear. Possibly for *nigama-vidita*, "known from the scriptures" (cf. 11), or connected with *nigama* in the sense of "seclusion", which the author uses in laharis 12–13 (lahari 13, note 4).

[^114-18]: "His hairs ceaselessly standing on end" — *pulakāvirāma* (*pulaka* + *avirāma*).

[^114-19]: "With his [young] wife" — *priyā saṅge*, that is, with Ichchha-dei (lahari 12).

[^114-20]: "Appears" — *sphure*; the edition gives in a footnote the variant *smare*: "apart from that form, he remembers nothing".

[^114-21]: "Without guile" — *niramāyāte*, according to the edition's gloss *akapaṭa-bhāve*, "sincerely". Who related it (*kaila*, 3rd person) is not stated: possibly the two prabhus themselves, Shyamananda and Rasikananda, or the author's father Rasamaya; the rendering is tentative. In 70 the author says that he himself saw the lilas of both from childhood.

[^114-22]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana* (lahari 10, note 13). "The treasure of love for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana*; the edition gives in a footnote the variant *kṛṣṇa-prāṇa-dhana*: "Krishna, the treasure of life".


## Lahari 15. The Journey from Vraja-dhama to Gauda

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasikendra thinks of Shyamananda without cease; in Vraja, Madana-gopala Sri Govinda at night commands Shyamananda to go to Utkala, instruct Rasika-Murari and preach prema-bhakti, and conveys the same command to him through Sri Jiva Gosvami; taking leave of Jiva and the Vaishnavas of Vraja, Shyamananda sets out with his disciples; in Agra the Mughal kotwal throws the Vaishnavas into prison, but at night an unknown person punishes him, and the kotwal begs forgiveness and serves them for a month; by way of Varanasi and Prayaga Shyamananda comes to Rohini and, learning that Rasika is at Ghantashila, goes there*

*The fifteenth lahari.*

*Raga Shri.*[^115-1]
*Ghosha: "O Hari, this time be merciful to me:*
*I hope to obtain the shade of Your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the joy of all,
at whose feet the bee is Rasikendra-chandra!

**2.** Rasikendra meditates on Shyamananda without cease;
apart from Shyamananda he knows nothing else.

**3.** Shyamananda-raya could not remain in Vraja:
by Govinda's command he came to see Rasika.[^115-2]

**4.** I shall tell all of this in detail:
for what reason Shyamananda wandered through Utkala,

**5.** for what reason Prabhu came to deliver living beings.
Listen, listen, all, attentively, with a steady heart.

**6.** One day Shyamananda, sitting at night,
was chanting the name of Hari, full of joy.[^115-3]

**7.** At that time Madana-gopala Sri Govinda,
appearing before him, says: "Listen, Shyamananda!

**8.** My dearest devotee is Rasika-Murari;
instruct him in the land of Utkala.[^115-4]

**9.** Preach My prema-bhakti, you two;
deliver all the living beings of Utkala.[^115-5]

**10.** He is My very soul, most dear to Me, a dweller of Vraja;
go to the world of Utkala and show him mercy."[^115-6]

**11.** Hearing these words, Shyamananda, startled,
fell to the ground, his body stretched out like a stick.

**12.** Rising, he saw that there was no one in that place;
he weeps long because of separation from Krishna.

**13.** Having heard those words, Shyamananda in joy
recalled in his mind the command of Hridayananda:

**14.** "The command he gave me earlier in private —
its confirmation I have now received before my eyes.[^115-7]

**15.** With my own ears I heard the command from the holy mouth;
[but] how shall I leave Vraja and go to Utkala?

**16.** If I do not go, Krishna's word will be broken;
I shall surely go and see [that] jewel among men."[^115-8]

**17.** Night and day he ponders these words in his mind;
his heart does not consent to leave Vraja.

**18.** Then one day Madana-gopala
gave a command to Jiva Gosai face to face:

**19.** "Listen, listen, O Jiva, to what I tell you:
tell Shyamananda to go to Utkala.

**20.** Rasika-Murari is very dear to Me;
taking him [along], he will crush Utkala.[^115-9]

**21.** He will give My prema-bhakti to every single person."
Three times He gave him the command, to make it certain.[^115-10]

**22.** "He will serve My dweller of Vraja;
to Utkala the dweller of Vraja will go.

**23.** My dweller of Vraja suffers in Utkala:
no one knows [his] greatness, all have sinful hearts.

**24.** Removing the blindness of the darkness of sin, [granting] divine knowledge,
Shyamananda [and] Rasika will deliver [them]."[^115-11]

**25.** Hearing Krishna's words, Jiva-mahashaya
recounted everything to Shyamananda in due order:[^115-12]

**26.** "Listen, listen, O jewel among men:
Krishna has commanded you [to go] to the world of Utkala.

**27.** Rasika-Murari there is a person dear to Krishna;
making him your companion, deliver the living beings."

**28.** Hearing all these words from Jiva Gosai,
Shyamananda then gained conviction in his mind:

**29.** "I shall certainly go to the world of Utkala;
I shall see that Rasika-Murari, the one dear [to Krishna].

**30.** The one on whom there is such mercy of Krishna —
I shall surely meet that man."

**31.** Thus after some days Shyamananda-raya
took leave of Jiva Gosai.

**32.** Haripriya Dasa and all the other mahajanas,
the adhikaris, the dwellers of the kunjas — whoever were [there] —[^115-13]

**33.** taking leave of them all, Shyamananda
set out with joy in his heart.

**34.** He took with him all the scriptures of prema-bhakti;
Kishora, the young Shyamadasa of pure mind —

**35.** these three disciples [were with him], and with them one brother,
Thakura Prasadadasa, famous everywhere.[^115-14]

**36.** Taking these four along with him,
leaving Vraja, he came and stopped at Agra.[^115-15]

**37.** They all settled down inside Agra;
the kotwal of the capital, for his part, goes about on patrol.[^115-16]

**38.** Inside the city he sees the Vaishnavas;
seeing [them], the Mughal kotwal became very angry:

**39.** "Thieves or robbers [they may be], or sadhus — I do not know for certain;
why have they stayed fearlessly in the middle of the city?"

**40.** He gave a command to the guards: "Bring them all!";
the wicked men seized [them] and put [them] in prison.

**41.** He himself went and lay down on his bed;
suddenly someone enters that room.

**42.** Quickly lifting him together with the bed,
he dashed [him] down on the floor of that room with a crushing blow.[^115-17]

**43.** Throwing him to the ground, sitting on his chest, [the visitor] says to him:
"Listen, listen, you villain, sinner, evildoer!

**44.** My dear ones, having all settled down
in the middle of the city, sit and chant the name of Hari.

**45.** You seized them all and put them in prison;
today I shall destroy [you] together with all [your] family."

**46.** Suffering torment, the wicked man cries out in a terrible voice:
"My life has come up to my throat, I have fallen into calamity!"[^115-18]

**47.** His household came and surrounded [him] on all sides;
blood flows from his mouth, he breathes heavily.

**48.** They all lifted [him] up, put water in his mouth,
sat him up and brought him to his senses.

**49.** Then they ask him: "Why [are you] on the ground?"
Blood flows from his mouth, his eyes are closed.

**50.** Then the kotwal says: "Listen, all:
in the prison there are five vairagis.[^115-19]

**51.** They are not men — they are dear to Krishna;
quickly bring them to me."

**52.** Ten or twenty guards went, [carrying out] the command exactly,
[and] said: "All of you, come [with us]."

**53.** Hearing the guards' words, [Shyamananda] was startled;
feeling embarrassed in his mind, he remembered Krishna.

**54.** Then Shyamananda went to the kotwal;
seeing [him], the kotwal fell to the ground in reverent awe.

**55.** Stretched out like a stick, he fell at [his] feet:
"Forgive [my] offence — I take shelter in you.

**56.** I did not know that you are dear to Krishna;
for that offence I have suffered punishment needlessly."[^115-20]

**57.** The yavana praised [him] in many ways;
pleased, Shyamananda speaks:

**58.** "I beg this alms, listen, mahashaya:
you will certainly serve the Vaishnavas."

**59.** Receiving the command, the yavana ruler rejoiced;
from that day he serves sadhus.[^115-21]

**60.** From that [time] the joyful service of sadhus first [began]:
[even] yavanas serve at his command.[^115-22]

**61.** Thus the yavana kept [them] for a month
and joyfully served [them] with loving care.

**62.** [Shyamananda] held many discussions on knowledge with him;
then Shyamananda joyfully departs from there.[^115-23]

**63.** For some days he stayed at Varanasi [and] Prayaga;
after some days he came to the town of Rohini.[^115-24]

**64.** In the village he asked: "Where is Rasika?"
All said: "Surely at Ghantashila.

**65.** The mahashaya is there with his whole household."
Hearing this, Shyamananda went there.[^115-25]

**66.** How Shyamananda met with Rasika,
[how] on seeing each other both [were swept by] waves of prema —

**67.** of all this I shall tell something in detail;
hearing [it], the son of Nanda will feel joy.[^115-26]

**68.** Listen to "Rasika-mangala", all devotees of Krishna:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.[^115-27]

**69.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the fifteenth lahari, called "The Journey from Vraja-dhama to Gauda".*

[^115-1]: Raga Shri (*śrī*) — as in lahari 5 (note 1). The ghosha (refrain) is the same as in lahari 4 (there *tũyā pada-chāyā*, here *taba pada-chāyā*), and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of the lahari: after the heading, the raga and the ghosha, the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "brajadhāma haite gauṛa-yātrā-nāma pañcadaśa-laharī"; Gauda here means the east in a broad sense (Bengal and the neighbouring lands): in this lahari Shyamananda goes to Utkala.

[^115-2]: "The bee at whose feet" (1) — *caraṇera bhṛṅga*: one who drinks the nectar of the feet, that is, a devotee. Govinda is Krishna; further on in this lahari "Madana-gopala Sri Govinda" appears to Shyamananda at night, and then conveys the same command through Sri Jiva Gosvami. According to BR, it was Sri Jiva Gosvami who sent Shyamananda to Utkala.

[^115-3]: "At night" — *niśite*; the edition gives in a footnote the variant *nibhṛte*, "in seclusion" (cf. 14).

[^115-4]: Madana-gopala Sri Govinda is Krishna (note 2); He speaks as one person (*kahe*, singular), and in 18 is called simply Madana-gopala. "In the land of Utkala" — *utkala purī*, literally "[in] the city (abode) of Utkala"; Utkala in general is meant, not Puri.

[^115-5]: "You two" — *dõhe*: so in the 1941 edition, i.e. Shyamananda and Rasika (cf. 24).

[^115-6]: "My very soul" — *mora ātmā*; "a dweller of Vraja" — *brajabāsi-jana*: so Krishna calls Rasikananda (as the editor of the edition also understands it; cf. 22–23). That Rasikananda is an eternal dweller of Vraja and the "soul" of Krishna is the view of the author, who exalts his hero (cf. lahari 12, note 43; lahari 14, note 11).

[^115-7]: Hridayananda is Hridaya Chaitanya of Ambika (Kalna), Shyamananda's guru (lahari 1, note 13). "In private" — *nibhṛte*. "Before my eyes" — *yugate*, glossed by the edition as *sākṣāte*, "directly, in person". What the guru's earlier command was the author does not say here; according to BR, Hridaya Chaitanya sent Shyamananda to Vrindavana to Sri Jiva Gosvami, who later sent him to Utkala (cf. note 2).

[^115-8]: "Will be broken" — *bhañjana haya*. "Jewel among men" — *puruṣa-ratana*: here Rasika; in 26 Jiva so addresses Shyamananda.

[^115-9]: Jiva Gosai (18) is Sri Jiva Gosvami. "He will crush Utkala" — *utkala karibe dalana*, literally "will trample, crush"; apparently he will crush the sinfulness of Utkala (cf. 23–24), i.e. conquer it with prema-bhakti.

[^115-10]: "To make it certain" — *pramāṇe*, "for confirmation, [as] proof". "Him" — *tā̃re* (honorific), i.e. Jiva.

[^115-11]: In 22–23 it is not clear who serves whom: "My dweller of Vraja" is apparently Rasika (cf. 10 and 23: "My dweller of Vraja suffers in Utkala"), and "the dweller of Vraja will go to Utkala" is apparently Shyamananda; it is also possible to read "[Rasika] will serve My dweller of Vraja", i.e. Shyamananda. "Removing the blindness of the darkness of sin" — *pāpa timirāndha chāṛāiyā*.

[^115-12]: "In due order" — *sandarbhe*, "coherently, in proper sequence"; *sandarbha* is also the name of Jiva Gosvami's works (the "Shat-sandarbha"), but here it is apparently used in its general sense.

[^115-13]: Haripriya Dasa (*haripriyā dāsa*) is unidentified; "the servants of Haripriya" is also possible. Mahajanas are revered Vaishnavas. Adhikaris (*adhikārī*) are here apparently the servants (managers) of the temples of Vraja; "dwellers of the kunjas" — *kuñjabāsī*, Vaishnavas living in the groves of Vrindavana.

[^115-14]: Line 34 can be divided in different ways. "These three disciples" (35) require three names; the text has *kiśora bālaka śyāmadāsa śuddhamati*: Kishora (Kishoradasa, Shyamananda's disciple; BR 15, 41), the [young] Shyamadasa and possibly a third, hidden in the words *bālaka* ("boy") or *śuddhamati* ("of pure mind"), which can also be understood as epithets; the reading is tentative. "Brother" — *bhāi*: a brother by birth or a spiritual brother (fellow devotee). "Thakura Prasadadasa" — *ṭhākura-prasāda-dāsa*; "Thakura-prasada Dasa" is also possible. The five vairagis in 50 are Shyamananda and these four.

[^115-15]: "These four" — *cāri vigraha*, literally "four forms (persons)"; *vigraha* here means "person". "Taking along" — *saṅgati kariyā*, as in 34 ("took the scriptures with him"). "Stopped" — *utare*, "put up, took lodging". Agra was the capital of the Mughal empire.

[^115-16]: A kotwal (*koṭāla*) is the chief of the city guard and police; "the kotwal of the capital" — *rājadhānī koṭāla*. "Mughal" (38) — *mogala*, i.e. a Muslim of the Mughal service nobility.

[^115-17]: "With a crushing blow" — *nirghāta kariñā*, "striking"; "dashed down" — *āchāṛila*. The visitor is apparently the Lord Himself: he calls the Vaishnavas "My dear ones" (44). The verb *kahena* (43) is honorific.

[^115-18]: "My life has come up to my throat" — *kaṇṭhāgata haila prāṇa*, i.e. "I am at my last breath". "I have fallen into calamity" — *paṛilũ pramāde*.

[^115-19]: Vairagis (*vairāgī*) are detached wandering Vaishnavas. The five are Shyamananda and his four companions (34–36, note 14).

[^115-20]: "Needlessly" — *akāraṇa*, "without cause": the kotwal seized the Vaishnavas for nothing and so brought punishment on himself; "I suffered punishment without [knowing my] fault", i.e. through ignorance, is also possible.

[^115-21]: A yavana (*yavana*) is a Muslim (glossary of the "Prema-vilasa"). "Ruler" — *rājana*, here the kotwal.

[^115-22]: "His" — *yā̃hāra* (honorific), i.e. Shyamananda's. "The joyful service of sadhus" — *sādhu sevā-pramoda*; the line can also be understood thus: "from here the joy of serving sadhus first [arose]: [for] even a yavana serves at his command".

[^115-23]: "With loving care" (61) — *samprīti-vidhāna*, "with loving attentiveness". "Discussions on knowledge" — *jñāna-goṣṭhī*, spiritual conversations. "Joyfully" — *raṅge*.

[^115-24]: Prayaga (Allahabad) is the confluence of the Ganga and the Yamuna. Rohini — *nagara rohiṇa*: Rasikananda's native village in Mallabhumi (lahari 3, note 6; in BR 15, Rayani).

[^115-25]: "Surely" — *sarvathā*, "in any case, certainly". "With his whole household" — *sarvārambhe*, literally "with all [his] establishment"; cf. lahari 14, 7: Rasika settled at Ghantashila "together with his family". Ghantashila — lahari 14, note 4. "Went" — *vijaya karila*, the honorific "deigned to go".

[^115-26]: "The son of Nanda will feel joy" — *ānanda pābe nandera nandana*; "[the listener] will obtain joy [and] the son of Nanda" is also possible.

[^115-27]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana* (lahari 10, note 13; lahari 14, note 22).


## Lahari 16. The Meeting with Sri Shyamananda

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; at Ghantashila Rasika listens to the "Bhagavata" in the raja's assembly and questions the brahmanas about its meaning; Shyamananda enters, and the raja and everyone receive him with reverence; Rasika and Shyamananda recognize each other in their hearts and weep; in private Rasika falls at his feet, Shyamananda embraces him and says that he has come from Vrindavana by Krishna's command to see him; spending the chaturmasya together, they discuss the scriptures, and Shyamananda reveals to Rasika the path of worshipping Radha and Krishna in Vrindavana in the mood of madhurya and the power of prema, by which Krishna is conquered; Shyamananda embraces and blesses Rasika; thus the Purva-vibhaga concludes*

*The sixteenth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^116-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!*
*O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of all [the world]!
Be merciful, so that I may describe [your] glory.[^116-2]

**2.** How the meeting of Shyamananda with Rasika came about —
of that I tell in detail.

**3.** Rasika lives joyfully in the village of Ghantashila;
day and night he sees Shyamananda in meditation.[^116-3]

**4.** One day all are sitting in the raja's assembly;
before the raja a brahmana began [to recite] the "Bhagavata".

**5.** Rasika, sitting there, listens to the "Bhagavata";
Raja Vaikuntha listens to the narration of the "Bhagavata".[^116-4]

**6.** The assembly in the capital is large and beautiful to see;
the great brahmanas are like the foremost [knowers] of the Vedas.[^116-5]

**7.** Rasika joyfully questions them all:
one after another he asks about the inner meaning of the "Bhagavata".[^116-6]

**8.** At that time Shyamananda came;
entering the midst of the assembly, he presented himself [there].[^116-7]

**9.** A body beautiful to see, a golden form,
arms reaching to the knees, a captivating face.

**10.** A face with a gentle, gentle smile, a beautiful glance,
a gait unhurried like that of a king of elephants — most captivating.[^116-8]

**11.** Seeing great power in [his] form, all are amazed;
the raja with all his courtiers quickly rose.

**12.** Stretched out like a stick, he fell at [his] feet;
all saw [him] as if he were a second Narayana.[^116-9]

**13.** Seeing [that] wondrous form, the raja, leaving [his own] seat,
carefully seats [him] upon [that] seat.

**14.** Seeing Shyamananda, Rasika [was filled with] blissful jubilation:
Prabhu, the giver of prema-bhakti, has appeared.[^116-10]

**15.** Shyamananda sat down with a joyful heart;
looking around on all sides, he observes the people one by one.

**16.** Seeing Rasika's form, he is enchanted at heart:
"This man must be Rasika-shekhara."

**17.** Neither knows the other [by sight], [yet] both know in their minds;
seeing each other's form, both wept.[^116-11]

**18.** Soon, having heard the "Bhagavata", the raja-mahashaya
and all [with him] withdrew into the palace.

**19.** The brahmanas all went away, each to his own place;
Rasika remained alone, knowing for certain [who had come].[^116-12]

**20.** In that assembly Shyamananda settled down;
Shyamananda, the jewel among men, sat there.[^116-13]

**21.** In private Rasika went and fell at [his] feet;
streams of bliss flow from Rasika's eyes.

**22.** Rising, Shyamananda-raya took [him] into his embrace
[and] asked everyone: "Whose son is this man?

**23.** What is this youth's name? Tell me.
His form is sweet to see, a gentle smile is on his face."[^116-14]

**24.** All give [his] name — Murari,
the son of Achyuta, the lord of Mallabhum.[^116-15]

**25.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda seated him by his side
[and] asked about everything in detail.

**26.** He asked about the worldly affairs of [his] people, one by one,
and then carefully spoke of the highest goal.[^116-16]

**27.** "Leaving Vraja, I have come to see you,
by the command of Krishna and of all the dwellers of Vraja.[^116-17]

**28.** You, the son of Achyuta, are an associate of Krishna;
to see [you] I have come, leaving Vrindavana."[^116-18]

**29.** Hearing [this], Rasika speaks with embarrassment:
"Birth after birth I am the servant of your feet.

**30.** Regarding [me] as your own servant, be gracious [to me] in your heart:
you have granted me the sight of you by [your] grace."[^116-19]

**31.** Thus the two conversed with each other;
taking leave, Rasika came home.

**32.** For the [period of] chaturmasya Shyamananda stayed there,
joyfully holding discussions with Rasika.[^116-20]

**33.** The two ceaselessly [hold] talks about Krishna, [forgetting] food;
night and day the two sit in seclusion.[^116-21]

**34.** First they examined all the shastras:
Mimamsa, Patanjali's [yoga] and the others — the essence of the truth of the Vedas.

**35.** Sankhya, Sankhyayana and the truth of the Bhagavata —
all [this] Rasika explains in agreement with Svami.[^116-22]

**36.** He explains prema-bhakti in agreement with the shastras:
all the shastras call loving devotion to Krishna the essence.

**37.** Hearing Rasika's explanation — the greatness of bhakti —
Shyamananda took [him] into his embrace and showed [him] mercy.

**38.** Thus day after day the examination of the shastras
the two carry on, sitting [together], and know nothing else.

**39.** Thus Shyamananda, in seclusion, to Rasika
explains one by one everything about what bhajana should be.

**40.** Citing all the shastras and all the tantras as authority,
Shyamananda spoke to Rasika.

**41.** "The Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Sri Nrisimha, Vamana,
Parashurama, Rama, Bala — the son of Rohini,

**42.** Buddha, Kalki — [and] all the avataras,
as many as are proclaimed on the authority of the shastras —

**43.** whoever desires whichever form worships that very form;
[but I] speak of the true nature of the worship of Chaitanya.[^116-23]

**44.** Once the sages questioned Narada;
he expounded the truth of the shastras, keeping [it] hidden.

**45.** Those who heard Narada's words
began to worship [Krishna] in the mood of madhurya.[^116-24]

**46.** Krishna, the Lord of Vrindavana, is Bhagavan Himself;
[worship Him] as the Shrutis meditated [on Him].[^116-25]

**47.** The bank of the Yamuna, charming Vrindavana;
at the root of a wish-fulfilling tree — the beautiful circle of the rasa.

**48.** Various jewels and gems shine on the jewelled throne;
the rays of the gems are [like] the radiance of millions of suns.

**49.** The ground [there] is chintamani; it rains nectar;
the earthly world became blessed by touching it.[^116-26]

**50.** The women of that abode are Lakshmis indeed;
all the men there are truly Vishnus.[^116-27]

**51.** Within and beyond millions of universes
[this] abode shines eternally, exceedingly charming.

**52.** The city of jewels and gems is splendidly adorned;
it cannot be told in words; Indra and the other gods worship it.

**53.** In such an abode, [beneath] a wish-fulfilling tree, on a jewelled throne —
dark, beautiful Krishna, [and] Radha-jiu on [His] left.

**54.** A graceful, thrice-bent form, a youth in fresh kishora age;
curling hair gathered in a topknot, crowned with a peacock feather.

**55.** Around the topknot are strings of various jewels and gems,
jati, yuthi, mallika, malati, kera-kera.[^116-28]

**56.** On the beautiful forehead shines a line of gorochana;
the fine hairs above it look like a line of bees.[^116-29]

**57.** The pair of brows looks like the bow of Kama;
His two eyes surpass the petals of the lotus.

**58.** The nose surpasses the tila flower; a pearl sways [on it];
on the crimson lips a row of teeth glitters.

**59.** On the face is a gentle smile, the speech is sweet;
the face shines, surpassing the autumn moon.

**60.** Earrings adorn the ears, swaying at the cheeks;
seeing that beauty, the people of the world lose their minds.

**61.** A necklace of gems and pearls adorns the neck;
on the chest is the Kaustubha gem; [He] is marked with the Shrivatsa.

**62.** On the shapely arms are armlets, golden bracelets;
rings of gems and jewels are the ornaments of the fingers.[^116-30]

**63.** A beautiful deep navel; three folds [of the belly] — [like] the Triveni;
the beautiful waist shines, surpassing millions of lions.[^116-31]

**64.** He wears a yellow dhoti with a swaying end;
on the waist, row upon row, little bells shine.

**65.** The beauty of the two thighs surpasses pillars of emerald;
this form, when they see it, captivates the hearts of the women of Vraja.

**66.** The two lotus feet are very soft —
[like] young shoots, the lotus, the newly risen sun.

**67.** Anklets of gems adorn both feet;
at the radiance of the nails millions of moons are put to shame.

**68.** The flag [and] the upward line are on His right foot,
the lotus, the thunderbolt, the svastika, the wheel — beautiful;

**69.** the umbrella and the goad adorn that same right foot;
on the left — the cow's hoofprint, the sky, the pot, the conch, the fish;

**70.** the rainbow [and] the triangle adorn the left foot;
the jambu fruit [and] the half-moon adorn that same place.[^116-32]

**71.** Such, in the attire of the best of dancers, is the Wearer of the forest garland;
on [His] left is beautiful Radhika, exceedingly enchanting.

**72.** At the eight corners of the throne are eight dear friends:
eight moon-faced ones serve Radhika and Krishna.

**73.** At the eight gates eight sakhis sit there;
in the four groups the group leaders play various instruments.[^116-33]

**74.** Such is the sweet worship of Radha and Krishna;
in this mood worship Krishna, taking pains."

**75.** And all that was in the storehouse of his own prema
he revealed to Rasika one by one.

**76.** "Being a man, becoming prakriti, abide with the son of Nanda:
worshipping in this mood, you will quickly attain Krishna.[^116-34]

**77.** This is a secret of the Vedas — no one else knows it;
only by Krishna's mercy does knowledge of the truth of prema come.

**78.** Without this prema Krishna is never attained:
Krishna, Sri Nandananda, is subject to prema.

**79.** Out of prema a gopi fed [Him] what she had chewed in her mouth;
out of prema He carried garments on His shoulder — [this] is well known.[^116-35]

**80.** Bhagavan is subdued by prema — [so] say all the shastras;
worship the son of Nanda in the mood of prema-bhakti.

**81.** Taking refuge in Him alone, worship Bhagavan —
and you will surely attain Krishna, the life of all."

**82.** Hearing Shyamananda's words, Rasika-shekhara
is drenched from head to foot by the streams [of tears from his] eyes.[^116-36]

**83.** Rasika fell at Shyamananda's lotus feet
and washed [his] holy feet with the water of [his] eyes.

**84.** Shyamananda-raya in prema embraced [him]
and with the greatest mercy blessed [him]:

**85.** "Ceaselessly Krishna sports in your heart;
you are the embodiment of love for Krishna, son of Achyuta.

**86.** With you I shall deliver all living beings."
Thus he accepted Rasika.

**87.** [Thus] took place the meeting of Shyamananda and Rasika;
now I shall tell of the instruction — listen, everyone.[^116-37]

**88.** The Rasika-mangala is exceedingly, supremely full of rasa;
hearing [it], O people, cross over [the ocean of] the age of Kali.

**89.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

**90.** Thus in the Purva-vibhaga [the author] has brought [the account] to completion —
[of] how Rasika met with Shyamananda.[^116-38]

*Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixteenth lahari, called "The Meeting with Sri Shyamananda".*

[^116-1]: Raga Kaushika — as in lahari 3 (note 1); the ghosha (refrain) is almost the same as there, and its translation is repeated: here it is "মুরারে ও মুরারে" (*murāre o murāre*, "O Murari" twice; in lahari 3, three times), and the word "ঘোষা" (ghosha) is present. There is no mangala-shloka at the beginning of the lahari: after the heading, the raga and the ghosha, the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. Lahari 15 ends with its colophon. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পূর্ব্ববিভাগে শ্রীশ্যামানন্দ-মিলন-নাম ষোড়শ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīśyāmānanda-milana*). This is the last lahari of the Purva-vibhaga.

[^116-2]: "The life of all [the world]" — *akhila-jīvana*. "So that I may describe" — *yena karihe varṇana*.

[^116-3]: Ghantashila — lahari 14, note 4; Rasika had settled there with his family (lahari 14, 7; lahari 15, 64–65). "Joyfully" — *kautuke*. In BR 15 (37) Rasika sees Shyamananda in a dream before their meeting.

[^116-4]: "Assembly" — *melā*, "gathering, meeting"; here the raja's audience hall (cf. 20). "Raja Vaikuntha" — *baikuṇṭharājā*: apparently the name of the raja of Ghantashila; the reading is tentative. "A raja [like the Lord] of Vaikuntha" is also possible. This episode is not in BR 15.

[^116-5]: "The assembly in the capital" — *rājadhānī sabhā*, i.e. at the raja's residence. "The foremost [knowers] of the Vedas" — *veda-vara*.

[^116-6]: "Inner meaning" — *tattvārtha*, "true meaning, essence".

[^116-7]: "Presented himself" — *upasana* (= *upasanna*, "having approached, presented himself"): clearly so in the 1941 edition.

[^116-8]: Arms reaching to the knees are one of the marks of a great personality (mahapurusha). "Unhurried like that of a king of elephants" — *gajendra-manthara-gati* (cf. lahari 14, note 9).

[^116-9]: "A second Narayana" expresses the onlookers' admiration, as elsewhere in the poem (lahari 12, note 43). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a pure devotee, a servant of Radha and a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, not an incarnation of Narayana (cf. lahari 1, note 2; lahari 14, note 11).

[^116-10]: "Has appeared" — *prakāśa haila*, "has revealed himself, become manifest". Prabhu here is Shyamananda.

[^116-11]: "Knows by sight" — *nāhi cine*, "does not recognize". In the "Rasika-mangala" Shyamananda comes to the raja's assembly and recognizes Rasika by his form; in BR 15 (37–44) Shyamananda first appears to Rasika in a dream and tells him that in the morning he will find him there, and at dawn Rasika sees Shyamananda coming along the road with his disciples and falls at his feet.

[^116-12]: "Soon" — *kṣaṇe*, literally "after a moment". "Palace" — *mandira*, "apartments, palace". "Each to his own place" — *yathā yā̃ra sthāna*. "Knowing for certain" — *jāniyā pramāṇa*.

[^116-13]: "In that assembly" — *se melāte*, i.e. in the same hall (note 4). "Jewel among men" — *puruṣa-ratana* (lahari 15, note 8).

[^116-14]: "This man" — *e puruṣa*; "this youth" — *e bālaka*, literally "boy". "Form" — *mūrti*.

[^116-15]: "Mallabhum" — *mallabhūma* = Mallabhumi (lahari 3, note 6): clearly so in the 1941 edition. "Lord" — *adhipati*: Achyuta was so called before (lahari 3, 54; lahari 9, 38 — *adhikārī*).

[^116-16]: "Of [his] people, one by one" — *jane jane*, literally "of each person"; "about the worldly life of each [of his household]" is also possible. "Spoke of the highest goal" — *paramārtha-kathā*, a conversation on spiritual matters.

[^116-17]: "And of all the dwellers of Vraja" — *āra brajabāsī yate*; cf. lahari 15, 7–28: Krishna's command was conveyed to Shyamananda by Sri Jiva Gosvami.

[^116-18]: "Associate of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-pāriṣada*, an eternal associate; cf. lahari 15, 10 and note 6.

[^116-19]: "Be gracious [to me] in your heart" — *anugraha kara mane*. "Granted me the sight of you" — *daraśana dilā*, granted darshan (lahari 14, note 10).

[^116-20]: Chaturmasya (*cāturmāsya*) — the four months of the rainy season, when Vaishnavas and sannyasis do not travel but stay in one place. "Holding discussions" — *goṣṭhī kariyā*.

[^116-21]: "[Forgetting] food" — *anaśane*, lit. "fasting, without eating." "In seclusion" — *nigame*, as in lahari 10 (note 17), 12 (note 68) and 13; likewise in 39.

[^116-22]: Mimamsa, the yoga of Patanjali and Sankhya are philosophical systems (darshanas). "Sankhyayana" — *sāṅkhyāyana*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; what the author means is unclear (possibly the Vedic school of Shankhayana, or simply a pair echoing "Sankhya"). Svami is Shridhara Svami, the commentator on the Bhagavata (lahari 9, note 14).

[^116-23]: 41–42 list the ten avataras in the order of the Gita-govinda (canto 1), where Balarama stands in Krishna's place: Matsya (the Fish), Kurma, Varaha, Nrisimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Balarama, Buddha, Kalki. "Bala — the son of Rohini" — *bali rohiṇī-nandana*; it can also be read "called the son of Rohini." In 43 "true nature" — *svarūpa*. 41–81 are Shyamananda's speech; where it ends is not marked in the text (75 is the author's words).

[^116-24]: The source of the account of Narada (44–45) has not been identified. Madhurya is the sweet, conjugal mood of love for Krishna, as of the gopis.

[^116-25]: "Bhagavan Himself" — *svayaṁ bhagavān*, cf. Bhag. 1.3.28 (*kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam*). The Shrutis are the personified Vedas; according to the Brihad-vamana Purana, wishing to serve Krishna as the gopis do, they took birth as gopis in Vraja (cf. Bhag. 10.87.23). The word "worship" is added from the sense.

[^116-26]: Cf. Brahma-samhita 5.29 and 5.56 (the ground made of chintamani, the water nectar, the trees wish-fulfilling trees). Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem. "It" — *yā̃hāra* (the respectful "whose [touch]"): possibly "by touching Him," i.e., Krishna.

[^116-27]: Cf. Brahma-samhita 5.56: *śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ* — "the beloveds [there] are goddesses of fortune (Lakshmis), and the lover is the Supreme Person." The words "all the men are Vishnus" are the author's own formulation; apparently he speaks of the spiritual nature of the abode's inhabitants, not of each of them being the Lord Himself.

[^116-28]: Jati, yuthi, mallika and malati are kinds of jasmine. "Kera-kera" — *kerā kerā*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; meaning unclear (possibly *keyā*, ketaki, or "bunch upon bunch"). "Strings of jewels" — *ratna-jhārā*, lit. "showers (streams) of jewels."

[^116-29]: Gorochana is a yellow pigment used for tilaka. "Fine hairs" — *romāvalī*; apparently the curls above the forehead.

[^116-30]: "Shapely" — *susañca*: so in the 1941 edition (the 1997 edition has a garbled form of the same word); meaning unclear, rendered from the context. "Armlets" — *tāṛ* (lahari 5, note 9).

[^116-31]: The Triveni is the confluence of three rivers (the Ganga, Yamuna and Sarasvati) at Prayaga; three folds on the belly (*tribalī*) are a mark of beauty. "Waist" — *udara*, lit. "belly": a slender waist like a lion's is a usual comparison.

[^116-32]: The marks on Krishna's feet (68–70): on the right — the flag, the upward line, the lotus, the vajra (thunderbolt), the svastika, the wheel (*rathāṅga*), the umbrella, the goad (*aṅkuśa*); on the left — the cow's hoofprint (*gopada*), the sky (*ambara*), the pot, the conch, the fish, the rainbow (*indradhanu*; in other lists, the bow), the triangle, the jambu fruit, the half-moon. In the usual Vaishnava list of nineteen marks the jambu fruit is on the right foot, and so are the barleycorn and the octagon, which are absent here.

[^116-33]: The eight friends (*aṣṭa-sakhī*) are Radha's principal sakhis (Lalita, Vishakha and the others). "Group leaders" — *yūtheśvarī*; the author does not say who these four are.

[^116-34]: "Becoming prakriti" — *prakṛti haiyā*, i.e., taking on the feminine (subordinate, serving) mood of the gopis. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching (Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati), this refers to the devotee's inner, spiritual identity — a maidservant of Radha under the guidance of the gopis — which is revealed by the mercy of guru and Krishna at the mature stage of pure bhakti; external imitation of a woman's appearance and behaviour (as among the sakhi-bhekis) is rejected by this teaching. Cf. Krishna as the one *puruṣa*, and all jivas as His energy (*prakṛti*).

[^116-35]: Line 79a apparently refers to chewed betel (*carvita*) with which a gopi feeds Krishna from her own mouth; 79b apparently to the stealing of the gopis' garments (Bhag. 10.22): Krishna carried their garments up a tree. The subject of the second line is not named; the reading is tentative.

[^116-36]: "Drenched" — the 1941 edition has *jaya jara*, apparently a misprint for *jara jara* (as in the 1997 edition; cf. lahari 14, 9).

[^116-37]: "Instruction" — *upadeśa*: here the initiation (diksha), told at the beginning of the Dakshina-vibhaga (lahari 1, 9–31).

[^116-38]: "Has brought to completion" — *kaila samādhāna*. The Purva-vibhaga is the first of the poem's four parts; it ends with lahari 16. The lahari's title follows the colophon: "শ্রীশ্যামানন্দ-মিলন-নাম ষোড়শ-লহরী" (*śrīśyāmānanda-milana*).


# Dakshina-vibhaga

*The Southern Part*

## Lahari 1. The Deliverance of Damodara

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda lives at Ghantashila, holding kirtana in every house; in Rasika's house he lets little Devaki hear the sixteen names "Hare Krishna"; Rasika, recalling Krishna's command and Dayaladasi's prediction, asks for initiation and receives the mantra, and his wife Ichchha-dei receives initiation and the name Shyamadasi; in the raja's assembly Shyamananda in anger strikes the distracted Rasika with his foot, and Rasika sees in this release from bondage; Shyamananda prepares to go to Nilachala and to Vraja, tells Rasika to stay at home for a while and then come to Vraja, promising to take him along from there; on the way they come to Chakuliya, to Damodara, a learned yogi; Shyamananda reveals bhakti to him, and in the forest by the river Kharva Krishna appears to Damodara with Shyamananda on His left in the form of His beloved; Damodara with his family accepts initiation; Shyamananda departs for Nilachala and Vraja; the author says he heard all this from the lips of Damodara and Rasika*

*Glory to Sri Sri Radha and Govinda!*
*Sri Sri Rasika-mangala.*
*Dakshina-vibhaga.*
*The first lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^201-1]
*Ghosha: "Rama, glory [to You]! Govinda, Rama, glory [to You]!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of the fallen,
the friend of all, the treasure of Rasika's life!

**2.** Thus Shyamananda, in the village of Ghantashila,
out of love for Krishna knows nothing [else] night and day.

**3.** In house after house he holds hari-sankirtana
and constantly meets with Rasika.

**4.** One day Shyamananda went to Rasika's house,
happy, with joy in his heart.

**5.** Seeing [him], Rasika with all his family fell at [his] feet;
in the house he prepared a seat and seated [him].

**6.** Washing both his feet with fragrant water,
Rasika himself wipes [them] with the finest cloth.

**7.** At that time Rasika's daughter Devaki
came into Shyamananda's presence.[^201-2]

**8.** Mahaprabhu asked: "Whose daughter [is this]?"
The household say: "Rasika's daughter."[^201-3]

**9.** Taking Devaki on his lap, Shyamananda-raya
let her hear the sixteen names "Hare Krishna."[^201-4]

**10.** Seeing [this] mercy to Devaki, Rasika
humbly speaks to Shyamananda:

**11.** "Listen, listen, mahashaya, kind to the devotees:
earlier Krishna gave me a firm command:

**12.** 'Your instructor is Shyamananda-raya.'
That is why you have mercifully come.[^201-5]

**13.** In my childhood Dayaladasi Thakurani
out of mercy herself let me hear the name.

**14.** Without guile that mother told me:
'The beloved of Krishna will meet [you] as [your] instructor.'[^201-6]

**15.** The guru's command [and] Krishna's command have proved true:
that is why you have unexpectedly come to me.

**16.** Instruct me in your own prema-bhakti,
by which I may attain Radha and Krishna, the lords of [my] life.

**17.** All the very names and very mantras of Radha and Krishna —
[reveal them to me] in mercy, Mahaprabhu — the truth of love for Krishna."[^201-7]

**18.** Having heard all Rasika's words, Shyamananda
at once gave [him] instruction — tantra [and] mantra.[^201-8]

**19.** Then Rasika fell at [his] lotus feet;
Shyamananda, lifting Rasika up, took [him] in his embrace.

**20.** Then Rasika went in to Ichchha-devi
[and] told [her] about Shyamananda:[^201-9]

**21.** "If you are truly my beloved,
then take instruction from Shyamananda.

**22.** Leaving all family, fear, shame, the customs of the family,
at once take shelter of Shyamananda."[^201-10]

**23.** Having heard her husband's words, Ichchha-devi, devoted to her husband, [said]:
"Whatever your path is — that is fitting for me too."

**24.** Hearing his beloved's words, Rasika joyfully [took]
camphor, betel, garlands, fragrant sandal paste,

**25.** various articles, various jewels, the finest garments;
filling trays, the companions took [them] along.[^201-11]

**26.** They were granted the sight of Shyamananda's feet;
Rasika, at [his] feet, tells him everything:

**27.** "Show mercy to [my whole] family, Shyamananda-raya:
birth after birth husband [and] wife are servants of your feet."

**28.** Having heard [this], Shyamananda-raya, with a joyful heart,
let Srimati Ichchha-dei hear the mantra in her ear.[^201-12]

**29.** He gave [her] the name Shyamadasi, famed in the world,
[and] dedicated [her] for life to the service of Krishna.

**30.** He commanded: "Shyamadasi, listen to my words:
you yourself will give the Vaishnavas food and water.

**31.** Wherever you settle by my command,
there the eight siddhis [and] nine treasures will come to you."[^201-13]

**32.** Having given Shyamadasi this blessing,
he granted Rasika the mercy of prema-bhakti.

**33.** The two always stay, sitting in seclusion;
filled with prema, they constantly read the tantra-granthas.[^201-14]

**34.** Shyamananda-raya is the embodiment of love for Krishna;
Rasika became the embodiment of prema by the mercy of [his] feet.[^201-15]

**35.** Thus one day, in the raja's assembly,
all are listening to the "Bhagavata" with joyful hearts.

**36.** Rasika cast a glance in another direction —
in anger Shyamananda struck [him] twice with his foot.[^201-16]

**37.** Having received two blows of the foot, Rasika, the crest-jewel [of rasikas],
fell to the ground, prostrate like a stick.

**38.** "Today my karma, both auspicious and inauspicious, is destroyed:
twice Shyamananda-raya struck [me] with his foot.

**39.** Today release from the bonds of material existence has come:
by the blow I have obtained both feet of Prabhu.[^201-17]

**40.** From today the darkness is destroyed" —
so he tells everyone, with tears in his eyes.

**41.** Seeing Rasika's devotion, Shyamananda-raya,
pressing [him] to his chest, weeps — Prabhu cannot restrain himself.

**42.** Thus Shyamananda spent some days,
always rejoicing together with Rasika.

**43.** Shyamananda said: "I will go to Jagannatha,
and from there I will go quickly to Vraja."[^201-18]

**44.** Hearing [this], Rasika says to Shyamananda:
"Take me with you to Vraja."

**45.** He commanded Rasika: "Listen to [my] words:
without you all [your] family will be sorrowful at heart.

**46.** Stay at home calmly for some time,
and afterwards you will come to Vraja — [so] I tell you.

**47.** First I go to Vraja — I tell [you] for certain;
and from Vraja, taking you [with me], I will go there."[^201-19]

**48.** Rasika accepted this command as binding;
from there Shyamananda set out.

**49.** For some distance Rasika goes with him;
he expounded books on bhakti and love for Krishna.[^201-20]

**50.** Coming to the village of Chakuliya, the two entered
the house of Sri Damodara Dasa Gosani.[^201-21]

**51.** I will tell in detail of the instruction given to him —
why Damodara received mercy.

**52.** The mahashaya practises yoga most intensely;
in his heart he ceaselessly contemplates the knowledge of yoga.

**53.** Most steadfast, an excellent scholar, of fathomless greatness —
Rasika knows the weight of his learning.

**54.** From childhood the two delight in learning;
by Shyamananda's mercy [he] became manifest [as a devotee].[^201-22]

**55.** Thus Shyamananda, in Damodara's house,
taking Rasika with him, speaks to him of the truth of prema.

**56.** He spoke to him of the truth of Sankhya [and] the truth of knowledge,
and then began to preach prema-bhakti for Krishna.[^201-23]

**57.** Hearing from Shyamananda of the greatness of bhakti,
Damodara began to extol knowledge.

**58.** Then Shyamananda explained both truths
[and] revealed the subtle bhakti within jnana-yoga.[^201-24]

**59.** In all of these [we] find the evidence of the scriptures about Krishna:
the subtle truth of the scriptures speaks of the marks of bhakti.

**60.** He revealed ninefold bhakti according to the scriptures
[and] its sixty-four limbs — in due order.[^201-25]

**61.** Among them the highest is prema-bhakti for Krishna —
[that] mood in which the young wives of Vraja are Krishna's beloveds.

**62.** And all else concerning the truth of prema he told him,
examining the truth of the Vedas, the truth of the scriptures [and] the tantras.

**63.** Damodara heard everything, one point after another,
and then fixed his mind on love for Krishna.

**64.** Rasika told Damodara in detail:
"Leaving everything, worship the feet of Shyamananda.

**65.** With all my family I have sold myself to these feet;
you too accept initiation (diksha) into the mantra of Krishna."[^201-26]

**66.** Then Damodara says to Rasika:
"Certainly I will sell myself to the feet of this Prabhu.

**67.** When I see some manifestation of his,
[then] with all my family I will become the servant of this Prabhu."[^201-27]

**68.** Thus for some days in Damodara's house
Shyamananda stayed, [absorbed] in his own pastimes.

**69.** One day, after the meal and so on, Shyamananda
sits with Rasika in the joy of [talks about] Krishna.[^201-28]

**70.** Damodara anointed [his] body with camphor and sandal;
Rasika, with joy in his heart, serves betel.

**71.** From there Damodara went quickly
into the forest — for breath practice.[^201-29]

**72.** There is a river there named Kharva;
Damodara came to that place.[^201-30]

**73.** A dense forest, a divine, delightful place;
Damodara saw with his own eyes:

**74.** suddenly in that place he beholds a wish-fulfilling tree,
a throne of gems, a city of jewels;[^201-31]

**75.** a youthful kishora form, dark and beautiful,
bent in three places, graceful, holding a flute and a peacock feather,

**76.** clad in yellow garments, in a captivating dress;
at His left side he saw Shyamananda.

**77.** Seeing the two present on the jewelled throne —
Shyamananda in his own form offering betel —[^201-32]

**78.** seeing Shyamananda-raya in the form of Krishna's beloved,
Damodara in amazement fell at [their] feet.[^201-33]

**79.** Tears of bliss, hair standing on end — it cannot be described,
[as he] saw with his own eyes the form of the two.

**80.** Rising, Sri Damodara weeps —
[and] the son of Nanda disappeared.

**81.** Where did the breath practice and the thoughts of yoga go!
Intoxicated with prema, he quickly set off home.[^201-34]

**82.** At home he sees Shyamananda with Rasika:
the two are sitting [talking] of Krishna in great delight.

**83.** Seeing Shyamananda from afar, Damodara
joyfully fell to the ground, his body prostrate like a stick.

**84.** In the highest joy Shyamananda embraced [him]
and, showing Damodara mercy, speaks fondly:

**85.** "The form that you saw with your own eyes —
leaving everything, meditate on that form."

**86.** Having heard Prabhu's words, Damodara says:
"If you show mercy, [you are my] shelter [and] brother.[^201-35]

**87.** I cannot understand anything of your greatness;
who in the three worlds will understand your artful play?[^201-36]

**88.** Be merciful to me, Prabhu, son of Durika:
with all my family I have sold myself to your feet."

**89.** Having heard Damodara's words, Shyamananda,
with joy in his heart, gave [him] initiation (diksha) into the mantra of Krishna.

**90.** Then his two wives [and] his fortunate mother —
the whole family, with pure minds, sold themselves at [his] feet.

**91.** For some days Shyamananda stayed there;
the three of them constantly speak of Krishna.
