**92.** All the tantras, mantras, scriptures, [all that is] full of bhakti and prema,
he mercifully told Rasika [and] Damodara.

**93.** First of all these two disciples, great souls,
became manifest by Shyamananda's mercy.

**94.** Earlier Netrananda, Kishora, Haridasa became famed;
then Rasika [and] Damodara became renowned in the world.[^201-37]

**95.** Then Shyamananda-raya went to Nilachala;
staying [there] some days, he went to the Mathura region.[^201-38]

**96.** Waiting for Rasika in Vraja,
he ceaselessly wanders from forest to forest.

**97.** Listen, all, to this account of the instruction —
words from the lips of Damodara [and] Rasika.

**98.** With faith [I] questioned the three prabhus;
whatever they told me out of mercy —[^201-39]

**99.** that account ceaselessly awakens in my heart;
now I have made [it] known, receiving the command on my head.

**100.** Whatever the son of Achyuta told me —
just so I have composed [this account of his] glory.[^201-40]

**101.** Let the learned and noble not hold faults in this against me;
listen to "Rasika-mangala", all you devotees of Krishna.

**102.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the first lahari, called "The Deliverance of Damodara".*

[^201-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of a new part of the poem, as at the beginning of the Purva-vibhaga (Purva, lahari 1); they are given in italics without a number. 16th lahari of the Purva-vibhaga. The raga Karuna-shri and the ghosha (refrain) are the same as in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1 (note 8), and the translation of the ghosha is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "দামোদর-উদ্ধারনাম প্রথম-লহরী" (*dāmodara-uddhāra*). Damodara is the yogi whom Shyamananda turned to bhakti (cf. BR 15, 55–58).

[^201-2]: Devaki is Rasikananda's daughter; the author offers obeisances to her in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1, 109.

[^201-3]: Mahaprabhu here is Shyamananda (cf. Purva, lahari 2, note 2); likewise in 17. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition Mahaprabhu is Sri Chaitanya.

[^201-4]: The sixteen names are the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare" (cf. the Kali-santarana Upanishad). This is not diksha, only the mercy of letting her hear the holy name (cf. Purva, lahari 7, note 15).

[^201-5]: On Krishna's command see Purva, lahari 14 (Krishna appears to Rasika and declares that Shyamananda will be his instructor). "Instructor" — *upadeśa-kartā*, here the one who gives initiation (the diksha-guru). "Have come" — *karilā vijaya*, the respectful "have been pleased to arrive."

[^201-6]: Dayaladasi Thakurani is the saintly Vaishnavi who let Rasika hear the holy name in infancy (Purva, lahari 4, note 18; lahari 7, 22–49, notes 10, 11, 15, 16); the text has *dayāla dāsī*. "Mother" is a respectful address to her (Purva, lahari 7, note 11). "Without guile" — *niramāyā*, "sincerely" (Purva, lahari 14, note 21). "The beloved of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-priyā* (feminine), i.e., Shyamananda: thus the author exalts him; see the theological explanation in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 14, note 11, and lahari 1, note 2. In lahari 7 (48–49) Dayaladasi calls the future instructor Rasika's "lord of life," without this epithet.

[^201-7]: "The very names and very mantras" — *nija-nāma nija-mantra*: apparently the names and mantras belonging to Radha and Krishna Themselves; it can also be read "your own." In 18 Shyamananda gives Rasika "tantra and mantra" — initiation.

[^201-8]: "Tantra [and] mantra" — *tantra mantra upadeśa*: initiation (diksha) into the mantra according to the sacred manuals (tantras, agamas); cf. BR 15, 47: Shyamananda gave Rasika initiation into the mantra of Radha and Krishna. "Instruction" (*upadeśa*) here, as in 12, 14, 16, means initiation.

[^201-9]: Ichchha-devi — *icchādevī* (20, 23); in 28 *icchādei*, as in the Purva-vibhaga (lahari 10, note 26): Rasika's wife, daughter of Balabhadra, the governor of Hijli. Shyamadasi (29) is her initiated name (Purva, lahari 1, note 47).

[^201-10]: "Truly" — *paramāṇa*, "indeed, certainly". "Customs of the family" — *kulācāra*. "Take shelter" — *śaraṇa paśaha*, literally "enter the shelter". "At once" — *tatakāla* (= *tatkāla*).

[^201-11]: "Companions" — *sakhīgaṇa*, Ichchha-devi's companions; with the verb *lailena* (honorific) the line can also be taken as "[she] took her companions along". "Filling trays" — *thāli puri*.

[^201-12]: "Let her hear the mantra in her ear" — the rite of diksha: the guru speaks the mantra into the disciple's ear. Srimati is a respectful title for a woman.

[^201-13]: The eight siddhis are the mystic perfections of yoga (anima, laghima and others); the nine treasures (nava-nidhi) are the treasures of Kubera. Here they stand for abundance: wherever Shyamadasi lives, she will have all she needs to feed the Vaishnavas (30). For a pure devotee they are no goal in themselves.

[^201-14]: "The two" — *dõhe*: apparently Shyamananda and Rasika (cf. 34); possibly Rasika and Shyamadasi. "In seclusion" — *nigame* (Purva, lahari 16, note 21). "Tantra-granthas" — *tantragrantha*: here apparently Vaishnava manuals of worship (agamas, Pancharatra); cf. 18, 62, 92.

[^201-15]: "By the mercy of [his] feet" — *rasika-caraṇa-kṛpāya*: taken as "Rasika [became the embodiment of prema] by the mercy of [Shyamananda's] feet"; grammatically "by the mercy of Rasika's feet" is also possible.

[^201-16]: "Struck him twice with his foot" — *mārilena dui lātha*, literally "gave two kicks". The author presents the guru's anger as mercy: Rasika sees in the blow the destruction of karma and liberation (38–40), since he has been touched by the guru's feet. This episode is not in BR 15; cf. BR 15, 52: "Shyamananda tested Murari".

[^201-17]: "Release from the bonds of material existence" — *bhava-bandha-vimocana*. "By the blow" — *nirghāte*, "by a blow; certainly". "Darkness" (40) — *timira*, the darkness of ignorance.

[^201-18]: "To Jagannatha" — to Puri (Nilachala; cf. 95).

[^201-19]: "There" — *tathāya*: apparently to Utkala; cf. lahari 2, 64: Shyamananda, having met Rasika in Vraja, sets out with him for Utkala. The line can also be taken as "[returning] from Vraja, I will take you there [to Vraja]". "Calmly" (46) — *niścale*.

[^201-20]: The subject of the second line is not named: apparently Shyamananda expounds [to Rasika] on the way; possibly Rasika. "Expounded" — *bākhāna* (= *vyākhyāna*).

[^201-21]: Chakuliya — *cākuliyā*; apparently present-day Chakulia in East Singhbhum district (Jharkhand), east of Ghatshila. Sri Damodara Dasa Gosani is the former yogi who became Shyamananda's disciple (BR 15, 55–58); the author bows to him in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1, 72–74 (note 37) and 96.

[^201-22]: "The two" — Rasika and Damodara: apparently friends from childhood (cf. 53; Purva, lahari 1, 74). "[He] became manifest" — *hailā parakāśa*, "was revealed, came forth"; the subject is not named — apparently Damodara [as a devotee]; cf. 93, where the same expression is used of the two disciples. Also possible: "[their learning] became manifest".

[^201-23]: Sankhya — a philosophical system (darshana) (Purva, lahari 16, note 22); "knowledge" — *jñāna*, the path of knowledge leading to the impersonal Brahman.

[^201-24]: "Both truths" — *dui tattva*: apparently jnana and bhakti. "The subtle bhakti within jnana-yoga" — *jñānayoga-madhye bhakti sūkṣma*: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, knowledge and yoga bear fruit only through an admixture of bhakti, whereas pure bhakti does not depend on them (SB 10.14.4; CC, Madhya 22).

[^201-25]: Ninefold bhakti — hearing, chanting, remembering and so on (SB 7.5.23–24); the sixty-four limbs (angas) of sadhana-bhakti — according to the "Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu" (1.2) and CC, Madhya 22. "In due order" — *nikhila-yugate*, glossed by the editor as *saṅgati-mata*, "accordingly, properly".

[^201-26]: "Sold myself" — *bikāyinu*: gave myself over completely, became a servant; likewise in 66, 88, 90. "These feet" — Shyamananda's feet.

[^201-27]: "Some manifestation of his" — *ihāra prakāśa*: some display of his [spiritual] power. Damodara's condition is fulfilled in 74–79.

[^201-28]: "In the joy of [talks about] Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera sānande*, literally "in the joy of Krishna": so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition; cf. 82.

[^201-29]: "Breath practice" — *pavana-sādhana* (in 81 *pavana-abhyāsa*): pranayama, the control of the breath in yoga.

[^201-30]: Kharva — *kharbbā*; the river is not identified. "Came" — *uttarilā*, "arrived; crossed".

[^201-31]: The wish-fulfilling tree (kalpa-vriksha), the throne and the city of jewels are features of the spiritual Vrindavana (cf. "Brahma-samhita" 5.29, 5.56: abodes of chintamani stones amid wish-fulfilling trees).

[^201-32]: "In his own form" — *nija veśe*, literally "in his own dress", i.e. in the form of Shyamananda; offering betel is service to Krishna. The 1997 edition is corrupt here.

[^201-33]: "In the form of Krishna's beloved" — *kṛṣṇapriyā-rūpa* (the edition misprints *śyānānanda* for *śyāmānanda*); the place at Krishna's left (76) is Sri Radha's. Thus the author exalts Shyamananda (cf. note 6). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, not Radhika Herself (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). BR 15 (55–58) does not describe Damodara's vision: there Shyamananda, showing him mercy, "immersed him in bhakti-rasa".

[^201-34]: "Intoxicated with prema" — *premamaye mattā*: so in the 1941 edition (the feminine ending apparently for the rhyme with *cintā*).

[^201-35]: "Shelter [and] brother" — *śaraṇa sodara*: clear in the 1941 edition (and so in the 1997 edition); the meaning is unclear. Taken as an address to Shyamananda; possibly "be [my] shelter, like a brother born of the same mother".

[^201-36]: "Artful play" — *cāturī*, "skill, ingenuity".

[^201-37]: Netrananda, Kishora, Haridasa — early disciples of Shyamananda. Kishora is apparently Kishoradasa (BR 15, 41, 60); Netrananda — cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 36; Haridasa is not identified. The 1997 edition prints "কিশোর-হরিদাস": possibly one person, Kishora-Haridasa. "First" (93) — apparently the first in these parts (in Utkala), since earlier disciples are named just after.

[^201-38]: Nilachala — Puri (cf. 43). The Mathura region — *mathurā-maṇḍala*, Vraja.

[^201-39]: "Questioned" — *śudhāila*: a third-person form; taken as the author's words (cf. "me" in the second line and 99–100); the subject may be someone else. The three prabhus are apparently Shyamananda, Rasika and Damodara (cf. 97).

[^201-40]: The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda. "Composed" — *granthana*, literally "strung together, woven". "Devotees of Krishna" (101) — *kārṣṇa-jana* (Purva, lahari 10, note 13; lahari 14, note 22).


## Lahari 2. Sri Rasika's Darshan of Vraja-mandala

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda stays in Vraja; Shyamadasi, by the order of Sadashiva Dasa, is staying in Hijli, while Rasika lives at Taniya, in the house of Ananta; Rasika tells her that he is leaving for Vraja, and when she begs him to take her along, he tells her to serve the sadhus at home and promises to take her later; through the forest country Rasika hastens to Vraja: in Mathura he sees the place of Krishna's appearance, in Vrindavana Madana-gopala and Govinda, and goes round the twelve forests; at Govardhana Krishna appears to him in the form of a Vrajavasi and commands him to return to Utkala and give bhakti, saying that Shyamananda is waiting for him in Mathura; in Mathura Rasika meets Shyamananda and asks to be allowed to stay in Vraja, but Shyamananda reminds him of the command given at Govardhana; amazed, Rasika obeys, and together they go to Utkala; at Segala Vishnudasa with his family becomes a disciple and receives the name Dasa Rasamaya; Rasika returns home*

*The second lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^202-1]
*Ghosha: "Where shall I go to find Shyamananda, my life?"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of all [the world]!
Be merciful to me: [let] me sing [your] virtues every moment.[^202-2]

**2.** Thus, having shown mercy to Rasika [and] Damodara,
Shyamananda stayed in Sri Vraja-mandala.

**3.** At that time, by the order of Sadashiva Dasa,
Shyamadasi Thakurani came there.[^202-3]

**4.** For some days she stayed in the Hijli country;
again people went to bring [her].[^202-4]

**5.** Meanwhile, after some days, Rasika-shekhara
came to Taniya, to the house of Ananta.[^202-5]

**6.** Rasika stayed there for some days;
at that time the Thakurani came to that place.

**7.** For some days they stayed, rapt in talks about Krishna;
Prabhu joyfully says to Shyamadasi:[^202-6]

**8.** "I will go to Vraja — I tell [you] for certain;
you go and live in the home of [our] relatives."

**9.** Hearing [this], the Thakurani became very sad:
"Whatever is your will, Prabhu — what can I say?

**10.** Making me leave home, you brought [me] here,
and now you go, leaving [me] alone — what am I to do?

**11.** If there is compassion [in you], take me with you" —
so she said humbly to Rasika.

**12.** Hearing [this], Rasika says to Shyamadasi:
"Service to the sadhus gives the fruit of [pilgrimage to] millions of tirthas.[^202-7]

**13.** So serve the sadhus, staying at home;
[when] I, having seen Sri Vraja, come back once —[^202-8]

**14.** then I shall certainly take you [with me]."
[Thus] he firmly agreed with Thakurani.

**15.** Then Shyama Thakurani went home;
Rasikendra took leave of everyone.[^202-9]

**16.** Through the forest country he went by the road to Ayodhya;
full of loving longing, he went swiftly to Vraja.[^202-10]

**17.** First Rasika came to the city of Mathura;
seeing the place of Krishna's appearance (lit. "birthplace"), he [sheds] streams of tears.

**18.** Then he arrived at Vrindavana-dhama;
with care he beholds Madana-gopala [and] Govinda.[^202-11]

**19.** Wandering from kunja to kunja, he sees all the temples;
one by one he greets all the adhikaris.[^202-12]

**20.** Seeing the bank of the Yamuna, his mind rejoiced;
going round Vrindavana-puri, he looks [at it] again and again.

**21.** Staying there some days with joy in his heart,
Sri Rasikananda went to see Vraja.

**22.** He views all the twelve forests one by one —
where Krishna playfully performed which lila:

**23.** Bhadravana, Loha, Shrivana, Bhandiravana,
Mahavana, Talavana, the forest of Khadira,

**24.** Bahula, Kamoda, Kamya, Madhu, Vrindavana —
and all the upavanas, as many as there are.[^202-13]

**25.** He saw all the places, wandering and wandering,
constantly weeping, absorbed in Krishna.

**26.** His mind maddened with renunciation, no outward awareness;
he roams from forest to forest, viewing the places of the lilas.

**27.** Seeing Govardhana hill, he lost consciousness;
then he had darshana of Sri Gopala-raya.[^202-14]

**28.** That day he stayed at Govardhana;
sitting in seclusion, he remembers Krishna.[^202-15]

**29.** At that time Krishna, taking the form of a resident of Vraja,
came and gave Rasika darshana:[^202-16]

**30.** "Listen, Rasika, to My words:
go quickly to the land of Utkala.

**31.** Give My bhakti to all living beings, gladdening [them],
so that they may serve My resident of Vraja with a pure heart.[^202-17]

**32.** My Shyamananda is waiting for you;
go to Mathura and see his feet."[^202-18]

**33.** Hearing all these words, Rasika looked up —
and with his own eyes saw Krishna in the form of a resident of Vraja.

**34.** Seeing [that] enchanting form, Rasika fainted
and fell to the ground, clasping [His] feet.

**35.** Rising, he saw: there was no one in that place;
he wept much in separation.

**36.** Having heard with his own ears of Shyamananda in Mathura,
he set out swiftly for Shyamananda.[^202-19]

**37.** Then Rasikendra, having seen Govardhana,
went round Vraja and came to Vrindavana.

**38.** For three days he stayed there unrecognized;
wandering, he viewed all the places where Krishna's lilas [took place].

**39.** At Govardhana he had received darshana of Krishna —
[and] constantly he weeps in the ecstasy of prema.

**40.** All over his body the hairs stand on end, [like] a kadamba flower;
tears flow from his eyes without cease.[^202-20]

**41.** Sweat, trembling, a faltering voice, rapid breathing;
Rasika rolls on the ground, unable to restrain his words:

**42.** "Krishna, lord of my life, leaving me, where have You gone?
How shall I live without seeing the boy of Nanda?"

**43.** The eight sattvika-bhavas appear in his body;
constantly he delights in love for Krishna.[^202-21]

**44.** He knows neither night nor day, there is no outward awareness;
he always meditates on Krishna, the lord of [his] life.

**45.** There is neither hunger nor thirst: he always thinks of that form;
his heart is in great longing, contemplating that form.

**46.** At that time Shyamananda, for the sake of darshana,
went from Vrindavana to Mathura.

**47.** In Mathura [he] joyfully beheld Keshava;
in that [very] place [Rasika] received darshana of Shyamananda.[^202-22]

**48.** Seeing each other, both were enraptured at heart;
Rasika fell at Shyamananda's feet.

**49.** Shyamananda-raya swiftly took [him] into his embrace;
in prema both their voices falter, tears flow.

**50.** Wiping Rasika's face, Shyamananda-raya
took him and seated him near [his own] seat.

**51.** With jubilation in his heart he asked about everything:
"I have been especially waiting for you.

**52.** It is good [that] I have seen [you]: you have come to Vrindavana.
Now go to your own home."

**53.** Hearing [this], Rasika says: "Listen, Prabhu, to [my] words:
I am thinking of staying a few days in Vraja.

**54.** I have not yet properly seen the whole land of Vraja,
hearing whose name I could find no rest at home.

**55.** How shall I go, leaving that land?
Allow me to stay a few days in Vrindavana."[^202-23]

**56.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda speaks sweet words:
"Without you [your] household there will suffer.

**57.** Everyone will lay all kinds of blame on me;
go, my child, do not make trouble.[^202-24]

**58.** You [and] I have the command to go to Utkala:
we shall give prema-bhakti for Krishna in every home.

**59.** 'Serve My sadhus with a pure heart' —
[so said] Krishna, whom you saw face to face in the form of a resident of Vraja.[^202-25]

**60.** He who spoke to you at Govardhana —
how will you disobey His command?"

**61.** Hearing [this], Rasika was deeply astonished:
"Truly, Shyamananda is an avatara dear to Krishna![^202-26]

**62.** I received darshana in seclusion, alone,
[yet] here he has told me all the details."[^202-27]

**63.** Then Rasika says to Shyamananda:
"Whatever your command, Prabhu, that is [my] rule."[^202-28]

**64.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda, greatly delighted,
set out for Utkala, taking Rasika with him.

**65.** By the forest road the two came [back] swiftly;
by way of Nagpur they arrived at Segala.[^202-29]

**66.** [There] lives a fortunate [man] named Vishnudasa;
coming to his house, Prabhu rested.

**67.** That mahashaya with all his family became a disciple;
[Prabhu] ordered his name [to be] "Dasa Rasamaya."[^202-30]

**68.** After some days they came swiftly from there
and entered Rasika's house.

**69.** Seeing Rasika, all [were plunged] in an ocean of joy;
[the news of] Shyamananda [and] Rasikendra spread [everywhere].[^202-31]

**70.** Rising [like the sun] to destroy the blinding darkness of Utkala,
the son of Achyuta came together with Shyamananda.

**71.** For the sake of the mercy of Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of rasikas],
I have briefly described [his] glory.[^202-32]

**72.** Learned and good people, do not impute faults [to me] in this;
listen to the Rasika-mangala, all you people of Krishna.[^202-33]

**73.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the second lahari in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala, called "Sri Rasika's Darshan of Vraja-mandala."*[^202-34]

[^202-1]: Raga Karuna-shri — as in lahari 1 (note 1) and in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1 (note 8); the ghosha (refrain) is new: "কোথা গেলে পাব শ্যামানন্দ জীবন আমার" (*kothā gele pāba śyāmānanda jīvana āmāra*); it is repeated in lahari 3. There is no mangala-shloka: after the heading, raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. Lahari 1 ends with its colophon at the top of. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে শ্রীরসিকের ব্রজমণ্ডল-দর্শননাম দ্বিতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīrasikera brajamaṇḍala-darśana*).

[^202-2]: "The life of all [the world]" — *akhila-jīvana* (Purva, lahari 16, note 2). "Sing every moment" — *guṇa gāi anukṣaṇa*, literally "[may] I sing [your] virtues at every moment".

[^202-3]: Sadashiva Dasa — apparently Sadashiva, the brother of Balabhadra, the governor of Hijli (Purva, lahari 10, 86; lahari 11, note 8), i.e. Shyamadasi's uncle (Ichchha-dei is Balabhadra's daughter). "There" — *tathāya*: apparently to Hijli (4), to her native place. Thakurani — a respectful "lady". Shyamadasi is Rasika's wife (lahari 1, 28–32).

[^202-4]: Hijli — Purva, lahari 10, note 21. Who sent the people is not said; apparently Rasika (cf. 10).

[^202-5]: Taniya — *taniyā*; location not identified. Ananta — not identified (cf. Ananta-raya, to whom the author bows in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1, 105). Rasika-shekhara — "crown of rasikas", an epithet of Rasika.

[^202-6]: Prabhu here is Rasika (as also in 9).

[^202-7]: "The fruit of [pilgrimage to] millions of tirthas" — *koṭi tīrtha-phala*; cf. SB 1.13.10: devotees are themselves living holy places.

[^202-8]: The sentence continues in 14: "...then I will surely take you [with me]."

[^202-9]: Shyama Thakurani is Shyamadasi, Rasika's wife (*śyāmā ṭhākurāṇī*, in short). "Firmly agreed" — *satya karila nirṇaya*, lit. "settled the promise." "Took leave" — *karila melānī*.

[^202-10]: "The forest country" — *banabhūmi*: apparently the wooded lands west of Medinipur (now Jharkhand), through which the roads from Utkala to the north ran; likewise in 65. "By the road to Ayodhya" — *ayodhyāra pathe*: possibly past the Ayodhya hills (now Purulia district, West Bengal) on the forest road westward, or else by the northern route through Ayodhya (Awadh) to Vraja.

[^202-11]: Madana-gopala and Govinda are Deities of Vrindavana (Purva, lahari 1, note 24). "Beholds" — *dekhe*, "sees," here: receives darshana.

[^202-12]: Kunjas are the groves of Vrindavana. Adhikaris — here apparently the servitors (managers) of the temples (Purva, lahari 15, note 13).

[^202-13]: The twelve forests of Vraja (23–24): Bhadravana, Lohavana, Shrivana (Bilvavana), Bhandiravana, Mahavana, Talavana, Khadiravana, Bahulavana, Kamoda (usually Kumudavana), Kamyavana, Madhuvana, Vrindavana; the text has *loha*, *śrībana*, *kāmoda*, *madhu* in short. Upavanas are the lesser groves of Vraja.

[^202-14]: "Lost consciousness" — *harila cetana*, lit. "[it] stole [his] consciousness." Sri Gopala-raya is apparently the Gopala found by Madhavendra Puri on Govardhana hill (CC, Madhya 4; cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 26).

[^202-15]: "In seclusion" — *nigame* (Purva, lahari 16, note 21); likewise in 62.

[^202-16]: "Taking the form of a resident of Vraja" — *brajabāsi-rūpa haiñā*: Krishna appears to Rasika as a simple Vrajavasi (cf. 33, 59). For the vision of Krishna commanding Rasika to go to Shyamananda cf. Purva, lahari 14; BR 15 has no pilgrimage of Rasika to Vraja.

[^202-17]: "Gladdening [them]" — *ānandite*. "My resident of Vraja" — *mora brajabāsī*: apparently Shyamananda (cf. 32: "My Shyamananda"); cf. Purva, lahari 15, note 11, where the same expression is ambiguous.

[^202-18]: Krishna calls Shyamananda "His own" and sends Rasika to him; on how the author exalts Shyamananda see Purva, lahari 1, note 2, and lahari 14, note 11.

[^202-19]: The order of events in 36–47 is not quite clear: in 36 Rasika hastens to Shyamananda, but in 37–38 he goes round Vraja and stays three days in Vrindavana, and the meeting in Mathura takes place only in 46–48. "Having heard with his own ears" — *śuniyā śravaṇe*, i.e. apparently from Krishna's lips (32). The darshana at Govardhana in 39 is the same as in 29–33.

[^202-20]: Hairs standing on end in ecstasy (*pulaka*) are compared to the kadamba flower, covered with bristling stamens.

[^202-21]: The eight sattvika-bhavas (*aṣṭa sāttvika-bhāva*) are stupor, perspiration, hairs standing on end, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of complexion, tears and loss of consciousness (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 2.3.16). "In his body" — *se śrī-aṅge*, lit. "in that holy body."

[^202-22]: Keshava is Keshava-raya (Keshavadeva), the Deity of Krishna in Mathura (Purva, lahari 1, note 26). The subject in 47a is not named: Keshava is apparently seen by Shyamananda (46), and darshana of Shyamananda is received by Rasika; it can also be taken that Rasika sees Keshava. "Received" — *pā'la*.

[^202-23]: "I am thinking of staying" — *rahibāre anumāni*. "Whose name" — *yā̃hāra nāma* (respectful pronoun), i.e. the name of the land of Vraja.

[^202-24]: "Do not make trouble" — *nā kara jañjāla*, "do not create confusion, bother."

[^202-25]: 59a — *mora sādhujana-sebā kara śuddhacite*: apparently Shyamananda is repeating Krishna's command (cf. 31), hence "My sadhus"; it can also be taken as Shyamananda's own words ("my sadhus"). Line 59b is taken as a continuation: "Krishna, whom you saw face to face (*dekhile sākṣāte*) in the form of a resident of Vraja."

[^202-26]: "An avatara dear to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapriya śyāmānanda avatāra*; it can also be taken as "the incarnation of Krishna's beloved" (cf. *kṛṣṇa-priyā*, Dakshina, lahari 1, note 6): thus the author exalts Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; lahari 14, note 11). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, not an avatara. Rasika is amazed that Shyamananda knows of the darshana at Govardhana (62).

[^202-27]: "In seclusion" — *nigame* (cf. 28). "He has told" — *kahilena* (respectful): Shyamananda.

[^202-28]: "That is [my] rule" — *sei paramāṇe*, lit. "that [is the] measure (authority)."

[^202-29]: "Came [back]" — *āilā*. Nagpur is apparently Chota Nagpur (the plateau in present Jharkhand), through whose forest lands the roads from northern India to Utkala ran. Segala (*segalā*) — the place is not identified; the edition gives in a footnote the variant *semulā*.

[^202-30]: Vishnudasa is not identified. "Prabhu" (66) is Shyamananda or Rasika (cf. note 6); whose disciple Vishnudasa became is not quite clear. The name "Dasa Rasamaya" — *dāsa rasamaya*, i.e. Rasamayadasa; the author's father Rasamaya bore the same name (Purva, lahari 1, 135, 141, notes 46, 56), but whether this is the same person the author does not say here.

[^202-31]: "Spread [everywhere]" — *haila paracāra*: Shyamananda and Rasikendra became known.

[^202-32]: "For the sake of the mercy" — *kṛpāra kāraṇa*; it can also be taken as "by the mercy of Rasikendra." "Crest-jewel" — *cūṛāmaṇi*.

[^202-33]: "People of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana*; read in the 1941 edition (a superscript repha), lahari 1, note 66).

[^202-34]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 3. The Manifestation of Sri Gopivallabhapur

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; by Shyamananda's mercy prema grows in Rasika's heart; he cares nothing for the household, serves the Vaishnavas and guests, drinks the water from their feet and partakes of their remnants without regard to caste; after Achyuta's departure the brothers quarrel, and the relatives revile Rasika and blaspheme the Vaishnavas; unable to bear this, Rasika, together with Shyamadasi, who resolves to follow him, leaves home and on the bank of the Suvarnarekha finds a beautiful hidden village — "the hidden Vrindavana"; he settles there, at Kashipur, taking with him only the family Deity, whom a raja of the Bhanja line had earlier taken by force, and serves the Vaishnavas; Shyamananda comes, and Rasika and Shyamadasi serve him; Shyamananda names the Deity Gopivallabha-raya and the village Sri Gopivallabhapur, foretells the manifestation of Govinda there, and makes Shyamadasi the overseer of the service*

*The third lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^203-1]
*Ghosha: "Where shall I go to find Shyama, my life?"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of all [the world]!
Be merciful to me: [let] me sing [your] virtues every moment.

**2.** Thus day by day the jubilation of prema
became manifest in Rasika's heart.

**3.** By Shyamananda's mercy prema-bhakti arose [in him];
apart from Krishna, Rasika knows neither day nor night.

**4.** From [his time in] the womb Rasika meditated on prema-bhakti;
then he found [its] confirmation in the Vedas, the shastras [and] the Puranas.[^203-2]

**5.** Then, hearing the truth from the guru's lips,
night and day he became mad with love for Krishna.[^203-3]

**6.** The sixty-four angas of bhakti, confirmed by the shastras —
all of them constantly dwell in Rasika's heart.[^203-4]

**7.** For household affairs he takes no care at all;
for this reason all the household suffer.

**8.** Moreover, after Achyuta's departure to Vaikuntha,
brother against brother — each against each — they quarrel.[^203-5]

**9.** But Rasika [stays] constantly in the company of sadhus,
constantly speaking of Krishna with joy.

**10.** Apart from Krishna's affairs he knows nothing else;
whatever is found in the house — with [that] he feeds guests.[^203-6]

**11.** If there is [nothing] in the house, he begs alms himself;
night and day Rasika serves guests.

**12.** He feeds the Vaishnavas [dishes] of six tastes;
he worships the sadhus as equal to Krishna.[^203-7]

**13.** Every day he drinks the water [that has washed] the sadhus' feet,
every day with devotion he partakes of [their] remnants.[^203-8]

**14.** He clears away the leaf-plates himself, with his own hands;
he gives no thought to caste — a mala on the neck is enough.

**15.** Whatever caste [the Vaishnava] may be, he does not consider;
Thakurani [and] Rasika take his remnants.[^203-9]

**16.** After everyone, husband and wife take their meal;
seeing such signs, the household burn with anger.

**17.** All say: "This son has fallen;
because of him disgrace will come upon the family.

**18.** Whose son he is — and what he does!
He will shame [us] in the society of our kin."

**19.** Thus all revile Rasika;
some to his face, some behind his back — they speak constantly.

**20.** All those words he does not value even as a straw:
the son of Achyuta does twice as much.

**21.** He instructs everyone, [citing] the views of various shastras,
[that] serving sadhus is serving Krishna, in many ways.

**22.** Hearing these words, some gain a pure mind;
[but] among them a few are evil-minded pashandas.[^203-10]

**23.** Seeing this conduct, they constantly burn [with spite];
on various pretexts, in various ways they speak harsh words.

**24.** Hearing words blaspheming the sadhus, Rasika —
Prabhu — cannot bear [it], becoming filled with anger.[^203-11]

**25.** First he deliberated with Thakurani:
"The reproaches of the kinsmen cannot be borne.

**26.** However much they say about me [and] about you — I can bear it;
blasphemy of the sadhus I cannot bear.

**27.** The Vaishnava thakura is greater to me than Krishna;
because of me he is abundantly reviled.[^203-12]

**28.** I cannot serve the sadhus without fear;
why then should I waste time in vain at home like this?

**29.** You are my faithful wife, very dear;
if you want [to be with] me — come along yourself.[^203-13]

**30.** I shall certainly not stay with all of them;
if not — you stay, and I shall live freely in joy."[^203-14]

**31.** Hearing these words, Shyamadasi Thakurani [says]:
"Wherever you go, there I too shall go with you.

**32.** What happiness would I have staying here without you?
With you, even at the foot of a tree there is beauty.

**33.** With you, even a grove I shall consider good;
be sure to take me with you, and soon.[^203-15]

**34.** Wealth without you — may lightning strike it!
Without you, what have I to do in this house?"[^203-16]

**35.** Hearing these words from Thakurani,
he set out, looking for a lovely place.

**36.** He roams, looking at both banks of the Suvarnarekha;
eagerly he saw a delightful place.

**37.** He saw a beautiful, captivating place —
is it not Vrindavana he sees before him?[^203-17]

**38.** The bank of the Suvarnarekha is very beautiful;
on all four sides groves of mango [and] jackfruit shine.

**39.** Beautiful is the sandy bank, the river is lovely to see;
its water is like [the water] of the Yamuna — I see [it] fragrant.[^203-18]

**40.** The place is so soft that it cannot be described;
however much it rains, there is no mud.

**41.** In the pargana of Mallabhumi is the tappa of Chorchita;
within it is Nuyabasan, a very beautiful [land].[^203-19]

**42.** Near it lies this captivating village;
it had been hidden, visible to no one.

**43.** That place is devoutly worshipped by Indra and [the other gods];
a place equal to Vaikuntha, [its] soil is chintamani.[^203-20]

**44.** On all four sides I see forests, fragrant;
fresh, dense kunjas, beautiful to see.

**45.** Various trees shine with various blossoms, fruits [and] flowers;
always [they] abide in the village — within and without.[^203-21]

**46.** The beauty of that village cannot be described at all;
all people sing of [it], calling it "the hidden Vrindavana."

**47.** Rasikendra-chandra made his abode there;
even with a hundred mouths his virtues cannot be told.

**48.** I shall tell how it came about — listen, everyone:
how Rasika went there.

**49.** Rasika's elder brother, Kashinatha Dasa,
made known [the village] by the name Kashipur.[^203-22]

**50.** By providence the lord of the land, of his own wish,
made his abode in the village of Kashipur.[^203-23]

**51.** Seeing that village, Rasika, joyful at heart,
went there together with his family.

**52.** From long ago [the family] had had an ancestral Deity;
the Bhanja raja took Him away by force.

**53.** [Rasika] himself went there and brought the Deity;
binding Him to his breast, Rasika set out.[^203-24]

**54.** He had great wealth, equal to Kubera's —
[yet] he took nothing of it, not so much as a sesame seed.

**55.** Husband and wife, the two of them, and with them the Deity,
left home in only the clothes they wore.

**56.** In Kashipur Rasika-shekhara remained;
in the middle of the village he built a fine house.

**57.** With Rasika are the eight siddhis [and] nine nidhis;
wherever he stays, there they serve [him] — this is well known.[^203-25]

**58.** Here all the brothers grieve without Rasika;
the property was split up, [passing] from hand to hand.

**59.** Rasika Murari is the dear devotee of Lakshmikanta:
all the wealth went along with him to Kashipuri.[^203-26]

**60.** Thus Rasika-shekhara lives there;
hundreds upon hundreds of sadhus he serves constantly.

**61.** As his heart desires, he serves the Vaishnavas:
food [and] water, [dishes of] six tastes, clothes, ornaments.

**62.** With his own hands he washes the sadhus' feet;
he himself carries away the leaf-plates, [lifting them] onto his head.

**63.** Fearlessly, joyfully he partakes of [their] remnants,
casting far away all fear for [the honour of] his family, and shame.[^203-27]

**64.** Day by day Rasika became more renowned;
hearing [of him], all the servants of Krishna come there.[^203-28]

**65.** Thus Rasikendra lives [there] for some time;
after some time Shyamananda arrives.

**66.** Seeing [him], Rasika could not contain his joy;
with his body [outstretched] like a rod he fell on the ground at [his] feet.[^203-29]

**67.** Prabhu Shyamananda lifted [him] up and embraced [him];
joyfully he spoke of Krishna.

**68.** Day and night Rasika serves [his] two feet;
I have come to know for certain: Shyamananda is dear to Krishna.[^203-30]

**69.** He worships Prabhu more than Krishna;
Rasika himself serves [him] constantly.[^203-31]

**70.** Shyamadasi Thakurani cooks herself —
Rasika's wife, descended as a portion of Lakshmi.[^203-32]

**71.** She cooks all the dishes like nectar;
with [dishes of] six tastes she feeds Shyamananda.

**72.** Afterwards the two of them accept the remnants;
apart from serving Shyamananda they know nothing else.

**73.** In body, mind and speech [they] take shelter of Shyamananda;
without guile the two serve constantly.

**74.** Whatever command Shyamananda gives, pleased at heart —
[Rasika], staking his very life, carries it out without delay.

**75.** When Shyamananda speaks an inviolable word,
Rasikendra-chandra unfailingly carries it out.[^203-33]

**76.** In Shyamananda's presence he has no awareness of the body;
constantly he serves [his] holy feet.

**77.** Lying down, dreaming, falling asleep [or] awake —
constantly he meditates on Shyamananda.

**78.** Apart from Shyamananda he has no other refuge;
Rasika always worships [him] with a pure mind.

**79.** With his whole being — at Shyamananda's feet
he has sold himself together with his whole family, and knows nothing else.[^203-34]

**80.** Such a devotee of the guru there has never been, nor will be —
[save] as formerly Krishna [and] Baladeva served [Their] guru.[^203-35]

**81.** Thus the guru, Krishna [and] the Vaishnavas
he worships as non-different, firm of mind.[^203-36]

**82.** Great mercy [shows] Shyamananda-raya to Rasika:
wherever he goes, he takes [him] there and wanders with him.

**83.** One day Rasikendra, in Shyamananda's presence,
told [him] about the Sri Murti in [his] house:

**84.** "The Sri Murti has been in [our] house since long ago;
command [us] His name — whatever comes to your heart."[^203-37]

**85.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda speaks in sweet words:
"Everyone will call [Him] Gopivallabha-raya.

**86.** The name of this village is Sri Gopivallabhapur;
here the service of the sadhus [and] of Krishna will be abundant.

**87.** There will be great joy in this village;
it will become renowned as equal to Vrindavana.

**88.** Of the glory of this village I cannot tell even a little:
here Govinda Himself will become manifest.

**89.** The form in which I behold [Him] in meditation —
that very form all will see before their eyes.

**90.** After some time Krishna in such a form, suddenly —
Govinda — will become manifest in this village.[^203-38]

**91.** The overseer of this village is Mother Shyamadasi."
From then on he appointed her to the service.[^203-39]

**92.** "Rasika is detached: he, with me,
will constantly wander to deliver the living beings."[^203-40]

**93.** Sri Gopivallabhapur, the service of the sadhus [and] the service of Krishna
he entrusted to Shyamadasi.

**94.** From that day the service grows day by day;
by [his] command the place came to shine brilliantly.[^203-41]

**95.** Shyamananda [and] Rasikendra entered Utkala;
from then on prema-bhakti increases especially.

**96.** Even with a hundred mouths it cannot be told;
who has the power to fathom that bhakti?

**97.** Only a little have I briefly proclaimed —
what the son of Achyuta told me.[^203-42]

**98.** Learned and good people, do not count this as a fault;
and do not take to heart any faults in the order [of events].[^203-43]

**99.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**100.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the third lahari in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala, called "The Manifestation of Sri Gopivallabhapur."*[^203-44]

[^203-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("তৃতীয়-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Karuna-shri — as in laharis 1 and 2 of the Dakshina-vibhaga (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 1). The ghosha (refrain) and couplet 1 are the same as in lahari 2 (notes 1, 2), and their translation is repeated; but in the ghosha there it has "Shyamananda," here "Shyama" (*śyāma*): apparently Shyamananda in short; it can also be taken as a name of Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল দক্ষিণ-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুর-প্রকাশ-নাম তৃতীয়লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīgopīvallabhapura-prakāśa*). Gopivallabhapur is a village on the Suvarnarekha (now Jhargram district, West Bengal), the chief place of Rasikananda's service (BR 15, 81).

[^203-2]: "From [his time in] the womb" — *garbha haite*, i.e. from birth (cf. Purva, lahari 4). "Confirmation" — *pramāṇa*, proof from the shastras.

[^203-3]: The guru is Shyamananda (Dakshina, lahari 1, the initiation). "Mad" — *unamattā*: a feminine form, apparently for the rhyme.

[^203-4]: The sixty-four angas (limbs) of bhakti are listed in Rupa Gosvami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2) and in CC, Madhya 22.

[^203-5]: Achyuta is Rasika's father (Purva, lahari 3, note 5). "Departure to Vaikuntha" — *baikuṇṭha-gamana*: so the author speaks of Achyuta's departure from this world. "Brother against brother" — *bhāi bhāi*: apparently Rasika's brothers are dividing the inheritance.

[^203-6]: "Krishna's affairs" — *kṛṣṇa-byabahāra*, in contrast to "household affairs" (*gṛha byabahāra*, 7).

[^203-7]: "Of six tastes" — *ṣaṛ-rasa*: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent and astringent, i.e. a full, refined meal.

[^203-8]: "Remnants" — *abaśeṣa*, the remnants of the sadhus' meal. Drinking the water that has washed the devotees' feet and partaking of their remnants are traditional forms of honouring Vaishnavas (cf. CC, Antya 16: *bhakta-pada-dhūli āra bhakta-pada-jala, bhakta-bhukta-avaśeṣa*).

[^203-9]: "Leaf-plates" — *patrābali*: after the meal Rasika himself clears away the leaves from which the Vaishnavas ate. "A mala on the neck is enough" — *mālā mātra gale*: he counts as a Vaishnava anyone who wears beads (a tulasi-mala) on the neck, of whatever caste.

[^203-10]: Pashandas (*pāṣaṇḍa*) — the godless, hostile to Vaishnavas. "Evil-minded" — *durmati*; the edition gives in a footnote the variant *durgati*, "wretched."

[^203-11]: Prabhu here is Rasika (cf. lahari 2, note 6); in lahari 1 Shyamananda is so called (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 3).

[^203-12]: Cf. Shiva's words in the Padma Purana (CC, Madhya 11.31): of all kinds of worship the highest is the worship of Vishnu, but higher still is honouring His devotees. "Thakura" — the respectful "master." "He" — *tā̃ra* (respectful), i.e. the Vaishnava.

[^203-13]: "Very dear" — *priyasvinī*: so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 ed.; an unusual form (apparently from *priyā*, "dear").

[^203-14]: "I shall live freely" — *kheliba*, lit. "I shall play, frolic," i.e. live free of household cares.

[^203-15]: "A grove" — *upabana*, i.e. even life in the forest. "Soon" — *sakāla*, "early, without delay."

[^203-16]: "May lightning strike it" — *tāhe paṛu bāja*, a curse.

[^203-17]: The Suvarnarekha is the river on which Gopivallabhapur stands (note 1). The place he finds is the future Gopivallabhapur: the village of Kashipur, which Shyamananda will name Sri Gopivallabhapur; in 46 people call it "the hidden Vrindavana." "Is it not Vrindavana" — *kibā bṛndābana hena*, "as if Vrindavana."

[^203-18]: "Sandy bank" — *pulina*: the word also used for the banks of the Yamuna in Vraja, the place of Krishna's pastimes. "Fragrant" — *parimala*, "fragrance": so in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 ed.; the rhyme with *sundara* is loose (cf. 44, where *parimala* rhymes with *sundara* in the same way), so the reading *nirmala*, "pure," is not assumed. The comparison with the Yamuna continues the thought of 37 and 46 ("the hidden Vrindavana").

[^203-19]: A pargana (*paragaṇā*) is a revenue district; a tappa (*tapā*, *tappā*) is a smaller unit within it. Mallabhumi is the land of Rasika's native village (Purva, lahari 3, note 6). "The tappa of Chorchita" — *coracitā tapā*; Nuyabasan — *nuyābasāna*. Apparently these are the present villages of Chorchita and Nayabasan near Gopivallabhapur on the Suvarnarekha (Jhargram district); the identification is provisional.

[^203-20]: Chintamani — "the wish-fulfilling gem": so the soil of the spiritual world is described (cf. Brahma-samhita 5.29: *cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu*). "Indra and [the other gods]" — *debendrādi*.

[^203-21]: "Abide" — *thākena* (respectful form); the subject is not named: apparently the trees, blossoms and fruits (45a), cf. 44; it can also be taken of the gods of 43. "Without" — *bāhāre* (= *bāhire*).

[^203-22]: Kashinatha Dasa is Rasika's elder brother; nothing more is said of him here or in BR 15 (the Kashinatha in Purva, lahari 1, 129 — in the list of Vaishnavas to whom the author bows — is apparently another person). The village was apparently named after him.

[^203-23]: "The lord of the land" — *rājya-adhipati* (1997 ed.: *rājā adhipati*); apparently Kashinatha himself, who after Achyuta's departure became lord of his land (cf. note 5; Achyuta was earlier called *adhipati* — Purva, lahari 3, 54). "By providence" — *daive*, "by the will of Providence, by chance."

[^203-24]: The ancestral Deity — *baṃśābali ṭhākura*: later Shyamananda will name Him Gopivallabha-raya. The Bhanja raja — apparently the raja of Mayurbhanj (cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 49). "Himself went there" — apparently to the raja; the author does not say how Rasika recovered the Deity. "Binding Him to his breast" — *hṛde bā̃dhi*.

[^203-25]: The eight siddhis are the mystic perfections (anima and others; cf. Dakshina, lahari 1, note 13); the nine nidhis are Kubera's treasures. The sense: though Rasika took nothing from home (54), wealth and power serve him of themselves. Cf. the Narada-pancharatra (quoted in Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.1): all the siddhis follow bhakti like maidservants. "Serve" — *khāṭena*, lit. "work, labour."

[^203-26]: Lakshmikanta — "the beloved of Lakshmi," i.e. Vishnu, Narayana. The sense: since Rasika is dear to Lakshmi's consort, wealth (Lakshmi) went after him, while at home the property was split up (58). Kashipuri is Kashipur.

[^203-27]: The leaf-plates and remnants — cf. 13–15 and notes 8–9 (here the remnants are *śeṣa*). "Fear for [the honour of] his family" — *kula-bhaya*: fear of losing caste standing, cf. the reproaches of the kinsmen in 17–18.

[^203-28]: "The servants of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇadāsa*, i.e. Vaishnavas (not a name). "Became more renowned" — *haila parakāśa*, "became manifest, famous."

[^203-29]: "With his body like a rod" — *daṇḍabata-kāya*: the dandavat obeisance, full prostration.

[^203-30]: "I have come to know" — *jāninu* (1st person): apparently the author's words; it can also be taken as Rasika's conviction. "Dear to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-priya* (masculine), ordinary praise of a devotee, without exalting Shyamananda as "the beloved of Krishna" (cf. Dakshina, lahari 1, notes 6 and 33; on the theological side — Purva, lahari 1, note 2, and Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^203-31]: "Prabhu" is Shyamananda. Honouring the guru above Krishna — cf. note 12 (the Vaishnava above Krishna). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the guru is honoured as Hari Himself because he is the Lord's dear servant (Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Gurv-ashtaka, 7: *sākṣād-dharitvena samasta-śāstrair… kintu prabhor yaḥ priya eva tasya*); Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha and Krishna (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^203-32]: Shyamadasi is Rasika's wife, formerly Ichchha-devi (Dakshina, lahari 1). "Descended as a portion of Lakshmi" — *lakṣmī-aṃśe abatīrṇa*: thus the author exalts her (cf. 59: Rasika is a devotee of Lakshmikanta); BR 15 says nothing of the kind.

[^203-33]: "Inviolable" — *alaṅghya*, "that which may not be transgressed." Rasikendra-chandra — "the moon Rasikendra," i.e. Rasika.

[^203-34]: "With his whole being" — *sarbātma-bhābete*. "Has sold himself" — *bikāila*, i.e. has given himself into [his] power; "together with his whole family" — *sabaṃśe*: with his family and household.

[^203-35]: Krishna and Baladeva served Their guru Sandipani Muni in Avanti (Bhagavatam 10.45). Understood thus: no one but They ever served the guru as Rasika did.

[^203-36]: "As non-different" — *abheda-rūpe*. Cf. note 31: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the guru is honoured as Hari Himself because he is the Lord's dear servant; on Shyamananda as a devotee and servant of Radha see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^203-37]: The Sri Murti is the family Deity whom Rasika recovered from the Bhanja raja and brought to Kashipur (note 24). "Command [us] His name" — *tā̃ra nāma ājñā kara*: Rasika asks Shyamananda to name the Deity. Gopivallabha — "the beloved of the gopis," a name of Krishna; -raya is the respectful "lord." The village is Kashipur (note 17), henceforth Sri Gopivallabhapur (86).

[^203-38]: 88–90 are Shyamananda's words: he foretells the manifestation (*prakāśa habena*, "will become manifest") of the Deity Govinda in the village, in the form he beholds in meditation. "Suddenly" — *ācambite*. "Renowned" (87) — *paracāre* (= *pracāre*); "abundant" (86) — *paracura* (= *pracura*).

[^203-39]: "Overseer" — *adhikārī*: the one to whom the village and the service are entrusted. "Mother" — *mātā*, respectfully of Shyamadasi. The second line is the author's; "he appointed" — *karila niyojitā*, apparently Shyamananda (cf. 93).

[^203-40]: Shyamananda's words again. "Detached" — *udāsīna*: free from household cares; hence the service in the village is entrusted to Shyamadasi (93).

[^203-41]: "Shine brilliantly" — *mahādīpta*. "By [his] command" — *ājñā paramāṇe* (= *pramāṇe*), i.e. as Shyamananda had foretold.

[^203-42]: The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda: the author says he heard this account from Rasika himself. The author's father Rasamaya and his family were Rasika's disciples (Purva, lahari 1, 135–141, note 56; cf. Dakshina, lahari 4).

[^203-43]: "Faults in the order [of events]" — *anukrama doṣa*: the author admits that the sequence of events may be inexact.

[^203-44]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল দক্ষিণ-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুর-প্রকাশ-নাম তৃতীয়লহরী সম্পূর্ণা"; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 4. The Meeting of Rasamaya and Tulasi

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda asks Rasika for alms — to deliver all living beings by giving everyone the sixteen names "Hare Krishna" and prema-bhakti, from the raja to the chandala — and Damodara receives the same command; Rasika begins to accept disciples — the first ten are named — and kirtana and the service of Vaishnavas spread throughout Utkala; Rasika goes first to Dharenda, ruled by the impious Bhima Shirikara, who sacrifices animals and mocks the Vaishnavas; Rasika stays with Bhima's grandsons Rasamaya and Vamshi, early Shyamanandis and disciples of Damodara, who receive him with honour, drink the water from his feet and beg mercy for Bhima and his brother; during the meal the young Tulasidasa, son of Gopaladasa, a disciple of Hridayananda, sings a song about Krishna, and Rasika listens to it in ecstasy all night; from that day Rasika takes Rasamaya's family, together with Tulasi, into his company*

*The fourth lahari.*

*Raga Mallar.*[^204-1]
*Ghosha: "Crusher of the Daityas, enemy of the Daityas."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda! I bow to [his] holy feet.
Be merciful: [let] me describe [your] glory.

**2.** Thus day by day Rasika [and] Sri Shyamananda-raya
awakened bhakti.[^204-2]

**3.** One day Shyamananda says to Rasika:
"Give me one alms with joy in your heart.

**4.** This is the alms: deliver all living beings,
give everyone the sixteen names 'Hare Krishna.'[^204-3]

**5.** Brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras — as many people as there are,
chandalas, pukkashas, Hunas — as many people as there are —

**6.** to all of them give prema-bhakti for Krishna:
this is the alms I beg of you without fail.[^204-4]

**7.** Be it a raja, be it a subject, be it a sadhu,
be it a child, be it an old man, be it women —

**8.** to all of them you yourself will go constantly
[and] make them take up the name of Hari in every house."

**9.** Hearing Shyamananda's words, Rasika-shekhara
bowed down and rose, joining his palms.

**10.** After some time Shyamananda-raya [left] that place;
to deliver the living beings he wanders as he pleases.[^204-5]

**11.** To Damodara he diligently gave the same command:
"Quickly make all living beings hear the name of Hari."[^204-6]

**12.** From then on the son of Achyuta accepts disciples;
to all he gave the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**13.** Day by day bhakti spread;
the whole world became filled with love for Krishna.

**14.** Brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras or other people —
by Rasika's touch they become exclusively surrendered [to Krishna].

**15.** As iron, touching the philosopher's stone, becomes gold,
so by Rasika's touch all people became Krishna's.[^204-7]

**16.** The whole world became filled with prema-bhakti:
in Utkala the moon — Rasika — rose.

**17.** He began sankirtana in every house,
and everywhere established the service of Vaishnavas.

**18.** The first disciples — Kalandi, Bhaktadasa the yavana,
then Shyamagopala, humble Shyamanarayana,

**19.** then Ramakrishna, Paramananda, Bhudhara,
Goura-gopala, Gopinatha, Sri Gokula.

**20.** At first these ten people became disciples;
how many became disciples after that — who can count?[^204-8]

**21.** Briefly I shall tell something of this —
in which village what pastime the son of Achyuta performs.

**22.** There is a holy place called Dharenda;
to that village Rasika set out first.

**23.** A most captivating place, beautiful to see;
the lord of that village is Bhima Shirikara.

**24.** Both have great wealth, [they are] great men,
the family of the pure gopa caste, highly esteemed.[^204-9]

**25.** They worship various gods and goddesses, installing [them],
and slaughter goats and buffaloes beyond count.[^204-10]

**26.** Bereft of sense, they kill various living beings;
they do not know who He is that is called Krishna.

**27.** On seeing Vaishnavas, they mock:
"Unable to support your family, you have left home!

**28.** Since you all cannot fill your bellies,
I shall give you all food — do this service [for me]."[^204-11]

**29.** Seeing sadhus, they mock in various ways;
the sadhus cannot say [anything] — they call on Krishna as witness.

**30.** Most perverse, wicked Bhima Shirikara;
the subjects [and] the sadhus constantly fear [him].

**31.** Giving the raja bribes of thousands upon thousands of rupees,
vying [with one another], they slaughter goats and buffaloes in frenzy.[^204-12]

**32.** They do not listen to kirtana, do not take the name of Hari;
apart from wicked deeds, they have no other business.

**33.** Whether Ajamila or Jagai and Madhai —
these two brothers are greater asuras than they.[^204-13]

**34.** From the womb of Bhima's daughter were born
three brothers — Sri Rasamaya, Vamshi [and] Mathura.

**35.** He became renowned as one of the first Shyamanandis;
with their families they lived in that village.[^204-14]

**36.** Earlier they had received instruction from Damodara:
the two brothers became true Vaishnavas.[^204-15]

**37.** At their house Rasika-shekhara arrived,
[coming] quickly, knowing [them] to be his own dear servants.

**38.** Seeing [him], Rasamaya [and] Vamshi, filled with joy,
fell to the ground with their bodies like sticks, rolling at [his] feet.

**39.** Preparing an excellent seat, they seat Rasika,
and joyfully wash [his] feet with scented water.

**40.** With their whole family they drank the water of [his] holy feet;
with their whole family they deemed that today their birth had borne fruit.

**41.** Most fortunate are Vamshi [and] Rasamayadasa:
Prabhu, seating [them] beside [him], asked about everything.[^204-16]

**42.** "Shyamananda firmly commanded me:
'Awaken prema-bhakti in Utkala.'

**43.** Taking that command on my head, I set out,
to make [people] give up wicked deeds and make [them] virtuous.[^204-17]

**44.** I have heard that Bhima Shirikara is a great asura;
how can all these wicked ones become Vaishnavas?

**45.** If these wicked ones become Vaishnavas, it will be a great deed:
seeing [them], the whole kingdom will become Vaishnava."

**46.** Then Rasamaya [and] Vamshi tell everything:
"Both are the greatest of asuras, famous in [all] the world.

**47.** If you show mercy to them,
then they will have prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**48.** Whomever you diligently favour,
however wicked he may be, will become a sadhu."

**49.** Vamshi [and] Rasamaya know Rasika's greatness;
they understood: these two will surely become sadhus.

**50.** In Rasamaya's house there is full contentment in everything;
they feed the best of the twice-born [with dishes] of six tastes.[^204-18]

**51.** Milk, curd, ghee, excellent shali rice,
fried dishes [and] sweets they offered [to Krishna] as bhoga.[^204-19]

**52.** Forming a circle for the meal, Rasika sat down
[and] began to honour prasada together with the Vaishnavas.

**53.** At that time, with [his] father, Sri Tulasidasa
was living together with Rasamaya [and] Vamshi.

**54.** Rasamaya's eldest son, with Tulasi,
from childhood lived in inseparable union.[^204-20]

**55.** At first [he was] a youth, beautiful to see:
Tulasi sings like a sweet-voiced cuckoo.[^204-21]

**56.** At that time he entered the place
where Rasika-chandra was taking his meal.

**57.** Joyfully, fearing no one, he began to sing:
"Not only is Kanu dark — he is also bent in three places."[^204-22]

**58.** [A song] surpassing the cuckoo, most captivating to the ear —
hearing the song, Rasika's heart breaks.

**59.** All his clothes were soaked with the tears from [his] eyes;
Rasikendra floated on the waves of prema.

**60.** Fondly taking [the youth], he seated [him] beside [him],
and again and again especially had [him] sing this pada.

**61.** From evening they sat to perform bhajana;
where the night went — [they did not notice], singing this pada.[^204-23]

**62.** His heart overwhelmed by feeling, the weeping does not stop;
seeing [his] ecstasy, all are astonished.

**63.** Composing himself for a moment, he asks: "Whose son is this?"
Rasamaya told everything as it was:

**64.** "A disciple of Hridayananda, living on the Ganga —
father and son — manifested kirtana here.

**65.** Thakura Gopaladasa is a great mahajana,
a disciple of Subala, devoted to the name of Hari.[^204-24]

**66.** Seeing [their] sankirtana, Shyamananda-raya
carefully kept father and son here."

**67.** Hearing [this], Rasika, joyful, in love for Krishna, [said]:
"Surely this family will wander with me."[^204-25]

**68.** From that day Rasamaya's family, together with Tulasi,
Rasika joyfully took into his company.

**69.** I have told something of the first jubilation;
listen to the Rasika-mangala, all sadhus.[^204-26]

**70.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the fourth lahari in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala, called "The Meeting of Rasamaya and Tulasi."*[^204-27]

[^204-1]: The lahari's heading ("চতুর্থলহরী") is in italics without a number. Raga Mallar. The ghosha (refrain) consists of names of Krishna: "Crusher of the Daityas" (*daitya-dalana*), "Enemy of the Daityas" (*daityāri*). Couplet 1 is marked "ধ্রু" (*dhru*, *dhruvā* — "the fixed [verse]," the song's refrain). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল দক্ষিণ-বিভাগে রসময়-তুলসী-মিলন-নাম চতুর্থ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*rasamaya-tulasī-milana*).

[^204-2]: "Awakened bhakti" — *bhaktira udaya karilena*, lit. "brought about the rising of bhakti." The subject is twofold: Rasika and Shyamananda.

[^204-3]: "Alms" — *bhikṣā*: Shyamananda, like a beggar, asks his disciple for the gift of delivering all living beings. The sixteen names are the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare."

[^204-4]: Chandalas and pukkashas are the lowest castes; the Hunas are foreign "barbarians." Cf. Bhagavatam 2.4.18: *kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśāḥ… śudhyanti*, "the Kiratas, Hunas, Andhras, Pulindas, Pulkashas… are purified" by taking shelter of the Lord's devotees. "Without fail" — *nidāna*, "in the end, by all means."

[^204-5]: "As he pleases" — *āpanā līlāya*, lit. "by his own play."

[^204-6]: Damodara is Rasika's disciple (Dakshina, lahari 1, "The Deliverance of Damodara"). The command was apparently given by Shyamananda (the subject of 10); it can also be understood that Rasika gave Damodara the command. "Diligently" — *yugate*, following the edition's gloss ("যত্ন সহকারে"); cf. Dakshina, lahari 1, note 25.

[^204-7]: The philosopher's stone — *paraśa* (*sparśa-maṇi*), which turns iron into gold. "Krishna's" — *kārṣṇa*; cf. *kārṣṇa-jana* (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 40).

[^204-8]: The division of the list into ten names is not obvious; understood thus: Kalandi (*kālandī*), Bhaktadasa the yavana, Shyamagopala, Shyamanarayana, Ramakrishna, Paramananda, Bhudhara, Goura-gopala, Gopinatha, Gokula; "humble" (*dīna*) is taken as an epithet. If Dina and Goura are separate names, there are twelve disciples. A yavana (*yabana*) is a Muslim or other non-Hindu by birth: Rasika accepts him too as a disciple. Shyamagopala, Ramakrishna, Bhudhara and Gokula are also named among the associates in the Purva list (lahari 1, 81, 88, 110, 131–132; there also "Dinashyama"). The persons are not identified.

[^204-9]: Dharenda is a village in Utkala, Shyamananda's birthplace (Purva, lahari 2, notes 6, 29). Shirikara is apparently a surname (Purva, lahari 1, note 39). "Both" — *dohāra*: apparently Bhima and his brother, whom the author does not name (cf. 33, 46, 49: "these two"). Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 9) and the author's family (Purva, lahari 1, 139) were also of the gopa caste. "Highly esteemed" — *baṛai calana*, "of great standing."

[^204-10]: "Goats" — *bodā* (cf. Oriya *boda*, "he-goat"): blood sacrifices to gods and goddesses. "Installing" — *sthāpanā*, i.e. setting up images of the gods for worship.

[^204-11]: Mockery of the poor Vaishnavas: "do this service" — i.e. work for me for your keep.

[^204-12]: "Bribes" — *nāca diyā*, following the edition's gloss ("উৎকোচ দিয়া," "giving a bribe"). "Vying" — *bādābādi*. "Goats and buffaloes" — *bodā-poṛa*: *bodā* is a he-goat (note 10), *poṛa* is taken as *pāṛā*, "young buffalo"; the reading is unclear. The sense is apparently that by bribing the raja they obtain leave for mass sacrifices.

[^204-13]: Ajamila is the sinner delivered by uttering the name of Narayana (Bhagavatam 6.1–2); Jagai and Madhai are the villainous brothers delivered by Nityananda and Chaitanya (CB, Madhya 13; CC, Adi 17). "These two brothers" are Bhima Shirikara and his brother (note 9).

[^204-14]: Rasamaya is the author's father, Vamshi (Vamshi Mathuradasa) his paternal uncle (Purva, lahari 1, 135–137, notes 56–57). Here a third brother, Mathura, is also named; apparently "Vamshi Mathuradasa" in the Purva is two persons. Bhima Shirikara is thus Rasamaya's maternal grandfather. "One of the first Shyamanandis" — *ādya śyāmānandī*: this confirms the reading *ādya* in Purva, lahari 1, 137 (note 57). "He" — *tĩha* (singular): apparently Vamshi (as in the Purva, 137) or Rasamaya.

[^204-15]: "Instruction" — *upadeśa*, i.e. initiation (cf. Dakshina, lahari 1, note 8). The two brothers are Rasamaya and Vamshi (cf. 38–49). "Vaishnavas" — *boiṣṇaba*, an Oriya form.

[^204-16]: Prabhu is Rasika (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 11). "Rasamayadasa" is Rasamaya (Purva, lahari 1, note 46). 42–45 are Rasika's words.

[^204-17]: "Virtuous" — in the 1941 edition "সন্থশীল" (*santhaśīla*), likewise in the 1997 ed.; apparently a misprint for *sattvaśīla*. The rhyme (*bāhāra* / *-śīla*) is imperfect.

[^204-18]: "The best of the twice-born" — *dvijabara*, i.e., apparently, Rasika, the son of Achyuta (or the brahmana guests in general). "Of six tastes" — Dakshina, lahari 3, note 7.

[^204-19]: Shali is a choice variety of rice. "Offered as bhoga" — *bhoga kaila nibedana*: the food is first offered to Krishna, and Rasika and the Vaishnavas then honour the prasada (52).

[^204-20]: The line can be understood in two ways. Adopted: "Rasamaya's eldest son" (*rasamaya jyeṣṭha putra*, genitive without ending, as in 50 and 68) was inseparable from Tulasi from childhood; in the Purva list the first of Rasamaya's five sons named is the author himself (Purva, lahari 1, 140), but seniority is not stated there. Alternatively: "Rasamaya, with the eldest son — Tulasi — was inseparable from childhood" (Tulasi being Gopaladasa's eldest son; cf. the lahari's title "The Meeting of Rasamaya and Tulasi"). Tulasidasa is apparently the "guru of sankirtana" to whom the author bows (Purva, lahari 1, 64–66, note 34; the conjecture there that he is Tulasi Thakura, Rasika's uncle, is not borne out here: Tulasidasa is Gopaladasa's son, 64–65).

[^204-21]: "At first" — *prathame*: apparently of that time — Tulasi was then a youth (*kiśora-mūrti*).

[^204-22]: Kanu is an endearing name of Krishna. "Bent in three places" — *tinu ṭhā̃i bā̃kā*: Krishna in the tribhanga pose. The words are taken as the opening of the pada Tulasi sings; the pada is not identified.

[^204-23]: "Bhajana" — here the singing of kirtana. "Where the night went" — *kon dike rātra gela*, lit. "in which direction the night went."

[^204-24]: Hridayananda (Hridaya Chaitanya) is Shyamananda's guru. "Living on the Ganga" — *gaṅgāte nibāsa*: apparently of Gopaladasa, who came from Bengal, from the banks of the Ganga (Hridayananda lived at Ambika-Kalna on the Ganga). "A disciple of Subala" — apparently in the sense of succession: Subala is Gauridasa Pandita, the guru of Hridayananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 16; Hridayananda is "the son of Subala," Purva, lahari 2, note 12). Father and son are Gopaladasa and Tulasidasa.

[^204-25]: "Will wander with me" — *biharibe*, lit. "will roam, spend time." "Family" — *goṣṭhī*: Rasamaya's family (68), together with Tulasi.

[^204-26]: "The first jubilation" — *prathama pramoda* (*pramoda*, "joy, festivity"): apparently the first festival of Rasika's preaching — his arrival in Dharenda (22); cf. at the beginning of lahari 5: *prathama pramode*.

[^204-27]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1. Lahari 5 begins.


## Lahari 5. The Deliverance of Bhima Shrikara

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; for four months Rasika stays in Rasamaya's house at Dharenda and holds sankirtana everywhere; Bhima Shirikara, the lord of Dharenda, rebukes Achyuta's young son for abandoning his studies and becoming a Vaishnava; Rasika proposes to summon the pandits and decide by the shastras which dharma is highest; in the debate he crushes the pride of all the brahmanas, expounding the shastras according to Svami, and Bhima with his brother and his whole family take shelter of him and give up the killing of living beings; Rasika instructs people of every caste, and Dharenda becomes like Vraja; with boys dressed as the maidens of Vraja and as Krishna he enacts Krishna's forest pastimes and returns to the village with music and sankirtana, and the people call him an incarnation*

*The fifth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^205-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda! I bow to [his] holy feet:
may I sing [his] glory in sankirtana without cease.

**2.** Then Rasika-shekhara, in Rasamaya's house,
was absorbed in love for Krishna [and] in sankirtana.[^205-2]

**3.** For four months Rasika remained in that village;
he held sankirtana of love for Krishna in place after place.

**4.** From then on he gave his heart to the first jubilation:
he delivered king and subjects — the whole world.[^205-3]

**5.** To all living beings Rasikendra gave the shade of [his] feet;
I shall tell of it — listen attentively.

**6.** How he made Bhima Shirikara a Vaishnava —
I shall tell of it; listen, everyone.[^205-4]

**7.** One day Bhima Shirikara, having called an assembly,
was sitting within his own house.

**8.** There Rasika, taking his companions with him,
went and cheerfully greeted Bhima Shirikara.

**9.** Seeing that Rasikendra-chandra in the dress of a Vaishnava,
[Bhima] out of embarrassment said nothing, [but] grew blind with anger.

**10.** Unable to bear it, Bhima speaks reproachfully:
"What have you done, being Achyuta's son?[^205-5]

**11.** You are only twenty years old —
for what pleasure have you become a Vaishnava, child?[^205-6]

**12.** Who gave you such an idea — to give up your studies?
You ran away wearing rags, knowing of the quarrel [in your family].[^205-7]

**13.** On whose word have you become a Vaishnava at this age?
How will you support your family?

**14.** Achyuta is the lord of the land of Mallabhumi,
and in his line has been born such a worthless son!

**15.** You will wander from door to door begging alms;
because of you there will be shame on Achyuta's line.

**16.** It is good that I have met you, my boy:
go back and study at home.

**17.** All this talk of dhaturvada does not become you;
I say all this to you out of affection for Achyuta."[^205-8]

**18.** Hearing Bhima's words, so harsh,
Rasika, smiling, speaks sweet words:

**19.** "Listen, Bhima Shirikara, to my words:
all the reciters of the Puranas there are here with you —

**20.** call them all quickly into the assembly:
[let them say] which highest dharma the shastras proclaim.

**21.** The six shastras, the Vedas, the smritis, the Gita, the Bhagavata,
the views of Vyasa, Shuka, Janaka and [others], Narada and [others] —[^205-9]

**22.** by [all] the various shastras I will hold a discussion today:
which dharma is the highest by the reasoning of the shastras.[^205-10]

**23.** If all the shastras declare Krishna [the highest] established [truth],
then, giving up [all else], meditate on Krishna alone."[^205-11]

**24.** Bhima Shirikara had [good] tendencies from the past,
and besides, upon him was Rasika's great mercy.[^205-12]

**25.** Hearing, he said: "These words are the very essence,"
and had pandits of that realm brought, without number.

**26.** At Bhima's command all the brahmanas came —
knowers of all the shastras, devoted to the four Vedas.

**27.** Janaki Harichandana [and] all [the rest] came;
king, subjects, bhattacharyas — all entered.[^205-13]

**28.** All sat in a circle for the discussion;
Rasika-shekhara delights them all.[^205-14]

**29.** No one can overturn Rasika's exposition:
[it is] a discussion of the Vedas and shastras in accord with Vyasa.

**30.** Rasika crushed the pride of all;
no one could give [another] true meaning of the shastras.

**31.** A single shloka Rasika expounds in many ways;
he establishes the conclusion on the meaning of the words, [taking] Svami as the authority.[^205-15]

**32.** All the brahmanas were unable to answer;
without guile they said to Bhima Shirikara:

**33.** "What Rasika speaks is the word of Vyasa."
Everyone accepted Rasika's words [and abided by them].

**34.** Hearing [this] from their own mouths, Bhima Shrikara joyfully
took shelter, with [all] his family, of Sri Rasikananda.

**35.** Those two brothers took exclusive shelter;
all [of them] — and both [brothers] — began to worship Krishna's feet.[^205-16]

**36.** The killing of living beings and all [such things] they promptly gave up;
taking exclusive shelter, [they became] servants of Krishna.[^205-17]

**37.** Rasika gave instruction to all;
day by day [people] began to come in throng after throng.

**38.** Whether brahmana, shudra or outcaste —
receiving instruction, all gave their hearts to Krishna.[^205-18]

**39.** Rasika gave prema-bhakti to all;
by Rasika's touch all became pure in mind.

**40.** The town of Dharenda became like Vrajapura:
in every house there is abundant sankirtana.[^205-19]

**41.** All float in joy, in love for Krishna;
seeing that prema, everyone is amazed.

**42.** In that village Prabhu remained, caring [for the people];
the place is beautiful to see, most charming.

**43.** Seeing all the other people, too, full of love for Krishna,
he constantly performs the pastime of roaming the forest.

**44.** As formerly Krishna, taking all the boys,
roamed the forest in play, —[^205-20]

**45.** following that, Prabhu performs various pastimes:
from childhood he has played the games of Krishna's pastimes.[^205-21]

**46.** Gathering boys of youthful age,
he dresses each according to his looks.

**47.** Stringing various flowers, he brings [them] in various ways:
[the boys] are dressed just like the young maidens of Vraja.

**48.** Among them he makes someone Krishna;
the wondrous beauty of the sight cannot be described.[^205-22]

**49.** Clad in divine garments, with ankle-bells [and] belts of small bells —
thus Rasika dresses them himself.

**50.** He himself also puts on costume along with them all;
with dancing and singing they joyfully come back from the forest.

**51.** Vina, venu, rabab, mridanga, karatalas,
pakhavaj, dampha, bamshi, sweet-sounding mandiras;

**52.** some play the kapinasha, saranga, pinaka;
they tune the svara-mandala and various [other] instruments together.[^205-23]

**53.** The boys dance, striking various poses;
Tulasi [and] Rasamaya's family [sing] sankirtana together [with them].[^205-24]

**54.** From that day all these sport together [with him];
birth after birth all these are Rasika's servants.

**55.** As in Vraja Krishna comes home from the forest,
in that very way Rasika-shekhara performs his pastimes.

**56.** Lamps, torches, chandrodayas burn in plenty;
hundreds and hundreds of people come to see.[^205-25]

**57.** Seeing [this], all the people are amazed;
all say: "Rasikendra is a partial incarnation."[^205-26]

**58.** With various songs, various music, in the rasa of sankirtana,
in great bliss they enter the village.

**59.** Day after day thus performs various pastimes
Achyuta's son — in sankirtana in every house.[^205-27]

**60.** With a form of supreme sweetness he enchants the people of the world;
to all he speaks of Krishna constantly.

**61.** Hearing those words, all rejoice;
by the mere sight [of him] all become pure in heart.

**62.** Thus at Dharenda, having found great happiness,
he remained for some time, absorbed in prema.

**63.** All those joyful [pastimes] cannot be told;
in brief I have composed a little by Rasika's mercy.

**64.** All the pastimes Murari performed moment by moment —
not even with ten million mouths could I tell those pastimes.

**65.** So the little of [his] nature that I have described —
[it is] Achyuta's son who speaks it, dwelling [in my] heart.[^205-28]

**66.** Listen, whole world, to the Rasika-mangala:
singing [it] joyfully, cross over the terrible age of Kali.

**67.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifth lahari, called "The Deliverance of Bhima Shrikara".*

[^205-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("পঞ্চম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. The raga in the 1941 edition is *nārānī gauṛā*, i.e. Narayani-gauda (Purva, lahari 7, note 1; lahari 10, note 1); the ghosha (refrain) is the same as there and in Purva, lahari 14, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title is from the colophon: "ভীম-শ্রীকর-উদ্ধার-নাম পঞ্চম-লহরী" (*bhīma-śrīkara-uddhāra*); within the lahari he is almost everywhere Bhima Shirikara (*śīrikara*; note 4).

[^205-2]: Rasamaya (Rasamayadasa) is the author's father ("the son of Rasamaya", 67); how Rasika came to his house at Dharenda and met Tulasi is told in lahari 4. "That village" (3) is Dharenda (40, 62), Shyamananda's native village in Utkala (Purva, lahari 1, note 9; Purva, lahari 2, note 6).

[^205-3]: "The first jubilation" — *prathama pramoda*: apparently the author's name for Rasika's first preaching journey — his coming to Dharenda, the first festival of his preaching (lahari 4, 69, note 26); the exact sense of the word here is not clear (cf. 28, note 14). "Delivered" — *uddhārila*: turned to bhakti.

[^205-4]: Bhima Shirikara (*bhīma śīrikara*) is the lord (*adhipati*) of Dharenda, of the gopa caste, formerly a persecutor of Vaishnavas (lahari 4, 23–33); of his daughter were born Rasamaya, Vamshi and Mathura (lahari 4, 34, note 14), so he is Rasamaya's maternal grandfather. Shirikara is apparently a surname (cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 39); in 34 and in the colophon it is Shrikara (*śrīkara*).

[^205-5]: "Reproachfully" — *dhikkāriyā*, "reviling, censuring". Achyuta is Rasika's father (Purva, lahari 3, note 5), lord of Mallabhumi (14). "Unable to bear it" — *sahite nā pāri*; the 1997 ed. reads *kahite nā pāri*.

[^205-6]: "Child" — *śiśubara*, lit. "best of children", mockingly. The age — *biṃśati baṯsara*, twenty years.

[^205-7]: "Rags" — *kānā* (cf. Oriya *kanā*, "rag, piece of cloth"); "wearing" — *pĩdhi* (Oriya *pindhi*). Cf. Dakshina, lahari 3: after the brothers' quarrel Rasika left home in nothing but the clothes he wore. "You ran away" — *pālāile*; the 1997 ed. reads *bolāile*.

[^205-8]: "Talk of dhaturvada" — *dhāturbādya kathā*; reading and sense unclear. *Dhātuvāda* is "alchemy" (the art of transmuting metals), and possibly also "the doctrine of verbal roots", i.e. learned disputation; apparently Bhima mockingly so calls Rasika's theological talk.

[^205-9]: The six shastras are the six philosophical systems (darshanas; cf. Purva, lahari 16, note 22). Vyasa, Shuka, Janaka, Narada are authorities who know the true dharma; cf. the list of twelve mahajanas in the Bhagavata (6.3.20), which includes Narada, Janaka and Shuka (*vaiyāsaki*).

[^205-10]: "By the reasoning" — *yugate*, taken as *yukti-te*, "by reasoning"; in lahari 4, 11 the editor glosses the same word as "with diligence" (lahari 4, note 6) — then: "which dharma is highest, [examining] the shastras diligently".

[^205-11]: "Established" — *paramāṇa* (= *pramāṇa*), "proof, authority". The sense: if by all the shastras the highest truth is Krishna, give up everything and meditate on Him alone.

[^205-12]: "Tendencies from the past" — *pūrbera bāsanā*: impressions (pious merits) of past births. "And besides" — *āre*.

[^205-13]: Janaki Harichandana (*jānakī haricandana*) — apparently a local ruler or notable: Harichandana is an Oriya title of landholders (further on the poem mentions "the raja, the lord, Harichandana's brother"). It may also be read as two names — Janaki [and] Harichandana. "Bhattacharyas" — learned brahmanas.

[^205-14]: "Delights" — *pramoda kare*; it may also be understood as "prevails in the debate". Cf. note 3.

[^205-15]: Svami is Shridhara Svami, author of the commentary Bhavartha-dipika on the Bhagavata (Purva, lahari 9, note 14; Purva, lahari 16, note 22). "Expounds in many ways" — cf. CC, Madhya 24, where Sri Chaitanya explains the single *ātmārāma* verse in sixty-one ways.

[^205-16]: "Those two brothers" — *yei dui bhāi*: Bhima Shirikara and apparently his brother (lahari 4, 24 and 33, notes 9 and 13; the brother's name is not given). "Exclusive shelter" — *ananya śaraṇa*.

[^205-17]: "The killing of living beings" — *jībahatyā*: the sacrifices of goats and buffaloes to various gods and goddesses (lahari 4, 25–26, 31, notes 10 and 12).
