[^205-18]: "Outcaste" — *antyaja*, "last-born", outside the castes. Cf. CC, Madhya 8.128: whether a brahmana, a sannyasi or a shudra — whoever knows the science of Krishna is a guru.

[^205-19]: Vrajapura is Vraja, Krishna's abode.

[^205-20]: "Roaming the forest" — *bana-behārana* (= *bana-bihāra*): the pastimes of Krishna and His cowherd friends in the forests of Vrindavana (Bhagavata 10.11–12 and elsewhere).

[^205-21]: "Following that" — *sei anveṣaṇe*, lit. "in pursuit of that"; the editor's note gives the variant *anukrame*, "in order, following [that]" (the editor's note is not translated). "From childhood" — cf. the Purva-vibhaga, where the boy Rasika plays at Krishna's pastimes.

[^205-22]: With the boys Rasika enacts the pastimes of Krishna and the maidens of Vraja as a sacred performance (cf. the drama Sri Chaitanya staged in Chandrashekhara's house — CB, Madhya 18). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching this is a glorification of the Lord's pastimes for the pleasure of the devotees, not an imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of Krishna.

[^205-23]: Rabab — a bowed or plucked string instrument; pakhavaj — a double-headed drum; dampha (*ḍampha*) — a frame drum; bamshi — a bamboo flute (like the venu); mandiras — small cymbals; kapinasha (*kapināśa*) — a kind of vina; saranga — the sarangi, a bowed instrument; pinaka — a bowed string instrument; svara-mandala — a kind of zither. "Sweet-sounding" — *rasāla*.

[^205-24]: Tulasi (Tulasidasa) is a singer, the son of Thakura Gopaladasa, a disciple of Hridayananda; Rasika met him in Rasamaya's house and took him into his company together with Rasamaya's family (lahari 4, 53–68, notes 20 and 24). "Rasamaya's family" — *rasamaẏa goṣṭhī*.

[^205-25]: Deuti (*deuṭī*) — oil lamps on stands; mashal — torches; chandrodaya (*candrodaya*) — apparently a large lamp with many wicks (or fireworks).

[^205-26]: "A partial incarnation" — *aṃśa abatāra*: the rapturous words of the onlookers. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 69); his guru Shyamananda is a servant of Radha and Krishna (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^205-27]: "Achyuta's son" — *acyutera bālā* (cf. Purva, lahari 7, note 22).

[^205-28]: "[His] nature" — *sbabhāba*; the 1997 ed. reads *prabhāba*, "[his] power, glory". "Achyuta's son speaks it, dwelling [in my] heart" — the author ascribes his inspiration to Rasikananda.


## Lahari 6. Description of the Wedding of Sri Sri Gopivallabha-raya

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; while living at Dharenda, Rasika plans the wedding of Gopivallabha-raya: craftsmen manifest the Deity of Thakurani, and in the house of Rasamaya and Vamshi provisions and gifts are prepared; sadhus and brahmanas are invited, Rasamayadasa performs the adhivasa and has the Deity brought, and over three festivals the Divine Couple are united; Rasika in ecstasy beholds Them, feeds the sadhus and sends them off with honour, and returns home with the Deity; the people of Dharenda, like the maidens of Vraja, pine in separation from him, while Rasika weeps remembering his pastimes there and sends them a letter describing those pastimes; at the reading of the letter all weep, and Rasika's elder brother Pattanayaka Jagannatha loses consciousness; the author extols the fortune of those who played with Rasika*

*The sixth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi — panchali metre.*[^206-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the bliss of love for all,
the giver of prema to the whole world!
Be merciful to me, Prabhu: may your virtues become manifest [in me],
may I sing the song of your glory.

**2.** Thus at Dharenda he stayed some days,
performing sankirtana with various joys.
For Sri Gopivallabha-raya in his own abode
he set his mind on a wedding.[^206-2]

**3.** Having craftsmen called, manifesting Thakurani,
he prepared there everything for the wedding.
In the house of Rasamaya [and] Vamshi provisions [and] gifts were prepared;
he tells everyone about the wedding:[^206-3]

**4.** "Two or three festivals — all of you, give your hearts to this —
I will hold in Rasamaya's house."
Hearing this, all joyfully came with every preparation,
with various provisions [and] various gifts.[^206-4]

**5.** Wherever there were sadhus — sending them invitations,
Rasika-shekhara had [them] brought.
Having brought the brahmanas, [fixing] the lagna at an auspicious moment —
the best of the brahmanas sounded the Vedas.[^206-5]

**6.** Having performed the adhivasa of the festival, Rasamayadasa
had the Deity brought there.
Holding three festivals, uniting the Two,
[he] set everyone afloat in joy.[^206-6]

**7.** [Amid] the clamour of various instruments the wedding was auspiciously performed;
night and day [people] know nothing [else] for happiness.
All, giving up household cares, are intoxicated with this rasa;
all the people float in love for Krishna.

**8.** Seeing the Divine Couple, Rasika found happiness:
from [his] eyes flowed a hundred streams.
Perspiration, trembling, a faltering voice, hair standing on end all over the body —
again and again, many times, he gazes [at Them].[^206-7]

**9.** In the great joy of the festival Rasikananda is absorbed,
intoxicated with love for Krishna day and night.
Various kinds of dishes, foods of six tastes —
the sadhus dine together.[^206-8]

**10.** Having held three festivals, he sent everyone off,
[giving them] as was fitting loads of clothes and goods.
Satisfying all, lovingly [asking pardon] with humility,
he showed the sadhus due honour.[^206-9]

**11.** Thus, having completed the wedding, Prabhu went to his own town,
taking the Deity with him.
In Dharenda all the people, their hearts distraught with separation,
repeat [the name of] Rasika day and night.[^206-10]

**12.** Children, old men, women weep and cannot compose their hearts;
night and day they meditate on Rasika.
As formerly the maidens of Vraja pined in separation from Krishna —
[so he] stole away everyone's senses.[^206-11]

**13.** And here Rasika-raya, remembering them all,
weeps in Krishna's mood:
all the pastimes he performed in love for Krishna — which one in which place —
remembering them again and again, he weeps on and on.[^206-12]

**14.** After some time he wrote a letter, as it pleased him —
in what place he had performed what pastime;
in a deeply intimate mood, describing everything as he had experienced it —
with whom he had played what games.[^206-13]

**15.** Where Achyuta's son had performed what pastime of Krishna —
of all this [he] wrote in detail:
that beautiful lake, the most fragrant places,
the dense forest, the trees.[^206-14]

**16.** As many people as live there — he named them all in the letter,
those with whom he had spoken of Krishna.
Having described everything one by one, he sent [the letter] with his own men —
Narayana [and] Ramakrishna — joyfully.[^206-15]

**17.** Having completed the sankirtana, [all] sat down in a circle
to hear Rasika's letter.
Hearing [it] verse by verse, everyone's heart breaks;
[all] began to weep aloud.[^206-16]

**18.** All, overwhelmed, hearing that letter of love,
no one can hold back [his] heart.
All float in love for Krishna, in hope of Rasika's feet;
all the people lost consciousness in prema.[^206-17]

**19.** Rasika's elder brother, Pattanayaka Jagannatha,
hearing the letter, lost his senses.
In the mood of Krishna [and] the maidens of Vraja, in the loving anguish of separation —
[such] were all those details in the letter.[^206-18]

**20.** Hearing [it], all the people weep in the bliss of Rasika's love;
some roll on the ground.
Hearing the letter, Jagannatha fell to the ground in ecstasy —
his weeping cannot be described.

**21.** As once the maidens of Vraja, in love for Krishna, in loving anguish,
hearing all those words of love —
[so] all, overwhelmed, remembering Rasika,
sing the song of Rasika's virtues.[^206-19]

**22.** Thus all the people, night and day, every moment,
meditate on Rasika's holy feet.
Blessed is the fortune of them all, [it is] the fruit of their austerities:
he plays [with them] every moment.[^206-20]

**23.** The Rasika-mangala, the song of [his] glory — sing it, all of you;
worship Rasika's holy feet.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^206-21]

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixth lahari, called "Description of the Wedding of Sri Sri Gopivallabha-raya."*[^206-22]

[^206-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("ষষ্ঠ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*). "Panchali metre" (*pāñcālī chanda*) is tripadi; in the edition each stanza is set in four lines and is translated likewise (cf. Purva, lahari 11, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title is from the colophon: "শ্রীশ্রীগোপীবল্লভ-রায়-বিবাহ-বর্ণন-নাম ষষ্ঠলহরী" (*śrīśrīgopīvallabha-rāya-bibāha-barṇana*). Stanza 13 begins at the foot of and ends at the top of.

[^206-2]: Gopivallabha-raya is Rasika's family Deity, whom Rasika brought to Kashipur and to whom Shyamananda gave this name. "Wedding" — *bibhā* (*bibāha*). "In his own abode" — *āpanāra nijālaẏe*: apparently of the Deity residing in Rasika's home (at Gopivallabhapur; cf. 6 and 11); it may also be understood as "[remembering] his own home".

[^206-3]: Thakurani is the Deity of Sri Radha, consort of Gopivallabha-raya. "Manifesting" — *prakāśiyā*: so the author speaks of the Deity's being made by craftsmen (*kārikara*). The "wedding" of Deities is the installation of Radha's Deity beside Krishna's Deity, performed with the rites of marriage. Vamshi is Rasamaya's brother (lahari 4, 34, note 14). "Were prepared" — *kaila*: the subject is not named (Rasika or the hosts).

[^206-4]: "With every preparation" — *sarbārambhe*, lit. "with all undertakings".

[^206-5]: Lagna (*lagna*) — the moment astrologically auspicious for a rite.

[^206-6]: Adhivasa (*adhibāsa*) — the preliminary rite of consecration on the eve of a festival (anointing with fragrances, etc.). Rasamayadasa is Rasamaya, the author's father. "Had the Deity brought" — apparently Gopivallabha-raya, from Gopivallabhapur to Dharenda (cf. 11). "The Two" — *dõhāra*: Gopivallabha and Thakurani.

[^206-7]: The Divine Couple — *yugala-rūpa*, "the form of the Couple", Radha and Krishna. Perspiration, trembling, a faltering voice, hair standing on end, tears are the sattvika-bhavas, bodily signs of ecstatic love (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 2.3).

[^206-8]: "Six tastes" — Dakshina, lahari 3, note 7. "Dine together" — *bhojana saṅgati*, "a common meal".

[^206-9]: "[Asking pardon] with humility" — *binaẏa kariẏā*: so guests are customarily seen off, with a request to forgive the shortcomings of the hospitality. "Showed due honour" — *karila byabahāra*, lit. "dealt [as was proper]".

[^206-10]: Prabhu is Rasika (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 11). "His own town" — *nija-purī*: apparently Gopivallabhapur. "Repeat [the name of] Rasika" — *rasika japai*.

[^206-11]: The gopis pining in separation from Krishna when He left for Mathura (Bhagavata 10.39; 10.47). "Stole away" — *hari' nilā*: the subject is not named — apparently Rasika (or the separation itself).

[^206-12]: "Here" — *ethā*: apparently at Gopivallabhapur. "In Krishna's mood" — *kṛṣṇa-bhābe*: apparently like Krishna longing in Mathura for Vraja (cf. 12); it may also be understood as "in love for Krishna". "Which one in which place" — his pastimes at Dharenda (lahari 5, 43–59).

[^206-13]: "As it pleased him" — *abhimata*, "as desired, at [his own] discretion." "In an intimate mood" — *rahasya-bhābe*. "As he had experienced it" — *anubhabe*. "Games" — *khelā*: Rasika's pastimes with the boys and people of Dharenda (lahari 5, 43–59).

[^206-14]: "Achyuta's son" — *acyuta-bālā* (lahari 5, note 27). "Wrote" — in the 1941 edition *lekhilũ*, in the 1997 edition *lekhila*, "wrote"; translated by the sense (the subject is Rasika, cf. 14, 16). The lake and groves of Dharenda are not identified.

[^206-15]: Narayana and Ramakrishna (*nārāẏaṇa rāmakṛṣṇa*) — apparently two disciples of Rasika sent as messengers; Ramakrishna is named among his first disciples (lahari 4, 19, note 8). "Joyfully" — *raṅge*.

[^206-16]: "Verse by verse" — *eka eka pada*: *pada* is "line, verse" (or "song"; the letter was perhaps written in verse). "Heart" — *prāṇī* (= *prāṇa*, "life, soul").

[^206-17]: "In hope of Rasika's feet" — *rasika-caraṇa āśe*. "Lost consciousness" — *agiẏāna*; the editor glosses it in a footnote as "অজ্ঞান" (the editor's note is not translated).

[^206-18]: Rasika's elder brother — *rasikera jyeṣṭha bhrātaḥ*; "Pattanayaka" (*paṭṭanāeka*) is an honorific title also borne by Rasika's father Achyuta (Purva, lahari 3, note 23). In Dakshina 3 (49) Rasika's elder brother is named Kashinatha Dasa (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 22); whether Jagannatha is another elder brother or this is a discrepancy is unclear. Where he heard the letter — in Dharenda or in Rasika's family home — the author does not say. The second half of the stanza is understood as describing the content of the letter: Rasika writes of his pastimes in the mood of separation of Krishna and the gopis (cf. 13, note 12).

[^206-19]: Cf. the gopis hearing Krishna's message brought by Uddhava (Bhagavata 10.47). "In love for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-bhābe*. "Remembering" — *samariẏā* (= *smariẏā*).

[^206-20]: "Austerities" — *tapasyā*. The last line is understood thus: the fortune of those with whom Rasika played (14) is the fruit of their past austerities; it can also be understood as "[in meditation] he plays with them every moment."

[^206-21]: The author's signature is given in the standard formula (§ 4); here it is in tripadi metre and reads slightly differently: "Placing Shyamananda's feet joyfully on his head, the son of Rasamaya sings" (cf. Purva, lahari 5, note 14).

[^206-22]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 7. The Manifestation of the Sixty-four Limbs of Bhakti

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika lives in his own home, and day by day prema-bhakti grows, and service is rendered to thousands of Vaishnavas; he honours the sadhus more than Krishna and himself dresses Sri Gopivallabha-raya with Thakurani; the author lists how Rasika firmly practises the sixty-four limbs of bhakti — from taking shelter of the guru to residing in Mathura in his mind — and, practising them himself, teaches them to others; a mere glance from him is enough for a person to surrender exclusively to Krishna; Rasika never transgresses the orders of the guru, Krishna and the sadhus, is ready to give himself with his whole family to the sadhus, and honours anyone on whom he sees the mark of a Vaishnava as equal to Krishna, be he a brahmana or a Huna or a mleccha; by his mercy all become pure in heart*

*The seventh lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^207-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Pay heed to fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of the world,
the dear treasure of the life of Rasika-deva!

**2.** Thus Rasika remains in his own home;
day by day he awakened prema-bhakti.

**3.** Day by day [his] radiance grew ever greater:
to thousands upon thousands of Vaishnavas daily service is rendered.

**4.** He honours the sadhus more than Krishna;
apart from service to the sadhus he knows nothing else.[^207-2]

**5.** Day by day the service grew greatly;
apart from Krishna, Achyuta's son knows [nothing].

**6.** Sri Gopivallabha-raya together with Thakurani
he himself, sitting down, joyfully dresses.[^207-3]

**7.** On different days he arranges different dresses in different ways;
apart from service to Krishna he knows [nothing], day or night.

**8.** The sixty-four limbs of bhakti he performs without cease;
practising [them] himself, he diligently teaches [them] to all.[^207-4]

**9.** One by one he always performs all [the limbs of] bhakti;
Rasika's deeds cannot be described.

**10.** Firmly he took shelter of Sri Guru;
firmly [he took] initiation into [the service of] Krishna and so on [and] certainly learned [from the guru].[^207-5]

**11.** With firm faith he served Sri Guru;
whatever path the sadhus speak of — that he firmly follows.

**12.** Firmly he inquires about the true dharma from the sadhus;
firmly in mind he renounces enjoyment for Krishna's sake.[^207-6]

**13.** Firmly Rasika-ramana wanders through holy places —
in Dvaraka, on the Ganga, in Vraja, near Krishna.[^207-7]

**14.** Firmly [keeping] all the customs of which all people speak,
he does only what is needed for the purpose — beyond that nothing for himself.[^207-8]

**15.** Firmly he honours the day of Hari;
[he honours] the ashvattha, tulasi, dhatri, all holy places.[^207-9]

**16.** Living beings averse to Krishna he avoids from afar;
he has no desire to make many disciples.[^207-10]

**17.** Great undertakings and the like he never begins;
by his very nature [he is such] an auspicious undertaking as is not found in the three worlds.[^207-11]

**18.** The many books [and] arts that turn one away from Krishna —
knowing their nature, he does not study them.

**19.** Avoiding disputes, he delights everyone [with his] explanation;
in his dealings he shows no miserliness at all.[^207-12]

**20.** From grief and the like he is free;
other gods he never disdains.

**21.** He causes no distress to any living being on earth;
never are there offences in his service or toward the [holy] name.

**22.** Haters of Krishna, haters of the devotees, all who revile [them] —
with them he never keeps company.[^207-13]

**23.** All the marks of a Vaishnava are on Rasika's body:
he writes the syllables of Hari's name on every part of the body.[^207-14]

**24.** Nirmalya and the like he [accepts] before Krishna;
dancing, prostrating [in obeisance] like a rod — he performs them one by one.[^207-15]

**25.** Firmly he rises to greet the sadhus on seeing them;
seeing the sadhus, he accompanies [them] and brings [them to his home].[^207-16]

**26.** Temples, the Sri Murti and the like, all holy places —
the fortunate Rasika circumambulates them.

**27.** Firmly Rasikendra worships Krishna;
firmly Rasika-shekhara performs service.[^207-17]

**28.** With a sweet voice he sings songs before Krishna,
now sankirtana, now japa.

**29.** Joyfully Rasikendra recites hymns;
he tastes the naivedya, the water [that bathed the] feet, the nectar.[^207-18]

**30.** He inhales the fragrance of incense, garlands, sandal and the like;
he touches the Sri Murti — [as] the shastras enjoin.

**31.** He firmly beholds Krishna
[and] the aratis and all of Krishna's festivals.

**32.** Firmly he hears of Krishna's virtues and glory;
humbly he entreats Krishna, crying out [to Him].[^207-19]

**33.** Firmly he remembers Krishna's virtues and names;
firmly Rasika meditates on Krishna.

**34.** Sometimes he [is] with Krishna in the mood of a servant,
sometimes in the love of a friend for Krishna.

**35.** Sometimes with Krishna — in the rasa of prema-bhakti:
in those eight sattvika-bhavas he floats in the bliss of prema.[^207-20]

**36.** Rasika surrenders himself to Krishna;
all that is dear to him he offers to Krishna.

**37.** He makes various endeavours for Krishna's sake;
with his whole being Rasika is under Krishna's shelter.

**38.** Ceaselessly he serves Krishna's devotees;
he worships the feet of a devotee, honouring [him] as equal to Krishna.

**39.** As equal to Krishna he worships according to the rules
tulasi, the shastras, Mathura, the Vaishnavas and so on.[^207-21]

**40.** According to [his] means gathering all that is needed for this,
Rasika holds festivals together with his circle.

**41.** In Karttika he performs special service to Krishna;
[he celebrates] the yatras, the [festival of His] birth and all the rest, dedicating [them to Him].[^207-22]

**42.** The feet of the Sri Murti, with special affection,
Rasika-chandra worships with firm feeling in his heart.

**43.** Discourses on the Bhagavata, together with his circle,
Rasika-chandra relishes in every way.[^207-23]

**44.** Seeing excellent sadhus alike [to himself] in all aspirations,
with such sadhus he keeps company without cease.[^207-24]

**45.** Rasika always performs nama-sankirtana;
in his mind Achyuta's son dwells in Mathura.[^207-25]

**46.** Rasika's bhakti cannot be described:
that great soul is bhakti for Krishna embodied.[^207-26]

**47.** To whomever Rasika-shekhara shows mercy,
he becomes devoted to the sixty-four [limbs of] bhakti.

**48.** By the mere sight [of him one] surrenders exclusively [to Krishna]:
apart from Krishna, no one knows anything else.

**49.** He manifested the feeling of love for Krishna in all directions;
by Rasika's mercy [people] came to love Krishna.

**50.** Day by day prema-bhakti arose:
[this] Shyamananda [and] Rasika-raya brought about.[^207-27]

**51.** In meditation, in shelter and the like, in sleeping [and] eating,
Rasika knows nothing apart from Shyamananda.[^207-28]

**52.** Whether at home, within, or in other lands,
Rasikendra serves the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus.

**53.** Practising [this] himself, he teaches all people;
seeing [his] bhakti, the three worlds are amazed.

**54.** The orders of the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus he does not transgress:
Rasika-chandra carries [them] out, staking [his very] life.

**55.** Whatever a sadhu orders — feasible [or] unfeasible —
Achyuta's son unfailingly does it with joy.[^207-29]

**56.** Should a sadhu [wish to] sell [or] buy Rasika with his whole family,
Rasika with his whole family gives himself up for sale with a joyful heart.[^207-30]

**57.** In whomever he sees even a mere mark of a Vaishnava,
him he firmly worships as equal to Krishna.

**58.** Be it a brahmana, be it a sannyasi, be it a shudra and others,
Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas, antyajas, Pukkashas and others —[^207-31]

**59.** all are filled with bliss at Rasika's touch:
apart from Krishna, the lord of their life, they care for nothing [else].[^207-32]

**60.** Thus at home Rasika Mahashaya
with an unshakable heart serves the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus.

**61.** To all living beings he gave prema-bhakti,
explaining the truth and meaning of the Vedas and shastras.

**62.** Day by day prema-bhakti kept growing;
by Rasika's mercy all became pure in mind.

**63.** Rasika's greatness cannot be described:
he is endowed with all virtues, [he is] the very majesty of loveliness.

**64.** By his grace I have made known a little
of the holy fame and glory of Shyamananda [and] Rasika.[^207-33]

**65.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**66.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the seventh lahari, called "The Manifestation of the Sixty-four Limbs of Bhakti."*[^207-34]

[^207-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("সপ্তম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; cf. Dakshina, lahari 6, note 1). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. "Pay heed" — *kara abadhāna*; the 1997 edition has *anudhāna*. The title follows the colophon: "চতুঃষষ্টি-ভক্ত্যঙ্গ-প্রকাশ-নাম সপ্তম-লহরী" (*catuḥṣaṣṭi-bhaktyaṅga-prakāśa*).

[^207-2]: "More than Krishna" — *kṛṣṇake ādhikya kari'*, lit. "making [them] higher than Krishna." Cf. the Padma Purana (CC, Madhya 11.31): of all kinds of worship the highest is the worship of Vishnu, but higher still is the worship of His devotees (*tadīyānāṃ samarcanam*).

[^207-3]: Thakurani — apparently the Deity of Sri Radha, whose "wedding" with Gopivallabha-raya is described in lahari 6 (note 3). In Dakshina 3 Rasika's wife Shyamadasi is called Thakurani (Dakshina, lahari 3, 15); then one could read: "together with Thakurani [Shyamadasi] he himself… dresses Sri Gopivallabha-raya." "Dresses" — *beśa karāẏena*, a causative form: "has [Them] dressed" or "attires."

[^207-4]: The sixty-four angas (limbs) of bhakti — Dakshina, lahari 3, note 4. Below (10–45) the author lists them in almost the same order as the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2.74–92) and CC (Madhya 22.115–128), repeating "firmly" (*dṛṛhe*, *dṛṛhabhābe*); the notes below mark only departures and unclear places. "Diligently" — *tatpara*; it can also be read "teaches all [to be] devoted [to them]."

[^207-5]: Cf. in the list of angas: taking shelter of the guru's feet, initiation (*dīkṣā*) and instruction (*śikṣā*) from the guru, serving the guru with trust, following the path of the sadhus. "Certainly learned" — *śikhila niścaẏa*.

[^207-6]: "Inquires about the true dharma" — *saddharma-pṛcchā*, as in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (*sad-dharma-pṛcchā*). "Renounces enjoyment for Krishna's sake" — *bhoga-tyāga kṛṣṇera nimitte*.

[^207-7]: "Rasika-ramana" — *rasika-ramaṇa*, apparently an epithet of Rasika ("delightful Rasika"; cf. "Rasika-shekhara," "Rasika-chandra"). The anga is residing in Krishna's holy places (Dvaraka and others) and by the Ganga. "Near Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-sannidhāne*.

[^207-8]: The couplet corresponds to the anga *yāvad-artha-anuvartitā* — "accepting only as much as is needed" for life and service. Reading by the 1941 edition: *dṛṛhe sarbajana kaẏe saba byabahāra / sei kare ye arthe byatīta āpanāra* (the 1997 edition has *artha*); the sense of the first line is unclear, the translation is tentative.

[^207-9]: The day of Hari (*haribāsara*) is Ekadashi. Dhatri (*dhātrī*) is the amalaki tree. In the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu the anga is honouring the ashvattha (sacred fig), tulasi, dhatri, cows, brahmanas and Vaishnavas; the author adds "all holy places."

[^207-10]: 16–22 are the angas of "rejection": giving up the company of those averse to Krishna, not making many disciples, not undertaking great enterprises, not studying many books, avoiding disputes, not being miserly, not yielding to grief, not disdaining the demigods, not distressing living beings, avoiding offences in service and to the holy name, not tolerating blasphemy of Krishna and His devotees.

[^207-11]: "Great undertakings" — *mahā ārambha*: elaborate worldly enterprises. The second line is understood tentatively: *sbabhābe ye śubhārambha nāi tribhubane*; it can also be read "by nature [he needs no] auspicious undertakings [such as abound] in the three worlds."

[^207-12]: The Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu has "avoiding the study of many books, commentaries and disputes" (*bahu-granthakalābhyāsa-vyākhyā-vāda-vivarjanam*); in the author's version, on the contrary, Rasika's explanation (*byākhyā*) delights everyone. "Shows no miserliness in his dealings" — *byabahāre akārpaṇya*.

[^207-13]: In the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu the anga is not tolerating blasphemy of Krishna and His devotees; the author renders it as avoiding the company of blasphemers.

[^207-14]: The marks of a Vaishnava — tilaka, tulasi beads and so on. "The syllables of Hari's name" — *harināmākṣara*: names of Hari that Vaishnavas write on the body with gopi-chandana clay.

[^207-15]: Nirmalya (*nirmālya*) — the remnants of what was offered to the Deity: garlands, flowers and so on; the anga is wearing them. "Prostrating like a rod" — *daṇḍa-paraṇāma*, dandavat. "One by one" — *eke eke*, i.e. he performs each of the angas.

[^207-16]: "Rises to greet" — *abhyarthanā* (cf. *abhyutthāna*); "accompanies" — *anubraje*. In the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu both angas concern the Deity (rising at His appearance, following His procession); the author applies them to the sadhus.

[^207-17]: "Rasika-shekhara" — *rasikaśekhare*, apparently the subject form (agentive in *-e*); it can also be read "serves Rasika-shekhara," but the whole list speaks of Rasika. The angas are worship (*pūjā*) and service (*paricaryā*) of the Deity.

[^207-18]: Naivedya — food offered to the Deity. "The water [that bathed the] feet" — *pādya*: charanamrita. "Nectar" — *makaranda*, lit. "flower nectar," apparently also charanamrita, or honey offered to the Deity.

[^207-19]: "Humbly entreats, crying out" — *binaẏa… kariẏā kākuti*: the anga *vijñapti*, humble supplication.

[^207-20]: In the list of the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, dasya and sakhya are followed by self-surrender (*ātma-nivedana*, 36); couplet 35 is the author's own addition. The eight sattvika-bhavas — becoming stunned, perspiration, hair standing on end, faltering voice, trembling, change of complexion, tears, fainting (cf. Dakshina, lahari 6, note 7).

[^207-21]: The anga is serving what is connected with Krishna (*tadīya*): tulasi, the shastras, Mathura, the Vaishnavas.

[^207-22]: Karttika (*kārttika*, *ūrja*; October–November) is the month of special service to Krishna. "Yatras" are festive processions of the Deity; "the [festival of His] birth" is Janmashtami. "Dedicating" — *kariẏā uddeśa*, lit. "with [Him] in view, on the occasion."

[^207-23]: The Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu has relishing the meaning of the Bhagavata together with *rasikas*, connoisseurs of rasa; the author says "together with his circle" (*sagoṣṭhī*).

[^207-24]: The anga is association with sadhus who are like-minded, affectionate and more advanced (*sajātīyāśaye snigdhe sādhau saṅgaḥ svato vare*). The word in the 1941 edition and in the 1997 edition is *kāmpe*; understood as *kāmye*, "in aspirations"; the reading is unclear.

[^207-25]: The anga is residing in Mathura-mandala; the author says "dwells in Mathura in his mind" (*mane mathurāte sthiti*).

[^207-26]: "Embodied" — *mūrtimanta*, "having taken form." Mahashaya — respectful "great soul."

[^207-27]: "Shyamananda [and] Rasika-raya brought about" — *karilena śyāmānanda rasika rāẏa*; it could also be read "Rasika-raya made [manifest the bhakti of] Shyamananda," but there appear to be two subjects (cf. lahari 4, 2, note 2).

[^207-28]: "In shelter" — *śaraṇa*; possibly for *smaraṇa*, "remembrance." Rasika is wholly absorbed in thoughts of his guru.

[^207-29]: "Feasible [or] unfeasible" — *sughaṭana durghaṭana*, "easy [or] difficult, possible [or] impossible."

[^207-30]: "Sell [or] buy" — *bice kine*; "gives himself up for sale" — *bikāẏa*, "is sold": Rasika with his whole family is entirely at the sadhus' disposal, like a purchased servant.

[^207-31]: Sannyasi — *nyāsī*. Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas, Pukkashas — foreigners and the lowest classes; antyajas — untouchables (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 4; Dakshina, lahari 5, note 18).

[^207-32]: "Care for nothing" — *nāi bāse*, lit. "feel [attraction] for nothing."

[^207-33]: "By his grace" — *tā̃ra anugrahe*: apparently by Rasika's grace (cf. Dakshina, lahari 5, 65, note 28). "I have made known" — *karila bidita*, by the sense about himself (the author).

[^207-34]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 8. The Display of Devotion to the Guru

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasika; the author praises Rasika's virtues — his beauty, learning, eloquence, humility and mercy to all living beings — and blesses Utkala, his parents, his village and all who see his feet; Shyamananda comes to Balarampur, where he gains many disciples, and sends Rasika a letter: "Come to me quickly"; the letter reaches Rasika at his meal, and without finishing he rises at once and goes alone, at dusk and in the rain, through a forest where tigers, rhinoceroses and elephants live; Shyamananda, learning from the servants how he travelled, is grieved, tells him to convert the forest country (Vanabhumi), and plans the Panchama-dola festival in the month of Vaishakha at Barakola; the author urges that their pastimes not be considered human*

*The eighth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^208-1]
*Ghosha: "Having beheld the moon-like face — not seeing [that] beauty, I die:*
*how can a woman keep her life?"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the moon of the gopa clan!
Glory to Rasikendra-chandra, the beloved of Krishna![^208-2]

**2.** Thus day by day the awakening of bhakti
Achyuta's son brought about in all lands.

**3.** Rasika's deeds are exceedingly, supremely deep:
all his virtues and deeds cannot be described.

**4.** Like Vyasa, Narada and others, [as] equal to Narayana,
the people of the world worship [him], calling [him] Ishvara.[^208-3]

**5.** All the virtues that Krishna, the life of the world, possesses —
all those marks abide in Rasika's body.[^208-4]

**6.** Exceedingly lovely is the body of Rasika-shekhara;
endowed with every auspicious mark is the best one, Rasikendra.

**7.** He is so lovely that it cannot be told;
wholly full of radiance is the form of Achyuta's son.

**8.** Mighty with the strength of bhakti, youthful — [immersed] in bhajana,
in bhajana his form is wholly absorbed [in it], ever young.[^208-5]

**9.** In various lands, in various languages — wondrous speech
Rasika-chand utters, with rare skill.[^208-6]

**10.** Of all truths speaks the son of Achyuta;
like nectar are the words he speaks.

**11.** A great orator, an excellent scholar, he has no equal;
no one has an intelligence equal to Rasika's.

**12.** If [he] is answered, he gives a reply to the answer;
expert in every virtue is Rasika, the jewel of virtues.

**13.** Rasika-shekhara is full of great resourcefulness;
the son of Achyuta is perfect in the refined arts.

**14.** The crest-jewel of the clever is Achyuta's son;
adept in all tasks, discerning is the great soul.

**15.** All the dharmas of good deeds he knows directly;
constantly he keeps firmly the vow [of service] to Krishna.[^208-7]

**16.** Rasikendra is renowned [for knowing] place, time and the worthy;
the scriptures are his constant sight: [for this] he is famed in the world.[^208-8]

**17.** Exceedingly pure is Prabhu, the life of the world;
by love of Krishna he has won over these three worlds.

**18.** Supremely steady is Rasika-shekhara;
surpassing the hosts of Indras, he is an ascetic [in his very] body.[^208-9]

**19.** Immensely wondrous forgiveness he shows to all living beings;
such goodness of character no one has had or will have.

**20.** Most profound and steadfast is Rasika Murari;
equal-minded to all living beings, possessed of every virtue.

**21.** A great giver is Rasika, there is none [like him];
there is no one in the world to compare him with.

**22.** In all dharmas righteous is Rasika Mahashaya;
mighty with the strength of bhakti, [he] destroys the sins of the world.

**23.** A wondrously compassionate form, mercy to all living beings;
he honours those worthy of honour, being kind.

**24.** Every day Rasikendra-chandra is very happy;
he is the friend of all, he is the joy of all.

**25.** Very much subject to love is the son of Achyuta;
Rasikendra does good to these three worlds.

**26.** Mighty in bhakti to Krishna is Rasika-chudamani,
by whose might false learning has left the earth.[^208-10]

**27.** The fame of Rasika-deva is known to the world;
all people are devoted [to him] for his life.

**28.** The shelter of all people [and] sadhus is Rasikendra;
by the power of bhakti he steals the hearts of multitudes.

**29.** Most fortunate are all the people of the world
who see Rasika: [they] honour [him] as equal to Krishna.[^208-11]

**30.** Worshipful to all is Rasika Mahashaya;
[his] wealth is highly esteemed, [he is] the dawn of great happiness.[^208-12]

**31.** Of most courteous character is Rasika-shekhara;
his soul is renounced, [in his whole] body he is most humble.

**32.** Most modest is Rasikendra, the great one;
he is surely the protector of those who take shelter [of him].

**33.** Supremely great [are his] virtues, equal to [those of] Ishvara;
not even with a hundred mouths can the host of his virtues be told.[^208-13]

**34.** Blessed is the earth, blessed is Utkala, blessed is the holy abode!
Blessed is the father, blessed the mother in whose womb [he] rested![^208-14]

**35.** Blessed is that village where he took birth;
blessed is that place where those feet tread.

**36.** Blessed is that village where he dwells;
blessed is that place where the pastimes of love [take place].

**37.** Blessed are the companions with whom he sports;
blessed are [his] kin, friends and all his household.

**38.** Blessed are all the men and women of Utkala
who behold Rasika's feet.

**39.** By [his] darshana all sins are dispelled;
hearing Rasika's words, the ears are refreshed.

**40.** Soft, deep, gentle, sweet is his speech;
nowhere is this sweetness heard mixed [with anything].[^208-15]

**41.** Every syllable is sprinkled with nectar;
hearing those words, all forget themselves.

**42.** A gentle smile ever rains from [his] lips;
seeing [his] form, all people float in the bliss of love.

**43.** He destroyed all evil desires in people's minds;
all people became embodiments of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**44.** Thus Rasika at home, night and day,
constantly serves the guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

**45.** Thus after some days Shyamananda-raya
made his way to Greater Balarampur.[^208-16]

**46.** Prabhu delighted [all] with the rasa of talks about Krishna;
he especially took all under Shyamananda's shelter.[^208-17]

**47.** Many men and women in that village became [his] disciples:
Gopinatha, Jagannatha, Akrura, Sri Hari,

**48.** the charming boy Radhavallabhadasa,
Shyamadasa and others — all followers of Shyamananda.[^208-18]

**49.** The raja [and] the subjects all became [his] followers;
all received initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna, giving up their own [former] views.

**50.** In the forest country he showed mercy to all the people;
to all Shyamananda gave the shade of [his] feet.[^208-19]

**51.** After some days, from there Shyamananda-raya
sends a messenger to bring Rasika.

**52.** With his own hand he wrote a letter:
"Come quickly yourself and see me."

**53.** Having done the service of Krishna [and] the service of the sadhus, Rasika
then sat down to his meal, taking prasada.

**54.** He had only just taken the first mouthful
when at that very moment the letter arrived.

**55.** In the letter, the order: "Come quickly."
The second mouthful of prasada is [still] in his hand.[^208-20]

**56.** Rasikendra rose, hearing the guru's order;
he himself washed his hands in the Suvarnarekha.

**57.** Having done achamana, he set off at once in that direction;
the day came to an end, darkness lay ahead.[^208-21]

**58.** Tigers, rhinoceroses, elephants — all live in the forest parts;
[even] by day [people] do not go alone — it is so fearsome.

**59.** Along that road Rasika went alone;
a light rain fell, clouds covered the sky.

**60.** In the darkness one cannot see oneself;
at such an hour, alone, disregarding his meal,

**61.** bearing the order on his head, chanting the name "Hare Krishna,"
Rasikendra entered Balarampur.[^208-22]

**62.** Seeing [him], Shyamananda was very pleased;
embracing him, he seated him before himself.

**63.** Seeing his face withered by the fatigue of the road and by fasting,
he asked how he had come so quickly.

**64.** [Rasika] says not a word, his head bowed in shyness.
After a while all the servants arrived there.

**65.** They told how everything had gone on the way;
hearing it, Prabhu was boundlessly grieved.[^208-23]

**66.** Having bathed, eaten and so on, sitting down and gathering an assembly,
he said: "Listen, child, Rasika Murari.

**67.** I have heard that you made Dharenda Vaishnava;
now instruct the whole forest country.

**68.** There is one desire in my heart:
I will hold the Panchama-dola in the month of Vaishakha.[^208-24]

**69.** The place Barakola is very beautiful to see:
dense forest, mango [groves], a charming river.[^208-25]

**70.** I will begin the great festival at that place;
come in good time with all the provisions.

**71.** I will go there first and proclaim [it];
and you, there in Dharenda, make everything ready."[^208-26]

**72.** From there Shyamananda departed.
Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends!

**73.** In which places which pastimes the two of them performed,
of that I will briefly describe something.

**74.** Do not think [these are] human pastimes:
from yuga to yuga, descending, [they perform] pastimes in different ways.[^208-27]

**75.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus [ends] in the Sri Rasika-mangala, in the Dakshina-vibhaga, the eighth lahari named "The Display of Devotion to the Guru."*[^208-28]

[^208-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("অষ্টম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Kaushika (*kauśika*; cf. Purva, lahari 3, note 1). The ghosha (refrain) is the words of a gopi longing for Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "গুরুভক্তিপ্রদর্শন-নাম অষ্টম-লহরী" (*gurubhakti-pradarśana*). The summary line covers the whole lahari: Balarampur (*baṛa balarāmapura*), Vanabhumi (*banabhūmi*), Barakola (*baṛakolā*) should be checked when translating.

[^208-2]: "The moon of the gopa clan" — *gopakula-śaśī*: Shyamananda was of the gopa caste (Purva, lahari 1, note 9); it is also an epithet of Krishna. "The beloved of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera preẏasī* (feminine): in this way the author exalts Rasika, speaking of him as a gopi. On the same word applied to Shyamananda, and on Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching that Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, not Radhika Herself, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11; on Rasikananda — Purva, lahari 1, note 69 (a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord). The line can also be read as three praises: "Glory to Rasikendra-chandra, [glory] to the beloved of Krishna [Sri Radha]!"

[^208-3]: "Calling [him] Ishvara" — *īśbara baliẏā*: "Lord, master." These words describe how people honour him; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Purva, lahari 1, note 69; Dakshina, lahari 5, note 26). Cf. Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Gurv-ashtaka (7): all the shastras call the guru Hari Himself, and the sadhus regard him so, because he is dear to the Lord. Vyasa and Narada are great sages and devotees, honoured as empowered manifestations of the Lord; Narayana is the Lord.

[^208-4]: Verses 5–33 follow, almost in order, the list of the fifty virtues of Krishna as hero in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 2.1 (cf. CC, Madhya 23): a lovely body, auspicious marks, radiance, strength, youth, knowledge of languages, eloquence, learning, resourcefulness, refinement, adroitness, firmness in vows, knowledge of place, time and the worthy, seeing through the scriptures, purity, steadiness, forgiveness, profundity, equanimity, generosity, righteousness, compassion, humility, modesty, protection of the surrendered, subjection to love, might, fame, being the shelter of sadhus, being worshipful to all, wealth, greatness and, finally, "Ishvara." In this way the author praises Rasikananda (cf. lahari 7: the sixty-four limbs of bhakti). According to the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (2.1), these virtues are present in a small measure, "in drops," in living beings as well, but in fullness only in Krishna; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Purva, lahari 1, note 69).

[^208-5]: "Youthful — [immersed] in bhajana" — *kiśora bhajana*: apparently "youthful" (*kiśora*, cf. "youth" in the list of the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu); it can also be understood as "[his] bhajana is [worship of] Kishora," that is, of the youthful Krishna. "Wholly absorbed" — *tanmaya-mūrti*.

[^208-6]: "In various languages" — *nānā-bhāṣā*. Rasika-chand (*rasika-cā̃da*) is Rasikananda.

[^208-7]: "All the dharmas of good deeds" — *sukṛti-sakala dharma*; at this point the list of the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu has "grateful" (*kṛtajña*). "The vow [of service] to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-brata*.

[^208-8]: "Place, time and the worthy" — *deśa kāla supātra*: he knows what is fitting in which place, at which time and with which person (*deśa-kāla-supātra-jña*). "The scriptures are his sight" — *śāstra-dṛṣṭi* (*śāstra-cakṣus*).

[^208-9]: "The hosts of Indras" — *indra-gaṇa*; in view of the sense (at this point the list of the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu has "one who has subdued the senses"), the reading *indriya-gaṇa* is possible: "having conquered the senses." "An ascetic" — *tapobanta*.

[^208-10]: "False learning" — *kubidyā*: in the 1941 edition the ligature looks like "কুবিত্তা," taken as কুবিদ্যা. Rasika-chudamani — "the crest-jewel of rasikas," Rasikananda.

[^208-11]: "Honour [him] as equal to Krishna" — *mānī kṛṣṇa-sama*. These are the author's words; cf. notes 3 and 4.

[^208-12]: "[His] wealth is highly esteemed" — *bahumāna sampatti*: at this point the list of the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu has "wealthy" (*samṛddhimān*); the sense of the line is approximate.

[^208-13]: "Ishvara" — *īśvara*, the Lord. The author's rapturous words; cf. verse 4 and notes 3 and 4. "With a hundred mouths" — cf. Ananta-Shesha, who sings the Lord's glory with a thousand mouths.

[^208-14]: Utkala is Orissa. "The holy abode" — *puṇya-dhāma*. Rasikananda's father and mother are Achyuta and Bhavani (Purva-vibhaga).

[^208-15]: The line is unclear: *kothāo miśrita nahe se madhura śuni* — apparently "nowhere is such pure (unmixed) sweetness heard"; it can also be understood as "his sweet speech is mixed with nothing."

[^208-16]: Greater Balarampur — *baṛa balarāmapura* (*baṛa*, "big"): Balarampur, where Shyamananda preached (BR 15, 59: "what prema-bhakti merciful Shyamananda made manifest in Balarampura cannot be told"); in 61 — *balarāmapurī*. "Made his way" — *karilā bijaẏa*, a respectful expression for the arrival of a saint.

[^208-17]: "Prabhu" here is Shyamananda. "Under shelter" — *āśre*. The line can also be understood as "all [of them] especially took Shyamananda's shelter."

[^208-18]: Gopinatha, Jagannatha, Akrura, Sri Hari, Radhavallabhadasa, Shyamadasa are Shyamananda's disciples in Balarampur; Akrura and Jagannatha are also named in BR 15 (64) among Shyamananda's disciples. Not identified.

[^208-19]: "The forest country" — *banabhūmi* (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10): the wooded lands west of Medinipur; likewise in 67.

[^208-20]: 53–55: at the guru's order Rasika leaves his prasada, having barely begun the meal — hence the name of the lahari (colophon). "The letter arrived" — *likhā āsi haila upasanna*, lit. "the letter came and was at hand."

[^208-21]: Achamana (*ācamana*) — rinsing the mouth and hands with water after eating. The Suvarnarekha is the river on whose bank Gopivallabhapur stands; apparently Rasika is at home at this time (44). "In that direction" — *sei mukhe*; it can also be understood as "right then."

[^208-22]: Balarampur — *balarāmapurī* (cf. 45 and note 16).

[^208-23]: "Prabhu" is Shyamananda. "How everything had gone on the way" — *gamanera saba byabahāra*.

[^208-24]: Panchama-dola (*pañcama-dola*) — the swing festival (dola) of Krishna; apparently the Pancha-dola celebrated in Utkala after the Dola-purnima (the spring full moon). The author places the festival in the month of Vaishakha (April–May) and calls its night "the spring full moon" (lahari 9, 18). "Vaishakha" — *boiśākha*, so in the 1941 edition.

[^208-25]: Barakola (*baṛakolā*) — the village where Shyamananda held the festival (laharis 9–10). "Mango [groves]" — *āmra*, so in the 1941 edition; it can also be taken as the name of the river.

[^208-26]: "In good time" — *sakāle*, "in time, beforehand" (or "in the morning"). "Make everything ready" — *karaha susāra*, "arrange properly."

[^208-27]: "The two of them" (73) — Shyamananda and Rasikananda. "Descending" — *abatari'*: in this way the author exalts them (cf. Purva, lahari 1, notes 2 and 69; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, and Rasikananda is his disciple, a devotee and associate; neither is an incarnation of the Lord, but their pastimes, like those of all pure devotees, are not ordinary human doings.

[^208-28]: The name is given by the colophon: "গুরুভক্তিপ্রদর্শন-নাম অষ্টম-লহরী" (*guru-bhakti-pradarśana*). The colophon ends the lahari (cf. note 1); lahari 9 begins.


## Lahari 9. Preparations for the Panchama-dola

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika stays at Balarampur; twenty Vaishnavas come to him, and at midnight, when there is no ghee to feed them, he himself goes into the town for it and in the dark enters the house of a mleccha, a Mughal; the man beats him, and Rasika says with a smile that he will hurt his hand on his hard body; the astonished Mughal falls at his feet, but within a few days loses his horses, elephants, wealth and family; terrified, he seeks Rasika's shelter, and Rasika tells him to worship Krishna and be merciful to all living beings; the yavana becomes a sadhu and is rich again; at Shyamananda's order Rasika gathers provisions, comes to Dharenda, to Rasamaya's house, and tells everyone to prepare for the Panchama-dola on the spring full moon of Vaishakha; all joyfully bring offerings*

*The ninth lahari.*

*Raga Kamoda — panchali metre.*[^209-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, revered by the people of the three worlds,
in the garb that purifies the world!
O life of the world, treasure of Rasika's life,
kind one, compassionate to living beings![^209-2]

**2.** At Balarampur Rasika-shekhara
stayed for some days.
At that time twenty Vaishnavas
came there one day.[^209-3]

**3.** Having greeted [them], they gave sweet food,
gave all the raw provisions and so on.
Only ghee there was none; midnight came;
a servant told Rasika [of it].[^209-4]

**4.** Hearing this, at once, to fetch ghee,
[he] went into the town.
The night was dark, the road could not be made out —
he entered the house of a mleccha.[^209-5]

**5.** On a couch the ill-behaved mleccha
sits together with his wife.
Rasika went there;
in anger the wicked man seized [him] by the hand.

**6.** The wicked, ill-behaved man struck a blow
on Rasika's tender body.
Rasika, seeing [this], says with a smile,
playfully holding him by the hand:

**7.** "Listen, good sir, why do you strike?
There is no need for that at all.
Your hand, I know, will be hurt:
this body of mine is hard."[^209-6]

**8.** Hearing this, the Mughal was astonished
and let go of Rasika's hand.
Pleading, clasping [his] feet,
he at once fell to the ground.

**9.** Rasika quickly brought that ghee
[and] gave it to the assembly of Vaishnavas.
Within two or three days that very yavana
met with misfortune.[^209-7]

**10.** His horses, his elephants — all suddenly perished;
his wealth went who knows where.
His wife and the rest — all were struck down;
[he himself] barely held on to life.[^209-8]

**11.** Seeing Rasika's greatness, all the people
were filled with wonder.
In terror the Mughal came:
"Prabhu, [I seek] your shelter!

**12.** I am an offender; what good sense have I?
Fathomless, great is [your] greatness.
[You are] a sure stronghold of refuge, the possessor of all virtues:
be merciful to me."[^209-9]

**13.** Hearing his words, [Rasika] himself says:
"Listen, listen, good sir:
go and worship Krishna, [be] merciful to all living beings —
and wealth will surely come."[^209-10]

**14.** Accepting those words, that yavana became a sadhu
and took Rasika's shelter.
Once more he had boundless wealth,
by Rasika's mercy.

**15.** Rasika's greatness has no limit;
it is famed in this world.
Then Rasikendra, at Shyamananda's order,
gathered many provisions there.[^209-11]

**16.** Taking all the provisions, coming to Dharenda,
Rasika entered [the village].
In Rasamaya's house Rasika-shekhara
stayed there that day.[^209-12]

**17.** All who seek the highest good [he] had quickly brought,
[and] told [them] everything in detail:
"Shyamananda-raya has given me an order —
for the sake of the Panchama-dola.[^209-13]

**18.** All the preparations — each whatever [he can] — make,
many things in various ways.
On the spring full moon, on the night of Vaishakha,
[there will be] a festival, wondrous beyond words.[^209-14]

**19.** I shall go ahead, prepare the place,
build the pavilion,
tell Shyamananda everything, —
and all of you come after."[^209-15]

**20.** Hearing [this], everyone, with joyful hearts,
made up many loads of provisions.
[For this] first meeting everyone, happy,
made many preparations.[^209-16]

**21.** Of Rasika's virtues hear, all people;
worship Rasika's feet.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^209-17]

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the ninth lahari, called "Preparations for the Panchama-dola."*[^209-18]

[^209-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("নবম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 9 begins. Raga Kamoda (*kāmoda*). "Panchali metre" (*pañcālī chanda*) is tripadi; in the edition each stanza is set in four lines and is translated likewise (cf. lahari 6, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The name is given by the colophon: "পঞ্চমদোল-আয়োজন-নাম নবম-লহরী" (*pañcamadola-āẏojana*). Stanza 16 begins at the bottom of and ends at the top of.

[^209-2]: "In the garb that purifies the world" — *bhubana-pābana-bānā*: *bānā* is taken as "garb, attire" (the Vaishnava appearance); the sense is approximate. "Treasure of Rasika's life" — *rasikera prāṇa-dhana*: Shyamananda is Rasika's guru.

[^209-3]: Balarampur — lahari 8, 45 and 61. "Twenty" — *biṃśete*. (possibly *triṃśe*, "thirty").

[^209-4]: "Raw provisions" — *śidā* (= *sidhā*): uncooked foodstuffs given to guests for preparing their meal. Ghee is clarified butter.

[^209-5]: Mleccha (*mleccha*) — a non-Hindu, "barbarian"; here a Muslim, further on called a Mughal (8, 11) and a yavana (9, 14; cf. Purva, lahari 15, note 21).

[^209-6]: "Good sir" — *mahājana*, a polite address. "There is no need for that at all" — *tāra nāhi kichu dāẏa*; it can also be understood as "there is no fault [on my part]."

[^209-7]: "That very yavana met with misfortune" — *haila tā'ra akāje*, lit. "it turned to his harm." The author links the Mughal's misfortunes with the offence done to Rasika: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, offence against a Vaishnava (*vaiṣṇava-aparādha*) is ruinous (CC, Madhya 19), although Rasika himself, as 6–7 show, bears his assailant no anger.

[^209-8]: "Were struck down" — *haila hata*, "were slain (stricken)." "Barely held on to life" — *prāṇa laiẏā ṭānāṭāni*, lit. "[his] life was pulled this way and that."

[^209-9]: "Offender" — *aparādhī*. "A sure stronghold of refuge" — *śaraṇa pañjara*, lit. "a cage (enclosure) of refuge," i.e. a safe protection.

[^209-10]: "Good sir" — *mahāśaẏa*. Rasika promises the Mughal grandee the return of his wealth; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, devotional service is not performed for worldly gain, but the Lord is merciful also to those who come to Him with desires (Bhagavata 2.3.10: "whether free of desires or full of desires… one should worship the Supreme Person"), and purifies them.

[^209-11]: "Has no limit" — *dite nāhi sīmā*, lit. "there is no limit [for one] to give [its description]." "Gathered" — *kaila*, lit. "made." Shyamananda's order — lahari 8, 70–71.

[^209-12]: Rasamaya's house at Dharenda — Dakshina, laharis 4 and 6. "Entered [the village]" — *prabeśa hailā*.

[^209-13]: "All who seek the highest good" — *saba paramārthi* (*paramārthī*), i.e. pious people, devotees; apparently the people of Dharenda (16). "Had brought" — *ānā'ẏe*. "Me" — *moẏa* (an Oriya form; in the 1997 edition *mora*). Shyamananda's order — lahari 8, 68–71. Rasika's words run from 17 (second half) to 19.

[^209-14]: "On the spring full moon, on the night of Vaishakha" — *basanta-pūrṇamī, boiśākha yāminī*: on the time of the festival see lahari 8, note 24. "Festival" — *yātrā*, a festive procession (the dola-yatra). "Each whatever [he can]" — *kara ye yāhāra*, lit. "make, each whatever [he has]".

[^209-15]: "Tell Shyamananda everything" — *śyāmānanda-sthāne kahi bibaraṇe*; it can also be taken as "[there] where Shyamananda is, having told everything — and all of you come after." Pavilion — *maṇḍapa* (cf. lahari 10, 13–14).

[^209-16]: "Made up many loads" — *kaila bahu drabya bhāra*, lit. "made many burdens of things." "First meeting" — *prathama milana*: apparently the first joint festival of Shyamananda and Rasika (cf. lahari 10, 43: "the first pastime").

[^209-17]: The author's signature is given by the common formula; here, in the tripadi metre, it reads differently: "Shyamananda's feet are all the wealth of the son of Rasamaya" (*śyāmānanda-pada, sakala sampada, rasamaẏera nandana*; cf. Purva, lahari 11, note 15).

[^209-18]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণ-বিভাগে পঞ্চমদোল-আয়োজন-নাম নবম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা"; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 10. The Description of the Panchama-dola

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; on the way from Dharenda Rasika stays at Vasantapur with three disciples of Shyamananda, accepts many disciples there and calls everyone to the Dola-yatra; at Barakola he meets Shyamananda and promises that provisions will be brought from every land; at Shyamananda's order a pavilion for the rasa is built and the place adorned like Vaikuntha, and Rasika brings the Deity Shyama-raya from Dharenda; on the full moon of Vaishakha the Dola-yatra is celebrated: kirtan parties, rajas and bhunyas, the subadar of Medinipur and hundreds of thousands of people gather and throw phagu and abir — this is the first joint pastime of Shyamananda and Rasika; at the festival Vishvanatha Bhunya, brother of Raja Harichandana, skilled in music and letters, at Vamshi's request receives initiation from Rasika and the name Shyama-manohara, gives up worldly life, defeats the adherents of all doctrines in debate and accepts many disciples; Shyamananda sends the Vaishnavas off with gifts*

*The tenth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^210-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Pay heed to fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of Vallabha,
friend of the whole world, the source of mercy![^210-2]

**2.** Thus Rasikendra set out;
that day he rested at Vasantapur.

**3.** Madhava, Sri Haridasa, Madanamohana —
these three are disciples of Shyamananda Prabhu.[^210-3]

**4.** In their house Rasika-shekhara stayed,
with him ten or twenty young companions.[^210-4]

**5.** Two or three days he stayed in that village;
Rasika accepted many disciples there.

**6.** He told everyone about the festival:
"Let us all go to see the Dola-yatra!

**7.** Whatever each wishes — take loads of various provisions;
proclaim these words to everyone everywhere."[^210-5]

**8.** From there Rasikendra set out [further];
in the village of Barakola he met Prabhu.[^210-6]

**9.** Shyamananda asked Rasika:
"What provisions have you brought, having procured [them]?"[^210-7]

**10.** Rasikendra said to Shyamananda:
"Do not worry about any provisions.

**11.** By the time of the great festival the loads of provisions will come:
everyone will bring as much as he can.

**12.** From land to land I have proclaimed everything;
many provisions will come, various gifts."

**13.** Hearing this, Shyamananda-raya rejoiced;
he ordered everyone to build a pavilion.

**14.** Receiving the order, everyone built the pavilion:
a pavilion — a place for the rasa — they raised.[^210-8]

**15.** In various ways they stretched canopies, set up arches;
of various cloths [and] garlands of flowers there was no counting.[^210-9]

**16.** On the four sides they planted banana trees;
a place beautiful to see — a dense forest.

**17.** Mango, jackfruit, lemon, jambira, kamala,
tabha, shatakara — on every tree cluster upon cluster.[^210-10]

**18.** A most charming place, beautiful to see,
it became like Vaikuntha, supremely radiant.

**19.** In various ways it was adorned with silks [and] chamaras;
the moon of the Vaishakha full moon — bright was that night.[^210-11]

**20.** From all lands came rajas [and] subjects —
women, men, children, hundreds of thousands of people.

**21.** Shyamananda-raya gave Rasika an order:
"Bring Thakura Shyama-raya from Dharenda."[^210-12]

**22.** Receiving the order, Rasikendra set out;
going to Bhima's house, he arrived [there].

**23.** He said to Rasamaya, Chintamani [and] Vamshi:
"Bring Shyama-raya in procession to Barakola.

**24.** The holy Panchama-dola-yatra will be there:
quickly bring Shyama-raya there in procession."[^210-13]

**25.** Hearing this, all set out joyfully;
taking the Thakura, everyone went there.

**26.** Conches, mahuri, various instruments, rabab, vina;
crying "jaya, jaya," they beat the dundubhis.[^210-14]

**27.** All entered Barakola;
that same day they performed the adhivasa with fragrances.[^210-15]

**28.** On the full moon they joyfully arranged the great festival —
the great festival of the Dola-yatra, in great happiness and bliss.

**29.** Many parties came to sing kirtan;
a great many Vaishnavas came from all sides.

**30.** Countless people came — they could not be counted;
rajas [and] bhunyas came with music.[^210-16]

**31.** The subadar of Medinipur came there;
there were hundreds of thousands of people — it cannot be told.

**32.** Lamps, torches, chandrodayas of various kinds;
in their joy people do not know day from night.[^210-17]

**33.** Many provisions came, various gifts;
everyone gave provisions of various kinds.

**34.** Be they rajas, be they subjects, be they pilgrims —
all of them, one by one, he satisfied.

**35.** Sankirtana, dundubhis, music of various kinds;
shinga, venu, vishana, songs of many sorts.[^210-18]

**36.** Heaven, earth and the nether world were filled with cries of "jaya";
for the roar of the dundubhis nothing else could be heard.

**37.** The world of the gods [and] the world of men, coming together,
dance in joy [and] happiness, forming circles.

**38.** All were immersed in bliss, unaware of the body;
all those places became greater than Vaikuntha.[^210-19]

**39.** Seeing that happiness, all are amazed:
hundreds of thousands of maunds of phagu, chuya — load upon load.[^210-20]

**40.** Camphor, sandal, fragrant garlands of flowers —
who brings, who gives, no one knows.

**41.** All became many-coloured, adorned with abir;
phagu fell on the ground a hand deep.

**42.** All say: "Never have we seen such happiness!"
All the men and women were immersed in bliss.

**43.** Not even with a hundred mouths can that happy pastime be told —
the first pastime of Shyamananda [and] Rasika.[^210-21]

**44.** At this time Vishvanatha Bhunya Mahashaya,
the youngest son of Shashadhara Bhunya,[^210-22]

**45.** brother of Harichandana, lord of the realm,
skilled in music and letters, very pure in mind,

**46.** endowed with every virtue, [eminent] in family, character and honour, —
set out to go there to see the festival.

**47.** With Rasamaya [and] Vamshi [he had] an inseparable friendship;
he beheld Shyamananda [and] Rasika.[^210-23]

**48.** Vamshi tells Rasika everything:
"Be gracious, Prabhu, take care [of him].

**49.** He is very accomplished in music and letters;
quickly give him prema-bhakti.

**50.** [He is] the brother of Harichandana, lord of the realm:
be merciful to him, Rasika Gosani.

**51.** When such a worthy disciple becomes yours,
he will deliver many living beings."

**52.** Hearing Vamshi's words, Rasika-shekhara says:
"Quickly make [him] a disciple of Shyamananda."[^210-24]

**53.** Hearing these words, Vishvanathadasa says:
"Birth after birth I am your own servant, your slave.

**54.** Apart from your feet I have no other goal;
you are the lord of my life, my family, character and caste.

**55.** Apart from your feet I know nothing else:
grant me prema-bhakti for Krishna."[^210-25]

**56.** Hearing his very firm words,
Rasika spoke to Vishvanatha about Krishna.

**57.** Rasika-shekhara gave [him] instruction in the mantra;
with love he gave him the name Shyama-manohara.[^210-26]

**58.** All the tantras [and] mantras he gave to Shyama-manohara;
he ordered: "Deliver all living beings."

**59.** From that day Shyama-manoharadasa
gave up all endeavours [and] worldly enjoyments.

**60.** By Rasika's touch he became exclusively surrendered [to him];
he accepted many disciples in every land.

**61.** By virtue of much austerity, birth after birth,
he with his whole family took shelter at Rasika's feet.

**62.** Apart from Rasikendra-chandra he knows nothing else;
from his very birth he meditates on Rasika.[^210-27]

**63.** The master of music, Shyama-manohara,
by Rasika's mercy is prema embodied.

**64.** Very eloquent [and] learned is that mahashaya:
no one could answer him face to face.

**65.** Debaters [and] opponents — [adherents of] logic, of Patanjali's [teaching] and others,
of Sankhya, Sankhyayana, Mimamsa — all the famous ones,[^210-28]

**66.** Shaivas, Shaktas, Sauras, Ganapatyas — all of them:
Shyama-manohara crushed them all.

**67.** By Rasika's mercy he became the knower of all the shastras,
the expounder of the essence of the four Vedas.

**68.** Swaying in prema for Krishna, [he walks] with the gait of a king of elephants;
in the bliss of Krishna he sports throughout the world.[^210-29]

**69.** Such is the unfathomable greatness of Rasika:
in the three worlds there is no comparison for it, no limit.

**70.** Thus, having joyfully celebrated the Dola-yatra,
Prabhu bade farewell to the Vaishnavas.[^210-30]

**71.** Giving cloths [and] ornaments, he bade [them] farewell;
all that happiness cannot be told.

**72.** Briefly I have described something, as it was;
hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends.[^210-31]

**73.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the tenth lahari, called "The Description of the Panchama-dola."*[^210-32]

[^210-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("দশম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*); the ghosha is the same as in lahari 7 (note 1). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "পঞ্চমদোল-বর্ণন-নাম দশমলহরী" (*pañcamadola-varṇana*). On the Panchama-dola see lahari 8, note 24. The whole lahari is; the summary line follows the 1941 edition.

[^210-2]: "The life of Vallabha" — *ballabhera prāṇa*: Vallabha ("the beloved") is apparently Krishna, Gopivallabha ("the beloved of the gopis"; cf. Rasika's Deity Gopivallabha-raya, Dakshina, lahari 6). Thus the author exalts Shyamananda, as when he calls him "Krishna's beloved"; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, not Radhika Herself (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "The source of mercy" — *karuṇā-nidāna*, lit. "the prime cause of compassion".

[^210-3]: Vasantapur (*basantapura*) — a village on the way from Dharenda to Barakola; not identified. Madhava, Sri Haridasa, Madanamohana — disciples of Shyamananda; not identified (cf. Madhava and Madanamohanadasa in the list of disciples, Purva, lahari 1, 94 and 101).

[^210-4]: "In their house" — *tāra ghare* (singular): apparently in the house of one of the three, or of all three. "Young companions" — *bālaka … sahacara*: young disciples accompanying Rasika.

[^210-5]: "Festival" — *yātrā* (6), i.e. the dola-yatra, the swing festival (lahari 8, note 24). "Loads of various provisions" — *nānādrabya bhāra*: gifts for the festival (cf. 11).

[^210-6]: "He met Prabhu" — *prabhu karilā darśana*: in Barakola Rasika met Shyamananda, who had gone there before him (lahari 8, 71). In the 1997 edition the first line reads *karila gamana*, the second *kahilā darśana*.

[^210-7]: "Having procured" — *kariẏā saṅgati*, "having arranged, gathered".

[^210-8]: "A place for the rasa" — *rāsasthalī*: a pavilion arranged like the place of the rasa dance — for the Deity at the festival.

[^210-9]: Canopies — *candrātapa* (awnings over the festival ground); arches — *toraṇā* (*toraṇa*), festive gateways. "Garlands of flowers" — *phula-jhārā*, hanging tassels of flowers.

[^210-10]: Banana trees (*rambhā-bṛkṣa*, 16) are set up around a festival ground as an auspicious sign. The names of the fruits are given as in the edition: jackfruit (*panasa*), jambira (*jambira*, a kind of citron), kamala (*kamalā*, mandarin orange), tabha (*ṭābhā*, a large lemon), shatakara (*śatakarā*, not identified) — cf. Purva, lahari 3, note 11. "Cluster upon cluster" — *jhārā jhārā*.

[^210-11]: "Silks" — *pāṭa-neta* (*pāṭa*, silk; *neta*, fine cloth). Chamaras are yak-tail whisks. "The Vaishakha full moon" — *boiśākha pūrṇimā* (April–May).

[^210-12]: Shyama-raya (*śyāmarāẏa*) — a Deity of Krishna in Dharenda; Thakura (*ṭhākura*) — the Deity. Apparently this is Shyamananda's Deity, served in Dharenda (later in the poem Shyama-raya is mentioned together with Thakurani).

[^210-13]: "To Bhima's house" — *bhīmera mandire* (*mandira*, house or temple): Bhima Shirikara, the ruler of Dharenda who had become a Vaishnava (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 4); apparently Shyama-raya was with him. Rasamaya is the author's father, Vamshi his uncle (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14); Chintamani is apparently a disciple of Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 38). "Bring in procession" — *bije karāiha*, a respectful expression for the procession of a Deity.

[^210-14]: Mahuri — a reed wind instrument of Utkala, a kind of shehnai. Rabab — a stringed instrument (Purva, lahari 4, note 19); vina — a stringed instrument; dundubhi — a large drum, kettledrum (Purva, lahari 3, note 26).

[^210-15]: Adhivasa with fragrances — *gandha adhibāsa*: the preliminary rite on the eve of a festival (Dakshina, lahari 6, note 6).

[^210-16]: "Parties" — *sampradā* (*sampradāẏa*): kirtan groups. Bhunyas (*bhuñā*) — bhuiyans, local landholders and chiefs in Utkala and Medinipur. "Countless" — *apramita*, so in the 1941 edition.

[^210-17]: Lamps — *deuṭī*, oil lamps on stands; torches — *maśāla*; chandrodaya — apparently a large lamp with many wicks, or a firework (Purva, lahari 3, note 26; Dakshina, lahari 5, note 25). Subadar (*subā*, 31) — a governor or administrator (Purva, lahari 10, note 28).

[^210-18]: Shinga and vishana — horns; venu — a flute (Purva, lahari 4, note 19).

[^210-19]: Vaikuntha — the spiritual abode of Lord Narayana. "Greater than Vaikuntha" (*baikuṇṭha adhika*) — the author's rapturous comparison (cf. 18).

[^210-20]: Phagu (*phāgu*) — red powder that people throw on one another at the dola festival; abir (*ābira*, 41) — fragrant coloured powder; chuya (*cuẏā*) — fragrant oil. A maund (*maṇa*) is a measure of weight (about 37 kg): "hundreds of thousands of maunds" is hyperbole. "A hand deep" (41) — *hātek pramāṇa*, lit. "to the measure of a hand".

[^210-21]: "The first pastime" — *prathama bihāra*: apparently the first festival that Shyamananda and Rasika celebrated together (cf. lahari 9, 20, note 16).

[^210-22]: Vishvanatha Bhunya (*biśvanātha bhuñā*), afterwards given the name Shyama-manohara (57); not identified in other sources. "The youngest son of Shashadhara Bhunya" — *śaśadhara bhuñā āra kaniṣṭha tanaẏa*: *āra* is taken as the genitive ending (*bhuñāra*); it can also be understood as "and [his] youngest son", i.e. Vishvanatha and Shashadhara's youngest son came. Harichandana (45) — an Oriya title of landholders and rulers (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 13); "lord of the realm" — *rājya-adhipati*, a raja; which principality is not stated. Mahashaya — "great soul", a respectful form of address.

[^210-23]: "Inseparable friendship" — *abheda milana*, lit. "undivided union".

[^210-24]: "Quickly make [him] a disciple of Shyamananda" — *śyāmānanda sthāne śiṣya karaha satbara*, lit. "with Shyamananda": apparently Rasika out of humility refers the petitioner to his own guru; Vishvanatha, however, asks for shelter from Rasika himself (53–55), and Rasika initiates him (57).

[^210-25]: "My family, character and caste" — *kula śīla jāti*: all that a person holds dear in the world is, for Vishvanatha, in Rasika.

[^210-26]: "Instruction in the mantra" — *mantra upadeśa*, i.e. initiation (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 8). Shyama-manohara (*śyāma manohara*), "Shyama who captivates the heart" — the initiation name; in 59 — Shyama-manoharadasa. "Tantras [and] mantras" (58) — *tantra mantra*: the rules of worship and the mantras.

[^210-27]: "From his very birth" — *garbha haite*, lit. "from the womb": according to the author, by virtue of the austerities of past lives (61) Vishvanatha was devoted to Rasika from birth.

[^210-28]: 65–66 list the learned opponents: *bādī bibādī* — debaters and opponents; *tarka* — logic (Nyaya); *pātañjala* — the yoga of Patanjali; *sāṅkhya* — Sankhya; *sāṅkhyāẏana* — apparently Shankhayana (a Vedic school) or a distortion of the name of Vatsyayana, the commentator on Nyaya; the reading is unclear; *mīmāṃsā* — Mimamsa. Shaivas, Shaktas, Sauras (worshippers of Surya), Ganapatyas (worshippers of Ganesha) — followers of non-Vaishnava doctrines. "Crushed" (*dalana*) — defeated in debate.

[^210-29]: "Swaying" — *ḍagamagī*, "rocking, staggering" with prema. "With the gait of a king of elephants" — *karīndra gamana*, a majestic walk. The second line is *kṛṣṇānande khele se sakala bhubana*; it can also be understood as "in the bliss of Krishna the whole world sports".

[^210-30]: "Prabhu" — apparently Shyamananda (cf. lahari 11, 2: "Mahashaya … bade farewell to all the Vaishnavas").

[^210-31]: "As it was" — *sbabhāba*: "a description of [their] nature", or "simply, as it is" (cf. lahari 11, 67: *barṇilu sbabhābe*).

[^210-32]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 11. The Curse Laid on Shyamadasi for an Offence in Krishna's Service

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; after the Dola-yatra Harabola, the yavana ruler, seeing the festival, calls Shyamananda Narayana, holds a three-day festival of sankirtana at Alamganj in Medinipur and worships him as Ishvara; Shyamananda accepts many disciples in Dharenda; at the request of Rasamaya, Vamshi and Bhima Shirikara he enters married life and in Greater Balarampur takes as his wife Shyamapriya, the daughter of Jagannatha; Rasika returns home; one day Shyamadasi, while preparing vegetables for the offering to the Deity, leaves her work to feed her crying first-born son Vrajananda, and Rasika in anger says that her sons will not remain with her; so six sons one after another leave this world, and by his mercy three remain — Radhananda, Krishnagati and Radhakrishnadasa; Hridayananda comes to Dharenda and orders Shyamananda, Rasika and Damodara to give everyone in Utkala Chaitanya's prema-bhakti and the name Hare Krishna*

*The eleventh lahari.*

*Raga Mallar.*[^211-1]
*Ghosha: "Crusher of the Daityas, enemy of the Daityas."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, mercy incarnate!
Giving prema-bhakti, he delivered the living beings.

**2.** Then, having celebrated the Dola-yatra, Mahashaya
bade farewell there to all the Vaishnavas.

**3.** At this time the yavana ruler of that region,
named Harabola — a villain, a very wicked man —[^211-2]

**4.** came and saw the dola festival with his own eyes;
seeing this wonder, the yavana ruler says:

**5.** "Not a man — this great person is Narayana!
I have beheld his feet."[^211-3]

**6.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda says to Rasika:
"Come, let us go and see the yavana ruler."

**7.** Prabhu went [and] saw the yavana ruler;
seeing [him], the villainous yavana showed [him] great honour.[^211-4]

**8.** That very yavana says to Shyamananda:
"Hold a great festival here; listen, good sir.

**9.** All the provisions I shall give — [you] have no concern at all;
all the Hindu adhikaris I shall send off [with gifts]."[^211-5]

**10.** "Go to the house and take care of all the provisions,
so that the sadhus may eat happily."

**11.** In Medinipur there is the place Alamganj —
there at last the great festival was arranged.[^211-6]

**12.** For three days [and] three nights, in great bliss,
sankirtana [and] the cry of "Hari" sounded on all four sides.

**13.** That very yavana was greatly delighted;
without pause he watches the sankirtana.

**14.** Great faith arose in him towards Shyamananda:
calling [him] Ishvara, he firmly began to worship [him].[^211-7]

**15.** Such is the might of Shyamananda [and] Rasika:
even a yavana chants his name.[^211-8]

**16.** From there Shyamananda set out
and, coming to Dharenda, arrived [there].

**17.** Shyamananda accepted many disciples there:
Chintamani, Madhuvana, Mathura, Mukunda,

**18.** Shyamasundara and the fortunate Narasimha,
Kanudasa, Hiradhara, the fortunate Kanu,[^211-9]

**19.** Uddhava, Akrura and others — how many names shall I take?
Many in that village Shyamananda made [his] disciples.[^211-10]

**20.** Then Rasamaya, Vamshi, Bhima Shirikara,
joining their palms, say to Shyamananda:[^211-11]

**21.** "Fulfil the word of us all;
we make a request — if you will not reject it.

**22.** You have long wandered through the holy places;
now, Prabhu, live a household life for a while.

**23.** If you give the order, I shall find [you] a bride."
Hearing [this], Shyamananda became somewhat afraid.[^211-12]

**24.** "Very well — as you all decide."
From there Shyamananda set out.

**25.** At that very place he took leave of Rasika
[and] went to Greater Balarampur.[^211-13]

**26.** There lives the fortunate Jagannatha;
he gave his daughter to Shyamananda.

**27.** Her name is Shyamapriya, she is very beautiful;
in beauty [and] virtues a portion of Lakshmi, enchanting the world.[^211-14]

**28.** Joyfully holding a festival of sankirtana,
Shyamananda married Shyamapriya.

**29.** Having married, [he] sent the bride to Dharenda;
for some days she stayed in Chintamani's house.[^211-15]

**30.** Then Shyamananda came to Radhanagar;
there for some days he first set up [his own] house.[^211-16]

**31.** Rasikendra then went to his own place;
without pause he serves guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

**32.** Every day Shyamadasi Thakurani at home
serves the Thakura lovingly, without pause.

**33.** One day, for the Thakura's bhoga,
the mother sat down diligently to cut the vegetables.[^211-17]

**34.** At that time her son was lying in the cradle;
the son began to cry, distressed by hunger.[^211-18]

**35.** His name was Vrajananda, his form most charming:
the first son, Rasika's excellent child.

**36.** Hearing the crying, the mother grew anxious,
left the vegetables, came and took her son on her lap.

**37.** She gives her own son milk to drink;
at that time Rasika arrived at that place.

**38.** Seeing with his own eyes that no one was cutting the vegetables,
seeing the delay in the bhoga, with angry words —

**39.** in anger Rasika said: "Listen, Shyamadasi!
Leaving Krishna's service, what are you doing, sitting [here]?"

**40.** Shyamadasi said to Rasika:
"The child was crying hard because of hunger.

**41.** When I have given [him] milk, I shall make the offering."
In anger Rasika says: "Listen, listen again and again!

**42.** In ignorance you have left the service of Krishna, the lord of life;
taking the son of maya on your lap, you have sat down with care.

**43.** Leaving the service of Krishna, the lord of my life,
you are bewildered in delusion because of maya.

**44.** Leaving love for Krishna, you have given great love to your son."
In great anger Rasikendra says to her:[^211-19]

**45.** "Whenever Krishna's service is broken even for a moment,
however many sons you have, they will not remain with you.[^211-20]

**46.** The one whom you raise without offence —
that son will remain on earth: I have told [you] the reason."

**47.** All were astonished on hearing those words:
