by the word of [his] order six sons were struck down.[^211-21]

**48.** Service to guru, Krishna and the sadhus goes on [there] without pause;
whenever, even for a moment, [Rasika] sees a lapse with his own eyes,

**49.** then he orders that son to go;
thus, year after year — six sons.[^211-22]

**50.** Parted from her sons, Shyamadasi Thakurani,
the mother of the world, grieved greatly.

**51.** Then Prabhu, out of mercy — the jewel of compassion and virtues —
out of mercy kept three sons on earth:[^211-23]

**52.** Radhananda, Krishnagati, Radhakrishnadasa;
without pause they delight in the bliss of Krishna.[^211-24]

**53.** Before guru, Krishna and the sadhus they are free of offence;
they are embodiments of prema, most pure in mind.

**54.** Thus in Sri Gopivallabhapur
Rasika-chandra ever joyfully abides.[^211-25]

**55.** At that time Sri Hridayananda Adhikari,
Prabhu, came and arrived at the town of Dharinda.[^211-26]

**56.** Hearing of the manifest [greatness] of Shyamananda [and] Rasika,
he came to see [them], bringing his associates.

**57.** Staying at Dharenda, he quickly sends people
to bring Shyamananda, Rasika, Damodara.[^211-27]

**58.** Hearing the order, the three Prabhus came in haste
[and] received the darshan of Adhikari Thakura.

**59.** Seeing [this] circle, Sri Hridayananda was pleased;
embracing [them], he ordered: "Listen, Shyamananda:

**60.** Chaitanya's prema-bhakti, the name 'Hare Krishna' —
give them to all living beings in Utkala.[^211-28]

**61.** Seeing this circle, I have become very glad:
without pause make devotion to Krishna manifest."

**62.** He showed great mercy to Rasika;
for some days he stayed in the company of all.

**63.** Then Adhikari Prabhu went to his own land;
Shyamananda especially presented [him] with many gifts.

**64.** Having received great joy, Sri Hridayananda departed;
seeing [him] off, Shyamananda went a good distance.[^211-29]

**65.** Having taken leave [of him], all quickly returned
[and] arrived at the house of Rasamaya [and] Vamshi.[^211-30]

**66.** In Rasamaya's house — Shyamananda's meal;
for some days the three stayed there.

**67.** Day by day he showed mercy to all living beings.
I have described a little of the Rasika-mangala — [his] nature.[^211-31]

**68.** Listen, all, attentively, leaving other talk;
by listening, destroy the pain of the fear of worldly existence.

**69.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eleventh lahari, called "The Curse Laid on Shyamadasi for an Offence in Krishna's Service."*[^211-32]

[^211-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("একাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Mallar; the ghosha is the same as in lahari 4 (note 1). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "কৃষ্ণসেবাপরাধে শ্যামদাসী-প্রতি অভিশাপপ্রদান-নাম একাদশ-লহরী" (*kṛṣṇasebāparādhe śyāmadāsī-prati abhiśāpa-pradāna*). The summary line covers the whole lahari: Alamganj (*ālamagañja*), Shyamapriya (*śyāmapriẏā*), Vrajananda (*brajānanda*), Krishnagati (*kṛṣṇagati*) should be checked when those couplets are translated.

[^211-2]: The yavana ruler (*yabana rājana*) — a Muslim ruler or nobleman of "that region" (of Barakola). Harabola — *harabolā*, so in the 1941 edition; in the edition's table of contents — "হরিবোলা" (*haribolā*). Not identified. "Named" — *bali*, lit. "called".

[^211-3]: These are the yavana's words; "this great person" (*mahājana*) is apparently Shyamananda (cf. 6–8). Thus the author exalts Shyamananda (cf. Dakshina, lahari 8, note 3, on Rasika being honoured as Ishvara); according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, not the Lord Himself (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^211-4]: "Prabhu" — Shyamananda, apparently together with Rasika (6). "Showed great honour" — *bahu mānya kailā*. Couplet 7 ends at the bottom of; begins with ॥ 8 ॥.

[^211-5]: "[You] have no concern at all" — *nāhi kichu dāẏa* (cf. lahari 9, note 6). "Hindu adhikaris" — *hindu adhikārī*: apparently the yavana ruler's term for the Hindu teachers and temple servants, the guests of the festival; "send off [with gifts]" — *kariba bidāẏa*, "dismiss with honour" (cf. 2; lahari 10, 70–71). It can also be understood as "I shall dismiss all the Hindu officials." The yavana's words run from 8 to 10.

[^211-6]: Medinipur — a town in West Bengal (cf. the Purva-vibhaga); Alamganj (*ālamagañja*) — apparently a quarter of Medinipur. "At last" — *nidāna*; not translated). The festival was apparently held at the yavana's expense (8–10).

[^211-7]: "Calling [him] Ishvara" — *īśvara baliẏā*: this is how the yavana sees Shyamananda (cf. 5 and note 3). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the guru is honoured as the Lord's most intimate servant, not as the Lord Himself (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "Firmly" — *niścaẏa*; the 1997 edition has *niścala*, "unwaveringly."

[^211-8]: "Might" — *paratāpa* (= *pratāpa*). "His name" — *yā̃ra nāma*: apparently Shyamananda's name. The yavana is Harabola (3, note 2).

[^211-9]: Chintamani, Uddhava, Akrura and Madhuvana are also named in BR 15 (63–65) among Shyamananda's disciples; Chintamani appears again below, 29. Mathura is possibly Rasamaya's brother (Dakshina, lahari 4, 34–35). The others are not identified. "Kanu" (18) may be the same Kanudasa or another person. "Fortunate" — *bhāgyabān*; the second time the 1941 edition has the misprint "তাগ্যবান্".

[^211-10]: "Many in that village Shyamananda made [his] disciples" — *bahuśiṣya śyāmānanda karila se grāma*, lit. "Shyamananda made that village [a village] of many disciples."

[^211-11]: Rasamaya is the author's father, Vamshi his brother; Bhima Shirikara is the ruler of Dharenda converted by Rasika (Dakshina, lahari 5; Shirikara — as in Purva, lahari 1, note 39).

[^211-12]: "Live a household life" — *karaha saṃsāra*. "I shall find [you] a bride" — *kanyā … kariba sañjāta*, lit. "I shall make a maiden appear." BR 15 says nothing of Shyamananda's marriage; the Rasika-mangala tells of it here (26–29) and further on (lahari 12, 12).

[^211-13]: Greater Balarampur — *baṛa balarāmapura* (lahari 8, note 16). Jagannatha (26) is possibly the same disciple of Shyamananda at Balarampur (lahari 8, note 18).

[^211-14]: "A portion of Lakshmi" — *lakṣmī aṃśe*: poetic praise, usual in describing a bride.

[^211-15]: "Married" — *bibhā karilena* (28), "having married" — *bibhā kari*. "Bride" — *kanyā*. Chintamani is Shyamananda's disciple at Dharenda (17). Dharenda is spelled here *dhārandā*.

[^211-16]: Radhanagar (*rādhānagara*) is not identified. "First set up [his own] house" — *gṛha … prathame karilā*; the sense is approximate.

[^211-17]: "The Thakura" — *ṭhākura*: the Deity served in Rasika's house (cf. lahari 7, 6: Sri Gopivallabha-raya with the Thakurani). Bhoga is the food cooked to be offered to the Deity. "The mother" — *mātā*: Shyamadasi, "the mother of the world" (50; Purva, lahari 1, 108).

[^211-18]: "In the cradle" — *dulīra upare*: *dulī* is a hanging cradle. Vrajananda (35) is Rasika's first-born; in the Purva-vibhaga (lahari 1, 110, note 48) Radhananda is called the eldest son — the eldest of those who remained (51–52).

[^211-19]: "I shall make the offering" (41) — *kari upahāra* (the 1997 edition has *upacāra*, "I shall perform the service"). "The son of maya" (42) — *māẏā-putra*: a son as a bond of worldly attachment. The author calls Rasika's words (44–46) a curse (see the colophon) and presents it as the consequence of aparadha — an offence in Krishna's service: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, service to the Deity stands above family attachments, a lapse in it is an offence, and the coming and going of every living being is in the Lord's hands. This episode is not in BR 15.

[^211-20]: "Even for a moment" — *pala mātra*: a pala is a measure of time (about 24 seconds). "Will not remain with you" — *nā rahibe saṅga*. "Without offence" (46) — *nir-aparādhe*, i.e. without lapses in Krishna's service.

[^211-21]: "By the word of [his] order" — *ājñā pramāṇe*. "Were struck down" — *hata hailā* (cf. lahari 9, note 8): six sons departed from life, each one when Rasika noticed a lapse in the service (48–49).

[^211-22]: "A lapse" (48) — *kruṭī* (= *truṭi*). "He orders that son to go" — *ājñā karena yāite se nandana*.

[^211-23]: "Prabhu" — here apparently Rasika. "On earth" — *dharaṇī*.

[^211-24]: Radhananda, Krishnagati, Radhakrishnadasa — Rasika's sons (Purva, lahari 1, 110, 122, 124; note 48).

[^211-25]: Gopivallabhapur — a village on the Suvarnarekha, the chief place of Rasika's service (Dakshina, lahari 3).

[^211-26]: Hridayananda — Hridaya Chaitanya, Shyamananda's guru, servant of the Deities at Ambika-Kalna (Purva, lahari 1, note 13; BR 15, 94). "Adhikari" (*adhikārī*) — the title of the head of a temple's service. Dharinda (*dhārindā*) is Dharenda (57).

[^211-27]: Damodara — the learned yogi of Chakulia, Shyamananda's disciple (Dakshina, lahari 1). "The three Prabhus" (58) — Shyamananda, Rasika and Damodara.

[^211-28]: "Embracing" (59) — *kole kari*, lit. "taking on the lap (in the arms)." According to BR 15 (101) Shyamananda settled in Utkala at the order of the Gosvami; here the order to preach in Utkala is given by Hridayananda.

[^211-29]: "Seeing [him] off" — *anubraje*: by custom a guest, all the more a guru, is accompanied for some distance.

[^211-30]: Rasamaya and Vamshi are brothers (note 11); their house is at Dharenda (lahari 9, note 12).

[^211-31]: "[His] nature" — *sbabhābe*, i.e. a description of Rasika's nature (cf. lahari 10, 72: *sbabhāba barṇana*); the 1997 edition has *prabhābe*, "greatness."

[^211-32]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণ-বিভাগে কৃষ্ণসেবাপরাধে শ্যামদাসী-প্রতি অভিশাপপ্রদান-নাম একাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*kṛṣṇasebāparādhe śyāmadāsī-prati abhiśāpa-pradāna*, lit. "The Pronouncing of a Curse on Shyamadasi for an Offence in Krishna's Service"); the 1997 edition omits Shyamadasi's name in the colophon. Lahari 12 begins.


## Lahari 12. The Meeting with Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda travels through the country with Rasika: at Naihati, at Arjuni's, he holds three festivals and accepts disciples, Rasika accepts many disciples at Kashiyari, Shyamananda shows mercy to Haridasa at Jhatiyara and to Bhimadhana at Murura, who gives him the village of Sri Govindapur, where Shyamananda builds a house and where Shyamapriya, Gaurangadasi and Yamuna come; Shyamananda orders Rasika to deliver the king and subjects of Utkala; Rasika comes to Rajgarh, to the learned assembly of Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja and his two brothers, versed in the shastras but ignorant of devotion to Krishna; the author describes Rasika's beauty, with the Bhagavata in his hands; women, scholars, friends, servants, sadhus and men of knowledge see in him a jewel among men, like Narayana; the three brothers fall at his feet, wash them, glorify him as Narayana and entertain him with honour; the author promises to tell next of the instruction*

*The twelfth lahari.*

*Raga Dhanashri.*[^212-1]
*Ghosha: "Sweet words, O enchanting the mind!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, fathomless [his] greatness,
friend of all the worlds, compassion [incarnate] for living beings![^212-2]

**2.** Having stayed at Dharenda, after some days Shyamananda
set out, taking Rasika with him.

**3.** Coming there, to Arjuni of Naihati,
he joyfully held three festivals.

**4.** Prabhu accepted many disciples there:
Jagannatha, Damodara and the women of the family,[^212-3]

**5.** Shyamadasa, Arjuni's son, and others.
From there Prabhu went to the village of Kashiyari.[^212-4]

**6.** Rasika accepted many disciples in that village:
Vrajamohana, Shyamadasa and Narayana,

**7.** Radhamohana the bhakta and Yadavendradasa;
day by day he brought forth many [new] disciples.[^212-5]

**8.** From there [they] came and stayed in the village of Jhatiyara;
there Prabhu showed mercy to Haridasa.[^212-6]

**9.** From there [they] entered Murura;
[there] Shyamananda showed mercy to Bhimadhana.

**10.** That bhuiyan gave [him] the village of Sri Govindapur;
in that village Shyamananda Thakura built a house.[^212-7]

**11.** For some days Shyamananda stayed there,
without pause delighting in absorption in Krishna.

**12.** Shyamapriya Thakurani came there,
Gaurangadasi Thakurani, Yamuna — all.[^212-8]

**13.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of the fallen:
giving bhakti, he conquered every land.[^212-9]

**14.** Shyamananda-raya gave an order to Rasika:
"Save all living beings, O Mahashaya.

**15.** Deliver the king and the subjects of Utkala;
spread the rasa of prema-bhakti for Krishna."

**16.** Receiving the order, Rasikendra set out
and, coming to Rajgarh, arrived [there].

**17.** Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja; Chhota-raya Sena [and]
Rautra are his younger brothers: [all] three are fortunate.[^212-10]

**18.** The three brothers are of great splendour, very mighty;
born in the pure Solar line, very mighty.[^212-11]

**19.** Hundreds and hundreds of learned pandits stay in [their] assembly;
they always study Vedic learning [and] the Bhagavata.

**20.** They know the six shastras, they are equal to Brihaspati;
devotion to Krishna they do not know — [their] labour is in vain.[^212-12]

**21.** At that time Raja Vaidyanatha, having convened the assembly —
the three brothers were seated, having finished the fivefold worship.[^212-13]

**22.** At that time Rasikendra went [there];
coming into the midst of the assembly, he arrived [before them].

**23.** A dark, beautiful body, a sweet form,
a softly, softly smiling face, that unhurried gait.

**24.** Curling locks, very long cheeks;
from beautiful lips — soft, gentle, gentle words.[^212-14]

**25.** Arms reaching to the knees, eyes beautiful;
a nose [like] a sesame flower, a row of teeth charming.

**26.** A broad chest, a navel deep [and] lovely;
a waist [like] a lion's, thighs [like] plantain [trunks], a bright-hued cloth.[^212-15]

**27.** Most tender are those two feet;
the row of nails glitters, surpassing the moon.

**28.** A fine cloth, [folded] double, adorns his left shoulder;
seeing that sweet form, the people of the world are enchanted.[^212-16]

**29.** Holding in his hand the manuscript of the Bhagavata,
he entered the assembly like the sun.[^212-17]

**30.** Having bowed to all the brahmanas,
he came near the king and sat [before him].[^212-18]

**31.** Seeing [him], the three brothers were greatly amazed:
with their own eyes they saw a form like Narayana.[^212-19]

**32.** He is the embodiment of all dharma, all radiant with splendour;
this Mahashaya is the destroyer of adharma.

**33.** The three brothers saw this form;
the women in the house, seeing [him], are enchanted — [the whole] world [is enchanted].[^212-20]

**34.** All say: "Where were you, jewel among men?
Your body surpasses Kandarpa — it enchants the world."[^212-21]

**35.** Shaivas, Shaktas, debaters [and] opponents — all say:
"He will easily crush the pride of us all."[^212-22]

**36.** The brahmanas versed in the six shastras, averse to Krishna —
they all saw [him] as if in the form of Vyasa [and] Shuka.[^212-23]

**37.** "He it is who will destroy the pride of us all;
he will reveal the essential truth of the Vedas and shastras."

**38.** All the wives of the family say: "The son of Achyuta,
this Mahashaya, is a moon illuminating the family.[^212-24]

**39.** Through him all our kin will live in happiness;
by the good fortune of us all he was born like this."

**40.** All the elders say: "A son of [our] family!
May he live long — protect [him], Narayana!

**41.** We shall see his sons [and] grandsons with our own eyes!" —
such parental affection all the elders show.[^212-25]

**42.** All the friends say: "He is our very own friend;
apart from him there is no dearer friend in the three worlds."

**43.** The companions say: "He is my dear brother;
with him I roam the world without fear.

**44.** With him one never knows any sorrow;
the eight siddhis [and] nine nidhis — [that] happiness is with him."[^212-26]

**45.** All the servants say: "He is the foremost of men;
even with ten million mouths his qualities cannot be described."

**46.** All the sadhus say: "He is the crown of men:
he will distribute prema-bhakti for Krishna from house to house.

**47.** This Mahashaya will deliver all living beings;
his greatness cannot be expressed even in part."

**48.** The learned brahmana panditas speak affectionate words:
"This person is not a man — we all know [it].

**49.** This Mahashaya is expert in all the shastras;
he will make prema-bhakti for Krishna arise.

**50.** Mimamsa, Patanjala [yoga] and the rest, Sankhya, Sankhyayana —
this person will crush the pride of them all."[^212-27]

**51.** All the jnanis say: "He is like Narayana,
Whom the yogis call the Param Brahman.

**52.** In this boy we see that very form present before us;
by his darshan my ignorance has been dispelled.[^212-28]

**53.** Such a sweet form we have never seen;
seeing the enchanting form, the eyes cannot turn away.[^212-29]

**54.** Truly this Mahashaya is like Narayana:
he has risen to destroy the blinding darkness of dreadful Kali."

**55.** Thus he gave darshan to all:
as each one sees [his] form, so everyone speaks.[^212-30]

**56.** One moon filled the hearts of all;
seeing [his] moon-face, all are enchanted by his darshan.

**57.** Everyone fell into Rasika's snare:
the son of Achyuta brought all under his sway.

**58.** At this time the king, seeing that form —
the three brothers fell to the ground at [his] feet.

**59.** They seated Rasikendra-chandra on a seat;
the king washes [his] feet with joy in his heart.[^212-31]

**60.** One brother drew water and joyfully handed [it];
the king himself washed [his] lotus feet.

**61.** Another brother wiped the holy feet with a cloth:
birth after birth these three are Rasika's servants.

**62.** The three brothers sat on the ground with joined palms;
seeing [his] manifest [glory], the king trembled at heart.[^212-32]

**63.** Bowing down, he says to Rasika:
"By the good fortune of us all you have come to [our] home.

**64.** Today my birth has become fruitful:
I have seen your feet with my own eyes.

**65.** For millions upon millions of births I performed austerities —
that is why, Prabhu, I have seen your feet.

**66.** You have appeared to deliver us all;
age after age, for the sake of your servants, you accept dwelling in a womb.[^212-33]

**67.** You take form by your own will — who can know [you]?
Prabhu, affectionate to devotees, brother to those who take shelter![^212-34]

**68.** You create [and] maintain the entire universe;
you are the universal form, Prabhu, the god Narayana.

**69.** By your maya the moving and the unmoving come and go;
you are the soul of all, the enclosure of shelter.[^212-35]

**70.** Seeing the living beings in the dreadful Kali-yuga,
you took birth to deliver [them], bringing your associates and companions."

**71.** In many ways King Vaidyanatha offered praises;
he worshipped [his] holy feet as [one worships] Narayana.[^212-36]

**72.** He offered [him] a seat in his own palace
and with care [served] a meal of six tastes and so on.[^212-37]

**73.** The king, sitting [there] himself, serves [him] tambula;
he reveals all the pain of his heart at [his] feet.[^212-38]

**74.** Now I shall tell the account of the instruction;
listen, all, attentively to the "Rasika-mangala."[^212-39]

**75.** Who can comprehend [these] most wondrous pastimes?
What Rasika-shekhara told me —[^212-40]

**76.** in that order I have described something;
learned and good people, do not count this as a fault.

**77.** This I composed in the Dakshina-vibhaga,
making Rasika's feet the ornament of my head.

**78.** I shall make known something of the "Rasika-mangala":
listen, all, attentively to the description of [his] nature.[^212-41]

**79.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the twelfth lahari, called "The Meeting with Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja."*[^212-42]

[^212-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("দ্বাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 12 begins. Raga Dhanashri (*dhānaśrī*). The ghosha is *madhura bacana mana mohanā re*: "enchanting the mind" (*mana mohanā*) can also be taken as the name-address "Manamohana" ("Enchanter of the heart," Krishna): "Sweet words, O Manamohana!" There is no mangala-shloka; the numbering is that of the edition. The name is given by the colophon: "রাজা বৈদ্যনাথ-ভঞ্জ-মিলন-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী" (*rājā baidyanātha-bhañja-milana*). The summary line covers the whole lahari. Couplet 30 is the last; begins with ॥ 31 ॥.

[^212-2]: "Compassion [incarnate] for living beings" — *jībera karuṇā*, lit. "the compassion of living beings."

[^212-3]: Naihati (*naihāṭī*) — here apparently a village in Utkala or Medinipur, not Naihati on the Ganges (glossary); not identified. Arjuni (*arjjunī*) — apparently the master of the house where Shyamananda stayed (his son is Shyamadasa, 5); not identified. "The women of the family" — *badhūgaṇa*: the wives (daughters-in-law) of the house. Jagannatha and Damodara (4) are not identified (not Damodara of Chakulia).

[^212-4]: Kashiyari — *kāśīẏāṛī purī*; possibly present-day Keshiary (West Medinipur); not identified.

[^212-5]: Vrajamohana, Shyamadasa, Narayana, Radhamohana, Yadavendradasa — Rasika's disciples; Radhamohana is also named in the Purva-vibhaga (lahari 1, 80). "The bhakta" — *bhakta*: possibly Radhamohana's byname or the epithet "devotee." "Brought forth" — *kailā parakāśa*, lit. "made manifest."

[^212-6]: Jhatiyara is not identified. Haridasa is not identified.

[^212-7]: Murura and Sri Govindapur are not identified. Bhimadhana is "that bhuiyan" (*bhuñā*): a local landholder, lord of villages.

[^212-8]: Shyamapriya is Shyamananda's wife (lahari 11, 26–29). Gaurangadasi Thakurani and Yamuna are apparently women of Shyamananda's household; not identified. "Thakurani" is a respectful title of a Vaishnava teacher's wife.

[^212-9]: "Conquered" — *karila dalana*, lit. "crushed": he conquered by bhakti (cf. lahari 10, 66).

[^212-10]: Rajgarh (*rājagaṛa*) is not identified. Vaidyanatha Bhanja — apparently a raja of the Bhanja dynasty (cf. Purva, lahari 1, 113 and note 49). "Chhota-raya Sena [and] Rautra" — *choṭa rāẏa sena, rāutrā*: the reading and division of the names are unclear; "Chhota-raya" ("the younger raya") and "Rautra" (the Odia title *rāutarāẏa*) may be titles. Understood as the raja's two younger brothers, three brothers in all (18, 21).

[^212-11]: "The Solar line" — *sūryabaṃśa*, the dynasty of the Sun (the line of Ikshvaku and Rama). "Very mighty" — *baṛai pratāpī*, repeated in both lines, as in the original.

[^212-12]: "The six shastras" — *ṣaṛśāstra*: the six philosophical systems (darshanas). Brihaspati is the preceptor of the demigods, a model of learning.

[^212-13]: "having finished"; *pañcapūjā*, worship of the Lord with five offerings, panchopachara; the gloss is not translated). "Having convened the assembly" — *sabhā kari*.

[^212-14]: "Curling locks" — *cā̃cara cikura keśa*. "Very long cheeks" — *sudīrgha kapola*. "Gentle, gentle" — *lahu lahu*.

[^212-15]: "Thighs [like] plantain [trunks]" — *rambhā jānu*: *rambhā*, the plantain tree, a traditional simile in descriptions of beauty; *jānu*, knees (thighs).

[^212-16]: "A fine cloth" — *jhinabāsa*; "[folded] double" — *dosarā*: apparently an upper wrap (chadar) of two layers; the sense is approximate.

[^212-17]: "The manuscript of the Bhagavata" — *bhāgabata pũthikhāni*: Rasika was famed for his exposition of the Srimad-Bhagavatam (BR 15, 120). "The sun" — *dinamaṇi*, lit. "the jewel of the day."

[^212-18]: "Sat [before him]" — *haila upasana*, lit. "drew near, came to be beside" (the same word as in 16, 22).

[^212-19]: "Like Narayana" — *nārāyaṇa sama*; the panditas and jnanis say the same (51, 54), and the king himself glorifies Rasika as Narayana (65–71). These are the rapturous words of the onlookers: thus the author exalts Rasika. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Purva, lahari 1, note 69; Dakshina, lahari 8, note 3); his guru Shyamananda is a servant of Radha and Krishna (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). The guru and the great devotee are honoured as Hari Himself because he is dear to the Lord (Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Gurv-ashtaka, 7).

[^212-20]: "The women in the house" — *gṛhe nārīgaṇa*. "[The whole] world [is enchanted]" — *mohita dharaṇī*, lit. "the earth is enchanted"; it can also be understood as "[fell] enchanted to the ground" (cf. 58: *caraṇe paṛilā dharaṇī*). The 1997 edition reads the same.

[^212-21]: "Jewel among men" — *puruṣa-ratana*. Kandarpa is Kamadeva, the god of love, the model of beauty.

[^212-22]: "Debaters [and] opponents" — *bādī bibādī* (lahari 10, note 28). "Easily" — *e hele* (*helāẏa*, "playfully, without effort"); "এ" is taken as "he" ("this one").

[^212-23]: "The six shastras" — note 12. "Averse to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇere bimukha*. Vyasa is the compiler of the Vedas and Puranas, the author of the "Bhagavata"; Shuka is Shukadeva Gosvami, the speaker of the "Bhagavata."

[^212-24]: "The wives of the family" — *kulabadhū*: the wives and daughters-in-law of the royal house. The son of Achyuta is Rasika (Achyuta is his father; Purva-vibhaga). "A moon illuminating the family" — *kuloddīpana candra*: the women, and then the elders (40–41), see Rasika as though he were a son of their own family. The scene recalls the "Bhagavata" (10.43.17): Krishna, entering Kamsa's arena, appears to each according to his relationship with Him — to the wrestlers as a thunderbolt, to the women as Kamadeva embodied, to the cowherds as their own kinsman, and so on; so here (33–55) each sees Rasika in his own way (cf. 55).

[^212-25]: "Parental affection" — *bātsalya* (vatsalya).

[^212-26]: "The companions" (43) — *saṅgī jana*. "Without fear" — *nirbhaẏete* (in the 1997 edition *nirbharete*, "relying [on him]"). The eight siddhis are the mystic perfections of yoga (anima and the others); the nine nidhis are the nine treasures of Kubera.

[^212-27]: The list of doctrines is as in lahari 10, 65–66 (note 28): *mīmāṃsā* — Mimamsa; *pātañjala* — the yoga of Patanjali; *sāṃkhya* — Sankhya; *sāṃkhyāẏana* — apparently Shankhayana (a Vedic school); the reading is unclear.

[^212-28]: Jnanis (*jñānī*) — followers of the path of knowledge. Param Brahman (*paraṃbrahma*) — the Supreme Absolute Truth. "Present before us" — *bidyamāna*. "My ignorance has been dispelled" — *harilā ajñāna*, lit. "[he] has stolen [my] ignorance."

[^212-29]: "The eyes cannot turn away" — *nā pichale ā̃khi*, lit. "the eyes do not slip off."

[^212-30]: "As each one sees [his] form, so everyone speaks" — *yei jana rūpa dekhe bale sarbajana*; understood as a summing-up of 33–54 (cf. note 24).

[^212-31]: Rasikendra-chandra — "the moon Rasikendra," an affectionate name of Rasika (cf. Rasika-chandra, lahari 11, 54). Washing the feet is the first of the offerings to an honoured guest and to the guru.

[^212-32]: "Manifest [glory]" — *prakāśa*. "Trembled at heart" — *ḍarilā antara*, lit. "was afraid at heart": reverential awe.

[^212-33]: "For the sake of your servants" — *bhṛtya lāgi*; "you accept dwelling in a womb" — *laha garbhabāsa*: the words of the king, who sees in Rasika the Lord descending for the sake of His devotees (note 19). The 1997 edition reads *lai* ("[I] accept"): "age after age, to be [your] servant, I accept dwelling in a womb."

[^212-34]: "You take form by your own will" — *sbecchāmaẏa rūpa* (the 1997 edition: "স্বেচ্ছাময় প্রভু তুমি কে কহিতে পারে," "…who can describe [you]?"). "Brother to those who take shelter" — *śaraṇa sodara*, lit. "brother [giving] shelter"; the same in lahari 13, 67.

[^212-35]: "The enclosure of shelter" — *śaraṇa-pañjara*, lit. "cage of shelter": a protecting enclosure for those who take refuge.

[^212-36]: "As [one worships] Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa sama* (note 19).

[^212-37]: "In his own palace" — *āpanā mandire*: *mandira* is a palace, living quarters (or a temple). "Of six tastes" — *ṣaṛrasa*: sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent.

[^212-38]: Tambula — betel, served after a meal. "The pain of his heart" — *manera bedanā*: apparently spiritual longing; next the king asks for instruction (lahari 13, 2–3).

[^212-39]: "The account of the instruction" — *upadeśa-kathā*: the instruction and initiation of the three brothers, in lahari 13.

[^212-40]: Rasika-shekhara — "crown of the rasikas," an epithet of Rasika (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 5): the author says he heard the account from Rasika himself (cf. lahari 3, 97, note 42).

[^212-41]: "The description of [his] nature" — *sbabhāba-barṇanā* (lahari 10, note 31; lahari 11, note 31). "Composed" (77) — *karila racana* (in the 1997 edition *kahila*, "told").

[^212-42]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে রাজা বৈদ্যনাথ-ভঞ্জ-মিলন-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা."


## Lahari 13. The Establishment of Krishna's Worship through the Examination of All the Scriptures

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Raja Vaidyanatha asks Rasika to instruct the three brothers, and Rasika promises to initiate them and teaches them to worship Krishna alone, giving up the worship of various gods; the court bhattacharyas demand a learned debate, and Rasika, examining Sankhya, Mimamsa, Patanjali's yoga, logic, Vaisheshika, Vedanta, the four Vedas, the thirty-six smritis, poetry and grammar, shows that the essence of all the shastras is prema-bhakti for Krishna; the panditas admit that they cannot answer him, call him an avatara of Vyasa and Shuka and equal to Narayana; the raja asks about the truth of the living being, and Rasika tells how the jiva, not knowing Krishna, wanders by his karma in the cycle of births, suffers in the womb, remembers his past births and prays to Narayana for deliverance; the brothers ask why, once born, he forgets Krishna*

*The thirteenth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^213-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory to Rama and Krishna, O Murari!*
*O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, purifier of the worlds!
Be merciful, so that I may always sing [your] glory.

**2.** Thus the king speaks at Rasika's feet:
"Carefully instruct the three brothers.[^213-2]

**3.** Birth after birth we all are your servants;
seeing [us as] servants, be merciful, ocean of mercy."

**4.** Hearing the king's words, Prabhu says:
"I shall certainly give initiation to [you] three brothers.[^213-3]

**5.** Listen attentively, I shall say one thing:
taking exclusive shelter, worship Narayana.

**6.** Do not worship various gods any more;
worship wholeheartedly the son of Nanda.[^213-4]

**7.** From Krishna all bodies have their origin;
Krishna is the life of all, Krishna is the goal of all.

**8.** If one worships Krishna, whose mind [still holds] fear?
By Krishna's qualities all are intoxicated, rejoicing in bliss."

**9.** According to various shastras he explained the essence to him:
"All is false, Krishna is true — this is the conclusion of the shastras."[^213-5]

**10.** Hearing Rasika's words, the king rejoiced:
"Whatever you command, Prabhu, that word is true."

**11.** Hearing the talk of initiation, all the bhattacharyas present [said]:
"Listen, maharaja, what are you doing?

**12.** Here are hundreds upon hundreds of bhattacharyas [and] chakravartis;
we shall hold a learned debate with him.[^213-6]

**13.** The dharma that is established in all the shastras —
in that dharma we too shall take shelter."

**14.** Hearing [this], Rasika, greatly delighted,
with joined palms, says to the brahmanas with a smile:

**15.** "The word you have spoken is the very essence;
I shall examine the truth of the Vedas [and] the six shastras."[^213-7]

**16.** The king [and his brothers], the three, sat down joyfully;
all began to examine the shastras.[^213-8]

**17.** Rasika sat down joyfully, remembering Krishna,
like Brihaspati, Vyasa [and] Shuka embodied.[^213-9]

**18.** First he examined Sankhya [and] Sankhyayana:
in the truth of Sankhya he established the worship of Krishna.[^213-10]

**19.** Prabhu tells everyone the essence of the truth, drawn out [of the shastras];
no one knows any other reasoning about it.[^213-11]

**20.** No one says a word — they sit with heads bowed;
inwardly they go over their books: "That is indeed the meaning."[^213-12]

**21.** Then he examined the Mimamsa-shastra:
in it he established Krishna as the essence drawn out.

**22.** Then he examined the shastra of Patanjali:
in it he showed the worship of Krishna as the dharma of firm faith.[^213-13]

**23.** Then he expounded all the Tarka-shastra:
in it steadfastness in Krishna's dharma is enjoined by scripture.

**24.** Then he revealed the Vaisheshika-shastra:
in it he established steadfastness in the dharma of Shrinivasa.[^213-14]

**25.** Then he expounded the Vedanta-shastra:
in it the worship of Krishna was ascertained.

**26.** He explained all the truths of the four Vedas:
in them the proof of bhakti for Krishna is ascertained.

**27.** The thirty-six smritis and the other [books] that exist on earth —
in them he established bhakti for Krishna unshakeably.[^213-15]

**28.** Rasikendra established the conclusion of all the shastras;
no one in the host of panditas can refute it.

**29.** Poetry and drama, all the upashastras and the rest —
in all the shastras he explains bhakti for Krishna as the accepted [truth].

**30.** He explains the roots [and] sutras in their accepted form,
he explains the commentaries and glosses one by one.[^213-16]

**31.** With many words he draws conclusions in many ways —
the meaning of words, the meaning of the Vedas — in agreement with Shuka [and] Vyasa.

**32.** Drawing out the essence of all the shastras [and] the truth of the Vedas,
he made prema-bhakti for Krishna the essence of all the shastras.

**33.** In all the shastras, he says, firm faith is the worship of Krishna;
not knowing [this], the panditas wander in vain.

**34.** One shloka Rasika explains in many ways:
the worship of Krishna is true — such is the truth of the shastras.

**35.** The host of panditas does not understand the truth of the shastras;
[he] establishes bhakti for Krishna in all the shastras.

**36.** Hearing Rasika's explanation, all were amazed;
the brahmanas say: "An avatara of Vyasa and Shuka!"[^213-17]

**37.** "We have all studied the four Vedas [and] the six shastras,
[but], not knowing the truth, we wander in anxiety of mind.

**38.** Hearing from a boy's lips the settled meaning of the shastras,
now we have understood the worship [that is] firm faith in Krishna."[^213-18]

**39.** No one could refute Rasika's explanation;
what Rasikendra says, that alone is right.

**40.** All the bhattacharyas told the king:
"Rasika is not a boy: he is equal to Narayana."[^213-19]

**41.** The king [and his brothers], the three, say: "Listen, best of brahmanas:
all of you, answer the boy."

**42.** Hearing [this], all the brahmanas say to the king:
"He is not a boy — he is equal to Narayana.

**43.** Either Vyasa, Shuka, Narada and the other sages,
or Brihaspati himself has taken birth.

**44.** The very shastras we studied at the cost of our lives —
those same shastras Rasika explains in so many ways!

**45.** One shloka he explains in many ways —
the meaning of the Vedas, the meaning of words, the truth of the shastras [with] proof.

**46.** He explains the roots [and] sutras, all that is accepted;
this boy's intelligence is equal to [that of] Vyasa [and] Shuka.

**47.** We could not set this boy [a single] problem;
what Rasika says, that alone is proof."[^213-20]

**48.** Hearing [this] from the brahmanas' lips, the king rejoiced
and with faith asks Rasika about everything.

**49.** He raised before Rasika [the question of] the truth of the living being;
Rasika tells everyone in detail:[^213-21]

**50.** "The jiva, subordinate to Ishvara, wanders under the sway of karma;
not knowing the truth of Krishna, he roams in samsara.[^213-22]

**51.** Wandering through various species, the jiva becomes senseless
and does not worship his own Lord, God Narayana.[^213-23]

**52.** I shall tell of the course of the jiva; listen, everyone:
rajas and virya are a single substance, arranged by the Creator.[^213-24]

**53.** From water are born blood, flesh, bones, skin;
[the jiva] enters the womb, taking his own karma with him.[^213-25]

**54.** In the seventh month the jiva becomes manifest in the womb;
much suffering does the jiva undergo, dwelling in the womb.[^213-26]

**55.** Pungent, bitter, salty and other things that the mother eats —
all of it pricks [him] in every pore, and it cannot be borne.

**56.** In distress the jiva seeks shelter;
in the womb he takes shelter of God Narayana.[^213-27]

**57.** All the births he has had under the sway of karma,
one by one — all of it comes to his mind in the womb.[^213-28]

**58.** Then, seized with terror, he calls to Narayana:
'Deliver me, Prabhu, I take shelter of You!

**59.** Blinded by sense objects, I did not worship You;
for that reason, Prabhu, You gave me the torments of the womb.

**60.** The five pranas [and] the twenty-five tattvas dwell in the body;
kama, anger, greed, delusion are especially enemies;

**61.** pride and envy dwell [there too] — these are [my] six riches;
sound, touch, form, taste, smell — this is [my] retinue.[^213-29]

**62.** All these enemies are with me without cease;
they did not let me worship Your lotus feet.

**63.** Thus birth after birth I undergo much suffering:
I did not take Hari's name in Hari-sankirtana,

**64.** I did not serve the sadhus, did not travel to holy places,
I showed no mercy to living beings — [my] life has been fruitless.

**65.** Brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras — Narayana is [their] father;
not recognising the father, they wander, bewildered.[^213-30]

**66.** Now be merciful to me, Prabhu Bhagavan,
that birth after birth I may meditate on Your feet.

**67.** Be merciful, Narayana, brother of those who take shelter [of You],
that birth after birth I may worship Your feet.[^213-31]

**68.** Without worshipping You the jiva is not delivered;
thus he ever wanders through various species.

**69.** Brahma, Shiva [and] Purandara, by Your maya,
wander on the wheel of samsara by Your lila.[^213-32]

**70.** The one whom You accept [as Your own], showing mercy,
that person easily attains Your feet.'

**71.** Thus in yoga and meditation within the womb
the jiva offers various prayers, having come to know the Lord."

**72.** Hearing all these words, the three brothers [asked]:
"Why then, once born, does [the jiva] forget Krishna?"[^213-33]

**73.** Rasika tells everything as it is set forth in the shastras;
who could relate all those words even with a hundred mouths?

**74.** In brief I shall compose something of it;
listen to the Rasika-mangala, all you sadhus.

**75.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the thirteenth lahari, called "The Establishment of Krishna's Worship through the Examination of All the Scriptures."*[^213-34]

[^213-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Kaushika; the ghosha — *jaẏa re rāmakṛṣṇa murāre / o murāre o murāre* — is almost the same as in the Purva-vibhaga, laharis 3 and 16 (note 1 there): Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari ("enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna, which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে সর্ব্বশাস্ত্রবিচারে কৃষ্ণভজন-স্থাপন-নাম ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*sarbaśāstrabicāre kṛṣṇabhajana-sthāpana*). The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^213-2]: "Instruct" — *upadeśa karaha*: give instruction, i.e. initiation (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 8; cf. 4). ("listen, brother") instead of "তিন ভাই," apparently a recognition error. Servants (3) — *kiṅkara*.

[^213-3]: Initiation — *dīkṣā* (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 8; lahari 10, note 26). "Prabhu" — Rasika.

[^213-4]: "Do not worship various gods any more; worship wholeheartedly the son of Nanda" — cf. the Bhagavad-gita (9.23–24; 18.66). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the demigods are respected as servants of the Lord but are not worshipped as independent lords; the devotee worships Krishna alone (*ananya-śaraṇa*, 5).

[^213-5]: "All is false, Krishna is true" — *saba mithyā kṛṣṇa satya*. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the world is a real, though temporary, energy of the Lord, not an illusion (CC, Madhya 6, the debate with Sarvabhauma on vivarta-vada); "false" here means everything apart from its relation to Krishna is futile and transient.

[^213-6]: Bhattacharya, chakravarti — titles of learned brahmanas. "We shall hold a learned debate" — *bidyāra bibāda kari*; "with him" — *uhāra saṅgati*.

[^213-7]: "The very essence" — *sei sāroddhāra*, lit. "the essence drawn out": Rasika accepts the brahmanas' condition (13). The six shastras are the six philosophical systems (lahari 12, note 12); Rasika then examines them one by one (18–25).

[^213-8]: "The king [and his brothers], the three" — *rājā tina bhāi* (likewise in 41).

[^213-9]: "Joyfully" — *raṅge*. "Remembering" — *samariẏā* (= *smariẏā*). Brihaspati, Vyasa, Shuka — lahari 12, notes 12 and 23. "Embodied" — *mūrttimanta*.

[^213-10]: Sankhya, Sankhyayana — lahari 10, note 28; lahari 12, note 27. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition the true Sankhya is the teaching of Kapila, the son of Devahuti, which leads to bhakti ("Bhagavata," Canto 3, chs. 25–33). "He established the worship of Krishna" — *niṣṭhā kaila kṛṣṇera bhajana*: he showed that the conclusion of Sankhya is the worship of Krishna; likewise below (21–27).

[^213-11]: "No one knows any other reasoning about it" — *keha jāne nāhi āra ihāra bicāra*; the sense is approximate: no one could object.

[^213-12]: "With heads bowed" — *heṭa māthe*. "Inwardly they go over their books: 'That is indeed the meaning'" — *mane mane pũthi cinte sei artha haẏe*; the sense is approximate.

[^213-13]: The shastra of Patanjali is the Yoga-sutras. "The dharma of firm faith" — *niṣṭhā-dharma*. The Tarka-shastra (23) is logic (Nyaya); "enjoined by scripture" — *śāstrapraṇihita*.

[^213-14]: Shrinivasa (*śrīnibāsa*), "the abode of Shri (Lakshmi)," is a name of Vishnu. "He established steadfastness in the dharma of Shrinivasa" — *karila niṣṭhā dharma śrīnibāsa*; it can also be understood as "he established the firm [conviction]: dharma is Shrinivasa."

[^213-15]: The thirty-six smritis are the traditional count of the dharma-shastras (codes of sacred law). ("thirty"), apparently a recognition error.

[^213-16]: Upashastras (29) — the auxiliary sciences. "Roots [and] sutras" — *dhātu sūtra*: grammar (verbal roots and rules, sutras). "Commentaries and glosses" — *ṭīkā*, *ṭippanī*.

[^213-17]: "An avatara of Vyasa and Shuka" — the rapturous words of the brahmanas, as is "equal to Narayana" (40, 42–43; lahari 12, note 19).

[^213-18]: "A boy" — *bālaka*: Rasika was young at the time. "The worship [that is] firm faith in Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-niṣṭhāra bhajana*.

[^213-19]: "Equal to Narayana" — *nārāyaṇa sama*: the words of the panditas (cf. 42); on the theological side see lahari 12, note 19 (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^213-20]: "Problem" — *samasyā*: a difficult question, a riddle to test learning. "Proof" — *paramāṇa* (*pramāṇa*), i.e. beyond dispute.

[^213-21]: "He raised … [the question of] the truth of the living being" — *jībatattba pracārila*: apparently the king (48); it can also be understood as "Rasika expounded." Next (50–71) Rasika describes the life of the jiva in the womb.

[^213-22]: "Subordinate to Ishvara" — *īśbara adhīna*. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the jiva is the eternal servant of Krishna; having forgotten Krishna, he wanders under the sway of karma in the cycle of births (CC, Madhya 20). Rasika's speech continues (51–71).

[^213-23]: "Senseless" — *acetana*, "devoid of consciousness": having forgotten himself and God. Rasika's speech, begun in 50, continues to 71; the jiva's prayer in the womb (58–70) is a speech within the speech. The teaching on the jiva in the womb (51–71) is close to Kapila's teaching in the Bhagavatam (3.31).

[^213-24]: "Rajas and virya" — *rajobīryya*: the female and male seed. "Arranged by the Creator" — *bidhātā-ghaṭana*; Vidhata is the Creator, Brahma.

[^213-25]: "From water" — *jala haite*: apparently from the fluids of conception. "His own karma" — *ātmakarmma*, the fruits of past actions that determine the new body.

[^213-26]: "Becomes manifest" — *haẏa parakāśa*: in the seventh month he gains consciousness (cf. Bhagavatam 3.31).

[^213-27]: "Seeks shelter", "takes shelter" — *śaraṇa*; in Middle Bengali *śaraṇa* may also stand for *smaraṇa* — then: "remembers God Narayana."

[^213-28]: "All of it" — *saba tattva*, lit. "all the truths (circumstances)": in the womb the jiva remembers his former births.

[^213-29]: The five pranas are the vital airs (prana, apana, vyana, udana, samana); the twenty-five tattvas are the principles of existence according to Sankhya. The six enemies (*ṣaṛ ripu*) are kama (*kāma*, worldly desire), anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy; "six riches" (*ṣaṛ sampatti*) is bitter irony. "Retinue" — *saṅgati*: the five objects of the senses.

[^213-30]: "Brahmanas, kshatriyas" — *brahmakṣetrī* (= *brahma-kṣatriya*). Cf. lahari 14, 22–24.

[^213-31]: "Brother of those who take shelter [of You]" — *śaraṇa sodara* (cf. lahari 12, 67).

[^213-32]: Purandara is Indra. "By Your lila" — *tomāra līlāẏa*: by Your will, in Your play. Thus the author speaks of the Lord's power over all the demigods; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Brahma and Indra are jivas in the highest posts of the universe, while Shiva is a special category distinct from ordinary living beings (CC, Madhya 20; Brahma-samhita 5.45).

[^213-33]: "Forget" — *pāśare* (= *pāsare*). Rasika's answer is in lahari 14.

[^213-34]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে সর্ব্বশাস্ত্রবিচারে কৃষ্ণভজন-স্থাপন-নাম ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*sarbbaśāstra-bicāre kṛṣṇabhajana-sthāpana*); the 1997 edition reads the same; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 14. The Examination of the Truth of the Jiva and of Abhidheya

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika continues to instruct the raja and the three brothers: once born and touching the earth, the jiva by maya forgets Krishna and in childhood, youth, maturity and old age does not worship Him, wandering through eighty-four lakhs of species; Krishna is the Lord and father of all, and the four varnas were born from Him; the human body is rare and fleeting, its end is certain, kinsmen are strangers, pride ruins; Rasika bids them chant the name without delay, serve the sadhus and Vaishnavas while staying at home, take shelter of a guru wholly surrendered to Krishna, of whatever caste he may be, and never take instruction from one who is not devoted to Krishna, even if he is learned in the Vedas; the panditas cannot refute him, all give up the worship of other gods and surrender to Krishna; the author promises to tell how they gave up the killing of living beings*

*The fourteenth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^214-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Pay heed to fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the son of Durika!
Glory, glory to the life of Rasika, the treasure of [his] life![^214-2]

**2.** Thus Rasika speaks to the raja;
motionless, with affection, the three brothers listen.

**3.** He told of the jiva within the womb:
[there] the jiva meditates on Narayana without cease.

**4.** The jiva who comes forth from the womb onto the earth —
[that] jiva forgets everything by the Lord's maya.[^214-3]

**5.** Subject to the Lord, the jiva wanders by the fruits of karma;
as soon as he touched the earth, all [his] knowledge was stolen away.[^214-4]

**6.** In childhood the jiva wanders senseless,
having forgotten Krishna, the lord of his life.

**7.** Then in the age of pauganda, for so many days,
leaving Krishna's feet, the jiva is intoxicated with the taste of learning.[^214-5]

**8.** In the age of kishora the jiva is intoxicated with pride;
he does not worship Krishna's feet, absorbed in ignorance.

**9.** Then, after some days, comes the time of [mature] age;
blinded by various sense objects, he does not worship Krishna.[^214-6]

**10.** Then, after some days, old age enters the jiva;
not worshipping Krishna, the jiva suffers various afflictions.

**11.** In this way [go] the appearance and dissolution of the jiva;
not worshipping Krishna, he wanders through various species.

**12.** For eighty-four lakhs [of births] the jiva wanders through various species;
he does not worship Narayana, does not hear the words of the sadhus.

**13.** I shall tell in detail of the eighty-four lakhs [of births] of the jiva;
I shall tell the essential meaning of the shastras — listen attentively.[^214-7]

**14.** Twenty lakhs [of births] the jiva wanders as the immovable and the like —
I speak in accordance with the shastras, as is well known.

**15.** Then [he] becomes an aquatic: nine lakhs of births;
when one does not worship Krishna, all this comes about.

**16.** Eleven lakhs he wanders in various species of worms;
birth after birth he suffers, not knowing Krishna.

**17.** Then ten lakhs are births in the species of birds;
he wanders on the wheel of maya, not knowing Krishna the Lord.

**18.** Thirty lakhs he wanders in various species of animals;
not worshipping Krishna, the living being suffers much.

**19.** Then four lakhs of births as a human being:
[he] wanders in various low births, not knowing Krishna.[^214-8]

**20.** Then a hundred births, known as brahminhood;
not worshipping Krishna, [the jiva] is bewildered by false learning.[^214-9]

**21.** The brahmana reads various shastras, [remaining] senseless:
he does not accept, does not worship the feet of Sri Krishna.

**22.** Krishna is the Lord of all, the father of all;
they do not recognise Krishna the father, being bewildered.

**23.** From Krishna's mouth the brahmanas were born;
from Krishna's arms came the birth of the kshatriyas;

**24.** from Krishna's thighs came the birth of the vaishyas;
and the shudras were born from Krishna's feet.[^214-10]

**25.** His own father, Krishna, the jiva forgets by maya;
thus birth after birth he suffers much.

**26.** Exceedingly rare is this human body;
in a moment it perishes, unsteady as lightning.[^214-11]

**27.** Only then is this human body called rare
when [one] has love for Krishna [and] for the company of sadhus.[^214-12]

**28.** If one keeps the company of sadhus, one will attain Narayana;
without worship this body gets [only] much toil.

**29.** All that I have told of the jiva's birth and dying —
without worshipping Krishna [he] sets out on his wanderings again.

**30.** The end — now, or in a hundred years?
Together with the body its dying is born — such is the judgement of the shastras.[^214-13]

**31.** Having obtained such a body, why do they neglect [it]?
To cross the ocean of existence, Krishna's name is the raft.[^214-14]

**32.** The city of Kritanta has drawn near;
in the grip of Time, day by day life and strength depart.[^214-15]

**33.** Therefore make Narayana's name your provision [for the road];
the end is certain — this is the truth; meditate on Krishna.[^214-16]

**34.** Sing of Krishna, worship Krishna, remember Krishna;
be merciful to all living beings, serve the Vaishnavas.

**35.** Performing Krishna-sankirtana, take Hari's name;
with reverence hear of the host of Krishna's qualities.

**36.** Constantly serve the sadhus with a glad heart,
without guile, in the company of sadhus, in an abundance of prema.[^214-17]

**37.** Staying in your own home, worship Narayana;
with prema serve the sadhus, [perform] Krishna-sankirtana.

**38.** Gladly give food and water to guests;
leaving everything, worship Krishna, purified in mind.

**39.** Time always walks alongside the jiva;
child, youth [or] old man — that cannot be determined.

**40.** Some on the lap, some in the hand, some in the mouth [it holds]:
thus is the jiva subject to Time.[^214-18]

**41.** Mother, father, wife, son, friend, brother —
no one is one's own; know that all are strangers.[^214-19]

**42.** The one you call brother — he it is who will set fire to [your] mouth;
love Krishna, O living being — why perish in sorrow?[^214-20]

**43.** The pride of wealth, the pride of learning, the pride of youth,
the pride of family, the pride of kingdom and whatever [other] possession —

**44.** beguiled by these, do not perish in falsehood;
with firm attachment worship Narayana's feet.[^214-21]

**45.** Without worshipping Narayana there is no deliverance;
in the Vedas, shastras [and] Puranas the essence is devotion to Krishna.

**46.** True is Krishna, true is Krishna — know this for certain;
knowing all [else] to be false, take shelter of Krishna.[^214-22]

**47.** Blessed is that devotee of Krishna, [though] he live [but] five days;
what use is it, not worshipping Krishna, [to live] millions of kalpas?[^214-23]

**48.** Leaving everything, Prabhu, take shelter of Krishna;
child, youth [or] old man — do not be deluded.[^214-24]

**49.** There is no fixed age for worshipping Krishna:
Dhruva, Prahlada, Shuka, Hanu — from their very childhood.[^214-25]

**50.** Without delay worship Krishna, taking pains;
at the guru's place hear the narrations about Krishna.

**51.** As long as the jiva has not received [the mantra] in his ear from the guru,
know for certain: that person is called an animal.[^214-26]

**52.** All that [is offered] by his hand is like nectar,
but otherwise water is [as] urine: such is the testimony of the shastras.[^214-27]

**53.** Be he versed in the four Vedas, an ascetic in his conduct —
even leaving the body in a holy place, he still does not attain deliverance.

**54.** Shraddha and all else that he performs — all [leads] downward,
as long as he does not take shelter of Krishna the Lord.[^214-28]

**55.** Take shelter of a guru wholly surrendered [to Krishna],
of the guru who releases from the bonds of existence.

**56.** With your whole being take shelter at the guru's feet;
receiving instruction, enter Krishna's shelter.

**57.** [Be he] a brahmana of noble family, [versed] in the four Vedas and six shastras,
a sannyasi, an ascetic, shining with great knowledge —

**58.** whoever is not a devotee of Krishna wholly surrendered [to Him],
from him never take instruction.[^214-29]

**59.** If [a man] is wholly surrendered [to Krishna], of whatever caste he may be,
[and] with his whole being has taken shelter of Krishna —

**60.** take shelter of such a guru firmly:
by the mercy of such a guru the agitation of the mind departs.

**61.** With faith worship the feet of such a guru —
then without delay you will obtain the treasure of devotion to Krishna.[^214-30]

**62.** Thus Rasika speaks to the raja,
[citing] the testimony of the six shastras, the Bhagavata [and] the Nigama.[^214-31]

**63.** Then the assembly of panditas listened [to him]:
who has the power to refute such [words]?

**64.** All accepted Rasika's words as true;
abandoning ignorance, all began to meditate on Krishna.

**65.** Abandoning the worship of various other gods, all the people
with their whole being took shelter of Krishna.[^214-32]

**66.** How they gave up the killing of living beings and the like —
that I shall tell in detail; listen, everyone.[^214-33]

**67.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**68.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Examination of the Truth of the Jiva and of Abhidheya."*[^214-34]

[^214-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("চতুর্দশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*); the ghosha is the same as in laharis 7 and 10 (lahari 7, note 1). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "জীবতত্ত্ব ও অভিধেয়-তত্ত্ববিচারনাম চতুর্দশ-লহরী" (*jībatattva o abhidheya-tattva-bicāra*); the 1997 edition reads the same. Jiva-tattva is the truth of the jiva (lahari 13, note 22). Abhidheya is the means of attaining the goal, i.e., the practice of bhakti (cf. sambandha, abhidheya, prayojana — CC, Madhya 20–25). The whole lahari is; the summary line follows the scans.

[^214-2]: Durika is Shyamananda's mother (Purva, lahari 1, note 11). "The life of Rasika, the treasure of [his] life" — *rasika-jībana prāṇadhana* (cf. lahari 7, 1).

[^214-3]: Jiva (*jība*) — as in lahari 13 (50–71; lahari 13, note 22). "Comes forth onto the earth" — *bhūmigata haẏa*. In the 1997 edition the first line reads "তাহাতে সেই জীব…" ("then that jiva…").

[^214-4]: "As soon as he touched the earth" — *pṛthbī paraśite*: once born and fallen onto the ground, the infant loses the memory of his prayers in the womb (cf. Bhagavatam 3.31). "Wanders by the fruits of karma" — *phire karmmaphale*.

[^214-5]: Pauganda is the age from five to ten, kishora (8) from ten to fifteen. "Intoxicated with the taste of learning" — *matta bidyārase*: absorbed in study for worldly ends. "With pride" (8) — *made*.

[^214-6]: "The time of [mature] age" — *baẏasa samaẏa*, lit. "the time of age".

[^214-7]: The count of species (14–19): immovable — 20 lakhs, aquatic — 9, worms — 11, birds — 10, animals — 30, humans — 4; in all 84 lakhs (8,400,000), as in the verse usually cited from the Padma Purana (*jalajā nava-lakṣāṇi…*). A lakh is one hundred thousand. The hundred births as a brahmana (20) are the author's addition beyond this count.

[^214-8]: "Low births" — *antyaja-yoni*: births outside the four varnas.

[^214-9]: "Brahminhood" — *brahmaṇya*. "False learning" — *kubidyā*.

[^214-10]: Cf. Bhagavatam 11.5.2 and the Purusha-sukta (Rigveda 10.90): from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet of the Purusha the four varnas were born.

[^214-11]: "Perishes" — *bhaṅgura*; "unsteady as lightning" — *taṛita-asthira*. Cf. Bhagavatam 11.9.29: human birth is rare and impermanent, yet it grants the highest goal.

[^214-12]: "Love" — *senaha* (= *sneha*; the gloss is not translated). The line may also be understood as "has love for Krishna in the company of sadhus."

[^214-13]: "The end", "dying" — *maraṇa*, *mṛtyu*. "Together with the body its dying is born" — *deha saṅge mṛtyu jāta*; cf. Bhagavad-gita 2.27.

[^214-14]: "Raft" — *bhelā*.

[^214-15]: "The city of Kritanta" — *kṛtānta-nagara*: the abode of Yama, lord of the netherworld (Kritanta, "He who makes an end"). "In the grip of Time" — *kālagraste*. "Life and strength" — *āẏurbbalā*; the gloss is not translated).

[^214-16]: "Provision [for the road]" — *sambala*.

[^214-17]: "In an abundance of prema" — *prema atireke*.

[^214-18]: *keha kole keha hāte keha-i mukhete*: understood as a figure of Time (Kala) holding the jivas — some on its lap, some in its hand, some already in its mouth; the sense is approximate. "Thus" — *hena-i yugate* (*yugati* = *yukti*, "manner"); it can also be understood as "in such a yuga".

[^214-19]: "Wife" — *strīri* (so in the edition).

[^214-20]: "Will set fire to [your] mouth" — *sei poṛe mukhe*: the rite of mukhagni — at the funeral pyre a son or brother touches fire to the mouth of the one who has left the body. "Perish" — *mara*, lit. "die".

[^214-21]: "Possession" — *sampada*. "Do not perish in falsehood" — *nā mara mithyāẏa*, lit. "do not die by falsehood (in vain)". "With firm attachment" — *dṛṛha anurāge*.

[^214-22]: "All [else] is false" — *saba mithyā*: cf. lahari 13, 9 and note 5.

[^214-23]: "Five days" — *pā̃ca dina*: i.e., a very short time. "Millions of kalpas" — *koṭi kalpe*; a kalpa is a day of Brahma.

[^214-24]: "Prabhu" — Rasika's address to the raja. "Do not be deluded" — *nā kara bharama*: do not think that the time for serving Krishna has not yet come (cf. 49).

[^214-25]: Dhruva (Bhagavatam 4.8–9), Prahlada (Bhagavatam 7.5–9), Shuka(deva) and Hanu(man) were devotees from childhood. "Hanu" — *hanu*, Hanuman.

[^214-26]: "Has not received [the mantra] in his ear from the guru" — *gurukarṇa … nāhi haẏa*, lit. "there has been no guru-ear": has not received initiation (the guru speaks the mantra into the disciple's ear). "Is called an animal" — *paśu bali*.

[^214-27]: "By his hand" — *tā'ra hāte*: by the hand of the initiated. "But otherwise water is [as] urine" — *tā nā ha'le jala mūtra*: the offering of the uninitiated is impure.

[^214-28]: "Leaving the body" — *maile*, lit. "on dying": it was held that departing this life in a holy place (Kashi and others) grants liberation by itself. Shraddha is the memorial rite for the ancestors. "[Leads] downward" — *adhogati*. "Krishna the Lord" — *kṛṣṇapati*.

[^214-29]: "Devotee of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa*: the 1941 edition has "কাষ্ণ´", with the reph shifted to the right (cf. *kārṣṇa-jana*, Purva, lahari 10, note 13). (garbled). "Wholly surrendered" — *ananya-śaraṇa*. Cf. the verse of the Padma Purana cited in the Hari-bhakti-vilasa (first vilasa): a brahmana expert in the six duties, mantras and tantras cannot be a guru if he is not a Vaishnava, while a Vaishnava, even one born among dog-eaters, can.

[^214-30]: 55–61: the guru is defined not by caste but by devotion to Krishna (59); cf. CC, Madhya 8: "Whether a brahmana, a sannyasi or a shudra — whoever knows the science of Krishna, he is a guru."

[^214-31]: "Nigama" — the Vedas. "The six shastras" — lahari 12, note 12. "Testimony" — *paramāṇe* (= *pramāṇe*).

[^214-32]: "The worship of various other gods" — *nānā debāntara-pūjā*: thus Rasika's instruction at the beginning of lahari 13 is fulfilled (6; lahari 13, note 4).

[^214-33]: "The killing of living beings" — *jībahatyā*: apparently animal sacrifice; the account is in lahari 15.

[^214-34]: The colophon is; on the title see note 1. Lahari 15 begins.


## Lahari 15. The Instruction to Maharaja Vaidyanatha Bhanja on Meditation on Vrindavana and on Worship

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; before the king and the bhattacharyas Rasika speaks of the greatness of the sadhus and of their association: one who does not worship Krishna lives like a tree, breathes like a blacksmith's bellows, and in intelligence is like a hog, a dog, a camel and an ass, while a brahmana averse to Krishna is lower than a devoted shvapacha; the gods are Krishna's servants, and one may worship Him while remaining at home; subjects of every class surrender to Krishna; Rasika asks the three brothers for alms — the giving up of the killing of living beings — and names the eight who fall into hell for killing an animal; the brothers and all the people take exclusive shelter, the bhattacharyas acknowledge Rasika as an associate of Krishna and bless him, the king worships his feet, and the brothers receive the Krishna-mantra; Rasika teaches them to meditate on Krishna, the Lord of Vrindavana, in the mood of madhurya and describes Vrindavana — the Kalindi, the twelve forests, the wish-fulfilling trees, the jewelled pavilion and temple, the throne, the form of Radha and Krishna, the playing of the flute and the circle of the gopis; the brothers firmly devote themselves to the worship of Krishna*

*The fifteenth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^215-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory to Rama and Krishna, O Murari!*
*O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, renowned in [all] the world,
the shining moon of the family among all the cowherd lineages![^215-2]

**2.** At that time Rasika speaks to the king,
[and] the great bhattacharyas listen.[^215-3]

**3.** With tears, with thrills [of joy] they hear Rasika's words;
giving up ignorance, they entered Krishna's shelter.

**4.** Then he speaks firmly of the greatness of the sadhus;
hearing [it], everyone was freed from the anxiety of the mind.

**5.** "Listen, listen, everyone, to the greatness of the sadhus:
even Brahma cannot tell its limit.

**6.** If by good fortune association with a sadhu happens even for a moment,
by [his] sight the sin that binds one to births is destroyed.[^215-4]

**7.** All the holy places of the gods he purifies forever;
the mere sight of a sadhu is the highest blessing.[^215-5]

**8.** Keep the company of such sadhus, giving up all [other] talk:
in the company of sadhus all the pains of birth in the world are ended.

**9.** For the good of the sadhus Krishna is always [with them];
the heart of a sadhu is Sri Krishna's own home.[^215-6]

**10.** Keep the company of such sadhus, worship Lord Krishna:
without the company of sadhus one never attains Krishna.

**11.** Keeping the company of sadhus, worship Krishna's feet;
why waste the human birth in vain?

**12.** If one does not worship Krishna, the living being suffers great misery:
he always sinks in the most terrible hell.

**13.** The rod of Yama constantly strikes the jiva;
now rising, now falling, he perishes in hell.[^215-7]

**14.** When, giving up everything, he takes shelter of Narayana,
then he is delivered in this round of worldly existence.[^215-8]

**15.** The living being who does not worship Krishna lives like a tree;
like a blacksmith's bellows, he [merely] breathes.[^215-9]

**16.** Whatever a being not devoted to Krishna eats —
whatever he eats is called impure.

**17.** His intelligence is like a hog's: he does not discriminate;
his intelligence is like a dog's: such is that wicked one.

**18.** His intelligence is like a camel's: he does not worship Krishna,
he eats thorns and the like, filling his belly.

**19.** Like an ass, the being carries various burdens
all the days that he does not hear the nectarean words about Krishna.

**20.** Even if he is the best of brahmanas, endowed with twice six qualities —
if he does not worship Krishna, he is called a shvapacha.[^215-10]

*Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam:*

**21.** *"Than a brahmana endowed with twice six qualities but averse to the lotus feet*
*of the Lotus-naveled [Lord], better, I consider, is a shvapacha*
*who has offered to Him his mind, speech, activities, wealth*
*and life: he purifies [his] family, but not one [full] of pride."*[^215-11]

**22.** All the gods and goddesses are Krishna's servants;
all of them are constantly enchanted by the taste of Krishna's happiness.

**23.** If one worships Krishna, the gods are not angry:
if one waters the root of a tree, the leaves [too] are satisfied.[^215-12]

**24.** Gods, asuras, humans, yakshas, kinnaras, gandharvas and others —
all are blessed if [one] worships Krishna.

**25.** The supreme bliss of all is Lord Narayana;
giving up everything, all of you, worship Krishna's feet.

**26.** By no means waste this rare birth in vain:
if one worships Krishna, all the pains of worldly existence are ended.

**27.** Wife, sons and the rest, one's own household affairs,
wealth, people, kinsmen [and] family are false.[^215-13]

**28.** Offering [them] to Krishna with body, mind and speech,
all of you, with one mind, worship Krishna abundantly.

**29.** Remaining amid all this, worship Krishna firmly:
if you worship Krishna exclusively, you will quickly attain [Him].

**30.** Fix your mind unceasingly on Krishna's feet;
with body, mind and speech take shelter of Krishna.

**31.** Rejecting nectar, do not drink poison:
Krishna is nectar, and the rest is like poison."

**32.** Thus, expounding the truths of all the shastras,
Rasikendra spoke to the three brothers.

**33.** All the subjects who were in the king's assembly —
kshatriyas, vaishyas, brahmanas, shudras — gave their minds to Krishna.[^215-14]

**34.** For all who heard Rasika's words
suffering was ended: [they took] Krishna's shelter.

**35.** The sixty-four [kinds of] bhakti come at once to one
to whom the son of Achyuta is gracious.[^215-15]

**36.** A supreme Vaishnava, with a perfectly pure mind, becomes [one]
who hears Rasika's words with faith.

**37.** Then Rasika-shekhara commanded:
"Give me one alms, three brothers."[^215-16]

**38.** Hastily the three brothers joined their palms:
"Wealth, people, life — all are at your disposal.

**39.** Whatever you wish, command, considering [us] servants:
I have offered everything to your feet."

**40.** Hearing [this], the son of Achyuta says joyfully:
"Give me as alms [the giving up of] the killing of living beings.[^215-17]

**41.** If one does violence to living beings, great sin results:
at the end [of life] the being goes and falls into the terrible [hell] Raurava.[^215-18]

**42.** Eight persons fall into terrible hell;
I shall tell — listen attentively, with care.

**43.** The one who, seeing the animal, gives consent [to the killing];
the one who is the ruler of that village;[^215-19]

**44.** and the one who catches the animal and leads [it] away;
the one who buys, the one who sells, deluded by maya;

**45.** that lowest of brahmanas who offers the animal in sacrifice;
the one who cuts, the one who eats — these are the eight persons.

**46.** These eight persons fall into the most terrible hell —
[all] who, bereft of sense, kill an animal.[^215-20]

**47.** As many hairs as there are on the animal's body,
so many years they lie in these hells.

*Thus [it is said] in the Padma Purana:*

**48.** *The one who consents, the overseer, the slayer, the buyer [and] the seller,*
*the one who prepares it, the one who serves [and] the eaters — the eight killers.*[^215-21]

**49.** *He dwells in terrible hell for [as many] years [as] the animal's hairs —*
*so measured — that wicked one who kills animals contrary to the injunctions.*

**50.** For the destroyer of his own soul, the wicked one, there is no deliverance:
thus birth after birth passes for him in vain.[^215-22]

**51.** In all living beings Narayana dwells in a subtle form:
be it a worm or Brahma — [in each] He dwells in His own form.[^215-23]

**52.** All beings who thus do violence to living beings
fall into the Maharauravas and wander in births among the lowborn.

**53.** Thus, giving up everything, give your mind to Krishna;
offer home, sons, wealth to Krishna.

**54.** Krishna is mother, Krishna is father, Krishna is destroyer [and] creator;
Krishna is the Lord of all, Krishna is the protector.

**55.** Krishna is wealth, Krishna is kin, Krishna is friends;
knowing that Krishna is the soul, enter Krishna's shelter.[^215-24]

**56.** Seeing this suffering of the jivas, I am moved to compassion;
therefore I have told [it all] in order.

**57.** Heed my words, give your mind to Krishna,
make this human birth fruitful."

**58.** Seeing one another, all took exclusive shelter;
all the bhattacharyas say to the king:[^215-25]

**59.** hearing Rasika's words, the great best of kings —
the three brothers — became exclusive Vaishnavas.

**60.** Such wicked [men] became sadhus by the word of Rasika —
the son of Achyuta, whose vow is to crush the asuras.[^215-26]

**61.** When the king [and his brothers], the three noble ones, became sadhus,
hearing [of it], all the people took shelter of Krishna.

**62.** Whether women, children or the old —
seeing one another, all took exclusive shelter.

**63.** All the bhattacharyas say to the king:
"What Rasika says is the word of Shuka [and] Vyasa.

**64.** Much did [we] debate according to the doctrines of the six shastras,
[but] could not answer Rasika.

**65.** By the truth of the shastras he established the worship of Krishna;
no one had the power to refute [it].

**66.** We wandered so long, not knowing [the truth];
in vain did we all study, not knowing Krishna.

**67.** He has proclaimed this secret [hidden] in the Vedas:
this son of Achyuta is an associate of Krishna.[^215-27]

**68.** Blessed are King Vaidyanatha Bhanja [and his brothers], the three,
to whom Rasika Gosani has shown mercy!"

**69.** Thus the brahmanas, praising Rasika,
blessed [him], having found joy in their minds.

**70.** Seeing Rasika's power, the maharaja
worshipped Rasika's feet in many ways.

**71.** The three brothers received instruction in the Krishna-mantra;
[Rasika] began to speak [to them] of Krishna according to the nigama.[^215-28]

**72.** Prabhu explained to them what [true] worship is;
the three brothers listen, motionless.

**73.** "[It is] one's own mood: prema-bhakti for Krishna,
the mood in which the cowherd men and gopis of Vraja attained Krishna.[^215-29]

**74.** Krishna, the Lord of Vrindavana, is Bhagavan Himself;
meditate on Krishna in the mood of madhurya."

**75.** Rasika says: "King, listen with a firm mind:
I shall tell briefly something of the beauty of Vrindavana."

**76.** The three brothers hear all that account
which Rasikendra-chudamani related.[^215-30]

**77.** "The greatness of Vrindavana cannot be expressed —
[that Vrindavana] on which Devendra and all the other gods meditate.

**78.** In Vrindavana the trees are in flowers and [young] leaves;
the trees are adorned with flowers, [there are] various birds.

**79.** In swarms the bees come, maddened;
all of them, circling, [sing] with a resounding hum.[^215-31]

**80.** Around Vrindavana is the lovely Kalindi;
[her] water is very cool, the waves are beautiful.

**81.** In Vrindavana trees, creepers, various flowers shine;
the trees adorned with flowers enchant the gods.

**82.** In that abode the moon and the sun rise at the same time;
kindled by [their] radiance, that place always shines.[^215-32]

**83.** Lotuses — kamala, utpala, kahlara;
the ground everywhere is adorned with pollen.[^215-33]

**84.** All the forest creatures always play there;
various deer always serve there.

**85.** There are no enemies or friends [there] — all play in bliss,
always beholding the lotus feet of Radha and Krishna.

**86.** In it are places where the twelve forests shine,
and also eighteen upavanas, as [the shastras] attest.[^215-34]

**87.** The beautiful forests shine, full of great beauty;
their beauty, surpassing Vaikuntha, cannot be described.

**88.** The ground, [made] of jewels — chintamani — is beautiful;
that world always shines [like] hosts of suns.[^215-35]

**89.** Meditate on such wish-fulfilling trees in Vrindavana:
pendants of gems hang [from them] — they cannot be described.[^215-36]

**90.** Those trees constantly shower various jewels;
by the rays of the jewels the place is full of splendour.

**91.** On all sides that place is inlaid with rubies;
in its midst is a beautiful pavilion of gems.

**92.** The pavilion is built, adorned with various jewels;
the place is all full of radiance — it has no comparison.

**93.** All the paintings of the pavilion shine [like] the moon;
the place is beautiful to behold, full of fragrance.[^215-37]

**94.** On all sides hang chamaras [and] jewelled pendants;
on the arches hang various gems in clusters.[^215-38]

**95.** The altar, adorned with rubies, shines brightly;
[its] light is ever new, [it] is skilfully built to behold.[^215-39]

**96.** On all sides strings of various pearls sway;
rubies blaze, surpassing millions and millions of suns.

**97.** The temple is adorned with various gems and rubies;
a single ruby [there] holds the radiance of a million suns.

**98.** The pavilion is adorned with an eight-petalled lotus;
by the rays of the gems the place blazes with bright radiance.

**99.** Four doors grace that beautiful temple;
eight panels of gems and rubies are enchanting.[^215-40]

**100.** How many, how many jewelled lamps burn there!
They always illumine the circle of the rasa.[^215-41]

**101.** In its midst is a wish-fulfilling tree, beautiful to behold;
a jewelled palace, a jewelled altar are most enchanting.[^215-42]

**102.** On all sides in that place there is a rain of jewels;
the six seasons abide in that forest without cease.[^215-43]

**103.** Nectar always rains down in the midst of Vrindavana;
thus the wish-fulfilling tree always abides [there] in splendour.

**104.** The leaves of the wish-fulfilling tree are in rapturous delight;
coral stalks all shine beside it.[^215-44]

**105.** The wish-fulfilling tree is adorned with jewelled shoots;
gems, pearls [and] various jewels shine.

**106.** [Its] fruits are padmaraga rubies, in clusters;
various gems and rubies hang down in streams.[^215-45]

**107.** All the gems and rubies are dazzling to behold;
that best of trees takes away the heat of samsara.

**108.** The shade of that tree [brings] blessing to all;
the wondrous best of trees takes away the threefold heat.[^215-46]

**109.** At the root of such a tree shines a jewelled palace;
in its midst is a sweet jewelled throne.

**110.** The radiance of millions and millions of suns, brightly shining,
the eight-petalled throne is made of gems.

**111.** In such a Vrindavana, on the throne beneath the wish-fulfilling tree,
always behold Krishna, meditate [on Him].[^215-47]

**112.** Krishna wearing yellow garments, Radha-jiu at [His] left;
both hands are rosy, the feet are red.[^215-48]

**113.** Both eyes are tinged with red, the lips rosy;
on [His] chest [He] wears the Kaustubha gem [and] various jewels.[^215-49]

**114.** On the neck are a double string of pearls, a necklace of various jewels;
the ornaments of His body are set with various jewels.

**115.** The crown sparkles with various jewels and rubies;
on the neck a necklace shines, flashing [like] lightning.

**116.** Earrings, armlets, bracelets, little bells shine;
the form glitters and shimmers, the glance is sweet.[^215-50]

**117.** On the heart is the mark of Shrivatsa, most enchanting;
the two lotus feet are beautiful to behold.[^215-51]

**118.** On both feet shine anklets of gems;
a supremely sweet sound — [they] sing the panchama.[^215-52]

**119.** That sound steals the minds of the three worlds [when they] hear it:
so sweetly [the anklets] ring, resting on the feet.

**120.** Gorochana [and] kunkuma shine very brightly;
on the forehead shines a tilaka like a bee.[^215-53]

**121.** On the beautiful, sweet face is a sweet smile;
revealing [His] glance, [He] has conquered the three worlds.

**122.** Enchanting, surpassing millions and millions of Kandarpas,
the form of supreme loveliness is beautiful to behold.

**123.** On the beautiful belly shine three folds, as [befits];
the waist surpasses a lion's, the thighs [like plantain stems] are most shapely.[^215-54]

**124.** In such a form Krishna, taking the flute in His hand
and putting the flute to His lips, began to play.

**125.** In what divine ragas all began to sing
[in] Vrindavana, on the sandy bank of the Yamuna, beneath the trees![^215-55]

**126.** In the middle are Radha and Krishna, on all sides the gopis;
thousands and thousands of groups — who can count [them]?[^215-56]

**127.** As the filaments of a lotus are surrounded by the petals,
so the gopis surround Radha and Krishna on all sides.[^215-57]

**128.** The form that enchants the three worlds is beyond the three worlds;
according to your own nature contemplate [Him] without cease.[^215-58]

**129.** If you worship, you will attain Radha and Krishna, the lords of [your] life;
worship [Them] firmly, O raja, with firm resolve."

**130.** [Citing] the testimony of various tantras [and] various shastras,
