he set forth the truth of the Vedas, explaining [it].[^215-59]

**131.** Hearing Rasika's words, the three brothers
firmly and unceasingly worshipped Krishna.

**132.** Who can describe the boundless ocean of [his] lilas?
In brief I have proclaimed something.[^215-60]

**133.** This is proclaimed in the Dakshina-vibhaga;
all of you, listen attentively, without disputing.[^215-61]

**134.** The Rasika-mangala is supremely sweet:
hearing [it], all living beings, cross over the [age of] Kali.[^215-62]

**135.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifteenth lahari, called "The Instruction to Maharaja Vaidyanatha Bhanja on Meditation on Vrindavana and on Worship."*[^215-63]

[^215-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("পঞ্চদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 15 begins at the top of. Raga Kaushika; the ghosha is the same as in lahari 13 (note 1 there): Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari is a name of Krishna, which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon, after ॥ 135 ॥: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে মহারাজা বৈদ্যনাথ ভঞ্জের প্রতি বৃন্দাবন-ধ্যান-ভজনোপদেশ-নাম পঞ্চদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*mahārājā baidyanātha bhañjera prati bṛndābana-dhyāna-bhajanopadeśa*). The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^215-2]: "Cowherd lineages" — *gopabaṃśa-samūha*; "the moon of the family" — *kulacandra*. According to tradition, Shyamananda came from the Sadgopa ("good cowherd") caste.

[^215-3]: Bhattacharya — lahari 13, note 6. "Ignorance" (3) — *abidyā*; "entered the shelter" — *paśilā śaraṇa*. "Anxiety of the mind" (4) — *manera udbega*.

[^215-4]: "A moment" — *laba* (lava, the smallest unit of time). Cf. CC, Madhya 22: "'Association with sadhus, association with sadhus' — [so] say all the shastras: even by a moment's association with a sadhu every perfection is attained." "The sin that binds one to births" — *janmabandha-pāpa*.

[^215-5]: "The holy places of the gods" — *debatīrtha*. Cf. Bhagavatam 1.13.10: great devotees by their presence make the holy places holy.

[^215-6]: "For the good of the sadhus" — *sādhujana-hite*. Cf. Bhagavatam 9.4.68: "The sadhus are My heart, and I am the heart of the sadhus."

[^215-7]: "The rod of Yama" — *yamadaṇḍa*. "Now rising, now falling" — *uṭhu paṛu haññā*; "perishes" — *mare*.

[^215-8]: "In this round of worldly existence" — the 1941 edition has *prabhabasaṃsāre*; the 1997 edition has *e bhabasaṃsāre*; the latter is adopted.

[^215-9]: 15–19 — cf. Bhagavatam 2.3.18–19: "Do the trees not live? Do the bellows not breathe? … A man praised by those like dogs, hogs, camels and asses is [himself] an animal," if he does not hear of the Lord. "Lives" — *jīẏe*. "A blacksmith's bellows" — *kāmārera yā̃tā*. "Impure" (16) — *amedhya*.

[^215-10]: "Twice six qualities" — *dbiṣaṛ guṇa*: the twelve virtues of a brahmana (truthfulness, self-control, austerity and others). A shvapacha, "dog-eater," is a person of the lowest station.

[^215-11]: Bhagavatam 7.9.10 (the prayer of Prahlada). "The Lotus-naveled" — *aravinda-nābha*, Vishnu. Shlokas 21, 48 and 49 have their own numbers in the edition's common count of couplets. Below the shloka (and below 48–49) the edition gives its Bengali prose translation (*ślokārtha*) — the editor's apparatus, not translated.

[^215-12]: Cf. Bhagavatam 4.31.14: as watering the root of a tree nourishes the trunk, branches and leaves, so the worship of Achyuta satisfies all. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the gods are Krishna's servants (22), and the worship of Krishna includes respect for them (lahari 13, note 4).

[^215-13]: "False" — *asatya*: transient when not related to Krishna (lahari 13, note 5). "Remaining amid all this" (29) — *e sabāte thāki'*: without leaving home and family (cf. lahari 14, 37). "Abundantly" (28) — *atireke*.

[^215-14]: "Kshatriyas" — *kṣetrī* (= *kṣatriẏa*). "Subjects" — *prajāgaṇa*.

[^215-15]: The sixty-four kinds of service (*catuḥṣaṣṭi bhakti*) — the list of sadhana-bhakti in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2) and CC, Madhya 22. The son of Achyuta (*acyuta-nandana*; 40 *acyuta-tanaẏa*, 67 *acyuta-kumāra*) is Rasika (lahari 12, note 24).

[^215-16]: Rasika-shekhara — lahari 12, note 40. "Alms" — *bhikṣā*. "Considering [us] servants" (39) — *sebaka-giẏāne* (*giẏāna* = *jñāna*). "I have offered everything" (39) — *saba samarpinu mui*: apparently the king speaks for the three.

[^215-17]: "[The giving up of] the killing of living beings" — *jībahatyā bhikṣā*, lit. "alms — the killing of living beings": Rasika asks that the killing of animals cease, above all sacrifices (45); at the beginning of lahari 16 it is said that in the land of the Bhanjas the Shaivas and Shaktas gave up the killing of living beings. Vaishnavas do no violence to living beings and do not eat meat.

[^215-18]: Raurava, Maharaurava (52) — hellish worlds to which those who do violence to living beings go (Bhagavatam 5.26.10–12).

[^215-19]: 43–45 — the eight participants in killing; cf. shloka 48 and the Manu-smriti (5.51), which lists the same eight. "Gives consent" — *anumāna kare* (cf. *anumantā*, 48). "The ruler of that village" — *grāmera adhipati* (cf. *adhiṣṭhātā*, 48). "Sells" (44) — *bice* (= *bece*). "The lowest of brahmanas" (45) — *dbijādhama*.

[^215-20]: "Kill" — the 1941 edition has *baddha kare*; understood as *badha kare* ("kills"). "Bereft of sense" — *haiẏā acetana*.

[^215-21]: The source is given by the edition as the Padma Purana; not verified. The first half is close to the Manu-smriti (5.51); on years in hell by the number of the animal's hairs cf. the Manu-smriti (5.38). "Overseer" — *adhiṣṭhātā*; "the one who prepares" — *saṃskartā*; "the one who serves" — *upahartā*. "Contrary to the injunctions" (49) — *avidhinā*.

[^215-22]: "The destroyer of his own soul" — *ātmaghātī*: one who, having obtained a human birth, does not worship the Lord and so destroys himself (cf. Bhagavatam 11.20.17).

[^215-23]: "In a subtle form" — *sūkṣmarūpe*: the Paramatma, who dwells in the heart of every being (cf. Bhagavad-gita 18.61). "In His own form" — *sbarūpe*.

[^215-24]: "Kin" — *jana*; the mark at this word refers to the editor's note: the variant reading "প্রাণ" (*prāṇa*, "life"). "Enter" — *paśa*.

[^215-25]: Couplet 58 repeats the second line of 62 and the first line of 63; apparently a copying slip. Translated as it stands; the bhattacharyas' speech is in 63–68.

[^215-26]: "Wicked" — *duṣṭa*. "Whose vow is to crush the asuras" — *asuradalanabānā*; *bānā* is understood as "vow, habit" (Bengali বানা); the reading and sense are unclear.

[^215-27]: "Secret [hidden] in the Vedas" — *beda-gopya kathā*. "An associate of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapāriṣada*: the words of the panditas; on the position of Rasika and Shyamananda see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11 (cf. lahari 12, note 19).

[^215-28]: "Received instruction in the Krishna-mantra" — *kṛṣṇamantre upadeśa*: initiation (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 8; lahari 13, 4). "According to the nigama" — *nigamete*: according to the Vedas.

[^215-29]: "One's own mood" — *nijabhāba*: the sense is approximate — the "intimate" or "true" mood (possibly Rasika's own mood). The cowherd men and gopis of Vraja attained Krishna in the moods of sakhya, vatsalya and madhurya; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching this is the path of raganuga-bhakti, following the residents of Vraja (CC, Madhya 22). "Bhagavan Himself" (74) — *sbaẏaṃ bhagabān*; cf. Bhagavatam 1.3.28. Madhurya is conjugal love, the mood of the gopis. "Meditate" — *dhiẏāna* (= *dhyāna*).

[^215-30]: "Related" — *karila bikhyātā*, lit. "made known." Chudamani, "the jewel on the crest": Rasikendra-chudamani is an epithet of Rasika.

[^215-31]: "With a resounding hum" — *mukharaba-dhbani*. "[Sing]" — the 1941 edition has *pāẏena* ("obtain, find"); apparently a misprint for *gāẏena* ("sing"); the reading is unclear.

[^215-32]: "At the same time" — *ekakāle*. "Kindled by [their] radiance" — *teje uddīpana*.

[^215-33]: Kamala — lotus; utpala — blue water lily; kahlara — white water lily. "Pollen" — *parāgadhūli*.

[^215-34]: The twelve forests of Vraja (Madhuvana, Talavana, Kumudavana and others); upavanas are lesser groves. Usually twenty-four upavanas are named; here eighteen. "As [the shastras] attest" — *paramāṇa* (*pramāṇa*); it can also be understood as "in number."

[^215-35]: "The ground of jewels — chintamani" — *ratnamaẏa bhūmi-cintāmaṇi*; cf. the Brahma-samhita 5.29, 5.56 (ground of chintamani, wish-fulfilling trees). "Hosts of suns" — *sūryya yūtha yūtha*.

[^215-36]: Wish-fulfilling tree — *kalpataru*. "Pendants of gems" — *maṇimaẏa jhārā*: hanging clusters, fringes. "Cannot be described" — *nā yāẏa bākhāna* (*bākhāna* = *byākhyāna*).

[^215-37]: "Shine [like] the moon" — *candrake ujjbala*; it can also be understood as "brighter than the moon." "Fragrance" — *parimala*. The description of Vrindavana continues (from ॥ 94 ॥).

[^215-38]: The description of Vrindavana in Rasika's speech continues from 77. Chamaras are whisks of yak tails. "Pendants" — *jhārā* (cf. 89, note 36; 106). "Arches" — *toraṇa*, decorated gateways. "In clusters" — *kerā kerā*: the meaning is unclear, understood as "in clusters, in bunches".

[^215-39]: "Altar" — *bedī*, a raised platform. "Skilfully built" — *subandhāna*, "well-formed, shapely" (cf. 123).

[^215-40]: "Four doors" — *caturtha duẏāra*, lit. "the fourth door"; understood as "four doors", each with two panels, eight in all.

[^215-41]: "The circle of the rasa" — *rāsa-maṇḍalī*: the place of the rasa dance.

[^215-42]: "In its midst" — *tā'ra madhye*: in the midst of the temple or of the rasa circle. On the wish-fulfilling trees and the ground of chintamani see note 35.

[^215-43]: "The six seasons" — *ṣaṛ-ṛtu*: in Vrindavana all the seasons abide at once.

[^215-44]: "Stalks" — *dāṇḍi*, "stems, stalks".

[^215-45]: Padmaraga is the "lotus-coloured" ruby. "In clusters" — *kerā kerā* (note 38). "In streams" — *jhārā jhārā*.

[^215-46]: The threefold heat (*tribidha tāpa*) is the three kinds of suffering: from one's own body and mind, from other living beings, and from the forces of nature.

[^215-47]: "Behold" — *dekhaha*, lit. "look"; "meditate" — *karaha dhiẏāne* (*dhyāna*). The raja is addressed in the singular, as in 75 and 89.

[^215-48]: "Radha-jiu" — *rādhājīu*: the respectful "Radha-ji". "Rosy" — *aruṇima*; "red" — *rātula*.

[^215-49]: "Tinged with red" — *rātula*. Kaustubha is the jewel on the chest of Vishnu-Krishna. The 1941 edition has "কোউস্তভ".

[^215-50]: "Armlets" — *keẏūra*; "little bells" — *kiṅkiṇī*, bells on the girdle.

[^215-51]: Shrivatsa is the auspicious mark (a curl) on the chest of Vishnu-Krishna.

[^215-52]: "Anklets" — *mañjira*. Panchama (*pañcama*) is the fifth note of the Indian scale, traditionally the voice of the cuckoo.

[^215-53]: Gorochana is a bright yellow pigment (Purva, lahari 6, note 8); kunkuma is a red powder. "Like a bee" — *ali paramāṇa*: *ali* is a bee, *paramāṇa* (= *pramāṇa*) "measure, likeness"; understood as comparing the tilaka to a bee (in shape or colour); the sense is approximate.

[^215-54]: "Three folds" — *tribalī* (Purva, lahari 16, note 31). "As [befits]" — *pramāṇa*, "in due measure". "Thighs" — *rambhā*, "plantain": thighs like plantain stems (cf. lahari 12, 26). "Shapely" — *subandhāna* (cf. 95).

[^215-55]: "All began to sing" — *saba gāite lāgilā*: at the sound of the flute everything around sings; it may also be understood as "[He] began to sing of everything". "Sandy bank" — *pulina* (lahari 3, note 18). "Beneath the trees" — *tarutalā*.

[^215-56]: "Groups" — *yūtha*: bands of gopis, each with its own leader.

[^215-57]: The number "॥ ১২৭" is printed without the closing "॥". "The filaments … surrounded by the petals" — *padmera keśara dala yena-i beṣṭita*.

[^215-58]: "Beyond the three worlds" — *trailokyera para*. "According to your own nature … contemplate" — *āpanāra sbabhābete bhāba*: it may also be understood as "meditate in your own mood (bhava)"; cf. 73 (*āpanāra nijabhāba*, note 29). Rasika's speech, begun in 77, ends in 129.

[^215-59]: "Testimony" — *pramāṇa*. "Tantras" — *tantra*: here, sacred scriptures (agamas, pancharatra).

[^215-60]: "The boundless ocean of [his] lilas" — *apāra samudra-līlā*; it may also be understood as "lilas boundless [as] the ocean". The author's words.

[^215-61]: "Is proclaimed" — *karilā pracāra* (a third-person form; in sense, the author's words). "Without disputing" — *nā kara bicāra*: without doubting.

[^215-62]: "Cross over the [age of] Kali" — *tara kalikāla*.

[^215-63]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে মহারাজা বৈদ্যনাথ ভঞ্জের প্রতি বৃন্দাবন-ধ্যান-ভজনোপদেশ-নাম পঞ্চদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা"; on the title see note 1.


## Lahari 16. The Deliverance of Uddanda

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; through Rasika's instruction the three brothers become wholly devoted, and in Bhanjabhum all the people, Shaivas and Shaktas, give up the killing of living beings; when during a reading of the Bhagavata the raja is distracted by his steward, the brahmana Ramakrishna, Rasika's disciple, slaps him; the raja restrains the enraged courtiers, falls at Ramakrishna's feet and thanks him for his deliverance, and Rasika is convinced that the raja has become a Vaishnava; taking leave of the raja, Rasika returns to Shyamananda at Govindapur; Shyamananda goes with Rasika to Nrisimhapur, to the bhuiyan Uddanda-raya, who robs and beats Vaishnavas; at night a mahapurusha appears to Uddanda and bids him take shelter of Shyamananda, and, seeing Shyamananda, he takes his shelter with his whole family; Shyamananda has Shyama-raya brought from Dharenda and holds three festivals; Uddanda serves the sadhus, repents of having destroyed thousands of sadhus and hands over the gudris taken from the Vaishnavas — seven hundred and eighteen — and Shyamananda distributes them to the Vaishnavas; seeing him, everyone becomes a sadhu; thus the Dakshina-vibhaga ends*

*The sixteenth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^216-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of the whole [world]!
Be merciful, so that I may compose [a song of your] glory.

**2.** Thus Vaidyanatha received instruction;
day by day prema-bhakti began to grow.[^216-2]

**3.** The three brothers became wholly devoted;
the towns of Utkala became filled with love for Krishna.[^216-3]

**4.** Rasika accepted many disciples there;
for some days he stayed in that village of the raja.

**5.** The three brothers became wondrous Vaishnavas;
there is none to compare [them] with in all the world.[^216-4]

**6.** In Bhanjabhum all the people became Vaishnavas;
Shaivas [and] Shaktas — all gave up the killing of living beings.[^216-5]

**7.** One day Rasika-shekhara, having gathered an assembly,
was sitting in the raja's chambers.[^216-6]

**8.** The three brothers listen to the narration of the Bhagavata;
with joy in his heart Rasika Gosani speaks.

**9.** At that time the raja's steward [came] to that place
and, making obeisance with an offering, stood before [him].[^216-7]

**10.** As soon as [he] made a sign, [the raja] looked at him;
in anger Ramakrishna, the best of brahmanas, rose.[^216-8]

**11.** He is Rasika's disciple, wholly surrendered [to Krishna];
all people praise him, calling him the blessing of the world.[^216-9]

**12.** Rising, he said: "Raja, you have lost your senses!
Leaving the nectarean words about Krishna, you are listening to [other] talk."[^216-10]

**13.** With force he struck the raja on the face with a slap;
the raja fell senseless, everyone was grieved.

**14.** All the great men, seized with anger,
drawing their swords, rush roaring to kill [him].[^216-11]

**15.** Seeing this, the raja in agitation rose quickly
and fell at the feet of Ramakrishnadasa.

**16.** Joining his palms, he says before the assembly:
"For [my] offence the punishment was in due measure.[^216-12]

**17.** Rasika speaks the nectarean words about Krishna,
and I myself, leaving them, looked the other way.

**18.** In all the shastras it is said: the worship of Krishna is true;
everything apart from Krishna is the eating of poison.

**19.** Whoever, beside the narration about Krishna, listens to other talk
is a great sinner; he falls into dense darkness.

**20.** Know: his mind is like a dog's [or] a hog's —
leaving the rice on a jewelled plate, to eat leavings.[^216-13]

**21.** Leaving nectar, he partook of poison;
leaving the narration about Krishna, he turned his mind elsewhere.[^216-14]

**22.** This punishment is just, in measure with the offence;
today brother Ramakrishna has delivered [me].

**23.** I have understood in my heart: [he] bears me great love;
he has delivered me from the eighty-four [lakhs of births]."[^216-15]

**24.** Embracing Ramakrishna by the neck, [the raja] began to weep;
with the tears of his eyes the raja bathed [his] body.[^216-16]

**25.** Seeing [this], all in the assembly were amazed:
the saintliness of Vaidyanatha is wondrous to tell.[^216-17]

**26.** Taking Ramakrishna by the hand, the raja says playfully:
"Your hand has been hurt by this hard body."

**27.** With a rebuke he restrained all the people,
took Ramakrishnadasa and seated him beside [himself].[^216-18]

**28.** Without guile he showed [him] much affection;
Rasika knew for certain: [the raja] had become a Vaishnava.

**29.** Rising, Rasika Gosani embraced the raja [and] the three brothers,
without guile he showed [them] mercy.[^216-19]

**30.** Such sadhus — Vaidyanatha [and] the three brothers —
unceasingly worship Rasikendra-chudamani.[^216-20]

**31.** Lying down, eating, in sleep, night and day [theirs is] meditation:
apart from Rasika's feet they know nothing else.

**32.** Seeing the raja's prema-bhakti, all the people,
following one another's example, became wholly surrendered [to Krishna].

**33.** Day by day bhakti was kindled;
Achyuta's son showed mercy to all.

**34.** Then, having stayed there for some days,
[Rasika], telling the raja, went to Shyamananda.

**35.** Because of the separation the raja became very sad;
giving much wealth [and] cloth, he fell at [his] feet.

**36.** From there Rasikendra set out
and at Govindapur saw Shyamananda.[^216-21]

**37.** In Utkala Yamuna Thakurani was born;
Rasikendra brought her [and] gave [her] to Shyamananda.[^216-22]

**38.** All the wealth [and] cloth he gave to Shyamananda;
at [his] feet he told of the raja's instruction.[^216-23]

**39.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda-raya rejoiced:
"There is one more matter; I shall tell you.

**40.** The bhuiyan of Nrisimhapur, that Uddanda-raya,
is always hostile to Vaishnavas [and] brahmanas.[^216-24]

**41.** Hundreds and hundreds of gudris he takes away;
greedy for goods, intoxicated, he beats the Vaishnavas.[^216-25]

**42.** If such a man becomes a sadhu, it will be good;
let us go to him, you and I."

**43.** Saying this, Shyamananda set out;
coming to Narasimhapur, he arrived [there].[^216-26]

**44.** That night Raja Uddanda was lying [in bed]:
he had only just lain down and was still awake.[^216-27]

**45.** At that time a certain great, supreme mahapurusha
came and appeared before the bhuiyan.[^216-28]

**46.** In a soft, sweet voice he spoke [to him] face to face:
"Take shelter of Shyamananda with a firm heart.[^216-29]

**47.** Surrender everything to Shyamananda."
Having spoken these words to him, he vanished.

**48.** [Uddanda] himself saw the form, heard the words;
rising, he saw that no one was there.

**49.** Having received this vision, he gained divine knowledge:
"When shall I behold the feet of Shyamananda?"[^216-30]

**50.** At that time Prabhu came there;
the two Prabhus arrived at Uddanda's house.[^216-31]

**51.** Shyamananda, taking Rasika-Murari with him,
came and entered into Uddanda-raya's presence.

**52.** Seeing the two, the raja rejoiced greatly:
the Prabhu whose words he had heard with his ears [stood] before him.[^216-32]

**53.** In many ways he worshipped [their] feet;
firmly he took shelter of Shyamananda.

**54.** Without guile [Shyamananda] bestowed prema-bhakti on him;
the fortunate bhuiyan took shelter with his whole family.[^216-33]

**55.** Very mighty, a great asura he had been;
by Shyamananda's touch he became a supreme sadhu.[^216-34]

**56.** Seeing [this], all the people are amazed:
apart from guru, Krishna and sadhu they know nothing else.[^216-35]

**57.** He had Shyama-raya brought from Dharenda;
Shyamananda-raya held three festivals.[^216-36]

**58.** From that day [Uddanda] became a great Vaishnava;
he began to serve sadhus by the hundreds and hundreds.

**59.** Having completed the dadhi-kada, Shyamananda sat down;
the bhuiyan, with joy in his heart, makes a humble request:[^216-37]

**60.** "I am a great villain, a great sinner, of evil conduct:
thousands upon thousands of sadhus I have destroyed.[^216-38]

**61.** A whole room is filled with their gudris;
if you order it, I will bring [them] before you."[^216-39]

**62.** Hearing [this], Shyamananda at once gave the order;
the gudris were brought and piled up like a mountain.[^216-40]

**63.** On counting, they came to seven hundred and eighteen;
seeing [this], all the devotees of Krishna are amazed.[^216-41]

**64.** Then Prabhu gave [them] one by one to the Vaishnavas;
receiving the gudris, all give [him] their blessings.[^216-42]

**65.** Many clothes, much wealth he gave to the sadhus;
firmly he took shelter of Shyamananda.

**66.** Following his example, all the people became sadhus;
of Uddanda's saintliness nothing can be told.[^216-43]

**67.** Such is the might of Shyamananda [and] Rasika,
by whose touch the three sins of worldly existence are destroyed.[^216-44]

**68.** Thus, day by day, prema dawns:
giving up wicked deeds, all worship Krishna.

**69.** All the greatest sinners, giving up wicked deeds,
became supreme Vaishnavas, wholly surrendered [to Krishna].[^216-45]

**70.** Even if described with millions of mouths, it could not be described;
of [his] nature I have briefly composed something.[^216-46]

**71.** In the Dakshina-vibhaga I have revealed this;
listen to the Rasika-mangala, filled with delight.

**72.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Dakshina-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixteenth lahari, called "The Deliverance of Uddanda."*[^216-47]

[^216-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari, in italics without a number. The raga in the 1941 edition is *nārāni gauṛā*, i.e. Narayani-gauda (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as there, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-দক্ষিণবিভাগে উদ্দণ্ড-উদ্ধার-নাম ষোড়শ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*uddaṇḍa-uddhāra*) — "The Deliverance of Uddanda"; the 1997 edition reads the same. This is the last, sixteenth lahari of the Dakshina-vibhaga. The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^216-2]: "Received instruction" — *upadeśa hailā*: received initiation and instruction (lahari 15, 71).

[^216-3]: "Wholly devoted" — in the 1941 edition *ananya śaraṇa*. "The towns of Utkala" — *utkalanagara*; it may also be understood as "the whole land of Utkala".

[^216-4]: The number "॥ ৫ ॥" is not printed in the edition (only "॥" after the couplet); the edition's count 4 → [5] → 6 is unbroken.

[^216-5]: Bhanjabhum (*bhañjabhūma*) is "the land of the Bhanjas", the domain of the rajas of the Bhanja line (lahari 12, note 10). Shaivas and Shaktas are worshippers of Shiva and of Shakti-Durga (Purva, lahari 9, note 8). "The killing of living beings" — *jībahatyā*: animal sacrifice (lahari 14, 66, note 33; lahari 15, 40–52).

[^216-6]: "In the chambers" — *mandira-bhitara*: *mandira* is a house, palace or temple (cf. lahari 10, note 13).

[^216-7]: "Obeisance with an offering" — *niuchāni*: according to the editor's explanation, an obeisance with an offering of cloth (*bastrabheṭa diẏā praṇāma*; the gloss is not translated).

[^216-8]: "As soon as [he] made a sign" — *iṅgita karibāmātra*: the subjects are not named; understood as: the steward attracted the raja's attention with a sign, and the raja, distracted from the Bhagavata, looked at him. Ramakrishna (in 15, 27 — Ramakrishnadasa) is a disciple of Rasika (lahari 4, 19, note 8; lahari 6, note 15). "The best of brahmanas" — *dbijabara*.

[^216-9]: "The blessing of the world" — *bhubanamaṅgala*.

[^216-10]: "You are listening to [other] talk" — *kathā kara pāna*, lit. "you drink talk".

[^216-11]: "taking out"; the gloss is not translated). "To kill" — *māribāre*: it may also be understood as "to strike".

[^216-12]: "In due measure" — *paramāṇe* (= *pramāṇe*): justly, in proportion (cf. 22).

[^216-13]: "On a jewelled plate" — *ratnasthāli*. "Leavings" — *jhuṭā*. "Know" — *jānaha*: the raja addresses the assembly.

[^216-14]: The subject of 21 is not named: understood as continuing 19–20 (about one who listens to other talk); the raja says this of himself.

[^216-15]: "From the eighty-four" — *caurāśī*: from the cycle of eighty-four lakhs of births (lahari 14, 12–19, note 7).

[^216-16]: "Embracing by the neck" — *galā dhari*. "Bathed [his] body" — *aṅga pākhālilā*; it may also be understood as "bathed [his own] body": the subject and object of lines 24a–b allow both readings.

[^216-17]: "Wondrous" — the 1941 edition has "অদ্ভুন", understood as *adbhuta*, "wondrous". "Saintliness" — *sādhu kathā*, lit. "the account of the sadhu (of the saintly one)".

[^216-18]: "With a rebuke he restrained" — *nibārila tāṛanā kariyā*: understood as: the raja, with a shout, stopped the people who had rushed at Ramakrishna (14).

[^216-19]: "The raja [and] the three brothers" — *rājā tina bhāi*: the raja and his brothers, all three (lahari 12, 17–18). "Embraced" — *karila kole*, lit. "took onto his lap (to his breast)".

[^216-20]: "Worship" — *bhaja* (an imperative form; understood as indicative; it may also be understood as the author's call: "worship…"). Chudamani — "the jewel on the crown" (lahari 15, note 30). The guru is honoured as Hari Himself, since he is the Lord's dear servant (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 31); on how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2, and lahari 14, note 11.

[^216-21]: Govindapur is Sri Govindapur, the village given to Shyamananda by the bhuiyan Bhimadhana; there Shyamananda built a house (lahari 12, 10, note 7).

[^216-22]: Yamuna Thakurani — cf. lahari 12, 12 and note 8 (Yamuna among the women of Shyamananda's household). The sense of the couplet is unclear: "was born" (*janmechilā*) — apparently Yamuna came from Utkala, and Rasika brought her to Shyamananda; the person is not identified.

[^216-23]: "At [his] feet" — *caraṇe*: respectfully. "Of the raja's instruction" — *rājā upadeśa kathā*: of how the raja received instruction.

[^216-24]: Nrisimhapur (*nṛsiṃhapura*; in 43 *narasiṃhapura*) is a village in Utkala; in BR 15 (80) it is "Sri Nrisimhapura", where Shyamananda held sankirtana; Uddanda is not named there. Bhuiyan (*bhuñā*) — a local landholder (lahari 12, note 7; in lahari 10, note 16 — "bhunya"). Uddanda-raya (*uddaṇḍa rāẏa*): *uddaṇḍa* means "unruly, fierce"; in 44 and 52 he is called a raja.

[^216-25]: "Gudris" — *gudhaṛi* (= *gudaṛi*): the patchwork quilt or cloak of a wandering Vaishnava, serving him as both bedding and bag. "Takes away" — *laẏa chāṛāiẏā*. "Intoxicated" — *matta*.

[^216-26]: "Narasimhapur" — so in 43 (*narasiṃhapura*); the same village as Nrisimhapur in 40. "Arrived" — *haila upasana* (= *upasanna*).

[^216-27]: "Had only just lain down and was still awake" — *śaẏana kariẏā mātra jāgrata āchilā*, lit. "had just lain down, was waking": the vision was in waking.

[^216-28]: Mahapurusha (*mahāpuruṣa*), "great personage": the author does not say who this is; according to 52 the voice heard at night is that of Shyamananda himself, i.e., it was Shyamananda who appeared to Uddanda at night. On how the author exalts Shyamananda, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2, and lahari 14, note 11. "Appeared" — *haila adhiṣṭhāna*.

[^216-29]: "Sweet" — *susbara*; "deep". (the editor's note is not translated). "Face to face" — *sākṣāte*.

[^216-30]: "Divine knowledge" — *dibya jñāna*. "Shall I behold" — *pāmu … darśana*, lit. "shall I obtain the sight" (*pāmu* is a first-person future form).

[^216-31]: "Prabhu" is Shyamananda; "the two Prabhus" are Shyamananda and Rasika. "Arrived" — *bīje kaila* (*bijaẏa*): a respectful word for a procession.

[^216-32]: "The Prabhu whose words he had heard" — *ye bāṇī śunila karṇe se prabhu sākṣāte*: understood as: the one whose voice the raja had heard at night now stood before him (note 28).

[^216-33]: "With his whole family" — *sabaṃśe*. "Fortunate" — *bhāgyabān*.

[^216-34]: "Asura" — *asura*: a villain, a man of demonic nature. "Mighty" — *pratāpī*. "By the touch" — *paraśe*.

[^216-35]: Numbering: in the 1941 edition this couplet is numbered "॥ ৫৭ ॥", and the next one is also "॥ ৫৭ ॥"; there is no 56. By the count this is 56 (a misprint of the edition), and it is given so; the next is 57. "দক্ষিণ বিভাগ-পঞ্চদশ-লহরী". ("fifteenth lahari"), is also an error of the edition. "Apart from guru, Krishna and sadhu" — *guru kṛṣṇa sādhu bine*.

[^216-36]: Shyama-raya — a Deity of Krishna in Dharenda (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 12). "He had … brought" — *ānāilā*: the subject is not named; apparently Shyamananda (cf. Pashchima, lahari 1, 2); it can also be understood as "[Uddanda] had … brought". "Dharenda" — in the 1941 edition *dhārandā*. "Three festivals" — *tina mahotsaba* (cf. Dakshina, lahari 7). "To serve sadhus by the hundreds and hundreds" (58) — *śata śata sādhusebā*; in the 1997 edition — "সাধু-সব".

[^216-37]: Dadhi-kada (*dadhi kādā*, "curd [and] mud") is a festive game in which the participants douse one another with curd mixed with water and turmeric and dance in this "mud" (so Nandotsava, the celebration of Krishna's appearance in Nanda's house, is kept); here it is apparently the conclusion of the festival. "Having completed" — *sāri*. "Sat down" — *basilena*; in the 1997 edition — *balilena*, "said". "Makes a humble request" — *nibedana kare*. The bhuiyan is Uddanda (note 24).

[^216-38]: "Destroyed" — *saṃhāra karinu*: killed or ruined (cf. 41: "he beats the Vaishnavas"). "Of evil conduct" — *durācāra*.

[^216-39]: Gudri — note 25. "Their" — *tāhāra* (singular): apparently the gudris of those sadhus. "A whole room" — *eka ghara*, lit. "one house (one room)".

[^216-40]: "At once" — *anibāre*, lit. "unhindered, irresistibly". "Piled up like a mountain" — *kaila parbbata ākāre*, lit. "made [them] in the shape of a mountain".

[^216-41]: "Seven hundred and eighteen" — *sāta śata aṣṭādaśa*; in the 1997 edition — *śata śata aṣṭādaśa*, "hundreds and hundreds, eighteen". "The devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa jane*: in the 1941 edition "কাষ্ঞ´" with the repha shifted to the right (cf. lahari 14, note 29); in the 1997 edition — "কার".

[^216-42]: "Prabhu" — Shyamananda. "Give [him] their blessings" — *āśīrbāda kare*: the Vaishnavas bless Shyamananda or Uddanda; whom is not said.

[^216-43]: "Following his example" — *tā'ra dekhādekhi*. "Saintliness" — *sādhutā*.

[^216-44]: "Might" — *paratāpa* (= *pratāpa*). "The three sins of worldly existence" — *bhaba tina pāpa*: the meaning is unclear; apparently the three kinds of suffering (*tāpa-traẏa*: from one's own body and mind, from other beings and from the forces of nature), or the sins of body, speech and mind. "Are destroyed" — *khaṇḍe*. On how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^216-45]: "The greatest sinners" — *mahā mahā pāpā*. "Wholly surrendered" — *ananyaśaraṇa*.

[^216-46]: "Described" — *baṇile* (= *barṇile*). "Of [his] nature" — *sbabhāba*: the meaning is unclear; cf. Pashchima, lahari 1, 68: *sbabhāba-barṇana*, "a description of [Rasika's] nature (character)". It can also be understood as "according to my own understanding (my own nature) I have briefly…". "Composed" — *karinu racana*.

[^216-47]: The title is "The Deliverance of Uddanda". The colophon stands below ॥72॥; below it is a rule. With this lahari the Dakshina-vibhaga ends.


# Pashchima-vibhaga

*The Western Part*

## Lahari 1. Preparations for the Spring Rasa at Sri Gopivallabhapur

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda comes with the Deity Shyama-raya to Kashiyari, manifests Thakurani, celebrates the wedding of Thakura and holds three festivals, and there Purushottama, Damodara, Mathuradasa, Haraghosha Mahapatra and the brahmana Haridasa receive the mantra from him; in Dharenda, at an assembly with Rasika, Damodara and other devotees, Shyamananda orders a great Rasa-yatra to be proclaimed for the spring full moon of Vaishakha and entrusts Rasika with gathering the provisions; Rasika's followers spend a whole year clearing the thorny thickets from the site at Sri Gopivallabhapur and build a pavilion, while Rasika himself in one year gathers mountains of grain, sweets, fruits, vegetables and spices; an octagonal circle of the rasa is built with paintings, a fence, four gates and high platforms, with the gods, instruments, banners and indrajala; the circle is adorned with cloths, garlands and canopies, and by the wish-fulfilling tree at the eight corners eight Deities are installed with eight Thakuranis; the author says that he cannot describe it and writes by the mercy of Rasika, whom he saw with his own eyes from childhood*

*Glory to Sri Sri Radha and Govinda!*
*Sri Sri Rasika-mangala.*
*Pashchima-vibhaga.*
*The first lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^301-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Turn Your attention to the fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of the fallen!
Glory, glory to the treasure of the life of Rasika-deva![^301-2]

**2.** Thus, after some days, Shyamananda-raya
left that place, taking Shyama-raya with him.[^301-3]

**3.** Coming to the town of Kashiyari, he stayed [there];
manifesting Thakurani for Shyama-raya,[^301-4]

**4.** joyfully arranging the wedding of Thakura,
in great bliss he held three festivals.

**5.** Great joy came to the town of Kashiyari:
men and women look on with eyes brimming, happy.[^301-5]

**6.** Sri Purushottama, Damodara, Mathuradasa,
Haraghosha Mahapatra, the brahmana Haridasa[^301-6]

**7.** received instruction in the mantra from Shyamananda:
giving up their family dharma, [they came] to Shyamananda's shelter.[^301-7]

**8.** Staying there some days, Shyamananda-raya
entered Dharenda together with Shyama-raya.

**9.** Bringing Thakurani in procession together [with Him],
for some days he joyfully spoke there of Krishna.[^301-8]

**10.** One day Shyamananda-raya held an assembly;
with him there were Rasikendra, Damodara,[^301-9]

**11.** Netrananda, Kishora, Thakura Haridasa,
Bhima Shirikara, Rasamaya, Vamshidasa,[^301-10]

**12.** Chintamani and all the other devotees of Krishna.
Shyamananda took counsel with Rasika:[^301-11]

**13.** "Proclaim one great Rasa-yatra,
so that the people of the three worlds may be amazed.

**14.** [It is] spring, and [soon] the full moon of Vaishakha:
a bright moon, [as in] autumn, a clear night.[^301-12]

**15.** Carefully entrust everyone with duties;
from today turn your mind to gathering provisions.

**16.** Give the order and the duties to all — the raja and the subjects:
let each, as far as his strength allows, prepare provisions."[^301-13]

**17.** In Rasamaya's house he tells [this] to everyone;
in great joy he fixed the Rasa-yatra.[^301-14]

**18.** Prabhu went to Sri Govindapur;
he ordered Rasika: "Turn your mind to the provisions."[^301-15]

**19.** Making Shyamananda's feet a necklace upon his heart,
Rasika went out to collect alms.

**20.** The order was given: "At Sri Gopivallabhapur
there will be a Great Rasa-yatra, shining over the three worlds."[^301-16]

**21.** Rasika ordered all [his] followers:
"All of you, clear the site for the rasa."[^301-17]

**22.** At the order hundreds and hundreds of followers set to work:
cutting down the thorns and the rest, they cleared [the site].

**23.** For about a year hundreds and hundreds of people laboured;
only then were the thorny thickets uprooted.[^301-18]

**24.** The whole site became even, like flower pollen;
in its midst they built a pavilion.

**25.** Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Narayanadasa,
Shyamagopala, Sri Rasamaya, Vamshidasa —[^301-19]

**26.** leaving all of them at Sri Gopivallabhapur
and saying, "Do all the work here," —

**27.** he himself went out to gather provisions:
in one single year he gathered provisions in many ways.[^301-20]

**28.** First [gathering] all the provisions for the festival,
he carefully brought rice and the rest, mung [and] biri.[^301-21]

**29.** Putting [them] into granaries, they stored [them] like mountains:
for the festival, in great joy, all this is the chief [supply].

**30.** Wheat, maida, chickpeas, khesari — without end;
ghee, oil, gur, guya — hundreds and hundreds of loads.[^301-22]

**31.** Fried dishes [and] sweets were made of many kinds;
bananas of various sorts, well ripened — without end.[^301-23]

**32.** Very soft laddus of many, many kinds —
filling hundreds and hundreds of pots, they quickly stored [them].

**33.** They filled hundreds and hundreds of baskets with saliya-ukhra,
filled hundreds and hundreds of baskets with fine, thin chida.[^301-24]

**34.** Hundreds and hundreds of baskets of khai, making [it] into hudum;
luchis [and] puris, filling hundreds and hundreds of pots.

**35.** Various fried dishes — hundreds and hundreds of loads;
curd, milk, cream, sugar — of many kinds.

**36.** At the proper time the household people bring
greens, badis, mangoes, maja, rambha, eggplants,[^301-25]

**37.** kushmanda gourds, bananas and the rest, palata, karela;
taba, jambira, nembu — hundreds of loads, kamala,[^301-26]

**38.** shatakara, pomegranates, lovely narenga:
all bring many different provisions in abundance.

**39.** Much khadira, tambula and lime arrived;
hingu, methi, nutmeg, mahuri and also jira,[^301-27]

**40.** camphor and pepper were brought in abundance:
for the festival — beautiful dishes of the six tastes.

**41.** And all the other subsidiary provisions they carefully brought —
all the provisions the Creator made in creation.[^301-28]

**42.** Countless different provisions all the people bring;
all say: "Mahalakshmi has appeared."

**43.** At the proper time all these loads of provisions
the household people brought and stored in [their] places.

**44.** Then they built the circle of the rasa:
in the shape of an eight-petalled [lotus], octagonal in its measure.[^301-29]

**45.** All around it they made various paintings;
seeing the site of the rasa, all the people are seized with awe.[^301-30]

**46.** Quickly bringing all the huge logs,
they planted the logs beautifully around the circle.

**47.** Even if a maddened elephant pushes, it cannot be moved —
such a firm fence shines on all sides.[^301-31]

**48.** On the four sides are four gates of supreme beauty;
on all four sides are very high, charming platforms.[^301-32]

**49.** Brahma, Shiva, Purandara [and] all the [other] gods
they carefully set up in [their proper] places.[^301-33]

**50.** Various instruments [and] banners they set up in various places;
at the sound the earth trembles, [there is] a rain of flowers.[^301-34]

**51.** Thus, on high, are great platforms, beautifully adorned;
on them indrajala shines — it cannot be described.[^301-35]

**52.** From them hang chamaras [and] various pendants of gems;
[all is] colourful — in cloths of many kinds, in clusters.[^301-36]

**53.** Colourful flower pendants of shola — of how many kinds!
Various fragrant flower pendants — in rows.[^301-37]

**54.** The circle [of the rasa] was adorned with indrajala in various styles;
on tall, tall poles they tied all the banners.[^301-38]

**55.** On them golden pitchers shine in rows;
from the arches hang pendants — captivating.

**56.** They wrapped all the pillars in colourful cloths;
everywhere they decorated [with designs of] rice flour.[^301-39]

**57.** To behold — supreme beauty, brilliantly shining:
[as if] Vrindavana had appeared before the eyes.[^301-40]

**58.** In the midst of the rasa circle a pavilion shines;
within it, a throne blazing with splendour.

**59.** In the midst of the pavilion — a beautiful wish-fulfilling tree
[with] pendants of various gems and jewels, wondrously skilful.[^301-41]

**60.** The tree is overlaid with gold, various gems blaze [on it];
by the radiance of that tree all four directions are lit.

**61.** At the foot of the tree — an octagonal jewelled throne;
at the eight corners [Rasika] placed eight Deities,[^301-42]

**62.** with eight Thakuranis, full of splendour,
in various ornaments — it cannot be described.

**63.** On all sides they stretched canopies of many kinds;
on the arches chamaras [and] pendants hang in clusters.[^301-43]

**64.** Seeing the circle [of the rasa], one marvels at [its] beauty;
Rasika's greatness cannot be described.[^301-44]

**65.** The qualities that Vyasa, Shuka, Narada and others glorify —
what power have I to describe them?[^301-45]

**66.** Yet by the mercy of Rasika's remnants
[I tell what] Rasikendra, dwelling in [my] heart, makes me speak.[^301-46]

**67.** With my own eyes I saw all his qualities [and] pastimes,
all the play [I] had with him from childhood.[^301-47]

**68.** In brief I have composed a certain description of [his] nature.
Hear the Rasika-mangala, all you people who long [for it].[^301-48]

**69.** This is the first description in the Pashchima-vibhaga:
I have composed [an account] of something of the great festival of the rasa.[^301-49]

**70.** Rasika held a great rasa, glorious [and] renowned;
in part I have made its description known.[^301-50]

**71.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the first lahari, called "Preparations for the Spring Rasa at Sri Gopivallabhapur."*[^301-51]

[^301-1]: The lines before the raga are the opening lines of the vibhaga and the lahari ("শ্রীশ্রীরাধাগোবিন্দৌ জয়তঃ / শ্রীশ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল / পশ্চিম বিভাগ / প্রথম-লহরী"), in italics without a number, as at the beginning of the Dakshina-vibhaga. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*); the ghosha is the same as in Dakshina, laharis 7, 10 and 14 (Dakshina, lahari 7, note 1), and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon after ॥ 71 ॥: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুরে বাসন্তরাসোত্থমনাম প্রথম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" — *bāsantarāsotthama*: understood as *bāsanta-rāsa-udyama*, "the preparation (undertaking) of the spring rasa" (which also fits the content of the lahari); possibly *-rāsottama*, "the excellent spring rasa"; the reading is unclear. The summary line covers the whole lahari. For the Pashchima-vibhaga there is no second reading (the 1997 edition).

[^301-2]: "The purifier of the fallen" — *patitapābana*. "Rasika-deva" — *rasikadeba*.

[^301-3]: "Thus" — the narrative of Dakshina, lahari 16 continues: Shyamananda and Rasika are with Uddanda in Nrisimhapur, where Shyama-raya had been brought from Dharenda (Dakshina, lahari 16, 57, note 36). Shyama-raya — a Deity of Krishna (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 12). "Taking with him" — *saṅge kari*.

[^301-4]: Kashiyari — *kāśīẏāṛi nagara*; in 5 — *kāśīẏāṛī purī* (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 4). "Stayed" — *utarila*. Thakurani is the Deity of Sri Radha; "manifesting" (*prakāśa kariyā*) is how the author speaks of making and installing a Deity, and "the wedding of Thakura" (4) is the installation of the Deity of Radha beside the Deity of Krishna (cf. Dakshina, lahari 6, note 3). The line can also be understood as "manifesting Shyama-raya [and] Thakurani".

[^301-5]: "Look on with eyes brimming, happy" — *naẏana bhariẏā sukha dekhe*, lit. "filling their eyes, they see happiness".

[^301-6]: 6–7 — new disciples of Shyamananda in Kashiyari; not identified. "Mathuradasa" — *mathurā dāsa*; it can also be understood as two names. Whether this is the same Damodara as in 10 (Shyamananda's disciple from Chakulia, Dakshina, lahari 1) is unclear. "Haraghosha Mahapatra" — *hāṛaghoṣa mahāpātra*; Mahapatra is an Oriya title or surname. "The brahmana Haridasa" — *dbija haridāsa*.

[^301-7]: "Received instruction in the mantra" — *mantra upadeśa kaila*: initiation (Dakshina, lahari 15, note 28). "Family dharma" — *kuladharma*: family customs and the worship of family gods (cf. Dakshina, lahari 13, note 4).

[^301-8]: "Bringing in procession" — *bijaẏa kariẏā*: said respectfully of a Deity's procession (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 31). "Together [with Him]" — *eka saṅge*: Thakurani together with Shyama-raya. "Joyfully" — *raṅge*.

[^301-9]: Rasikendra — Rasika. Damodara — Shyamananda's disciple from Chakulia (Dakshina, lahari 1). "There" — *tāẏa*.

[^301-10]: Netrananda, Kishora, Thakura Haridasa — apparently disciples of Shyamananda; it can also be understood as "Kishora Thakura, Haridasa". Bhima Shirikara — the ruler of Dharenda who became a Vaishnava (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 4); Rasamaya and Vamshidasa (Vamshi) are his grandsons, the author's father and uncle (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14).

[^301-11]: Chintamani — apparently a disciple of Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 38; Dakshina, lahari 10, note 13). "Took counsel with Rasika" — *bicārila rasikera sthāne*. 13–16 are Shyamananda's words to Rasika.

[^301-12]: The Rasa-yatra (*rāsaẏātrā*) is the festival of the rasa, Krishna's dance with the gopis (Bhagavatam 10.29–33); it is usually celebrated on the autumn full moon (Kartika), but here on the spring (*basanta*) full moon of the month of Vaishakha (April–May; cf. the spring rasa in the Gita-govinda, canto 1). "A bright moon, [as in] autumn" — *śarada ujjbala candra*; *śarada* can also be understood as "autumnal". "Full moon" — *pūrṇimī* (= *pūrṇimā*). "A clear night" — *nirmmala-yāminī*. The spring full moon of Vaishakha was also the time of the Panchama-dola at Dharenda (Dakshina, lahari 10).

[^301-13]: "Entrust with duties" — *bhāra deha*. "Gathering provisions" (15) — *drabya karibāre*. "As far as his strength allows" — *yāra yata śaktirūpe*; "prepare provisions" — *karaha sambhāra*.

[^301-14]: "In Rasamaya's house" — *rasamaẏa-gṛhe*: in Dharenda (cf. Dakshina, lahari 10). "Fixed" — *nirṇaẏa karila*: Shyamananda (or Rasika) fixed the time of the festival.

[^301-15]: Sri Govindapur — Shyamananda's village (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7; lahari 16, note 21). "Went out" (19) — *bāhāra* (= *bāhira*). "To collect alms" — *bhikṣā karibāra*: to gather provisions for the festival (cf. 27).

[^301-16]: Sri Gopivallabhapur — Rasika's village on the Suvarnarekha (Dakshina, lahari 3). "Shining over the three worlds" — *trailokya birāje*.

[^301-17]: "Followers" — *anucara*: Rasika's disciples and servants. "The site for the rasa" — *rāsasthala*. "Clear" — *pariṣkāra*.

[^301-18]: "About a year" — *batsareka*. "The thorny thickets" — *kaṇṭakera bana*, lit. "the forest of thorns". "Even, like flower pollen" (24) — *parāga dhūli samāna*: *samāna* means both "even" and "like"; it can be understood as "[soft] like flower pollen". "Pavilion" — *maṇḍapa*.

[^301-19]: Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Shyamagopala — disciples of Rasika (cf. Purva, lahari 1, 131–132); Narayanadasa is a new name; Rasamaya and Vamshidasa — note 10. Ramakrishna is apparently the brahmana Ramakrishna(dasa) of Dakshina, lahari 16, 10. "Do all the work here" (26) — *ekhānera sarbbakāryya karaha*.

[^301-20]: "Himself" — *āpani*: Rasika (cf. 19). "In many ways" — *nānārūpe*. "In one single year" — *ekai batsare*.

[^301-21]: "Mung [and] biri" — *muga biri*: mung beans and biri (urad, black gram). "Granaries" (29) — *marāi*: round woven bins for grain. "The chief [supply]" — *pradhāna*: apparently the main provisions for the festival. After the first line of 29 the 1941 edition has "॥" instead of "।".

[^301-22]: Maida (*maẏadā*) — finely milled wheat flour; "chickpeas" — *cholā*; khesari (*khesārī*) — grass pea, a pulse. Gur and guya — unrefined cane sugar and areca nut (Purva, lahari 11, note 9). "Loads" — *bhāra*: a load carried on a shoulder pole (Purva, lahari 12, note 4).

[^301-23]: "Fried dishes" — *pakvānna*; "sweets" — *miṣṭānna*. "Bananas" — *kadalī*; "well ripened" — *supakka*. "Laddus" (32) — *lāṛu*; "pots" — *hā̃ṛī*; "quickly" — *tvarati*.

[^301-24]: "Baskets" — *ḍola*: large woven baskets. Saliya-ukhra (*sāliẏā ukhaṛā*) — according to the editor's note, "the best murki", puffed rice in sugar syrup; *sāliẏā* apparently means "of shali rice". Chida — flattened rice; "thin" — *saru*. Khai (34) — puffed rice; hudum (*huṛuma*) — according to the editor's note, a kind of roasted chida; "making [it] into hudum" — *huṛuma kariẏā*, the sense is approximate. Luchis and puris — wheat breads fried in oil or ghee. The editor's notes are not translated.

[^301-25]: "Cream" (35) — *sara*: the skin of boiled milk. "Household people" — *parijana* (in 43 — *paribāra*). Badis (*baṛi*) — sun-dried balls of pulse paste. Maja (*mājā*) — according to the editor's note, the pith of the banana stem (*thoṛ*). Rambha (*rambhā*) — bananas (plantains). "Eggplants" — *bāigana*.

[^301-26]: Kushmanda — a gourd (ash gourd). Palata (*palatā*) — apparently patol (pointed gourd) or its leaves. Karela (*karalā*) — bitter gourd. Taba (*ṭābā*), jambira (*jāmbira*), nembu (*nembu*) — kinds of lemon; kamala — oranges. Shatakara (38) — according to the editor's note, pomelo (*bātāpi nebu*); narenga (*nāreṅga*) — oranges; "pomegranates" — *dāṛimba*.

[^301-27]: Khadira (*khadira*) — the astringent extract of catechu acacia, tambula — betel leaves, "lime" — *cūrṇa*: all for pan. Hingu — asafoetida; methi — fenugreek; "nutmeg" — *jāẏaphala*; mahuri (*mahurī*) — fennel (in Dakshina, lahari 10, *mahuri* is a musical instrument); jira — cumin. "Pepper" (40) — *marica*, black pepper. "Dishes of the six tastes" — *ṣaṛarasa byañjana*.

[^301-28]: "Subsidiary provisions" — *upadrabya*. "The Creator" — *bidhātā*. "Countless" (42) — *apramita*. Mahalakshmi — the goddess of prosperity; "has appeared" — *haila upasana* (cf. Dakshina, lahari 16, note 26). "Stored in [their] places" (43) — *yathāsthāne … purila*.

[^301-29]: "The circle of the rasa" — *rāsa-maṇḍalī* (Dakshina, lahari 15, note 41). "In the shape of an eight-petalled [lotus]" — *aṣṭadalākṛti*; "octagonal in its measure" — *aṣṭakoṇa parimāṇa*.

[^301-30]: "Paintings" — *nānācitra*. "Are seized with awe" — *pāẏa trāse*, lit. "feel fear": reverent awe.

[^301-31]: "It cannot be moved" — *ṭhelā nāhi haẏa*. "A firm fence" — *goṛā bāṛa*: understood as *bāṛa* (= *beṛā*), "fence", and *goṛā*, "base, root", i.e. firmly planted; the reading and sense are approximate.

[^301-32]: "Platforms" — *mañca*: high stands around the circle.

[^301-33]: Purandara — Indra. "Set up" — *sthāpilena*: apparently figures of the gods on the platforms, as if watching the rasa (cf. Bhagavatam 10.33.3: the gods in their celestial chariots watch the rasa).

[^301-34]: "Banners" — *niśāna*: banners; *niśāna* is also a large drum (kettledrum). "Trembles" — *tharahara*. "A rain of flowers" — *puṣpa bariṣaṇe*.

[^301-35]: Indrajala (*indrajāla*, lit. "Indra's net, magic") — apparently patterned net-like canopies and hangings. "On high" — *ucce*. Couplet 51 is the last and is complete; and 134 are inset plates, and the lahari continues with ॥ 52 ॥.

[^301-36]: The description of the festive decoration of the rasa circle begins in 44–51. "From them" — *tāhe*: from the tall platforms (51). Chamaras are whisks of yak tails. "Pendants" — *jhārā*: hanging clusters, fringes (Dakshina, lahari 15, notes 36, 38). "In clusters" — *kerā kerā*: the meaning is unclear, understood as in Dakshina, lahari 15, note 38.

[^301-37]: Shola (*śolā*) is the light white pith of a marsh plant, from which festive decorations are carved in Bengal. "Of how many kinds" — *kata bhānti* (= *bhā̃ti*). "In rows" — *pā̃ti pā̃ti*.

[^301-38]: Indrajala (*indrajāla*) — apparently patterned net-like awnings and pendants (note 35). "In various styles" — *nānā chā̃de*. "Poles" — *kāṣṭhete*, lit. "on wooden [posts]".

[^301-39]: "[Designs of] rice flour" — *taṇḍulera cūrṇe*: patterns (alpana) of rice flour with which the festival ground is decorated.

[^301-40]: "Before the eyes" — *dṛggocara*, "visible to the eye".

[^301-41]: "Pavilion" — *maṇḍapa*. "Wish-fulfilling tree" — *kalpataru* (Dakshina, lahari 15, note 36). "Wondrously skilful" — *ati bicakṣaṇa*. Cf. the description of Vrindavana in Rasika's speech (Dakshina, lahari 15, 101–110): the wish-fulfilling tree and the jewelled throne at its foot.

[^301-42]: "Octagonal" — *aṣṭakoṇe*, lit. "at the eight corners" (cf. 44: the rasa circle is eight-petalled, octagonal). "Eight Deities" — *aṣṭa śrīmūrati*, with eight Thakuranis (62): apparently eight Deities of Krishna, each with a Thakurani — a Deity of Radha (cf. Dakshina, lahari 11, note 17: Gopivallabha-raya with the Thakurani); which ones, the author does not say. "Placed" — *dila bāre*: the sense of *bāre* is unclear. The subject is not named; understood as Rasika.

[^301-43]: "Canopies" — *cā̃duẏā*: cloth awnings stretched over the festival ground. "In clusters" — *yutha yutha*, lit. "in flocks, in throngs".

[^301-44]: "Greatness" — *anubhabe*: it can also be understood as Rasika's "spiritual insight (experience)" (cf. lahari 2, 67).

[^301-45]: Vyasa is the compiler of the Bhagavata; Shuka (Shukadeva) narrated it to Parikshit; Narada is Vyasa's teacher. "Qualities" — *guṇa*: apparently the qualities [of Krishna and His pastimes], including the rasa that Rasika re-enacted.

[^301-46]: "Remnants" — *abaśeṣa* (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 8). Rasikendra is Rasikananda. The author ascribes his inspiration to Rasika dwelling in his heart (cf. Dakshina, lahari 5, note 28).

[^301-47]: The subject is not named (*dekhila*, *kaila* — third person, often used of oneself in this language); understood as the author: he saw Rasika with his own eyes and was near him from childhood (the author is the son of Rasamaya, Rasika's disciple; cf. lahari 2, 45: "Gopijana-vallabha, the son of Rasamaya" among the boys at the festival). It can also be understood as "all the play that [Rasika] had from childhood with [his companions]".

[^301-48]: "Description of [his] nature" — *sbabhāba-barṇana* (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 41). "Who long [for it]" — so the 1941 edition's reading «কাঙ্ক্ষ´জন» is understood (*kāṅkṣa-jana*?, cf. *kāṅkṣī*, "desirous"; checked at ×4): the reading is unclear.

[^301-49]: "Great festival of the rasa" — *rāsa-mahotsaba*. "I have composed" — *karila racanā* (third person, understood as first; cf. note 47).

[^301-50]: "Glorious [and] renowned" — *yaśa khyātā*, lit. "fame known"; rhyme *khyātā / bikhyātā*. "Made known" — *karilu bikhyātā*.

[^301-51]: The colophon is: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুরে বাসন্তরাসোদ্যমনাম প্রথম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*bāsanta-rāsa-udyama*); the ligature «দ্য» (×4) has the same form as in «বিদ্যমান» (57). In note 1 the same place is read «রাসোত্থম» and understood as *-rāsodyama*; the 1941 edition apparently has precisely «দ্য»: *udyama*, "undertaking, preparations". On the spring rasa at the full moon of Vaishakha — note 12; on the rasa-lila — lahari 2, note 7.


## Lahari 2. The Description of the Adhivasa of the Rasa

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; having gathered everything needed over a year, Rasika opens the Rasa-yatra on the spring full moon of Vaishakha; there arrive Shyamananda, Hridayananda, Auliya Thakura, Vidyutmala Thakurani, Subaladasa, the descendants of Nityananda and Advaita, the followers of the twelve gopalas and the sixty-four mahantas, kings and countless people; in the evening the adhivasa of the festival is performed, and Rasika worships Shyamananda, Hridayananda and the mahantas; hundreds of thousands partake of prasada, the demigods serve unrecognized together with the people, and all call Rasika a partial incarnation; eight boys, among them Rasamaya's son Gopijana-vallabha, are dressed as the eight sakhis, and the boy Raghunatha as Krishna; all forget themselves in bliss, as though Vrindavana had appeared*

*The second lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^302-1]
*Ghosha: "[My] life is Radhanatha, O, [my] soul is Gopinatha."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the sweet form!
Be merciful, so that I may sing [your] glory day and night.[^302-2]

**2.** At that time Rasikendra, going round all four directions,
gathered everything [needed] within one year.[^302-3]

**3.** In spring, when the month of Vaishakha had become full,
on the full-moon day he opened the festival.[^302-4]

**4.** First came Shyamananda-raya;
Sri Hridayananda [Rasika] invited with care.[^302-5]

**5.** Auliya Thakura came rejoicing;
[there came] Vidyutmala Thakurani — Lakshmi herself.[^302-6]

**6.** They came to see the Rasa-yatra —
great mahajanas with their followers.[^302-7]

**7.** Thakura Subaladasa, a great mahajana,
performs kirtana together with Jagatvallabha.[^302-8]

**8.** Shyama, Mathuradasa, Vallabha the drummer —
with Hridayananda came all his own servants.[^302-9]

**9.** Bada Balaramadasa Thakura came;
the sons and grandsons of Nityananda came and entered.[^302-10]

**10.** All the sons and grandsons of Advaita arrived,
the disciples and grand-disciples of the twelve gopalas.[^302-11]

**11.** The servants of the sixty-four mahantas and the servants of their servants
hastily entered in time for the Rasa-yatra.[^302-12]

**12.** Ramadasa Thakura, Krishnadasa the renunciant,
Sri Prasada Thakura, Sri Jagannathadasa —[^302-13]

**13.** Dvaraka, Mathura, Vrindavana, Nilachala:
as many companions of Krishna as there were in each of these places,

**14.** all came to see the Rasa-yatra;
hundreds and hundreds of maharajas came there.[^302-14]

**15.** People without count from all four directions:
brahmanas, sannyasis, sadhus, kings, subjects — crowd upon crowd.[^302-15]

**16.** Women, men, and children, the old and the rest —
all came, having locked up their houses and doors.

**17.** The countless people cannot be described even with a hundred mouths:
throw a mustard seed, and it would never fall to the ground.[^302-16]

**18.** To perform sankirtana, a great many parties
came crowd upon crowd from all four directions.[^302-17]

**19.** They performed the auspicious adhivasa of the festival:
with clothes and ornaments they honour all the Vaishnavas.[^302-18]

**20.** Setting up the auspicious pot, [performing] the auspicious arati,
[placing] turmeric, rice, durva grass, grain, mango leaves,[^302-19]

**21.** setting a coconut on top of that pot —
around the pot burn four lamps of jewels;

**22.** together with curd, milk, ghee, honey, sugar,
and with garlands, sandal, clothes and ornaments as well;

**23.** kunkuma, musk, chuya, abir, saffron,
camphor, sandal — hundreds of pots together.

**24.** Thus, having joyfully performed the adhivasa,
first of all Rasika worshipped Shyamananda.[^302-20]

**25.** Then he worshipped the feet of Sri Hridayananda;
then at the sankirtana he honoured Tulasidasa.

**26.** To adorn [them] with clothes, ornaments, garlands, sandal,
Rasikachandra worships [them] with his own hands.

**27.** Rasika's god-brothers [and] worthy disciples —
one person to each mahanta —

**28.** camphor, sandal, garlands, clothes, ornaments
were offered, as befitting, by hundreds and hundreds of people.[^302-21]

**29.** Thus, having performed the adhivasa in the evening,
Rasikendra-raya began the festival.[^302-22]

**30.** Hundreds and hundreds of people entered the storerooms
and began to give out cooling provisions [and] sida.[^302-23]

**31.** Hundreds and hundreds of kings, subjects, Vaishnavas, brahmanas —
all were satisfied and served food.[^302-24]

**32.** Hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas do the cooking;
a hundred elderly brahmanas serve out the food.[^302-25]

**33.** Hundreds and hundreds of people carry water on their shoulders;
hundreds and hundreds of people, seated, sprinkle the leaf-plates.

**34.** Hundreds and hundreds of leaf-plates are before Krishna:
shali rice, hundreds of dishes of six tastes,[^302-26]

**35.** khira, pitha, fried delicacies — various gifts;
brahmanas of righteous conduct offer [them] to Krishna.

**36.** Then, taking the prasada, they give it to all;
five hundred thousand sit down at one time.[^302-27]

**37.** Thus they sit down in rows again and again;
hundreds and hundreds of servants clear away the leaf-plates.

**38.** The splendour of the festival seems a wonder;
all say: "Rasikendra is a partial incarnation."[^302-28]

**39.** The world of the gods [and] the world of men, joined together,
make merry in every way in the great bliss of the Rasa-yatra.

**40.** Someone cooks, someone serves out the food;
no one recognizes anyone: the demigods are [there] in secret.[^302-29]

**41.** What power have humans to accomplish such a work?
Seeing that assembly, gods [and] men are astonished.

**42.** A most wondrous lila [he], the friend of the three worlds,
Rasikendu, manifested on earth.[^302-30]

**43.** Having sought out people one by one for all these tasks,
they then dressed the boys close by.[^302-31]

**44.** They settled on eight sakhis [and] one Krishna;
beforehand they had taught them all to dance.

**45.** Devakidasa and Gokula Mahashaya,
Gopijana-vallabha, the son of Rasamaya,[^302-32]

**46.** Gaura, Gopaladasa, the boy Gokula,
Narayanadasa, Gopijivana of Bhupura.

**47.** These eight boys — to the number of the eight sakhis;
in the dress of Krishna — one boy named Raghunatha.[^302-33]

**48.** With care they dressed them all;
these young boys are most skilled in dance.

**49.** They plaited the hair on their heads into braids;
to them they deftly bound knots with pendants of jewels.[^302-34]

**50.** Stringing various jewels [and] pearls on double threads,
they tied [them] beautifully and neatly, encircling the head.[^302-35]

**51.** On everyone's forehead they put fragrant sandal;
in the midst of the gorochana — a lovely dot of phagu.[^302-36]

**52.** On the eyes they put kajal — most charming;
on the nose shine a row of jewels [and] the finest pearl.

**53.** On the lips is the red of tambula, beautiful to see;
in the ears jewelled ornaments sparkle.[^302-37]

**54.** The neck is beautifully adorned with [necklaces] of various jewels and gems;
on the breast [necklaces] hang in tiers, dazzlingly bright.

**55.** Golden bajubandhas grace both arms;
on them golden pendants shine beautifully.[^302-38]

**56.** Beside them golden bracelets look lovely;
wondrous patterned conch-shell bangles shine on both hands.[^302-39]

**57.** Above the conch-shell bangles — golden kankanas on the hands;
beside them — bajubandhas, golden ornaments.

**58.** All the fingers are adorned with jewelled rings;
on everyone's breast — wondrous bodices.

**59.** Blue, yellow, silken, fine, wondrous garments
they put on all the boys in various styles.

**60.** Over that — a golden wrap;
at the waist they tied to it [a girdle] of inlaid little bells.[^302-40]

**61.** On the feet — double rows of bells [and] sweet-sounding nupuras:
they made everyone's form one of supreme sweetness.[^302-41]

**62.** It is as if one sees the young women of Vraja in person.
One boy they took care to make [like] Krishna:

**63.** every limb they adorned with ornaments in various styles;
in various styles they put [on him] yellow garments;

**64.** [he] is coated with sandal, kunkuma [and] musk;
on his head they set a most beautiful crown:

**65.** it sparkles, various gems blaze in it,
and in it — peacock feathers, most charming.

**66.** Thus they dressed Krishna and the young women of Vraja:
seeing [this], all the men and women are enchanted.

**67.** Rasika's power cannot be told:
it is as if Vrindavana itself had come and appeared [here].[^302-42]

**68.** All were immersed in bliss, with no awareness of the outer world;
there are no enemies [or] friends — all have one life.

**69.** They know no sorrow, all are drunk with happiness;
all think themselves young immortals.

**70.** No one has anger, pride, conceit;
no one has strangers — all are their own.

**71.** They know neither night nor day — [only] jubilation in bliss;
seeing what Rasika has manifested, they are amazed.

**72.** Whatever provision they think of comes there;
the eight siddhis [and] the nine nidhis follow in attendance.[^302-43]

**73.** Such is [Rasika] — an ocean of mercy, a sweet form,
for whom Krishna is the treasure of life, family, character and caste.

**74.** Rasika's greatness cannot be told at all:
by remembering him one attains Krishna, the lord of life.[^302-44]

**75.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will gain the treasure of prema and bhakti for Krishna.

**76.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the second lahari in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala, called "The Description of the Adhivasa of the Rasa".*[^302-45]

[^302-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading («দ্বিতীয়-লহরী»), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*) — Purva, lahari 8, note 2. The ghosha reads in the 1941 edition: *jībana rādhānātha re parāṇa gopīnātha*: Radhanatha ("the Lord of Radha") and Gopinatha ("the Lord of the gopis") are names of Krishna; *re* is an exclamation. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাসাধিবাস-বর্ণন-নাম দ্বিতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsādhibāsa-barṇana*) — "The Description of the Adhivasa of the Rasa". Adhivasa is the rite of consecration on the eve of a festival (19–29). The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^302-2]: "The sweet form" — *madhura mūrati*.

[^302-3]: Rasikendra is Rasikananda. "Going round all four directions" — *phiri cāridike*: gathering provisions for the festival (lahari 1, 26–43). "Gathered everything" — *saba karila saṃyoge*.

[^302-4]: "When the month of Vaishakha had become full" — *baiśākha pūrṇa māsa*: understood as the full moon of Vaishakha (April–May); cf. "the spring full moon, the night of Vaishakha" — the time of the Panchama-dola (Dakshina, lahari 8, note 24; lahari 9, note 14). "Opened the festival" — *yātrā karila prakāśa*, lit. "manifested the festival (festive procession)". The spring rasa — colophon of lahari 1.

[^302-5]: "Came" — *bīje karilā* (*bijaẏa*): respectful, of a ceremonial arrival (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 31); "arrival". (gloss not translated). Hridayananda is Hridaya Chaitanya, Shyamananda's guru (Purva, lahari 1, note 13). "Invited with care" — *ānāilā yatane*, lit. "had [him] brought with care"; the subject is not named, understood as Rasika.

[^302-6]: Auliya Thakura (*āuliẏā ṭhākura*) and Vidyutmala Thakurani (*bidyutmālā ṭhākurāṇī*, "garland of lightning") — not identified. *Āuliẏā* means "free, ecstatic [in love of God]", a byname of wandering Vaishnavas (cf. Chaitanya Dasa the Auliya in the Prema-vilasa). "Rejoicing" — *kautuke*. "Lakshmi herself" — *lakṣmīra sbarūpe*, lit. "in the form of Lakshmi": of her beauty and grace.

[^302-7]: The Rasa-yatra (*rāsa-yātrā*) is the festival of the rasa-lila, the circle dance of Krishna with the gopis headed by Sri Radha (Bhag. 10.29–33; Purva, lahari 7, note 29). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the rasa-lila is the summit of Krishna's pastimes, a manifestation of the gopis' pure prema, in which there is not a trace of mundane desire (kama); whoever hears of it with faith attains the highest devotion and is freed from the heart's disease of mundane desires (Bhag. 10.33.39). The Bhagavata describes the autumn rasa; the spring rasa is sung in Jayadeva's Gita-govinda (canto 1). At the festival the Deities are placed on the rasa-mancha in the middle of the decorated circle (lahari 1, 44–63). "Mahajanas" — *mahājana*: great Vaishnavas. "With their followers" — *saṅge anucare*.

[^302-8]: Thakura Subaladasa (*ṭhākura subaladāsa*) and Jagatvallabha (*jagataballabha*) are not identified; *jagataballabha* may also be taken as an epithet, "beloved of the world". "A great mahajana" — *baṛa mahājana*: a great Vaishnava (note 7).

[^302-9]: "Shyama, Mathuradasa, Vallabha the drummer" — *śyāma mathurā dāsa bāẏena ballabha*; the names may also be divided otherwise (e.g. "Shyama-Mathuradasa"). *Bāẏena* is a musician who plays the drum (khol). Whether this Mathuradasa is the one in lahari 1, 6 is unclear. "His own servants" — *nija bhṛtya*: Hridayananda's disciples.

[^302-10]: Bada Balaramadasa Thakura — *baṛa balarāma dāsa ṭhākura* (*baṛa*, "elder, great"); cf. Purva, lahari 1, 38 (note 21) and 62 (Balaramadasa, note 33); not identified. "Sons and grandsons" — *putra pautra*: the descendants of Nityananda (of Virachandra and his line); likewise of Advaita in 10.

[^302-11]: The twelve gopalas are associates of Nityananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 18). "Disciples and grand-disciples" — *śiṣya praśiṣya-gaṇa*: their spiritual descendants.

[^302-12]: The sixty-four mahantas — Purva, lahari 1, note 20. "The servants of their servants" — *tadbhṛtya*. "Hastily" — *tvarita*.

[^302-13]: Ramadasa Thakura, Krishnadasa, Sri Prasada Thakura (cf. Purva, lahari 1, 62, note 33) and Sri Jagannathadasa are not identified. "The renunciant" — *bairāgī*: a Vaishnava who has renounced the world (cf. Purva, lahari 1, 63: "renounced, devoted to Krishna").

[^302-14]: Nilachala is Puri. "Companions of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-sahacara*: Vaishnavas. "Maharajas" — *mahārājā*: ruling princes.

[^302-15]: "Without count" — *samuccaẏa nāi*, lit. "there is no reckoning". "Sannyasis" — *nyāsī*. "Crowd upon crowd" — *yūthe yūthe*.

[^302-16]: "Cannot be described even with a hundred mouths" — *śatamukhe kahā naẏa*. A mustard seed would not fall to the ground — so tightly packed were the people.

[^302-17]: "Parties" — *sampradā* (= *sampradāẏa*): kirtana groups. "A great many" — *bahuta*.

[^302-18]: Adhivasa is the rite of consecration on the eve of a festival (note 1). "Auspicious" — *maṅgala*.

[^302-19]: 20–23 describe the rite of adhivasa. The auspicious pot (*maṅgala ghaṭa*) is a pot of water crowned with a coconut and mango leaves, a sign of the divine presence in the rite. "Grain" — *dhānya*: unhusked rice. "Mango leaves" — *āmrapatrī*. Chuya (*cuẏā*) is a fragrant oil (perfume); abir is a fragrant red powder; "saffron" — *keśara*. "Pots" — *hāṇḍī*; "together" — *ekatara*.

[^302-20]: Rasika first worships Shyamananda, his guru, then Hridayananda, Shyamananda's guru (Purva, lahari 1, note 13). Tulasidasa (25) is the "guru of sankirtana" whom Rasika revered from childhood (Purva, lahari 1, 64, note 34). "Honoured" — *bandilā*. Rasikachandra (26) is Rasika.

[^302-21]: "God-brothers" — *guru-bhāi*: Shyamananda's disciples. "One person to each mahanta" — *eka eka mohāntera eka eka jane*: understood as each mahanta being presented with gifts by a separate person. "As befitting" — *yathāyogya*.

[^302-22]: "Began the festival" — *mahotsaba juṛilena*: opened the festive meal (the distribution of prasada). Rasikendra-raya is Rasika.

[^302-23]: "Cooling provisions" — *śītala sāmagrī*: meaning unclear; possibly raw (uncooked) foodstuffs. Sida (*sidā* = *sidhā*) is a dry ration (rice, dal and so on) given to brahmanas and sadhus so that they may cook their food themselves.

[^302-24]: "Served food" — *prabeṣaṇa kaila*: according to the editor's footnote, *prabeṣaṇa* = *paribeṣaṇa*, "serving out (distributing) food" (footnote not translated); so also in 32, 40.

[^302-25]: "Elderly" — *baẏesiẏā*: understood as "advanced in years" (from *baẏasa*, "age"); reading unclear. "Leaf-plates" (33) — *patra*: leaves used as plates; "sprinkle" — *śiñcena*: wash them by sprinkling with water.

[^302-26]: "Before Krishna" — before the Deity, for offering. "Shali rice" — *śāli anna*. "Dishes of six tastes" — *ṣaṛarasa byañjana* (cf. lahari 1, 40). Khira (35) is rice cooked in thickened milk; pitha are sweet cakes; "fried delicacies" — *pakvānna*. "Of righteous conduct" — *sadācāra*.

[^302-27]: "Five hundred thousand" — *pā̃ca śata sahasra*, lit. "five hundreds of thousands"; it may also be taken as "five hundred, a thousand". "Rows" (37) — *maṇḍalī*.

[^302-28]: "A partial incarnation" — *aṃśa abatāra*: so the people at the festival say; this is the author's exalted praise. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda. On how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^302-29]: "In secret" — *gupte*: the demigods, unrecognized, served on a par with the people. "Gods [and] men" (41) — *sura nara*.

[^302-30]: "The friend of the three worlds" — *tribhubana-bandhu*; Rasikendu, "the moon of the rasikas", is Rasika. "Manifested" — *prakāśa karilā*.

[^302-31]: 43–66 describe the preparation for a performance of the rasa-lila: boys portray the sakhis and Krishna (cf. Purva, lahari 7, 107–111, note 29); on the rasa-lila — note 7. "Having sought out people one by one" — *loka khũji eke eke*. "Dressed" — *beśa karila*; "close by" — *samīpe*. "Settled on" (44) — *karila niścaẏa*; "beforehand" — *pūrbba haite*.

[^302-32]: Gopijana-vallabha, the son of Rasamaya, is the author of the poem himself (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14). The other boys are not identified. "Mahashaya" is a respectful title. In 46 the names may also be divided otherwise: "Gaura-Gopaladasa" as one name, in which case the eighth is Bhupura. Here *bhupura* is taken as a place name ("of Bhupura"); reading unclear.

[^302-33]: "To the number of the eight sakhis" — *aṣṭa sakhī paramāṇa*, lit. "eight sakhis as the measure". The eight sakhis are the principal companions of Sri Radha (Lalita, Vishakha and the others). Raghunatha is not identified. "Young" (48) — *naba*; "most skilled" — *baṛa … bicakṣaṇa*.

[^302-34]: "Knots with pendants of jewels" — *maṇi-khopa-jhārā*: understood as a knot of hair (*khõpā*) with pendants (*jhārā*) of gems; meaning approximate. "Deftly" — *susāra*.

[^302-35]: "On double threads" — *dosati* (taken as *do-sūti*); "neatly" — *susañca*: meaning unclear, rendered approximately.

[^302-36]: Gorochana is a yellow pigment for decorating the forehead; phagu (*phāgu*) is red powder (abir). "Kajal" (52) — collyrium. "A row of jewels [and] the finest pearl" — *ratna pā̃ti muktābara*: a nose ornament.

[^302-37]: Tambula is betel. "Jewelled ornaments" — *ratnakāpa*: understood as earrings (Oriya *kāpa*, "earring"). "Sparkle" — *jhalamala*. "In tiers" (54) — *thare thare*; "hang" — *lambe*.

[^302-38]: A bajubandha (*bājubandha*) is an armlet worn on the upper arm. "Golden pendants" — *khopa soṇā jhā̃pā*: meaning approximate.

[^302-39]: "Bracelets" — *tāṛa*: heavy bracelets. "Patterned conch-shell bangles" — *khãjā śā̃khā*: *khãjā* taken as "notched, patterned"; reading unclear. A kankana (57) is a bracelet. Bajubandhas are mentioned twice (55, 57) — so in the text. "Bodices" (58) — *kāñculī*. "Silken, fine" (59) — *pāṭa neta*.

[^302-40]: "Wrap" — *uṛaẏāni*: a veil or wrap (cf. *oṛhanī*). "At the waist" — *ā̃ṭāẏa*: according to the editor's footnote, "at the waist" (*kaṭite*; footnote not translated). "Inlaid little bells" — *khañjita kiṅkiṇī*.

[^302-41]: "Double rows of bells" — *ghughũrī dosarī*. Nupuras are anklets with little bells. "Sweet-sounding" — *rasāla*.

[^302-42]: "Power" — *anubhaba*: also "realization, experience"; it may be taken as "what Rasika experienced (manifested)". "As if" — *kibā*.

[^302-43]: The eight siddhis are mystic perfections (the ability to become minute and the rest); the nine nidhis are the nine treasures of Kubera. The sense: everything needed comes to Rasika of itself. "Follow in attendance" — *saṅgete beṛāẏa*.

[^302-44]: "The treasure of life, family, character and caste" (73) — *prāṇadhana kulaśīla jāti*: Rasika has no family or standing other than Krishna. "By remembering him one attains Krishna" — the author's exalted praise; on how he exalts Rasika — note 28.

[^302-45]: The title is "The Description of the Adhivasa of the Rasa". The colophon stands below ॥76॥ in the right column; below it are a rule and the editor's footnote to 60.


## Lahari 3. The Description of the Rasa

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; at Sri Gopivallabhapur on the bank of the Suvarnarekha, on the spring full moon of Vaishakha, Rasika opens the rasa: amid the thunder of instruments and sankirtana, amid hosts of people and gods, boys enact the rasa-lila following the five chapters of the Bhagavata — the call of the flute, the coming of the gopis, the words of Krishna sending them home to their husbands, the gopis' weeping and their reply that they will not leave His feet; Krishna smilingly calls the gopis, and the boys dance the rasa in the midst of the circle of sankirtana; the bliss of Vrindavana appears, the people are amazed and call Rasika a second Narayana; the author writes by the grace of Rasika, the son of Achyuta*

*The third lahari.*

*Raga Kamoda.*[^303-1]
*Ghosha: "Blessed, O blessed is the union of Radha and Shyama!*
*How many waves have risen in the ocean of nectar!"*[^303-2]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the refuge of the helpless,
the friend of Vallabha's life, the son of Durika![^303-3]

**2.** Sri Gopivallabhapur is a charming place
on the bank of the Suvarnarekha, beautifully laid out.

**3.** On all four sides are forests, most charming;
a very soft place — a beautiful river sandbank.[^303-4]

**4.** In such a place Rasikendra began the rasa;
all the hosts of the gods came to see.[^303-5]

**5.** People without count — they became innumerable;
various instruments and dundubhis sound on all four sides.

**6.** Cries of "Hari!", the sound of conches, flutes and horns;
with the sound of the various instruments the earth shakes.[^303-6]

**7.** The sankirtana [and] the dundubhis are most tremendous;
with the sound "dulu-dulu" the earth trembles.

**8.** At that time Rasikendra manifested the rasa;
the people of the three worlds were immersed in bliss.

**9.** The full moon of Vaishakha, a very bright moon;
that night is [like] eternity, there is no limit to it.[^303-7]

**10.** In springtime the wish-fulfilling tree is beautiful;
in the middle of the circle of the rasa is a throne of jewels.

**11.** Krishna went up onto it and remained [there];
bent in three places, [He plays] a most sweet song on the flute.[^303-8]

**12.** He calls the gopis by name, one after another;
hearing the murali, the gopis came [to Him].[^303-9]

**13.** Seeing Krishna's face, [they] lost their senses;
with the tears from their eyes the gopis' garments grew wet.

**14.** Seeing the gopis, Krishna, bowing His head,
stood still for a moment, leaning on the wish-fulfilling tree.[^303-10]

**15.** Seeing Krishna displeased, all the gopis,
their heads bowed, drawing on the ground, weep.

**16.** Sobbing and sobbing they weep, unaware of their bodies.
[Then] the Lord — God, Bhagavan — began to speak.[^303-11]

**17.** In the order of the Bhagavata, according to its every rule,
Sri Rasika, the treasury of virtues, manifested the rasa.[^303-12]

**18.** Krishna speaks sweet words to the gopis:
"Leaving your homes, on what business have you come to the forest?[^303-13]
