**19.** At home your relatives are anxiously searching for you;
why have you come to the forest at this dreadful midnight?

**20.** The blue waters of the Yamuna, the beautiful sandbank,
the trees, [their] shoots — are most charming:

**21.** you have seen all these places — go home;
the children are crying bitterly.

**22.** If you have come to see Me out of love for Me —
you have seen Me; now go home quickly.

**23.** Serve your husbands at home, filled with joy;
worship [them] firmly as Vishnu.

**24.** Even if a husband is poor, unhappy, sick —
know him for certain to be equal to Vishnu.

**25.** Serve your husbands thus with firm attachment;
why do you wander in the forest with anxious minds?"[^303-14]

**26.** All [the rasikas] who are like Rasika, together with Rasika,
on various instruments, with various music, sing in various delightful ways.[^303-15]

**27.** Pakhoyaj, mridanga, and dampha [and] dhol,
and all the other various instruments raised a thunder.[^303-16]

**28.** Vina, venu, murali, upanga — delightful;
someone joyfully plays the svara-mandala.

**29.** Kapinasha, saranga, and pinaka, kinnari,
rabab, madol, kansi, muchung, mahuri,

**30.** kartal, mandiras and the rest, the sweet panchama;
surrounding the gopis, all sing in many ways.[^303-17]

**31.** Someone sings the five chapters on the rasa from the Sri Bhagavata;
following their order, they have the boys enact the lila.[^303-18]

**32.** That gait, that posture, that conduct,
those tears of bliss — someone [among them] presents.[^303-19]

**33.** The children are all skilled in music and poetry;
one after another [they] enact all the pastimes in various ways.[^303-20]

**34.** With dance, song [and] movement they enchant the people of the world;
choked with prema, the children all speak.

**35.** The children dance most charmingly;
seeing the dance, men and women are spellbound.[^303-21]

**36.** Having danced, turning round, they speak sweet words:
they enact that pastime in the order of the Bhagavata.[^303-22]

**37.** Then, hearing Krishna's harsh words,
heads bowed, sighing, [the gopis] speak.[^303-23]

**38.** Their lips dried up; all weep;
their garments were soaked with tears, [the tears] washed their feet.[^303-24]

**39.** Falling at [His] feet, they speak sweet words:
"Hear, Prabhu, ocean of mercy, O Bhagavan!

**40.** Your flute calls all of us by name;
we could not stay at home — [our] hearts were distraught.

**41.** Leaving household affairs, sons, property [and] wealth,
we came to the forest at night to see [Your] feet.

**42.** Your flute called us and brought [us here];
and now You say: 'Go home, all of you, return.'

**43.** All the rules of the Vedas that You have told us —
[I] shall tell their explanation; listen, O Vamshidhara.[^303-25]

**44.** The four Vedas meditate on Your feet,
and yet they cannot see this treasure — the feet.

**45.** The feet on which Indra and the other gods, the best of sages and others, meditate —
those unattainable feet we have today obtained by good fortune.[^303-26]

**46.** Leaving such feet, what have we to do at home?
Without You, may a thunderbolt strike every other happiness![^303-27]

**47.** You are wealth, You are kin, You are friend [and] husband;
apart from these feet I know nothing.

**48.** All the rules of the Vedas that You have told us —
service to the husband, service to the guru, the consideration of one's own dharma —[^303-28]

**49.** [yet] You are the husband of all, the life of the world;
You abide in all beings, divine Narayana.

**50.** You are the destroyer of all, the sustainer of all;
knowing [this], the gopis do not leave Your feet.[^303-29]

**51.** Many austerities I diligently performed;
that is why the gopis have obtained Your feet.[^303-30]

**52.** The ill-fated gopis are utterly wretched;
the one hope of all [of them] is Your two feet.

**53.** Without these feet the gopi does not live even a moment;
we have entered [Your] shelter, leaving all delusion.[^303-31]

**54.** Without You the gopi has no hope of home;
leaving all happiness, I have made You my support.

**55.** If in this Bhagavan will not show mercy,
the gopi will surely perish — of this there is no doubt."[^303-32]

**56.** Hearing the gopis' exceedingly firm words,
the Lotus-eyed One, smiling, called the gopis.[^303-33]

**57.** Rejoicing, the gopis surrounded Gopala;
in that same mood the children all dance in the rasa.[^303-34]

**58.** Around the circle, on all four sides, is sankirtana;
in the middle the children dance in various ways.

**59.** Whatever music there is on earth —
all, joined together, sounds in merriment.[^303-35]

**60.** All the happiness of Vrindavana became manifest;
seeing [it], all the people are seized with great awe.[^303-36]

**61.** Rasika's glory is altogether a wondrous tale;
all say: "Rasika is a second Narayana."[^303-37]

**62.** The pastimes that he displayed at every moment
could not be described even with ten million mouths.[^303-38]

**63.** By his grace I have described a little —
what the son of Achyuta, abiding in [my] heart, tells.[^303-39]

**64.** The Rasika-mangala is supreme, full of sweetness;
hearing it, all living beings, cross over [the age of] Kali.[^303-40]

**65.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the third lahari, called "The Description of the Rasa."*[^303-41]

[^303-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading («তৃতীয়-লহরী»), in italics without a number. Raga Kamoda (*kāmoda*) — Dakshina, lahari 9, note 1. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাস-বর্ণন-নাম তৃতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsa-barṇana*) — "The Description of the Rasa". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^303-2]: The ghosha reads in the 1941 edition: *dhanya re dhanya rādhāśyāma saṅga / amiya-sāgare kata bāṛila taraṅga*; "union" — *saṅga*, lit. "company, togetherness"; "nectar" — *amiya* (= *amṛta*). This lahari describes the rasa of Radha and Krishna. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the rasa-lila is a pastime of the Lord's internal energy (the hladini-shakti), pure prema, having nothing in common with mundane love: kama is the desire to please one's own senses, prema is the desire to give joy to Krishna; they differ as iron differs from gold (CC, Adi 4). Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati taught that the rasa-lila must not be understood with the mundane mind or imitated; one hears of it with faith under the guidance of pure devotees (cf. Pashchima, lahari 2, note 7). Here the rasa is enacted by boys as a sacred performance following the text of the Bhagavata (17, 31).

[^303-3]: "The refuge of the helpless" — *anātha-śaraṇa*. "The friend of Vallabha's life" — *ballabha-jībanabandhu*: Vallabha ("the beloved") is apparently Krishna, Gopivallabha (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 2); it may also be taken as "the beloved, the friend of [our] life". Durika is Shyamananda's mother (Purva, lahari 1, note 11). On how the author exalts Shyamananda — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^303-4]: "Beautifully laid out" (2) — *subandhāna*. "Sandbank" — *pulina*: a sandy riverbank; cf. the sandbank of the Yamuna, the place of the rasa in the Bhagavata (10.29.45; 20 below). The Suvarnarekha is the river on whose bank Gopivallabhapur stands (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 16).

[^303-5]: Cf. Bhag. 10.33.3: the demigods in their celestial chariots watch the rasa (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 33). Rasikendra is Rasika.

[^303-6]: "Horns" — *biṣāṇa*: according to the editor's footnote. "With the sound" — *cahale*: according to the editor's footnote, "with sound". "Shakes" — *kampabān*. Dundubhis (5, 7) are large drums, kettledrums (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 14). "Dulu-dulu" (7) is onomatopoeia; "trembles" — *tharahara*.

[^303-7]: The full moon of Vaishakha — the spring rasa (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 12). "That night is [like] eternity, there is no limit to it" — *cirakāla sei rātra nāhi tā'ra sīmā*; cf. Bhag. 10.33.38: the night of the rasa lasted a night of Brahma.

[^303-8]: The wish-fulfilling tree (10) — *kalpataru*: apparently the tree in the middle of the circle of the rasa (cf. Pashchima, lahari 1: the Deities by the wish-fulfilling tree at the eight corners of the circle). "Went up onto it" — *tā'ra madhye … giẏā*, lit. "going into its midst". "Remained" — *haila sannidhāna*. "Bent in three places" — *tribhaṅgima chānde*: the form of Krishna bent at the neck, waist and knee. In the performance Krishna is played by a boy (Pashchima, lahari 2, 47).

[^303-9]: "Murali" — the flute. "Gopis" — in the 1941 edition *gopā* (= *gopī*). Cf. Bhag. 10.29.3–4.

[^303-10]: "Bowing His head" — *heṭa māthā haiẏā*. "Leaning" — *āujiẏā*: according to the editor's footnote, "resting against". "Displeased" (15) — *birasa*. "Drawing on the ground" — *bhūmi lekhi*: cf. Bhag. 10.29.29 (the gopis, heads bowed, draw on the ground with their feet).

[^303-11]: "Sobbing" — *usasi usasi*. "Unaware of their bodies" — *nāhi deha-jñāna*. "The Lord — God, Bhagavan" — *prabhu deba bhagabān*: Krishna (in the performance, the boy playing Krishna).

[^303-12]: "In the order of the Bhagavata, according to its every rule" — *bhāgabata-anukrame yathā prati bidhi*: Rasika staged the rasa as a performance, following the text of the Bhagavata in order (10.29–33; cf. 31). "The treasury of virtues" — *guṇanidhi*.

[^303-13]: 18–25 are Krishna's words, a retelling of Bhag. 10.29.18–27. "To the forest" — *araṇa* (= *araṇya*). "Anxiously" (19) — *utkaṇṭhite*.

[^303-14]: "The children are crying" (21) — cf. Bhag. 10.29.22. 23–24 — cf. Bhag. 10.29.24–25. "As Vishnu" — *biṣṇu sama*. "Wander" — *bhrami bula*. According to the Bhagavata and Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, with these words Krishna tests the gopis and reveals the depth of their prema, which has left everything for His sake (note 2).

[^303-15]: "All [the rasikas] who are like Rasika" — *rasika samāna saba*: understood as Rasika's companions, akin to him in their taste for the rasa; it may also be taken as "all, like Rasika, together with Rasika". 26–30 describe the kirtana and music around the performance.

[^303-16]: Pakhoyaj (*pākhoẏāja*) is the pakhavaj, a double-headed drum; the dampha is a frame drum (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 23); the mridanga and dhol are drums. "Raised a thunder" — *karila tumula*. After the first line of 27 the 1941 edition has «॥» instead of «।». Vina, venu, murali — a stringed instrument and flutes; the upanga (*upāṅga*) is apparently a wind instrument; the svara-mandala is a kind of zither (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 23).

[^303-17]: The kapinasha is a kind of vina; the saranga is a bowed instrument; the pinaka is a stringed instrument (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 23); the kinnari (*kinnarī*) is a kind of vina; the rabab is a stringed instrument; the madol (*mādola*) is a drum; the kansi (*kā̃si*) is a bronze gong (cymbal); the muchung (*mucuṅga*) is a jew's harp; the mahuri is a reed wind instrument of Utkala (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 14); kartal and mandiras are small cymbals. "The sweet panchama" — *pañcama rasāla*: understood as the fifth note of the scale (panchama), sounding especially sweet; it may also be taken as the name of an instrument. "Surrounding the gopis" — *gopī beṛi*: around the boys playing the gopis. "In many ways" — *bahu parakāra*.

[^303-18]: The five chapters on the rasa are the rasa-panchadhyaya, Bhagavata 10.29–33. "Someone sings" — *ke gāẏa*. "They have the boys enact the lila" — *līlā śiśure karāẏa*. Couplet 31 is the last and complete; begins with ॥32॥.

[^303-19]: Continuation of lahari 3; begins with ॥ 32 ॥. "Gait… posture… conduct" — *gati… bhaṅgī… ācaraṇa*: the boys reproduce the bearing and movements of Krishna and the gopis, following the one who sings the five chapters on the rasa from the Bhagavata (31; Bhag. 10.29–33). "Presents" — *nibedaẏa*, lit. "offers, presents". "Someone" — *kona jana*: it can also be understood as "each one". On the rasa as pure prema and on the boys' performance, see note 2 (cf. Dakshina, lahari 5, note 22).

[^303-20]: "Skilled" — *parabīṇa* (= *prabīṇa*). "In music and poetry" — *saṅgīta-sāhitye*: in singing and in the poetic (dramatic) art.

[^303-21]: "Are spellbound" — *moha pāẏa*, lit. "fall into a swoon".

[^303-22]: "Turning round" — *phiri*. "In the order of the Bhagavata" — *bhāgabata anukrama*: in 18–56 the author retells Bhag. 10.29.18–42 — Krishna's speech to the gopis (18–25; 10.29.18–27) and their reply (37–55; 10.29.29–41).

[^303-23]: "Harsh words" — *niṣṭhura bākya*: Krishna tells the gopis to return home to their husbands (18–25). "Heads bowed" — *heṭa māthe*.

[^303-24]: "With tears" — *lohe* (*loha*, "tears", = *lora*).

[^303-25]: Vamshidhara (*baṃśīdhara*) — "the Holder of the flute", a name of Krishna. "The rules of the Vedas" — *beda bidhi*: Krishna's instruction on a wife's duty (23–25). "Explanation" — *bibaraṇa*. "[I] shall tell" — *kahi*: the gopis speak now in the plural, now in the singular (cf. 47, 51, 54).

[^303-26]: "Indra and the other gods, the best of sages and others" — *debendrādi munīndrādi*. "Meditate" — *bhābe*. "Unattainable" — *durlabhe*, "hard to obtain".

[^303-27]: "May a thunderbolt strike" — *paṛu bāja*, lit. "may thunder fall": a curse.

[^303-28]: 48–50 form one thought: cf. Bhag. 10.29.32–33 — the gopis reply that the instruction on a wife's duty towards her husband and relatives is fulfilled in service to Krishna Himself, the Soul and the beloved of all. "The consideration of one's own dharma" — *sbadharmma bicāre*.

[^303-29]: "Destroyer" — *harttā*: it can also be understood as "the One who takes away [everything]". "Sustainer" — *pālana*, lit. "maintenance".

[^303-30]: "I performed" — *sādhinu*, first person.

[^303-31]: "Does not live" — *jiẏe*. "Even a moment" — *tileka*. "Leaving all delusion" — *chāṛi saba mohe*: it can also be understood as "leaving all attachments".

[^303-32]: "The gopi will surely perish" — *abaśya maribe gopī*: cf. Bhag. 10.29.35 — the gopis say they will give up their bodies in the fire of separation. "There is no doubt" — *ithe nāhi āna*, lit. "in this there is nothing else".

[^303-33]: Cf. Bhag. 10.29.42. The Lotus-eyed One (*kamalalocana*) is Krishna.

[^303-34]: Gopala is Krishna. "In that same mood" — *sei bhābe*: the children represent how the gopis surround Krishna and dance with Him.

[^303-35]: "Joined together" — *eka mela kari*. "In merriment" — *kutūhale*.

[^303-36]: "Great awe" — *mahātrāsa*, lit. "great fear": understood as reverent trembling at the sight of a wonder.

[^303-37]: "A second Narayana" — the rapturous words of the onlookers (cf. Pashchima 2, 38: "a partial incarnation", and note 28 there). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 26; Purva, lahari 1, note 69); his guru Shyamananda is a servant of Radha and Krishna (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^303-38]: "Displayed" — *karilena*: the subject is not named; understood as Rasika (61). "With ten million mouths" — *koṭī mukhe*. The second line lit. "even describing with ten million mouths, that play would not come out [fully]".

[^303-39]: "By his grace" — *tā̃ra anugrahe*. The son of Achyuta is Rasika (Achyuta is his father; Purva, lahari 3, note 5). Cf. Pashchima 1, 66 and note 46 there: the author ascribes his inspiration to Rasika in his heart. "I have described" — *karilu barṇana*.

[^303-40]: "Full of sweetness" — *rasāla*, "juicy, full of rasa". "Cross over" — *tara*: understood as an imperative; it can also be understood as "cross over" in the third person ("all living beings cross").

[^303-41]: The colophon is: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাস-বর্ণন-নাম তৃতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsa-barṇana*) — "The Description of the Rasa".


## Lahari 4. The Description of the Rasa-yatra

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; at Sri Gopivallabhapur, as in a second Vrindavana, Rasika continues the Rasa-yatra, and the boys, in the order of the Bhagavata, represent how Krishna hides from the proud gopis, taking one gopi away with Him, how the gopis search for Him through the forests, questioning the trees, in their absorption enact His pastimes, find the chosen one whom He has left, and all together sing of Him; all say Rasika was born of a portion of Narayana; when Rasika comes from his house to the place of the rasa, a cobra bites him on the foot; he tells no one anything and all night watches the rasa in bliss, the snake perishes in the crowd, trampled to dust, and in the morning two fangs are taken out of his foot, and the poison vanishes without any charms; the author glorifies Rasika and promises prema-bhakti to the hearers of the Rasika-mangala*

*The fourth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^304-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna is a treasury of virtues,*
*the refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the deliverer of all!
Be merciful, so that I may compose [a song of your] glory.[^304-2]

**2.** Thus at the place [called] Sri Gopivallabhapur
[Rasika] manifested the rasa, as though in a second Vrindavana.[^304-3]

**3.** What beauty of the circle [of the rasa] — it cannot be told!
What dance and song, what Krishna-sankirtana!

**4.** What majesty in the dance of all the boys!
What attire, what ornaments on all the people![^304-4]

**5.** What harmonious music — a wondrous tale!
What sweet sound, enchanting the world!

**6.** What dundubhi drums, thundering mightily!
What a jewelled throne, what a splendid tree![^304-5]

**7.** Thus [he] manifested the Rasa-yatra;
Rasikendra, the jewel, ever performs [his] pastimes.[^304-6]

**8.** Thus all became intoxicated with the taste of the rasa;
all the people were immersed in bliss without end.[^304-7]

**9.** The children, holding each other's hands, circle closely,
as though the women of Vraja were sporting around Krishna.[^304-8]

**10.** In manifold happiness [they] passed [the time] in the taste of the great rasa;
one after another the children dance in jubilation.[^304-9]

**11.** At times, playfully, they tell the pastimes of the Bhagavata —
how Krishna [and] the wives of Vraja played.[^304-10]

**12.** Those movements of the body the children reproduce playfully;
seeing [it], the people of the three worlds are amazed.

**13.** At times the children, in the mood of the gopis, say everything [as it was]:
"We have completely subdued Krishna."[^304-11]

**14.** Hearing of the gopis' pride, Krishna disappeared;
after a moment the gopis realized: "Where has Krishna gone?"[^304-12]

**15.** Not seeing Krishna, the gopis lost consciousness;
all began to search [for Him] diligently.

**16.** One fortunate gopi named Vrindavati
Krishna led away, making [her His] companion.[^304-13]

**17.** Seeking the footprints of the two,
all the gopis, searching, wander from forest to forest.[^304-14]

**18.** Krishna's gait, smile, glance, speech —
remembering them again and again, the gopis weep aloud.[^304-15]

**19.** Thinking of those pastimes full of the taste of the rasa, the young [gopis]
wander through the forest in love, deeply afflicted.[^304-16]

**20.** In the forests of ashvattha, kurubaka, ashoka,
in the groves of naga, punnaga, champaka, tulasi[^304-17]

**21.** [they] asked: "Have you seen the Lord of our life on this path?
He has gone, leaving us all, making [us] helpless."

**22.** Mallika, malati, jati, yuthi — from forest to forest —
all [the gopis] say: "Have you seen Narayana on this path?"[^304-18]

**23.** Going into the mango grove, the gopis ask each [tree];
in the forests of piyala, panasa, ashana, pomegranate:

**24.** "Have you seen the son of Nanda going along this path?"
Asking, [they] looked along the path for Krishna, the treasure of [their] life.[^304-19]

**25.** In the forests of jambu, bel, kadamba, bakula — from forest to forest,
on the bank of the Yamuna the gopis search from forest to forest.

**26.** The gopis ask everyone: "Where has Krishna gone?
Tell me, all of you, have you seen my son of Nanda?"[^304-20]

**27.** Saying [this] again and again, the gopis lost consciousness;
becoming one in spirit with Him, all the gopis search [for Him].[^304-21]

**28.** All the pastimes that Bhagavan performed in Vraja
the gopis enact, [their] consciousness filled with Krishna.[^304-22]

**29.** One says: "I destroyed Putana";
some gopi sucks the breast, holding on firmly.[^304-23]

**30.** "I overturned the cart," says someone;
some gopi, rolling on the ground, cries.

**31.** One says: "I slew Trinavarta";
another says: "I destroyed the wicked Baka."

**32.** "I am Krishna," says some gopi;
the flute sounds, a gentle smile, an unhurried gait.[^304-24]

**33.** Some gopi, turning her garment over her left hand,
calls everyone and says: "I have lifted Mandara!

**34.** What can King Indra, lord of the gods, do —
a terrible storm [and] downpour, as much as his power [allows]?"[^304-25]

**35.** Another gopi says: "I am the Subduer of Kaliya;
my name is Destroyer of the wicked, Slayer of the evil."

**36.** Another gopi, putting her hand to her mouth, calls everyone:
"I have destroyed the forest fire — look, every one of you!"[^304-26]

**37.** One gopi, tying her garment at her waist, cries out:
"Playfully I broke the yamala-arjuna [trees]!"[^304-27]

**38.** Another says: "Blessed is the life of that gopi
whom the Lord of [our] life has taken away [with Him]!"[^304-28]

**39.** "Beside the footprints of Krishna are the footprints of that gopi;
blessed is the gopi — she has subdued the son of Nanda!

**40.** [He] whose feet Lakshmi ever holds in her heart —
[that] divine Narayana sported with the gopi in seclusion."[^304-29]

**41.** Thus, seeking [Krishna and enacting] Krishna's pastimes,
all the cowherd women wander from forest to forest.[^304-30]

**42.** Then the gopi whom Krishna had taken away,
thinking of what lay deep in her heart, said to Krishna:[^304-31]

**43.** "I cannot walk; listen, Narayana."
Krishna says: "Sit on [My] shoulder, O gopi."

**44.** Going a little way, Krishna disappeared;
the gopi fell face down on that [very] spot.[^304-32]

**45.** Lamenting, she weeps, uttering Krishna's name;
hearing the weeping, all came and joined [her].[^304-33]

**46.** With body, mind and speech becoming one in spirit with Him,
the gopis sing of Krishna's virtues, remembering [Him].[^304-34]

**47.** Thus all the children, with manifold delight,
[enacted] the pastimes one by one in the order of the Bhagavata.

**48.** That gait, that posture, that conduct,
the movements of the body [they] show wondrously.[^304-35]

**49.** All the children are most skilled in dance;
seeing [them], all the assembly is amazed.

**50.** All the pastimes that Krishna [and] the gopis performed in the taste of the rasa,
all the children reproduce in every detail.[^304-36]

**51.** All say: "Vrindavana has become visible before our eyes;
the son of Achyuta was born of a portion of Narayana."[^304-37]

**52.** Blessed is the fortune of the earth, blessed is this place,
where Rasikendra-chandra dwelt![^304-38]

**53.** At this time Rasikendra-chandra, from his house,
with joy in his heart came to the place of the rasa.[^304-39]

**54.** There was a cobra there;
that snake bit Rasika on the foot.[^304-40]

**55.** The most wicked [snake] bit with tremendous force;
two fangs broke off and remained in the flesh.[^304-41]

**56.** A stream of blood began to flow from the foot;
amazed, [Rasika] remembered Krishna.[^304-42]

**57.** His companions brought lamps [and] look:
in the press of the people the snake had given up its life.[^304-43]

**58.** People without number; by the blows of [their] feet
the snake's body, turned to dust, was scattered in all directions.[^304-44]

**59.** Rasikendra-mahashaya went on to the place of the rasa,
saying nothing to anyone, [though] the poison [was] burning.[^304-45]

**60.** At the place of the rasa he remains in great bliss, in joy [in] Krishna;
four praharas passed — [and] no suffering at all.[^304-46]

**61.** All night, rejoicing in the sight of the rasa,
the son of Achyuta delights in the dance [and] song.[^304-47]

**62.** In the morning all saw on the foot:
[there were] two fangs, and blood was flowing without stopping.

**63.** All carefully drew out the fangs;
Rasika's pastime amazes the three worlds.[^304-48]

**64.** He let no one charm away [the poison] — [and] the poison vanished;
seeing [this] manifestation of Rasika, all are amazed.[^304-49]

**65.** The greatness of Rasika cannot be told at all;
"[He is] a part of Narayana," all the people sing.[^304-50]

**66.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.[^304-51]

**67.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourth lahari, called "The Description of the Rasa-yatra."*[^304-52]

[^304-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading («চতুর্থ-লহরী»), in italics without a number. The raga in the 1941 edition is *nārānī gauṛā*, i.e. Narayani-gauda (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Dakshina, laharis 5 and 16, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাসযাত্রা-বর্ণন-নাম চতুর্থ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsayātrā-barṇana*) — "The Description of the Rasa-yatra". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^304-2]: "The deliverer of all" — *akhilatāraṇa*. The second line is as in Dakshina, lahari 16, 1.

[^304-3]: "Manifested" — *prakāśilā*; the subject is not named; understood as Rasika (cf. 7 and lahari 3). The account continues of the Rasa-yatra opened on the spring full moon of Vaishakha (Pashchima 2, note 4). On the rasa-lila and the Rasa-yatra, see Pashchima 2, note 7, and Pashchima 3, note 2: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the rasa is a manifestation of the gopis' pure prema, in which there is not a trace of mundane desire (kama; cf. CC, Adi 4); Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati warned against any mundane understanding of these pastimes. The boys represent the pastimes of Krishna and the gopis as a sacred performance — a glorification of the Lord's pastimes, not an imitation of Krishna (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 22).

[^304-4]: "Majesty" — *garimā*. "On all the people" — *sarbbajanā*: it can also be understood as "on all the participants".

[^304-5]: Dundubhis are large kettledrums. "Splendid tree" — *tarubara*, "best of trees": the wish-fulfilling tree in the middle of the circle of the rasa (Pashchima 1, 59–61, note 41).

[^304-6]: "Rasikendra, the jewel" — *rasikendramaṇi*. "Performs [his] pastimes" — *karena bilāsa*.

[^304-7]: "Intoxicated" — *bhora* (*bhor*): "drunk, absorbed". "Without end" — *nāi ora*.

[^304-8]: "Closely" — *ghane*. "Women of Vraja" — *brajāṅganā*. "Sporting" — *biharaṇe*.

[^304-9]: "Passed [the time]" — *bañcilena*. "One after another" — *eke āre*.

[^304-10]: "Playfully" — *kouutuke* (= *kautuke*). "Wives of Vraja" — *brajabadhū*: the gopis.

[^304-11]: "Say everything [as it was]" — *kahe sarbbakathā*. "Completely" — *sarbbathā*. Cf. Bhag. 10.29.47–48: the gopis became proud, and Krishna disappeared.

[^304-12]: "Realized" — *jānilā*, lit. "knew, understood": understood as "noticed that Krishna had gone".

[^304-13]: Vrindavati — in the Bhagavata this gopi is not named (Bhag. 10.30.28: "She has truly worshipped (*ārādhitaḥ*) Him"); according to the Gaudiya Vaishnava interpretation she is Sri Radha. The name "Vrindavati" for her is unusual; perhaps the author so calls Radha as the mistress of Vrindavana. "Fortunate" — *bhāgyabatī*. "Making [her His] companion" — *kariẏā saṃhati*.

[^304-14]: Cf. Bhag. 10.30.25–28: the gopis find Krishna's footprints and beside them the footprints of the chosen gopi. "Wander" — *bharame* (= *bhrame*).

[^304-15]: Cf. Bhag. 10.30.2. "Remembering" — *samari* (= *smari*).

[^304-16]: "Those pastimes full of the taste of the rasa" — *rāsa-rasa bihāra*. "The young [gopis]" — *yubatī*. "In love" — *anurāge* (anuraga — ever-increasing loving attachment). "Deeply afflicted" — *ati duḥkhamati*.

[^304-17]: 20–25 — cf. Bhag. 10.30.5–9: the gopis ask the trees and creepers about Krishna. Ashvattha — the sacred fig; kurubaka — a shrub with red flowers; ashoka — a tree with red flowers; naga (nagakeshara) and punnaga — trees with fragrant flowers; champaka — a tree with golden fragrant flowers; tulasi — the sacred plant dear to Krishna.

[^304-18]: Mallika, malati, jati, yuthi (*mallikā, mālatī, jāti, yūthī*) are kinds of jasmine. Narayana — so the gopis in the author's text call Krishna (cf. 40, 43).

[^304-19]: Piyala (*piẏāla*, *priyāla*) — a tree with edible fruit; panasa (*panasa*) — the jackfruit tree; ashana (*aśana*) — a forest tree; "pomegranate" — *dāṛimba*. "Asking, looked" — *puchiẏe dekhila*: it can also be understood as "asked: have [you] seen…".

[^304-20]: "My son of Nanda" — *nandabālā*, lit. "Nanda's boy".

[^304-21]: "Becoming one in spirit with Him" — *tadātmikā*: Bhag. 10.30.3, 43 (*tad-ātmikāḥ*) — the gopis, wholly absorbed in Krishna, begin to behave as He does.

[^304-22]: "[Their] consciousness filled with Krishna" — *kṛṣṇamaẏa jñāna*. 29–37 — cf. Bhag. 10.30.14–23: the gopis in their absorption enact Krishna's pastimes (one as Putana, another as Krishna sucking her breast, and so on).

[^304-23]: Putana — the rakshasi who came to kill the infant Krishna with her poisoned breast (Bhag. 10.6). "Some gopi" — *kona gopā*. The gopis speak in Krishna's person, in the masculine.

[^304-24]: "The flute sounds" — *beṇu sphure*. "A gentle smile" — *mandasmita*. "An unhurried gait" — *manthara gamana*.

[^304-25]: 33–34: "Mandara" — *mandara*: the mountain with which the ocean was churned; here apparently instead of Govardhana, which Krishna lifted to protect Vraja from Indra's downpour (Bhag. 10.25; cf. 10.30.20: a gopi raised the edge of her garment, as Krishna the hill). "Turning… over" — *pālaṭi*, lit. "turning over". Indra is the king of the gods (*surapati*).

[^304-26]: Kaliya — the serpent subdued by Krishna in the Yamuna (Bhag. 10.16). "Putting her hand to her mouth" — *mukhe kara diẏā*: Krishna swallowed the forest fire (Bhag. 10.19). "Every one of you" — *pratyeke*, lit. "each one"; "before your eyes". (not translated).

[^304-27]: Yamala-arjuna — the two arjuna trees that the little Krishna, tied by Yashoda to a mortar, uprooted (Bhag. 10.10). "Tying her garment at her waist" — *kaṭite basana bā̃dhi*. "Cries out" — *ḍāke*, lit. "calls".

[^304-28]: 38–40 — cf. Bhag. 10.30.28–34. "The Lord of [our] life" — *prāṇanātha*.

[^304-29]: Lakshmi — the consort of Narayana, the goddess of fortune; even she longs for Krishna's feet. "Ever" — *anukṣaṇa*. "Sported… in seclusion" — *ekānte ramila*. The first line is understood as referring to Narayana, that is, Krishna.

[^304-30]: "Seeking [Krishna and enacting] Krishna's pastimes" — *kṛṣṇalīlā anbeṣaṇa kari*, lit. "searching out Krishna's pastimes"; understood in the light of 27–37. "Cowherd women" — *gopanārī*. "Wander" — *bhrami bule*.

[^304-31]: 42–45 — cf. Bhag. 10.30.36–40: the chosen gopi, becoming proud, asks Krishna to carry her, and He disappears. "What lay deep in her heart" — *marmmakathā*, lit. "a word [from] the depths of the heart".

[^304-32]: "Face down" — *mukha māṛi*, lit. "pressing the face": understood as "fell on her face"; the reading is unclear.

[^304-33]: "Weeping" — *kāndanā*. "Joined [her]" — *milena*.

[^304-34]: Cf. Bhag. 10.30.43–44: the gopis, one in spirit with Krishna (*tad-ātmikāḥ*), sing of His virtues. "With body, mind and speech" — *kāẏamanobākye*.

[^304-35]: The first line is as in lahari 3, 32. "Wondrously" — *ati bilakṣaṇa*, "extraordinarily".

[^304-36]: "In the taste of the rasa" — *rāsarase*. "In every detail" — *aśeṣa-biśeṣe*.

[^304-37]: "Has become visible before our eyes" — *sākṣāta haila*. "The son of Achyuta" is Rasika (Purva, lahari 3, note 5). "Was born of a portion of Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa-aṃśe janma*: the rapturous words of the onlookers (cf. lahari 3, 61: "a second Narayana"). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 26; Purva, lahari 1, note 69); his guru Shyamananda is a servant of Radha and Krishna (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^304-38]: "Blessed is the fortune of the earth" — *dhanya bhāgya pṛthibīra*. "Dwelt" — *biśrāma karilā*, lit. "rested, had his abode". Rasikendra-chandra is Rasika ("the moon Rasikendra").

[^304-39]: "Came" — *bije kaila*: respectful, of a ceremonial arrival (Pashchima 2, note 5). "From his house" — *gṛha haite*. 53–64 — an account not found in BR 15.

[^304-40]: "Cobra" — *gokṣura* (*gokhurā*), the spectacled cobra; *nāga* — snake. "One" — *ekai*. "Snake" — *sarapa* (= *sarpa*).

[^304-41]: "The most wicked" — *duṣṭabara*, lit. "the best of the wicked". "With tremendous force" — *mahāteje*.

[^304-42]: "Amazed" — *camatkāra haiẏā*. "Remembered Krishna" — *kaila kṛṣṇa-saṅaraṇe*. The subject is not named; understood as Rasika.

[^304-43]: "Lamps" — *deuṭī* (torches, lamps). "In the press of the people" — *manuṣya-gahale*: *gahala* is understood as "crowd, throng"; the reading is unclear.

[^304-44]: "People without number" — *samuccaẏa nāhi loka* (cf. lahari 3, 5). "By the blows of [their] feet" — *caraṇera ghāte*. "In all directions" — *cāribhite*.

[^304-45]: Mahashaya is a respectful title. "[Though] the poison [was] burning" — *biṣa tejomaẏa*, lit. "the poison — fiery (potent)".

[^304-46]: "In joy [in] Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-sukhe*. A prahara is a quarter of the night or day, about three hours: four praharas are the whole night.

[^304-47]: "All night" — *cira niśi*. "Delights" — *biharena*.

[^304-48]: "Carefully" — *kariẏā yatana*. "Amazes the three worlds" — *camatkāra tribhubana*.

[^304-49]: "Charm away" — *jhāṛite*: *jhāṛā* is the folk healer's "removal" of poison by incantations and fanning. "Manifestation" — *prakāśa*: Rasika's manifested power. The author describes a miracle, exalting Rasika; this account is not in BR 15.

[^304-50]: Continuation of lahari 4; begins with ॥ 65 ॥. "Cannot be told at all" — *kichu kahana nā yāẏa*. "A part of Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa-aṃśa*: the rapturous words of the people, as in 51; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (note 37).

[^304-51]: "Friends" — *bandhugaṇa*. "Without delay" — *abilambe*. "The treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapremabhakti-dhana*.

[^304-52]: The colophon is: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাসযাত্রা-বর্ণন-নাম চতুর্থ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsayātrā-barṇana*) — "The Description of the Rasa-yatra".


## Lahari 5. The Completion of the Rasa-lila

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; following the order of the Bhagavata, the boys enact the gopis' lament for Krishna, His return, the consoling of the gopis and the dance of the rasa, and all call Rasika a partial incarnation; the next day, at the people's request, Rasika orders the rasa to be prepared again, but in the evening a storm breaks, and Shyamananda declares that the measure of the rasa is one night; in the morning a dadhi-kada is held with kirtana, in which Hridayananda dances; Rasika bows to Shyamananda, Hridayananda and the elders, embraces the Vaishnavas, sports in the waters of the Suvarnarekha, feeds and honours everyone and sends the guests off with honour; all praise Rasika, who gave prema-bhakti in every house; the author promises the listeners deliverance from the age of Kali*

*The fifth lahari.*

*Raga Kafi-bhatiyari.*[^305-1]
*Ghosha: "My heart, oh, pines for Shyama, [my] friend."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, renowned in the world!
Be merciful at every moment — I shall sing [his] deeds.[^305-2]

**2.** Thus Rasikendra manifests the rasa-lila;
seeing [it], gods and men are immersed in bliss.[^305-3]

**3.** The children enact the pastimes of the Sri Bhagavata —
with such movements of the body as the gopis in the dance.[^305-4]

**4.** All those words [of the gopis] they utter, lamenting;
all the people, seeing that dance, are spellbound.[^305-5]

**5.** Not finding Krishna, the gopis [are full of] wounded pride;
taking up that role, a child expounds [it].[^305-6]

**6.** The gopis ask everyone: "Where has Krishna gone?"
Not finding a trace [of Him], [they] lamented long.

**7.** All the virtues that Kanai showed from childhood
the gopis remember and weep — no one is conscious.[^305-7]

**8.** "From the poisoned water Gopala saved us,
[and] from the serpent, the rakshasa, the downpour, the irresistible wind;[^305-8]

**9.** from the bull demon You saved everyone.
You are not [merely] the son of Yashoda — [You are] the Lord of all![^305-9]

**10.** You are the Soul of all, the divine Bhagavan;
in this world [You are] the deliverance of the saintly.[^305-10]

**11.** Destroy the distress of the wives of Vraja:
show [us] Your moon-like face, O You who wear yellow!"[^305-11]

**12.** Thus, lamenting in various ways,
the wives of Vraja lamented exactly [as in the Bhagavata].[^305-12]

**13.** One by one the children enact all the pastimes;
seeing [this], men and women are amazed.

**14.** As the gopis poured out [their] entreaties to Krishna —
that pastime all the children show exactly.[^305-13]

**15.** [Prolonging] all these pastimes only a little, for sport,
[Krishna] gladdened the gopis beyond measure.[^305-14]

**16.** Krishna, the life of all, appears [to them];
seeing Krishna, the gopis regained [their] life.[^305-15]

**17.** One takes [His] hand in [her] hand, another [places His] arm on [her] shoulder;
one, with a light smile, asks for the betel chewed [by Him].[^305-16]

**18.** Some [He] won over by leaving nail-marks on the breast;
some [He] won over with the arrows of glances from beneath the brows.[^305-17]

**19.** One, biting her lip, stands at a distance;
another embraces [Him] with the greatest tenderness.[^305-18]

**20.** Thus the desire of all was fulfilled;
under the guise of wounded pride [the gopis] voiced something.[^305-19]

**21.** Hearing [these] clever words, the One who loves His devotees
dispelled all the doubts of the gopis.

**22.** Softening, the Beloved of the gopis says:
"You all never give up your crookedness.[^305-20]

**23.** I am always with you, in delight;
I have truly told you: [you are] My dear ones."[^305-21]

**24.** Having thus gladdened the gopis,
the Lord, the Lotus-eyed, began the rasa.[^305-22]

**25.** A beautiful sandbank, a grove on the bank of the Yamuna;
picking flowers, stringing garlands, [the gopis] adorned Gopala.

**26.** Thus Bhagavan manifests the rasa-lila:
each gopi — [and with her] Krishna, the abode of virtues.[^305-23]

**27.** Some gopi wins [Him] over with sweet speech,
some gopi wins [Him] over with sweet singing,

**28.** some gopi wins [Him] over with music full of flavour,
some gopi wins Damodara over with dance.[^305-24]

**29.** Some girl wins [Him] over with the play of her glances;
thus all the children enact many kinds of pastimes.[^305-25]

**30.** Holding hands, the children circle again and again;
the waist-bells [and] anklets sound without pause.[^305-26]

**31.** Most skilfully the children dance;
they enact that pastime in the order of the Bhagavata.

**32.** The steps [and] movements of the body cannot be described;
seeing the children's dance, all the people are spellbound.

**33.** On various instruments, with various music — in one tune;
dance, singing, movements of the body, the sweetest song.[^305-27]

**34.** In heaven, on earth and in the netherworlds [arose] "Glory, glory!";
staying in heaven, the gods shower flowers.

**35.** In mid-heaven the dundubhis sound again and again;
all the people were immersed in the great bliss of the rasa.[^305-28]

**36.** Thus [he] made the Rasa-yatra known to the world;
the son of Achyuta performs a wondrous pastime.[^305-29]

**37.** The splendour of Vrindavana, the pastimes of love for Krishna
the son of Achyuta made visible.[^305-30]

**38.** Seeing [this], all the people [were plunged] into an ocean of bliss;
all say: "Rasikendra is a partial incarnation."[^305-31]

**39.** Thus [he] held the rasa on a sweet night;
on the next day, expecting the rasa [again],[^305-32]

**40.** a multitude of people, seeing [him], all made a request:
"Today too have the rasa performed, O son of Achyuta!"

**41.** [He] was not inclined, yet at the words of all
[he] gave the order: "All you children, put on your costumes!"[^305-33]

**42.** Receiving the order, all dressed with care;
at that time a dreadful cloud covered the sky.

**43.** In the evening rain came with a great dreadful roar;
the earth trembles at the thunder of the cloud.

**44.** Strokes of lightning, storm and rain rage irresistibly;
until the fourth prahara the rain fell without ceasing.[^305-34]

**45.** Then Shyamananda Raya commanded:
"The measure [of the rasa] is one night; more is not fitting."[^305-35]

**46.** That word all accepted as authority;
on the morning after, they began the dadhi-kada.[^305-36]

**47.** Hundreds and hundreds of pots of curd with turmeric,
phagu, chuya and sandal [they] pour without measure.[^305-37]

**48.** Quickly bringing flowers [and] garlands of various kinds,
the crest-jewel of Rasikendras holds the dadhi-kada.[^305-38]

**49.** Musk, kunkuma, aragaja, saffron —
hundreds and hundreds of people, filling pots, take [them] in hand.[^305-39]

**50.** Some — curd [with] turmeric, some — sandal,
some — flowers, oil, chuya: hundreds and hundreds of people.

**51.** Hundreds of people offer garlands of fragrant flowers;
with garlands, sandal and the rest all were adorned.

**52.** Hundreds and hundreds of groups perform kirtana;
the sound of the mridangas [and] dundubhis touches the sky.[^305-40]

**53.** "Glory, glory!" — the cries of "Hari" thunder in bliss;
the circle of the earth took on the beauty of Vaikuntha.[^305-41]

**54.** The music, the roar of the dundubhis — most tremendous;
from the cries of countless people the earth sways.

**55.** People without count, dense cries of "Hari";
shingas, flutes, horns, many instruments are heard.[^305-42]

**56.** Sri Hridayananda Prabhu danced;
the third prahara came — all were amazed.[^305-43]

**57.** Thus [all] put the dadhi-kada on every limb;
all, holding hands, dance with various sports.

**58.** In the bliss of the taste of the rasa the fourth prahara passed;
in the evening the excellent Rasikendra brought [the festival] to completion.[^305-44]

**59.** Completing the sankirtana, Rasikendra Raya
fell flat with his body on the ground at Shyamananda's feet.[^305-45]

**60.** Then [he] bowed to Hridayananda;
the abode of virtues honoured all the elders.[^305-46]

**61.** With all the Vaishnavas [he] conversed;
in jubilation he embraced his companions.

**62.** Disciples, disciples of [their] disciples, and also servants [and] disciples —
then Rasikendra embraced all the people.[^305-47]

**63.** Having joyfully exchanged prostrations and embraces,
Rasika went to sport in the water.[^305-48]

**64.** The water of the Suvarnarekha is clear [and] deep;
a beautiful sandbank [and] groves adorn both banks.[^305-49]

**65.** Into that water Rasikendra Raya entered;
they splash water on one another, hand against hand, on the body.[^305-50]

**66.** Sporting in the water for a short while, [he] quickly returned;
he fed all the Vaishnavas.[^305-51]

**67.** [He] tore [cloth into] thousands upon thousands of kaupinas
[and], giving [them] to the multitude of Vaishnavas, took leave [of them].[^305-52]

**68.** With a steady [heart] he honoured all the elders
with coins, gold, sandal and the rest, garments, ornaments.[^305-53]

**69.** Then he honoured the brahmanas [and] sannyasis;
he sent off [with gifts] the rajas, the subjects, the residents of Vraja.[^305-54]

**70.** To all the [kirtana] groups he gave garments [and] ornaments;
then Rasikendra honoured his own people.[^305-55]

**71.** He sent off [with gifts] the dancing children:
garments, ornaments, decorations he put on [their] bodies.

**72.** Each one he sent off as befitted him;
all go away singing the virtues and fame of Rasika.

**73.** All the mahantas [and] Vaishnavas went to their own places,
reflecting in their minds on the fame and glory of Rasika.[^305-56]

**74.** All say: "Such a yatra we have never seen;
Rasika is not a human being — Krishnachandra is witness."[^305-57]

**75.** Even speaking with a hundred mouths, it cannot be told;
such a yatra [he] brought forth on earth.[^305-58]

**76.** Blessed, blessed is Rasikendra, blessed [his] mother [and] father;
blessed is the circle of the earth where [there was] such a yatra.

**77.** Such a yatra Rasikendra made known to the world,
by the sight of which people were delivered.

**78.** Thus Rasikendra on earth
gave prema-bhakti for Krishna in every house.

**79.** Day by day bhakti for Krishna arises more and more;
the son of Achyuta delivered tens of millions.[^305-59]

**80.** The holder of all virtues is Rasikendra-chandra,
whose glory gods [and] men sing.

**81.** What power have I to sing that glory?
Whatever the prince of Achyuta, dwelling in [my] heart, says —[^305-60]

**82.** in accordance with that I have described a little.
Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all you saintly ones.

**83.** In brief [I] have told a little of the rasa;
hearing [it], all people, cross over the [age of] Kali.[^305-61]

**84.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifth lahari, called "The Completion of the Rasa-lila."*[^305-62]

[^305-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading («পঞ্চম-লহরী»), in italics without a number. Lahari 5 begins. The raga in the 1941 edition is *kāphi bhāṭiẏāri*: Kafi and Bhatiyari are names of ragas; here apparently a combination of the two. The ghosha reads in the 1941 edition: *jhure re prāṇa śyāmabandhu lāgiẏā*; "pines" — *jhure*, "weeps, yearns"; *re* is an exclamation. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাসলীলা-সমাপন-নাম পঞ্চম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsalīlā-samāpana*) — "The Completion of the Rasa-lila". The whole lahari is; the summary line follows the 1941 edition.

[^305-2]: "Renowned in the world" — *bhubanabidita*. "At every moment" — *anukṣaṇa*. "Deeds" — *carita*: life, deeds (apparently Rasika's).

[^305-3]: The account of the Rasa-yatra at Gopivallabhapur continues (Pashchima, laharis 2–4): following the order of the Bhagavata, the boys enact the end of the rasa-lila — the gopis' song in separation, Krishna's return and the dance of the rasa (Bhag. 10.31–33). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the rasa is a pastime of the Lord's internal energy, the pure prema of the gopis, having nothing in common with mundane love: kama is the desire to please one's own senses, prema is the desire to give joy to Krishna (CC, Adi 4); Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati taught that these pastimes must not be understood with the mundane mind or imitated (see further Pashchima, lahari 3, note 2; lahari 2, note 7). The boys' performance is a glorification of the Lord's pastimes, not an imitation of Krishna (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 22). "Manifests" — *kare*, lit. "performs". "Immersed" — *magana*.

[^305-4]: "With such movements of the body" — *tena aṅgabhaṅgī*. "As the gopis in the dance" — *yena nṛtye gopīgaṇe*.

[^305-5]: "All those words" — 8–11: the gopis' song in separation (Bhag. 10.31, the "Gopi-gita"). "Are spellbound" — *moha pāẏa*, lit. "fall into a swoon" (cf. Pashchima, lahari 3, note 21).

[^305-6]: "Wounded pride" — *abhimāna*: the hurt pride of love. "Taking up that role" — *sei aṅga dhari*, lit. "taking that part (that role)". "Expounds" — *karaẏe bākhāna*.

[^305-7]: Kanai is an affectionate name of Krishna. "Virtues" — *guṇa*: here, His beneficent deeds (8–9). "Remember" — *saṅariẏā* (= *smariẏā*).

[^305-8]: 8–11 retell the "Gopi-gita" (Bhag. 10.31.3–6). Cf. Bhag. 10.31.3: "from perishing in the poisoned water, from the serpent-demon, from rain, wind, lightning and fire, from the bull, from the son of Maya…". The poisoned water is the Yamuna poisoned by the serpent Kaliya (Bhag. 10.15–16); the serpent is Aghasura (Bhag. 10.12); the downpour is the one sent by Indra (Bhag. 10.25); the wind is the demon Trinavarta (Bhag. 10.7). "Irresistible" — *durbbāra*.

[^305-9]: "The bull demon" — *ṣaṇḍāsura*, understood as *ṣaṇḍa-asura*, "the bull asura": Arishtasura, whom Krishna slew (Bhag. 10.36; cf. 10.31.3: *vṛṣa*). "You saved" — *rākhile*. The second line — cf. Bhag. 10.31.4: "You are not merely the son of a gopi — You are the witness in the hearts of all embodied beings." "The Lord of all" — *akhila īśvara*.

[^305-10]: "The Soul of all" — *akhilera ātmā*. "The deliverance of the saintly" — *sādhujana-paritrāṇa*: cf. Bhagavad-gita 4.8 (*paritrāṇāya sādhūnām*).

[^305-11]: Cf. Bhag. 10.31.6 (*vraja-janārti-han*, "O destroyer of the distress of the people of Vraja") and 10.31.2, 10.31.6 ("show us Your face"). "Distress" — *ārata* (= *ārti*). "You who wear yellow" — *pītabāsa*: Krishna in yellow garments (cf. Bhag. 10.32.2).

[^305-12]: "Exactly [as in the Bhagavata]" — *se sbarūpe*, lit. "in that [very] form": the boys who portray the wives of Vraja lament just as the gopis do in the Bhagavata (cf. 14).

[^305-13]: "Poured out entreaties" — *nibedana kaila*, "made supplication". "As" — *yatarūpe*, lit. "in all the ways in which". "Exactly" — *sbarūpe*.

[^305-14]: The subject is not named; understood as Krishna (16). "Only a little" — *kṣaṇeka*, lit. "for a moment". "For sport" — *kautuke*. "Beyond measure" — *atireke*.

[^305-15]: Cf. Bhag. 10.32.2–3. "The life of all" — *akhilera prāṇa*. "Regained [their] life" — *pāilā parāṇa* (*parāṇa* = *prāṇa*).

[^305-16]: 17–19 — cf. Bhag. 10.32.4–8. "Another [places His] arm on [her] shoulder" — *keha bāhe bāhu*, lit. "someone — arm on arm"; cf. Bhag. 10.32.4: another placed His arm on her shoulder. "Chewed betel" — *carbbita tāmbūla*: cf. Bhag. 10.32.5: one received in her joined palms the betel He had chewed — the Lord's remnants (prasada). "With a light smile" — *hāsya lahu*.

[^305-17]: The subject is not named; understood as Krishna ("some… some" — different gopis); it can also be understood that the gopis win Krishna over (cf. 27–29). "Nail-marks" — *nakharekha*; "on the breast" — *kuce*. "The arrows of glances from beneath the brows" — *bhuru cāhani biśikhe*. The translation is exact; on the rasa as pure prema, see note 3.

[^305-18]: Cf. Bhag. 10.32.7: one gopi, beside herself with loving anger, bit her lips and looked at Krishna as if wounding Him with her glances. "With the greatest tenderness" — *parama senehe* (*seneha* = *sneha*).

[^305-19]: "Under the guise of wounded pride" — *abhimāna chale*. Cf. Bhag. 10.32.16: with feigned resentment the gopis ask Krishna who reciprocates love in what way; His answer is 10.32.17–22. "Clever words" (21) — *cāturyyabāṇī*. "The One who loves His devotees" — *bhakata-batsala*.

[^305-20]: "Softening" — *sadaẏa haiẏā*, "becoming full of mercy". "The Beloved of the gopis" — *gopikā-ramaṇa*. "You all never give up your crookedness" — *tomā sabā kuṭilatā nā chāṛa kakhana*: the meaning is unclear; apparently an affectionate reproach to the gopis for their trick question (20); it can also be understood as "[I] never [show] crookedness towards you". Cf. Bhag. 10.32.20–22: Krishna says that He hid in order to intensify their love and that He is unable to repay them for their devotion.

[^305-21]: "In delight" — *kautuke*. "Truly" — *sbarūpe*. "My dear ones" — *nija priẏa*. Cf. Bhag. 10.32.21 ("do not be angry with Me, O dear ones, your Beloved").

[^305-22]: Cf. Bhag. 10.33.2. "Having gladdened" — *santoṣa kariẏā*. "The Lotus-eyed" — *kamalalocana*.

[^305-23]: Cf. Bhag. 10.33.3: Krishna, expanding Himself, stood between each pair of gopis. "The abode of virtues" — *guṇadhāma*.

[^305-24]: "Full of flavour" — *rasāla*. Damodara is a name of Krishna ("bound by the waist", Bhag. 10.9).

[^305-25]: "Girl" — *bālā*. "With the play of her glances" — *cāhani bhaṅgīte*. "Pastimes" — *khelā*.

[^305-26]: "Again and again" — *ghane ghane* (cf. 35). Waist-bells — *kiṅkiṇī*; anklets — *mañjīra*. "Without pause" — *saghane*. Cf. Bhag. 10.33.6.

[^305-27]: "In one tune" — *eka tāna*: in harmony, in unison.

[^305-28]: "In mid-heaven" — *arddhasbarge*, lit. "halfway to heaven". Dundubhis are large kettledrums (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 5). Cf. Bhag. 10.33.4: kettledrums sounded in the sky and the gods rained down flowers. "Were immersed" — *majila*.

[^305-29]: "Made known to the world" — *karila pracāra*, lit. "spread, proclaimed". The son of Achyuta is Rasika (Purva, lahari 3, note 5); *acyuta-kumāra*.

[^305-30]: "Splendour" — *baibhaba*. "The pastimes of love for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-prema-līlā*. "Made visible" — *dṛggocara karāila*. "The son of Achyuta" — *acyutera bālā*, lit. "Achyuta's boy".

[^305-31]: "A partial incarnation" — *aṃśa-abatāra*: the rapturous words of the people (cf. Pashchima, lahari 2, note 28; lahari 4, 51 and note 37). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation of the Lord; on how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "Into an ocean of bliss" — *ānande pāthāra*.

[^305-32]: "On a sweet night" — *madhura yāminī*. "Expecting the rasa [again]" — *rāsa karibāre anumāni*, lit. "supposing [there would be] a rasa held": the subject is unclear; understood as the people (40); it can also be understood as "[Rasika] intended to hold the rasa on the next day too". 39–40 form one sentence.

[^305-33]: "[He] was not inclined" — *mane nāhi laẏa*, lit. "the mind does not accept". "Put on your costumes" — *beśa kara*: dress for the performance (cf. Pashchima, lahari 2, 43–66).

[^305-34]: "Irresistibly" — *durabāra* (= *durbbāra*). "Until the fourth prahara" — *caturtha prahara*, lit. "the fourth prahara": understood as until the end of the night. A prahara is a quarter of the night or day, about three hours (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 46). "Without ceasing" — *anibāra*.

[^305-35]: Shyamananda Raya is Shyamananda (*rāẏa* is an honorific). "The measure [of the rasa] is one night" — *ekarātri pramāṇa*; "more is not fitting" — *āra nā yogāẏa*, lit. "more does not suit".

[^305-36]: "Accepted as authority" — *paramāṇa karila* (= *pramāṇa*). "On the morning after" — *tāhāra bihāna*. The dadhi-kada is a festive game in which the participants drench one another with curd mixed with turmeric and water and dance in this "mud", as at the Nandotsava (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 37).

[^305-37]: "Pots" — *hāṇḍī*. Phagu is a red powder (abir; Pashchima, lahari 2, note 36); chuya is a fragrant oil (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 19). "Without measure" — *apramite*.

[^305-38]: "Of various kinds" — *nānā bhānti*. "The crest-jewel of Rasikendras" — *rasikendra-cūṛāmaṇi*: Rasika. "Holds the dadhi-kada" — *dadhi kādā kare*.

[^305-39]: Kunkuma is saffron or a red powder for adornment; aragaja (*aragajā*) is a fragrant paste of sandal, aguru, musk and other substances; "saffron" — *keśara*. "Filling pots" — *hā̃ṛī pūri*.

[^305-40]: "Groups" — *sampradāẏa*: kirtana groups (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 17). The mridanga is a clay drum (khol). "Touches the sky" — *paraśe gagana*.

[^305-41]: "Thunder" — *cahala*: the meaning is approximate (in Pashchima, lahari 3, 6 the editor glosses *cahale* as "with the sound"; note 6 there). "The beauty of Vaikuntha" — *baikuṇṭhera śobhā*. "The circle of the earth" — *abanimaṇḍala*.

[^305-42]: "Without count" — *samuccaẏa nāhi* (cf. Pashchima, lahari 4, note 44). The shinga (*śiṅgā*) is a curved horn; "horns" — *biṣāna* (Pashchima, lahari 3, note 6). "Flutes" — *beṇu*.

[^305-43]: Hridayananda (Hridaya-Chaitanya) is Shyamananda's guru (Purva, lahari 1, note 13); "Prabhu" is an honorific. "Were amazed" — *camakita*. On the prahara, see note 34.

[^305-44]: "In the bliss of the taste of the rasa" — *rāsa-rasānande*. "In the evening" — *sandhyāte*. "Brought to completion" — *kailā pūraṇa*. "The excellent Rasikendra" — *rasikendrabara*.

[^305-45]: "Fell flat with his body on the ground" — *daṇḍabata kāẏa kṣiti*, lit. "[a bow like] a stick — the body to the ground". "At the feet" — *pāẏa*.

[^305-46]: "Elders" — *gurujana*: revered elders, teachers. "The abode of virtues" — *guṇadhāma*: Rasika.

[^305-47]: "Disciples of [their] disciples" — *anuśiṣya*. "Servants [and] disciples" — *bhṛtya śiṣyagaṇe*; it can also be understood as "servant-disciples". "Embraced" — *kole kaila*, lit. "took into his arms".

[^305-48]: "Prostrations and embraces" — *daṇḍabata kolākoli*. "To sport in the water" — *jalakeli*.

[^305-49]: The Suvarnarekha is the river on whose bank Gopivallabhapur stands (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 16; lahari 3, note 4). "Sandbank" — *pulina*.

[^305-50]: "On one another" — *eke āre*. "Hand against hand" — *hātāhāti*. "On the body" — *gāẏa*.

[^305-51]: "For a short while" — *kṣaṇe*. "He fed" — *bhojanādi karāila*, lit. "arranged the meal and so on".

[^305-52]: "Tore" — *cirilena*: tore (cloth) into strips. The kaupina is the loincloth of renunciants; in the 1941 edition *kouupinī*. "Multitude" — *samūha*. "Took leave" — *karila melānī*: sent [them] off with parting gifts.

[^305-53]: "With a steady [heart]" — *niścale*. "Coins" — *ṭaṅkā*: silver coins (rupees). "Elders" — *gurujana* (note 46).

[^305-54]: "Sent off [with gifts]" — *bidāẏa karila*: saw off with honours and presents. "The residents of Vraja" — *brajabāsī*: apparently Vaishnavas who had come to the Rasa-yatra from Vrindavana (cf. Pashchima, lahari 2, 13).

[^305-55]: "Groups" — *sampradā* (note 40). "His own people" — *ātmagaṇa*: relatives and his own circle.

[^305-56]: "Mahantas" — *mohānta*: heads of Vaishnava communities. "Fame and glory" — *yaśaḥkīrtti*.

[^305-57]: "Yatra" — *yātrā*: festival (the Rasa-yatra). "Rasika is not a human being" — *rasika manuṣya nahe*: the exalted praise of the people (note 31). "Krishnachandra is witness" — *kṛṣṇacandra sākṣī*: an oath formula.

[^305-58]: "Even speaking with a hundred mouths" — *śatamukhe kahileo*. "Brought forth" — *karila udaẏa*, lit. "caused to rise".

[^305-59]: "Arises" — *udaẏa*, lit. "rises". "Tens of millions" — *koṭi koṭi*, lit. "crores upon crores".

[^305-60]: 81–82 form one sentence. "The prince of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kuṅara* (*kuṅara* = *kumāra*): Rasika. The author attributes his inspiration to Rasika in his heart (cf. Pashchima, lahari 3, note 39).

[^305-61]: "Told" — *karila pracāra*. "Cross over" — *tara*: understood as an imperative; it can also be understood as "cross over" in the third person (cf. Pashchima, lahari 3, note 40). "The [age of] Kali" — *kalikāla*.

[^305-62]: The colophon is: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে রাসলীলা-সমাপন-নাম পঞ্চম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*rāsalīlā-samāpana*) — "The Completion of the Rasa-lila".


## Lahari 6. The Departure for Banapur

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; after the Rasa-yatra Shyamananda stays some days in the village, and Rasika with his family serves him; at Shyamananda's bidding the bashful Rasika expounds Krishna-katha in the assembly, so that the learned are amazed and people of all classes, even mlecchas, take shelter of Krishna; Raghunatha sends his brother with news that a Yavana is oppressing Sri Radhanagar; Shyamananda hastens with Rasika to Dharenda, Raghunatha Pattanayaka asks that men be sent to the subahdar Ahmed Beg, and Rasika with attendants and Vamshidasa sets out for Banapur*

*The sixth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi — panchali metre.*[^306-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the supreme bliss of all,
the giver of happiness to the whole world!
The great rasa of Rasika became manifest in the world,
renowned among all people in the three worlds.[^306-2]

**2.** Having sent everyone off, Shyamananda Raya then
stayed some days in that village.
Worshipping the Sri-murti more zealously still, Rasika Murari
knows nothing other than service.[^306-3]

**3.** Husband, wife, kinsfolk — [all] serve Shyamananda's holy feet
with firm devotion.
When Rasika-deva sits before Shyamananda,
[he sits] with his feet covered by his cloth.[^306-4]

**4.** With head bowed, full of bashfulness, with a faint, most sweet smile,
he speaks with no one.
Fixing both his holy eyes on Shyamananda's holy feet,
[he sits, and his] body floats in waves of tears.[^306-5]

**5.** Having offered himself [to his guru], Achyuta's son remains
the crest-jewel of composure and steadiness.
When Shyamananda says eagerly:
"Child, tell everyone about Krishna, explaining [it all]," —[^306-6]

**6.** faint with bashfulness, smiling softly and sweetly,
he utters a word or two very slowly;
as if [afraid] that someone might hear, he speaks in sweet words —
hearing them, [even] stone melts.

**7.** On one side words press forward, on the other — bashfulness, head bowed:
he is shy before Shyamananda.
Understanding [this], Shyamananda-raya rises on some pretext and goes away,
having given his command to Achyuta's son.[^306-7]

**8.** Receiving the command, Shyama-pati — [like] Shuka, Vyasa, Brihaspati —
seated in the assembly in great splendour,
joyfully speaks of Krishna, [unfolding] one meaning in many ways,
weeping and weeping in love for Krishna.[^306-8]

**9.** Hearing Rasika's words, [even] Brihaspati falls silent;
those assembled are amazed.
All the learned pandits say: "In vain have we studied all this time!
Rasika speaks the very essence."[^306-9]

**10.** The truth that Rasika speaks is the view of Vyasa [and] Shuka;
establishing [it] with the Svami's assent, [he says:]
"The Vedas, the shastras, the Bhagavata, the Puranas and all there is —
all say: set your mind on Krishna."[^306-10]

**11.** Saying this, the assembly of pandits praises Rasikendra,
and all began to follow it.
Hunas, Pulindas and others, mlechchhas, antyajas, Pukkashas and others —
all took refuge in Krishna.[^306-11]

**12.** Thus for some days Shyamananda in that place
remained in supreme bliss.
At that time Raghunatha sent [his] brother;
[he] tells everything at [Shyamananda's] lotus feet.[^306-12]

**13.** The brother says to the Prabhu: "In the village of Sri Radhanagar
a certain yavana has caused oppression.
Kindly come there quickly and, having heard, Prabhu, the whole account,
judge the whole matter."[^306-13]

**14.** Hearing [this], troubled at heart, together with Achyuta's son
Shyamananda-raya set out.
Very quickly [they] came, entered Dharenda
[and] stayed at Rasamaya's house.[^306-14]

**15.** The Prabhu says: "Listen, Vamshi: quickly bring everyone
[and] Raghunatha Pattanayaka."
Receiving the command, Vamshidasa went to them all
[and] promptly brought them all.[^306-15]

**16.** All, [coming] to Shyamananda, bowed to [his] holy feet
[and] told all the news:
"Hear, Prabhu, attentively; we will tell everything in detail:
a villain has seized the village.[^306-16]

**17.** Let ten or twenty devotees of Krishna quickly go
to the subahdar Ahmed Beg —
then [you] will hold that village undisturbed;
this we say at your feet for certain."[^306-17]

**18.** Hearing this, Shyamananda-raya looks at Rasika's face;
Rasikendra understood the hint:
"Let there be a command for me, Prabhu, to go to Banapur;
give me a company of followers."[^306-18]

**19.** Hearing Rasika's words, Shyamananda, delighted,
gave him all the companions;
all the singers and musicians — as he wished —
and with them gave the servant Vamshi.[^306-19]

**20.** Having made the auspicious setting-out, they went a little way and halted,
[and then] proceeded to Banapur.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^306-20]

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixth lahari, called "The Departure for Banapur."*[^306-21]

[^306-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading («ষষ্ঠ-লহরী»), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2). "Panchali metre" (*pā̃cāli chanda*) is the tripadi; each stanza is set in four lines in the edition and is translated likewise (cf. Purva, lahari 11, note 1). There is no ghosha or mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title follows the colophon: «ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে বানপুরোদ্দেশ্যে গমন-নাম ষষ্ঠ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা» (*bānapuroddeśye gamana*, "going with the aim of [reaching] Banapur") — "The Departure for Banapur". Banapur (*bānapura*; in stanza 20 *bāṇapura*) is not identified; possibly Banpur in Utkala (now Khurda district). The summary line covers the whole lahari. Stanza 3 begins and ends at the top of.

[^306-2]: "The supreme bliss of all" — *sabāra paramānanda*. "The great rasa of Rasika" — *rasikera baṛa rāsa*: the Rasa-yatra held by Rasika (Pashchima, laharis 2–5). On the rasa as pure prema, having nothing in common with mundane love (CC, Adi 4) — Pashchima, lahari 5, note 3; lahari 3, note 2. "Renowned" — *khyātā*.

[^306-3]: Shyamananda Raya is Shyamananda (Pashchima, lahari 5, note 35). "In that village" — *se grāme*: apparently Gopivallabhapur, where the Rasa-yatra took place. "Sri-murti" — *śrīmūrti*: usually the Deity; in connection with stanza 3 (Rasika and his family serve Shyamananda) it may also mean the "sacred person" of Shyamananda himself. "More zealously still" — *adhika kari'*, lit. "making more"; the meaning is approximate. Rasika Murari is Rasika.

[^306-4]: "Husband, wife" — *pati patnī*: apparently Rasika and his wife Shyamadasi. "Kinsfolk" — *goṭhī jana*: members of the clan, the household. "With firm devotion" — *dṛṛhabhābe*. "Before Shyamananda" — *śyāmānanda-sthāne*, lit. "at Shyamananda's place". "With his feet covered by his cloth" — *caraṇete ḍhākiẏā basana*: out of respect for the guru one does not uncover one's feet before him.

[^306-5]: 4–7 — Rasika's humility and bashfulness before his guru. "With head bowed" — *heṭa māthe*. "A faint smile" — *lahu hāsya*. "Tears" — *lohera* (*loha* = *lora*, "tears"). "[He sits, and]" — added for the connection; in the original the subject is "body".

[^306-6]: "Having offered himself" — *ātmanibedana kari'*: having surrendered himself wholly to his guru. "Crest-jewel of composure and steadiness" — *gāmbhīryya dhairyya śiromaṇi*. "Eagerly" — *kutūhale*. "Child" — *bāchā*, an affectionate address. "Explaining" — *bākhāni*.

[^306-7]: "On one side… on the other" — *ekamukhe … āre*: understood thus — he is drawn to speak, but bashfulness holds him back; it can also be taken as "on his lips — words". "Is shy" — *saṅkucita*. "On some pretext" — *kona chale*. "Before Shyamananda" — *śyāmānanda-sthāne*, lit. "in Shyamananda's presence".

[^306-8]: Shyama-pati (*śyāmāpati*), "husband of Shyama" — Rasika, husband of Shyamadasi (Purva, lahari 1, note 47); he is so named in the Uttara-vibhaga as well. Shuka (Shukadeva) is the speaker of the Bhagavata; Vyasa its compiler; Brihaspati the preceptor of the gods, a model of eloquence and learning. "In great splendour" — *mahāteje*. "One meaning in many ways" — *eka artha nānāchande*; cf. CC, Madhya 24, where Sri Chaitanya explains one verse in many ways.

[^306-9]: "Falls silent" — *tūṇi*. "In vain have we studied" — *byartha paṛi*. "The very essence" — *sāroddhāra*, lit. "extraction of the essence".

[^306-10]: The Svami is Shridhara Svami, author of the Bhavartha-dipika commentary on the Bhagavata (Purva, lahari 9, note 14). "Establishing" — *thāpiẏā*. "Set your mind on Krishna" — *kṛṣṇe deha mati*.

[^306-11]: "Saying this" — *hena bali'*: understood as the pandits, having said this (9–10), praising Rasika; it can also be taken as "Rasikendra said this". "Began to follow it" — *kaila sei ācaraṇa*. Hunas, Pulindas, Pukkashas — foreign and forest peoples and low castes; mlechchhas — those outside Vedic practice; antyajas — the lowest castes. Cf. Bhagavatam 2.4.18 (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 4): *kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pulkaśāḥ… śudhyanti* — they are purified by taking shelter of the Lord's devotees.

[^306-12]: "In that place" — *sei sthāne*: apparently Gopivallabhapura, where the Rasa-yatra took place (cf. 2: "in that village"). Raghunatha is Raghunatha Pattanayaka (15); not identified; apparently the holder of the village of Radhanagar (13, 16–17). "Brother" — *bhrāta*, i.e. his brother. "Tells everything" — *kahe sabe*, lit. "tells all"; understood as *saba*, "everything".

[^306-13]: Radhanagar — the village where Shyamananda first set up his home (Dakshina, lahari 11, note 16); not identified. "Yavana" — a Muslim. "Kindly come" — *bije haibe*: respectful of a holy person's going. "Having heard… judge" — *śuni prabhu saba bibaraṇa*, *bicāribe saba kathā*: the last half-line is taken as continuing the brother's speech.

[^306-14]: "Troubled at heart" — *ucāṭa mana*. Dharenda — the village of Rasamaya and Vamshi (Dakshina, lahari 4, 22). "Stayed at Rasamaya's house" — *utarilā gṛhe rasamaẏa*, lit. "stayed at the house — Rasamaya": understood thus.

[^306-15]: Vamshi (Vamshidasa) — Rasamaya's brother, the author's uncle (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14). Pattanayaka (*paṭṭanāyaka*; here *paṭṭanāẏeka*) — an honorific title of the Karanas of Utkala (Purva, lahari 3, note 23). "Went to them all" — *prabeśilā sabā pāśa*.

[^306-16]: "A villain" — *durācāra*: the yavana of 13. "Has seized the village" — *grāma harila*.

[^306-17]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇajana*. Ahmed Beg (*āhammada bega*) — apparently Ahmad Beg Khan, the Mughal governor of Orissa in the 1620s; the identification is tentative. Subahdar (*subā*) — governor (Purva, lahari 10, note 28). "Will hold" — *bhoga karibe*, lit. "will enjoy (have the use of)": the subject is not named — understood as Shyamananda. "For certain" — *niścaẏa*.

[^306-18]: "Understood the hint" — *iṅgita bujhena*. Banapur (*bānapura*, so here and in the colophon; *bāṇapura* in 20 and in lahari 7) — see note 1: possibly Banpur in Orissa (now Khurda district); according to lahari 7 the governor Ahmed Beg was staying there, which fits this identification, but it remains tentative.

[^306-19]: "Singers and musicians" — *saṅgīta-sāhitya*, lit. "singing and accompaniment": apparently the whole kirtan party (cf. lahari 7, 46). "As he wished" — *āpanāra manomata*: understood as Rasika's wish. "The servant Vamshi" — *dāsa baṃśī*: Vamshidasa (15).

[^306-20]: "Having made the auspicious setting-out" — *śubha anukūla kailā*: apparently the custom of setting out at an auspicious moment — going a little way and halting (*kata dūra giẏā railā*) before continuing the journey; the sense is approximate. The author's signature (the second half of the stanza) is given by the common formula; in the tripadi metre it reads: "Making the holy feet of Shyamananda an ornament on his head, the son of Rasamaya sings" (cf. Purva, lahari 5, note 14).

[^306-21]: Colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে বানপুরোদ্দেশ্যে গমন-নাম ষষ্ঠ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*bānapuroddeśye gamana*) — "The Departure for Banapur".


## Lahari 7. The Preaching of the Holy Name and the Description of the Wild Elephant's Ravages

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika, intoxicated with love for Krishna, travels to Banapur, staying nowhere longer than two days, and everywhere thousands become his disciples; he commands his disciples Ramakrishna and Dinashyama, and also Vamshidasa, to give the Hari-nama to all, from rajas to chandalas, and countless low-born people in the forest country and in Utkala are converted; at Banapur is camped the cruel governor Ahmed Beg, who has ruined the rajas and bhunyas of Orissa and keeps them about him in fear; Rasika stays with Raja Vaidyanatha, rajas, subjects, officials and hundreds of yavanas flock to him, and Shyamananda's affair concerning the village is settled by a document; the governor, seeing the crowds going to Rasika with the cry of "Hari," grows angry, reviles him as a cheat and sends for him, demanding a miracle like Kabir's; the rajas are afraid and his companions urge Rasika to flee, but he goes to the governor; meanwhile a wild, maddened elephant is ravaging Banapur, and when Rasika arrives the elephant bursts into the town, all flee in terror to the rooftops, and Rasika resolves to save everyone and make the elephant a sadhu — that elephant will become his servant*

*The seventh lahari.*

*Raga Mallar.*[^307-1]
*Ghosha: "Crusher of the Daityas, enemy of the Daityas.*
*Glory to the Son of Yadu, worshipped in the three worlds,*
*Slayer of invincible asuras!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of mercy!
At this time Rasikendra set out on his way.[^307-2]

**2.** In great intoxication with the bliss of Krishna [his] body trembles;
his whole body is wet with the tears of his eyes.[^307-3]

**3.** Unceasingly — conversations about Krishna;
on the roads and at the landings — an unceasing search for Krishna.

**4.** Not for a moment does he know anything but Krishna;
lying down, eating, sleeping — always remembrance of Krishna.[^307-4]

**5.** Wherever he sits for a moment, tired from the road,
thousands upon thousands of people come to see [him].

**6.** Seeing [his] sweet form, they forget themselves;
hearing the words from [his] holy mouth, they rejoice within.

**7.** [His] half-spoken words are like nectar;
hearing [them], all people find their hearts at peace.[^307-5]

**8.** As soon as they hear those words the three kinds of suffering depart;
wholly surrendered, [people] serve Krishna with bhakti.[^307-6]

**9.** By Rasika's touch [they] become embodiments of prema;
day after day hundreds of thousands become disciples.[^307-7]

**10.** In one place he halts, in another he bathes,
somewhere [he takes] food — [but] he does not rest.

**11.** Though hundreds of thousands of people [came to him] on the road,
he did not stay two days [anywhere], [following] his guru's command.[^307-8]

**12.** In village after village there arose a multitude of disciples;
[and] disciples' disciples, servant-disciples — they cannot be counted.[^307-9]

**13.** Rasika's disciples Ramakrishna [and] Dinashyama —
both are very great treasuries of prema-bhakti.[^307-10]

**14.** Seeing the pure hearts of those two,
Rasika-shekhara commanded [them] again and again:

**15.** "You two, give the Hari-nama to all people;
deliver the poor, the fallen — down to the chandalas.

**16.** Give the Hari-nama to all the rajas and subjects;
give prema-bhakti to everyone [in] the forest country.[^307-11]

**17.** Shyamananda-raya begged alms of me:
'Deliver living beings by my command.'[^307-12]

**18.** In the same way I beg alms of you two:
give the Hari-nama to everyone in Utkala."

**19.** Hearing this, both fell at [his] feet in obeisance:
"What paltry power have I, O son of Achyuta!"[^307-13]

**20.** Earlier Shyamananda had commanded these two:
"Whomever you touch will have Vishnu-bhakti."[^307-14]

**21.** By that command, through the sight [and] touch of these two,
millions upon millions in the land of the forest country became disciples.

**22.** All manner of low-born castes were delivered;
apart from service to sadhus they know nothing else.[^307-15]

**23.** They serve the guru, serve Krishna, serve the brahmanas;
all, wholly surrendered, [became] servants of Krishna.

**24.** Thus Rasikendra says to his disciples:
"Wherever anyone may be — give everyone the Hari-nama."[^307-16]

**25.** Rasikendra commanded Vamshidasa:
"Giving the Hari-nama, accept disciples in crowds."[^307-17]

**26.** Thus for some days Rasika-Murari,
joyfully playing [on the way], went on and reached Banapur.[^307-18]

**27.** Listen, everyone, I will tell how it was:
Ahmed Beg was a very wicked yavana.[^307-19]

**28.** All the rajas [and] bhunyas who live in the land of Orissa —
he especially ruined all their homes.[^307-20]

**29.** He destroyed houses [and] homesteads, cut down all the groves;
the yavana seized them all and took them along with him.[^307-21]

**30.** Very mighty is the wicked yavana ruler;
all the bhunyas [and] rajas tremble.

**31.** All serve [him] there in Banapur;
from fear a single day passes like a yuga.[^307-22]

**32.** Every day he kills two or four;
very wicked deeds that yavana does.[^307-23]

**33.** Everyone's heart is anxious, [all are] distraught with fear;
within their minds [they] remember Krishna.

**34.** At this time Rasikendra entered that village;
he stayed there with Raja Vaidyanatha.[^307-24]

**35.** Seeing [him], the raja fell at [his] feet with reverence;
washing [his] feet, he seated [him] on a seat.

**36.** Rasika-shekhara speaks the nectar of talks about Krishna;
hearing the words from [his] holy mouth, all are overwhelmed [with bliss].

**37.** The raja was very happy at seeing Rasika;
in his own palace he gave [him] lodging in a splendid place.[^307-25]

**38.** Every day all the rajas go there;
the Prabhu tells everyone of the truth of Krishna.

**39.** Day and night rajas [and] subjects go to that lodging;
an enormous crowd of people — beyond counting.[^307-26]

**40.** Following one another, all, hearing of it, run quickly
to see Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of devotees].[^307-27]

**41.** Hearing [his] sweet words, all in bliss
took refuge in Sri Rasikananda.

**42.** All the rajas became wholly surrendered [to him];
following their example, all their people came as well.

**43.** All the Hindu clans, his kayasthas [and] karanas —
all took refuge in Rasikendra.[^307-28]

**44.** By Rasika's touch [they] became wholly surrendered [to Krishna];
remaining in worldly affairs, all are intoxicated with the taste of Krishna.[^307-29]

**45.** That village of Banapur was stirred to its depths;
in the taste of sankirtana [people] do not know night from day.[^307-30]

**46.** Unceasingly [he] plays with singing and music;
Achyuta's son gave prema to all people.[^307-31]

**47.** [In] the matter for which Shyamananda-raya had sent [him] —
as soon as he heard [of it], he had everyone [draw up] a document.

**48.** The document was sent to Shyamananda;
for some days Rasikendra remained in that village.[^307-32]

**49.** In Banapur [was] the subahdar, and with him a crowd of yavanas;
every day they come and see Rasika.

**50.** Only the subahdar does not go to that place;
rajas, subjects, Hindus and others, all the yavanas —

**51.** all go every day to see Rasika;
hundreds upon hundreds of yavanas and others easily became disciples.[^307-33]

**52.** A great festival arose in that village of Banapur;
people beyond counting come night and day.[^307-34]

**53.** The wicked subahdar sits on his terrace;
he saw with his own eyes: hundreds of thousands of people standing there.[^307-35]

**54.** Every day, constantly, thus [they] come and go;
seeing [this], the villain grew angry [and] asks everyone:

**55.** "Where are you all going, on what business?
You go by hundreds of thousands, crying 'Hari!' on the road."

**56.** Hearing this, all the eminent people say:
"Sri Rasika-Murari is Krishna's very own form.[^307-36]

**57.** [He is] the greatest mahanta in all this Orissa,
with whom Jagannatha converses constantly.[^307-37]

**58.** All the rajas [and] subjects who live in Orissa —
all have become disciples at Rasika's feet.

**59.** All these people who are [now] around you —
all have become Rasika's disciples.

**60.** Hundreds upon hundreds of yavanas have become his disciples;
