he is not a man — he is a partial incarnation."

**61.** In many ways everyone told [of his] greatness;
the subahdar says: "I will see him — bring [him] before me."[^307-38]

**62.** That yavana ruler was very wicked;
hearing of [his] greatness, he speaks evil words in anger:

**63.** "Let him make Hindus his disciples — that is no concern of mine;
[but] it is not fitting for him to make yavanas his disciples.[^307-39]

**64.** With false show he deceives people;
he performs tricks and shows to take [their] goods.[^307-40]

**65.** When he shows me a miracle,
then I will acknowledge him as Narayana."[^307-41]

**66.** He quickly sent a messenger to bring Rasika:
"When he shows me a miracle —[^307-42]

**67.** [for] formerly divine great souls — Kabir and others,
a host of mahantas — have shown miracles.[^307-43]

**68.** Then I will acknowledge all [of them] as equal to Ishvara,
if I see any miracle at all with these eyes."[^307-44]

**69.** The yavana said to all the Hindu rajas:
"Bring Rasika-Murari-dasa here."[^307-45]

**70.** All the rajas were greatly afraid on hearing [this]:
"Why has Prabhu come to where the yavana is?[^307-46]

**71.** We do not know what miracle he wants to see;
if he does not see [one] — who knows what [this] villain will do."

**72.** Great sorrow arose in the hearts of the rajas;
the son of Achyuta heard [of it] from everyone.[^307-47]

**73.** Prabhu declared: "I shall go to him."
In many ways [his] companions tried to dissuade [him]:[^307-48]

**74.** "Why, Prabhu, will you go to the yavana?
Come, let us all flee — from forest to forest.

**75.** Saving our lives, come, let us flee home.
Why [deal] with a yavana — what is there to deliberate so much?"[^307-49]

**76.** At that time in Banapur, day after day,
a forest elephant was wreaking havoc.[^307-50]

**77.** Many houses it has smashed; men and women,
horses [and] elephants it kills day after day.

**78.** [People] do not go along the roads or to the landings for fear and terror of it;
the subahdar and everyone else were especially afraid.[^307-51]

**79.** By night or by day the king of elephants comes
[and] every day wreaks havoc in Banapur.

**80.** Prabhu went beyond everyone's words
[and] quickly set out to see the subahdar.[^307-52]

**81.** When the ruler was sitting on his terrace
[and] all the Hindu rajas were sitting around [him], —[^307-53]

**82.** at that time he set out for the subahdar;
[his] companions go [with him], delighting in various rasas.

**83.** Overwhelmed with love for Krishna, [his] heart rejoices.
Now listen attentively to the greatness of Rasika.[^307-54]

**84.** At that time, suddenly, that king of elephants
came [and] burst into Banapur.

**85.** A maddened forest elephant, most terrible,
of furious might, vicious, of huge body.

**86.** The elephant, crazed by great mada, heeds nothing;
all the houses [and] doors it smashes [and] breaks to pieces.[^307-55]

**87.** It lets out a most dreadful roar incessantly;
the earth trembles, and [even] the clouds.

**88.** With its breath the dust flies up into the vault of heaven;
under the weight of its steps the earth sinks into Rasatala.[^307-56]

**89.** Seizing them with its trunk, it uproots all the trees by force;
seizing horses [and] elephants, it kills [them] for sport.[^307-57]

**90.** The maddened elephant killed many people;
in confusion all fled to other lands.

**91.** Some onto the tops of houses, some onto terraces —
they hastily climbed up to high places.[^307-58]

**92.** In great fear all Banapur trembles;
thinking [it was] the end of the world, all were in turmoil.

**93.** All say: "Protect us, Lord Narayana!
For nothing we have all lost our lives!"[^307-59]

**94.** Thus everyone cries out "alas!";
the prince of Achyuta knew the minds of all.[^307-60]

**95.** He resolved in his mind: "Today I shall save everyone;
I shall make the elephant a supreme, wholly devoted sadhu."

**96.** Such a forest elephant [became] the servant of Rasika —
I shall tell how it happened; listen attentively.[^307-61]

**97.** Listen, listen, all, to the Rasika-mangala —
without delay you will obtain the wealth of prema-bhakti for Krishna.[^307-62]

**98.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the seventh lahari, called "The Preaching of the Holy Name and the Description of the Wild Elephant's Ravages."*[^307-63]

[^307-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("সপ্তম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Mallar; the ghosha is as in Dakshina, lahari 4 (note 1): names of Krishna, "Crusher of the Daityas" (*daitya-dalana*), "Enemy of the Daityas" (*daityāri*); here it is continued by a tripadi line: *jaẏa yadunandana, tribhubana-bandana, durjjaẏa asura-saṃhārī*. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল পশ্চিম-বিভাগে হরিনাম-প্রচার ও বন্যহস্তীর উপদ্রব-বর্ণন-নাম সপ্তম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*harināma-pracāra o banyahastīra upadraba-barṇana*) — "The Preaching of the Holy Name and the Description of the Wild Elephant's Ravages". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^307-2]: "Set out on his way" — *prayāṇa karila*: to Banapur (lahari 6, 18–20).

[^307-3]: "Trembles" — *jara jara*: "is overcome, all aquiver".

[^307-4]: "Not for a moment" — *eka tila*, lit. "[not for] a sesame seed". "Remembrance" — *dhyāna*, "meditation".

[^307-5]: "Half-spoken words" — *ādha ādha kathākhāni*: soft, broken speech (cf. lahari 6, 6). "Find their hearts at peace" — *juṛāẏa parāṇa*, lit. "life is cooled (comforted)".

[^307-6]: "The three kinds of suffering" — *tina tāpa*: those caused by one's own body and mind, by other beings, and by the forces of nature. "Wholly surrendered" — *ananyaśaraṇa*, "having no other refuge".

[^307-7]: "Embodiments of prema" — *premamaẏa mūrti*. "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣa lakṣa*, "lakhs and lakhs" (a lakh is a hundred thousand); so also below.

[^307-8]: "Though… [came]" — *tabe … pathete yāite*: the sense of the line is approximate; understood as: although crowds flocked to him on the road, he stayed nowhere longer than two days. "His guru's command" — Shyamananda's (lahari 6, 18–19).

[^307-9]: "Disciples' disciples, servant-disciples" — *anu-śiṣya bhṛtya-śiṣya*.

[^307-10]: Ramakrishna and Dinashyama (*dinaśyāma*) are disciples of Rasika (Purva, lahari 1, 132; Pashchima 1, note 19). "Treasuries" — *nidhāna*.

[^307-11]: "The forest country" — *banabhūmi* (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10).

[^307-12]: On the alms Shyamananda begged of Rasika, see Dakshina, lahari 4, 3 ff.

[^307-13]: "What paltry power have I" — *mui kona chāra śakti*: singular — understood as the words of each of the two. "O son of Achyuta" — addressed to Rasika (*acyuta-nandane*).

[^307-14]: "Vishnu-bhakti" — *biṣṇubhakti*, devotion to Vishnu (Krishna).

[^307-15]: "Low-born castes" — *antyaja jāti*.

[^307-16]: "Wherever anyone may be" — *yathāẏa ye yāhā*.

[^307-17]: Vamshidasa — the author's uncle, Rasamaya's brother (lahari 6, 15, 19). "In crowds" — *bṛnda bṛnda*.

[^307-18]: "Joyfully playing [on the way]" — *kheli kheli*, lit. "playing, playing": apparently with sankirtana. "Banapur" — here *bāṇapurī* (lahari 6, 18, 20).

[^307-19]: Ahmed Beg — the subahdar (lahari 6, 17). "Yavana" — a Muslim. "How it was" — *tā'ra bibaraṇa*. BR 15 (83–85) says briefly that Rasikananda made a disciple of the elephant a villain had set upon him, and that "that villain, the yavana king," bowed before him.

[^307-20]: Orissa — *uṛiṣyā*. Bhunyas (*bhuñā*) — bhuiyans, local landholders and chiefs (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 16). "Especially" — *biśeṣe*.

[^307-21]: "Seized them all and took them along with him" — *saṅge dhari' laila*: apparently he forced the rajas and bhunyas to stay in attendance on him (cf. 31).

[^307-22]: "Serve [him]" — *sebā kare*: apparently they were in attendance on the governor. A yuga is a world-age, an immense span of time.

[^307-23]: "Kills" — *saṃhāraṇa kare*.

[^307-24]: Raja Vaidyanatha (*baidyanātha*) — not identified (cf. Purva, lahari 1, 132 and note 49: Rasika's disciple Vaidyanatha). "Village" — *grāma*: Banapur. "Stayed" — *utarila*.

[^307-25]: "Palace" — *mandire*: here a house or palace. "Lodging" — *bāsā*.

[^307-26]: "Beyond counting" — *nāhi samucaẏa* (cf. lahari 4, note 44).

[^307-27]: "Following one another" — *dekhā dekhi*, lit. "seeing [one another]" (so also in 42). "Crest-jewel" — *cūṛāmaṇi*, "the jewel in a crown".

[^307-28]: Kayasthas and karanas (*kāẏeta karaṇa*) — castes of scribes and officials (Purva, lahari 3, note 23). "His" — *tā'ra*: apparently the Hindu officials in the governor's service; unclear.

[^307-29]: "Remaining in worldly affairs" — *biṣaẏe thākiẏā*: without leaving home and duties. "The taste of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇarase*.

[^307-30]: "Was stirred to its depths" — *ṭalaṭala hailā*. "Do not know night from day" — *niśi diśi nāi jāna*.

[^307-31]: "Singing and music" — *saṅgīta sāhitya* (lahari 6, note 19). "Achyuta's son" — *acyutera bālā*.

[^307-32]: 47–48: "Document" — *patra*, "letter, deed". Understood as the matter of the village of Radhanagar (lahari 6, 12–17): as soon as he hears of it, [the rajas and officials] draw up a document at Rasika's word, and it is sent to Shyamananda. Literally "by mere hearing he makes all [do] a document" (*śrabaṇa mātreke patra karāẏa sabāẏa*); the sense is approximate.

[^307-33]: "Easily" — *hele*, "lightly, effortlessly".

[^307-34]: "A great festival" — *mahāyātrā*.

[^307-35]: "On his terrace" — *jagatīte*: *jagatī* — a raised platform or terrace (cf. 81). "Standing" — *ubhā* (cf. Purva, lahari 10, note 30).

[^307-36]: 56–60 are the words of the eminent people to the subahdar. "Krishna's very own form" — *kṛṣṇera svarūpa*; "partial incarnation" (60) — *aṃśa-abatāra*: rapturous praise. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation (Pashchima 2, note 28). On how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^307-37]: "Mahanta" — *mohānta* (*mahānta*), a revered teacher, the head of a community. Jagannatha is the Lord, the Deity of Puri. "With whom Jagannatha converses constantly" — a tradition expressing Rasika's intimacy with the Lord; it is not in BR 15.

[^307-38]: "Bring [him] before me" — *āna bidyamāne*, lit. "bring into [my] presence".

[^307-39]: "That is no concern of mine" — *tā'ra nāhi dāẏa*. "It is not fitting" — *nā yuẏāẏa*.

[^307-40]: "Show" — *āṛambari*. "Deceives" — *bhāṇḍibāre*, "in order to deceive". "Tricks and shows" — *caṭaka nāṭaka*. "Goods" — *drabya*, "property".

[^307-41]: "Miracle" — *keramati* (Arabic-Persian *karāmat*, a saint's miracle). The author exalts Rasika with accounts of miracles (cf. lahari 4, note 49).

[^307-42]: The second line of 66 repeats 65; the subahdar's speech continues in 67–68, so it is left open in the translation.

[^307-43]: 67–68 conclude the subahdar's speech (65–66; note 42). Kabir (*kabira*) — the fifteenth-century poet-saint of Varanasi, revered by Hindus and Muslims alike. "Divine great souls" — *deba mahājana*. "A host of mahantas" — *mohāntera gaṇa* (note 37). "Miracles" — *keramati* (note 41). "Have shown" — *dekhā'lena*.

[^307-44]: "Acknowledge as equal to Ishvara" — *māni īśvara-samāne*, "honour on a par with God". "All [of them]" — *sabā*: apparently Kabir and the other mahantas who showed miracles (and so Rasika too, if he shows one — cf. 65). "With these eyes" — *e-naẏane*.

[^307-45]: "The yavana said" — *kahila yabane*: *yabane* is taken as the subject ("the yavana said to all the Hindu rajas"); grammatically "all the Hindu rajas said to the yavana" is also possible, but from 70 and lahari 8, 5 the order comes from the subahdar. Rasika-Murari-dasa (*rasika-murāridāsa*) is Rasika.

[^307-46]: Prabhu is Rasika (cf. 38; so the author calls him). "To where the yavana is" — *yabanera sthāne*, lit. "to the yavana's place": to Banapur.

[^307-47]: "From everyone" — *sabāsthāne*. The son of Achyuta (*acyuta-nandana*) is Rasika (note 13).

[^307-48]: "Declared" — *ājñā karilena*, lit. "commanded". "In many ways" — *bahurūpe*.

[^307-49]: "From forest to forest" — *bane bane*. "Saving our lives" — *prāṇa laiẏā*, lit. "taking [our] lives". "What is there to deliberate so much" — *kena eta ki bicāre*; the sense of the line is approximate: understood as "why have anything to do with a yavana at all".

[^307-50]: The wild elephant of the lahari's title (note 1). "Was wreaking havoc" — *pīṛane karaẏe*, "oppresses, torments". "Forest" — *araṇyera*.

[^307-51]: "Do not go along the roads or to the landings" — *patha ghāṭa nāhi cale*. "For fear and terror" — *bhaẏa-trāse*. The subahdar is Ahmed Beg (note 19).

[^307-52]: "King of elephants" — *gajarāja*. 80: "Went beyond everyone's words" — *karilā laṅghana*: he did not heed their dissuasion (73–75).

[^307-53]: 81–82 form one sentence. "The ruler" — *nṛpati*: the subahdar. "On his terrace" — *jagatīte* (note 35; cf. 91). "Around" — *cāribhiti*, "on four sides". 82: "Delighting in various rasas" — *nānārasa-binode*: apparently with singing and talk of Krishna.

[^307-54]: "Overwhelmed" — *jara jara* (note 3); understood as Rasika's heart. "Now" — *ibe*.

[^307-55]: *Mada* — the season of frenzy in bull elephants (musth), when fluid flows from the temporal glands; "crazed by great mada" — *mahāmada-matta*. "Heeds nothing" — *kichu nāi māne*. "To pieces" — *khāne khāne*.

[^307-56]: "The vault of heaven" — *gagana-maṇḍala*, "the circle of the sky". Rasatala is one of the lower worlds. "Under the weight of its steps" — *padabhare*.

[^307-57]: "For sport" — *kutūhale*.

[^307-58]: 90: "In confusion" — *āste byaste*, "in haste". "To other lands" — *deśāntare*. 91: "Onto the tops of houses" — *aṭṭālikā upare*: onto the tops of tall (masonry) houses. "Onto terraces" — *jagatī*. "Hastily" — *tvarati*.

[^307-59]: 92: "The end of the world" — *pralaẏa*, the dissolution of the universe. 93: "For nothing" — *akāraṇe*, "without cause, without fault". "We have lost our lives" — *hārāinu*: the past tense of what is felt to be inevitable.

[^307-60]: "Cries out 'alas!'" — *hāhākāra*. "The prince of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kumāra*: Rasika (cf. Pashchima, lahari 5, note 60).

[^307-61]: 95: "A supreme, wholly devoted sadhu" — *parama ananya sādhu*. 96: "Servant" — *bhṛtya*; cf. BR 15, 84 (note 19): Rasikananda made the elephant a disciple and engaged it in the service of Krishna and the Vaishnavas. The account of how it happened (*tā'ra bibaraṇa*) is in lahari 8.

[^307-62]: "Without delay" — *abilambe*. "The wealth of prema-bhakti for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapremabhaktidhana*.

[^307-63]: The colophon is (note 1). Lahari 7 ends with the author's signature (98).


## Lahari 8. The Deliverance of the Maddened Elephant

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; the subahdar, sitting on his terrace, orders the rajas to bring Rasika: let him give the Holy Name to the elephant ravaging Banapur, and if he survives he will be acknowledged as Narayana; the rajas despair, but Rasika, relying on Krishna's shelter, goes out to meet the elephant; his companions flee, and the subahdar repents of having summoned a sadhu to his doom; Rasika instructs the elephant to serve Krishna, reminding it of Indra and Gajendra; the elephant, gaining divine knowledge, falls at his feet, receives in its ear the sixteen names of "Hare Krishna" and the name Gopala Dasa, and, intoxicated with prema, goes off into the forest; all see Rasika's power, and Ahmed Beg falls at his feet and begs forgiveness; Rasika explains that Narayana, the maintainer of countless universes, dwells in the heart of every being, and so he did no violence to the elephant but gave it Krishna's name; the elephant gives up its wicked deeds, and the king of the yavanas rejoices*

*The eighth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^308-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!*
*O Murari, O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of compassion,
the supremely merciful Prabhu, the life of the world![^308-2]

**2.** At that time that wicked lord of the yavanas,
sitting on his terrace, summoned all the rulers.[^308-3]

**3.** To all the rajas the yavana ruler says:
"This elephant has today brought calamity on everyone.

**4.** Horses, elephants, men — it has killed many.
Make an effort so that it is stopped."[^308-4]

**5.** Then that yavana says to all the rajas:
"Bring Rasika-Murari-dasa here.

**6.** All the Hindus call him Narayana —
let him today give this elephant the Holy Name.[^308-5]

**7.** If the mahashaya comes through unharmed from the elephant,
then I shall surely acknowledge [him] as Narayana."[^308-6]

**8.** Hearing this, all the people were stunned;
great sorrow arose in everyone's heart.

**9.** All say: "Well, today [has come] utter ruin!
Why did Prabhu come to this villain?"[^308-7]

**10.** All remembered Krishna within;
among the rajas, in no one [, it seemed,] was there life left.[^308-8]

**11.** At that time Rasika, hearing these words,
declared: "I shall go to the subahdar without fail.

**12.** If I have truly taken shelter of Krishna, the Lord,
then what can a forest elephant do?"[^308-9]

**13.** Prabhu set out to see the subahdar;
with tears in his eyes he remembers Krishna.

**14.** Prabhu drew near the village
[and] saw: along the road comes an elephant crazed with mada.[^308-10]

**15.** Whomever it catches nearby it deprives of life;
seeing [its] fury, no one comes near.

**16.** Hearing the roar — a most dreadful sound —
[people think]: "What calamity has befallen the land of Banapur!"[^308-11]

**17.** They saw [it] coming along the road, like a mountain;
houses [and] doors it destroyed, broke to pieces.

**18.** Many people [and] horses it kills, mighty [as] a lion;
swinging its trunk, crazed, it goes unhurriedly.[^308-12]

**19.** All the people flee in fear of it;
today the elephant has destroyed many.

**20.** At that time Rasika comes along that road;
swiftly the untamable [elephant] came and stood face to face with him.[^308-13]

**21.** Seeing [this], the companions in fear say to Rasika:
"Come, let us flee into the town!

**22.** This elephant's ferocity cannot be told;
in an instant it will take the lives of all at once."[^308-14]

**23.** Prabhu did not listen to anyone's words;
standing, he remembers the name of Krishna.

**24.** The companions fled, [saving] their lives in panic;
stumbling and falling, all rushed far off into the wilds.[^308-15]

**25.** Prabhu remained alone, with joy in his heart;
without timidity, without fear he chants the Holy Name.[^308-16]

**26.** Staying on his terrace, the fierce yavana watches;
within he prays: "Protect him, Narayana!

**27.** Without cause I summoned a sadhu here;
I have become a partaker in the killing of a sadhu — this I fully understand.[^308-17]

**28.** The mahashaya has fallen into the clutches of this untamable [elephant];
today I shall surely know [whether] that promise of Krishna [holds]."[^308-18]

**29.** Thus that yavana ruler thinks within himself;
all the Hindu rajas are in turmoil:

**30.** most wicked is this yavana ruler:
by force he has summoned the son of Achyuta;

**31.** most mighty is the wicked, untamable elephant, —
[and] within [they] remember Krishna.[^308-19]

**32.** Everyone weeps with one another;
seeing this, the companions are barely alive.[^308-20]

**33.** With joy in his heart, with tears in his eyes, Prabhu
again and again remembers: "Krishna, Krishna."[^308-21]

**34.** When the maddened elephant came face to face [with him],
the elephant saw with its own eyes the beautiful Rasika.

**35.** Seeing Rasika, the elephant at once stops;
looking into its face, Rasika-shekhara says:[^308-22]

**36.** "Listen, listen, O maddened elephant!
Serve Krishna, serve the sadhus unceasingly.

**37.** Why do you ruin yourself in vain, doing all kinds of wicked deeds?
Everything apart from Krishna is wasted labour.[^308-23]

**38.** Chant [the name of] Krishna, meditate on Krishna, give your mind to Krishna;
becoming wholly devoted, serve Krishna's feet.

**39.** All the scriptures in essence speak of the service of Krishna;
giving up ignorance, serve Krishna's feet.[^308-24]

**40.** All that you see apart from Krishna is not your own;
from today do not do wicked deeds any more.

**41.** Krishna is mother, Krishna is father, Krishna is life itself;
not serving Krishna, why perish for nothing?

**42.** To serve Krishna, do not be intoxicated [and] proud:
the pride of Airavata [and] Indra [He] swiftly crushed.[^308-25]

**43.** Once a crocodile seized the best of the kings of elephants;
destroying the crocodile, [the Lord] delivered the elephant.[^308-26]

**44.** Prabhu, the divine Bhagavan, is an ocean of mercy;
giving up intoxication [and] pride, meditate on Prabhu Krishna.

**45.** Hearing the words of a sadhu, my child, give your mind to Krishna;
the Son of Nanda will be merciful to you."[^308-27]

**46.** As the fruit of former austerities [came] the sight of Rasika;
at the sight [its] heart melted, [and] it gazes intently [at him].[^308-28]

**47.** It saw Rasika as if a second Narayana;
with tears in its eyes the elephant thinks within itself:

**48.** "This person is not a man, [but] a portion of Narayana;
the truth he has told me is the conclusion of the scriptures."[^308-29]

**49.** Divine knowledge dawned in the elephant's heart;
it knew for certain that Krishna is the truth.[^308-30]

**50.** Hearing Rasika's words, the maddened elephant
quickly fell at Rasika's feet.

**51.** Laying its head at [his] holy feet, with joy in its heart,
it washed Rasika's feet with tears.

**52.** Into the elephant's right ear Rasika-shekhara
made the name of Krishna heard, placing his hand on its head.

**53.** The sixteen names of "Hare Krishna," thirty-two syllables,
Rasika-shekhara made heard in the elephant's ear.[^308-31]

**54.** Hearing Krishna's name, the elephant quickly rose
[and] prostrated its body on the ground at [his] feet.

**55.** Circumambulating [him], it bows down;
in hundreds of streams [tears] flow from the elephant's eyes.[^308-32]

**56.** Seeing Rasika's form, enchanted at heart,
the maddened elephant gazes intently.

**57.** In the waves of [his] beauty [its] eyes sank into an ocean;
intoxicated with prema, it forgets itself.[^308-33]

**58.** Then [Rasika] gave it the name Sri Gopala Dasa;
hearing it, the elephant falls at [his] feet again and again.[^308-34]

**59.** With tears it washed [his] two feet;
it itself saw [him] in the form of Narayana.[^308-35]

**60.** It has no wish to go away;
with firm faith it took shelter of Rasika.

**61.** Apart from Rasika's feet nothing else pleases it;
it knew for certain: all is false, Krishna is the truth.[^308-36]

**62.** Staying a moment, the elephant, having bowed,
all in tears [and] trembling, slowly goes away.

**63.** Placing Rasika's lotus feet in its heart,
having gained divine knowledge, it goes, intoxicated with prema.[^308-37]

**64.** The king of elephants, wholly devoted, went [and] entered the forest;
with its whole soul it took shelter of Rasika.[^308-38]

**65.** Everyone comes and sees Rasika —
rajas, subjects, Hindus and others, the host of yavanas.

**66.** All the people saw [the power] manifested by Rasika;
seeing [these] signs, all deemed [it] a wonder.[^308-39]

**67.** Seeing [this], the men and women were astonished;
all recognized Rasika as a portion of Narayana.[^308-40]

**68.** All the people say to one another:
"The maddened elephant fell at Rasika's feet!"

**69.** Rasika-shekhara gave a name to the maddened elephant;
this news spread widely in all four directions.[^308-41]

**70.** Hearing it, all the people went to see Rasika:
rajas, subjects, children, the old, women — crowd after crowd.[^308-42]

**71.** All the crowds of yavanas come and look;
the subahdar too came quickly, seeing the manifestation [of power].[^308-43]

**72.** In his heart the ruler of the yavanas was greatly afraid:
"For no reason at all I have offended Rasika!"[^308-44]

**73.** Coming, he presented himself before Rasika;
Ahmed Beg, coming, fell at [his] feet.[^308-45]

**74.** With joined palms the subahdar says to Rasika:
"I bring one plea to your feet.

**75.** I did not know that you are Ishvara Himself, in person;
that is why I sent for you, to have [you] brought.[^308-46]

**76.** Such a wicked deed I did in ignorance;
forgive [my] offence — [I] take refuge in you.

**77.** You are an ocean of mercy, a treasury of compassion;
you are the stronghold of refuge, the life of the world.[^308-47]

**78.** Bewildered by your maya, O Prabhu,
I offended [you], not knowing your greatness."

**79.** Hearing such humble words from the subahdar,
Prabhu, with tears in his eyes, began to speak:

**80.** "Listen, listen, O ruler of the yavanas:
I came in order to see you.

**81.** On the road [I] saw an untamable elephant;
the elephant rushed swiftly [at me] to kill me.[^308-48]

**82.** The elephant rushed swiftly to kill;
seeing it untamable, I remembered Krishna.

**83.** In all bodies dwells the one Lord, Bhagavan;
in the hearts of all living beings dwells the Treasury of compassion.[^308-49]

**84.** Patala, Sutala, Vitala, Rasatala,
the abode of Mahakurma, Mahatala, Atitala;

**85.** beneath them is the place of Padma, such-and-such a place;
[thus] the seven lower worlds — there is evidence for it.[^308-50]

**86.** Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka, Svarloka — three places,
Janaloka, Tapoloka — [so] the shastras testify;

**87.** above them are Maharloka, Brahmaloka and the rest:
these seven worlds above — [so] it is known.[^308-51]

**88.** An ordinary universe is these fourteen worlds;
in it are one Brahma, Indra [and] all the gods.[^308-52]

**89.** Be it seven worlds or a thousand worlds —
thus creating the universes,

**90.** hundreds of thousands, endless worlds and more —
each and every universe Hari creates in this way.[^308-53]

**91.** Four-faced, hundred-faced, ten-million-faced Brahmas,
and likewise the Indras — who can set [them] a limit?[^308-54]

**92.** Countless millions of universes exist in this way;
all of them arise in the pores of Narayana's skin.[^308-55]

**93.** Such is Narayana — the original light, the spotless one;
the Lord maintains all that moves and does not move.[^308-56]

**94.** In countless millions of universes, the unmoving and the moving:
insects, beasts, birds, worms, those born as humans —

**95.** all the moving, the unmoving and the rest, as many as there are in the endless worlds —
in the heart of all, in a subtle form, dwells Narayana.[^308-57]

**96.** Dwelling in the hearts of all, He maintains dharma;
the Destroyer of adharma is the god Narayana.

**97.** Age after age He establishes dharma;
all the wicked, devoid of dharma, He destroys.[^308-58]

**98.** Whoever attacks someone is attacked by him in turn;
whoever attacks one who does no harm will never be delivered.[^308-59]

**99.** So in the elephant's heart too is Narayana,
the Indwelling Lord of all, the Lord, one and spotless.

**100.** I never did it any harm;
seeing [him], I said: 'Remember Krishna.'

**101.** Hearing Krishna's name, the elephant fell at [my] feet;
with its tears it washed my feet.

**102.** Into the elephant's ear I spoke Krishna's mantra [and] Name;
circling [me], it went off to its own place."[^308-60]

**103.** That king of elephants gave up its wicked deeds;
hearing [this], the king of the yavanas rejoiced.[^308-61]

**104.** Listen, listen, all people, to the Rasika-mangala:
Rasika's pastimes are a wonder [to] the three worlds.

**105.** [His] pastimes are a boundless ocean: who can know [them]?
[Only] by Rasika's mercy is something revealed to me.[^308-62]

**106.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eighth lahari, called "The Deliverance of the Maddened Elephant."*[^308-63]

[^308-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("অষ্টম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Kaushika (*kauśika*; Purva, lahari 3, note 1). The ghosha — *jaẏa re rāmakṛṣṇa murāre / o murāre o murāre* — is as in Purva, laharis 3 and 16 (note 1 there), and is translated the same way; Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari is a name of Krishna which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে মত্তহস্তি উদ্ধার-নাম অষ্টম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*mattahasti uddhāra*) — "The Deliverance of the Maddened Elephant". The lahari runs 1–106; the summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^308-2]: "Treasury of compassion" — *karuṇānidhāna*. "The life of the world" — *jagatera prāṇa*.

[^308-3]: 2–10 repeat and develop the account of lahari 7, 65–75 (Rasika summoned to the subahdar). "Lord of the yavanas" — *yabana-adhipati*: the subahdar Ahmed Beg (Pashchima, lahari 7, 27). "On his terrace" — *jagatīte*: on a raised platform or terrace (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 35). "Rulers" — *nṛpati*: the Hindu rajas (3).

[^308-4]: "Make an effort" — *karaha yatana*. "So that it is stopped" — *kemane nibṛtta haẏa*, lit. "how [it might] cease".

[^308-5]: Rasika-Murari-dasa is Rasika. "Call him Narayana" — cf. Pashchima, lahari 7, 56–60, 65. "Let him … give" — *dibena*, honorific future: taken as a demand and a test.

[^308-6]: "Comes through unharmed from the elephant" — *hātī haite uturena*, lit. "comes across (gets through) from the elephant": remains unharmed. "Mahashaya" (*mahāśaẏa*, "great soul") is an honorific: Rasika.

[^308-7]: "Stunned" (8) — *camakita*. "Utter ruin" — *sarbbanāśa*. Prabhu is Rasika.

[^308-8]: "In no one [, it seemed,] was there life left" — *kāhāra dehete prāṇa nāi*, lit. "in no one's body is there life": the rajas were half dead with fear.

[^308-9]: "Declared" (11) — *ājñā kaila*, lit. "commanded". "Without fail" — *sarbbathā*. 12: "Truly" — *niśce* (= *niścaẏa*). "Krishna, the Lord" — *kṛṣṇapati*. Cf. Krishna's promise (note 18).

[^308-10]: "Drew near the village" — *parabeśa hailā … grāmera samīpe*, lit. "entered the vicinity of the village": Banapur. "Crazed with mada" — *mada-matta* (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 55). "Elephant" — *kari*.

[^308-11]: "Calamity" — *pramāda*. The subject of the second line is not expressed; understood as the people's exclamation.

[^308-12]: 17: "Coming" — *āse*. "Like a mountain" — *parbbata samāna*. 18: "Mighty [as] a lion" — *bikramī keśarī*, lit. "a mighty lion". "Swinging its trunk" — *śuṇḍa phirāiẏā*. "Unhurriedly" — *dhīri dhīri*.

[^308-13]: "Untamable" — *duranta*, "unruly, ferocious" (so throughout). "Stood face to face with him" — *karila sākṣāte*.

[^308-14]: "In an instant" — *ekatile*, lit. "in [one] sesame seed". "At once" — *eka ṭhā̃ẏa*, lit. "in one place".

[^308-15]: "In panic" — *prāṇera bikale*. "Stumbling and falling" — *uṭhu paṛu hañā*, lit. "rising [and] falling". "Far off into the wilds" — *tepāntare*: into distant open, deserted country.

[^308-16]: "Without timidity" — *nā saṅkoca*. "Chants" — *laẏa*, lit. "takes".

[^308-17]: 26–28 are the subahdar's thoughts. "Fierce" — *duranta* (note 13), here of the subahdar. "Protect" — *rakṣa*. 27: "Here" — *hethā*. "A partaker in the killing of a sadhu" — *sādhu-badhabhāgī*: one who bears the sin of killing a sadhu. "Fully" — *sarbbathā*.

[^308-18]: "Has fallen into the clutches" — *hāte ṭhekilena*, lit. "got caught in the hand"; *hāta* ("hand") may also hint at the trunk. "That promise of Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa-pratijñā*: cf. Bhagavad-gita 9.31: "O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes" (*kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati*).

[^308-19]: 29–31 are taken as one sentence: 30–31 are the thoughts of the Hindu rajas. "Thinks within himself" — *mane mane kare*. 30: "By force" — *haṭha kari'*. The son of Achyuta is Rasika. 31: "Elephant" — *kuñjara*.

[^308-20]: "With one another" — *eka āre*. "Barely alive" — *nā dhare parāṇe*, lit. "cannot hold on to life".

[^308-21]: "Again and again" — *ghane ghane*. "Remembers" — *sumaraṇa kare* (= *smaraṇa*).

[^308-22]: "Stops" — *dā̃ṛāẏa*, "stands, stops". Rasika-shekhara is Rasika.

[^308-23]: 36–45 are Rasika's instruction to the elephant. 37: "Ruin yourself" — *mara*, lit. "perish" (so also in 41). "Wasted labour" — *byartha pariśrama*.

[^308-24]: "In essence" — *tattve*. "Ignorance" — *abidyā*: avidya, the ignorance that binds the soul to the material world.

[^308-25]: "Do not be intoxicated [and] proud" — *mada garbba nā kariha*: *mada* is both the intoxication of pride and the elephant's mada (note 10); a play on words. Airavata is Indra's elephant. Krishna crushed Indra's pride by lifting Govardhana Hill (Bhag. 10.24–27); when taking the parijata tree Krishna defeated Indra, who fought mounted on Airavata (Bhag. 10.59). "Crushed" — *nāśilā*.

[^308-26]: The deliverance of Gajendra, the king of elephants, seized in the water by a crocodile: the Lord, on whom the elephant called, killed the crocodile and saved him (Bhag. 8.2–4). "The best of the kings of elephants" — *gajarājabare*.

[^308-27]: 44: "The divine Bhagavan" — *deba bhagavān*. 45: "My child" — *bāpu*: an affectionate address. The Son of Nanda is Krishna.

[^308-28]: "The fruit of former austerities" — *pūrbba-tapasyāra phale*: apparently the piety of the elephant's past lives (cf. Gajendra, in his past life King Indradyumna; Bhag. 8.4). "Melted" — *drabila*.

[^308-29]: 47–48 give the elephant's perception: "as if a second Narayana" (*dbitīẏa nārāẏaṇa*), "a portion of Narayana" (*aṃśa nārāẏaṇa*). On how the author exalts Rasika, and on the Gaudiya Vaishnava view of Rasika as a devotee and disciple of Shyamananda, see Pashchima, lahari 7, note 36; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "Person" — *puruṣa*. "The conclusion of the scriptures" — *śāstra nirūpaṇa*: what the scriptures establish.

[^308-30]: "Divine knowledge" — *dibyajñāna*. "Knew that Krishna is the truth" — *kṛṣṇa satya kariẏā … jānila*.

[^308-31]: Making the name of Krishna heard in the right ear is the rite of initiation into the Holy Name. 53: the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare / Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare" — sixteen names, thirty-two syllables (Purva, lahari 2, note 11). Cf. CC, Madhya 17: in the forests of Jharikhanda, by Sri Chaitanya's mercy, tigers, deer and elephants chanted the name of Krishna. "Placing his hand on its head" — *muṇḍe diẏā kara*.

[^308-32]: 54: "Prostrated its body on the ground" — *daṇḍabata kāẏa kṣiti* (Pashchima, lahari 5, note 45). 55: "Circumambulating [him]" — *parikramā kari'*: a reverent circling. "Bows down" — *paraṇāme* (= *praṇāma*). "Streams" — *dhārā*.

[^308-33]: "Enchanted at heart" — *mugudha antara*. 57: "In the waves of [his] beauty" — *rūpera hillole*; "sank into an ocean" — *paṛilā pāthāre*, lit. "fell into the boundless waters". "Intoxicated with prema" — *premamaẏe matta haiẏā*; it may also be understood as "intoxicated with the One full of prema", i.e. Rasika.

[^308-34]: Sri Gopala Dasa (*śrīgopāla dāsa*) is the name given to the elephant at initiation; in BR 15, 84 (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 19) the elephant's name is not given. The subject of the first line is not expressed; understood as Rasika. "Again and again" — *katabāra*, "how many times".

[^308-35]: "Two feet" — *caraṇa-dukhāni*. "It itself saw" — *dekhila āpani*: the elephant saw Rasika in the form of Narayana (note 29).

[^308-36]: 60: "Has no wish" — *nāhi laẏa mana*. "With firm faith" — *dṛṛha biśbāsete*. 61: "Pleases" — *bhāẏa*. "All is false, Krishna is the truth" — *saba mithyā kṛṣṇa satya*: everything transient without Krishna is worthless.

[^308-37]: 62: "All in tears [and] trembling" — *aśru-pulakita*: tears and trembling (hair standing on end) are signs of prema. 63: "Having gained divine knowledge" — *dibyajñāna haiẏā*.

[^308-38]: "The king of elephants, wholly devoted" — *gajendra ananya*. "With its whole soul" — *sarbbātmabhābe*.

[^308-39]: "[The power] manifested by Rasika" — *rasikera prakāśa*, "Rasika's manifestation". "Signs" — *lakṣaṇa*: marks [of his power]. "Deemed [it] a wonder" — *adbhuta mānila*.

[^308-40]: "A portion of Narayana" — *aṃśa nārāyaṇa*: the crowd's rapturous acclamation (cf. 48 and note 29: on how the author exalts Rasika, and on the Gaudiya Vaishnava view of him as a devotee and disciple of Shyamananda; Pashchima, lahari 7, note 36; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). Likewise 75–78.

[^308-41]: "Gave a name" — *nāma dila*: the name Sri Gopala Dasa (58, note 34). "News" — *śabada* (*śabda*), "word, report".

[^308-42]: "Women" — *strīri*. "Crowd after crowd" — *yūthe yūthe*.

[^308-43]: "Manifestation [of power]" — *prakāśa*, "manifestation": the taming of the elephant (66, note 39).

[^308-44]: "For no reason at all" — *akāraṇe*. "Offended" — *biṛambana* (likewise 78, *biṛambinu*): "humiliation, harassment".

[^308-45]: "Presented himself" — *upasana*. Ahmed Beg is the subahdar of Banapur (lahari 6, 17; lahari 7, 27). The subahdar's submission — cf. BR 15, 85: "That villain, the yavana king, bowed down [before him]." The author exalts Rasika with accounts of miracles (lahari 7, note 41).

[^308-46]: 75–78 are the subahdar's words: "Ishvara Himself, in person" (*īśbara sākṣāte*), "your maya" (78, *tomāra māẏāte*) — the yavana ruler's rapturous avowal; cf. note 40.

[^308-47]: "Stronghold of refuge" — *śaraṇa-pañjara*, lit. "enclosure (cage) of refuge", i.e. sure protection.

[^308-48]: "Untamable" — *duranta* (note 13; likewise 82; in 76 "wicked deed" — *duranta karmma*). "Elephant" — *kuñjara*.

[^308-49]: "In all bodies" — *saba ghaṭe*, lit. "in all vessels". Cf. BG 18.61 (*īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati*).

[^308-50]: 84–87 are the fourteen worlds. The usual list (cf. Bhagavata 5.24): lower — Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talatala, Mahatala, Rasatala, Patala; upper — Bhur, Bhuvar, Svar, Mahar, Jana, Tapa, Satya (Brahmaloka). The author lists them differently: instead of Talatala, "the abode of Mahakurma" (*mahākūrmma sthāna*, the Great Tortoise) and "the place of Padma" (*padma sthāna*, 85); *atitala* is apparently Atala. "Such-and-such a place" — *sei kona sthāna*: the sense is unclear. "Lower worlds" — *bhubanatala*.

[^308-51]: "Bhuvarloka", "Maharloka" — in the 1941 edition *bhubaloka*, *mahaloka*. "It is known" — *prasiddhi*.

[^308-52]: "An ordinary universe" — *sāmānya brahmāṇḍa*: a small universe with one Brahma. "Brahma" — in the 1941 edition *brahma*.

[^308-53]: "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣapati*, lit. "lord of a lakh"; the sense is unclear, taken as "hundreds of thousands [of worlds]". The thought of 89–90: universes are of different sizes, and Hari creates each one.

[^308-54]: Cf. CC Madhya 21: Krishna shows the Brahma of Dvaraka Brahmas with ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten million heads.

[^308-55]: "In the pores of the skin" — *romakūpe*: the universes issue from the pores of Maha-Vishnu (cf. Bhagavata 10.14.11; CC Adi 5).

[^308-56]: "The original light" — *ādi jyoti*; "spotless" — *nirañjana*, "untouched by maya" (likewise 99).

[^308-57]: "Those born as humans" (94) — *manuṣya-janama*. "In a subtle form" — *sūkṣmarūpe*: as the Paramatma.

[^308-58]: Cf. BG 4.7–8.

[^308-59]: "Attacks" — *hiṃse*, *hiṃsā kare*, "does violence, does harm"; "one who does no harm" — *ahiṃsaka*. Likewise 100 ("did no harm").

[^308-60]: "Spoke into the ear" — *śunāilũ*, "caused to hear": initiation (52–53, note 31). "Circling" — *parikramā kariyā* (note 32). "Went off" — *gelena*: an honorific verb form, used of the elephant.

[^308-61]: "King of elephants" — *gajarāja*. "King of the yavanas" — *yabanera rāja*: the subahdar.

[^308-62]: "Is revealed" — *sphure*, "appears, flashes [in the heart]".

[^308-63]: Colophon (note 1): *mattahasti uddhāra* — "The Deliverance of the Maddened Elephant".


## Lahari 9. The Taking of Refuge by the Subahdar Ahmed Beg and the Gajapati Nrisimhadeva

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika sets forth the truth to the subahdar Ahmed Beg with the evidence of the scriptures, and he, falling to the ground, recognizes him as a portion of Narayana; seeing the subahdar's humility, the rajas take shelter of Rasika, and in Banapur a multitude of people become disciples; Raja Harinarayana, the lord of Panchati, persuades the Gajapati Nrisimhadeva to see Rasika; Rasika himself comes to the Gajapati, the king prostrates himself before him and asks him to play the flute, and at the sound of the flute the king and the rajas swoon; declining to sit beside the king, Rasika sets forth the essence of the shastras — service to sadhus, the punishment of those who persecute sadhus, compassion for all beings — and asks the king as alms to give up the killing of living beings; the king gives it up, surrenders wholly to Rasika and honours his command like the command of Jagannatha; following him, the rajas take shelter of Rasika, and the subjects of Utkala become Vaishnavas*

*The ninth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^309-1]
*Ghosha: "O treasury of mercy, O compassionate Shyama!*
*Turn Your attention to the fallen, afflicted people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the deliverer of the fallen!
Be merciful, so that I may compose [a song of your] glory.[^309-2]

**2.** Thus [Rasika] set forth to the subahdar Ahmed Beg
the whole truth with the evidence of the scriptures.[^309-3]

**3.** Hearing the nectarean words from Rasika's mouth,
the subahdar fell to the ground in bliss.

**4.** He offered much praise with humble words;
in his mind he firmly understood [him] to be a portion of Narayana.[^309-4]

**5.** Seeing the subahdar's humility and devotion,
the rajas all took shelter at Rasika's feet.

**6.** A multitude [of people] became disciples in the settlement of Banapur;
the rajas and subjects became intoxicated with prema-bhakti.

**7.** Seeing the manifestation [of power], the rajas became disciples;
Raja Harinarayana came to see [him].[^309-5]

**8.** [He is] the lord of Panchati, greatly blessed by fortune;
all the rajas praise him.[^309-6]

**9.** Seeing Rasika's form, the raja was enchanted;
with his whole being he honoured [his] holy feet.

**10.** Harinarayana says to the Gajapati:
"Behold Rasika's feet!

**11.** [He is] a partial incarnation, [come] to destroy the horrors of Kali;
by Utkala's good fortune Rasika has appeared.[^309-7]

**12.** Quickly behold [his] lotus feet:
by seeing [them] sins are destroyed — [this is] the highest good."

**13.** Harinarayana knows Rasika's greatness;
in many ways he told the Gajapati [of him].[^309-8]

**14.** Hearing this, Nrisimhadeva, glad at heart,
resolved to go and see [his] feet.[^309-9]

**15.** Rasikendra, the indwelling lord, who knows all people,
himself went to the Gajapati and granted [him] his sight.[^309-10]

**16.** A sweet form, a gait like that of a king of elephants,
a gentle, most sweet smile, a beautiful moonlike face;

**17.** clad in fine garments, [with] a fine wrap;
in the hand of the Lord of [our] life — a flute that enchants the world.[^309-11]

**18.** All the singers and musicians who [were] with him
[and] the companions go along [with him], crowd after crowd.[^309-12]

**19.** Prabhu entered the Gajapati's presence;
the raja saw [him] as if he were a second Narayana.[^309-13]

**20.** Agitated, the raja quickly rose
and right [before him] fell prostrate like a rod.[^309-14]

**21.** That raja is the adhikari of Sri Jagannatha;
in many ways he honoured Rasikendrachandra.[^309-15]

**22.** The raja was very happy with Rasikendra;
standing, he gazes [at him] with eyes full of tears.

**23.** With joined palms the raja [says] to Rasika:
"Play the flute — hearing it, I will soothe my ears."[^309-16]

**24.** Hearing this, Rasikachandra, glad at heart —
Prabhu played the flute with his sweet lips.

**25.** The three gramas, the seven svaras, the murchhanas and the rest,
the six ragas that are renowned — [all] he played.[^309-17]

**26.** Hearing it, the raja swooned and lost consciousness;
all the rajas, as many as there were, swooned.[^309-18]

**27.** All say: "Such a flute we have never heard anywhere!
Krishna Himself, the Lord of Vrindavana, has come!"

**28.** As we hear in the Puranas of that sweetness of sound,
such is the flute we hear [from] Rasika-Murari.[^309-19]

**29.** Hearing the flute, all were astonished;
motionless, all listened on.

**30.** Not a word comes from the mouth of anyone in the assembly;
their eyes roll, tears flow unceasingly.[^309-20]

**31.** Hearing the flute, all were immersed in bliss;
having listened a while, the Gajapati makes a request:

**32.** "Sit on the seat, O Rasika-shekhara!"
Hearing this, the king of music replied:[^309-21]

**33.** "It is not fitting to sit beside the Gajapati;
such is the custom at court, [handed down] by succession."[^309-22]

**34.** Having said this, Rasika-chand, on the pretext of these words,
poured forth the nectar of talks on the rasa of Krishna.[^309-23]

**35.** The six shastras, the eighteen Puranas and the rest, as many as there are,
shruti, smriti, the four Vedas and the tantras — [of all] he spoke.[^309-24]

**36.** He speaks of the dharma of firm devotion to Krishna according to all the shastras;
[as] the essence of the shastras he speaks of service to sadhus with a firm heart.[^309-25]

**37.** "The gods, the holy places and the rest bring deliverance after a long time;
by the favour of sadhus — the highest good [at once].[^309-26]

**38.** The guru, Krishna and the sadhus are one and equal;
the heart of the guru and the sadhu is Krishna's own abode.[^309-27]

**39.** Sadhus should be honoured more than Krishna;
when sadhus are served, Krishna rejoices in His heart.[^309-28]

**40.** Narayana always wanders in the company of sadhus;
the dust of the sadhus' feet He makes an ornament for His body.[^309-29]

**41.** Whoever, turned away from Krishna, reviles sadhus —
to him Krishna gives great suffering birth after birth.

**42.** Kamsa, Keshi, Hiranyakashipu, Duryodhana,
Durvasa and others, Kumbhakarna, King Ravana,

**43.** Dantavakra, Shishupala, Naraka and the rest, as many as there were —
reviling sadhus, all lost their lives.[^309-30]

**44.** Devaki, Yashoda, Nanda, Vasu[deva], the line of Yadu —
persecuting them, Kamsa perished.[^309-31]

**45.** Keshi, Agha, Baka, Trina[varta], Putana and the rest, as many as there were —
persecuting the Vrajavasis, they lost their lives.[^309-32]

**46.** King Hiranya, who persecuted Prahlada,
was destroyed by the Husband of Kamala.

**47.** Together with [Hiranya]kashipu, all his wicked followers,
persecuting the sadhu, parted with their lives.

**48.** The five Pandava brothers [were] under Krishna's shelter;
persecuting them, Duryodhana perished.

**49.** Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Ashvatthama, Duhshasana,
the ninety-nine brothers perished through enmity toward the Pandavas.[^309-33]

**50.** Durvasa, best of rishis, having assailed Ambarisha —
Sudarshana caused him great suffering.[^309-34]

**51.** Having offended at Sita's feet, Ravana
perished with all his line, and Kumbhakarna too.

**52.** Dantavakra, Shalva, Shishu[pala] showed enmity [to Him];
Naraka and the rest the god Narayana destroyed.[^309-35]

**53.** Thus whoever persecutes sadhus,
Narayana destroys him together with all his line.

**54.** The Life of the world bears reviling of Himself,
[but] the Beloved of Kamala does not bear reviling of sadhus.[^309-36]

**55.** Such service to sadhus, O raja, perform with firmness —
then [even] the dread at life's end will be destroyed.[^309-37]

**56.** Associating with sadhus, worship the Son of Nanda —
you will surely attain Krishna, the jewel among persons.[^309-38]

**57.** Constantly serve brahmanas [and] Vaishnavas;
be compassionate to all living beings — listen, O best of kings!

**58.** In all beings dwells Krishna, the one Bhagavan;
with your whole being worship the Treasury of compassion.[^309-39]

**59.** Worship Krishna's feet with firm feeling in your heart;
know that all is false — the Son of Nanda alone is true."[^309-40]

**60.** [Thus] Rasika-shekhara explained the six shastras;
hearing, the raja was overwhelmed in every limb with love for Krishna.[^309-41]

**61.** Rasikendra begged as alms [the giving up of] violence to living beings;
hearing [this], the raja rejoiced in his mind.[^309-42]

**62.** From then on he no longer killed living beings;
apart from Jagannatha there was nothing else in his mind.

**63.** He gained great happiness from seeing Rasika;
he heard all [the teaching] from Rasika.

**64.** Giving up everything, he firmly gave his mind to Krishna;
seeing Rasika, he became one wholly surrendered.[^309-43]

**65.** The king gave up the killing of living beings and all the rest;
apart from guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus he has no other goal.

**66.** The maharaja became compassionate to all living beings;
he worshipped Rasika like Narayana.

**67.** Great faith arose [in him] toward Rasikendra;
the king honoured [his] command like [the command] of Jagannatha.[^309-44]

**68.** Seeing the gajapati's devotion, all the rajas
took refuge at Rasika's feet.

**69.** Seeing the [power] manifested by Rasika, the rajas
recognized Rasika as a second portion of Narayana.[^309-45]

**70.** Seeing on earth [this] wondrous manifestation —
Rasika gave prema to the maddened Gopala Dasa —[^309-46]

**71.** [seeing him] whose command even the yavana carries out at the risk of his life,
whose command the gajapati [and] the rajas carry out,[^309-47]

**72.** all began to serve the sadhus;
taking up beads and tilaka, all were adorned [with them].[^309-48]

**73.** Countless rajas [and] subjects became Vaishnavas;
giving up everything, all took refuge in Krishna.[^309-49]

**74.** Rasika's greatness is beyond the reach [even] of Indra and the other gods;
there is nothing to compare with it in the world.[^309-50]

**75.** Of him by whose command the raja serves the sadhus
I have made known a little.[^309-51]

**76.** The abode of Utkala was flooded with prema;
the Treasury of compassion showed mercy to all beings.

**77.** Rasika-shekhara — boundless greatness [and] virtues;
bestowing prema-bhakti, he overwhelmed everyone.

**78.** Even speaking with a hundred mouths one does not reach the limit of [his] qualities;
by his grace I have composed a little.

**79.** "Rasika-mangala" is supremely full of rasa:
hearing it, all beings, cross [the ocean of] the age of Kali![^309-52]

**80.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus ends the ninth lahari in the Pashchima-vibhaga of "Sri Rasika-mangala," called "The Taking of Refuge by the Subahdar Ahmed Beg and the Gajapati Nrisimhadeva."*[^309-53]

[^309-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("নবম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2; Pashchima 6, note 1). Ghosha: *kṛpānidhi he daẏāra śyāma / patita durgati jane kara abadhāna*; "Shyama" here is apparently Shyamananda (cf. 1: "deliverer of the fallen"); it may also be understood as Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে সুবা আহম্মদীবেগ ও গজপতি নৃসিংহদেবের শরণ-গ্রহণ-নাম নবম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*subā āhammadībega o gajapati nṛsiṃhadebera śaraṇa-grahaṇa*) — "The Taking of Refuge by the Subahdar Ahmed Beg and the Gajapati Nrisimhadeva". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^309-2]: "So that I may compose [a song of your] glory" — *yaśaḥ yena kariẏe racana*.

[^309-3]: "Thus" — with Rasika's speech (lahari 8, 80–102). Ahmed Beg — here *ahammadabega*; the subahdar of Banapur (lahari 6, 17; lahari 7, 27). "With the evidence of the scriptures" — *nigama-pramāṇe*.

[^309-4]: "A portion of Narayana" — *nārāyaṇa-aṃśa*; likewise "a partial incarnation" (11), "as if a second Narayana" (19), "the indwelling lord" (15) — rapturous words of the author and his characters. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation (Pashchima 2, note 28; Pashchima 7, note 36; Pashchima 8, note 29); on how the author exalts Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. The subahdar's submission — cf. BR 15, 85: "That villain, the yavana king, bowed down [before him]."

[^309-5]: "The manifestation [of power]" — *prakāśa* (lahari 8, 66, 71; note 39 there): the taming of the elephant. Raja Harinarayana (*harinārāẏaṇa*; in 10, *hari nārāẏaṇa*) is unidentified.

[^309-6]: Panchati — *pañcaṭī*; the domain is unidentified. "Blessed by fortune" — *bhāgyabān*. "Praise" — *bākhāna*.

[^309-7]: Gajapati ("lord of elephants") is the title of the kings of Orissa; here Nrisimhadeva (14), apparently Narasimhadeva of the Bhoi dynasty, who ruled from Khurda in the first half of the 17th century (the identification is tentative). BR 15 says nothing of Rasikananda meeting the Gajapati; the author exalts Rasika with an account of the king's reverence for him (cf. note 4). "The horrors of Kali" — *kalighora*. "Has appeared" — *haila pracāra*, "became known, manifested himself".

[^309-8]: "Knows" — *jāne*: Harinarayana apparently already knew Rasika's greatness.

[^309-9]: Nrisimhadeva — *nṛsiṃhadeba* (cf. note 7).

[^309-10]: "The indwelling lord" — *antaryāmī*; "who knows all people" — *jñāta sarbajana*: Rasika, knowing the king's intention, goes to him himself (cf. note 4).

[^309-11]: "A gait like that of a king of elephants" (16) — *gajendra-gamana*, a traditional comparison for a stately gait. "Fine" — *jhina* (*jhīna*). "Wrap" — *ācchādana*. "The Lord of [our] life" — *prāṇapati*: here apparently Rasika (cf. 23–24, where he plays the flute).

[^309-12]: "Singers and musicians" — *saṅgīta-sāhitya* (lahari 6, note 19; lahari 7, note 31).

[^309-13]: "Second" — *dbitī* (*dvitīya*).

[^309-14]: "Agitated" — *āsta byasta*, "hurriedly, in agitation". "Like a rod" — *daṇḍabata*: stretched full length.

[^309-15]: "Adhikari" — *adhikārī*, "one who holds the right [of service], the superintendent": the Gajapati is revered as the foremost servant of Jagannatha of Puri.

[^309-16]: "Play the flute" — *muralī bājāo*. "Soothe my ears" — *juṛāi śrabaṇe*, lit. "cool [my] ears".

[^309-17]: Gramas (*grāma*), svaras (*sbara*), murchhanas (*mūrcchanā*) are terms of Indian music theory: the basic scales, the seven degrees of the scale, and modal sequences. "The six ragas" — the six principal ragas. Rasika's flute-playing is not in BR 15 (cf. note 4).

[^309-18]: "Swooned" — *mūrcchita*: an echo of *mūrcchanā* (25).

[^309-19]: "In the Puranas" — on Krishna's flute in the Bhagavata (10.21; 10.35).

[^309-20]: "Not a word comes from the mouth" — *bāṇī nāhi sare*. "Roll" — *ghūrṇita*, "whirl".

[^309-21]: "The king of music" — *saṅgīta rāẏa*: apparently an epithet of Rasika (cf. 24–25); it may also be understood as a name (Sangita-raya) — unclear.

[^309-22]: "By succession" — *paramparā*. Out of humility Rasika does not sit beside the king.

[^309-23]: "On the pretext of these words" — *ei kathā chale*. "Poured forth" — *udgāre*.

[^309-24]: "The six shastras" — *ṣaṛ-śāstra*: the six philosophical systems (darshanas). "The four Vedas and the tantras" — *cāribeda-tantra*.

[^309-25]: "Firm devotion to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇaniṣṭhā*. "Service to sadhus" — in the 1941 edition *sādhuselā*, apparently a misprint for *sādhusebā*. 37–58 are apparently Rasika's words (note the address "O raja" in 55, 57).

[^309-26]: Cf. Bhagavata 10.48.31 (*na hy am-mayāni tīrthāni na devā mṛc-chilā-mayāḥ / te punanty uru-kālena darśanād eva sādhavaḥ*). "Bring deliverance" — *uddhāraẏe*; "after a long time" — *cirakāle*. "By the favour" — *prasannete*.

[^309-27]: Cf. Bhagavata 9.4.68 (*sādhavo hṛdayaṃ mahyaṃ sādhūnāṃ hṛdayaṃ tv aham*).

[^309-28]: Cf. Padma Purana (*ārādhanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣṇor ārādhanaṃ param / tasmāt parataraṃ devi tadīyānāṃ samarcanam*; CC Madhya 11) and Bhagavata 11.19.21 (*mad-bhakta-pūjābhyadhikā*).

[^309-29]: Cf. Bhagavata 11.14.16 (*anuvrajāmy ahaṃ nityaṃ pūyeyety aṅghri-reṇubhiḥ*).

[^309-30]: 42–53 list the enemies of the sadhus and of the Lord from the Puranas and itihasas; "lost their lives" — *prāṇe haila hata*, "were struck down". Durvasa (42, 50) is not an asura but a great sage who offended King Ambarisha (note 34).

[^309-31]: "Vasu[deva]" — *basu*. "Persecuting" — *hiṃsana kari'* (likewise 45–53: *hiṃsā*). "Perished" — *kṣaẏa haila*.

[^309-32]: Keshi, Agha, Baka, Trinavarta (*tṛṇā*), Putana — asuras sent by Kamsa to Vraja (Bhagavata, Canto 10).

[^309-33]: "The ninety-nine brothers" — *ūnaśata bhāi*: the sons of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana's brothers. Bhishma is revered as a devotee (one of the twelve mahajanas), and Ashvatthama, according to the Mahabharata, survived (cursed by Krishna); the author lists them among those who perished in the war against the Pandavas.

[^309-34]: Bhagavata 9.4–5: the Sudarshana disc pursued Durvasa until he begged Ambarisha's forgiveness.

[^309-35]: Shalva, Shishupala (*śiśu*), Dantavakra — enemies of Krishna (Bhagavata 10.74–78); Naraka is Narakasura (Bhagavata 10.59).

[^309-36]: "The Life of the world" — *jagata-jībana*; "the Beloved of Kamala" — *kamalā-ramaṇa*, the Husband of Lakshmi (likewise 46, "the Husband of Kamala").

[^309-37]: "The dread at life's end" — *maraṇe udbege*. "Will be destroyed" — *dhbaṃsana habe*.

[^309-38]: "The jewel among persons" — *puruṣaratana*.

[^309-39]: Rasika's instruction continues in 59.

[^309-40]: The portion begins. "Son of Nanda" — *nandasuta*. "All is false" — *saba mithyā*: everything other than Krishna is transient.

[^309-41]: "Six shastras" — *ṣaṛ śāstra* (cf. 35, note 24). "Overwhelmed" — *jara jara*, "broken, overcome" (likewise 77).

[^309-42]: "Begged as alms" — *bhikṣā māgilena*: as a Vaishnava, Rasika asks the king not for gifts but for the renunciation of *jībahiṃsā* — the killing of animals (hunting, sacrifices). This vow of the gajapati and his meeting with Rasika are not mentioned in BR 15 (note 7); the author exalts Rasika with an account of the king's submission to him.

[^309-43]: "Wholly surrendered" — *ananyaśaraṇa*, "having no other refuge" (likewise 73: "took refuge").

[^309-44]: "Like Narayana," "like [the command] of Jagannatha" — *nārāẏaṇa sama*, *jagannātha sama*: the author's rapturous words on the king's reverence for Rasika (note 4).

[^309-45]: "[Power] manifested" — *prakāśa* (note 5). "A second portion of Narayana" — *dbitīẏāṃśa nārāẏaṇa*; cf. 19 ("as though a second Narayana," note 13). The rajas' rapturous acclamation; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda (note 4; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^309-46]: "Manifestation" — *parakāśa* (= *prakāśa*). Gopala Dasa is the elephant initiated by Rasika (lahari 8, note 34). "Maddened" — *matta*, "in musth," the elephant's standing epithet (lahari 8); here the word can also mean "intoxicated [with prema]". 70–72 form one sentence.

[^309-47]: "The yavana" — the subahdar Ahmed Beg (lahari 8, 73–103). "At the risk of his life" — *prāṇapaṇe*, "with all his might". The second line can also be taken as "whose command the gajapati [has] the rajas carry out" (*kare rājāgaṇe*).

[^309-48]: "Beads and tilaka" — *mālā se tilaka*: tulasi beads and the Vaishnava tilaka on the forehead, the marks of a Vaishnava. "Were adorned" — *haila śobhā*.

[^309-49]: "Countless" — *ananta*.

[^309-50]: "Beyond the reach" — *agocara*; "Indra and the other gods" — *debendrādi*.

[^309-51]: "Him by whose command" — Rasika; "the raja" — the gajapati. "Made known" — *karilũ pracāre*.

[^309-52]: "Full of rasa" — *rasāla*, "juicy, delightful". "Cross" — *tara*: imperative; it can also be taken as "cross" in the indicative.

[^309-53]: Colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে সুবা আহম্মদীবেগ ও গজপতি নৃসিংহদেবের শরণ-গ্রহণ-নাম নবম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (note 1). Lahari 9 runs 1–80.


## Lahari 10. The Guru-Devotion and Sadhu-Service of the Elephant Gopala Dasa

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; after some days in Banapur, Rasika sets out to see Shyamananda, but the ruler of Hijli carries off his disciples, the singers Shyamadasa and Mohana; Rasika refuses food and returns to Banapur, and the rajas secure their release; the elephant Gopala Dasa comes to Rasika, hears Krishna-katha and goes off to wander among the holy places; when Rasika and his companions lose their way in the forest and are left without food, the elephant brings them rice from a householder; Rasika instructs him to serve the sadhus, and the elephant becomes a great Vaishnava, while Rasika's touch purifies people of every class; a description of Rasika's form; at night Jagannatha commands Rasika to manifest Him as Sri Govinda, and Rasika meets two brother craftsmen from Nilachala, Raghunatha and Ananda; convinced of Jagannatha's command, he longs in bliss to see Govinda*

*The tenth lahari.*

*Raga Dhanashri.*[^310-1]
*Ghosha: "Blessed, blessed is the glory of Gopala!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the friend of all,
the deliverer of the poor and lowly, the ocean of compassion![^310-2]

**2.** Having stayed some days in Banapur,
Rasikendra set out to see Shyamananda.

**3.** Having seen Jagannatha, he goes along the roads
together with his disciples — Shyamadasa, Mohana and others.[^310-3]

**4.** Formerly Shyamadasa [and] Mohana had been with the ruler of Hijli:
[they were] excellent singers.

**5.** On the road the ruler of Hijli saw them
and, turning both back, took them away with him.[^310-4]

**6.** Going back, [he] arrived at Banapur;
where [Rasika was, there came] a companion [and] reported at [his] feet.[^310-5]

**7.** Hearing [this], Rasika took no more food;
Prabhu turned back and went to Banapur.

**8.** Seeing [him], all the rajas rejoiced;
[but,] hearing of the fast, all were alarmed.

**9.** By many means [they] obtained the release of the two disciples
and brought both brothers to Rasika.[^310-6]

**10.** Having got both back, Prabhu was delighted;
finishing his meal and so on, he stayed there that day.

**11.** That night he spent in bliss in sankirtana;
the elephant Sri Gopala Dasa heard [of it] with his own ears.[^310-7]

**12.** Rasikendra again set out on his way;
[the elephant] resolved in his mind: "I shall see Prabhu."[^310-8]

**13.** The maddened best of elephants came, leaving the forest;
slowly, slowly he went, full of eagerness.

**14.** Prabhu, sitting in seclusion, is chanting the Hari-nama;
the maddened elephant came [and] entered that place.

**15.** Seeing Rasika, the elephant fell at [his] feet;
with his tears he washed both [his] feet.

**16.** Again prostrating like a staff, again circling [him],
again and again that maddened elephant gazes [at him].[^310-9]

**17.** Rasika spoke Krishna-katha [to him] in many ways;
he explained [to him] the essence of the shastras — the "Bhagavata" [and] the "Gita".[^310-10]

**18.** Hearing [this], the elephant gained divine knowledge:
he knew for certain that all is false, Krishna is the truth.

**19.** In tears [and] thrilling [at] Rasika's feet,
taking his leave, the elephant went into the forest.

**20.** The maddened best of elephants set off to wander among the holy places;
[his] body and heart were overwhelmed with the bliss of Krishna.[^310-11]

**21.** Going some distance ahead, he stayed in the forest,
in meditation on Rasika's feet, in [their] shelter [and] in bhajana.

**22.** At that time Rasikendra went on from there;
in the forest evening fell, [and they] lost their way.

**23.** All around there are no villages — a vast wasteland;
they stopped beneath a tree in the forest.[^310-12]

**24.** He remains without food together with many Vaishnavas;
to that place the elephant came in great joy.

**25.** He saw that all had lain down to sleep without food;
at once the elephant went off with the speed of the wind.

**26.** In his mind he knows where what provisions are to be found;
he came to a certain householder.

**27.** From his house he brought a bundle of rice;
the other provisions were with Rasika.

**28.** Knowing there was no rice, the best of elephants took [it]
[and] came to Rasika's feet.[^310-13]

**29.** Tired from the road, everyone was asleep;
the elephant bows at Rasika's feet.

**30.** Seeing the elephant, Rasikendra rose;
alarmed in his mind, he remembered Krishna.

**31.** Leaving sleep, all meditate on Krishna in their hearts:
"Today the elephant will take everyone's life!"[^310-14]

**32.** Knowing everyone's thoughts, the maddened best of elephants
placed the bundle of rice before Rasika.

**33.** He himself, going into the forest, stayed some distance away;
seeing the rice, Rasika-shekhara says —

**34.** he gave the command to the brahmanas to cook:
"All the sadhus are sorely tormented by hunger."[^310-15]

**35.** Hearing the command, the companions quickly set to [work];
cooking [the food], they feed the sadhus.

**36.** Afterwards Prabhu Rasika-shekhara sat [to eat];
to that place came the maddened best of elephants.[^310-16]

**37.** Seeing for himself the sadhus eating,
he fell to the ground, his body stretched out like a staff.

**38.** Circling [him], the fortunate king of elephants,
gazing at Rasika, meditates [on him].[^310-17]

**39.** He has no wish to go away [from him];
his whole body thrills, his eyes are full of tears.

**40.** Rasika was delighted seeing the elephant;
placing his hand on his head, he speaks, praising [him]:

**41.** "With firm faith serve the sadhus constantly;
wander from holy place to holy place.

**42.** Never do harm to the sadhus;
always serve the Vaishnavas [and] brahmanas."

**43.** [Thus] he told the maddened best of elephants the whole of dharma;
from then on the elephant always roams from land to land.[^310-18]

**44.** The story of Gopala Dasa cannot be told:
the mahashaya became prema-bhakti embodied.[^310-19]

**45.** Constantly he remembers the name of Krishna;
happy at heart, he wanders from forest to forest.

**46.** A place of Krishna, a place of a brahmana, a place of a Vaishnava —
he circles them from afar and [so] goes [on].[^310-20]

**47.** If good people are staying in the dense forest,
the elephant brings [and] gives [them] all provisions in that place.[^310-21]

**48.** Thus he constantly serves the sadhus;
the maddened best of elephants became a great Vaishnava.

**49.** When he comes into someone's field —
whoever [there] speaks, uttering the name of Rasika,

**50.** bowing to him, he leaves that place.
Even with a hundred mouths the elephant's qualities cannot be described.[^310-22]

**51.** By the power of the feet of such [a] Rasika
the elephant gladly serves hundreds and hundreds of sadhus.

**52.** Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas, various low castes —
by Rasika's touch all became pure in mind.[^310-23]

**53.** Seeing [him], all gave up their [former] nature;
rajas [and] subjects became great Vaishnavas.[^310-24]

**54.** All the lands overflowed with love for Krishna;
by Rasika's touch all became wholly surrendered.

**55.** There is nothing to compare with Rasika's greatness:
he possesses all virtues, [he is] the splendour of beauty.

**56.** There is no one equal to him in the world;
[he is] the friend, refuge [and] brother of the poor, the lowly, the suffering.[^310-25]

**57.** Rasika-shekhara, whose emblem is love for the devotees,
[is] a great ocean of mercy, the son of Achyuta.[^310-26]

**58.** How [wondrous] that sweet smile, those soft, soft words!
How [wondrous] that glance of eyes [like] lotus petals![^310-27]

**59.** How [wondrous] that unhurried gait, the gait of a king of elephants!
How [wondrous] that enchanting form that enchants the three worlds!

**60.** How [wondrous] the swaying of the arms, surpassing an elephant's trunk!
How [wondrous] those exceedingly tender two feet!

**61.** How [wondrous] the beautiful book in that tender hand!
How [wondrous] the remembrance of Krishna's name on those lips![^310-28]

**62.** How [wondrous] that sweet form, enchanting the world!
That face, once seen, steals the minds of the three worlds.

**63.** How [wondrous] those streams from the eyes that flow ceaselessly!
How [wondrous] that thrill in the body — beyond words!

**64.** How [wondrous] the radiance of that body — it enchants the people of the world!
How [wondrous] the colour of those lips, [how] the rows of teeth shine!

**65.** How [wondrous] that high forehead adorned with tilaka!
How [wondrous] that nose, [how] beautiful the conch-like neck![^310-29]

**66.** How [wondrous] that broad, broad chest!
How [wondrous] the charming garment shining on that waist!

**67.** How [wondrous] that dark body — it enchants the people of the world!
Hearing those sweet words, the heart rejoices.[^310-30]

**68.** Hundreds and hundreds of people come and look [at him];
no one wishes to go away.

**69.** In all the lands he manifested prema-bhakti;
[people,] becoming wholly surrendered, turned their minds to Krishna.

**70.** At that time Rasikendra is coming along the road;
at night Jagannatha unexpectedly gave [him] a command:

**71.** "Manifest Me there —
[as] Sri Govinda-raya, the graceful form bent in three places.

**72.** In His heart I shall constantly sport;
the three worlds will worship My feet.

**73.** As in Nilachala everyone serves [Me],
such faith [in Me] will there be in that place of yours."[^310-31]

**74.** Hearing these words with his own ears,
Rasika told everyone of Krishna's command, heard with his ears.[^310-32]

**75.** At that time the craftsmen Raghunatha [and] Ananda
unexpectedly met with Rasika.

**76.** They are two brothers born of one mother, residents of Nilachala,
[like] Vishvakarma, skilled in the shilpa-shastra.[^310-33]

**77.** Seeing [them], the son of Achyuta was delighted;
taking both brothers with him, he went on his way.

**78.** In his mind he understood for certain the command of Jagabandhu:
"The Friend of the three worlds will surely become manifest."[^310-34]

**79.** Rasikendra-chandra floats in an ocean of bliss:
"When will such good fortune come — that I shall see Govinda?"[^310-35]

**80.** The account of Rasikachandra cannot be told:
the world honoured [him] as equal to Narayana.[^310-36]

**81.** The blinding darkness of sin was destroyed on earth:
Rasikendra-chandra shone forth in Utkala.[^310-37]

**82.** The *Rasika-mangala* is a song of Rasika's virtues;
hearing it, destroy the pain of the bonds of worldly existence.[^310-38]

**83.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the tenth lahari, called "The Guru-Devotion and Sadhu-Service of the Elephant Gopala Dasa."*[^310-39]

[^310-1]: The lines before the raga are the lahari's heading ("দশম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Dhanashri (*dhānaśrī*; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 1). The ghosha is *dhanya dhanya gopālera yaśa nāre*; Gopala is apparently the elephant Gopala Dasa, the hero of this lahari (lahari 8, note 34); it may also be taken as Krishna. *nāre* is unclear: possibly a sung particle (*nā re*; cf. *mana mohanā re* in Dakshina, lahari 12) or "cannot" (*nāre* = *nā pāre*: "Gopala's glory cannot [be told]"). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে গোপালদাস-হস্তীর গুরুভক্তি ও সাধুসেবা-নাম দশম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*gopāladāsa-hastīra gurubhakti o sādhusebā*) — "The Guru-Devotion and Sadhu-Service of the Elephant Gopala Dasa". Lahari 10 runs 1–83. The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^310-2]: "The friend of all" — *akhilera bandhu*. "The deliverer of the poor and lowly" — *dīnahīna-tāraṇa*.

[^310-3]: "Set out" — *bijaẏa karilā*, said respectfully of a holy man's departure. "Having seen Jagannatha" — apparently in Puri (Nilachala); the author says nothing more about this. Shyamadasa (*śyāmadāsa*) and Mohana (*mohana*) are disciples of Rasika; not identified. "Along the roads" — *pathe pathe*.

[^310-4]: "Had been with the ruler of Hijli" — *chilā hijalī-adhipati sthāne*: apparently they had served as singers at his court. On Hijli see Purva, lahari 10, note 21; the ruler is not named here. "Excellent singers" — *baṛa sugāẏana*. "Turning back" — *phirāiẏā*: making them turn round. Rasika's dealings with rulers are as the author tells them; this episode is not mentioned in BR 15.

[^310-5]: The subject of the first line is not expressed; taken as the ruler of Hijli, returning with the singers to Banapur (where the rajas of Orissa were kept with the subahdar; Pashchima, lahari 7, note 21). It may also be read "[they] arrived". "Where [Rasika was]" — *yathāsthāne*, "at the place". "A companion" — *anucara*: one of Rasika's companions.

[^310-6]: 7: "Took no more food" — *āra nā kaila bhojana*: Rasika fasts until his disciples are returned. "Were alarmed" — *tarāsa* (*trāsa*). "Obtained the release" — *ānila chāṛāñā*, "brought, having freed". "By many means" — *bahurūpe*. "Brothers" — *bhāi*: apparently spiritual brothers (disciples of one guru).

[^310-7]: Gopala Dasa is the elephant initiated by Rasika (lahari 8, note 34); the author speaks of him in the respectful form (*śunilena*, "heard"). "Heard with his own ears" — *śunilena karṇe*: the elephant heard the sankirtana.

[^310-8]: The subject of the second line is not expressed; taken as the elephant (cf. 13).

[^310-9]: "Prostrating like a staff" — *daṇḍabata*: lying full length. "Circling" — *parikramā*, in token of reverence (lahari 8, note 32).

[^310-10]: The "Bhagavata" and the "Gita" — the "Srimad-Bhagavatam" and the "Bhagavad-gita". "The essence of the shastras" — *śāstratattva*.

[^310-11]: "To wander among the holy places" — *tīrtha-paryaṭane*. "Overwhelmed" — *jara jara*.

[^310-12]: "A vast wasteland" — *baṛa tepāntara*: an uninhabited plain. The subject of 22–24 is Rasika and his companions; "he" in 24 is Rasika.

[^310-13]: The elephant bringing rice to the hungry Vaishnavas is a miracle told by the author; cf. BR 15, 84: Rasikananda "engaged [the elephant] in the service of Krishna and the Vaishnavas" (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 19). "A bundle of rice" — *taṇḍulera puṛā*: a parcel (usually of straw or leaves) of husked rice. "The other provisions" — *upadrabya*. "Took" — *naila*. "Came" — *uttarila*, "arrived".

[^310-14]: "Alarmed" — *saṅkucita haiẏā*, lit. "shrinking [with fear]". "Remembered" — *saṅariẏā*. 31: the companions' thought: this is the same elephant that had once ravaged Banapur (laharis 7–8).

[^310-15]: "The brahmanas" — *dbijagaṇe*: the brahmanas among the companions, who cook the food. Lines 33–34 form one sentence.

[^310-16]: "Afterwards" — *paścāte*: after the sadhus had eaten.

[^310-17]: "King of elephants" — *gajendra*; "fortunate" — *bhāgyabān*.

[^310-18]: "The whole of dharma" — *sarba dharma*: all that it befits him to do. "Roams from land to land" — *phire deśāntare*.

[^310-19]: "Embodied" — *mūrtimanta*. "Mahashaya" — a respectful form of address; here, of the elephant.

[^310-20]: "A place of Krishna" — a temple; "a place of a brahmana, a place of a Vaishnava" — their dwellings; "circles them from afar" — *dūra haite parikramā kari'*: in token of reverence, without coming near. "Goes" — *yāna*, respectful form.

[^310-21]: "Good people" — *sujana*: sadhus. "All provisions" — *sarbadrabya*.

[^310-22]: "Into a field" — *kṛṣite*: wild elephants commonly ravage crops. 49–50: if anyone utters Rasika's name, the elephant bows and leaves the field.

[^310-23]: Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas, low castes — *hūna se pulinda mleccha nānā antyajāti* (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 11; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 4). "By the touch" — *paraśe* (*sparśe*) (likewise 54).

[^310-24]: "Seeing [him]" — *darśane*, "at the sight". "Their [former] nature" — *āpanāra sbabhāba*.

[^310-25]: "The splendour of beauty" (55) — *lābaṇya-garimā*. "Equal" — *paṭāntara*, lit. "difference", i.e. one who could compare with him. "Brother" — *sodara*, "brother born of the same mother".

[^310-26]: "Whose emblem is love for the devotees" — *bhakata-batsala-bānā*: *bānā* — "sign, vow, garb"; "loving to His devotees" (*bhakta-vatsala*) is an epithet of the Lord, here applied to Rasika. "The son of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kumāra*: Rasika.

[^310-27]: 58–67 describe Rasika's form; *kibā se* is an exclamation: "how [wondrous] that…". Such descriptions are usual for the form of Krishna and of Sri Chaitanya; the author transfers them to Rasika (cf. note 26).

[^310-28]: "Book" — *grantha*: apparently the "Bhagavata" (cf. 17). "Remembrance" — *saṅaraṇa* (*smaraṇa*): Krishna's name on his lips.

[^310-29]: "Conch-like neck" — *kambukaṇṭha*: a neck with three folds like the whorls of a conch, a mark of beauty.

[^310-30]: "Dark" — *śyāmala*: dark like a cloud, the colour of Krishna.

[^310-31]: Jagannatha's command is as the author tells it; according to BR 15, 81, it was Shyamananda who entrusted Rasika with the service of Sri Govinda in Gopivallabhapur; in the next lahari (11) Shyamananda likewise gives Govinda His name and orders the Deity to be made. "At night" — *rātre*: apparently in a dream. "Manifest Me" — *āmāra prakāśa tumi karaha*: install My Deity. "There" — *tathāẏa*: in Gopivallabhapur (cf. 73: "in that place of yours"). Sri Govinda-raya is the Deity of Gopivallabhapur (BR 15, 81); *tribhaṅga*, "bent in three places," is the form of Krishna with the flute; *lalita*, "graceful". "In His heart" — *tā'ra hṛde*: apparently in the heart of [the Deity] Govinda; Jagannatha promises to dwell in Him (according to Vaishnava teaching the Deity is the Lord Himself, the archa-avatara). It may also be taken as "in his heart" — Rasika's. "Sport" — *biharibe*. Nilachala is Puri.

[^310-32]: "Krishna's command" — *kṛṣṇa-ājñā*: Jagannatha is Krishna.

[^310-33]: Raghunatha and Ananda (*raghunātha ānanda*; in lahari 11, 7 — *raghu ānanda*) are master craftsmen who carve Deities; not identified. "Craftsmen" — *kāmilā*: apparently from Arabic-Persian *kāmil*, "perfect, skilled"; the sense is unclear. Vishvakarma is the architect of the gods; by tradition he carved Jagannatha. The shilpa-shastra is the science of sculpture and architecture, including the making of Deities.

[^310-34]: The subject is Rasika (77: "the son of Achyuta"). "For certain" — *niśce* (*niścaẏa*). Jagabandhu (*jagabandhu*, "friend of the world") is Jagannatha (Purva, lahari 2, note 28), who commanded Rasika to manifest the Deity of Govinda (70–73). "The Friend of the three worlds" — *trailokyera bandhu*: Sri Govinda, who is to become manifest in Gopivallabhapur (lahari 11).

[^310-35]: "Such good fortune" — *hena bhāgya*.

[^310-36]: "As equal to Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa sama*: the author's words of rapture; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation (Pashchima, lahari 9, note 4; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^310-37]: "The blinding darkness of sin" — *pāpa-timirāndha*. "Shone forth" — *prakāśila*, "appeared, became manifest". Utkala — *utakala*.

[^310-38]: "A song of virtues" — *guṇagāthā*. "Destroy" — *dhbaṃsana kara*; "the pain of the bonds of worldly existence" — *bhababandha-byathā*.

[^310-39]: Colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে গোপালদাস-হস্তীর গুরুভক্তি ও সাধুসেবা-নাম দশম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (note 1).


## Lahari 11. The Manifestation of the Deity of Sri Govinda in Sri Gopivallabhapur
