*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika comes to Shyamananda in Thuriya, who embraces him and asks about the events in Banapur; the companions tell of the elephant and all the rest, Rasika offers Shyamananda clothes, ornaments and jewels, and they spend days and nights in talk of Krishna; Rasika presents the craftsman brothers Raghu and Ananda, Shyamananda manifests a Deity and names Him Vrindavanachandra, and bids Rasika manifest Sri Govinda in Gopivallabhapur with the craftsmen; on an auspicious day Govinda-raya becomes manifest, Rasika rewards the craftsmen, installs the Deity in the temple and holds a great festival; thereafter he lives at home in the service of Govinda, in sankirtana and in service to guru, Krishna and the sadhus*

*The eleventh lahari.*

*Raga Kamoda — panchali metre.*[^311-1]

**1.** Glory to Shyamananda, conqueror of the world,
lord of all the worlds!
Life of the world, life of Rasika —
may I sing [his] virtues every day.[^311-2]

**2.** After some days the son of Achyuta went
to see Shyamananda.
In the town of Thuriya Rasika-shekhara
saw the feet of Prabhu.[^311-3]

**3.** Seeing [him], Shyamananda — great was Prabhu's joy —
lifted [him] up and embraced [him].
He seated [him] at his side and asked about everything —
all the pastimes in Banapur.[^311-4]

**4.** Hearing Shyamananda's words, Rasikendra
[sits] with head bowed from shyness.
The companions [who were] with him tell in detail
of the pastimes as they were, as is fitting.[^311-5]

**5.** They told of the naming of the king of elephants and the rest, of the renowned [deed];
hearing it, [Shyamananda] was delighted.
Having finished their meal and so on, they sit as an assembly;
Sri Shyamananda took his seat.[^311-6]

**6.** Clothes, ornaments, many jewels and riches
Rasika offered there.
In the rasa of talks about Krishna they sat absorbed,
knowing neither night nor day.[^311-7]

**7.** Quickly bringing Raghu [and] Ananda,
[Rasika] presented [them] to Prabhu:
"These two are truly the form of Vishvakarma," —
he tells everything in detail.[^311-8]

**8.** Hearing this, Prabhu Shyamananda, delighted,
manifested a shri-murti.
"Vrindavanachandra" — with joy in his heart
he gave Him this name.[^311-9]

**9.** Shyamananda says to Rasikendra-chandra:
"Go quickly.
Take the craftsmen and have a shri-murti made
in Sri Gopivallabhapur.[^311-10]

**10.** His name [will be] Sri Govinda, the incomparable;
He will become manifest in the world."
Hearing the command with his own ears, [Rasika] asked leave to depart —
with him the two brothers.[^311-11]

**11.** Reckoning an auspicious day, [when] all the good omens [were present],
Govinda-raya became manifest.
Seeing each of [His] limbs, Ananga is enchanted;
all float in bliss.[^311-12]

**12.** Seeing that form, Rasika in bliss —
[so] the command in the dream was confirmed —
gave the craftsmen many goods by the load
as a nichhani offering for Govinda's form.[^311-13]

**13.** Bringing Govinda and installing [Him] in the temple,
he began a great festival.
Bringing brahmanas, [having them] recite the shruti,
he did everything according to rule.[^311-14]

**14.** A great, great festival, a festival of bliss —
who can tell the limit of that happiness?
The virtues and pastimes of Krishna — that is his play;
Rasika is lost in happiness.[^311-15]

**15.** Thus in manifold delights, in great bliss —
Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of devotees],
ever [immersed in] the *Bhagavata*, intoxicated with the rasa of Krishna,
the jewel among all virtues.[^311-16]

**16.** For many, many days in his own home
he remains in the rasa of serving Krishna;
always in sankirtana, raining tears,
knowing neither night nor day.[^311-17]

**17.** On the form of Govinda, the embodiment of bliss,
he gazes constantly;
at the base of [His] lotus feet, with tulasi leaves,
Rasika-shekhara worships [Him].[^311-18]

**18.** Whether at home or in other lands —
[always] service to guru, Krishna and the sadhus.
Rasika's characteristics are wondrous [even] to tell;
who in the world compares [with him]?[^311-19]

**19.** Rasika's true nature is the very form of prema-bhakti;
seeing [it], all are amazed.
The people of the world, filled with prema,
held worldly existence to be false.[^311-20]

**20.** The *Rasika-mangala* — billows of bliss;
listen, all people!
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^311-21]

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eleventh lahari, called "The Manifestation of the Deity of Sri Govinda in Sri Gopivallabhapur."*[^311-22]

[^311-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("একাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 11 begins. Raga Kamoda (*kāmoda*; Dakshina, lahari 9, note 1). "Panchali metre" (*pā̃cālī chanda*) — tripadi; in the edition each stanza is set in four lines and is translated so (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুরে শ্রীগোবিন্দ-বিগ্রহ-প্রকাশ-নাম একাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīgopīballabhapure śrīgobinda-bigraha-prakāśa*) — "The Manifestation of the Deity of Sri Govinda in Sri Gopivallabhapur".

[^311-2]: "Conqueror of the world" — *bhubana bijaya*; it may also be understood as "[whose] coming [graces] the world" (*bijaya* is also the "arrival, procession" of a holy person). "Lord of all the worlds" — *akhila bhubana-pati*, "life of the world" — *jagata-jībana*: the author's rapturous titles for Shyamananda; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shyamananda is a devotee, a servant of the Lord (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "Life of Rasika" — *rasika-parāṇa*: Shyamananda is Rasika's guru. "May I sing" — *guṇa gāi yena niti*, literally "that I may sing [his] virtues daily".

[^311-3]: "After some days" — *kata dine*: after the events in Banapur (laharis 7–10). "The son of Achyuta" — *acyutera bālā*, literally "the boy of Achyuta" (Pashchima, lahari 5, note 30). Thuriya (*thuriyā*; "town" — *nagara*) is unidentified; Shyamananda lives there (lahari 12, 2). Prabhu is Shyamananda.

[^311-4]: "Great was Prabhu's joy" — *prabhura ānanda*; Prabhu is Shyamananda. "Embraced" — *kole karila*, literally "took onto his lap, pressed to his breast". Banapur — Pashchima, lahari 6, note 1; "the pastimes in Banapur" are the meeting with the subahdar Ahmed Beg, the taming of the elephant and the Gajapati (laharis 7–10).

[^311-5]: "With head bowed" — *heṭamāthe*. "The companions [who were] with him tell" — *saṅge saṅgigaṇe kahe bibaraṇe*: understood as Rasika keeping silent from shyness while his companions tell the story; it may also be read "together with his companions [Rasika] tells". "As is fitting" — *yathocite*.

[^311-6]: "The king of elephants" — *gajendra*: the elephant Sri Gopala Dasa (lahari 8, 58, note 34; lahari 10). "The naming and the rest" — *nāmādi*. "The renowned [deed]" — *prasiddhi*, "fame, renown"; the sense is approximate. The subject of "was delighted" is not expressed; understood as Shyamananda. "They sit as an assembly" — *baise sabhā kari'*.

[^311-7]: "Offered" — *dila*, "gave": apparently Rasika presents to Shyamananda the gifts he received in Banapur from the rajas and the Gajapati (lahari 9). "There" — *sesthāne* in the 1941 edition (= *se sthāne*). "Absorbed" — *ābeśe*. "Night nor day" — *niśi diśi*.

[^311-8]: Raghu and Ananda (*raghu ānanda*) are the brothers Raghunatha and Ananda, craftsmen from Nilachala whom Rasika met on the way (lahari 10, 75–77). "Presented" — *upadeśa*, literally "information, instruction"; understood as Rasika presenting them to Prabhu (Shyamananda). Vishvakarma is the architect of the gods; "the form of Vishvakarma" praises their skill (cf. lahari 10, 76). "Truly" — *sbarūpa*, "in their very nature".

[^311-9]: "Manifested a shri-murti" — *śrīmūrti prakāśa kailā*: apparently Shyamananda had the brothers fashion a Deity (cf. 9: "take the craftsmen"). The author speaks of the Deity as "manifested", "became manifest" (*prakāśa*, 8, 10–11): in the Vaishnava understanding a Deity installed according to rule is non-different from the Lord and manifests Himself. Vrindavanachandra (*bṛndābanacandra*, "Moon of Vrindavana") is a Deity of Shyamananda; BR 15 does not mention Him.

[^311-10]: "Craftsmen" — *kārikara* (*kārigar*), "artisan, craftsman". "Have made" — *banāha*. This is the Deity of Sri Govinda who was to become manifest by Jagannatha's command in the dream (lahari 10, 70–73). Cf. BR 15, 81: "he entrusted the service of Sri Govinda to Sri Rasika".

[^311-11]: "The incomparable" — *anupama*. "Asked leave to depart" — *māgila melāni*, the usual formula of farewell. The two brothers are Raghu and Ananda (7).

[^311-12]: "Reckoning an auspicious day" — *gaṇi' śubhadina*, by astrological calculation. "All the good omens" — *sarba sulakṣaṇa*. Govinda-raya (*gobinda rāẏa*) is Sri Govinda (10; lahari 10, 71). Ananga (*anaṅga*, "the Bodiless") is Kamadeva, the god of love: a common motif of Vaishnava poetry — Krishna's beauty enchants the god of love himself.

[^311-13]: "The command in the dream was confirmed" — *sbapna-ājñā paramāṇi* (*pramāṇa*, "proof"): the form of the Deity turned out as Jagannatha had commanded in the dream (lahari 10, 70–73). "By the load" — *bhāre*. "As a nichhani offering for Govinda's form" — *gobindarūpe nichāni*: nichhani is the custom of waving a gift around a beloved to ward off misfortune (Purva, lahari 9, note 21; Purva, lahari 10, note 25); here the gifts to the craftsmen are given as nichhani for the beauty of the Deity.

[^311-14]: "In the temple" — *mandire*. "Recite the shruti" — *śruti uccāraṇa*: Vedic mantras at the installation of the Deity. "According to rule" — *yathābidhi*.

[^311-15]: "Limit" — *ora*. "That is his play" — *sei kare khelā*, literally "that [he] makes his play"; the sense is approximate: Rasika is wholly absorbed in glorifying Krishna's virtues and pastimes. "Lost" — *bibhora*.

[^311-16]: "Manifold delights" — *nānā raṅge*. "Crest-jewel [of devotees]" — *cūṛāmaṇi*, "the jewel in a crown". "Ever [immersed in] the *Bhagavata*" — *sadā bhāgabata*; it may also be understood as "ever a bhagavata", i.e. a devotee. "The jewel among all virtues" — *sarbaguṇe guṇamaṇi*. The stanza has no main verb.

[^311-17]: "In his own home" — *āpanā sadane*: in Gopivallabhapur. "Raining tears" — *aśrubariṣaṇe*.

[^311-18]: "The embodiment of bliss" — *ānanda-sbarūpa*. "With tulasi leaves" — *tulasīra dale*.

[^311-19]: "Other lands" — *deśāntare*. "Characteristics" — *lakṣaṇa*. "Wondrous [even] to tell" — *adbhuta kathana*.

[^311-20]: "Rasika's true nature" — *rasika-sbarūpa*, "Rasika's own nature". "Worldly existence" — *saṃsāra*.

[^311-21]: "Billows of bliss" — *ānanda-kallola*. The author's signature (the second half of the stanza) is given in the standard formula; in the tripadi metre it reads: "Shyamananda's feet are [his] whole wealth — so sings the son of Rasamaya" (*śyāmānanda-pada sakala sampada gāẏa rasamaẏera nandana*; cf. Purva, lahari 5, note 14).

[^311-22]: Colophon (note 1).


## Lahari 12. The Manifestation of Shyamasundarpur

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda, living in Thuriya, calls Rasika to him; so many sadhus and guests arrive that he tells Rasika to beg for a few more homesteads, and the raja of Ghantashila gives them the village of Satuti, which is named Sri Shyamasundarpur; Shyamananda, while living in Ayodhya, builds a house there, lives in Little Govindapur and leaves three Thakuranis there; rajas and subjects give many villages, and the sadhus are served throughout Utkala; Shyamananda playfully tells everyone to call Rasika "Thakura Gosani"; the disciples of Shyamananda and Rasika number hundreds of thousands; in Thuriya, at the Dola festival, Shyamananda hears a call to go to Vraja and, in separation from Krishna, remains three days under a tree; Rasika, refusing food and water, and the rajas beg him to stay in Utkala; Shyamananda falls gravely ill, and Rasika brings from Harichandana in Balarampur the "Hemasagara" oil, which cures him; in Kashiyari a wicked Yavana official, enraged by the sankirtana, seizes everyone — apparently Shyamananda himself with his companions, soon loses everything and takes refuge with Shyamananda; in Narayanagarh Shyamananda tells the bhuiyan Shyamapala not to keep a Yavana guard at his door and, seeing his regard for the Yavanas, departs; from then on no Yavanas live in Narayanagarh*

*The twelfth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^312-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna, treasury of virtues,*
*refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the sure shelter!
Glory, glory to Rasikendra, the prince of Achyuta![^312-2]

**2.** Shyamananda dwells in his house in Thuriya;
he had Rasika brought to his place.[^312-3]

**3.** Crowd upon crowd of sadhus come there;
the throng of guests is so great it cannot be described.[^312-4]

**4.** Prabhu took counsel with Rasika:
"Beg, my child, for a few more homesteads as alms."[^312-5]

**5.** Then the two Prabhus went to the village of Ghantashila
and spoke to the raja about the service of sadhus.[^312-6]

**6.** That raja gave a village called Satuti;
there in many ways they settled people [and] tenants.[^312-7]

**7.** He gave it the name Sri Shyamasundarpur;
there service to the sadhus [and] yatras took place in abundance.[^312-8]

**8.** There Shyamananda-raya built a house;
for some days he made his abode in Ayodhya.[^312-9]

**9.** Many yatras [and] great festivals he held in that village;
all — the raja [and] the subjects — were immersed in bliss.

**10.** Little Govindapur he made another place of his;
for many, many days he stayed there.[^312-10]

**11.** Three Thakuranis he settled in that place;
in all those villages the sadhus are served abundantly.[^312-11]

**12.** All the rajas [and] subjects gave a great many villages;
in many ways the sadhus were served throughout Utkala.

**13.** Apart from service to the sadhus, [people] know nothing else:
in every house — service to the sadhus, by rajas [and] subjects.

**14.** Taking Rasika with him, Shyamananda-raya
wanders everywhere through the forest land, from region to region.[^312-12]

**15.** Playfully laughing, Shyamananda-raya says:
"All shall call [him] 'Thakura Gosani.'

**16.** Call Rasika 'Thakura Gosani.'"
From then on all people call [him] by this name.[^312-13]

**17.** To all Prabhu gave prema-bhakti for Krishna;
all, down to the chandalas, became pure in mind.[^312-14]

**18.** Hundreds upon hundreds of Vrajavasis come constantly;
the Gaudiyas of the guru's line — they cannot be counted.[^312-15]

**19.** Shyamananda [and] Rasika serve the sadhus,
giving food, cloth [and] various jewels to each one.

**20.** The towns of Utkala became the world of Vaikuntha;
all the people were overwhelmed with love for Krishna.[^312-16]

**21.** Many became disciples of Shyamananda;
Rasika's disciples cannot be counted.

**22.** Disciples of disciples, servant-disciples, their servants —
hundreds of thousands became disciples: it cannot be told.[^312-17]

**23.** One after another, mahantas who had conquered all the quarters became disciples;
throughout the forest land, on all four sides, they spread joy.[^312-18]

**24.** All are servants of Krishna, seeking no other refuge;
abandoning false knowledge, [they] serve the sadhus without cease.[^312-19]

**25.** Seeing [this] community, Shyamananda, with joy in his heart,
commanded: "All of you, accept disciples on all four sides."[^312-20]

**26.** Thus after some time Shyamananda-raya
went by his own will to Thuriya.

**27.** Rasika was with [him] at the house in Thuriya;
there they joyfully held the great Dola festival.[^312-21]

**28.** With them is Damodara Gosani;
ten, twenty brothers, servant-disciples — crowd upon crowd.[^312-22]

**29.** In that place they held a great festival-yatra.
Suddenly Shyamananda heard with his ears:

**30.** "Come to Vraja, making every effort."
Hearing the command, Shyamananda wept.[^312-23]

**31.** A great longing seized Shyamananda-raya;
in his mercy he entrusted everything to Rasika.

**32.** He declared: "I shall certainly go to Vrindavan."
Setting out on the journey, he went [and stopped] beneath a tree.[^312-24]

**33.** His heart was in great agitation from separation from Krishna;
night and day the streams of tears could not be held back.

**34.** For the third day he remained beneath the tree;
hearing [of it], the raja [and] the subjects quickly gathered.[^312-25]

**35.** Rasikendra gave everyone a sign:
"Gather, all of you, and make your plea before those feet.

**36.** Gather, all of you, [and] serve at [his] holy feet;
keep Prabhu in Utkala for at least a few days."[^312-26]

**37.** Receiving the instruction, the rajas fell at [his] feet;
in many ways they spoke to Prabhu:

**38.** "Rasika-shekhara has given up food and water;
hearing of separation from Prabhu, [his] heart is torn.

**39.** The tears of his eyes cannot be stopped;
night and day he weeps, thinking of you.

**40.** Rasikendra-mani has offered his life at [your] feet;
without you Rasika's life will not remain.

**41.** Rasikendra-chandra has offered his life at [your] feet;
why do you go, leaving him, Prabhu Shyamananda?"[^312-27]

**42.** Hearing the words of all, Shyamananda-raya,
seeing Rasika's grief, remained there.

**43.** Shyamananda was tormented by a severe wind disorder;
great physicians came in crowds.

**44.** Having examined [him], all said to Rasika:
"This wind will not subside without the 'Hemasagara' [oil].

**45.** With great labour this oil would be prepared;
quickly fetch [it] from the house of Harichandana."[^312-28]

**46.** Hearing this, Rasika went to Balarampur;
arriving, he met [him] at Harichandana's house.[^312-29]

**47.** In many ways [he] worshipped Rasika's feet;
with all his family he honoured [him] as a second Narayana.[^312-30]

**48.** Rasika told him everything:
"Bring that oil and relieve the illness."

**49.** Joyfully [he] went, taking the 'Hemasagara' oil;
hastening, he arrived at Shyamananda's place.

**50.** As soon as the oil was applied to the head, [Shyamananda] was at once made well;
for some days all stayed in that place.[^312-31]

**51.** In the bliss of the rasa of Krishna they pass the days and nights;
all are always absorbed in the sankirtana of Krishna.

**52.** At that time Rasika returned to his own place,
and Shyamananda went to Kashiyari.[^312-32]

**53.** At the sight of Prabhu all rejoiced;
in many ways all began to serve [him].

**54.** In every house the sankirtana of Krishna began;
raja [and] subjects reel [as if drunk] with love for Krishna.[^312-33]

**55.** The official of that place was a wicked Yavana;
hearing the sankirtana, he burned with anger without cease.

**56.** He asked everyone about Shyamananda;
all the people told [him] in many ways of [his] greatness.[^312-34]

**57.** Hearing this, the Mughal said in anger to everyone:
"The subjects of the forest land are his disciples.

**58.** If he is seized, all will come [and] present themselves [to me]."
Saying this, he sent many men.[^312-35]

**59.** Having brought [them], he held them all in confinement;
all the people [pleaded with] him in many ways.[^312-36]

**60.** That Yavana heeded no one's words;
within two or three days calamity befell him.

**61.** [He] lost his holdings, his wife [and] sons perished;
horses, wealth, people — all were ruined.[^312-37]

**62.** Great suffering came upon his body; the Yavana understood [the cause]
[and] addresses Shyamananda with humble words:[^312-38]

**63.** "Listen, listen, great Prabhu: I am wicked-minded;
not knowing you, [I brought on myself] so much misfortune.

**64.** Your greatness is beyond the reach of Indra and [the other] gods;
I did not know that you are the refuge, a brother born of the same womb."[^312-39]

**65.** In many ways that very Yavana praised [him];
he took refuge at Shyamananda's feet.

**66.** Having shown him mercy, Prabhu went from there;
coming to Narayanagarh, he entered [it].

**67.** He met with Shyamapala Bhunya,
[and] saw that the doorkeeper at his door was a Yavana.[^312-40]

**68.** Shyamananda commanded: "Listen, Shyamapala,
keep a Yavana doorkeeper inside no longer.

**69.** Where service to guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus takes place,
there brahmanas constantly come and go.

**70.** To see a Yavana [and] to touch [him] is needless;
from today keep only Hindus at the door."[^312-41]

**71.** Disregarding the command, [his] attendants speak [their mind];
Shyamananda, smiling, says to Shyamapala:[^312-42]

**72.** "I see you are much inclined towards the Yavanas;
it is not fitting for me to stay here.

**73.** In this place there are always many Yavanas."
Saying this, Shyamananda departed.

**74.** From then on no Yavanas remained in that place:
his command, unfailing, brings about the impossible.[^312-43]

**75.** He whose command Brahma [and] Shiva cannot break,
whose command Indra and [the other] guardians of the quarters accept,[^312-44]

**76.** in this way delivered the world;
even with millions upon millions of mouths [his] virtues cannot be described.

**77.** Listen, listen to the "Rasika-mangala," all people:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**78.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the twelfth lahari, called "The Manifestation of Shyamasundarpur."*[^312-45]

[^312-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("দ্বাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Narayani-gauda. Ghosha (refrain): *mora kṛṣṇa guṇanidhi / anātha-śaraṇa baṛa daẏāra abadhi*. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামসুন্দরপুর-প্রকাশ-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śyāmasundarapura-prakāśa*) — "The Manifestation of Shyamasundarpur". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^312-2]: "The sure shelter" — *śaraṇa-pañjara*, literally "cage (enclosure) of refuge", i.e. secure protection for those who take refuge. "The prince of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kuṅara* (*kuṅara* = *kumāra*): Rasika (Pashchima, lahari 5, note 60).

[^312-3]: Thuriya (*thuriyā*) is unidentified (lahari 11, note 3). "In his house" — *sadane*. "Had brought" — *ānāilā*.

[^312-4]: "Crowd upon crowd" — *yūtha yūtha*. "The throng of guests" — *atithera bhīṛa*.

[^312-5]: Prabhu is Shyamananda. "Took counsel" — *karilā bicāra*, "deliberated, discussed". "A few homesteads" — *daśa pā̃ca ghara*, literally "ten [or] five houses": apparently land with households to support the service of sadhus (cf. 5–6). "My child" — *bāpu*, an affectionate address to a younger person. "As alms" — *bhikṣā*: Shyamananda asks not for himself but for the service of sadhus (cf. 5).

[^312-6]: "The two Prabhus" — *dui prabhu*: Shyamananda and Rasika. Ghantashila (*ghaṇṭaśilā*) — Purva, lahari 14, note 4; Rasika formerly lived there with his family. The raja of Ghantashila is not named here (cf. Purva, lahari 16, note 4). "About the service of sadhus" — *sādhu-sebā-prasaṅga*.

[^312-7]: Satuti is unidentified; in 7 the village is given the name Sri Shyamasundarpur (the title of the lahari). "Settled" — *basāilā*: the subject is apparently Shyamananda and Rasika (or the raja).

[^312-8]: Sri Shyamasundarpur (*śrīśyāmasundarapura*, "the town of Shyamasundara," i.e. Krishna) is the new name of the village of Satuti (6, note 7); the lahari is named after it. "Yatras" — *yātrā*: festivals with a procession of the Deity; the edition notes a variant reading *tathā*, "there." "Took place in abundance" — *hailā pracura*.

[^312-9]: "There" — *tathā*: apparently in Shyamasundarpur. "House" — *bāṛi*, a homestead. Ayodhya (*ayodhyā*) is apparently a local village; not identified (cf. Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10). "Made his abode" — *karilā ālaẏa*.

[^312-10]: Little Govindapur — *sānā se gobindapura*; *sānā* means "small" (so the editor also explains). Whether this is the Sri Govindapur given to Shyamananda by the bhuiyan Bhimadhana (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7) is unclear. "Another place of his" — *kaila āra sthāna*. "Stayed" — *biśrāma karila*, lit. "rested, halted."

[^312-11]: The three Thakuranis — *tina ṭhākurāṇī*: apparently the three women of Shyamananda's household — Shyamapriya, Gaurangadasi and Yamuna (Dakshina, lahari 12, 12, note 8; "Thakurani" is an honorific title). It may also be understood as three Deities of Sri Radha (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 4). "Settled" — *rākhilena*, "placed, left."

[^312-12]: The forest land — *banabhũi* (= *banabhūmi*; Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10); likewise in 23 and 57.

[^312-13]: Thakura Gosani — *ṭhākura gõsāi*: an honorific ("lord-gosvami"; *gõsāi* is the same as *gosāñi*, Gosani). "Playfully" — *kautuke*. "All shall call [him]" (15) — *ḍākibe sabāẏa*; the object is Rasika, as 16 shows.

[^312-14]: "Down to the chandalas" — *ācaṇḍāla-ādi*: the chandalas are the lowest class. "Became pure in mind" — *haila śuddhamati*.

[^312-15]: Vrajavasis are the residents of Vraja. "The Gaudiyas of the guru's line" — *gurukula gauṛīẏā*: apparently Gaudiya Vaishnavas (from Gauda, Bengal) of the line of Shyamananda's guru, Hridaya Chaitanya; the sense is unclear. "Cannot be counted" — *gaṇana nā yāẏa*.

[^312-16]: "The towns of Utkala" — *utkala nagara*. "The world of Vaikuntha" — *baikuṇṭha-bhubana*. "Overwhelmed" — *jara jara*.

[^312-17]: "Disciples of disciples" — *anuśiṣya*; "servant-disciples" — *bhṛtya-śiṣya*; "their servants" — *tadbhṛtyagaṇa*. "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣa lakṣa*.

[^312-18]: "Mahantas who had conquered all the quarters" — *digbijaẏī mohānta*: renowned teachers, victors in learned debate. The line may also be understood: "each of the disciples became a mahanta, a conqueror of all the quarters." "Spread joy" — *pramoda karilā*.

[^312-19]: "Seeking no other refuge" — *ananya-śaraṇa*. "False knowledge" — *kubidyā*: apparently sorcery and false doctrines.

[^312-20]: "Community" — *goṣṭhī*: the circle of followers. "Accept disciples" — *śiṣya kara*. "On all four sides" — *cāribhite*.

[^312-21]: 26: "went" — *bije kaila* (*bijaẏa*), said respectfully of a saint's going; "by his own will" — *āpanā līlāẏa*, "in his own play." Thuriya — note 3. The great Dola festival — *dola-mahotsaba*, the spring swing festival (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 5).

[^312-22]: Damodara Gosani — *dāmodara gosāñī*: apparently Damodara, Shyamananda's disciple from Chakulia (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 21). "Brothers" — *bhāi*: apparently godbrothers. "Crowd upon crowd" — *yūthe yūthe*.

[^312-23]: The author does not say who calls Shyamananda to Vraja: he hears the voice "suddenly" (*ācambite*), and it is called a "command" (*ājñā*) — apparently a call from above (cf. 33: "from separation from Krishna"). "Making every effort" — *kariẏā yatana*. This episode is not mentioned in BR 15.

[^312-24]: "Longing" — *anurāga*: loving yearning (for Krishna and Vraja). "Entrusted everything to Rasika" — *saba samarpaṇa kaila rasike*: apparently the service and the disciples. "Setting out on the journey" — *yātrā kari'*: one leaving on a long journey goes out of the house at the appointed hour and halts outside it — here beneath a tree.

[^312-25]: "For the third day" — *tṛtīẏa dibasa*. "Quickly" — *satbare*.

[^312-26]: "Gave a sign" — *kahilā iṅgite*, "spoke by hint." "Before those feet" — *se caraṇa-agrete*: Shyamananda's feet.

[^312-27]: 38–41 are taken as the rajas' words to Shyamananda: 39–40 have *tuẏā*, "you." 38 may also be read as the author's narration. Rasika-shekhara, Rasikendra-mani, Rasikendra-chandra — "crown of the rasikas," "jewel [among] the lords of the rasikas," "moon…" — Rasika. "Has offered his life at [your] feet" — *prāṇa nibedila pāẏa*. "Thinking of you" — *tuẏā bhābe*, "in feeling for you." "His life will not remain" — *nā rahe parāṇī*.

[^312-28]: "A severe wind disorder" — *mahābāẏu*: in Ayurveda, a grave disturbance of vata, the "wind" in the body. "Physicians" — *boidya*. "In crowds" — *bṛnda bṛnda*. "Hemasagara" (*hemasāgara*, "ocean of gold") is a medicinal oil (*taila*, 45, 49); not identified. "With great labour this oil would be prepared" — *bahu kaṣṭe … haibe randhana*: medicinal oils are cooked at length with herbs; understood to mean that Harichandana has it ready. Harichandana is an Oriya title of landholders (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 13); he is not named here. Shyamananda's illness and the cure by the oil are not mentioned in BR 15.

[^312-29]: Balarampur — Dakshina, lahari 8, note 16.

[^312-30]: "With all his family" — *sabaṃśe*. "As a second Narayana" — *yena dbitīẏa nārāẏaṇe*: cf. Pashchima, lahari 10, 80. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the guru and the Vaishnava are honoured as the Lord Himself because they are His dearmost servants (Vishvanatha Chakravarti, Gurv-ashtaka 7); cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^312-31]: The subject of 49 is not expressed; understood as Rasika (it may also be Harichandana). "Arrived" — *utarilā*. "To the head" — *māthe*. The instant cure is as the author tells it.

[^312-32]: "His own place" — *nija sthāne*: apparently Gopivallabhapur. Kashiyari — *kāśīẏāṛī* (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 4).

[^312-33]: "Reel" — *ḍhalāḍhali*: sway and tumble against one another as if drunk.

[^312-34]: 55: "official" — *adhikārī*, an officer administering the locality; not named. Yavana — a Muslim; below he is called a Mughal (57; cf. Dakshina, lahari 9, note 5). "Asked" (56) — *sudhāila*.

[^312-35]: "All will come [and] present themselves" — *sabe milibe āsiẏā*: apparently the official's calculation: if Shyamananda is seized, all his disciples will come to him [in submission or with a ransom].

[^312-36]: "In confinement" — *nigama sthāne*: the sense is unclear; taken as "in prison" (perhaps *nigaṛa*, "fetters"). "Them all" — *sabāre*: apparently Shyamananda and his companions. "[Pleaded]" — *kahila*, "spoke": the people interceded for them.

[^312-37]: "Calamity" (60) — *aghaṭana*. "Lost his holdings" — *biṣaẏa chuṭila*: his post and property. The ruin of his family and property is as the author tells it: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, offence against a Vaishnava is ruinous (Dakshina, lahari 9, note 7).

[^312-38]: "Great suffering came upon his body" — *aṅge mahāduḥkha haila*: illness or grievous sorrow. "Understood" — *jānila*.

[^312-39]: "Great Prabhu" — *mahāprabhu*: here the Yavana's address to Shyamananda. "Beyond the reach of Indra and [the other] gods" — *debendrādi-agocara*. "The refuge, a brother born of the same womb" — *śaraṇa sodara*: apparently "a protector, close as a brother"; the sense is unclear.

[^312-40]: Narayanagarh (*nārāẏaṇagaṛa*) is apparently Narayangarh in Paschim Medinipur, the seat of an estate of that name. Shyamapala Bhunya (*śyāmapāla bhuñā*) is a bhuiyan, a landholder (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7), apparently the lord of Narayangarh; not identified. "Entered" — *parabeśa hailā*. "Doorkeeper" — *duẏāri* (68: *dbāri*).

[^312-41]: "Inside" — *bhitare*: in the house. "Brahmanas" — *dbijagaṇa*. "To see … [and] to touch … is needless" — *daraśe paraśe akāraṇa*: the concern is the ritual purity of the brahmanas who come where guru, Krishna and the sadhus are served; this is as the author tells it and reflects the customs of his time. "Hindus" — *hindugaṇa*.

[^312-42]: The line is unclear: *helana kariẏā ājñā saṅgīgaṇa bale* — understood as: Shyamapala's attendants, disregarding the command, raise objections; it may also be read "[Shyamapala] disregarded the command, the companions say." "Smiling" — *kutuhale*, "playfully."

[^312-43]: "Unfailing … brings about the impossible" — *aghaṭana ghaṭāẏa se ājñā paramāṇe*, lit. "by the measure (power) of that command the unheard-of comes to pass." The departure of the Yavanas from Narayanagarh is as the author tells it.

[^312-44]: Such things are usually said of the Lord; the author exalts Shyamananda (cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shyamananda is a servant of Radha, and the power of his word is the power the Lord grants to His devotee. "Accept" — *dhare*, "hold [on their heads]." The guardians of the quarters (*dikpāla*) are Indra and the other gods.

[^312-45]: The author's signature (78) and the colophon are: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামসুন্দরপুর-প্রকাশ-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śyāmasundarapura-prakāśa*; note 1).


## Lahari 13. The Description of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu's Separation at the Disappearance of Sri Sri Shyamananda Prabhu

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Shyamananda and Rasika give prema in all lands; in Ambika Adhikari Thakura departs, and Shyamananda, weeping for Hridayananda, says he will no longer remain on earth; in the month of Phalguna an aradhana festival is held in Shyamasundarpur, and the whole community gathers; in Govindapur, after Damodara's departure, a festival is held in his memory and again the day of Adhikari Gosani is kept; Shyamananda tells Rasika that he has fulfilled the Lord's command to deliver, together with him, the living beings of Utkala, and that Krishna bids him depart; in Nrisimhapur, in the house of Uddanda-raya, he is ill for four months, refuses treatment and in place of medicine orders unceasing sankirtana; when Rasika begs leave to go to Vrindavana, he tells him to remain in Utkala, preach and care for all, places his feet on his head, ties a cloth on him with his own hand, applies tilaka and gives him all authority in the community; in Shaka 1552, on the first day of the dark fortnight of Ashadha after the Snana-yatra, amid the sound of sankirtana, Shyamananda departs; Rasika falls unconscious and laments for him; the disciples console him, but he is inconsolable; in that village, by the rules of the shastras, the place of his departure is established; the author promises to tell of the festivals and asks pardon for faults in the order of the narrative*

*The thirteenth lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^313-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna, treasury of virtues,*
*refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of Rasika!
Glory, glory to Rasikendra, the son of Achyuta![^313-2]

**2.** Thus Shyamananda and Rasikendra-chandra
gave prema in all lands, with joy in their hearts.

**3.** At that time, after some days, in the land of Ambuya
Sri Adhikari Thakura attained Goloka.[^313-3]

**4.** After some days a servant [came] to Shyamananda
and told him everything that [had happened] there.

**5.** Hearing it, Shyamananda wept much;
he sent people to bring Rasika.

**6.** Rasikendra came as soon as he received the command;
Shyamananda said to Rasika:[^313-4]

**7.** "No longer shall I remain on the earth:
separation from Hridayananda tears [my] heart apart."[^313-5]

**8.** Shyamananda wept for a long time;
the whole community grew very sad.

**9.** He told Rasika everything:
"I shall hold a great festival in Shyamasundarpur.

**10.** Proclaim this word in all lands;
bring provisions from everywhere in every way."[^313-6]

**11.** Having received the command, Rasikendra set out;
he sent servants in all four directions.

**12.** Having received the command, [they] brought many provisions there;
at Rasika's command many people came.

**13.** In [the month of] Phalguna the great festival was held;
all the communities of Shyamananda's servants came.[^313-7]

**14.** There was great joy in Shyamasundarpur;
who could describe that happiness even with a hundred mouths?

**15.** Having held the aradhana festival that year,
Shyamananda went to Sri Govindapur.[^313-8]

**16.** After some days Damodara departed from this world;
hearing [of it], Shyamananda Prabhu was stricken to the heart.[^313-9]

**17.** Shyamananda gave a command to Rasika
[and said]: "Damodara has shown [me] the way — I see [it] in my heart."[^313-10]

**18.** [Rasika] held the aradhana festival in his [memory],
and again the day of Adhikari Gosani.[^313-11]

**19.** In Govindapur that festival was held;
before all the Shyamanandis Prabhu made [his will] known.[^313-12]

**20.** Seating Rasika beside him, he speaks softly:
"Listen, listen, O child, Rasika-shekhara!

**21.** Long ago Prabhu Bhagavan gave me the command:
'Taking Rasika, deliver the living beings.'[^313-13]

**22.** By that command I preached bhakti for Krishna
and delivered all the living beings of Utkala.

**23.** The whole world is intoxicated with prema for Krishna;
now you, taking them all [into your care], live [with them] in joy.[^313-14]

**24.** Krishna's command has come for me to go;
surely I shall no longer remain on earth."

**25.** Having said this, he entered Nrisimhapur:
taking Rasika with him, Prabhu went there.

**26.** At that time Shyamananda fell ill;
they all stayed in the house of Uddanda-raya.[^313-15]

**27.** Shyamananda-raya fell very gravely ill;
for four months he remained there with the community.

**28.** Ten or twenty physicians came and treated him;
each gave whatever medicine he wished.

**29.** The physicians treated [him] in every way;
day and night Rasika sat [by him] without sleep.

**30.** In no way did [his] body recover;
Shyamananda himself said to everyone:

**31.** "There is Krishna's command — I shall certainly go;
make no vain efforts; listen, all of you.

**32.** Hold sankirtana day and night;
unceasingly, sadhus, speak of Krishna.

**33.** Vina, venu, rabab, murali — many instruments:
this is the medicine; in this, I tell you, is [the whole] truth."[^313-16]

**34.** Hearing this, Rasika grew very sad;
in a voice choked with feeling he said to Prabhu:

**35.** "Command me, Prabhu, to go to Vrindavana:
how shall I keep my life in separation from you?"

**36.** Rasika-shekhara was deeply distressed;
hearing him, Shyamananda answered him:

**37.** "All the Shyamanandis who were born in Utkala —
with them live in joy for some time longer.

**38.** By my command remain in the land of Utkala;
know in your heart that you are always in Vrindavana.[^313-17]

**39.** For some time longer preach bhakti for Krishna;
fill the world to overflowing with prema for Krishna.[^313-18]

**40.** From house to house diligently [arrange] service to the sadhus;
give prema-bhakti for Krishna to all people, to each one.

**41.** [Uphold] what the shastras establish — shruti, smriti, the Bhagavata:
service to the guru, to Krishna and to the sadhus, and the brahmanas;

**42.** care for all people on earth."
He placed [his] lotus feet on Rasika's head.[^313-19]

**43.** Tying a cloth [on him] with his own hand, Shyamananda
with joy in his heart applied tilaka to his forehead.[^313-20]

**44.** Himself joining his palms, he spoke to all —
thus in Shyamananda's community he performed the anointing:[^313-21]

**45.** "All will abide by Rasika's command;
Rasikendra will care for all.

**46.** Let no one break Rasika's command:
whoever turns away from Rasika is no companion of mine."

**47.** He gave all authority to Rasika-shekhara,
entrusted everything to the son of Achyuta.

**48.** All the while the sound of sankirtana rises on every side;
looking at Shyamananda, everyone grew anxious.

**49.** In Shaka 1552 — such is the date —
Prabhu departed to Krishna.[^313-22]

**50.** [It was at] the Deity's Snana-yatra, at the close of the full moon,
on the first lunar day of the dark fortnight, at the entry of [the month of] Ashadha.[^313-23]

**51.** Cries of "Hari!", the sound of conches, the sound of sankirtana —
shouts of "Jaya!" reached the vault of the sky.

**52.** At that very moment Prabhu disappeared [from the world's sight].
Hearing [of it], the whole community lost their senses.[^313-24]

**53.** Rasika fell to the ground unconscious;
his companions lift him, hold him up, sprinkle water on his face.

**54.** His body was drowned in the streams of tears from his eyes;
lamenting, Rasika-shekhara says:

**55.** "When I was eighteen years old,
then Shyamananda-svami appeared to me.

**56.** For twenty years I served [his] feet;
now, leaving [me] alone, Prabhu has gone to his own abode.[^313-25]

**57.** He by whose touch [people] obtained prema-bhakti for Krishna,
by the sight of whom all became pure of mind;

**58.** by whose mercy ignorance was dispelled,
by whose favour [came] release from the bonds of worldly existence;

**59.** by whose grace Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas and others,
leaving their own occupations, went mad with prema for Krishna —[^313-26]

**60.** such a Prabhu has gone, leaving [me] — I shall not see [him] again;
now my whole world has become empty.[^313-27]

**61.** Who will now be kind to me, [loving me] with a father's tenderness?
With whom shall I wander, roaming from land to land?

**62.** With whom shall I go round the holy places?
Who will take me with him to Vrindavana?[^313-28]

**63.** No more shall I see those two feet!"
Saying this, Rasikendra fell to the ground.

**64.** All the devotees of Krishna, the Shyamanandis who were with [him],
consoling [him], all speak [to him] in many ways.[^313-29]

**65.** No one's consolation consoles Prabhu;
day and night streams flow from his two eyes.

**66.** Rasika's love cannot be described:
from separation from Shyamananda [his] heart breaks.

**67.** Even with millions of mouths it cannot be told —
he, hearing of whose love, a stone melts.[^313-30]

**68.** In that village they established the place of [his] disappearance,
according to the rules of the Vedas, [following] the testimony of the smriti-shastras.[^313-31]

**69.** Now I shall tell of the great festivals and the rest,
hearing of which one never again meets with sin.[^313-32]

**70.** Who can know the lilas, [boundless] as the waves of the ocean?
By Rasika's mercy I have told a little.[^313-33]

**71.** In the Pashchima-vibhaga I have composed this —
what Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, makes me speak.

**72.** Do not keep in mind any faults in the order [of the narrative];
may the learned sadhus listen with love.[^313-34]

**73.** The lord of everyone's life is Rasikendra-chandra;
listen, all, to his virtues, filled with joy.

**74.** Listen to the "Rasika-mangala," all devotees of Krishna:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**75.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the thirteenth lahari, called "The Description of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu's Separation at the Disappearance of Sri Sri Shyamananda Prabhu."*[^313-35]

[^313-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 13 begins. Raga Narayani-gauda; the ghosha is the same as in lahari 12. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীশ্রীশ্যামানন্দ প্রভুর তিরোভাবে শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ-প্রভুর বিরহ-বর্ণন-নাম ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*tirobhābe … biraha-barṇana*) — "The Description of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu's Separation at the Disappearance of Sri Sri Shyamananda Prabhu". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^313-2]: "The life of Rasika" — *rasika-jībana*: Shyamananda, Rasika's guru. "The son of Achyuta" — *acyuta-nandana* (Pashchima, lahari 5, note 60).

[^313-3]: Ambuya — Ambika (Kalna) and its surroundings (Purva, lahari 2, note 8; the editor understands it likewise). "Land" — *maluk* (*mulk*), "domain, region." Sri Adhikari Thakura is Hridayananda (Hridaya Chaitanya), Shyamananda's guru, servant of the Deities at Ambika-Kalna (7; Dakshina, lahari 11, note 26). "Attained Goloka" — *pāilā goloke*: so the author speaks of a Vaishnava's departure — a return to Krishna's eternal abode.

[^313-4]: "As soon as he received the command" — *ājñā prabeśite*, lit. "on the command's entering (arriving)"; it may also be understood as "to receive the command." "Said to Rasika" — *rasika-agrete*, lit. "before Rasika."

[^313-5]: "On the earth" — *abanimaṇḍale*, "on the circle of the earth." Hridayananda is Sri Adhikari Thakura (3).

[^313-6]: Shyamasundarpur — the village given by the raja of Ghantashila (lahari 12, 6–7). "Provisions" — *sambhāra*: everything needed for the festival.

[^313-7]: Phalguna — the month of February–March. "Was held" — *karila prakāśa*, lit. "manifested." "All the communities of Shyamananda's servants" — *saba goṣṭhī śyāmānanda dāsa*; it may also be understood as "all the communities [and] servants of Shyamananda."

[^313-8]: The aradhana festival (*ārādhanā mahotsaba*, lit. "festival of worship") — apparently a festival in memory of a departed Vaishnava, here Hridayananda (3–9; cf. 18). "Went" — *bije kaila* (*bijaya*, the "progress" of a holy person). Sri Govindapur is apparently Little Govindapur, where Shyamananda lived (lahari 12, 10, note 10), or the Sri Govindapur given by the bhuiyan Bhimadhana (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7).

[^313-9]: Damodara — the learned yogi of Chakulia, Shyamananda's disciple (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 21; Dakshina, lahari 11, note 27); in lahari 12, 28 he is "Damodara Gosani." "Departed from this world" — *haila antardhāna*, "disappeared." "Stricken to the heart" — *ākula parāṇa*, "his soul in turmoil."

[^313-10]: "Has shown the way" — *patha kāṛāilā*; the editor glosses *kāṛāilā* as *dekhāilā*, "showed." Understood: Damodara went first, showing the way by which Shyamananda too will soon depart (cf. 24); the sense is approximate. "Gave a command to Rasika" — *ājñā kaila … rasikera sthāne*: apparently to hold the festival (18).

[^313-11]: "In his [memory]" — *tāhāra*, i.e. in memory of Damodara. "The day of Adhikari Gosani" — apparently the anniversary of Hridayananda's departure (3; cf. 15). The subject of "held" is not expressed; understood as Rasika, by Shyamananda's command (17).

[^313-12]: Shyamanandis (*śyāmānandī*) — Shyamananda's followers. "Made [his will] known" — *prakāśilā*, "revealed, announced"; understood: Shyamananda announces his impending departure (20–24).

[^313-13]: "Prabhu Bhagavan" is Krishna: in Vraja, Madana-gopala Sri Govinda commanded Shyamananda to go to Utkala and instruct Rasika-Murari (Purva, lahari 15, 7–8, 18–20). "Deliver" — *kara … paritrāṇa*.

[^313-14]: "Taking them all" — *e sabāre laiẏā*. "Live [with them] in joy" — *karaha bihāra*, lit. "perform vihara" (strolling, sport, wandering); likewise in 37 (*biharaṇa*).

[^313-15]: Nrisimhapur — Dakshina, lahari 16, note 24. Uddanda-raya (*udaṇḍa rāẏa*) — the bhuiyan of Nrisimhapur, a disciple of Shyamananda (Dakshina, lahari 16). "Fell ill" — *asustha hailā*.

[^313-16]: The vina is a stringed instrument; the venu and murali are flutes; the rabab is a bowed (or plucked) stringed instrument. "Medicine" — *auṣadha*. "In this, I tell you, is [the whole] truth" — *ithe kahilāma tattba*.

[^313-17]: "Know in your heart that you are always in Vrindavana" — *manete jāniha sadā ācha bṛndābane*: serving in Utkala by the guru's command, Rasika inwardly abides in Vrindavana.

[^313-18]: "Fill the world to overflowing" — *ḍhalāḍhali karaha saṃsāra*: *ḍhalāḍhali* is "swaying, spilling over"; it may also be understood as "let the world sway (in rapture) with prema for Krishna."

[^313-19]: 41–42a form one instruction: *śruti-smṛti-bhāgabata śāstra-paramāṇa / gurukṛṣṇa-sādhusebā āra dbijagaṇa / sarbajana pālana karaha bhūmaṇḍale*; the verb "care for" (*pālana karaha*) apparently governs the whole list. "What the shastras establish" — *śāstra-paramāṇa*, "the testimony of scripture." "Placed his feet on his head" — a sign of blessing and of bestowing grace.

[^313-20]: "Tying a cloth [on him]" — *bastra bāndhi'*: apparently he tied a cloth (a turban) on his head, a sign of succession. "To his forehead" — *māthe*, "on the head, on the forehead."

[^313-21]: "Anointing" — *ṭīkā*: the mark (on the forehead) by which a successor or ruler is confirmed; *ṭīkā se sārilā*, "he performed that tika." Shyamananda hands over to Rasika the leadership of the community (45–47). On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^313-22]: Shaka 1552 is 1630 CE. "Such is the date" — *se pramāṇa*, "that is the evidence." "Departed to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera sannidhe … karilā praẏāṇa*, "set out to Krishna". On Shyamananda as an associate of the Lord, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^313-23]: The Snana-yatra (*deba-snānayātrā*, "the bathing festival of the Deity") — the bathing of Jagannatha on the full moon of the month of Jyaishtha. "The first lunar day of the dark fortnight" — *kṛṣṇa-pratipada tithi*: the first day after the full moon; when months are reckoned from the full moon, the beginning of Ashadha (June–July). In the 1941 edition, lines 49–50 and 52a are underlined by hand (a reader's marks); the text is clear.

[^313-24]: "Disappeared" — *hailā antardhāna*, "became hidden": the departure of an associate of the Lord is a disappearance, not an ordinary passing. "Lost their senses" — *harilā jñāna*, lit. "lost consciousness."

[^313-25]: Rasikananda was born in 1590 (Purva, lahari 4, note 8); eighteen years and twenty years of service (55–56) agree approximately with the date 1630 (49). "Appeared to me" — *darśana dilā*, "gave darshan" (Purva, lahari 16). "To his own abode" — *nija dhāme*.

[^313-26]: Hunas, Pulindas, mlecchas — *hūṇa-pulinda-mlecchādi*: foreigners and forest tribes (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 11; Pashchima, lahari 10, note 23). "Their own occupations" — *nija karma*, caste and worldly occupations. The sentence continues in 60: "Such a Prabhu…".

[^313-27]: The continuation of the sentence in 57–59: "He by whose touch… — such a Prabhu…". "Has gone, leaving [me]" — *chāṛi' gelā*. "Has become empty" — *śūnya bhela* (*bhela*, "became").

[^313-28]: "With a father's tenderness" — *bātsalya kariyā*: Shyamananda, the guru, loved Rasika as a father loves a son. "Wander, roaming" — *buliba bhramiyā*. "Go round the holy places" — *tīrtha-paryaṭana*.

[^313-29]: Shyamanandis — note 12. "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa* (Purva, lahari 10, note 13).

[^313-30]: "Love" — *anurāga*, loving attachment (likewise in 67). "A stone melts" — *pāṣāṇa milāẏa*, literally "a stone dissolves."

[^313-31]: "The place of [his] disappearance" — *tirodhāna-āsana*, literally "the seat of disappearance": apparently a samadhi, the memorial place where the transcendental body of a saint rests. "In that village" — apparently Nrisimhapur, where Shyamananda departed (25–26, 52). The subject is not expressed. "According to the rules of the Vedas, [following] the testimony of the smriti-shastras" — *bedabidhi smṛtiśāstra kariyā pramāṇe*.

[^313-32]: "The great festivals and the rest" — *mahotsaba ādi*: the festivals in Shyamananda's memory, told in the following laharis (14–16). "One never again meets with sin" — *pāpa sane dekhā nahe āra*.

[^313-33]: "The lilas, [boundless] as the waves of the ocean" — *samudra-taraṅga-līlā*; cf. *laharī*, "wave," the name of the poem's chapters. "Have told" — *kailũ paracāre*.

[^313-34]: "The son of Achyuta" is Rasika (note 2). "Makes me speak" — *more bolāẏa*: the author ascribes his words to Rasika. "Faults in the order [of the narrative]" — *anukrama doṣa*: departures from the sequence of events. "With love" — *suprīte*.

[^313-35]: The author's signature (75) and the colophon are: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীশ্রীশ্যামানন্দপ্রভুর তিরোভাবে শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ-প্রভুর বিরহ-বর্ণন-নাম ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" — the title agrees with the heading (note 1).


## Lahari 14. The Description of Shyamananda's Branches

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; in separation from Shyamananda, Rasika gathers the devotees of Krishna to hold the twelfth-day festival and appoints the first aradhana in Govindapur; he tells the brothers to invite all the Shyamanandis, to decide who will be adhikari of the community and of Sri Govinda's service, and to name to him all of Shyamananda's disciples; the devotees, praising Rasika's three sons and daughter, choose his eldest son, Radhananda, full of prema for Krishna; Rasika embraces him, ties a cloth on his head and entrusts to him the service of Sri Govinda; the brothers say the Shyamanandis are countless as the waves of the ocean; the author lists Rasika's disciples — brahmanas, kings, renunciants — among them Ramakrishna, who crossed a river on a crocodile, Gokula Dasa, who manifested bhakti in Kendujhar, and Govinda Bhattacharya, who preached in Bengal, — and says they cannot be counted*

*The fourteenth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^314-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!*
*O Murari, O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of the fallen,
the own dear treasure of the life of Rasika-chandra![^314-2]

**2.** In separation from Shyamananda, Rasika-shekhara
is constantly absorbed in ecstatic feeling; [his] body is overwhelmed.[^314-3]

**3.** Taking all the devotees of Krishna, he sat to deliberate
on holding the twelfth-day festival.[^314-4]

**4.** Govindapur was fixed as the place [of the festival]:
there — the first aradhana, the great festival.[^314-5]

**5.** "This great festival [should be] known to the world;
it is fitting to bring all the communities of Shyamanandis."[^314-6]

**6.** Rasikendra says: "I know nothing —
[my] meditation and remembrance are Shyamananda's feet.

**7.** Mad with prema for Krishna, I have spent all this time;
who lives where — I do not know them."[^314-7]

**8.** Rasika gave the command to all the brothers:
"Invite all the Shyamanandis, every one.[^314-8]

**9.** Who will be the adhikari in the Shyamanandi community?
Whom will you make [it] — deliberate on this.

**10.** The service of Sri Govinda and the great festival —
understand that this is [a duty we have] accepted, and consider [it].[^314-9]

**11.** For I shall wander, carrying out Prabhu's work;
[arrange it] so that the service here goes on in due order.[^314-10]

**12.** Tell me the names of Shyamananda's disciples,
the disciples of [their] disciples, the servant-disciples — all who are in Utkala.[^314-11]

**13.** Kings, subjects, mahantas, all the renunciants —
who is whose disciple — distinguish them all one by one.[^314-12]

**14.** In what family each was born, where each lives —
having ascertained [this], tell of the Shyamanandi servants.[^314-13]

**15.** What love each has for Krishna,
who seeks no other refuge, who has prema-bhakti;

**16.** who has affection for the company of sadhus, in whose heart is kindness,
who is firmly [devoted] to the guru — tell in detail.[^314-14]

**17.** Describe them to me one by one;
entrust to me the Shyamanandi community.

**18.** I shall write to all, as befits [each];
all those people will come to the great festival."[^314-15]

**19.** All said: "Prabhu, you are detached;
you have appeared in order to give prema to the destitute.[^314-16]

**20.** Appoint one adhikari equal to yourself;
entrust to him the service of Sri Govinda."[^314-17]

**21.** Then Rasikendra gave the command to all;
Rasika, [gathering everyone] in a circle, sat to deliberate:

**22.** "The one on whom all agree — he shall be [chosen];
quickly deliberate, come to a decision [and] bring [him]."[^314-18]

**23.** All the devotees of Krishna, gathering, deliberated:
Rasika has three sons, supremely magnanimous.

**24.** These three brothers, born of one mother, enchant the world;
by their glance the three worlds were delivered.[^314-19]

**25.** And he has one daughter, supremely steadfast,
an abode that has taken refuge in prema for Krishna, skilled in rasa.[^314-20]

**26.** All these names and [the account of their] glory
I proclaim only to purify myself.[^314-21]

**27.** The eldest son is Radhananda, great in wisdom;
Krishnagati — [his] mind and speech are incomparable;

**28.** [the third] is named Radhakrishna Dasa, an abode of prema for Krishna;
the daughter is named Vrindavati — she whose life is Krishna.[^314-22]

**29.** Now I shall tell the boundless glory of Radhananda —
of him to whom this authority is fitting.

**30.** All understand only a trace of Radhananda's glory:
unceasingly [they] see his striving towards Krishna.[^314-23]

**31.** On Krishna is [his] attachment, on Krishna his mind, in Krishna his abiding;
within and without, Krishna dwells in him.

**32.** When he falls asleep, he plays with Krishna;
when he wakes, in separation he weeps.

**33.** Weeping and weeping, he sees the form of Radha and Krishna;
immersed, he plunges into a well of bliss.[^314-24]

**34.** At times he smiles softly, ever so slightly;
he sinks and rises in the ocean of the nectar of prema for Krishna.

**35.** Like a blazing fire in the midst of the forest of worldly existence [is he];
seeing [him], the hordes of pashandis are consumed by burning.[^314-25]

**36.** Hunger, thirst and [the like] do not touch [his] body;
his mind, maddened with prema for Krishna, is overflowing with love.[^314-26]

**37.** He always has the strength to give Krishna and to take Krishna;
reassuring the destitute, he bestows prema.

**38.** Feeding [a person] the fruit of prema, he fills his belly;
his grief, pain [and] burning [suffering] he reduces to ashes.

**39.** Having eaten the fruit of prema, that one, maddened,
dances, sings, weeps, crying, "Krishna! Ha, ha, ha!"[^314-27]

**40.** All those devotees of Krishna, seeing all this,
firmly decided: he is the worthy one.

**41.** All went and said before Rasikendra:
"Worthy to be adhikari is Radhananda, the greatly fortunate."

**42.** They told of all his virtues;
hearing this, Prabhu was pleased, his eyes filled with tears.

**43.** Prabhu said to all: "Call [him] and bring [him]."
All went to bring him, rejoicing.

**44.** They told him everything in his presence;
hearing it, he was delighted, joyful at heart.[^314-28]

**45.** At the command [they] rose and quickly set out;
all the devotees of Krishna came before Prabhu.[^314-29]

**46.** Seeing Prabhu, [Radhananda] began to prostrate himself;
saying, "Rise, rise," Prabhu took [him] into his embrace.

**47.** Embracing [him] again, Rasikendra-raya
began to speak: "Dear one, listen quickly.

**48.** Before, you had Shyamananda's command;
now all the devotees of Krishna have surrounded you.[^314-30]

**49.** I too [give] you, dear one, this authority:
govern Shyamananda's community."[^314-31]

**50.** Prostrating himself again, he fell to the ground;
the devotees of Krishna tell Rasika to give [him] the cloth.

**51.** With everyone's consent Rasikendra-raya
quickly tied the cloth on Radhananda's head.[^314-32]

**52.** Having tied the cloth, Rasikendra walked around [him];
with prema in his heart Prabhu says, "Hari, Hari!"

**53.** He entrusted the service of Sri Govinda to Radhananda;
earnestly he told [him] to preach prema-bhakti.[^314-33]

**54.** Then Rasikendra again, to everyone,
spoke sweet words with love:

**55.** "All of you, devotees of Krishna, are supremely magnanimous;
you are able to give bhakti for Krishna to all and to receive [it].[^314-34]

**56.** Count the names of the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas
and bring [them to me], dear ones, with care."

**57.** Hearing Rasika's command, the brothers say:
"The communities of the Shyamanandis cannot be told.[^314-35]

**58.** The Shyamanandis are like the waves of the ocean;
the devotees of Krishna, the Shyamanandis, cannot be counted.

**59.** We shall name the chief ones in [your] presence;
all together will tell what they know, as is fitting."

**60.** Before, I described the disciples of Shyamananda;
now I shall tell of his disciples, servants [and their] disciples.

**61.** Briefly I shall relate something about them;
all you Shyamanandis, devotees of Krishna, listen attentively.[^314-36]

**62.** Motionless, Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, listens;
with great joy all the devotees of Krishna listen.

**63.** At the beginning of the book I offered all the obeisances:
all the disciples of Shyamananda I [named] one by one.

**64.** Now the brothers earnestly tell of the disciples;
the son of Achyuta listens [to them] with undivided mind.[^314-37]

**65.** I shall tell in detail of Rasika's worthy disciples,
praising the firmness of each one's bhakti, such as it is.

**66.** The first disciple is the brahmana Kalandi Bhaktadasa,
whose true abode is Rasika's feet.[^314-38]

**67.** Sri Shyamagopala Dasa, very pure of mind,
for whom Rasika-shekhara is lineage, character and caste.

**68.** He is the son of Kashinatha, renowned in the world,
very eloquent, intelligent, one who says what is fitting.

**69.** His mother, Govindadasi, is Rasika's servant;
by Rasika's mercy [she] is renowned [for knowing] the truth about the Vaishnavas.[^314-39]

**70.** In a village called Sri Jangha, a truly divine place,
lived a fortunate [man] named Ramadasa.

**71.** His wife, named Draupadi, was devoted to her husband;
she was born in the clan of the shishta-karanas, renowned [to all].[^314-40]

**72.** From her womb was born Dinashyama Dasa;
from childhood Rasika was manifest in his heart.[^314-41]

**73.** The disciple of Rasika, an embodiment of prema:
whatever Rasika commands, he unfailingly does.

**74.** Night and day he always meditates on Rasikendra;
at Rasika's feet he offered [his] caste [and] life.

**75.** He made many disciples in the land of Utkala;
all the elders honour [him] as equal to a guru.

**76.** Dinashyama Dasa is very dear to the Vaishnavas;
he always delights in the pastimes of prema for Krishna.

**77.** He brought much joy upon the earth;
giving prema-bhakti to all, he delivered [them].

**78.** The glory of Dinashyama cannot be told —
of him to whom [Rasika] entrusted his own prema-bhakti.

**79.** The brahmana Ramakrishna Dasa, very pure of mind,
who has no other goal than Rasikendra,

**80.** made many disciples in the land of Utkala;
all people sing of him as the blessing of the world.

**81.** For sport he sits on the backs of tigers and crocodiles;
by Rasika's mercy he fears no one.

**82.** Mounting a crocodile, he crosses the river —
Ramakrishna Mahashaya, the deliverer of the fallen.[^314-42]

**83.** Rasika's disciple is the renowned Narayana Dasa;
pure of heart, he knows no one but Krishna.

**84.** The brahmana Paramananda, very pure of heart,
by Rasika's mercy became a great scholar.

**85.** In a brahmana family was born Goura-gopala;
he knows nothing but Rasikendra.[^314-43]

**86.** The brahmana Gopinatha, a renunciant mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra [abides] unceasingly,

**87.** knows nothing but prema-bhakti for Krishna;
all his time was spent with Rasika.

**88.** Krishna's meals, offerings of six tastes,
Gopinatha, pure in conduct, cooks.[^314-44]

**89.** Prema-ankura Dasa is Rasika's servant;
among his servants and [his] servants' servants the kadamba blossomed.[^314-45]

**90.** Rasika's disciple from childhood, Sri Gokula Dasa,
manifested bhakti in the land of Kendujhar.

**91.** In the forest land the mahashaya made many disciples;
they know nothing but Rasikendra.[^314-46]

**92.** Shyama-manohara Dasa, very pure of mind,
who has no other goal than Rasika's feet —

**93.** earlier I made his greatness known;
a great scholar, he delivered all people.[^314-47]

**94.** Maharaja Vaidyanatha is a great mahajana;
with body, mind and words he firmly takes refuge in Rasika.

**95.** He left his body in the land of Utkala;
in Vrindavana he saw all the sadhus.[^314-48]

**96.** Chhota-raya [and] Rautra are very pure of mind;
they have no other goal than Rasikendra.

**97.** Both are very mighty, embodiments of prema;
seeing their deeds, all attained bhakti.[^314-49]

**98.** Shyamadasa [and] Mohana are Prabhu's own servants;
with the songs of Jayadeva they enchant everyone.[^314-50]

**99.** The brahmana Govinda Bhattacharya Mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra-chandra always [abides],

**100.** preached bhakti for Hari in Vanga;
hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas became his disciples.[^314-51]

**101.** Rasika's disciple is the fortunate brahmana Dube:
he knows nothing other than Rasikendra-chandra.

**102.** Tarkalankara Bhattacharya Shyamasundara —
he to whom Rasika-shekhara gave prema-bhakti.

**103.** Rasika's disciple is the brahmana Sundara-raya,
a mahashaya, prema-bhakti for Krishna embodied.[^314-52]

**104.** The best of brahmanas, the renunciant Sri Mohana Dasa,
from birth lived together with Rasika.

**105.** Leaving house, wife, sons, all his family,
the son of Rama went around [the whole] earth.[^314-53]

**106.** Rasika's servant is Mangaraja Harichandana;
Gopinatha Dasa Pattanayaka is a mahajana.[^314-54]

**107.** Radhavinoda Dasa, Kalandi Bhagavan,
Paramananda, Manohara, Kanu, Krishnanama,

**108.** Krishnacharana, the brahmana Achyuta, Shricharana,
Gokulananda, Govinda — those who took refuge in Rasika.[^314-55]

**109.** The brahmana Govinda Dasa, Rasika's servant —
with prema for Krishna, night and day his body is overwhelmed.

**110.** Rasika's disciple is Kalandi, the best of brahmanas,
whose true home is Rasika's feet.

**111.** Akrura, Gopala, Hari, Sri Tulasi-dasi,
Raja Mitra, Chitrasena, Suvarna Vayasi.[^314-56]

**112.** The brahmana Govinda Dasa, Krishnabhakta Dasa,
Vrajamohana, the brahmana Shyamamohana Dasa.

**113.** Sri Gopala Acharya, Kalandi Dharambara,
in whose heart unceasingly is the best one, Rasikendra;

**114.** his sons — Radhamohana, Bhudhara,
Sri Radhagovinda, Radhakrishna, the best of brahmanas —

**115.** with all their family became Rasika's disciples;
they know nothing but Rasikendra.[^314-57]

**116.** Great in steadfastness, an embodiment of prema, Sri Govinda Dasa,
a disciple of Rasika, lives in Ghantashila.

**117.** He made many disciples in the land of Bhanjabhum;
he especially flooded [it] with prema for Krishna.[^314-58]

**118.** Rasika's disciple is Gangadasa Mahashaya,
an embodiment of prema, the son of Shridhara;

**119.** Daityari, Shyamasundara, Shyamamohana,
Shyamadasa, Bhagavan — six brothers.

**120.** All [of them] are Rasika's nephews, his servants;
for them Rasikendra-raya is caste, life [and] wealth.[^314-59]

**121.** Vrindavana-kishora is Rasika's servant;
together with [his] community he spoke [of] Krishna-tattva.[^314-60]

**122.** Chintamani [and] Vihari are very fortunate:
for them Rasikendra-chudamani is caste, wealth [and] life.[^314-61]

**123.** Achyuta, Shyamakishora, Vrindavana Dasa,
Shrirama, Bali, Vamana, Jagu, Shyamadasa.[^314-62]

**124.** All Rasika's disciples seek no other refuge;
unceasingly [they] serve the guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

**125.** Ghanashyama Dasa, Sri Beraya Vishnudasa,
in whose hearts Rasika's feet are manifest.[^314-63]

**126.** Bahubalindra, Sri Shyama, Rasika Dasa,
Chandra, Bhanu and others are Rasika's own servants.[^314-64]

**127.** The brahmana Gopimohana, Shyamamohana Dasa,
in whose hearts Rasika's feet dwell.

**128.** Vrajamohana, the renunciant Shyamarasika,
Sakhishyama, Gokula — very experienced.[^314-65]

**129.** In the land of Hijli is Vaikuntha Dasa Mahashaya,
in whose heart is Rasikendra-chudamani.

**130.** Unceasingly he serves hundreds and hundreds of sadhus;
selling himself, [he] is firm in the service of the sadhus.[^314-66]

**131.** Lala, Purushottama, Shyamakishora, Yugala,
Akrura, Shyamasundara, Vamshi, Manohara.[^314-67]

**132.** Sadashiva Pattanayaka, the sadhu Uddanda,
Krishnananda Harichandana — very formidable.[^314-68]

**133.** The brahmana Jivadasa Bhunya, Raghunatha Dasa,
Krishnadasa Bhunya and others are Rasika's servants.[^314-69]

**134.** Gajendra, Mathuradasa are very pure of mind;
they have no other goal than Rasikendra.

**135.** Madhusudana, Dvarakananda Mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra [abides] unceasingly.

**136.** Raja Ramachandra, Chitreshvara, Sri Chandana —
all with body, mind and words take refuge in Rasika.

**137.** Madho, Manohara, Niranjana Mahashaya;
Uddhava, Hari, Keshava — the sons of Bhima.[^314-70]

**138.** Shyamasundara, Vrindavana — the sons of Vamshi;
all with their whole being take refuge in Rasika.[^314-71]

**139.** The brahmana Radhavallabha, the son of Purushottama;
princes are Rasika's disciples, crowd upon crowd.

**140.** The two — Radhavallabha [and] Shyamadasa:
in Gahamagarh [they have] hundreds of thousands of disciples.[^314-72]

**141.** The brahmana Shyamasundara is a very great mahajana:
he cooks the bhoga for Krishna at Rasika's.[^314-73]

**142.** The brahmana Radhamohana, Uddhava, Bhagavan,
Nilambara, Vanamali, Ramadasa, Shyama.

**143.** Krishnananda Bhunya is very pure of mind:
for him Rasika's feet are lineage, character and caste.

**144.** Gopala Bhunya, Krishnananda Harichandana,
Gopala, Madhava, Raja Keshobanai.[^314-74]

**145.** The brahmana Sri Radhamohana is a great scholar,
Rasika's disciple, full of prema, with an intoxicated heart.

**146.** Radhavallabha Dasa, the son of Vallabha,
is Rasika's servant, and also Vrindavana Dasa.[^314-75]

**147.** Radhamadhava, Shyamasundara, Anuraga;
Rasika's disciple is Vanamali, the greatly fortunate.

**148.** Mukunda, Paramananda, Kanu, Bhagavan,
Agata, Mohana and others — servants, as is attested.[^314-76]

**149.** Gangadasa, Keshava and others, Sri Chandrashekhara,
Shyamasundara, Vrajamohana — the best of brahmanas.

**150.** Radhamohana, Bhaktadasa, Purushottama,
Shyamadasa who lives under a tree, Vrajamohana.[^314-77]

**151.** Akrura, Mohanananda, Nandana, Balaka,
Manohara, Sri Radhavinoda — manifest before the eyes.[^314-78]

**152.** Krishnananda, Krishna-jivana, Bhudhara,
Sri Gopala Dasa, Radhacharana, Akrura.

**153.** Mohana, Vrajamohana, Shyamadasa and others,
Yadava, Shyamamohana — greatly renowned.

**154.** Sri Vinoda Dasa, Chintamani Dasa — famous,
expert in music, very, very [skilled in] poetry.[^314-79]

**155.** The brahmana Sri Murali Dasa, the brahmana Sri Gopala;
disciples of Rasika — Dvijadasa, Sri Dayala.[^314-80]

**156.** Shyamadasa, Harinarayana Mahashaya,
in whose heart is Rasikendra-chudamani.

**157.** The brahmana Gopimohana Dasa, Shyamamohana,
the brahmana Yadunatha — people dear to Rasika.

**158.** Nilashyama Dasa, Gopimohana, Akrura,
Ghanashyama, Ramadasa, Govinda — a brahmana.[^314-81]

**159.** Jayadeva Dasa, Laichhana, Krishnadasa,
Sri Viravara Deu, Shankara, Kanudasa.[^314-82]

**160.** Sri Govinda Bhanja, Jagannatha, Krishnadasa,
Shyama Bhanja, Telai, Shripati, Ramadasa.

**161.** Mithi Bhanja with [his whole] community, Gopala Bhanja-raya,
Shyamadasa, Kishora and Madha-raya.[^314-83]

**162.** Radhakrishna Dasa is Rasika's own servant.
[Among] women — throng upon throng of disciples, beyond measure.[^314-84]

**163.** Rasika's servants are [like] the waves of the ocean:
who has such power as to count [them]?

**164.** I have considered ten or twenty principal ones
[and] briefly named a few — those whose names I know.

**165.** Behind each name are hundreds and hundreds of disciples;
there is no counting all of Rasika's disciples.[^314-85]

**166.** Now I shall tell briefly of the brothers' disciples —
the disciples, the disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples — one by one.[^314-86]

**167.** In the Pashchima-vibhaga I have proclaimed this —
whatever the son of Achyuta makes me speak.[^314-87]

**168.** Rasika's disciples seek no other refuge;
taking refuge in them, one obtains the treasure of prema for Krishna.[^314-88]

**169.** I have made the "Rasika-mangala" known a little;
listen, all, attentively, filled with joy.

**170.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Description of Shyamananda's Branches."*[^314-89]

[^314-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 14 begins. Raga Kaushika (*kauśika*; Purva, lahari 3, note 1). The ghosha — *jaẏa re jaẏa rāmakṛṣṇa murāre, o murāre o murāre* — is the same as in Purva, lahari 3: Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari ("the enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দ-শাখাবর্ণন-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śyāmānanda-śākhā-barṇana*) — "The Description of Shyamananda's Branches": the "branches" are disciples and their disciples (cf. the branches of the Chaitanya tree, CC Adi 10–12). The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^314-2]: "The purifier of the fallen" — *patita-pābana*. "The own dear treasure of the life" — *nija priẏa prāṇadhana*: Shyamananda is Rasika's guru. On the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^314-3]: "Absorbed in ecstatic feeling" — *bhābābeśe*. "Overwhelmed" — *jara jara* (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 16).

[^314-4]: "The twelfth-day festival" — *duẏādaśa mahotsaba* (*duẏādaśa* = *dbādaśa*): apparently a festival in memory of the departed held on the twelfth day after his departure; it may also be understood as "twelve festivals." "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇajana* (Purva, lahari 10, note 13).

[^314-5]: Govindapur — cf. Sri Govindapur (lahari 13, 15, 19; note 8). "Was fixed" — *karila niścaẏa*; the subject is not expressed (Rasika with the devotees). "The first aradhana" — *ādya ārādhanā*: apparently the first festival in Shyamananda's memory (on the aradhana festival, lahari 13, note 8). 5 is taken as Rasika's words (cf. 6).

[^314-6]: "It is fitting to bring" — *ānibā ucita*. "Communities" — *goṣṭhī* (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 20).

[^314-7]: "Meditation and remembrance" — *dhyāna saṅaraṇa* (*saṅaraṇa* = *smaraṇa*). "I have spent all this time" — *gela eta kāle*, "so much time has passed": absorbed in prema, Rasika does not know all of Shyamananda's disciples or where they live.

[^314-8]: "The brothers" — *bhāigaṇe*: apparently godbrothers, disciples of Shyamananda. "Every one" — *sarbajane*.

[^314-9]: "Adhikari" (9) — *adhikārī*: a successor, the head of the community, to whom the service of the Deity is entrusted (cf. 20, 29). 10b — *ihā aṅgīkṛta bujhi kara anubhaba*: the sense is approximate.

[^314-10]: "Carrying out Prabhu's work" — *prabhukārya anbeṣiẏā*, literally "seeking out Prabhu's work": Shyamananda's mission. "In due order" — *subandhāna haña*, "being well arranged."

[^314-11]: "The disciples of [their] disciples, the servant-disciples" — *anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya* (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 17).

[^314-12]: "Mahantas" — *mohānta*, abbots, teachers. "Renunciants" — *udāsīna*, detached wanderers. "Distinguish one by one" — *kara bhinna bhinna*.

[^314-13]: "Tell of the Shyamanandi servants" — *kaha śyāmānandī dāsa*; it may also be understood as an address: "tell, O Shyamanandi servants."

[^314-14]: "Love" (15) — *suprīti*. "Seeks no other refuge" — *ananya-śaraṇa*. "Firmly [devoted] to the guru" — *gurute niścita*.

[^314-15]: "Entrust to me the community" (17) — *goṣṭhī more kara samarpaṇa*: apparently "hand over to me [the list of] the community." "I shall write" — *kariba lekhana*: apparently he will send letters of invitation.

[^314-16]: "Detached" — *udāsa*: Rasika does not cling to the world (cf. his wish to wander, 11). "You have appeared" — *haẏecha prakāśa*: the disciples speak of Rasika as one who has appeared in the world for the sake of mercy; on the author's attitude to Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "The destitute" — *akiñcane*, "those who have nothing."

[^314-17]: "Equal to yourself" — *ātmatulya*. The service of Sri Govinda — of the Deity of Sri Govinda in Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, lahari 11).

[^314-18]: 21b — *rasika maṇḍalī kari basila bicāre*: understood as "Rasika, [gathering everyone] in a circle, sat to deliberate"; it may also be understood as "the rasikas, forming a circle, sat to deliberate." 22 is taken as Rasika's words: *sabāre sammata yā're sei paramāṇa / tbarāẏa bicāri āna kari anumāna*; *āna* — "bring" (cf. 43); "come to a decision" — *kari anumāna*.

[^314-19]: Rasika's sons are Radhananda, Krishnagati and Radhakrishnadasa (27–28; Purva, lahari 1, 110, 122, 124, note 48; Dakshina, lahari 11, note 24). "Born of one mother" — *sahodara*. "By their glance the three worlds were delivered" — *yāhāra kaṭākṣe uddhārila tribhubana*: the author's rapturous praise.

[^314-20]: The daughter is named in 28: Vrindavati (Purva, lahari 1, 121). "An abode that has taken refuge in prema for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapremāśrita-dhāma*. "Skilled in rasa" — *rasika-caturā*; it may also be understood as "skilled [in serving] Rasika."

[^314-21]: "[The account of their] glory" — *mahimā bicāra*. "To purify myself" — *āpanā śodhite*.

[^314-22]: 27b — *kṛṣṇagatimati kathā ati anupama*: understood as "Krishnagati — [his] mind and speech are incomparable," i.e. the middle son (Purva, lahari 1, 122); it may also be read as praise of Radhananda: "whose mind is set on Krishna, whose speech is incomparable." The author calls Radhananda the eldest, although Rasika's first-born was Vrajananda (Dakshina, lahari 11, note 18). Radhakrishna Dasa is Radhakrishnadasa (Purva, lahari 1, 124). "Daughter" — *sutā*.

[^314-23]: "Unceasingly" — *abacchinne*. "Striving towards Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera uddeśa*, "seeking of Krishna"; the subject of "see" is taken as "all" (30a).

[^314-24]: "The form of Radha and Krishna" — *rādhākṛṣṇa-rūpe*. "A well of bliss" — *ānandera kūpe*.

[^314-25]: "The forest of worldly existence" — *bhabāṭabī*. Pashandis (*pāṣaṇḍī*) — unbelievers, opponents of bhakti. "Are consumed by burning" — *jbaliẏā mare*, literally "burning, they perish": the pashandis cannot bear his radiance (the metaphor of fire).

[^314-26]: "Overflowing with love" — *gara gara rāge*.

[^314-27]: "To give Krishna and to take Krishna" (37) — *kṛṣṇa dite kṛṣṇa nite*. "The fruit of prema" — *premaphala*. "His," "that one" (38–39) — *tā'ra*, *se*: the one to whom Radhananda gives prema. "Ha, ha, ha!" — *hā hā hā*, cries of longing.

[^314-28]: "In his presence" — *tā̃'ra bidyamāne*: Radhananda was told of the decision.

[^314-29]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇagaṇa*, *kārṣṇajana*, as in 3 and 23 (note 4). The subject of "rose" is Radhananda and those who had come for him (43–44). "Prabhu" here and below is Rasika.

[^314-30]: "Have surrounded you" — *beṣṭilā*: apparently "have agreed upon you, chosen you" (40–41).

[^314-31]: "Govern" — *nibāra karaha*; understood as *nirbāha*, "management, administration"; the reading is unclear. "Community" — *maṇḍalī*. "Authority" — *adhikāra* (note 9).

[^314-32]: "Cloth" — *śāṛī*: here apparently a head-cloth (turban), a sign of succession, as Shyamananda tied a cloth on Rasika (lahari 13, 43, note 20). Radhananda is Rasika's eldest son (27; Purva, lahari 1, 110, note 48).

[^314-33]: The service of Sri Govinda — note 17 (cf. 10, 20).

[^314-34]: *kṛṣṇabhakti dite nite pāra sabākāra*: may also be understood as "you are able to give bhakti for Krishna to all and to take [it] from all."

[^314-35]: "The brothers" — *bhāigaṇa* (note 8). "Cannot be told" — *nā yāẏa kathana*. 57b–59 are the brothers' words.

[^314-36]: "Before, I described" — in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1, 46–145 (cf. 63). "His disciples, servants [and their] disciples" — *tā'ra śiṣya-bhṛtya-śiṣyagaṇe*: apparently the second generation — Rasika's disciples and their disciples (note 11; cf. below, 166: *śiṣya anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya*). The speaker in 60–61 is apparently the author (cf. 63), though the words may also be ascribed to the brothers (57–59). "Briefly" — *saṃkṣepe*.
