[^314-37]: *ebe bhāigaṇa śiṣya kahiye yugate*: may also be understood as "now, brothers, I shall tell of the disciples" (an address) or "now I shall tell of the brothers' disciples" (cf. lahari 15, 2). "Earnestly" — *yugate* (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 6). "With undivided mind" — *eka mane*.

[^314-38]: Kalandi (*kālandī*) is apparently a surname (of a family?), not a separate name: cf. "Kalandi Bhagavan" (107), "Kalandi, the best of brahmanas" (110), "Kalandi Dharambara" (113); in Dakshina, lahari 4 (note 8), "Kalandi" and "Bhaktadasa the yavana" were taken as two disciples. "First" — *ādya*. "True abode" — *nijabāsa*, "own dwelling."

[^314-39]: Shyamagopala is a disciple of Rasika (Purva, lahari 1, 131; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8; Pashchima, lahari 1, note 19). Kashinatha is apparently Kashinatha Dasa, Rasika's elder brother (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 22); Shyamagopala would then be Rasika's nephew. "One who says what is fitting" — *ye kahe ucitā*. 69b — *rasika kṛpāẏa khyāta baiṣṇabera tattba*: the sense is approximate; it may also be understood as "[he] by Rasika's mercy is renowned [for knowing] the truth about the Vaishnavas."

[^314-40]: Sri Jangha — *śrījaṃha*: the village is unidentified, the reading unclear. Draupadi is Dinashyama's mother (72). The shishta-karanas (*śiṣṭakaraṇa*) are a subdivision of the karana (scribe) caste of Utkala (cf. Purva, lahari 3, note 23).

[^314-41]: Dinashyama — Purva, lahari 1, 132; Pashchima, lahari 7, 13, note 10. "All the elders honour [him] as equal to a guru" (75) — *guru-tulya mānya kare saba gurujane*. "Pastimes of prema" (76) — *premera bilāsa*. 78b — *nija premabhakti yā're kaila samarpaṇa*: the subject is not expressed; understood as Rasika; it may also be understood as "[Dinashyama], who entrusted his own prema-bhakti [to people]."

[^314-42]: Ramakrishna — Purva, lahari 1, 132; Pashchima, lahari 7, 13. "Blessing of the world" (80) — *bhubana-maṅgala*. "For sport" — *kutūhale*. The author ascribes the fearlessness before tigers and crocodiles to the guru's mercy (*rasika-kṛpāẏa*).

[^314-43]: Goura-gopala — Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8.

[^314-44]: "Six tastes" — *ṣaṛarasa* (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 7). "Pure in conduct" — *sadācāra*.

[^314-45]: Prema-ankura (*prema-aṅkura*, "sprout of prema") is taken as a name. "The kadamba blossomed" — *kadamba phuṭāla*: the kadamba flower is a traditional figure for hair standing on end in ecstatic love (pulaka); a play on the name: among his servants and his servants' servants the "sprout of prema" came into bloom. The sense is approximate.

[^314-46]: Gokula — Purva, lahari 1, 82; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8. "Disciple from childhood" — *bālya śiṣya*. Kendujhar (*kendujhuri*) is apparently Keonjhar, a principality in northern Utkala. "In the forest land" — *banabhūme*, Vanabhumi (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10; Dakshina, lahari 8).

[^314-47]: Shyama-manohara, formerly Vishvanatha Bhunya; on his initiation and glory see Dakshina, lahari 10, 44–66 (notes 22, 26).

[^314-48]: Maharaja Vaidyanatha is apparently Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 10; Pashchima, lahari 7). "Left his body" — *dehatyāga karilena*. 95b — *bṛndābane dekhilena saba sādhugaṇe*: apparently, having left his body, he attained Vrindavana, Krishna's eternal abode, and saw all the saints there; the sense is approximate.

[^314-49]: Chhota-raya and Rautra are the younger brothers of Raja Vaidyanatha (Dakshina, lahari 12, 17, note 10). "Both" — *dõhe*: this confirms that they are two persons. "Very mighty" — *baṛai pratāpī*. "Deeds" — *karaṇī*.

[^314-50]: "Shyamadasa [and] Mohana" — *śyāmadāsa mohana*; possibly one person. "Prabhu" is Rasika. The songs of Jayadeva — the *Gita-govinda*.

[^314-51]: Govinda Bhattacharya, who preached in Vanga, is also named in the Purva-vibhaga (lahari 1, 102), there among Shyamananda's disciples. Vanga — East Bengal (Purva, lahari 1, note 45).

[^314-52]: Dube (*dube*) is a brahmana surname (*dbibedī*); the given name is not stated. Tarkalankara (*tarkālaṅkāra*, "ornament of logic") is a scholarly title. "The brahmana Sundara-raya" — *dbijasundara se rāẏa*; it may also be taken as the name "Dvijasundara-raya."

[^314-53]: The edition's footnote gives a variant for 104b: *bilāsa* instead of *nibāsa* ("from birth delighted [in the company] of Rasika"). "The son of Rama" — *rāmera kumāra*: apparently Mohana Dasa is the son of a certain Rama; unidentified. "Went around [the whole] earth" — *pṛthbī-parikramā*: pilgrimage to the holy places.

[^314-54]: Mangaraja, Harichandana, Pattanayaka are Oriya titles of the nobility and of the karanas (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 13; Purva, lahari 3, note 23). Understood: Mangaraja Harichandana is one person.

[^314-55]: The division of the list in 107–108 is uncertain. Kalandi — note 38. "Krishnanama" (*kṛṣṇanāma*) is taken as a name; it may also be understood as "Kanu, [whose name is] Krishna." "Those who took refuge in Rasika" — *rasikaśaraṇa*; possibly also a name, Rasikasharana.

[^314-56]: Sri Tulasi-dasi (*śrītulasī dāsī*) is apparently a woman. The division of the second line is unclear: *rājā mitra citrasena subarṇa baẏasī*; "Vayasi" (*baẏasī*) may mean "contemporary, companion": "Suvarna, [their] companion." Taken as names.

[^314-57]: Dharambara, Radhamohana, Bhudhara — cf. Purva, lahari 1, 80–81, 100. "His sons" — *tā̃hāra nandana*: understood as the sons of Gopala Acharya (or of Kalandi Dharambara, if this is one person).

[^314-58]: Ghantashila — *ghaṇṭaśilā*; the edition's footnote gives the variant *thuṇṭāpāre*. Bhanjabhum — *bhañjabhũi deśa*, "the land of the Bhanjas" (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 5). "Flooded" — *ḍhalāḍhali karila* (lahari 13, note 18).

[^314-59]: Shridhara is apparently Rasika's brother: his six sons are "Rasika's nephews" (*rasika bhrātuṣputra*, brother's sons). A Shridhara is named in the Purva list (lahari 1, 129); Rasika's elder brother is Kashinatha (note 39). The six brothers are Gangadasa, Daityari, Shyamasundara, Shyamamohana, Shyamadasa, Bhagavan.

[^314-60]: "Together with [his] community" — *sagoṣṭhī sahite*. "Spoke [of] Krishna-tattva" — *balilena kṛṣṇatattba*: he preached the truth about Krishna.

[^314-61]: Chintamani and Vihari — Purva, lahari 1, 131. Rasikendra-chudamani is an epithet of Rasika (Purva, lahari 1, note 59).

[^314-62]: "Bali" (*bali*) is taken as a name (cf. "Vamana"); it may also be understood as "named": "named Shrirama" (as *baliẏā* in 70). Jagu — *jagu*; the edition's footnote gives the variant *jaẏa*.

[^314-63]: "Beraya" — *beṛaẏā*: apparently a surname (from a village?); unidentified.

[^314-64]: Bahubalindra (*bāhubalīndra*) is apparently an Oriya title of the nobility (*bāhubalendra*); taken as a name or surname. The division "Sri Shyama, Rasika Dasa" is uncertain: possibly "Sri Shyamarasika Dasa."

[^314-65]: Sakhishyama — *sakhīśyāma*; the edition's footnote gives the variant *duḥkhīśyāma* ("Duhkhishyama"). "Very experienced" — *baṛai prabīṇa*.

[^314-66]: Hijli (*hijalī maṇḍala*) — a coastal tract in south-eastern Medinipur (Purva, lahari 10, note 21). "Selling himself" — *āpanā bikāñā*: giving himself wholly to the service of the sadhus.

[^314-67]: "Yugala" (*yugala*, "pair") is taken as a name; it may be understood as "the two — Lala [and] Purushottama" or "Shyamakishora [with] his pair."

[^314-68]: "The sadhu Uddanda" — *sādhu uddaṇḍa*; it may also be understood as "the unrestrained sadhu" (an epithet of Sadashiva); cf. Uddanda-raya of Nrisimhapur (lahari 13, note 15) — the person is unidentified. Harichandana, Pattanayaka — note 54. "Formidable" — *pracaṇḍa*.

[^314-69]: Bhunya (*bhuñā*) — a bhuiyan, a landholder (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 22; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7). The division of 133a is uncertain; understood as "Jivadasa Bhunya" on the pattern of "Krishnadasa Bhunya" (133b, cf. 143–144); it may also be "Bhunya Raghunatha Dasa."

[^314-70]: Chitreshvara, Sri Chandana are unidentified. "The sons of Bhima" — *bhīmera tanaẏa*: apparently refers to Uddhava, Hari and Keshava (or "Harikeshava" is one name). Bhima is unidentified.

[^314-71]: Vamshi is possibly Vamshi, the author's uncle (Purva, lahari 1, 137, note 57; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14); unidentified. "With their whole being" — *sarbātmabhābete*.

[^314-72]: "Princes" — *nṛpasuta*, "sons of kings." "Crowd upon crowd" — *yūtha yūtha*. Gahamagarh is unidentified. "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣa lakṣa*.

[^314-73]: "The bhoga for Krishna at Rasika's" — *rasikera kṛṣṇabhoga*: the food that Rasika offers to Krishna.

[^314-74]: "Raja Keshobanai" — *keśobanāi rājana*: the reading and division are unclear; possibly "Kesho, Banai, the raja."

[^314-75]: "The son of Vallabha" — *ballabhanandana*: apparently Radhavallabha, the author's son (son of Gopijana-vallabha; Purva, lahari 1, 142, note 59).

[^314-76]: "Anuraga" (*anurāga*, "love") is taken as a name. "Agata" — *āgaṭa*: unidentified. "As is attested" — *paramāṇa*, "[such is] the evidence."

[^314-77]: The division of the list into names here and below (150–162) is conjectural; most of the persons are unidentified (cf. note 55). "Who lives under a tree" — *gāchataliẏā*: apparently Shyamadasa's byname — a hermit living under trees (cf. *gāchatalā*, "the foot of a tree"); it may also be a byname from a village Gachhtala.

[^314-78]: 151a — *akrūra mohanānanda nandana bālaka*: "Nandana, Balaka" are taken as names; it can also be read "Akrura, the young son (*nandana bālaka*) of Mohanananda." "Manifest before the eyes" — *pratyakṣa*, "visible, evident"; the sense is unclear (perhaps "known in person," "now living").

[^314-79]: "Sri Vinoda Dasa" — *dāsa śrībinoda* (the word order is for the metre). "Expert in music" — *saṅgīta biśārada*; it may refer to Chintamani Dasa alone (cf. Chintamani, 122; Purva, lahari 1, 78). "Very, very [skilled in] poetry" — *baṛa baṛai kabitā*, literally "great, very great poetry"; the sense is approximate.

[^314-80]: *dbijadāsa śrīdaẏāla*: "Dvijadasa" is taken as a name; it can also be read "the brahmana Dasa Sri Dayala" (cf. *dbija* before names in 155a, 157).

[^314-81]: "A brahmana" — *bhūsura*, "a god on earth"; it apparently refers to Govinda, but may refer to all named in 158.

[^314-82]: Laichhana — cf. Loichhana Parichha (lahari 15, 11). Deu (*deu*) is an Oriya title (= *deba*, "deva"); taken as "Sri Viravara Deu," one person.

[^314-83]: Bhanja (Govinda Bhanja, Shyama Bhanja, Mithi Bhanja, Gopala Bhanja-raya) — the family of the rajas of Mayurbhanj (Purva, lahari 1, note 49; Bhanjabhum — note 58); the persons are unidentified. Telai (*telāi*; cf. Tilai, lahari 15, 52) is unidentified. "With [his whole] community" — *sagoṣṭhī*, with all his kin. Madha-raya — *mādharāẏa*, apparently = Madhava-raya.

[^314-84]: *strīri*: the reading is unclear; taken as "among women" (*strī*): among Rasika's disciples there are also women (cf. the women disciples in lahari 15, 71–74). "Throng upon throng" — *yūtha yūtha*. "Beyond measure" — *apramita*.

[^314-85]: "The waves of the ocean" — cf. 58. "I have considered" — *kariluṃ bicāra*. "Those whose names I know" — *kichu nāma jāni yā'ra*. 163–165 are the author's words (or the brothers', cf. 57–59).

[^314-86]: "The brothers" — *bhāigaṇa* (note 8): Shyamananda's disciples, Rasika's spiritual brothers. "The disciples, the disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples" — *śiṣya anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya* (note 11). The promise is fulfilled in lahari 15 (2, 25, 42–43).

[^314-87]: "The son of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kumāra*, Rasika (lahari 13, note 34). "Makes me speak" — *bolāẏa more*: the author ascribes his words to Rasika. On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^314-88]: "Taking refuge in them" — *yāhāra śaraṇe*, "in whose refuge." "Seek no other refuge" — *ananyaśaraṇa* (note 14).

[^314-89]: The author's signature (170) and the colophon are: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দ-শাখাবর্ণন-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" — the title agrees with the heading (note 1).


## Lahari 15. The Description of Shyamananda's Sub-branches

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikendra; Rasika tells the brothers to name to him in order the disciples and the disciples' disciples of those to whom Shyamananda gave the shelter of his feet; they name the disciples of Damodara — the first Shyamanandis Rasamaya and Vamshidasa, those who gave themselves to Damodara with their whole families, Anandadasa called Sadavarta, and many others, — the disciples of Nagara Uddhava, Shyamarangini and Purushottama, and a multitude of other disciples of the brothers; then the principal disciples' disciples, followers of Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Vamshi, Manohara and Mukunda: a pujari, brahmanas, bhuiyans and Bhanjas, musicians, garland-makers, and women disciples bearing the names of gopis; the Shyamanandis, like the waves of the ocean, know no one but Krishna, and whoever hears their names at once obtains prema for Krishna*

*The fifteenth lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^315-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory, glory to Shyamananda-raya!*
*May I, birth after birth, worship your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy!
Glory, glory to Rasikendra, the son of Achyuta![^315-2]

**2.** Then Rasikendra gave the command to the brothers —
to count the disciples [and] the disciples' disciples of the brothers:[^315-3]

**3.** "Tell me of them all in order, in detail —
of all to whom Shyamananda gave the shelter of [his] feet."

**4.** Reverently [wishing] to hear the names of them all,
[he listens,] and all name [them] one by one to Rasika.[^315-4]

**5.** Disciples of Damodara — Rasamaya [and] Vamshidasa,
who appeared [among] the first of the Shyamanandis.[^315-5]

**6.** They came to have thousands and thousands of disciples;
giving [them] prema-bhakti for Krishna, they delivered [them].

**7.** With [their whole] families there gave themselves to Damodara
Madhava, Rasikananda, Sri Harichandana;[^315-6]

**8.** Mohanashyama, Uddhava and Ghanashyama,
Kishora, Govinda, the fortunate Haridasa;

**9.** Keshava, Krishnavallabha, Narayana Bhunya,
Mattagaja, Gokula, Bankura Krishna Bhunya;[^315-7]

**10.** Gokulananda, Mathura, Shrimanta, Shyamadasa,
Mathura, Ananta, Purushottama, Ramadasa;

**11.** Gokula, Gauranga, Vishnudasa, Gopidasa,
Loichhana Parichha, Mohana, Vamshidasa;[^315-8]

**12.** Kalindi, Radhacharana Dasa, Manohara,
Sri Rangacharana, Madhuvana, Madhukara;[^315-9]

**13.** Shyamamohana, the brahmana Shyamamohana Dasa,
Sri Ananta-raya, the brahmana Shyama, Yadudasa;

**14.** Akrura, Sri Hari, Kanudasa, Govardhana,
Sri Shyamavallabha, Shyamadasa, Vrindavana;

**15.** Purushottama, Akrura, Sri Radhakrishna Dasa,
Sri Kishorananda, Vrindavana, Vaishnavadasa;

**16.** Bhaktadasa, Krishnananda, Haribhakta Dasa,
Govinda, Madhuri, Sri Radhamohana Dasa;

**17.** Kanudasa, Keshava, Gopala, Govinda —
Damodara's disciples [live] in all four directions, throng upon throng.

**18.** A disciple of Sri Damodara is the famous Anandadasa,
known to the world by the name Sadavarta.[^315-10]

**19.** Gopivallabha, Shyamacharana, Haridasa,
Gopicharana, Shyamacharana, Gopakrishna Dasa.

**20.** Damodara's disciples seek no other refuge;
even with a hundred mouths one could not tell [of them].

**21.** Each disciple has hundreds of thousands of servants;
the disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples — who will count them?[^315-11]

**22.** A disciple of Nagara Uddhava is Mukundadasa:
he came to have many disciples; he lives in Bandar.[^315-12]

**23.** Shyamajivana Dasa is very pure in mind:
by Uddhava's mercy he attained prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**24.** A disciple of Sri Shyamarangini is Ananta Dasa;
a disciple of Purushottama is Mohana Vinoda Dasa.[^315-13]

**25.** A little more I shall tell briefly of the brothers' disciples,
and then I shall tell of the disciples' disciples, one by one.[^315-14]

**26.** The brahmana Ramadasa, Shyamadasa, Vanamali,
Krishnadasa, Gopidasa, Radha, Chandravali;[^315-15]

**27.** Shyamavinoda, Radhamohana, Bhudhara,
Gopinatha, Yadunatha — servants of Krishna;

**28.** Vrindavana, Mathura, Gokula, Krishnadasa,
Dvaraka, Ayodhya, Gangadasa, Gopidasa;

**29.** Purushottama, Vishnudasa, Gangarama Dasa,
Shyamasundara, Giridhara, Mohana by name;

**30.** Haridasa, Narahari, Rasika, Sundara,
Manirama, Kalurama, Ananta, Bhudhara;

**31.** Gopinatha, Yadunatha — servants of Krishna;
in Shyamananda's family the disciples are very many.[^315-16]

**32.** Vrindavana, Mathura, Gokula, Krishnadasa,
the brahmana Sri Vinoda Dasa, Narayana Dasa;

**33.** Manohara, Shitala, Vinoda, Shyamadasa,
the brahmana Vishnudasa, Sri Radhavallabha Dasa;

**34.** Sri Nayananandadasa, Sri Nandakishora,
Vrajamohana, Kalindi, Navina Kishora;[^315-17]

**35.** Krishnakishora, Krishnakalindi, Krishnananda,
Krishnabhakta, Haribhakta, Sri Paramananda;

**36.** Bhagavan, Gopala, Gauranga, Chaitanya,
Sri Radhacharana, Gopicharana — undivided [in devotion];[^315-18]

**37.** Govinda, Shridhara, Damodara, Nilambara,
Vasudeva, Yadavendra Dasa Shirikara;[^315-19]

**38.** Madhava, Govardhana, Balabhadra, Krishnadasa,
Narayanabhakta Dasa, Pitambara Dasa;

**39.** Ghanashyama, Jaladharashyama, Gopidasa,
Prasada, Akrura, Uddhava, Vaishnava Dasa;

**40.** Vrajasundara, Vrajananda, Vrajanandana,
Vrajajivana, Vrajavihari, Vrajabhushana;[^315-20]

**41.** Madhuvana, Subala, Sudama, Premadasa,
Harinama, Vinoda, Govinda, Shyamadasa.

**42.** This I have told briefly of the brothers' disciples:
behind one name are a hundred disciples, servants by hundreds of thousands.

**43.** I shall name the principal disciples' disciples,
making Rasika's feet the ornament of [my] head.[^315-21]

**44.** Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Vamshi, Manohara,
Mukunda and the others — all the Shyamanandi followers:

**45.** I shall name the famous, worthy disciples of them all —
those for whom Krishna is wealth, life, father [and] mother.[^315-22]

**46.** Pujari Shricharana, Gauranga, Vinoda,
Shyamakishora, Kunja, Bhagavan, Vinoda;[^315-23]

**47.** Tulasi, Vihari, Radhamohana, Ananta,
Bhagavata Dasa, Gopinatha Dasa — saints;

**48.** Kanudasa, the brahmana Ramakrishna, Manohara,
Bhagirathi, Nimi, Kuladasa, Damodara;[^315-24]

**49.** Kanu, Vasudeva Dasa, Sri Harichandana,
Raghunatha, Vrajananda, Sri Vrajanandana;

**50.** Vrajajivana Dasa, Sri Ananta Dasa;
Ramachandra Bhunya with [his whole] community — all servants [of Krishna];[^315-25]

**51.** the brahmana Praharaja, the brahmana Sundara-raya,
Sri Chandana, Gajendra Bhunya, Jagata-raya;

**52.** Tilai, Shankara Bhanja, Sahani, Ananta,
Krishnacharana, Shyamasundara — pure in heart;[^315-26]

**53.** Lalavihari, Shyama, Rasika the vina-player,
Rasikasundara, Ananta, Shyama the garland-maker;[^315-27]

**54.** Vihari, Nikunja, Ghanashyama, Nidhuvana,
Govinda, Sri Hari, Vasudeva, Narayana;

**55.** Vanavihari, Shyama, Kishora, Rasananda,
Krishnaramani, Vishnudasa, Paramananda.

**56.** Ramai Shekhara is very pure in body:
Rasika's feet are constantly in his heart.[^315-28]

**57.** Udanda, Damodara Bhunya, Sundara-raya,
Gopala, Akrura, Hari, Uttara-raya;[^315-29]

**58.** Ramasena, Shyamasena, Sri Radhacharana,
Nidhuvana, Govardhana, the brahmana Vrindavana;

**59.** Ananda, Vrajavallabha, Vamshi, Bhaktadasa,
Ranabaja, Ranabhima, Manohara Dasa;[^315-30]

**60.** Shyamaali, Shara, Shyama, Sri Raghunandana,
Krishnavallabha, Gopivallabha, Bhima — a mahajana;[^315-31]

**61.** Kalindi, Keshava, Narayana, Shyamadasa,
Krishna Bhanja, Hari Bhanja, Rasamaya Dasa;[^315-32]

**62.** Harivallabha, Shyamavallabha, Sri Murari,
Shridhara, Purushottama Dasa, Sri Vihari;

**63.** Gopikishora, Gopicharana, Shyamaghana,
Shyamapriya, Radhapriya, Sri Krishnajivana.

**64.** The brahmana Sri Nagara Shiromani Mahashaya;
Mukunda, Mohana — the sons of Harichandana;[^315-33]

**65.** Vaikuntha, Vanamali, Vasudeva Dasa,
Balabhadra, Lala, Vamshi — all servants of Krishna;[^315-34]

**66.** Gopala, Sundara Pala, Gangadasa and others,
Ramadasa, Shyamadasa, Govinda Dasa and others;

**67.** Krishnadasa, Vamshidasa, Uddhava, Akrura,
Jagamohana, Jagabandhu, Kalandi — a brahmana;

**68.** Gopala, Sundara, Hari, Mathuramohana,
Radhagopala, Sri Radhakishora — a brahmana;[^315-35]

**69.** Gokula, Shyamakrishna, Sri Karunasagara,
Dinabandhu, Navaghanashyama, Manohara;

**70.** Jagatavallabha, Jayadeva, Kanurama,
Balakara Dasa, Sasagara, Balarama;[^315-36]

**71.** Yadunatha, Vrajanatha; Vrajarama-dasi,
Lalita, Vishakha, Chandravali, Bhadra-dasi;[^315-37]

**72.** Radha-dasi, Shyama-dasi, Kalandi, Tulasi,
Krishnapriya, Haripriya-dasi, Hari-dasi;

**73.** Chitrarekha, Shakuntala, Sulochana-dasi,
Mayura, Yamuna, Rambha, Sri Vallabha-dasi;

**74.** Subhadra, Vinoda, Hari-dasi, Shyamapriya,
Madhumati, Shashirekha, Sushila, Radhapriya;

**75.** Sri Rasavallabha Dasa, Govardhana Dasa,
Bhakatavatsala, Akinchana, Gopidasa.[^315-38]

**76.** The brahmana Ananta, the brahmana Purushottama Dasa,
the brahmana Kanu, the brahmana Rama, the brahmana Shyamadasa;

**77.** Kunjavana, Navina-madana, Vrindavana,
Ghanashyama, Jaladharashyama, Navaghana;[^315-39]

**78.** Giridhara, Mukunda, Sri Rangacharana,
Nidhuvana, Kripala, Gadadhara, Shricharana;[^315-40]

**79.** the brahmana Vamshi, the brahmana Bhakta, the brahmana Radhadasa.
The servants [and] slaves among the Shyamanandis cannot be told.[^315-41]

**80.** The hosts of the Shyamanandis are like the waves of the ocean:
who has the power to describe [them] all?

**81.** Briefly I have named a few — [only] the principal ones;
all of them have disciples [and] disciples' disciples by hundreds of thousands.[^315-42]

**82.** All the Shyamanandis, the devotees of Krishna, seek no other refuge:
none [of them] knows anyone but Krishna.

**83.** From [the time when], coming out of the womb, they fell upon the earth, [their] meditation is Krishna;
their caste [and] the treasure of their life is Krishna, and [their very] life [is Krishna].[^315-43]

**84.** Whoever hears the names of them all
obtains without delay the treasure of prema for Krishna.[^315-44]

**85.** This "Rasika-mangala" I have made known —
what the son of Achyuta, abiding in [my] heart, speaks.[^315-45]

**86.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifteenth lahari, called "The Description of Shyamananda's Sub-branches."*[^315-46]

[^315-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("পঞ্চদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 15 begins. Raga Karuna-shri (*karuṇāśrī*; Purva, lahari 1, note 8; Dakshina, lahari 1, note 1). The ghosha is *jaẏa jaẏa śyāmānanda rāẏa / janame janame yena bandi tuẏā pāẏa*; "raya" (*rāẏa*) is a respectful form of address. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দোপশাখা-বর্ণননাম পঞ্চদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śyāmānanda-upaśākhā-barṇana*) — "The Description of Shyamananda's Sub-branches": the "sub-branches" (*upaśākhā*) are the disciples' disciples, the branches of the second generation (cf. the "branches" of lahari 14, note 1; CC Adi 10–12). The summary line covers the whole lahari. The division of the lists into names in this lahari is in many places conjectural; most of the persons are unidentified.

[^315-2]: "The ocean of mercy" — *karuṇāsāgara*. "The son of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kumāra*, Rasika (lahari 14, note 87). On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^315-3]: "The brothers" — *bhāigaṇe*: Shyamananda's disciples, Rasika's spiritual brothers (lahari 14, note 8). "The disciples' disciples" — *anuśiṣya* (lahari 14, note 11). The command — cf. lahari 14, 12, 166.

[^315-4]: "The shelter of [his] feet" (3) — *padachāẏā*: refuge, initiation. 4a — *śunibāre śraddhā kari se sabāra nāma*: the subject is not expressed; taken as Rasika. "Name to Rasika" — *kahe … rasikera sthāna*, "tell in Rasika's presence."

[^315-5]: Rasamaya is the author's father, Vamshidasa (Vamshi) his uncle; together with their brother Mathura they are the grandsons of Bhima Shirikara, the first Shyamanandis, disciples of Damodara (Dakshina, lahari 4, 34–35, note 14). Damodara is the former yogi who became Shyamananda's disciple (Dakshina, lahari 1). "Who appeared [among] the first of the Shyamanandis" — *ādya śyāmānandīte yā̃hāra parakāśa* (*yā̃hāra* is singular: it may refer to Vamshidasa alone, cf. Dakshina, lahari 4, 35); it can also be read as one name, "Rasamaya Vamshidasa."

[^315-6]: "Gave themselves" — *bikāila*, literally "sold themselves": surrendered wholly. Rasikananda (*rasikānanda*) here is apparently a namesake of Rasika, a disciple of Damodara. Harichandana is an Oriya title of the nobility (lahari 14, note 54).

[^315-7]: Bhunya (*bhuñā*) — a bhuiyan, a landholder (lahari 14, note 69). Mattagaja (*mattagaja*, "an elephant in rut") is taken as a name. "Bankura" (*bā̃kuṛā*) is apparently a byname from the district of Bankura (north of Medinipur); it can also be read as two persons — "Bankura, Krishna Bhunya."

[^315-8]: Mathura (10) is named twice — so in the edition. Loichhana Parichha (*loichana parichā*): Parichha is an Oriya title (a steward, an official); taken as one person; cf. Laichhana (lahari 14, 159).

[^315-9]: Kalindi is apparently the same byname as Kalandi (lahari 14, note 38; cf. 67, 72). Sri Rangacharana (*śrīrāṅgācaraṇa*, "crimson feet") — so in the 1941 edition; the same name occurs (78).

[^315-10]: Sadavarta (*sadābartta* = *sadābrata*) — "a perpetual distribution of food," a house where sadhus and the poor are fed; apparently a byname of Anandadasa, who fed everyone. "Famous" — *khyātā*.

[^315-11]: "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣā lakṣā*. "The disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples" — *anu-śiṣya bhṛtya-śiṣya* (lahari 14, note 11).

[^315-12]: Uddhava is a disciple of Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, 76; BR 15, 63–65; Dakshina, lahari 11). "Nagara" (*nāgara*) is apparently a byname ("townsman," "refined, elegant"); cf. "Nagara Shiromani" (64). "In Bandar" — *bandare*, literally "in the harbour, in the trading port"; possibly the name of a village; unidentified.

[^315-13]: Shyamarangini — cf. Sri Shyamaranginidasa, a disciple of Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, 83). Purushottama is apparently a disciple of Shyamananda (Purva, lahari 1, 81, 95; BR 15, 63). "Mohana Vinoda Dasa" is one person or two (Mohana, Vinoda Dasa).

[^315-14]: 25 is a transition: 26–41 list further disciples of the brothers (without naming their gurus), in 42 this list is closed, and from 43 the disciples' disciples begin. "A little more I shall tell briefly" — *kichu kahiye saṃkṣepe*.

[^315-15]: Radha, Chandravali (*rādhā candrābalī*) — so in the 1941 edition; among men's names, apparently the names of disciples (or of women disciples, cf. 71–74).

[^315-16]: 31a repeats 27b, and 32a repeats 28a: so in the edition; translated as it stands. "In Shyamananda's family" — *śyāmānanda paribāre*, in his spiritual lineage.

[^315-17]: Sri Nayananandadasa — *śrīnaẏanānandadāsa*; the edition's footnote gives the variant *nandanandana* ("Nandanandana"). "Navina Kishora" can also be read "young Kishora."

[^315-18]: "Undivided [in devotion]" — *ananya*; it can also be read as a name — Ananya.

[^315-19]: Shirikara is a byname (Purva, lahari 1, note 39); taken as "Yadavendra Dasa Shirikara," one person; it can also be read "Yadavendra Dasa, Shirikara." Yadavendradasa is also named in Purva, lahari 1, 70.

[^315-20]: The names in 40 are epithets of Krishna as the Lord of Vraja (*braja-*: "the beauty of Vraja," "the bliss of Vraja," and so on), given to disciples.

[^315-21]: "The principal disciples' disciples" — *pradhāna pradhāna … anu-śiṣyagaṇa*. 44 names their gurus: Dinashyama and Ramakrishna are disciples of Rasika (lahari 14, 72–82, notes 41–42); Vamshi — note 5; Manohara and Mukunda are unidentified (cf. Shyama-manohara, lahari 14, note 47). "Followers" — *anucara*. 46–75 are the disciples of these teachers.

[^315-22]: "Famous" — *bikhyātā*. "Those for whom Krishna is wealth, life, father [and] mother" — *yā sabāra kṛṣṇadhana prāṇa pitā mātā*.

[^315-23]: "Pujari" — *pūjārī*, a servant of the Deity who performs puja; taken as Shricharana's byname. Kunja (*kuñja*, "grove") — so in the 1941 edition; taken as a name. Vinoda is named twice.

[^315-24]: Nimi (*nimī*), Kuladasa (*kuladāsa*) — so in the 1941 edition. Bhagirathi is a man's name (or a woman disciple).

[^315-25]: "With [his whole] community" — *sagoṣṭhī* (lahari 14, note 83). "All servants [of Krishna]" — *sabe dāsa*; it can also be read "all [his] servants."

[^315-26]: Praharaja (*praharāja*) and Sahani (*sāhāni*) are Oriya titles or surnames; taken as names; it can also be read "Shankara Bhanja Sahani," one person. Tilai (*tilāi*) — cf. Telai (lahari 14, 160). Chandana — cf. lahari 14, 136. Bhanja — lahari 14, note 83. "Pure in heart" — *śuddha cita*.

[^315-27]: "The vina-player" — *bīṇākāra*; "the garland-maker" — *mālākāra*, apparently of the malakara (florist) caste; both words are taken as bynames of those named before them; they can also be read as separate persons.

[^315-28]: "Ramai Shekhara" is one person or two (Ramai, Shekhara). "Pure in body" — *śuddha kalebara*.

[^315-29]: Udanda — *udaṇḍa*; cf. Uddanda (lahari 14, 132, note 68). Uttara-raya — *uttara se rāẏa*; it can also be read "Hari Uttara-raya."

[^315-30]: Ranabaja (*raṇabāja*) and Ranabhima (*raṇabhīma*) — "sounding in battle," "terrible in battle": apparently martial bynames (Oriya nobility).

[^315-31]: 60a — *śyāmaalī śara śyāma śrīraghunandana*: the reading and the division are unclear; "Shyamaali" (*śyāma-alī*, "Shyama's bee"?) and "Shara" are taken as names. "Mahajana" — *mahājana*; taken as an epithet of Bhima.

[^315-32]: Krishna Bhanja and Hari Bhanja are of the Bhanja family (lahari 14, note 83); this Krishna Bhanja is apparently not the maharaja Krishna Bhanja-deva (Purva, lahari 1, 113). Rasamaya Dasa (*rasamaẏa dāsa*) is apparently a namesake of Rasamaya, the author's father (5); unidentified. Kalindi — note 9.

[^315-33]: "The brahmana Sri Nagara Shiromani" — *dbija śrīnāgara śiromaṇi*; "Shiromani" ("crown jewel") can also be read as an epithet: "Nagara, the crown jewel [of brahmanas]." Cf. Nagara Uddhava (22). Harichandana — note 6; Mukunda and Mohana are apparently the sons of a certain Harichandana.

[^315-34]: "All servants of Krishna" — *sabe kṛṣṇadāsa*; it can also be read "all [of them] Krishnadasas."

[^315-35]: "A brahmana" (67, 68) — *bhūsura* (lahari 14, note 81), *brāhmaṇa*; apparently referring to the last name of the line. Kalandi (*kālandi*) — note 9.

[^315-36]: 70b — *dāsa bālakara sasāgara balarāma*: the division is unclear; taken as "Balakara Dasa, Sasagara, Balarama."

[^315-37]: After Yadunatha and Vrajanatha (71a) come the women disciples (71–74): "-dasi" (*dāsī*), "maidservant," is part of the name. Many of them bear the names of gopis — Radha's friends and maidservants (Lalita, Vishakha, Chitrarekha (Chitra), Shashirekha and others), and also Chandravali and Bhadra. "Haripriya-dasi" (72) — *haripriẏā dāsī*; it can also be read "Haripriya, Dasi." Kalandi — note 9.

[^315-38]: "Bhakatavatsala" (*bhakatabatsala*, "loving to the devotees") and "Akinchana" (*akiñcana*, "possessing nothing") are taken as names; they can also be read as epithets of Gopidasa: "Gopidasa, loving to the devotees, the continuation (76–86, the author's signature and the colophon) is.

[^315-39]: The division of the list 76–79 into names is conjectural. "Brahmana" — *dbija* before a name. Navina-madana (*nabīnamadana*, "the young Madana") is taken as one name; Kunjavana, Vrindavana (cf. 14), Nidhuvana (78) are names after the groves of Vraja (cf. Madhuvana, 12, 41). Ghanashyama, Jaladharashyama — as in 39; Navaghana (*nabaghana*, "new cloud") — cf. Navaghanashyama (69).

[^315-40]: Sri Rangacharana — note 9. Kripala (*kṛpāla*, "merciful") is taken as a name. Shricharana — cf. Pujari Shricharana (46).

[^315-41]: "The brahmana Vamshi, the brahmana Bhakta" — *dbijabaṃśī dbijabhakta*: these may also be understood as the names "Dvijavamshi," "Dvijabhakta." "The servants [and] slaves among the Shyamanandis" — *śyāmānandī bhṛtyadāsa*.

[^315-42]: "The waves of the ocean" — cf. lahari 14, 58, 163. "[Only] the principal ones" — *pradhāna sbarūpe*, "as the principal ones." "Disciples' disciples" — *anuśiṣya* (note 11).

[^315-43]: "The devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇya*. "Seek no other refuge" — *ananyaśaraṇa* (lahari 14, note 14). 83 — *garbha haite bhūmigata haiñā kṛṣṇadhyāna / jāti prāṇadhana yā'ra kṛṣṇa āra prāṇa*: the sense is approximate — from their very birth they meditate on Krishna; Krishna is for them caste, the treasure of life and life itself (cf. lahari 14, 67, 143: Rasika's feet are "lineage, character and caste").

[^315-44]: The fruit of hearing the names — cf. lahari 13, 74.

[^315-45]: "Have made known" — *kariluṃ pracāra*. "The son of Achyuta" — *acyutakumāra*, Rasika; "abiding in [my] heart, speaks" — *hṛde thāki yebā bale*: the author ascribes his words to Rasika (lahari 13, note 34; lahari 14, note 87). On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^315-46]: The author's signature (86) and the colophon are: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দোপশাখা-বর্ণননাম পঞ্চদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" — the title agrees with the heading (note 1).


## Lahari 16. The Description of the Great Festival of Separation from Sri Sri Shyamananda Prabhu

*A song in glory of Shyamananda and Rasikendra; having heard from the brothers about the Shyamanandis, Rasika writes to everyone — kings, bhuiyans, Vaishnavas, sannyasis, brahmanas — inviting them to the great festival, and himself sets out to collect alms; mountains of rice, beans, flour, sugar, ghee and oil are stored, sweets, fruits, coconuts, spices, vegetables and utensils, and lodgings are built for the sadhus — four times as much as for the Great Rasa; the festival ground is adorned, and the circle of the rasa is built with a throne, canopies, banners and auspicious pots; on the full moon of Jyeshtha, the day of the Deity's bathing, Rasika performs the adhivasa; communities, mahantas, Vaishnavas, Vrajavasis, kings and subjects gather, and Rasika honours everyone with gifts, first of all Tulasi, who began the sankirtana; with the onset of the first day of the dark fortnight the festival begins: hundreds of brahmanas cook and serve, thousands at once honour prasada, and the demigods, unrecognised, feast and play with Rasika; after the meal with the mahantas and the brothers Rasika dances in the kirtana, showing all the signs of ecstasy, amid lights and the sounds of many instruments, as if Vrindavana had appeared before the eyes; the author asks the learned not to count his faults and concludes the Pashchima-vibhaga*

*The sixteenth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^316-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Turn Your attention to the fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of compassion!
Glory to Rasikendra-chandra, the treasury of all virtues!

**2.** Hearing from the mouths of the brothers about the community of the Shyamanandis,
Thakura Rasika rejoiced greatly.[^316-2]

**3.** To everyone, as was fitting [for each], he wrote:
"Come [and] behold the greatest festival."[^316-3]

**4.** To kings, subjects, bhuiyans, mahajanas, sadhus,
elders, Vaishnavas, sannyasis, brahmanas,

**5.** to the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas — as was fitting [for each] —
Rasika-Murari wrote, one by one.[^316-4]

**6.** He himself set out to collect alms;
for the festival he quickly [gathered] all the provisions.[^316-5]

**7.** First of all he [stored] rice beyond measure:
bringing [it] in mountains, they pour it into the granaries.[^316-6]

**8.** Much mung [and] biri they stored, filling baskets,
and much chona, chickpeas, khariya, khesari;

**9.** wheat, maida, barley, roasted-grain flour — in abundance;
gur, sugar, khanda-pheni, lovely misri.[^316-7]

**10.** Filling house after house, they stored [everything] in its place;
areca nuts [and] ghee — carefully, in hundreds and hundreds of jars;

**11.** mustard [and] sesame oil — in hundreds and hundreds of pots;
khai, chida, hudumba, ukhra — beyond measure.[^316-8]

**12.** Sweets fried in ghee, cakes of many kinds —
filling hundreds and hundreds of pots, they stored each [separately].

**13.** Luchi, puri, curd, milk, palo, cream, chhana
the household prepares at the proper time.[^316-9]

**14.** Very soft laddus, chida fried in ghee,
ripe mangoes [and] jackfruits — hundreds and hundreds of baskets;

**15.** bananas of many kinds, ripe [and] soft;
narengas, kamalas, fragrant mau-tabas.[^316-10]

**16.** Young coconuts, ripe coconuts, bana-pairas and dry coconuts
the disciples bring in hundreds and hundreds of loads.[^316-11]

**17.** Lime, khadira, areca nuts, betel leaves — beyond measure;
nutmeg, cloves, mace, bay leaves;

**18.** fennel, cumin, and also pepper, camphor,
ginger and the other pungent [spices] they quickly stored.[^316-12]

**19.** All [that is needed] for cooking people bring, one after another:
greens of many kinds, badi, bananas, eggplants,

**20.** tender lau, maja, kushmanda gourds, karelas,
palata, patara-phalas — they brought them in good time.[^316-13]

**21.** All this in many ways, in due order, the followers
brought and, filling the houses, stored.

**22.** Pots, jars, earthen lids, sarais, oil vessels,
spatulas, bontis, areca-nut cutters, brooms;[^316-14]

**23.** new kanduis [and] large baskets they made in plenty;
and sieves for washing rice, and winnowing fans they had brought in plenty.[^316-15]

**24.** Salt, methi, hingu, turmeric, ground mustard [they stored],
[and] flour of atapa rice to adorn the pavilion.[^316-16]

**25.** For the sadhus they built excellent lodgings;
blankets, bhota, mats — of many kinds.[^316-17]

**26.** Thus he quickly [gathered] various provisions.
As before, for the Great Rasa, [he had gathered] loads of provisions, —

**27.** compared with that the provisions were fourfold.
Prabhu proclaimed the greatest festival.[^316-18]

**28.** All made the festival ground radiant:
arches, hanging tassels, beautiful chamaras.

**29.** Many canopies they stretched on firm ropes;
on [all] four sides — banana trees [and] handsome banners.[^316-19]

**30.** They enclosed the place in a circle of many-coloured cloths;
in its midst — a throne, most beautiful.

**31.** Around it — a fence of many-coloured cloths;
in every direction hang tassels [and] chamaras.

**32.** Various flower garlands hang all along [the fence];
seeing the arrangement of the pavilion, [all] are amazed.[^316-20]

**33.** Around the pavilion shine jewelled kundas,
[and] auspicious pots with coconuts [and] mango leaves.[^316-21]

**34.** Thus they arranged the place of the rasa;
the beauty of the circle of the rasa enchants all people.

**35.** In the month of Jyeshtha, on the full-moon day of the Deity's bathing —
on that day the mahashaya performed the adhivasa.[^316-22]

**36.** Many communities came to that place,
many Vaishnavas, mahantas, sadhus.

**37.** Thousands and thousands of Vrajavasis — beyond count;
kings [and] subjects by hundreds of thousands came in haste.[^316-23]

**38.** With garments, ornaments, rings, garlands, sandal and the rest
he honoured everyone, according to the rules, as was fitting [for each].

**39.** Hundreds of people [carried] hundreds of cups of sandal;
the brahmanas gave [it] to all the mahantas [and] Vaishnavas.[^316-24]

**40.** First Tulasi performed the sankirtana:
him the son of Achyuta honoured before [all].

**41.** According to [each one's] rank he honoured the shantas:
garlands, sandal and the rest, garments he gave to each.[^316-25]

**42.** At the auspicious moment, with the onset of the first lunar day of the dark fortnight,
in the morning he began the festival.[^316-26]

**43.** Hundreds and hundreds of people entered the storerooms;
hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas set to the cooking.

**44.** Hundreds and hundreds of people prepare [everything] for the cooking;
hundreds and hundreds of water-carriers all go [and] bring water.

**45.** Hundreds and hundreds of people stitch leaf cups [and] leaf plates;
hundreds and hundreds joyfully sweep [and] sprinkle [the ground].

**46.** Hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas serve [the food];
five to ten thousand [people] sit at one time.[^316-27]

**47.** Ten or twenty dishes, excellent shali rice,
khir, pitha, fried delicacies — the offering to Krishna;

**48.** ghee, curd, milk, chhana — of many kinds;
around the leaf plates — the leaf cups: a delight to see.

**49.** Cream, sugar, bananas — gifts of six tastes —
the brahmanas of pure conduct offer before Krishna.[^316-28]

**50.** At the fragrance of the prasada the demigods are enchanted;
if one partakes of [it], the three [kinds of] miseries do not remain.

**51.** The world of the gods and the world of men, coming together,
merrily honour prasada, dancing [and] singing.

**52.** No one recognises anyone; they play in many ways;
the demigods sport together with Rasika.[^316-29]

**53.** First the Vrajavasis ate;
after everyone [Rasika] sits down [to the meal], taking the mahantas with him.

**54.** What a market of moons — the host of mahantas!
He himself sits down, taking the brothers with him.

**55.** The principal disciples, the throng of disciples' disciples,
[like] stars, surround Rasikendra-chandra in the middle.[^316-30]

**56.** Having honoured prasada, all went to the kirtana;
the son of Achyuta himself dances.

**57.** What a sweet dance, what a gait!
What streams of tears — dancing eyes![^316-31]

**58.** What beauty of pulaka — kadamba buds!
What a faltering voice — the eight sattvika-bhavas![^316-32]

**59.** With the tears from his eyes the cloth on his body is drenched;
unrestrained streams flow — they cannot be held back.

**60.** Casting [his] Sri-anga on the ground, he rolls about, over and over;
the place of the rasa floats away on waves of tears.[^316-33]

**61.** The dark, beautiful body is grey with dust;
on it sweat, drop by drop — beautiful to see.

**62.** On his neck sways a flower garland, flower bracelets [on his arms];
on [his] Sri-anga shines a fine cloth.

**63.** Sweet-sounding nupuras adorn both feet;
the beauty of the murali in his hand cannot be told.

**64.** What beauty of the body's poses, what a gait!
What a gentle, gentle smile, what a sweet form![^316-34]

**65.** Chandrodayas, lamps, deutis, chandrabanas,
bhumichampas and the rest — all blaze on the place of the rasa.

**66.** The holy circle of the rasa became [brighter] than day;
there — Rasika's dance, most joyful.[^316-35]

**67.** Vina, venu, mridanga, mandiras, karatalas,
sarangi, kinnari, sweet-sounding svara-mandala;

**68.** pinaka, khamaka, kapinash — delightful;
some play pakhavaj [and] muchung;

**69.** rabab, tambura, saptasvara, the sound of the bamshi;
ayuja, dampha, dholaki — they are heard in unison.

**70.** All the musical [instruments] there are, created by the Creator —
hundreds and hundreds of people play [them] in concert.[^316-36]

**71.** What a blending of music — all in one tune!
And there — Rasika's incomparable dance.

**72.** Vrindavana became visible before the very eyes;
in this happiness the son of Achyuta spent the night.[^316-37]

**73.** Night and day in this happiness Rasikendra plays;
throngs of mahantas — on all sides, crowd upon crowd.

**74.** Even with a hundred mouths the greatness of that happiness cannot be told;
briefly I have composed a little beautiful praise.

**75.** In the Pashchima-vibhaga I have described this;
may the learned, the good, not hold faults in it against me.[^316-38]

**76.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixteenth lahari, called "The Description of the Great Festival of Separation from Sri Sri Shyamananda Prabhu."*[^316-39]

[^316-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("ষোড়শ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Pashchima, lahari 1, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Pashchima, laharis 1 and 9, and its translation is repeated (Pashchima, lahari 9, note 1: "Shyama" here is apparently Shyamananda). There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্রীশ্রীশ্যামানন্দপ্রভুর বিরহ-মহোৎসব-বর্ণন-নাম ষোড়শ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*biraha-mahotsaba-barṇana*). "The great festival of separation" (*biraha-mahotsaba*) is the festival in memory of Shyamananda's departure, held on the anniversary of his disappearance (notes 22, 26; cf. lahari 13, 49–50, 69; lahari 14, 3–5).

[^316-2]: "About the community of the Shyamanandis" — *śyāmānandī goṣṭhī*: the list of Shyamananda's disciples, their disciples and their disciples' disciples (lahari 14, 57–170; lahari 15). "The brothers" — *bhāigaṇa*: Shyamananda's disciples, Rasika's spiritual brothers (lahari 14, note 8). "Thakura Rasika" — *ṭhākura rasike*.

[^316-3]: "Wrote" — *karila lekhana*: he sent out invitations (cf. lahari 14, 18). "The greatest festival" — *mahā-mahotsaba* (likewise in 27).

[^316-4]: Bhuiyans (*bhuñā*) are landholders (lahari 14, note 69). Mahajanas (*mahājana*) are respected people, probably merchants and moneylenders. "Elders" — *gurujana*. "Sannyasis" — *nyāsī*. Rasika-Murari is Rasikananda.

[^316-5]: "To collect alms" — *bhikṣā karibāre*: to collect provisions for the festival, as before the Rasa-yatra (Pashchima, lahari 1, 19, 27, note 15). "Quickly [gathered]" — *karilā satbare*.

[^316-6]: "Beyond measure" — *apramite*. "Granaries" — *marāi*: round wicker grain stores (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 21).

[^316-7]: Mung and biri (urad) are beans (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 21); "baskets" — *ḍola* (ibid., note 24). Chona (*conā*) and khariya (*khāṛiẏā*) are apparently kinds of pulses; not identified. "Chickpeas" — *cholā*; khesari is grass pea (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 22). Maida is finely milled flour; "roasted-grain flour" — *chātu*. Gur is unrefined cane sugar; khanda-pheni (*khaṇḍapheṇī*) — according to the editor's note, *bātāsā*, airy sugar drops; misri is crystal sugar.

[^316-8]: "Areca nuts" — *guẏā* (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 22). Khai is puffed rice; chida is flattened rice; hudumba is apparently the same as hudum (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 24); ukhra (*ukhaṛā*) — according to the editor's note, *muṛakī*, puffed rice in sugar syrup.

[^316-9]: "Cakes" (12) — *piṣṭaka*, pitha. "Each [separately]" — *pratyeke*. Luchi and puri are flatbreads fried in oil (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 24). Palo (*pālo*) is a starch flour (from tubers); the sense is approximate. "Cream" — *sara*, the skin of boiled milk; chhana is fresh curd cheese. "The household" — *parijanā*.

[^316-10]: "Baskets" (14) — *jhoṛā*. Narengas and kamalas are oranges (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 26); mau-taba is apparently a sweet (*mau*, "honey") taba lemon (ibid., note 26). "Fragrant" — *parimala*.

[^316-11]: 16a — *paiṛa nāṛiẏā bāna paiṛa se jhunā*: apparently coconuts of different ripeness — paira (cf. Oriya *paiḍa*), a young green coconut; nariya (cf. Oriya *naḍiā*), a ripe coconut; jhuna (*jhunā*), an old dry coconut; bana-paira (*bāna paiṛa*) is not identified. "Loads" — *bhāra*: burdens carried on a shoulder pole (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 22).

[^316-12]: Lime, khadira, areca nuts, betel leaves — everything for pan (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 27). "Betel leaves" — *pāga*: apparently a misprint for *pāṇa*. "Mace" — *jāi*: taken as *jaẏitrī*; the reading is unclear. "Bay leaves" — *tejapatra*. "Fennel" — *pāṇamauri*. "Ginger and the other" — *ādrakādi*; the editor explains: *ādā prabhṛti*, "ginger and the like."

[^316-13]: Badi, bananas (*rambhā*), eggplants, maja, kushmanda, karela, palata — Pashchima, lahari 1, notes 25–26. Lau (*lāu*) is the bottle gourd. Patara-phala (*patarphala*) — according to the editor's note, *jhiṅgā*, ridge gourd (luffa).

[^316-14]: Kitchen utensils. "Earthen lids" — *sarā*, shallow earthen lids or dishes; sarai (*saṛai*) is not identified, apparently a kind of earthenware; "oil vessels" — *telāni*. "Spatulas" — *cāṭu*. Bontis — *panakhī*: according to the editor's note, *bãṭhī*, a curved blade fixed on a stand. "Areca-nut cutters" — *khilikāti*: according to the editor's note, *jā̃ti*. "Brooms" — *sammārjanī*.

[^316-15]: Kandui (*kaṇḍui*) — according to the editor's note, *ṭucani*; apparently a kind of basket; not identified. "Large baskets" — *cāṅgāṛī*. "Sieves for washing rice" — *cāladhuẏā*. "Winnowing fans" — *kulā*.

[^316-16]: "Ground mustard" — *sariṣā guṛī*. "Flour of atapa rice" — *ābātaṇḍulera guṛī*: the editor explains *ābātaṇḍula* as *ātapa taṇḍula*, rice husked without parboiling (from sun-dried grain); with such flour auspicious patterns are drawn on the ground (cf. Dakshina, lahari 10, note 10). "To adorn the pavilion" — *maṇḍapa maṇḍite*.

[^316-17]: "Lodgings" — *bāsā*. Bhota (*bhoṭa*) — apparently woollen blankets from Bhota (Tibet, Bhutan). "Mats" — *maśinā* (cf. Oriya *masiṇā*).

[^316-18]: "Before, for the Great Rasa" — *pūrbbe … baṛa rāse*: for the Rasa-yatra at Sri Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, lahari 1, 19–43). "Fourfold" — *caturguṇa*. "Prabhu" is Rasika. "Proclaimed" — *karilā pracāra*.

[^316-19]: Arches — *toraṇā*; "hanging tassels" — *lambita jhārā*; chamaras are whisks of yak tails; "canopies" — *candrātapa* (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 9; Pashchima, lahari 1, note 36). "On firm ropes" — *subandhane*. Banana trees are set up at entrances as an auspicious decoration.

[^316-20]: "Enclosed in a circle" (30) — *maṇḍalī karila*; it may also be understood as "made the circle (the place of the rasa)" (cf. 34). "Fence" (31) — *bāṛa*. "Tassels" — *thupanā* (cf. Oriya *thupa*, "tuft, tassel"); the sense is approximate. "All along [the fence]" (32) — *tā'ra lāge lāge*, lit. "adjoining it."

[^316-21]: "Jewelled kundas" — *ratnakuṇḍa*: *kuṇḍa* is a pool, bowl or vessel; possibly a misprint for *ratnakumbha*, "jewelled pots" (cf. the rhyme *kumbhe*). "Auspicious pots" — *maṅgala kumbha*: water pots crowned with a coconut and mango leaves (purna-kumbha).

[^316-22]: "On the full-moon day of the Deity's bathing" — *debasnāna pūrṇimā-dibase*: the Snana-yatra on the full moon of Jyeshtha (lahari 13, note 23). Shyamananda departed on the first lunar day of the dark fortnight, at the onset of Ashadha, after the Snana-yatra (lahari 13, 49–50); that is, on the anniversary of his departure. The adhivasa is the preliminary rite on the eve of a festival (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 19). "The mahashaya" is Rasika.

[^316-23]: "Communities" — *sampradā* (= *sampradāẏa*). Vrajavasis are residents of Vraja (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 15). "Beyond count" — *apramite*.

[^316-24]: "Rings" (38) — *mudi* (= *mudrikā*). "Honoured" — *pūjilena*: presented gifts and honours. 39 — *śata śata candanera donā śata jane / mohānta baiṣṇaba sabe dila dbijagaṇe*: the sense is approximate; "cups" — *donā*, cups of leaves; it may also be understood as "[Rasika] gave [sandal] to all the mahantas, Vaishnavas [and] brahmanas."

[^316-25]: Tulasi (*tulasī*) is taken as a name — apparently the leader of the kirtana (cf. Tulasi, lahari 15, 47); at Vaishnava festivals the kirtana singers are honoured first with garlands and sandal. It may also be understood as "first they performed sankirtana [before] Tulasi," the sacred plant, and then "honoured her before [all]." "The son of Achyuta" is Rasika. "According to rank" (41) — *pada anusāre*. "The shantas" — *śāntagaṇe*: "the peaceful" — renunciants, sannyasis; possibly = *santagaṇe*, "the saints."

[^316-26]: "With the onset of the first lunar day of the dark fortnight" — *kṛṣṇa-pratipada parabeśa*: the first day of the dark fortnight of Ashadha (note 22). "In the morning" — *bihāne*. The subject is not expressed; understood as Rasika.

[^316-27]: "Water-carriers" (44) — *bhārī*. "Stitch" (45) — *śiñe*: they pin leaves together with slivers, making cups (*donā*) and plates (*patrābalī*). "Sweep [and] sprinkle" — *jhā̃ṭī chaṛā deẏa*: they sweep the ground and sprinkle it with water for purification. "Serve [the food]" (46) — *prabeṣaṇa* (= *pariveśana*). "Five to ten thousand" — *daśa pā̃ca sahasra*.

[^316-28]: "Shali rice" (47) — *śāli anna*, the finest rice. Khir is rice cooked in thickened milk; pitha are cakes; "fried delicacies" — *pakvānna*. "The offering to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera nibedana*: food is first offered to Krishna and so becomes prasada (50). "A delight to see" (48) — *dekhite susāra*. "Of six tastes" (49) — *ṣaṛarasa* (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 7). "The brahmanas of pure conduct" — *dbija sadācāra*. "Before Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera sannidhe*: before the Deity.

[^316-29]: "The three [kinds of] miseries" (50) — *tina tāpa*: those caused by one's own body and mind, by other beings, and by the forces of nature. "Honour prasada" (51) — *prasāda pāẏena*. Unrecognised demigods at Rasika's festivals — cf. Pashchima, lahari 2, note 29.

[^316-30]: "After everyone" (53) — *sarbba pāche*; the subject is not expressed; understood as Rasika (cf. 54). "A market of moons" (54) — *cā̃dera hāṭa*: a figure for a radiant assembly of beautiful persons. "The brothers" — note 2. "Disciples' disciples" (55) — *anuśiṣya* (lahari 14, note 11). Rasikendra-chandra ("moon") amid the stars — a play on the epithet.

[^316-31]: "Gait" — *calani*. "Dancing eyes" — *nayana nācanī*; 57b may also be understood as "what streams of tears from the dancing eyes."

[^316-32]: Pulaka is the standing of the hairs on end from ecstatic love — "kadamba buds" (*kadamba kalikā*; lahari 14, note 45). "A faltering voice" — *gada gada kaṇṭha*. "The eight sattvika-bhavas" — *aṣṭa sāttvikā*: being stunned, perspiration, pulaka, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears, and fainting (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 2.3).

[^316-33]: "Sri-anga" — *śrīaṅga*, "holy body" (likewise in 62). "Rolls about, over and over" — *gaṛi gaṛi bule*. "On waves of tears" — *lohera hillole* (*loha*, "tears"; Pashchima, lahari 3, note 24).

[^316-34]: "Fine" (62) — *jhīna*: according to the editor's note, *pātalā*, "thin." "Gentle, gentle" (64) — *lohu lohu* (= *lahu lahu*, "softly, gently"; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 14). 61–64: the dark body, the nupuras, the murali in his hand, the poses of the body — the author describes the dancing Rasika with features recalling the form of Krishna, thus exalting his guru (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasika is a devotee of Krishna, a disciple of Shyamananda. The murali may also be understood literally: Rasika dances with a flute in his hand.

[^316-35]: Chandrodaya, deuti, chandrabana, bhumichampa are festive lamps and fireworks (Purva, lahari 12, note 17). "Lamps" — *dīpaka*. "Became [brighter] than day" (66) — *dibasa adhika haila*. "The holy circle of the rasa" — *śrīrāsamaṇḍalī* (cf. 34).

[^316-36]: The instruments — Pashchima, lahari 3, note 17; Dakshina, lahari 5, note 23: vina, kinnari, kapinash are kinds of vina; venu and bamshi are flutes; the mridanga is a clay drum; mandiras and karatalas are hand cymbals; the sarangi is a bowed instrument; the svara-mandala is a kind of zither; the pinaka is a stringed instrument; the pakhavaj is a double-headed drum; the muchung is a jaw harp; the rabab is a stringed instrument; the dampha is a frame drum; dholakis are small drums; the tambura (*tāmburā*) is a stringed drone instrument. Khamaka (*khamaka*) is apparently a one-string plucked percussion instrument; saptasvara (*saptasbarā*, "of seven notes") and ayuja are not identified. "In unison" — *ekamila*, *ekamela*. "Play" (70) — *bāẏa*: according to the editor's note, *bājāẏa*. "Created by the Creator" — *bidhātā sṛjana*.

[^316-37]: "Became visible before the very eyes" — *sākṣāt haila dṛggocara*. "Spent the night" — *bañce*.

[^316-38]: "Beautiful praise" (74) — *suyaśa racanā*. "In the Pashchima-vibhaga" (75): with this lahari the Pashchima-vibhaga ends. "The learned, the good" — *paṇḍita sujana*; "not hold faults against me" — *doṣa nā laibe* (cf. lahari 13, 72).

[^316-39]: The author's signature (76) and the colophon are; the title agrees with the heading (note 1). With this colophon the Pashchima-vibhaga ends; below it is a rule. The Uttara-vibhaga begins.


# Uttara-vibhaga

*The Northern Part*

## Lahari 1. The Description of the Farewell of the Mahantas and Vaishnavas at the End of the Festival of Separation, and of the Attainment of Vrindavana by Kishora and Chintamani

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; the author begins the Uttara-vibhaga; Rasika dances for twelve days at the festival of separation, and at its close a dadhi-kada is held amid the thunder of mridangas, with turmeric, curd and abir, and the dancing lasts until evening; Rasika generously gives gifts and sends off the rajas, the subjects, the saints, his kinsmen and the kirtaniyas, and all call him a partial incarnation; from then on he institutes the festival of twelve days; the elders Sri Kishora and Chintamani Dasa, brothers by birth, throw down the garments offered to them and revile Rasika, but he rejoices that the cloth has fallen on his head, as Shyamananda once tied a cloth on it, and humbly begs them for mercy; that same night the brothers fall ill and in anger leave for Kashiyari; Rasika follows them alone through the forests, serves them and calls physicians; the brothers admit that they have offended Rasika, in whose heart dwell Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita, their associates, Krishna and Shyamananda, and call him a portion of Narayana; after some days they depart for Vaikuntha; Rasika mourns them, holds a festival in their memory and goes to Dharenda, where a brahmana celebrates the days of the aradhana of Damodara Gosani; Rasika wanders, absorbed in festivals; the author promises the listeners deliverance from the age of Kali*

*Glory to Sri Sri Radha and Govinda!*
*Sri Sri Rasika-mangala.*
*Uttara-vibhaga.*
*The first lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^401-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna, treasury of virtues,*
*refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the friend of the wretched and destitute,
the benefactor of all people, the friend of the whole [world]!

**2.** Now I shall proclaim the Uttara-vibhaga —
[that] which Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, makes me speak.[^401-2]

**3.** Thus Rasikendra, [absorbed in] the rasa of the great festival,
dances in great bliss for twelve days.[^401-3]

**4.** The happiness of the great festival cannot be described even in part:
Rasikendra-raya floats in the happiness of supreme bliss.

**5.** Having completed the great festival, they hold a dadhi-kada;
in heaven, on earth [and] in the nether world the dundubhis resound.[^401-4]

**6.** Hundreds of mridangas thunder deafeningly;
together with the rajas — countless instruments of every kind.[^401-5]

**7.** The sounds of instruments, the clamour of the crowd, the sounds of sankirtana —
the earth trembles with the uproar of the cries of "Hari!"

**8.** Chuya, sandal and the rest, phagu together with flowers —
they throw them by hundreds of pots, each as he can.[^401-6]

**9.** Hundreds of people throw turmeric with curd;
all the people have their bodies adorned with abir.

**10.** Holding hands, all the people dance;
in their midst dances the son of Achyuta.

**11.** Until the fourth prahara [lasts] the dance in this bliss;
as evening comes on, the sankirtana is completed.

**12.** Having sported in the water, all finished the meal and the rest;
Prabhu sent [the guests] off, [honouring each] as was fitting.

**13.** Silk, silken cloths, various garments, ornaments,
tankas, gold and the rest the son of Achyuta gives;[^401-7]

**14.** camphor, sandal, nutmeg, pepper and the rest,
ghee, oil, gur, areca nuts, pan, cloves and the rest.

**15.** Whatever anyone desires within his mind —
knowing [their] minds, he gives parting gifts to each one.

**16.** Whatever thing the saints desire,
that thing he gives them and fulfils [their] wish.

**17.** Such a great festival has never been and never will be;
seeing [it], the rajas and the subjects are amazed.

**18.** All rejoiced seeing the great festival:
[such is] the power of Rasika, the friend of the three worlds.[^401-8]

**19.** All say: "Such happiness we have never seen at any time:
Rasikendra-chudamani is a partial incarnation."[^401-9]

**20.** All — the rajas and the subjects — took their leave;
[Prabhu] honoured all, each one.

**21.** Then Prabhu honoured his kinsmen;
having taken leave, all went to their own places.

**22.** Prabhu took leave of the kirtaniyas:
garments, ornaments, money he gave to each one.[^401-10]

**23.** Thus [passed] the great festival at Sri Govindapur;
from then on he instituted the [festival of] twelve [days].[^401-11]

**24.** To the elders — Sri Kishora [and] Chintamani Dasa —
to these two Prabhu gave splendid garments.[^401-12]

**25.** The two did not accept them — they threw [them] down before him;
the cloth, [flying back], fell on Prabhu's head.

**26.** Then the two reviled [him] — with whatever came to their lips;
hearing [it], Prabhu rejoices [and] laughs with happiness in his heart:

**27.** "Today, after so long, my good fortune has come:
reviling [me], they have placed a cloth on my head.

**28.** Formerly Shyamananda tied a cloth on my head;
now the two brothers have given [it] out of great mercy."[^401-13]

**29.** Saying this, Rasikendra fell at [their] feet;
in great anger, reviling [him], they rose abruptly.

**30.** Smiling, the son of Achyuta speaks gently:
"I am an offender; I am not worthy [even of your] punishment.[^401-14]

**31.** You two brothers by birth are an ocean of mercy;
regarding [me] as a servant, be merciful, [be my] refuge and protection."[^401-15]

**32.** Much praise he offered to the two of them,
yet they were not appeased, firm in their anger.

**33.** That same night both fell ill;
in anger both went to Kashiyari.[^401-16]

**34.** After them went Prabhu with tears in his eyes;
remembering the qualities of Krishna, he weeps without cease.

**35.** And [in him was] love in separation from Shyamananda:
alone he entered the forest — no one could catch up with him.[^401-17]

**36.** Passing from forest to forest, he enters that abode;
having come, Prabhu stayed with these two.

**37.** Gravely ill were the two brothers;
Rasika-shekhara served [them] in many ways.

**38.** He brought many physicians from various lands;
[they] were treated in many ways, as the physicians judged.[^401-18]

**39.** Sri Kishora [and] Chintamani understood in their minds
that surely the two of them had stumbled before Rasika.[^401-19]

**40.** Before everyone the two said:
"We two have stumbled at Rasika's feet.

**41.** Surely the son of Achyuta is a portion of Narayana;
not knowing [his] glory, we reviled [him] without cause.[^401-20]

**42.** He in whose heart Sri Chaitanya dwells without cease,
in whose heart is Nityananda's own home;

**43.** in whose heart dwells Sri Advaita Mahashaya,
in whose heart dwells Sri Abhirama;[^401-21]

**44.** in whose breast is Sri Subala-chandra,
in whose heart dwell Sri the twelve gopalas;[^401-22]

**45.** in whose heart dwell the eight Giris [and] the eight Puris,
in whose heart dwell especially the eight Bharatis;

**46.** the sixty-four mahantas dwell in his heart,
in whose heart dwell together the eight boys;[^401-23]

**47.** [they] dwell within his heart with [their] associates and followers,
in whose heart dwells the whole society of Vaishnavas;[^401-24]

**48.** in whose heart dwells Hridayananda Chaitanya,
whose union with the Vrajavasis is undivided;[^401-25]

**49.** Krishna, in whose heart [He] abides without cease,
in whose heart is Sri Shyamananda's own home;

**50.** whose meditation, waking and dreaming, is Shyamananda,
for whom Shyamananda Prabhu is caste, wealth [and] life —[^401-26]

**51.** at the feet of such a Prabhu we have committed an offence:
what [further] desire [is left] to us in life?

**52.** Why do you give medicines in vain in so many ways?
The black serpent of offence has truly bitten [us]."[^401-27]

**53.** Very wise, the two understood [it all] truly;
before everyone they told [these] truths one by one.

**54.** Hearing of Rasika's glory, all were amazed:
all the people recognised [in him] the very form of Narayana.[^401-28]

**55.** In many ways Rasikendra treated the two,
yet the two brothers did not recover.

**56.** After some days both went to the world of Vaikuntha;
[Rasika] weeps much because of the separation.[^401-29]

**57.** Then Prabhu held a festival [in memory] of the two;
to that village many loads of provisions were brought.[^401-30]

**58.** Having completed the festival, Prabhu set out;
coming to Dharenda, Prabhu settled [there].[^401-31]

**59.** [Then came] the day of the aradhana of Damodara Gosani:
a brahmana held two or three festivals.[^401-32]

**60.** Intoxicated with the rasa of festivals, Rasika-shekhara
wanders in the bliss of Krishna through lands near and far.

**61.** [His] boundless, ocean-like lilas cannot be described;
Rasikendra-raya was born for the deliverance of living beings.

**62.** By his mercy I have made known a little —
something of the qualities, fame [and] praise of Rasika-deva.[^401-33]

**63.** This is the first lahari in the Uttara-vibhaga:
[about] the lilas that Sri Rasika-deva performed.

**64.** Hear the Rasika-mangala, all the world:
for one who hears [it], the dreadful age of Kali is destroyed.

**65.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the first lahari, called "The Description of the Farewell of the Mahantas and Vaishnavas at the End of the Festival of Separation, and of the Attainment of Vrindavana by Kishora and Chintamani."*[^401-34]

[^401-1]: The lines before the raga are the opening lines of the vibhaga and the lahari ("শ্রীশ্রীরাধাগোবিন্দৌ জয়তঃ / শ্রীশ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল / উত্তর-বিভাগ / প্রথম-লহরী"), in italics without a number, as at the beginning of the Purva-, Dakshina- and Pashchima-vibhagas (the line "Glory to Sri Sri Rasikananda-deva!", found in the Purva, is absent here). The Uttara-vibhaga ("northern part") is the last, fourth part of the poem; lahari 16. Raga Narayani-gauda; the ghosha is the same as in Pashchima, lahari 13 (note 1), and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে বিরহ-মহোৎসবান্তে মোহন্ত ও বৈষ্ণব-বিদায় এবং কিশোর-চিন্তামণির বৃন্দাবনপ্রাপ্তি-বর্ণননাম প্রথম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*biraha-mahotsabānte mohanta o baiṣṇaba-bidāẏa ebaṃ kiśora-cintāmaṇira bṛndābanaprāpti-barṇana*). "The festival of separation" is the festival in memory of Shyamananda's departure at Govindapur (Pashchima, lahari 16). For the Uttara-vibhaga there is no second reading (the 1997 edition).

[^401-2]: "The friend of the wretched and destitute" (1) — *dīnahīna-bandhu*; "the friend of the whole [world]" — *akhilera bandhu*. "Proclaim" — *kariba pracāra*. "Makes me speak" — *more bolāna*: the author ascribes his words to Rasika (cf. Pashchima, lahari 13, note 34). "The son of Achyuta" — *acyuta-kumāra*: Rasika.

[^401-3]: "Thus" — *henarūpe*: the narrative continues the festival of separation (Pashchima, lahari 16). "For twelve days" — *dbādaśa dibase*; it can also be understood as "on the twelfth day". Cf. 23; lahari 2, 5; Pashchima, lahari 14, note 4.

[^401-4]: Dadhi-kada — a festive drenching with curd mixed with water and turmeric (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 37; cf. 9). The subject of "hold" is not expressed. Dundubhis — great kettledrums (here, celestial ones). "In heaven, on earth [and] in the nether world" — *sbaraga marttya pātāla*. "Resound" — *abatare*, lit. "descend".

[^401-5]: "Together with the rajas" — *rājāgaṇa saṅge*: apparently musicians who came with the rajas' retinues. "Countless" — *agocara*, lit. "beyond perception".

[^401-6]: Chuya (*cuẏā*) — a fragrant mixture; phagu (*phāgu*) — the red powder people throw at one another at the spring festival; abir (9) — a coloured fragrant powder. "Each as he can" — *ye yemate*.

[^401-7]: "Silk, silken cloths" — *pāṭa paṭāmbara*. Tankas (*ṭaṅkā*) — coins. Gur (14) — unrefined cane sugar; areca nuts — *guẏā*; pan — betel leaf.

[^401-8]: "Power" — *anubhaba*. "The friend of the three worlds" — *trijagata-bandhu*.

[^401-9]: "A partial incarnation" — *aṃśa-abatāra*: the rapturous words of the people at the festival (as also in Pashchima, laharis 2 and 3). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation of the Lord (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 37). On the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^401-10]: Kirtaniyas (*kīrtanīẏā*) — kirtana singers. "To each one" — *gāẏa gāẏa*, lit. "body by body", i.e. to each personally (perhaps clothing them in the garments).

[^401-11]: Sri Govindapur — the place of the festival of separation (Pashchima, lahari 13, note 8; Pashchima, lahari 14, note 5). "Instituted" — *kaila paracāre*, "proclaimed, spread". "The [festival of] twelve [days]" — *duẏādaśa* (= *dbādaśa*), lit. "twelve": apparently the twelve-day festival in memory of Shyamananda, which became annual (3; lahari 2, 4–5); it can also be understood as "the festival of the twelfth day" (Pashchima, lahari 14, note 4).

[^401-12]: "The elders" — *baṛa bāpā*, lit. "elder fathers" (*bāpā* — "father"; *baṛa bāpā* — also "father's elder brother"): a respectful form of address to elders. The editor explains in a footnote: "Shyamananda Prabhu's senior disciples". Sri Kishora and Chintamani Dasa are brothers by birth (*sahodara*, 31, 37, 55); it can also be read as "Sri Kishora-Chintamani Dasa", but further on the text always speaks of two (the colophon: *kiśora-cintāmaṇira*). Kishora is apparently Kishoradasa, one of Shyamananda's early disciples (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 37; Pashchima, lahari 1, note 10; BR 15, 41); a Chintamani is named among Shyamananda's disciples in BR 15 (63–65) and by the author (Purva, lahari 1, 131; Dakshina, lahari 11, 17); the identity with them is not established. "Splendid garments" — *dibya dibya bāsa*. The author does not say why the brothers are angry; apparently they, as senior disciples, do not accept the primacy of Rasika, to whom Shyamananda handed over authority in the community (Pashchima, lahari 13, 45–47).

[^401-13]: "Cloth" — *śāṛī*, a length of cloth: Shyamananda tied a cloth on Rasika's head with his own hand, entrusting the community to him (Pashchima, lahari 13, 43, note 20). Rasika sees in the garment that fell on his head a repetition of that mercy. "After so long" (27) — *eta kāle*.

[^401-14]: "Offender" — *aparādhī*. "Not worthy [even of your] punishment" — *yogya nahi tāṛanāra*: the reproof and punishment of elders is a mercy of which Rasika considers himself unworthy; it can also be understood as "I am at fault, [but] do not deserve [such] reviling".

[^401-15]: "Refuge and protection" — *śaraṇa-pañjara* (Purva, lahari 1, note 62).

[^401-16]: "Fell ill" — *haila asusthe*. Kashiyari — Pashchima, lahari 1, note 4; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 4.

[^401-17]: "Love" — *anurāga*, loving attachment. 35b — *ekalā paśilā bane nāhi pāẏa lāga*: understood as "no one could catch up with him" (*lāga pāoẏā* — "to overtake, to find"); it can also be understood as "[he] cannot overtake them". "Abode" (36) — *dhāma*: apparently Kashiyari.

[^401-18]: "Treated" — *cāhila*, lit. "looked after, cared for" (likewise in 55). "As the physicians judged" — *baidya abhimate*.

[^401-19]: "Stumbled" — *ṭhekila* (40 — *ṭhekilũ*), "ran into, came to grief": the brothers understand that they have fallen ill for offending Rasika (cf. 51–52). "Before Rasika" — *rasikera sthāne*.

[^401-20]: "A portion of Narayana" (41) — *nārāẏaṇa-aṃśa*; "the very form of Narayana" (54) — *nārāẏaṇa-sbarūpe*: the words of the repentant brothers and the author's rapturous praise. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 37; cf. 19); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "Reviled" — *nindinu*.

[^401-21]: 42–50 form one enumerating sentence, continued in 51: "at the feet of such a Prabhu…". Abhirama (*abhirāma*) — apparently Abhirama Thakura (Ramadasa), an associate of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas.

[^401-22]: "Breast" — *bakṣaḥsthala*. Subala-chandra — apparently Gauridasa Pandita, who in Krishna's pastimes is the cowherd boy Subala (Purva, lahari 1, note 16), the guru of Hridayananda; cf. the aradhana of Subala-chandra (lahari 2, 10). The twelve gopalas — associates of Nityananda (Purva, lahari 1, note 18).

[^401-23]: The eight Giris, eight Puris, eight Bharatis (45) — apparently sannyasis of the Giri, Puri and Bharati orders connected with Sri Chaitanya (such as Ishvara Puri and Keshava Bharati); the exact list is not established. The sixty-four mahantas — Purva, lahari 1, note 20. "The eight boys" — *aṣṭa bālaka*: possibly the eight boys who enacted the sakhis at the Rasa-yatra (Pashchima, lahari 2, 47, notes 31–32); not established. "Together" — *yugate* (= *yukte*?); the reading is unclear. "In his heart" (46a) — *yā̃ra hṛdgate*.

[^401-24]: "With [their] associates and followers" — *sāṅgopāṅga saha*; the subject is not expressed — apparently all those named above.

[^401-25]: Hridayananda Chaitanya — Hridayananda (Hridaya Chaitanya), Shyamananda's guru. "Whose union with the Vrajavasis is undivided" — *brajabāsī saṅge yā̃ra milana abhinna*: Rasika is at one with the inhabitants of Vraja.

[^401-26]: 49 is understood thus: Krishna abides without cease in his heart (*kṛṣṇa yā̃ra hṛdaẏe thākena nirantara*). "Waking and dreaming" — *śaẏane sbapane*, lit. "lying down and in dreams". "Caste, wealth [and] life" — *jāti dhana prāṇa* (cf. Pashchima, lahari 15, 83).

[^401-27]: "The black serpent" — *kālasarpa*, the venomous cobra. "Truly" — *sbarūpe* (likewise in 53).

[^401-28]: See note 20. "Were amazed" — *camatkāra*.

[^401-29]: "Went to the world of Vaikuntha" — *gelā baikuṇṭha-bhubana*: so the author speaks of the departure of Vaishnavas from this world; the colophon has "the attainment of Vrindavana" (*bṛndābana-prāpti*). The subject of "weeps" is not expressed — apparently Rasika.

[^401-30]: "A festival [in memory] of the two" — *mahotsaba … dõhāra*: an aradhana festival in memory of the departed (Pashchima, lahari 13, note 8). "Were brought" — *ānāila*, "had brought". "That village" — apparently Kashiyari.

[^401-31]: Dharenda (*dhārandā*) — Shyamananda's birthplace (Purva, lahari 2, note 6). "Settled" — *upasana*: apparently *upasanna*, "arrived, settled"; the sense is approximate.

[^401-32]: Damodara Gosani — the learned yogi from Chakulia, a disciple of Shyamananda who departed before him (Pashchima, lahari 13, 16, note 9). "The day of the aradhana" — *ārādhana dina*: the day of remembrance. "A brahmana" — *dbija*, "twice-born"; who this is is not said. "Two or three festivals" — *dui tina*: apparently two or three days of festival (cf. lahari 2, note 5).

[^401-33]: "By his mercy" — *tā̃ra anugrahe*: by the mercy of Rasika. "Praise" — *kīrtta*. "Made known" — *karilũ bidita*. 63 — *karila yateka līlā*, "all the lilas that he performed".

[^401-34]: The author's signature (65) and the colophon are; the title is as in the heading (note 1).


## Lahari 2. The Determination of the Annual Festivals

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; in Dharenda Rasika, with astrologer brahmanas and his kinsmen, establishes the annual festivals: twelve days of Shyamananda's aradhana after the full moon of the Bathing of the Deity, a festival for the Ratha-yatra, Hera-panchami and the appearance of Sri Chaitanya, for which he himself begs alms of cowries and handfuls of rice, five days of the aradhana of Subala-chandra in the month of gamha, the appearance of Krishna, the appearance of Thakurani — Radha, Kumara-purnima, the rasa festival on the full moon after Utthana-ekadashi and eight days in memory of Hridayananda before Dola-purnima — thirty festivals in all; Rasika wanders with hundreds of sadhus, mahantas, Rasamaya's community, Thakura Tulasi and bhattacharyas, crowds stream to see him, and in the houses where he stays provisions appear from no one knows where; for the festival days he returns home; after Shyamananda's festival at Govindapur he announces to the community Shyamananda's order to settle the three mothers, the Thakuranis, with the Deities in one house at Shyamasundarpur; Shyamapriya agrees to follow Rasika, and he remains in that village*

*The second lahari.*

*Raga Shri.*[^402-1]
*Ghosha: "O Hari, this time be merciful to me:*
*I hope to obtain the shade of Your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy,
at whose feet the servant is Rasika-shekhara![^402-2]

**2.** At that time in Dharenda the excellent Rasikendra
established festivals for every year.[^402-3]

**3.** Taking the astrologer brahmanas [and] his kinsmen,
he sat [with them] and determined on which lunar day which festival [should be held].[^402-4]

**4.** The festival of Shyamananda's aradhana —
at the close of the full moon of the Bathing of the Deity, on the first lunar day.

**5.** Sometimes in Jyeshtha, sometimes in the month of Ashadha,
he firmly established twelve festivals.[^402-5]

**6.** At Sri Ratha-yatra, on the day of Hera-panchami,
on the day of the appearance of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu —

**7.** for this he firmly established one festival:
begging alms of cowries [and] handfuls, he holds the festival.[^402-6]

**8.** He himself begs cowries [and] handfuls from house to house;
hearing [of it], all rejoice, charmed in their hearts.

**9.** One person brings hundreds of loads of provisions:
Rasika's lila astonishes the three worlds.[^402-7]

**10.** On the thirteenth day of the bright half [before] the gamha full moon —
on that day is the aradhana of Subala-chandra.[^402-8]

**11.** Five festivals he firmly established on that day;
without cease Prabhu floats in the rasa of festivals.[^402-9]

**12.** In the month of Bhadra, on the day of the constellation of Krishna's appearance (lit. "birth"),
he firmly established one festival on that day.

**13.** The appearance (lit. "birth") of the Thakurani — on the eighth day of the bright half of Bhadra:
for this he openly established one festival.[^402-10]

**14.** On the day of Kumara-purnima — one festival:
Rasika-chand holds [it] by his own inspiration.[^402-11]

**15.** On the full moon after Utthana-ekadashi
he firmly established the festival of the rasa on that day.[^402-12]

**16.** On the twelfth day of the bright half [before] Dola-purnima
he carefully established the festival of Hridayananda.

**17.** Eight festivals he firmly established on that day;
every year the son of Achyuta holds [them].[^402-13]

**18.** He chose these thirty festivals:
every day with Rasika, life is a festival.

**19.** Every year thus he plays:
Achyuta's boy is intoxicated with the rasa of festivals.[^402-14]

**20.** For the sake of the festivals he wanders from land to land;
hundreds and hundreds of sadhus are always with him.

**21.** Ten or twenty mahantas [are with him] day and night;
with him are Rasamaya's kin [and] Thakura Tulasi.[^402-15]

**22.** All perform sankirtana in great joy
