with Rasika night and day, without pause.

**23.** All the singers and musicians there are on earth
constantly roam with Rasika.[^402-16]

**24.** Five or ten bhattacharyas [are with him] at every moment,
[to] seek talks of Krishna with Rasika.[^402-17]

**25.** In a divine palanquin sits the abode of all virtues;
he reads the Bhagavata, always [chants] the Harinama.[^402-18]

**26.** Ceaselessly streams of tears flow from [his] holy eyes;
seeing [his] form, all people float in bliss.

**27.** Hearing those sweet words, all in bliss
forget themselves, gazing at Sri Rasikananda.

**28.** North, south, east, west — always,
always Prabhu Rasikendra-raya plays.[^402-19]

**29.** Thousands and thousands of people come to see [him],
raising a clamour of the cry "Hari!" on every road.

**30.** Women, the old, children, youths run in joy
to see Prabhu Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of devotees].

**31.** Pregnant women — all run with faces raised;
in the joy of seeing [him] they do not tidy their hair.[^402-20]

**32.** With tears of bliss they go, with longing hearts;
their voices choke with prema, pulaka on their bodies.

**33.** When they see the moon of [his] face, the darkness is dispelled;
the son of Achyuta steals the hearts of all.

**34.** Thus Rasikendra conquers the quarters of the world;
at [his] darshana the hosts of gods and asuras rejoice.[^402-21]

**35.** Be it a king, be it a subject, be it the saints —
[whoever] has Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, staying in his house,

**36.** seeing [his] moon-face, gains as it were ten million jewels;
even if he is poor, he gains the happiness of great bliss.

**37.** The eight siddhis [and] the nine treasures appear in his house:
all these constantly attend on Rasika.[^402-22]

**38.** [He] in whose house there is not even one ser of rice —
when Rasikendra comes to his dwelling,

**39.** [he] with a pure heart feeds thousands and thousands of sadhus
with fried delicacies, sweets, curd, ghee [and] panchamrita.

**40.** Where the provisions come from no one knows:
such is the wondrous lila of the son of Achyuta.[^402-23]

**41.** He always travels from land to land;
for the six seasons, the twelve months, he does not stay at home.

**42.** In whatever month falls the lunar day of anyone's aradhana —
on that day Prabhu goes home.[^402-24]

**43.** For the adhivasa of the festival he arrives;
having completed the festival, he again wanders from land to land.[^402-25]

**44.** Again the festival-aradhana of Shyamananda
the son of Achyuta held in Govindapur.

**45.** Two [festivals] of twelve [days] took place in that village.
Having completed the festival, all sat in assembly:

**46.** the host of mahantas and the Shyamanandis,
kings, subjects, mahajanas, Vaishnavas, brahmanas.[^402-26]

**47.** To all Prabhu Rasika-shekhara says:
"Shyamananda's order has been made unalterable for me:

**48.** 'Your three mothers you shall settle in one house;
if [they] live apart, [they] will not be honoured [as they should].[^402-27]

**49.** Vrindavanachandra [and] Vrajamohana Thakura
you shall ceremonially bring to Sri Shyamasundarpur.[^402-28]

**50.** All will serve together in that place' —
three times he ordered me in the depth of my heart.

**51.** 'In three places you will not be able to serve the saints' —
this order Prabhu gave me in person.[^402-29]

**52.** So that Shyamananda's order is not transgressed,
all [of you] make a request to the Thakurani.

**53.** Shyamapriya Thakurani [and] Vrindavanachandra
will go there — [such is] Shyamananda's order.

**54.** Then I shall go [and] bring Yamuna Thakurani:
in one house the three Thakuranis will live."[^402-30]

**55.** Hearing Rasika's words, all joyfully
firmly accepted those words in their hearts.

**56.** All went to the Thakurani
[and] conveyed the whole matter in Rasika's words.

**57.** Hearing everyone's words, mother Shyamapriya [said]:
"Whatever [gives] Rasika happiness, that is fitting for me.

**58.** He is the shining moon of the lineage of Shyamananda's community;
and all authority Shyamananda gave [him].[^402-31]

**59.** How shall I break his word?
Come, I shall go to that place at Rasika's word.

**60.** He is father, he is son: whom else do I have?
Wherever he takes [me], there I shall go, following behind him."[^402-32]

**61.** Hearing [this], Rasika was very glad;
having taken leave of all, he stayed in that village.

**62.** Of [that] journey I shall tell [later];
listen, all, attentively, with joyful hearts.[^402-33]

**63.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**64.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the second lahari, called "The Determination of the Annual Festivals."*[^402-34]

[^402-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("দ্বিতীয়-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 2 begins. Raga Shri (*śrī*; Purva, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Purva, laharis 4 and 15 (*tuẏā pada-chāẏā*), and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল উত্তর-বিভাগে বার্ষিক মহোৎসব-নির্ণয়-নাম দ্বিতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা". The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^402-2]: "At whose feet the servant" — *yā̃ra caraṇera bhṛtya*: Rasika is Shyamananda's disciple.

[^402-3]: "At that time" — *henakāle*: after the festival in memory of Damodara (lahari 1, 58–59). Dharenda — lahari 1, note 31. "The excellent Rasikendra" — *rasikendra-bara*. "Established festivals" — *mahotsaba-niṣṭhā kaila*, lit. "established a firm [order] of festivals". "For every year" — *prati sambatsara*.

[^402-4]: "Astrologer brahmanas" — *daibajña brāhmaṇa*: experts in the calendar who determine the lunar days (*tithi*). "His kinsmen" — *ātmagaṇa*. "Festival" — *yātrā*, a festival (often with a procession).

[^402-5]: Shyamananda's aradhana is the festival in memory of his departure: on the first lunar day of the dark half after the full moon of the Snana-yatra (*deba-snāna pūrṇamī*, "the full moon of the Bathing of the Deity") — the day of Shyamananda's departure (Pashchima, lahari 13, 49–50, note 23). "Sometimes in Jyeshtha, sometimes in Ashadha" — depending on the reckoning of the lunar months. "Twelve festivals" — *duẏādaśa mahotsaba*: apparently twelve days of festival (lahari 1, 3, 23, notes 3, 11): counted thus, the festivals of this lahari add up to the "thirty festivals" (18): 12 + 1 (7) + 5 (11) + 1 (12) + 1 (13) + 1 (14) + 1 (15) + 8 (17). "Firmly" — *niścite*.

[^402-6]: Ratha-yatra — the chariot festival of Jagannatha (month of Ashadha). Hera-panchami — the fifth day after the Ratha-yatra, when Lakshmi goes out to see Jagannatha at Gundicha (CC, Madhya 14). The day of Sri Chaitanya's appearance — the full moon of the month of Phalguna (Gaura-purnima). 6–7 can be understood both as one festival for these days and as a festival for each; the count of "thirty" (note 5) implies one. "Cowries" — *kaṛā*, cowrie shells, small change; "handfuls" — *muṭhā*, a handful [of rice]: the humblest alms. "Firmly established" — *kaila niścaẏa*.

[^402-7]: "One person brings hundreds of loads" — *śata śata bhāra drabya āne ekajana*: apparently, by Rasika's mercy abundance comes even from a single giver; it can also be understood as "each one brings". "Astonishes the three worlds" — *camatkāra tribhubana*.

[^402-8]: Gamha-purnima (*gamā pūrṇimī*; the editor explains: *gamā* — Shravana) — the full moon of the month of Shravana (July–August; in Utkala *gamhā pūrṇimā* is the festival of Balarama's appearance). "The thirteenth day of the bright half" — *śukla-trayodaśī*. Subala-chandra — apparently Gauridasa Pandita (lahari 1, 44, note 22). Aradhana — a festival of remembrance (Pashchima, lahari 13, note 8).

[^402-9]: "Five festivals" — *pañca mahotsaba*: apparently five days of festival (note 5). "On that day" — *se dibase*.

[^402-10]: "On the day of the constellation of Krishna's appearance (lit. 'birth')" (12) — *kṛṣṇa-janma-nakṣatra dibase*: apparently Janmashtami — Krishna's appearance under the nakshatra Rohini in the dark half of Bhadra (August–September). The Thakurani (13) is Sri Radha (so also in the summary line of the lahari): Radhashtami, the eighth day of the bright half of Bhadra. "Openly" — *bidite*, "publicly, for all to know."

[^402-11]: Kumara-purnima (*kumāra pūrṇimā*; the editor explains: *kojāgara*) is the Kojagari-purnima, the full moon of the month of Ashvina (September–October). Rasika-chand is Rasika. "By his own inspiration" — *ātma-anubhaba*, lit. "[by] his own experience"; the sense is approximate.

[^402-12]: Utthana-ekadashi is the ekadashi of the bright half of Karttika, when Vishnu awakens from sleep; the full moon following it is the Karttika-purnima, when the Rasa-yatra is celebrated (cf. Pashchima, laharis 1–5: the Great Rasa in Gopiballavpur).

[^402-13]: Dola-purnima (*dola pūrṇamī*) is the full moon of Phalguna (February–March), the swing festival (Dola-yatra). "The twelfth day of the bright half" — *śukla-dbādaśī*. "The festival of Hridayananda" — *hṛdaẏānandera yātrā*: apparently the festival in memory of Hridayananda, Shyamananda's guru (aradhana — Pashchima, lahari 13, note 8). "Eight festivals" (17) — *aṣṭa mahotsaba*: apparently eight days of festival (notes 5, 9); this is how the count of "thirty festivals" (18) works out. "The son of Achyuta" is Rasika.

[^402-14]: "Chose" (18) — *abhīṣṭa karila*, "made [them] desired, chosen." 18b — *niti rasikera sane jībana utsaba*: the sense is approximate; it can also be understood as "[for those who are] with Rasika, life is a daily festival." "Achyuta's boy" (19) — *acyutera bālā*: Rasika.

[^402-15]: "From land to land" (20) — *deśāntara*. "Ten or twenty" (21) — *daśa biśa*. Rasamaya's kin (*rasamaẏa goṣṭhī*) and Thakura Tulasi (Tulasidasa), the singer — Dakshina, lahari 5, note 24; Pashchima, lahari 16, note 25.

[^402-16]: "Singers and musicians" — *saṅgīta-sāhitya* (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 19). "Roam" — *bihare*, "stroll, spend their time."

[^402-17]: Bhattacharya is the title of a learned brahmana (Purva, lahari 8, note 5). "Five or ten" — *daśa pā̃ca*. "At every moment" — *anukṣaṇe*.

[^402-18]: "Palanquin" — *sukapāla*. "Sits" — *bije*. "The abode of all virtues" is Rasika. 25b — *bhāgabata paṛena sadāi harināma*; it can also be understood as "he always reads the Bhagavata [and] the Harinama."

[^402-19]: "Plays" — *khelena*: he wanders, manifesting his pastimes (cf. 19). Rasikendra-raya is Rasika.

[^402-20]: "The crest-jewel [of devotees]" (30) — *cūṛāmaṇi*. "With faces raised" (31) — *ūrddhamukhe*: to see him from afar. "They do not tidy their hair" — *nā sambare keśapāśa*: they forget decorum.

[^402-21]: Pulaka (32) — the hairs standing on end from ecstatic love (Pashchima, lahari 16, note 32). "Conquers the quarters of the world" (34) — *digbijaẏa*: usually a king's victorious campaign or the tour of a scholar who wins debates; here, the wanderings of Rasika, who conquers hearts. "At [his] darshana" — *darśane*.

[^402-22]: "The saints" (35) — *santagaṇa*. "Ten million jewels" (36) — *koṭiratna*. The eight siddhis (37) are the mystic perfections of yoga (anima, laghima and others); the nine treasures (*nabanidhi*) are the treasures of Kubera. 37b — *satata rasika saṅge e saba bihare*: the siddhis and treasures, like servants, always follow Rasika.

[^402-23]: A ser (38) is a measure of weight, about 0.9 kg. "Comes" — *bije*. "Dwelling" — *mandira*. "Feeds" (39) — *sebe*, "serves." "Fried delicacies" — *pakkānna*; panchamrita, the "five nectars," is milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar.

[^402-24]: "The six seasons, the twelve months" (41) — *ṣaṛṛtu bāramāsa*: the whole year round. 42a — *yā̃ra yei māse haẏa tithi ārādhana*: apparently the days of remembrance of saints and the other festivals listed above (4–17). "Aradhana" is a festival of remembrance (note 8). "Home" — *bāṛīte*: apparently to Dharenda (2), where the festivals were established.

[^402-25]: The adhivasa is the preliminary rite on the eve of a festival (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 19). "Arrives" — *haẏena prabeśa*, "enters."

[^402-26]: "The festival-aradhana of Shyamananda" (44) — *śyāmānanda-mahotsaba ārādhana*: the annual festival in memory of Shyamananda (4–5). Govindapur is Sri Govindapur, the site of the first festival of separation (lahari 1, 23, note 11). "Two [festivals] of twelve [days]" (45) — *dui duẏādaśa*: apparently this was already the second twelve-day festival in memory of Shyamananda in Govindapur. The number 45 is missing in the edition: the couplet is printed without a number, and the next is ॥ ৪৬ ॥; the numbering is restored by count. "Sat in assembly" — *basilā samāje*. The Shyamanandis are Shyamananda's disciples (Pashchima, lahari 15); mahajanas — Pashchima, lahari 16, note 4.

[^402-27]: "Has been made unalterable for me" (47) — *more karila niścala*. "Your three mothers" (48) — *tina mātā tomāra*: the three Thakuranis (54) — apparently Shyamananda's wives, who for his disciples are mothers: Shyamapriya (53, 57), Yamuna (54) and one more, not named here (Gaurangadasi? — Pashchima, lahari 12, 11, note 11; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 8). "You shall settle" — *rākhibe*. 48b — *sbatantra rahile nā karibe ādare*: the sense is approximate; it can also be understood as "if [you] live apart, [they] will not show [you] affection." 48–51 are Shyamananda's words as reported by Rasika; the quotation marks follow the sense.

[^402-28]: Vrindavanachandra is Shyamananda's Deity (Pashchima, lahari 11, note 9). Vrajamohana Thakura (*brajamohana ṭhākura*) is apparently another Deity of Krishna (*ṭhākura* — "Deity"); not identified; it can also be understood as one Deity, "Vrindavanachandra Vrajamohana." "You shall ceremonially bring" — *bijaẏa karābe*: of a Deity's procession. Sri Shyamasundarpur is the village given to Shyamananda (Pashchima, lahari 12, 7, note 8); in lahari 3, 3 — "Sri Shyamanandapur."

[^402-29]: "In the depth of my heart" (50) — *marame*: apparently an inner command; it can also be understood as "insistently." "Serve the saints" (51) — *santasebā*. "In person" — *sākṣāte*, "face to face": during Shyamananda's lifetime. 51a is taken as Shyamananda's direct speech; the sense: living in three places, they could not feed the saints.

[^402-30]: The Thakurani (52, 56) is apparently Shyamapriya (cf. 57). "Will go" (53) — *bijaẏa karibe* (note 28). Shyamapriya is Shyamananda's wife (Pashchima, lahari 11, 26–29). Yamuna Thakurani — Dakshina, lahari 16, 37, note 22. "Thakurani" is a respectful title of the wife of a Vaishnava teacher.

[^402-31]: "Conveyed the whole matter in Rasika's words" (56) — *kahila sakala tattba rasika-bacane*. "Mother Shyamapriya" (57) — *śyāmapriyā mātā*. "Fitting" — *ucitā*. "The shining moon of the lineage" (58) — *kuladīpta-candra*. "All authority Shyamananda gave [him]" — *sarbba adhikāra dila*: Shyamananda handed over to Rasika the leadership of the community (Pashchima, lahari 13, note 21).

[^402-32]: "He is father, he is son" — *pitā sei putra sei*: for her Rasika is both a support, like a father, and a son (as her husband's disciple). "Takes" — *la'be*, "will take [with him]."

[^402-33]: "In that village" (61) — in Govindapur (44). "Having taken leave" — *bidāi kari*, "having sent off." "Of [that] journey" (62) — *gamanera bibaraṇa*: of the moving of the Thakuranis and the Deities (laharis 3–4).

[^402-34]: The author's signature (64) and the colophon are; the title matches the heading (note 1). Below come a rule and the heading of lahari 3.


## Lahari 3. The Description of the Crushing of the Pride of Uddanda the Bhuiyan and of the People of Hijli

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika stays in the village and at his pleasure composes thirteen padas on prema for Krishna; he announces to Uddanda the bhuiyan Shyamananda's order to settle the three mothers together in Sri Shyamanandapur, but the bhuiyan in his pride will not give up Vrindavanachandra; the angered Rasika vows not to drink water in his land, foretells that Uddanda will be no more on earth, and leaves home alone, but Shyamananda's voice stops him: "I have struck him down; take Vrindavanachandra and unite [everyone]"; in the guise of a Vrajavasi Rasika lives unrecognised in Mayna, initiates the brothers Chandrabhanu and Shyamarasika and others, and astonishes the learned, until Vamshidasa reveals to all who he is; in Hijli the scholars led by Mimamsa-mandana cannot answer him and revile Shyamananda; by a letter Rasika vows not to drink water in Hijli and foretells that they will all leave the body and, born again, receive the Harinama from him; the mimamsaka who ordered the letter tied to a dog's neck perishes, torn by a dog, and within half a year the others perish too; born again, they receive the Harinama from Rasika, and all Hijli turns to Krishna*

*The third lahari.*

*Raga Kamoda — panchali metre.*[^403-1]

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, revered in all the worlds,
the life of the world, the enchanter of hearts!
Dear to those who have nothing, the treasure of Rasika's life,
the abode of compassion, descended [into the world]![^403-2]

**2.** Thus for some days in that village
Rasikendra stayed, at his pleasure.
There thirteen padas — songs of the virtues of prema for Krishna —
Rasika composed in play.[^403-3]

**3.** Thus after some days to Uddanda the bhuiyan
he spoke of the reason for [his] departure:
"On my head is an order: the three mothers — together,
in the place Sri Shyamanandapur."[^403-4]

**4.** Hearing, the bhuiyan grew angry, disregarded Prabhu's order
[and] uttered proud words with his mouth:
"Is there anyone so able [as to] take Vrindavanachandra
while I am on the earth?"[^403-5]

**5.** Hearing the bhuiyan's words, Rasikendra-mani in anger
rose, remembering Krishna:
"I will not drink water here — as far as this land extends," —
[and] Prabhu left, overcome by anger.[^403-6]

**6.** "If Shyamananda-raya truly gave me the order,
Vrindavanachandra will come [to me].
If there is mercy upon me, the Lord will not remain there,
[and] Uddanda will not remain on the earth."[^403-7]

**7.** Having declared [this], Prabhu left; great grief arose [in him]:
"No longer will I stay in this land:
this pashanda has broken Shyamananda's order!" —
[and] in his strong emotion he went far away.[^403-8]

**8.** Leaving all his household, he went out alone,
[keeping] in his heart Shyamananda's lotus feet.
Prabhu had gone some distance [when] suddenly a voice arose:
Shyamananda began to speak.[^403-9]

**9.** "Over what trifle have you become so stirred?
I have destroyed him.
Taking Vrindavanachandra, go [and] unite [everyone] together;
go no further, my child, no further."[^403-10]

**10.** Hearing the order with his ears, Prabhu went no further;
turning back, he stopped at Mayna.
Prabhu went about alone, in the guise of a Vrajavasi —
no one could recognise [him].[^403-11]

**11.** Beginning with Chandrabhanu, [many] became disciples of Sri Murari;
he gave initiation to Shyamarasika.
Seeing the two brothers, Prabhu became very happy
[and] poured forth talks of Krishna.[^403-12]

**12.** Hearing the words from his holy mouth, [even] Brihaspati falls silent;
all are amazed.
The host of scholars says: "Is this not Narayana?
Who has the power to challenge him?"[^403-13]

**13.** Thus night and day, in search of talks of Krishna, —
no one in that village recognised [him].
After some days Vamshidasa came [and] met [him]
[and] bowed down to Rasika.

**14.** He tells everyone: "The one [living] here alone is Prabhu,
Rasika-shekhara-chudamani."
Hearing, all in joy, with heads bowed from shame [and] fear,
fell to the ground at [his] feet.[^403-14]

**15.** From there Prabhu went, taking Vamshidasa with him,
[and] arrived at the town of Hijli.
Sadashiva, Uddhava and others, Mimamsa-mandana and others
brought that Shyamasundara there.[^403-15]

**16.** Rasikananda held talks of Krishna with all,
expounded the six shastras.
All the scholars, as many as there were, were astonished:
they could not challenge [him].[^403-16]

**17.** Unable [to do so], the brahmanas reviled Shyamananda.
Hearing [this], Prabhu quickly rose:
"In all the villages of Hijli I will not drink water," —
[and] he wrote a letter to all:

**18.** "All will leave this body [and], coming again, will be born;
taking [them] on my lap, [I] will give [them] the Harinama."
A servant brought [and] delivered the letter; [it] was read out in the midst of the assembly.
Hearing [it], the ignorant mimamsaka says:[^403-17]

**19.** "Tie the letter to a dog's neck — that is my opinion."
Hearing [this], all stopped their ears.
The mimamsaka rose [and] went; suddenly a dog met [him]
[and] fiercely began to tear at his eyes [and] face.[^403-18]

**20.** Howling like a dog, the "lion among brahmanas" took to his heels
[and] right there gave up his life.
Sadashiva, Uddhava and others, that Shyamasundara and others —
within six months all perished.[^403-19]

**21.** Having clashed with Rasika, no one finds protection:
fathomless, boundless is that glory.
[His] vow is to crush the asuras; to fallen people he shows mercy;
in the three worlds he has no equal.[^403-20]

**22.** Seeing [this], all are amazed [and] say: "A partial avatara!"
As he had ordained in play, [so it came to pass]:
all were born again, [and] then he gave [them] the Harinama,
held talks of Krishna with all.[^403-21]

**23.** All the people of Hijli turned to Krishna,
seeing the manifestation [of the power] of Rasika.
All had devotion in love; all turned their minds to Krishna:
the firm hope of all was fulfilled.[^403-22]

**24.** Such is Prabhu Rasikendra, the unyielding Nagara-chandra:
to all living beings he gives prema.
He is the life [and] soul dear to those who have nothing, the deliverance from the terrible [age of] Kali:
not even with a hundred mouths can [he] be described.[^403-23]

**25.** Listen to the "Rasika-mangala," devotees of Krishna of the three worlds —
the word of Rasika's good fame.
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^403-24]

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the third lahari, called "The Description of the Crushing of the Pride of Uddanda the Bhuiyan and of the People of Hijli."*

[^403-1]: The lines before the raga are the heading of the lahari ("তৃতীয়-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Kamoda — apparently its first occurrence in the poem. "Panchali metre" (*chanda pā̃cālī*) is the tripadi; a stanza is set in four lines in the edition and is translated likewise (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল উত্তর-বিভাগে উদ্দণ্ড ভূঞা ও হিজলী-বাসীর দর্প-চূর্ণ-বর্ণননাম তৃতীয়-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*uddaṇḍa bhū̃ñā o hijalī-bāsīra darpa-cūrṇa-barṇana*). Lahari 3 comprises stanzas 1–25; the summary line covers the whole lahari. Stanza 5 begins and ends at the top of.

[^403-2]: "Revered in all the worlds" — *akhila bhubanabandya*. "Dear to those who have nothing" — *priẏajana akiñcana*; it can also be understood as "whose dear ones are those who have nothing." "Descended [into the world]" — *abatari*: the author speaks of Shyamananda as one who descended from above; on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^403-3]: "In that village" — apparently in Govindapur (lahari 2, 44, 61). "At his pleasure" — *āpanāra sukhe*. "Thirteen padas" — *trayodaśa pada*: songs by Rasika; not identified. "Songs of the virtues of prema for Krishna" — *kṛṣṇaprema-guṇa-gāthā*. "In play" — *kautuke*.

[^403-4]: Uddanda the bhuiyan (*uddaṇḍa bhū̃ñā*) is apparently Uddanda-raya, the bhuiyan of Nrisimhapur, a disciple of Shyamananda (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 24; Pashchima, lahari 13, note 15). "The reason for [his] departure" — *gamana-kāraṇe*. "On my head is an order" — *ājñā āche mora māthe*: "I carry an order" (lahari 2, 47–54). "The three mothers" — the three Thakuranis, apparently Shyamananda's wives (lahari 2, note 27). Sri Shyamanandapur is apparently the same as Sri Shyamasundarpur.

[^403-5]: "Disregarded Prabhu's order" — *prabhu ājñā helā kailā*: Prabhu here is Shyamananda. "Proud words" — *sagarbba bāṇī*. From 4 it appears that Vrindavanachandra was with Uddanda; where and since when is not said. "While I am on the earth" — *pṛthibīte mui se thākite*.

[^403-6]: Rasikendra-mani is Rasika. "Remembering" — *saṅariẏā* (= *smariẏā*). "I will not drink water here" — *nā khāiba ethā jala*: refusing to drink water in someone's domain means breaking off all dealings (cf. 17). "As far as this land extends" — *yatadūra ihā sthala*. "Overcome by anger" — *krodhābeśa haiẏā*.

[^403-7]: 6 is Rasika's speech. Shyamananda-raya is Shyamananda. "Will come [to me]" — *āsibena*: the Deity Himself will come to Rasika. "The Lord will not remain there" — *prabhu tathā nā rahibe*: apparently of Vrindavanachandra (the Deity will not remain with Uddanda); it can also be understood of Shyamananda. "Uddanda will not remain on the earth" is a prediction of his end.

[^403-8]: "Having declared" — *ājñā kari*, lit. "having commanded." Pashanda (*pāṣaṇḍa*) — an unbeliever, a blasphemer. "In his strong emotion" — *anurāge*; cf. *anurāgī* (9): *anurāga* usually means loving attachment; here it is apparently strong feeling — grief and resolve to leave the land. "Went far away" — *calilā biśeṣe*; the sense is approximate.

[^403-9]: "All his household" — *saba paribāra*; it can also be understood as "all his family, all his retinue." "Went out" — *hailā bāhāra*. By this time Shyamananda had already left this world (Pashchima, lahari 13); the voice that suddenly arose is his (cf. Dakshina, lahari 16, note 28: Shyamananda appears at night to Uddanda). In the Vaishnava understanding, the Lord's associates continue to guide their disciples even after their disappearance; on the author's attitude to Shyamananda — Purva, lahari 1, note 2.

[^403-10]: "Over what trifle" — *kona chāra kathā lāgi*. "So stirred" — *anurāgī* (note 8). "I have destroyed him" — *tā're mui karinu saṃhāra*: of Uddanda. "Unite [everyone] together" — *ekatra karaha*: the Deities and the three Thakuranis in one place (lahari 2, 48–54). "My child" — *bāpu*, an affectionate address.

[^403-11]: "Turning back" — *phiriẏā*. Mayna is apparently Moyna in Medinipur, north of Hijli. "Stopped" — *uttarilā*. "Alone" — *ekeśbara*. "In the guise of a Vrajavasi" — *brajabāsī beśa*: as a wanderer from Vraja.

[^403-12]: Chandrabhanu (*candrabhānu*) and Shyamarasika (*śyāmarasika*) are apparently "the two brothers" (11b); persons not identified; cf. "the renunciate Shyamarasika" among the disciples (Pashchima, lahari 14, 128) — whether he is the same is unclear. Sri Murari is Rasika (Rasika-Murari). 11a — *candrabhānu ādi kari, śiṣya hailā śrīmurāri*: it can also be understood as "…became disciples; Sri Murari gave initiation…". "Poured forth" — *udgāre*, lit. "pouring out."

[^403-13]: Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, the model of learning and eloquence. "Falls silent" — *tūṇī* (the editor explains: *tuṣṇī*, "silent"). "Is this not Narayana?" — the scholars' rapturous words (cf. 22). "Challenge" — *samasyā karite*: *samasyā* is a hard question, a problem posed in a learned dispute (cf. 16).

[^403-14]: "In search of talks of Krishna" (13) — *kṛṣṇakathā anbeṣaṇe* (lahari 2, 24). Vamshidasa is the author's uncle, Rasamaya's brother (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 17). "Bowed down" — *karaẏe paraṇāme*. "The one [living] here alone" (14) — *ekeśbara prabhu ethā*; it can also be understood as "Prabhu is here alone [without companions]." Rasika-shekhara-chudamani, "the crest-jewel of Rasika-shekharas," is Rasika. "With heads bowed" — *hẽṭamāthe*: from shame at not having recognised him.

[^403-15]: Hijli is a coastal region and town in south-eastern Medinipur (Purva, lahari 10, note 21). Sadashiva — cf. Sadashiva, brother of Balabhadra, the ruler of Hijli (ibid.); whether he is the same is not said. Uddhava is not identified here. Mimamsa-mandana (*mīmāṃsā maṇḍana*, "ornament of Mimamsa") is apparently a Mimamsa scholar (in 18–19 — *mīmāṃsā*); cf. Purva, lahari 8, note 5, where Rasika's teacher is so called. 15b — *tathā lailā se śyāmasundare*: the sense is approximate; Shyamasundara is apparently a scholar of Hijli (20), brought to dispute with Rasika; it can also be understood as "[Rasika] took Shyamasundara there with him."

[^403-16]: "Expounded the six shastras" — *ṣaṭśāstra prakāśa karilā*: the six philosophical systems (Purva, lahari 9, note 12). "Were astonished" — *camakita*. "Could not challenge" — *samasyā dibāre nā pārilā* (note 13).

[^403-17]: "Reviled Shyamananda" (17) — *nindā kaila śyāmānande*: according to Vaishnava teaching, blasphemy of a Vaishnava, and all the more of the guru, is the gravest offence (vaishnava-aparadha; CC, Madhya 19). "A letter" — *ekapatra*, "one letter." 18a is the text of the letter: Rasika foretells that they will leave the body and that in their next birth he will accept them as his children and give them the Harinama (fulfilled — 22). "Read out" — *prakāśila*. "The ignorant mimamsaka" — *mīmāṃsā-ajñāna*: Mimamsa-mandana (note 15).

[^403-18]: "Tie the letter to a dog's neck" — *śbāna gale bāndha patra*: a sign of utter contempt. "Stopped their ears" — *hāta dila karṇe*: so as not to hear the offence. "Met" — *melā*. 19b — *dṛṛhe tā'ra ā̃khi mukha jhune*: the sense of *jhune* is unclear; taken as "tear, maul."

[^403-19]: 20a — *kukura raba rā kāṛi, diẏe dbija siṃha raṛī*: "howling like a dog" (*rā kāṛā*, "to give voice"); "took to his heels" — *raṛī diẏe* (*raṛa deoẏā*, "to break into a run"); "lion among brahmanas" (*dbija siṃha*) is ironic. "Gave up his life" — *chāṛila parāṇe*. "Perished" — *binaśane*. The author presents the fulfilment of 18 ("will leave this body") as retribution for the blasphemy of Shyamananda (17).

[^403-20]: "Having clashed with Rasika" — *ṭheki rasikera ṭhāñe*. "[His] vow is to crush the asuras" — *asura-dalana-bānā*: *bānā* — a vow, a banner, a distinguishing mark; the sense is approximate. "Shows mercy" — *kara karuṇā*.

[^403-21]: "A partial avatara" — *aṃśa-abatāra*: the people's rapturous words; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, and not an avatara (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 28; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "As he had ordained in play" — *yei ājñā karilena raṅge*: what was said in the letter (18) came to pass. Rasika's punishment of the offenders and his subsequent mercy to them accord with the Vaishnava understanding that even a Vaishnava's chastisement purifies and leads to bhakti. Stanza 22 is the last; the continuation of the lahari (23–25) and the colophon are.

[^403-22]: Continuation of lahari 3; begins with the complete stanza ॥ 23 ॥. "Turned to Krishna" — *haila kṛṣṇa parāẏaṇa*. "Manifestation" — *parakāśa*: the power of Rasika made manifest (18–22). "Devotion in love" — *premabhakti*. 23c — *sabākāra premabhakti, kṛṣṇe dilā sabe mati*: it can also be understood as "[Rasika] gave all devotion in love, turned the minds of all to Krishna."

[^403-23]: "The unyielding Nagara-chandra" — *haṭhiẏā nāgaracandra*: *haṭhiẏā* — "stubborn, unyielding"; *nāgara-candra* — "the moon among nagaras" (*nāgara* — the refined, skilful lover, an epithet of Krishna), here of Rasika (cf. lahari 4, 25). "Dear to those who have nothing" — *akiñcanapriẏa-prāṇa* (cf. 1, note 2). "The deliverance from the terrible [age of] Kali" — *kalighora-paritrāṇa*. "Cannot be described" — *nā yāẏa bākhāna*.

[^403-24]: "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-jana* (Purva, lahari 10, note 13; Purva, lahari 11, note 15): in the 1941 edition the repha is printed to the right of the conjunct. "The word of good fame" — *suyaśaḥ-bacana*. The author's signature (the second half of the stanza) is given in the standard formula; in the tripadi metre it runs: "Making the holy feet of Shyamananda the ornament on his head, the son of Rasamaya sings" (Purva, lahari 11, note 15). The colophon is; the title is as in the heading of the lahari (note 1). Lahari 3 — stanzas 1–25, complete.


## Lahari 4. The Description of the Conspiracy against Rasikananda Prabhu Owing to Gaurangadasi's Unwillingness that the Three Thakuranis Live Together

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika comes to Gopivallabhapur and hears that Uddanda, for his offence, has perished with all his line, while the people glorify Rasika; he ceremonially brings Shyamapriya Thakurani and Vrindavanachandra to Shyamasundarpur, settles the three Thakuranis there together and celebrates the third twelve-day festival, to which kings, subjects, mahantas, Vrajavasis, Gaudiyas and the whole Shyamanandi community gather; but the Thakuranis do not get along, they quarrel and abuse Rasika, and he only laughs; Shyamapriya asks him to build three houses, but Rasika holds firmly to the guru's order; the angered elder Thakurani, Gaurangadasi, secretly conspires with Vidyutmala, Harikara and others: they write a forged letter in Rasika's name to Shyamapriya about poisoning Gaurangadasi, and she keeps it at her breast until the day of the dadhi-kada; some of the conspirators want to take Rasika's life on the spot, others to drive him away; during the dadhi-sankirtana Gaurangadasi demands judgement before the whole assembly and bids Padmanabha and Gopidasa read the letter; the author glorifies Rasika, by whose word poison becomes nectar*

*The fourth lahari.*

*Raga Kaushika.*[^404-1]
*Ghosha: "Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!*
*O Murari, O Murari, O Murari!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of all!
Be merciful, that I may compose [a song of your] glory.[^404-2]

**2.** From there Rasikendra set out
[and] arrived at Sri Gopivallabhapur.[^404-3]

**3.** There he heard that Uddanda had lost his life:
he had perished together with all his line.[^404-4]

**4.** Where did the wealth, the people, all the family go?
Because of the offence everything went to ruin.

**5.** Seeing the manifestation [of the power] of Rasika, all the people —
all the kings [and] subjects — were amazed.

**6.** All say: "Rasikendra is a second Narayana:
at his touch the wicked were pacified.[^404-5]

**7.** His word is heeded by Huns, Pulindas and the like,
his word is heeded by mlecchas, Pukkashas and the like;[^404-6]

**8.** his word is carried out by wicked kings,
his command is not transgressed by devas and asuras.

**9.** Krishna gave him (Uddanda) the punishment he deserved" —
all speak to one another of Rasika's glory.

**10.** Having crushed [his] pride, Rasikendra ceremonially brought
Shyamapriya Thakurani [and] Vrindavanachandra —

**11.** to Sri Shyamasundarpur he ceremonially brought [them];
the three Thakuranis he settled there together.[^404-7]

**12.** There he celebrated the third festival of twelve [days];
from all four directions he had an incredible [abundance of] provisions brought.[^404-8]

**13.** A great many kings [and] subjects came there;
all the mahantas, as many as [there were], came.

**14.** Vrajavasis, Gaudiyas — all the saints, as many as [there were] —
came; all the Shyamanandi kinsfolk came.[^404-9]

**15.** No one can transgress Rasikendra's command:
all came to see the festival.

**16.** Many kirtaniyas came there:
in the midst of the forest the world of Vaikuntha arose.[^404-10]

**17.** Whatever Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, has in mind —
the impossible at once comes to pass.

**18.** The lila that Prabhu performs by his own will
neither Brahma, nor Shiva, nor King Indra can break.[^404-11]

**19.** Thus he celebrated two [festivals] of twelve [days] there;
[but] among the three Thakuranis there was no harmony at all.[^404-12]

**20.** Constantly they quarrel without cause;
all three abuse the son of Achyuta.

**21.** Prabhu says nothing to anyone — hearing, he laughs;
yet they quarrel all the same, day and night.[^404-13]

**22.** Shyamapriya Thakurani is most composed;
she knows all truths [and] is exceedingly calm.[^404-14]

**23.** Having reflected, she speaks gently to Rasika:
"Quickly set up three houses in this village.

**24.** Together [we] cannot pass our days — I tell you for certain;
I do not know what more [will come] through you."[^404-15]

**25.** The unyielding Nagara, Prabhu would not even listen:
"We shall live together — the guru's order [is] the warrant.[^404-16]

**26.** Whoever, breaking the order by a single step, goes away,
to that person the Shyamanandis will not go."[^404-17]

**27.** These words Prabhu spoke firmly and resolutely;
the elder Thakurani, hearing [them], grew angry in her heart.[^404-18]

**28.** At the time of the third festival of twelve [days],
taking two or four [people], she confers in secret:[^404-19]

**29.** Vidyutmala, Nava-Gauranga, Balarama,
Sri Keshavananda, Harikara, Vishnurama,

**30.** Kalandi, Radhajivana — all the wicked ones,
[and] disciples' disciples, servant-disciples — all who were with them.[^404-20]

**31.** The elder Thakurani, deliberating with all, [says]:
"I will not let Rasika come here.

**32.** Let Shyamapriya [and] Yamuna go to their own places;
devise a plan so that I alone may remain in this place."[^404-21]

**33.** Hearing [this], Harikara says: "There is a better plan:
write a letter in Rasika's name,

**34.** as though he had written to mother Shyamapriya
that he will make Gaurangadasi drink poison

**35.** [and] will try by all sorts of means to kill her —
write all such words all over the letter.[^404-22]

**36.** At the festival, at the sankirtana, on the day of the dadhi-kada,
we will hold an assembly [and] seat all the saints:[^404-23]

**37.** kings, subjects, mahajanas, mahantas,
the Shyamanandi community, and sannyasis [and] brahmanas as well.

**38.** This letter we will bring [and] present in the midst of the assembly:
all, hearing [it], will revile Rasika.

**39.** On this pretext we will not let him come here again."
On the four edges of the sheet they wrote all this.

**40.** Wrapping the letter in silk cloth, they tied it carefully;
the elder Thakurani hid [it] in the garment she wore.[^404-24]

**41.** Keeping the letter with her as dearer than life,
day and night she carries it at her breast.

**42.** Here, meanwhile, Rasikendra-raya, intoxicated with the festival,
knows nothing but service to the guru, to Krishna [and] to the sadhus.

**43.** And here all the wicked ones confer in secret
how to bring Rasika-shekhara to disgrace.[^404-25]

**44.** Someone says: "When everyone hears the letter,
in an instant we will take Rasika's life on the spot."

**45.** Someone says: "Then and there we will strike with a yamadhara."
Someone says: "[So long as] he no longer stays here."[^404-26]

**46.** Thus all the wicked ones confer;
Rasika's people know nothing of all this.

**47.** All were joyfully performing the dadhi-sankirtana;
at that time the elder mother, before everyone,

**48.** summoning all with words not to be refused, [says]:
"Let all the people judge without guile.[^404-27]

**49.** I make one request of everyone:
all of you, listen with a firm mind to a letter.

**50.** Having heard the letter, by a proper judgement of righteousness
impose a fitting punishment — I say to all.[^404-28]

**51.** See: here are [all] the devotees of Utkala;
let all the people, without stirring, listen to the letter.

**52.** All of you continually lay the burden of blame on me:
'You have ruined Shyamananda's house.'

**53.** [So] hear, all of you, what my faults and merits are:
he writes to Shyamapriya [that she should] kill me.[^404-29]

**54.** From the day I received this letter
I have kept it carefully day and night myself.

**55.** I have no one I trust enough to put [it] in [their] hands:
Padmanabha [and] Gopidasa, read [it] before everyone."[^404-30]

**56.** Rasika's lila amazes the three worlds:
by his word poison becomes nectar.

**57.** Remembrance of him frees one from the bonds of worldly existence —
[and] such ignorant people would disgrace him![^404-31]

**58.** Listen, everyone — I shall tell what happened next:
the "Rasika-mangala" is supremely deep.

**59.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^404-32]

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourth lahari, called "The Description of the Conspiracy against Rasikananda Prabhu Owing to Gaurangadasi's Unwillingness that the Three Thakuranis Live Together."*

[^404-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("চতুর্থ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 4 begins. Raga Kaushika; the ghosha is the same as in Purva, lahari 3 (there without the word "ghosha"), and its translation is repeated: Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari is a name of Krishna, which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "তিন ঠাকুরাণীকে একত্র স্থাপনে গৌরাঙ্গ-দাসীর অনিচ্ছাহেতু রসিকানন্দ প্রভুর বিরুদ্ধে ষড়যন্ত্র-বর্ণন" (*tina ṭhākurāṇīke ekatra sthāpane gaurāṅga-dāsīra anicchāhetu rasikānanda prabhura biruddhe ṣaṛayantra-barṇana*), literally "The Description of the Conspiracy against Rasikananda Prabhu by Reason of Gaurangadasi's Unwillingness [to Allow] the Three Thakuranis to Be Settled Together."

[^404-2]: "The purifier of all" — *akhila-pābana*. 1b — *kṛpā kara yaśaḥ yena kariẏe racana*, literally "be merciful, that I may compose the glory."

[^404-3]: "From there" — from Hijli (lahari 3). "Arrived" — *upasana* (Uttara, lahari 1, 58, note 31): apparently *upasanna*, "arrived."

[^404-4]: Uddanda — Uddanda the bhuiyan, who refused to give up Vrindavanachandra (lahari 3, 3–6; cf. Uddanda-raya — Dakshina, lahari 16). In lahari 3 (6) Rasika said that if Shyamananda had truly given him the order, Uddanda would not remain on earth. "With all his line" — *sabaṃśa sahita*. "Offence" (4) — *aparādha*.

[^404-5]: "A second Narayana" — *dbitī nārāẏaṇa*: the enthusiastic words of the people (cf. Pashchima, lahari 3, 61). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation of the Lord (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 37); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. Verses 17–18 are to be understood likewise. "The wicked" — *duṣṭagaṇa*.

[^404-6]: Huns, Pulindas, Pukkashas (*pukaśa*), mlecchas — "low" and foreign peoples; cf. the Bhagavata (2.4.18): the Kiratas, Huns, Andhras, Pulindas, Pukkashas and others are purified by taking refuge in the Lord's devotees. "Heed his word" — *bacana śune*, literally "hear his word": obey.

[^404-7]: "Having crushed pride" — *garba dhbaṃsi*: the pride of Uddanda. "Ceremonially brought" — *bije karāila*: the ceremonial transfer of a Deity (Uttara, lahari 2, 49, note 28). Shyamapriya Thakurani is Shyamananda's wife (Dakshina, lahari 11, 26–29); Vrindavanachandra is a Deity of Shyamananda (Pashchima, lahari 11, note 9). Shyamasundarpur — Pashchima, lahari 12, note 8. The three Thakuranis are Shyamapriya, Yamuna and Gaurangadasi (34; Uttara, lahari 2, 48, 53–54, notes 27, 30; Pashchima, lahari 12, 11, note 11): so Shyamananda had ordered (Uttara, lahari 2, 47–54).

[^404-8]: "The third festival of twelve [days]" — *tṛtīẏa dbādaśa mahotsaba*: apparently the third annual twelve-day aradhana of Shyamananda (Uttara, lahari 1, note 11; lahari 2, note 5); cf. 19 and 28. "Incredible [abundance]" — *asambhaba*.

[^404-9]: Vrajavasis — the residents of Vraja; Gaudiyas — Vaishnavas from Gauda (Bengal). "The Shyamanandi kinsfolk" — *śyāmānandī saba ātmagaṇa*: the whole community of Shyamananda.

[^404-10]: Kirtaniyas (*kīrtanīẏā*) — kirtana singers (Uttara, lahari 1, note 10). "The world of Vaikuntha" — *baikuṇṭha-bhubana*.

[^404-11]: "The impossible comes to pass" (17) — *aghaṭana-ghaṭana*. "The son of Achyuta" — Rasika (Purva, lahari 3, note 5). "King Indra" — *indra-rāẏa*. On 17–18 see note 5.

[^404-12]: "Two [festivals] of twelve [days]" — *dui duẏādaśa*: apparently two annual festivals in memory of Shyamananda held at Shyamasundarpur; how this fits with the "third" festival (12, 28) is unclear. "There was no harmony at all" — *prīti nā haila sarbathā*, literally "there was no love whatever."

[^404-13]: "Quarrel" — *kandala kare*. "All three" (20) — *tina jane*.

[^404-14]: "Most composed" — *baṛa gabhīratā*, literally "great depth." "Knows all truths" — *sarba tattbajñāta*. "Exceedingly calm" — *atība dhīratā*.

[^404-15]: "Gently" — *sudhāmaẏa*, "[with words] full of nectar." "Houses" — *bāṛī*, homesteads. 24b — *nā jānihe tomā diẏā āra kibā haẏa*: the sense is unclear; understood as Shyamapriya's fear that harm will come of Rasika's insistence; it can also be understood as "I do not know what else can be done through you."

[^404-16]: "The unyielding Nagara" — *haṭhiẏā nāgara*: *haṭhiẏā* — "stubborn, unyielding," *nāgara* — "the refined, skilful [lover]," an epithet of Krishna; here of Rasika (cf. lahari 3, 24: *haṭhiẏā nāgaracandra*). "The guru's order" — Shyamananda's order (Uttara, lahari 2, 47–54). "Warrant" — *paramāṇe* (= *pramāṇe*).

[^404-17]: "By a single step" — *eka bhoṛā*: the editor explains in a footnote: *bhoṛā* — "step" (*pada*). The sense: whoever deviates even slightly from the order and leaves will be shunned by the Shyamanandi community.

[^404-18]: "Firmly and resolutely" — *dṛṛha bhālamate*. "The elder Thakurani" — *baṛa ṭhākurāṇī*, literally "the great Thakurani": according to the colophons of laharis 4 and 5, Gaurangadasi (cf. 34); further on she is also "the elder mother" (*baṛa mātā*, 47).

[^404-19]: "Two or four" — *dui cāri*: a few. "In secret" — *nigame* (cf. 43: *gupte*).

[^404-20]: Vidyutmala Thakurani — Pashchima, lahari 2, note 6 (there she comes to the Rasa-yatra). "Nava-Gauranga" — *naba gouraṅga*: it can also be understood as two names — "Nava, Gauranga." Keshavananda, Harikara, Vishnurama, Kalandi, Radhajivana, Balarama — not identified. "Disciples' disciples, servant-disciples" — *anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya*.

[^404-21]: "To their own places" — *yathāsthāne*. Yamuna Thakurani — Dakshina, lahari 16, 37, note 22.

[^404-22]: "Letter" — *lipi* (33), *likhā*, *patra* (39). "In Rasika's name" — *rasikera nāme*. "To mother Shyamapriya" — *mātā śyāmapriẏā sthāne*. "Her" (35) — *ihāre*: Gaurangadasi. "All over the letter" — *likhā cāribhite*, literally "on the four sides of the letter"; cf. 39: *patra cāri dhāre*.

[^404-23]: Dadhi-kada (*dadhikādā*) — the festive drenching with curd at the close of a festival (Uttara, lahari 1, 5, note 4); cf. 47: "dadhi-sankirtana." "We will hold an assembly" — *sabhā kari*.

[^404-24]: "Silk cloth" — *paṭabastra*. "In the garment she wore" — *pindhilā basane*.

[^404-25]: "Bring to disgrace" — *biṛambana* (also in 57): "to put to shame, expose to disgrace."

[^404-26]: "In an instant" (44) — *eka tile*. "On the spot" — *ṭhāẏa*. Yamadhara (*yamadhara*) — the editor explains in a footnote: "a kind of weapon"; apparently the *jamadhar*, the katar dagger.

[^404-27]: "The elder mother" — *baṛa mātā*: Gaurangadasi (note 18). "With words not to be refused" — *alaṅghya bacane*: imperiously, so that none could fail to come. 48b — *niṣkapaṭe bicāra karaẏe sarbajane*: understood as the beginning of her speech.

[^404-28]: "By a proper judgement of righteousness" — *yathocita sadharma bicāre*. "Impose" — *karibe*.

[^404-29]: "What my faults and merits are" — *āmāra ye doṣaguṇa*: "[here is] what my faults are." "He" — Rasika, in whose name the forged letter was written (33–35).

[^404-30]: "I have no one I trust" — *pratyaẏa nāhika mora*. Padmanabha [and] Gopidasa — *padmanābha gopīdāsa*: it can also be understood as one person, "Padmanabha Gopidasa" (in lahari 5, 14, 18 the verb with them is in the honorific form, which does not distinguish number); not identified (cf. the brahmana Padmanabha among Shyamananda's disciples — Purva, lahari 1, 79).

[^404-31]: "Poison becomes nectar" (56) — *garala amṛta haẏa*: a hint at the outcome (lahari 5). "The bonds of worldly existence" — *bhababandha*. "Ignorant people" — *ajñagaṇa*.

[^404-32]: "Supremely deep" (58) — *ati parama gahana*. The author's signature (59) and the colophon are; the title is as in the heading (note 1).


## Lahari 5. The Description of the Failure of Gaurangadasi's Conspiracy through the Power of the Glory of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; at the dadhi-kada Rasika, grey with the dust of the rasa and spattered with drops of curd, sits among his own with Krishna and Shyamananda in his heart, and the five sons of Rasamaya, as though sensing the plot, sit down around him, resolved to strike down the wicked and give their lives for Rasika; Padmanabha and Gopidasa read the letter, whose edge the elder mother holds — and in it appear verses of the Bhagavata from all twelve cantos, the siddhanta of the six shastras, the meaning of the Vedas, songs of Jayadeva and at the end three shlokas in glory of Rasika, threatening his revilers with hell; the conspirators, whispering, run off one after another, the Thakurani throws down the letter and weeps, and all acknowledge Rasika's glory; because of the incessant troubles Rasika resolves to hold the festivals at Gopivallabhapur and goes to Raja Ramachandra Dhal, and when the raja disregards his words, he leaves his land in anger, accepting not even water there, and foretells his ruin; the raja soon loses his life and many of his domains, and his son — a great Vaishnava, a disciple of Rasika — is placed on the throne; one festival of twelve days Rasika celebrates at Kusharada, in the kingdom of Patna; five such festivals took place in three villages, and twenty at Gopivallabhapur; the author promises to tell of them*

*The fifth lahari.*

*Raga Shri.*[^405-1]
*Ghosha: "O Hari, this time be merciful to me:*
*I hope to obtain the shade of Your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy,
at whose feet the servant is Rasika-shekhara![^405-2]

**2.** Thus Rasikendra, performing sankirtana,
danced much, celebrating the dadhi-kada.[^405-3]

**3.** His charming holy body is grey with the dust of the rasa,
and drops of curd are on his beautiful holy body.

**4.** Sandal paste, kunkuma, phagu, the pollen of flowers —
how [they] glitter on his long cheeks![^405-4]

**5.** His face, surpassing the moon, is exceedingly charming;
from his holy eyes tears flow in love for Krishna.

**6.** Holding Sri Nandanandana [and] the holy feet of Shyamananda
in his heart, the son of Achyuta remained.[^405-5]

**7.** Rasika's associates and followers together with his own people —
like a host of stars surrounding the moon.[^405-6]

**8.** As though knowing by a sign the plan of the wicked,
the five sons of Rasamaya sit down around Prabhu.

**9.** Within their minds the five brothers resolve:
"If anyone makes a disturbance against Prabhu,

**10.** we will strike down all these wicked ones,
and then give our lives before Sri Rasika."[^405-7]

**11.** Thus all together think within their minds;
all sat down carefully around Rasika.

**12.** Kings, subjects, brahmanas, sannyasis, gentle sadhus —
all the people sat around on all four sides.[^405-8]

**13.** At that time, bringing the letter, [they] presented [it].
Listen, all, attentively to this account.[^405-9]

**14.** Padmanabha [and] Gopidasa began to read;
reading the letter, they proclaimed [it] before all.

**15.** The elder mother holds the letter by one edge,
and they here, at the other edge, read [and] let [all] hear.[^405-10]

**16.** From the first canto to the twelfth —
ten shlokas [from each] were at the beginning of the letter.

**17.** Then — the siddhanta of the six shastras in subtle form:
they read ten or twenty shlokas, one after another.

**18.** Then in the letter the meaning of the truths of the Vedas appeared;
Padmanabha [and] Gopidasa went on reading.

**19.** Then — two or four songs of Sri Jayadeva;
on the four edges of the letter — narratives of the Bhagavata.[^405-11]

**20.** At the end, after that, three shlokas were written:
"Whoever reviles Murari is a sinner in this world.

**21.** Blameless is Rasika, known to all people;
the beloved of his life is Krishna; [he is] renowned in the world.[^405-12]

**22.** Whoever without cause lays blame on such a person
goes with all his line to a terrible hell.

**23.** One who is inseparably united with Krishna —
whoever reviles such a person is a sinner [and] a villain.[^405-13]

**24.** Rasikendra-raya is born of a portion of Narayana;
whoever reviles him, that sinner goes to ruin.[^405-14]

**25.** Rasika-shekhara is wholly devoted to every dharma;
whoever lays blame on such a person is a sinner, a base wretch.[^405-15]

**26.** By whose touch Krishna-bhakti [awakens] in all —
such a person the evil-minded revile, not knowing [him].

**27.** By whose darshana all bonds [fall away],
hearing whose words the ears are soothed;

**28.** by whose might the earth was rid of sin —
such a person the fool, the wicked creature reviles."[^405-16]

**29.** All heard these words in the letter;
the villains, gathering together, whisper to one another.[^405-17]

**30.** All heard in the letter narratives of the Bhagavata;
not knowing [how], all were thrown into confusion: [where were] those false words?[^405-18]

**31.** One by one, rising, the villains flee;
who goes in which direction cannot be told.

**32.** Suddenly the pride of all was crushed;
throwing down the letter, the Thakurani began to weep.

**33.** All people came to know Rasika's glory;
astonished, all went to their places.[^405-19]

**34.** Thus after some days Prabhu, [thinking of leaving] that place,
held counsel with his own people, as was fitting:[^405-20]

**35.** "Here troubles arise constantly;
my heart no longer consents to stay here.

**36.** The festival will be in Sri Gopivallabhapur;
the community of the Shyamanandis will not come here any more."[^405-21]

**37.** Having considered all this, Prabhu went to the raja;
sitting in private, he told him the whole matter.

**38.** Ramachandra Dhal, hearing [it], treated [it] with disregard;
in anger [Prabhu] departed from there.[^405-22]

**39.** He declared: "I will not come to your land again;
in a few days your pride will be brought to ruin."

**40.** From there Rasikendra departed;
in the Dhal land he no longer accepted water.[^405-23]

**41.** He declared: "Utter ruin will befall him:
in drunken pride this wretch has broken [my] word.

**42.** In his conceit he has wrecked Shyamananda's seat;
his life will hang by a thread, [he] will have to leave the country."[^405-24]

**43.** Rasika's word is never transgressed, on any day:
whatever order he gives to anyone is never overturned.

**44.** By his word durva grass becomes like wood,
[and] wood like durva: irresistible is [his] word.[^405-25]

**45.** From then on misfortune came upon the raja:
he lost his life, and many domains were lost.[^405-26]

**46.** Then after some days Sri-charana carefully
installed his son on the royal throne.

**47.** A great Vaishnava was [this] raja, known in the world;
a disciple of Rasika was the raja, honoured throughout the universe.[^405-27]

**48.** Seeing Rasika's power, all people,
deeming [it] a wonder, offer [him] praise.

**49.** Then one [festival] of twelve [days] — in the village of Kusharada:
in the kingdom of Patna he stayed some days.[^405-28]

**50.** These five [festivals] of twelve [days] took place in three villages,
and all the rest in Sri Gopivallabhapur.

**51.** Twenty [festivals] of twelve [days] took place in that village:
the son of Achyuta held [them] at his pleasure.[^405-29]

**52.** Of them I shall tell something;
listen, listen, all devotees of Krishna, with attention.[^405-30]

**53.** Who can know [Rasika's] boundless greatness and virtues?
Whatever by Rasika's mercy dawns upon me even a little —

**54.** [those] human pastimes [which] Prabhu, having descended upon the earth,
[displayed] in waves of play —

**55.** describing [his] nature, I have described something —
whatever the son of Achyuta speaks, dwelling [in my] heart.[^405-31]

**56.** Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**57.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fifth lahari, called "The Description of the Failure of Gaurangadasi's Conspiracy through the Power of the Glory of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu."*[^405-32]

[^405-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("পঞ্চম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 5 begins. Raga Shri (*śrī*; Purva, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Uttara, lahari 2 (note 1), and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ প্রভুর মহিমার গুণে গৌরাঙ্গ-দাসীর ষড়যন্ত্রের ব্যর্থতা বর্ণন" (*śrīśrīrasikānanda prabhura mahimāra guṇe gaurāṅga-dāsīra ṣaṛayantrera byarthatā barṇana*), literally "The Description of the Failure of Gaurangadasi's Conspiracy by Virtue of the Glory of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu."

[^405-2]: As in Uttara, lahari 2, 1 (note 2): Rasika is Shyamananda's disciple.

[^405-3]: "Celebrating the dadhi-kada" — *dadhikādā sāri*, literally "having performed, completed the dadhi-kada": the festive drenching with curd (lahari 4, 36, 47, note 23); this is the very dadhi-sankirtana at which Gaurangadasi calls the assembly (lahari 4, 47–55). On the 1941 edition there is a stray punctuation mark after *saṃkīrttana*.

[^405-4]: "Grey with the dust of the rasa" (3) — *rāsadhūli-dhūsara*: with the dust of the circle of the dance. Phagu (*phāgu*) — the red powder people throw at each other at the festival (abir). "The pollen of flowers" — *phulera keśara*. "Long cheeks" — *sudīrgha kapole*.

[^405-5]: Sri Nandanandana — Krishna, the son of Nanda. "The son of Achyuta" — Rasika (Purva, lahari 3, note 5).

[^405-6]: "Associates and followers" — *sāṅgopāṅga* (Uttara, lahari 1, note 24). "His own people" — *nijagaṇa*.

[^405-7]: "The five sons of Rasamaya" — *rasamaẏa pañcaputra*: the author of the poem is a son of Rasamaya, a disciple of Rasikananda (the author's signature), apparently one of these five; the brothers' names are not given. "By a sign" — *iṅgite*. 9b — *yabe prabhu diẏā kare keha gaṇḍagola*: *diẏā* — "through, concerning"; understood as "against Prabhu." "Give our lives" — *prāṇa diba*: readiness to give their lives for the guru.

[^405-8]: "All together" (11) — *paraspara*. "Sannyasis" — *nyāsī*. "Gentle sadhus" — *śānta sādhujana*. "Sat" — *basilena*.

[^405-9]: "Bringing the letter, presented" — *likhā āni kaila upasana*: the subject is not expressed — apparently the elder mother (lahari 4, 47–55) or her people; *upasana* — "arrival" (lahari 4, note 3), here apparently "presented."

[^405-10]: Padmanabha and Gopidasa — lahari 4, 55, note 30. "Proclaimed before all" (14) — *sabāsthāne karilā prakāśa*. "Holds by one edge" — *ekadike*: Gaurangadasi does not let the letter out of her hands (lahari 4, 54–55). 15b — *paṛiẏā śunaẏe ethā tā̃rā āra dike*: the sense is approximate.

[^405-11]: Instead of what the conspirators had written (lahari 4, 33–35, 39), the letter turns out to contain verses of the Bhagavata: "canto" — *skandha*, one of the twelve cantos of the Bhagavata; "ten shlokas" — *daśa daśa śloka*. "The siddhanta of the six shastras" — *ṣaṛśāstrera siddhānta*: of the six philosophical systems (lahari 3, note 16); "in subtle form" — *sūkṣmarūpe*. "The meaning of the truths of the Vedas" (18) — *bedatattba artha*. Jayadeva — the author of the Gita-govinda; "songs" — *gāthā*. "On the four edges" — *cāridike*: where the conspirators had written the slander (lahari 4, 35, 39). This story is not in BR 15.

[^405-12]: "Three shlokas" — the author gives their sense in Bengali; the Sanskrit text is not given. Murari — Rasika-Murari. "Blameless" — *adoṣita*. 21b — *prāṇera ballabha kṛṣṇa jagata-bikhyātā*: understood as "the beloved of his life is Krishna"; "renowned in the world" apparently refers to Rasika (the endings *-khyātā*, *-bikhyātā* are for the rhyme). "With all his line" (22) — *sabaṃśe*.

[^405-13]: "Inseparably united with Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera sahita yā̃ra abheda milana*, literally "whose union with Krishna is non-different": praise of Rasika. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, the devotee is eternally distinct from Krishna, and "non-difference" is understood as complete oneness of heart and will in love and service, not as merging; Rasikananda is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda (Pashchima, lahari 4, note 37; on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^405-14]: 24–28 continue the "three shlokas" found at the end of the letter (20–23, note 12); the quotation mark opened in 20 closes in 28. Rasikendra-raya is Rasika. "Born of a portion of Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa-aṃśe janma*: so say the miraculously changed words of the letter; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation of the Lord (note 13; Uttara, lahari 4, note 5; on the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "Goes to ruin" — *kṣaẏa yāẏa*.

[^405-15]: "Wholly devoted to every dharma" — *sarbbadharmma-parāẏaṇa*. "Lays blame" — *doṣe*. "A base wretch" — *adhama pāmara*. "By whose touch" (26) — *yā̃hāra paraśe*: by contact, association with him. "Not knowing [him]" — *nā jāniẏā*. "The evil-minded" — *duṣṭamati*.

[^405-16]: "All bonds" (27) — *sarbba bandha*: the bonds of worldly existence (cf. lahari 4, 57). "The ears are soothed" — *juṛāẏa śrabaṇa*, lit. "the ears are cooled, comforted." "Might" (28) — *pratāpe*. "The wicked creature" — *duṣṭa se parāṇī*.

[^405-17]: "Whisper to one another" — *kāṇākāni kare*: the conspirators (lahari 4, 29–30, 43–46).

[^405-18]: "Narratives of the Bhagavata" — *bhāgabata-kathā*: verses of the Bhagavata in place of the slander (16–19, note 11). 30b — *nā jāni bhulila sabe hena mithyā kathā*: the sense is approximate; understood as the confusion of the conspirators, who could not find their slander in the letter; it can also be understood as "no one knows how, all [in the letter] forgot those false words."

[^405-19]: The Thakurani (32) is Gaurangadasi, the "elder mother" (lahari 4, note 18). "The pride of all" — *sabākāra garbba*: of the conspirators. "To their places" (33) — *yathāsthāne*.

[^405-20]: "That place" — *tathā haite*, "from there": Shyamasundarpur, where the three Thakuranis lived (lahari 4, 11). "His own people" — *ātmagaṇa*. "Held counsel" — *yukti kaila*.

[^405-21]: "Troubles" (35) — *upadraba*, "disturbances, vexations." "My heart no longer consents" — *nāhi laẏa mane*. 36 is the decision to move the festivals to Gopivallabhapur (50–51; lahari 6); Gopivallabhapur is a village on the Suvarnarekha, Rasika's main place of service (Dakshina, lahari 3). "The community of the Shyamanandis" — *śyāmānandī goṣṭhī*.

[^405-22]: "To the raja" (37) — *rājāsthāne*. "In private" — *nigame* (lahari 4, note 19). "The whole matter" — *sakala tattba*. Ramachandra Dhal (*rāmacandra dhala*) is apparently the ruler of Dhalbhum ("the Dhal land," 40), a region on the Suvarnarekha around Ghantashila (Ghatshila; Purva, lahari 14, note 4), neighbouring Gopivallabhapur; *dhala* is the family name of the rulers of Dhalbhum; the identification is provisional. Among Rasika's disciples a "Raja Ramachandra" is named (Pashchima, lahari 14, 136) — whether this is the same person is not said. What exactly Rasika asked of the raja is not said (cf. 42). "Treated [it] with disregard" — *karila helana*. 38b — the subject is not expressed; apparently Rasika (cf. 40).

[^405-23]: "Declared" (39, 41) — *ājñā kaila*, lit. "ordered." "Brought to ruin" — *chārakhāra haibe*. "No longer accepted water" (40) — *jala āra nā kaila grahaṇa*: a severance of all relations (lahari 3, note 6). "The Dhal land" — *dhala deśa* (note 22).

[^405-24]: "Utter ruin" (41) — *sarbbanāśa*. "In drunken pride" — *madagarbbe*. "Has broken [my] word" — *bacana bhāṅgila*: has disregarded Rasika's request. "Shyamananda's seat" (42) — *śyāmānanda-pāṭa*: *pāṭa* is a place of service, a seat; the sense of 42a is approximate: apparently by his refusal the raja wrecked what had been arranged by Shyamananda's order (the three Thakuranis and the Deities together in Shyamasundarpur — lahari 2, 47–54; lahari 4, 10–11). "In his conceit" — *ātmagarbbe*. "His life will hang by a thread" — *prāṇa laiẏā ṭānāṭāni*, lit. "a tug-of-war over his life." "Will have to leave the country" — *deśatyāga ha'be*.

[^405-25]: "On any day" (43) — *sarbba dine*: always. "Is never overturned" — *nā haẏa khaṇḍane*. Durva (44) is a soft grass used in rites; the figure of speech: Rasika's word can make the soft hard and the hard soft. "Irresistible" — *alaṅghya*.

[^405-26]: "Misfortune came" — *hailā akāye*: understood as *akāja*, "misfortune, ill"; the sense is approximate. "He lost his life" — *prāṇa hata hailā*: what was said in 39, 41–42 came to pass. 45b — *āra tyāga bahu rājye*, lit. "and the abandonment of many kingdoms"; it can also be understood as "[his house] had to leave many domains" (cf. 42: "will have to leave the country").

[^405-27]: "Sri-charana" (46) — *śrīcaraṇe*, "the holy feet": an honorific designation; apparently Rasika (cf. lahari 6, 46); it can also be understood as "[Rasika] installed his son, [who had fallen] at [his] holy feet, on the throne." The raja's son is not named. "Installed on the royal throne" — *sthāpilena rājapade*. "Known in the world" (47) — *jagata-bidita*; "honoured throughout the universe" — *bhubana-pūjita*.

[^405-28]: Kusharada and the kingdom of Patna (*pāṭanā rājya*) are unidentified; apparently not Patna in Bihar but a local principality. "One [festival] of twelve [days]" — *eka duẏādaśa*: the annual twelve-day aradhana of Shyamananda (Uttara, lahari 2, 4–5, note 5). 49b is understood as an explanation: for the sake of the festival Rasika stayed there some days.

[^405-29]: "Five [festivals] of twelve [days] in three villages" (50) — *pā̃ca duẏādaśa haila tina grāme*: apparently two in Govindapur (Uttara, lahari 1, 23; lahari 2, 44–45, note 26), two in Shyamasundarpur (lahari 4, 19, note 12) and one in Kusharada (49); the count is conjectural (cf. the "third" festival — lahari 4, 12, 28, note 8). "In that village" (51) — in Gopivallabhapur: apparently twenty annual festivals in memory of Shyamananda held there by Rasika. The son of Achyuta is Rasika. "At his pleasure" — *āpana sukhe* (lahari 3, note 3).

[^405-30]: "I shall tell" — *kariba bidita*, "I shall make known": the account of the festival in Gopivallabhapur is lahari 6. "Devotees of Krishna" — *kārṣṇa-bṛnda*.

[^405-31]: "Greatness and virtues" (53) — *garima-guṇa*. "Dawns upon me" — *sphure*, "flashes [in the mind]." "Having descended upon the earth" (54) — *abatīrṇa haiẏā abanīmaṇḍale*: the author speaks of Rasika as one descended from above (note 14; Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11). "Human pastimes" — *mānabika līlā*. "In waves of play" — *kautuka-kallole*. "Describing [his] nature" (55) — *sbabhāba barṇanā* (cf. Purva, lahari 1, note 68). 53–55 form one sentence; the connection of the parts is approximate. The author ascribes his inspiration to Rasika dwelling in his heart (cf. lahari 6, 59).

[^405-32]: The author's signature (57) and the colophon are; the title is as in note 1. Below is a rule.


## Lahari 6. The Description of the Twelve-Day Festival in Sri Gopivallabhapur

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika resolves to hold the festival in Gopivallabhapur on the Suvarnarekha, which all call the hidden Vrindavana; in the kadamba grove, beneath trees adorned with canopies, strings of jewels, chamaras and garlands, is the circle of the rasa with a pavilion and a jewelled throne; around it are Vrajavasis, Gaudiyas, people of Utkala, Shyamanandis, rajas and subjects, and hundreds of traders bringing goods and beads from Vraja, and everything is sold; Rasika buys everything and lavishes sweets, provisions, clothes and ornaments beyond measure on hundreds of thousands of people; amid lights and fireworks, kirtana and music, Sri Govinda-raya in twelve attires goes in procession to the place of the rasa, Rasika sprinkles the way with sandal water, the rajas pelt one another with powders, and for twelve days Rasika dances, overcome by the eight sattvika-bhavas, and embraces everyone; calling himself ignorant, the author says he writes by the inspiration of the son of Achyuta*

*The sixth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^406-1]
*Ghosha: "O ocean of mercy, O merciful Shyama!*
*Turn Your attention to the fallen and wretched people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of those who have nothing,
the friend who purifies the fallen, the treasury of compassion![^406-2]

**2.** Thus in the place Sri Gopivallabhapur
he resolved in his mind to hold the festival.[^406-3]

**3.** A most charming place, beautiful to behold,
on the bank of the Suvarnarekha, most charming.

**4.** The glory of the village cannot be told at all:
all people sing [of it], calling [it] the hidden Vrindavana.

**5.** The beauty of the kadamba grove cannot be told;
beneath it the Sri circle of the rasa shines forth.[^406-4]

**6.** A dense forest — a wood of kadambas;
its wondrous beauty to behold cannot be described.

**7.** Row upon row the trees shine on every side;
in the shade of the thick leaves the [sun's] rays do not reach.

**8.** Beneath them, wondrous canopies tier upon tier;
from them hang strings of jewels [and] wondrous chamaras.

**9.** In their midst a wondrous pavilion was built,
adorned with various jewels, most skilfully made.[^406-5]

**10.** With various kinds of cloth it was adorned on every side;
tier upon tier hang various kinds of strings of gems.

**11.** In its midst is a most beautiful jewelled throne;
year after year [its] beauty is ever more extraordinary.[^406-6]

**12.** Strings of various jewels and gems hang from all the trees;
gateways [and] banners row upon row on all four sides.

**13.** The beauty of the circle of the rasa is extraordinary:
gods, asuras and humans are astonished.

**14.** From every tree hang hundreds and hundreds of strings,
*jhāna*, cloths, chamaras, tassels, garlands of flowers.[^406-7]

**15.** Every tree is adorned with various flowers;
the trees glitter, the night is bright.

**16.** The kadamba trees themselves are a wondrous adornment;
by the radiance of the trees the earth was lit up.[^406-8]

**17.** Hundreds and hundreds of such trees shine all around;
thousands and thousands of Vrajavasis are beside them.

**18.** Gaudiyas, people of Utkala, the Shyamanandis —
there is no counting them; who can count the sadhus?

**19.** Rajas, subjects, well-to-do folk — hundreds of thousands of people;
all stay around the kadamba grove.[^406-9]

**20.** Beside them sit hundreds and hundreds of traders;
day and night they sell [and] buy various goods.[^406-10]

**21.** Whatever goods there are of the Creator's making —
at the time of the festival all bring [them].

**22.** Various goods all bring, like mountains;
everything is sold — not a single grain remains.

**23.** Thousands and thousands of people bring divine beads:
from Mathura-mandala the traders gather.[^406-11]

**24.** Tulasi, *āṭhela*, wood, lovely strands —
from Vraja they bring hundreds and hundreds of sacks full.[^406-12]

**25.** Mountains of beads lie all around;
all the beads are sold in twelve days.

**26.** Whatever goods come from hundreds and hundreds of kroshas —
everything is sold, nothing remains at the end.

**27.** As was the abundance of goods before at the festival of the rasa, —
four times as much as that there is each time.[^406-13]

**28.** The goods are past counting, [they are] beyond measure;
all the goods Rasika buys up with joy.

**29.** Hundreds of thousands of people he honours [with gifts]:
sweets, refreshments, uncooked provisions, clothes, ornaments.[^406-14]

**30.** Where has there been, [where] will there be such a festival?
Sri Rasika-deva holds [it] with firm resolve.

**31.** As much chuya [and] sandal as he distributes to all —
who would be able to give out that much [even] of mud from a pond?[^406-15]

**32.** As many clothes as the son of Achyuta distributes —
who would be able to give out that much [even] of banana peel?

**33.** As many sweets [and] fried delicacies as he gave to all —
[no one] would be able [to give out that much even] of broken rice.

**34.** Shali rice with the six tastes he gives to the sadhus —
[no one] would be able [to give out that much even] of banana roots.

**35.** As much curd, milk, cream, chhana as he gave away,
ghee, honey, sugar, pana drinks, bananas — lavishly arranged —

**36.** and as many other various provisions as he gave to all —
no one would be able [to give out that much even] of buttermilk and water.[^406-16]

**37.** Seeing Rasika's festival, all people —
all, rajas and subjects — were astonished.

**38.** What beauty that circle has — it cannot be told!
What a procession of Sri Govinda-raya [there]![^406-17]

**39.** Hundreds and hundreds of chandrodayas, deutis, torches,
bhuichampas, chandrabanas, rockets without number.[^406-18]

**40.** The night becomes brighter than day;
with the music of the five sounds the earth trembles.

**41.** The earth sways with the sound of the kirtana;
shingas, venus, vishanas sound — various instruments.[^406-19]

**42.** Hundreds and hundreds of rajas [go] with staffs in hand,
and still hundreds of thousands of people push and jostle.[^406-20]

**43.** As if in rapture Prabhu Sri Govinda-raya moves;
by the effulgence of [His] body the four quarters were lit up.[^406-21]

**44.** What a sweet face, what a sweet glance!
What a gentle, gentle smile, the swaying of [His] body!

**45.** In twelve days there are twelve attires:
on whichever day, whichever attire — that one is resplendent.

**46.** What wondrous attire Sri-charana creates!
Seeing the attire, all people are astonished.[^406-22]

**47.** When Prabhu Sri Govinda goes in procession,
Rasikendra sprinkles sandal water ahead.[^406-23]

**48.** Some with phagu, some with chuya, some with argaja —
all the rajas pelt one another.[^406-24]

**49.** All float in the ocean of bliss night and day;
in great bliss Prabhu goes in procession with sankirtana.

**50.** Having brought Govinda in procession to the place of the rasa,
in great bliss Rasika-shekhara dances.[^406-25]

**51.** The eight sattvika-bhavas manifest in [his] holy body;
hundreds and hundreds of streams flow from the waves of [his] eyes.

**52.** Like kadamba buds, [his] body [bristles] with pulaka;
in the rapture of bhava [his] holy body rolls on the ground.[^406-26]

**53.** With a faltering voice he speaks soft, soft words;
with the tears of [his] eyes the earth turned to mud.

**54.** What a sweet smile, what sweet speech!
Clasping everyone by the neck, he floats in the bliss of prema.

**55.** To all Prabhu gives embraces;
in the rapture of bhava Prabhu has no outer awareness.

**56.** Thus for twelve days he dances,
intoxicated with prema for Krishna, Rasika-shekhara.

**57.** All that happiness cannot be told at all —
all the pastimes [the son of Achyuta displayed] moment by moment.[^406-27]

**58.** By his grace I have made known a little —
a little of the virtues, fame [and] glory of Rasika-deva.

**59.** I am without learning, without intelligence, a wretch;
[I write] whatever the son of Achyuta speaks, dwelling [in my] heart.[^406-28]

**60.** A description of [his] nature I have composed a little;
the learned and the good will not count this a fault.[^406-29]

**61.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the sixth lahari, called "The Description of the Twelve-Day Festival in Sri Gopivallabhapur."*[^406-30]

[^406-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("ষষ্ঠ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2); the ghosha is the same as in Pashchima, laharis 1 and 9 (note 1), and its translation is repeated; "Shyama" here is apparently Shyamananda (cf. 1); it may also be understood as Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল উত্তর-বিভাগে শ্রীগোপীবল্লভপুরে দ্বাদশ মহোৎসব-বর্ণননাম ষষ্ঠ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīgopīballabhapure dbādaśa mahotsaba-barṇana*), lit. "The Description of the Festival of Twelve [Days] in Sri Gopivallabhapur."

[^406-2]: "The life of those who have nothing" — *akiñcana-prāṇa*: dear as life to those who have nothing (cf. lahari 3, note 2). "The friend who purifies the fallen" — *patitapābana-bandhu*. "The treasury of compassion" — *karuṇānidhāna*.

[^406-3]: "Thus" — *henarūpe*: after the events of lahari 5, where Rasika decided that the festivals would be in Gopivallabhapur (lahari 5, 36, 50–51). "The festival" is the twelve-day festival in memory of Shyamananda (Uttara, lahari 2, 4–5, note 5; lahari 5, notes 28–29). Gopivallabhapur is Rasika's village on the Suvarnarekha (now in Jhargram district, West Bengal; BR 15, 81).

[^406-4]: "The hidden Vrindavana" (4) — *gupta-bṛndābana*: Gopivallabhapur is revered as a concealed Vrindavana. The kadamba grove (5) — *kadamba-khaṇḍi*: the place of the rasa in Gopivallabhapur, where the octagonal rasa-mancha ("Kadamkhandi") now stands (Pashchima, lahari 1, note 29). The Sri circle of the rasa — *śrīrāsamaṇḍalī* (ibid.; Pashchima, lahari 16, note 35).

[^406-5]: "Do not reach" (7) — *nā lāge*. "Canopies" (8) — *cā̃duẏā*. "Strings of jewels" — *ratna-jhārā*: hanging strings, pendants. Chamaras are yak-tail whisks. "Pavilion" (9) — *maṇḍapa*. "Most skilfully made" — *ati subandhāna*: understood as "well arranged"; the sense is approximate.

[^406-6]: "Various kinds" (10) — *nānā bhānti* (= *bhā̃ti*). "Year after year" (11) — *batsare batsare*: the festival is annual (lahari 5, 51).

[^406-7]: *jhāna* — so in the 1941 edition; the sense is unclear (perhaps a kind of pendant). "Cloths" — *bāsa*. "Tassels" — *thopanā*.

[^406-8]: "The night is bright" (15) — *ujala yāminī*: from the festive lights (cf. 39–40). 16a — *ekete kadamba bṛkṣa bicitra maṇḍanī*: the sense is approximate.

[^406-9]: Gaudiyas (18) are Vaishnavas from Gauda (Bengal; lahari 4, note 9). The Shyamanandis are the disciples of Shyamananda. "There is no counting them" — *samuccaẏa nāi*, lit. "there is no total." "Well-to-do folk" (19) — *sukhabāsī*, lit. "those living in comfort"; the sense is approximate.

[^406-10]: "Traders" — *pasārī*: shopkeepers, hawkers. "Sit" — *boise*. "Sell [and] buy" — *bicā kinā* (= *becā kenā*). "Day and night" — *diśi niśe*.

[^406-11]: "Not a single grain" (22) — *eka dhāna*, "one grain of paddy." "Beads" (23, 25) — *mālā*: rosaries and necklaces, apparently of tulasi (24); it can also be understood as "garlands." Mathura-mandala is Vraja. "The traders gather" — *byāpāra se melā*: *byāpāra* is trade, traders; *melā* is a gathering, a fair; the sense is approximate.
