[^406-12]: Tulasi is the sacred plant from whose stems rosaries and neck beads are made. *āṭhela* — so in the 1941 edition; the sense is unclear. "Wood" — *kāṣṭha*: apparently wooden beads. "Strands" — *jhurī*. "Sacks" — *chālā*. A krosha (26) is a measure of distance, about 3 km.

[^406-13]: "The festival of the rasa" is the Great Rasa in Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, laharis 1–5). "Abundance of goods" — *drabyabhāra*, "load of goods." "Each time" — *bāre bāra*: with every festival.

[^406-14]: "Beyond measure" (28) — *apramite*. "Honours" (29) — *sambhāṣaṇa*: greets and presents with gifts. "Refreshments" — *śītala*: apparently cooling drinks and refreshments. "Uncooked provisions" — *sidā*: rice, dal and other supplies given to a guest to cook for himself.

[^406-15]: 31–36 are a hyperbole: Rasika gave away so much that no one could give away as much even of the cheapest things — mud, banana peel, broken rice, banana roots, buttermilk. "Would be able" — *bhājana haibe*, lit. "will become a vessel, be worthy." Chuya (*cuẏā*) is a fragrant mixture (Uttara, lahari 1, note 6).

[^406-16]: "Fried delicacies" (33) — *pakkānna*. "Shali rice with the six tastes" (34) — *ṣaṛarasa śāli anna*: rice of the finest kind with all the seasonings. "Chhana" (35) — *chānā*, curd cheese. "Pana drinks" — *pānā*: sweet cooling drinks. "Lavishly arranged" — *subandhāna* (note 5). "Buttermilk and water" (36) — *takrapāni*.

[^406-17]: "That circle" (38) is the circle of the rasa (5, 13). "Procession" — *bijaẏa*: the solemn going forth of the Deity (Uttara, lahari 2, note 28). Sri Govinda-raya is the Deity of Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, lahari 10, note 31; lahari 11, note 12).

[^406-18]: Chandrodaya, deuti, chandrabana, bhuichampa (*bhũicampā*; cf. bhumichampa) are festive lamps and fireworks (Purva, lahari 12, note 17; Pashchima, lahari 16, note 35). "Rockets" — *hāui*.

[^406-19]: "The music of the five sounds" (40) — *pañcaśabda bājanā*: apparently an ensemble of five kinds of instruments. "Sways" (41) — *dulu dulu kare*. The shinga (*siṅgā*) is a curved horn, the venu a flute, the vishana a horn (Purva, lahari 4, note 19).

[^406-20]: "With staffs in hand" — *chaṛi kari hāte*: apparently the rajas themselves keep order in the crowd, as stewards of the procession. "Push and jostle" — *ṭhelāṭheli kare*.

[^406-21]: "As if in rapture" — *madamatte*: with a stately gait, like an elephant in rut. Prabhu Sri Govinda-raya is the Deity (note 17); in the Vaishnava understanding the Deity is the Lord Himself (the archa-avatara), and the author describes His procession as the living movement of the Lord.

[^406-22]: "Attire" (45–46) — *beśa*: the Deity's dress, a different one for each day of the festival. "Sri-charana" — *śrīcaraṇa*, "the holy feet": an honorific designation; apparently Rasika, who dresses the Deity (cf. lahari 5, 46, note 27); it can also be understood of Govinda Himself: "what wondrous attire [the Deity] assumes."

[^406-23]: "Goes in procession" — *bijaẏa kare*. "Sprinkles sandal water" — *candanera chaṛā deẏa*: sprinkles the Deity's path.

[^406-24]: Phagu (*phāgu*) is a red powder; chuya is a fragrant mixture (note 15); argaja (*aragajā*) — the editor explains in a footnote: "water with abir" (fragrant coloured powder). "Pelt one another" — *paraspara mārāmāri kare*, lit. "beat one another": playful festive sport.

[^406-25]: "Prabhu goes in procession" (49) — *prabhu bije kare*: apparently of Sri Govinda (cf. 47, 50); it can also be understood of Rasika. "Having brought in procession" (50) — *bije karāiẏā*. "The place of the rasa" — *rāsasthala*.

[^406-26]: The eight sattvika-bhavas (51) — *aṣṭa sāttbika bhāba*: being stunned, perspiration, pulaka, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears, fainting (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 2.3; Pashchima, lahari 16, note 32). Pulaka (52) is the standing of the hairs on end from ecstatic love — "kadamba buds" (*kadamba-kalikā*; ibid.). "In the rapture of bhava" — *bhābera ābeśe*.

[^406-27]: "Prabhu" (55) is Rasika. "Outer awareness" — *bāhyajñāna*. "Moment by moment" (57) — *tile tile*. The son of Achyuta (*acyuta-tanaẏa*) is Rasika.

[^406-28]: "By his grace" (58) — *tā̃ra anugrahe*: by Rasika's grace. "Glory" — *kīrtta* (= *kīrti*). "A wretch" (59) — *durācāra*: the author's self-abasement. The son of Achyuta (*acyuta-kumāra*) is Rasika; the author ascribes his inspiration to Rasika dwelling in his heart (lahari 5, 55).

[^406-29]: "A description of [his] nature" — *sbabhāba barṇanā* (lahari 5, note 31). 60b — *ithe doṣa nāi la'be paṇḍita sujana*: understood as "will not count [it] a fault"; it can also be understood as "there is no fault in this — [so] the learned and the good will accept [it]."

[^406-30]: The author's signature (61) and the colophon are; the title is as in note 1.


## Lahari 7. The Glorification of the Greatness of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu and the Description of Jagannathadeva's Command concerning the Journey to Nilachala

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; the great festival at Sri Gopivallabhapur grows day by day ten times more splendid than the earlier ones — the circle of the rasa, the procession of Sri Govinda-raya, the sankirtana, the feeding of the Vaishnavas, the lights, the kadamba groves, the bank of the Suvarnarekha — a hidden Vrindavan; when the river's stream moves away to the far bank, Rasika bids the Suvarnarekha, if she is a servant of Sri Chaitanya, to come to this bank, and that same night a flood brings the water back; a storm gathers over the feast of thousands of sadhus, Rasika bids Indra not to wet the assembly of Vaishnavas — and the rain pours all around the village without dropping a single drop in it; in the midst of the festival the elephant Gopala Dasa suddenly arrives, falls at Rasika's feet and, at his command, from then on comes only at night to hear kirtan and take prasada; at night in Nilachala Jagannatha bids the Mudiratha tell the maharaja to send for Rasika and give him the cloth from His holy body; the raja, receiving the same command, sends two brahmanas with the cloth; Rasika, keeping vigil at the festival, hears a voice: "Come quickly and see My lotus feet," and calls everyone to the Ratha-yatra; the brahmanas hand him the cloth and the raja's request, and Rasika ties it on his head; the author promises to tell of the pastimes in Nilachala that he saw while with him*

*The seventh lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^407-1]
*Ghosha: "[My] life is Radhanatha, O, [my] soul is Gopinatha."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of compassion,
the dear life of those who have nothing, the life of the world![^407-2]

**2.** In Sri Gopivallabhapur such a great festival
Rasikachandra, renowned in the world, celebrates.

**3.** However many provisions [and] how much splendour were seen before
at the rasa festivals and other aradhanas, [held] with diligence, —

**4.** ten times [more] than that comes about day by day;
the details of the festival cannot be described.[^407-3]

**5.** The beauty of the circle of the rasa cannot be told!
How in great bliss Sri Govinda-raya goes in procession!

**6.** How the sound of sankirtana touches the sky!
How [arranged are] the seats of the assembly of sadhus on all four sides!

**7.** And the kings, subjects, pilgrims, traders!
And the cries of "Glory, glory!" [and] the name of Hari — again and again!

**8.** And the bhoga [and] offerings to Sri Govinda-raya!
And the provisions that hundreds and hundreds of people bring!

**9.** And the order of the feeding of the Vaishnavas!
And the chandrodayas, lamps, torches, deutis!

**10.** And all the various provisions that stand in rows!
And the kadamba groves surrounding [all] on all four sides![^407-4]

**11.** And the beauty of the village — a hidden Vrindavan!
And the beauty of the riverbank [and] the dense forest!

**12.** And the charming waters of the Suvarnarekha!
And the wonderful pastimes of Rasika-shekhara![^407-5]

**13.** How wonderful the festival is cannot be told;
the son of Achyuta is intoxicated with the sweetness of the festival.

**14.** At the time of the festival the river's stream,
going far away, began to flow by the other bank.

**15.** Seeing the water far off, Rasika-shekhara in anger
said something to the Suvarnarekha:

**16.** "If you are truly a servant of Sri Chaitanya,
then by tomorrow let [your] stream flow by this bank.

**17.** Without water my sadhus suffer;
you must come to this bank."

**18.** And so, unexpectedly, that very night
a flood suddenly came and flowed by this bank.

**19.** Seeing [this], all the men and women were astonished;
from that time the river's water flows by this bank.[^407-6]

**20.** From that time various festivals are held in that place;
Rasika's glory [became] renowned throughout the world.

**21.** One day he seated the Vaishnavas for a meal;
two or four thousand sadhus sat down.[^407-7]

**22.** At that time terrible clouds covered the sky;
a fearsome wind, lightning — flash upon flash.

**23.** Thunderbolts strike, the clouds roar, the earth trembles.
Seeing this, Rasikendra himself speaks:

**24.** "All my sadhus have sat down to the meal;
in Gopivallabhapur there will be no rain.

**25.** If you are truly [like] Prahlada, O King Indra,
then you will not wet the assembly of my Vaishnavas."[^407-8]

**26.** Hearing Rasika's words, Indra, the lord of the gods,
did not rain on the village — it pours on all four sides.

**27.** Around the village he poured the heaviest rain,
[but] he did not let a single drop fall within the village.

**28.** The Vaishnavas joyfully took their meal;
all the men and women, seeing [it, marvelled at] the wonder.

**29.** Such is Rasika's command, inviolable [his] word:
Brahma, Shiva, the gods [and] men do not transgress [it].[^407-9]

**30.** One day, at the time of the great festival,
unexpectedly the elephant Gopala Dasa came.

**31.** Seeing [him], all the people trembled with fear;
hearing [of it], Rasika-shekhara came out.[^407-10]

**32.** He came up to the elephant —
the elephant fell at [his] feet, [stretched out] like a stick.

**33.** Placing his hand on its head, Rasika-shekhara
commanded: "Listen, intoxicated best of elephants!

**34.** Seeing you, people are greatly afraid.
Come to hear the kirtan at night.

**35.** Every day, coming here, you will receive prasada."
Bowing down, the elephant went away.[^407-11]

**36.** From then on it comes for darshana at night:
all carry out Rasika's command.

**37.** Devas, asuras, men, beasts do not transgress
[his command]; in the three worlds his word is not broken.[^407-12]

**38.** Rasikendra-chandra is intoxicated with the sweetness of the festival;
together with him his associates always delight.

**39.** At that time in Nilachala Jagannatha-deva
at night, appearing in person, gave a command to the Mudiratha:[^407-13]

**40.** "My dear one, My devotee, is Rasika-shekhara;
great is My desire to see him.

**41.** Go quickly to the maharaja [and] tell him:
let him send messengers and bring him here.

**42.** I will give him the neta-shari from My holy body;
at every Ratha-yatra he will come and see Me."[^407-14]

**43.** Hearing the command, the Mudiratha told the king;
hearing it, the king rejoiced in his heart.

**44.** That same night a divine command came to the king:
"Send messengers and bring Rasika-shekhara."

**45.** The divine command [confirmed his] faith in the Mudiratha's words:
the worthy king floats in an ocean of bliss.[^407-15]

**46.** He sent two brahmanas to Rasika;
with care he sends the neta-shari from the holy body.

**47.** Meanwhile here, keeping awake at night in the sweetness of the festival,
Rasika-shekhara was sitting alone.[^407-16]

**48.** Unexpectedly Rasikendra heard a command:
"Come quickly and see My lotus feet."

**49.** Startled, he looks around — there is no one in that place;
[yet] the soft, deep voice he heard with his own ears.

**50.** To his own people he told everything in detail:
"I have heard Jagannatha's command.

**51.** Let us all go now and see the Ratha-yatra:
the chariot that enchants the world is renowned throughout the world."[^407-17]

**52.** Prabhu speaks these words to everyone —
at that time two brahmanas arrived.

**53.** They began to say: "Listen, Rasika-shekhara!
Your glory has no comparison.

**54.** Jagannatha Himself gave the cloth from His body;
He gave the command to the Mudiratha, taking him by the hand:

**55.** 'My very dear devotee is Rasikendra-chandra;
to see him is a great joy for Me.'

**56.** He commanded the king: 'Bring [him] quickly,
so that he may come soon and have darshana at the chariot.'

**57.** Here, take the garment from Jagannatha's [holy] body;
hear the king's humble letter.

**58.** Set out quickly to see the chariot:
the maharaja asked us [to say this] in many ways.

**59.** Be sure to have darshana of Sri Jagadbandhu."
Hearing [this], the son of Achyuta floats in bliss.[^407-18]

**60.** In many ways he served the king's messengers;
on his head he tied the neta — the garment from the holy body.[^407-19]

**61.** Now I will tell of the pastimes in Nilachala —
whatever of [his] lila I saw while staying with him.[^407-20]

**62.** A description of [his] nature I have composed a little.
Listen to the Rasika-mangala, all you sadhus!

**63.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the seventh lahari, called "The Glorification of the Greatness of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu and the Description of Jagannathadeva's Command concerning the Journey to Nilachala."*

[^407-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("সপ্তম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2). The ghosha in the 1941 edition — *jībana rādhānātha he parāṇa gopīnātha* — is the same as in Pashchima, lahari 2 (there *re*; note 1), and its translation is repeated: Radhanatha ("Lord of Radha") and Gopinatha ("Lord of the gopis") are names of Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দপ্রভুর মহিমাকীর্ত্তন ও নীলাচল-গমনে জগন্নাথদেবের প্রত্যাদেশ-বর্ণন" (*śrīśrīrasikānandaprabhura mahimākīrttana o nīlācala-gamane jagannāthadebera pratyādeśa-barṇana*). "Command" — *pratyādeśa*: a command of the Deity revealed from above (in a dream or by a voice; 44–45, 48).

[^407-2]: "The dear life of those who have nothing" — *akiñcanapriya prāṇa*; cf. Uttara, lahari 3, 1 ("dear to those who have nothing").

[^407-3]: "Great festival" (2) — *mahāyātrā*; apparently the same twelve-day festival at Gopivallabhapur spoken of in laharis 5–6. "The rasa festivals and other aradhanas" (3) — *rāsamahotsaba ādi ārādhane*: the rasa festival — Pashchima, laharis 2–3; aradhana — a festival of worship (Uttara, lahari 2). "Were seen" — *dekhila*, the subject not expressed. "Ten times" — *daśaguṇa*.

[^407-4]: Sri Govinda-raya — the Deity whom Rasika served at Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, lahari 11). "Goes in procession" (5) — *bije*, respectfully of the procession of the Deity. "Traders" (7) — *pasāriẏā*, stall-keepers at the festival market. "Again and again" — *ghane ghana*. Chandrodaya, deuti — festive lamps (Purva, lahari 12, note 17). "Stand in rows" (10) — *sāri sāri baise*. "Kadamba groves" — *kadambakhaṇḍi*.

[^407-5]: "A hidden Vrindavan" (11) — *gupta-bṛndābana*: the author likens Gopivallabhapur and its surroundings to Vrindavan. "Riverbank" — *pulina*, the sandy bank of a river (like the bank of the Yamuna in Vrindavan). The Suvarnarekha — the river on which Gopivallabhapur stands.

[^407-6]: 14–19 — the Suvarnarekha changes its course at Rasika's word. "Began to flow by the other bank" (14) — *āra taṭe lāge bahibāra*. "A servant of Sri Chaitanya" (16) — *śrīcaitanyera sebaka*. "By tomorrow" — *kālai*. "Flood" (18) — *banyā*. On the author's view of Rasika — note 9.

[^407-7]: "Two or four thousand" — *dui cāri sahasra*: "several thousand." "Sadhus" (21, 24) — *santa*.

[^407-8]: The line is clear in the 1941 edition: *yabe tumi niścaẏe prahlāda indrarāja*, literally "if you are truly Prahlada, King Indra"; understood as an address to Indra: "if you are [devoted like] Prahlada" — cf. 16 ("if you are truly a servant of Sri Chaitanya"). Prahlada is a great devotee of the Lord (Bhag. 7); according to a tradition of the Mahabharata, he himself once held the throne of Indra. Another understanding of *prahlāda* — "gracious, gladdened" (?) — is possible. Cf. the Govardhana lila: Krishna protected Vraja from Indra's downpour (Bhag. 10.25).

[^407-9]: "Inviolable" — *alaṅghya*. Indra, Brahma and Shiva submit to Rasika's word — the author's rapturous praise (cf. Uttara, lahari 4, 8, note 5). According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation of the Lord; the Lord, who loves His devotees, Himself fulfils their word. On the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. 15–19 and 37 are to be understood in the same way.

[^407-10]: The elephant Gopala Dasa (*gopāladāsa hātī*) — the mad elephant whom Rasika tamed and initiated into the holy name (Pashchima, lahari 8, note 34; on its devotion to the guru and service of the sadhus — Pashchima, lahari 10). "Came out" — *bāhāra hailā*.

[^407-11]: "Came up" (32) — *upasana* (Uttara, lahari 4, note 3). "[Stretched out] like a stick" — *daṇḍabat haiẏā*: a full prostration. "Intoxicated best of elephants" (33) — *matta karibara*: in the state of musth (Pashchima, lahari 8, note 10). "Prasada" (35) — *parasāda*. On the 1941 edition 35 is followed by a single "।".

[^407-12]: The same in Uttara, lahari 4, 8 (note 5); see note 9.

[^407-13]: Nilachala — Puri, the abode of Jagannatha. The Mudiratha (*mudiratha*) — a servant of the Jagannatha temple who stands in for the gajapati in the temple rites (the editor glosses "মুদিরথ—সেবক," "servant"). "In person" — *sākṣāta*. The maharaja (41) — the king of Utkala, the gajapati; his name is not given.

[^407-14]: Neta-shari (*netaśāṛī*; in 54, 60 — *neta*) — a fine cloth that has been on the Deity of Jagannatha: prasada cloth, a sign of special favour. "From My holy body" — *mora śrīaṅgera*. "Will come and see Me" — *āsi' dekhibe more*.

[^407-15]: "Rejoiced" (43) — *ānanda … hailē*. "Divine command" (44–45) — *pratyādeśa* (note 1). 45a — *pratyādeśa mudiratha-bāṇīte pratyaẏa*, literally "the command — confidence in the Mudiratha's words": understood to mean that the command received by the king himself confirmed the Mudiratha's words.

[^407-16]: "Keeping awake at night" — *niśi ujāgare*. "Alone" — *nigame*: "in private, in seclusion," as in lahari 4 (note 19) and lahari 5 (note 22).

[^407-17]: "Startled" (49) — *camakite*. "To his own people" (50) — *ātmagaṇe*. "The chariot that enchants the world" (51) — *bhubanamohana ratha*: Jagannatha's chariot at the Ratha-yatra (Uttara, lahari 2, note 6).

[^407-18]: "Has no comparison" (53) — *dite nāi paṭāntare*: *paṭāntara* — "comparison, likeness." "Taking him by the hand" (54) — *dhari' tā'ra hāta*. "Humble letter" (57) — *binaẏa-patra*. "Sri Jagadbandhu" (59) — *śrījagabandhu*, "Friend of the world" — Jagannatha.

[^407-19]: "Served" — *karila sebana*: received the messengers with honour. "The neta — the garment from the holy body" — *neta śrīaṅga basana* (note 14). "Tied on his head" — a sign of reverence for the prasada cloth.

[^407-20]: "The pastimes in Nilachala" — *nīlācala khelā*: they are told in the following laharis. 61b — *ye kichu dekhila līlā saṅge thāki' tā̃ra*: understood as the author speaking of himself (forms in *-ila* are not rare in the poem for the first person); it can also be understood as "what [people] saw while staying with him." "A description of [his] nature" (62) — *sbabhāba-barṇanā* (lahari 6, 60, note 29).


## Lahari 8. The Manifestation of His Own Glory at Muktapur on the Way to Nilachala

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; hearing the message from the brahmanas' lips, Rasika sets out for Nilachala with singers and men of letters and countless sadhus, kings, subjects and pilgrims; in every village people marvel at the thousands of his companions and bring sida, and Rasika has the gifts distributed first to the elders, Vaishnavas and brahmanas, and then to all in turn; the eight siddhis and nine treasures follow him unfailingly; at Muktapur the wicked headman of the village refuses shelter to thousands of Vaishnavas: "Stay under the trees," — and Rasika, reproaching him in jest, gladly settles with everyone under the trees; a north wind rises, fire flares up and burns hundreds of large houses; in fear the villagers say: "Rasika has brought ruin," fall at his feet and beg for protection; Rasika, hearing the praise, looking with nectarean eyes, his voice faltering with the bliss of Krishna, asks the fire to spare the wretched, the fire is at once put out, and all the people of the village become Rasika's servants*

*The eighth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi — panchali metre.*[^408-1]

**1.** Glory to Shyamananda, revered in the three worlds,
whose vow is to purify the world!
The life of the world, the life of Rasika,
mercy to suffering people![^408-2]

**2.** Hearing the message from the brahmanas' lips, Rasikendra
set out on the journey, in order to go.
Singers and men of letters, as many as there were,
he took with him as his companions.[^408-3]

**3.** With him — countless sadhus, crowd upon crowd;
he set out [on the way] joyfully.
In whatever village he halts — [people] are astonished,
[seeing] thousands upon thousands with him.

**4.** Kings and subjects, Vaishnavas, brahmanas,
with him — pilgrims without number.
Wherever the son of Achyuta stays,
[they] bring [him] sida of every kind.[^408-4]

**5.** The lord of the village [places] before Rasika
provisions of every kind.
Seeing [this], Rasikendra-chandra in joy
gives a command to his companions:

**6.** "First distribute to the elders, the Vaishnavas, the brahmanas —
as befits [each];
then — to the pilgrims, the kings and the subjects,
to all, one after another."[^408-5]

**7.** Wherever Rasika-shekhara halts,
the eight siddhis [and] nine treasures —
all these with him
unfailingly travel; splendour — as befits.[^408-6]

**8.** Going along the way, at Muktapur
Prabhu stopped.
The headman there, a wicked villain,
spoke harsh words:[^408-7]

**9.** "For a thousand Vaishnavas, kings, subjects — all,
brahmanas, sannyasis and the rest
no house will be found: stay under the trees," —
so firmly said [this] "wise man."[^408-8]

**10.** Hearing [this], the servants say to Prabhu:
"No house will be found here.
All [are to stay] under the trees, together, —
so says the headman."

**11.** Hearing this, Rasika says in jest:
"Many houses [you] have enjoyed;
my sadhus will stay outside —
for what purpose [then] did [you] build houses?

**12.** Very well, let us all go and stay under the trees,
gladly arranging our seats."
Surrounding Rasika, joyfully remain
with him all the mahajanas.[^408-9]

**13.** Soon a north wind began to blow —
unexpectedly fire rose up.
Blazing fiercely, on all sides burn
the large houses, by the hundreds.

**14.** From one side much caught fire —
goods of every kind, clothing, all there was.
Distraught with fear, [people] say to one another:
"Rasika has brought ruin!"[^408-10]

**15.** In fear all quickly went
[and] fell at Prabhu's feet:
"O stronghold of refuge, possessor of all virtues,
protect [us] all, Prabhu!

**16.** Who will know the limit of your glory?
[Your] vow is to crush the proud.
I am a villain, I disregarded [you] —
[be] merciful to suffering people!"[^408-11]

**17.** Hearing the words of praise, Rasikendra-mani
looks with nectarean eyes.
Immersed in the rasa of Krishna's bliss, in a faltering voice
he speaks sweet words:[^408-12]

**18.** "O Brahma, servant of Hari, do not destroy
all these wretched people!
Forgive the living beings, burn no more —
listen to my words."[^408-13]

**19.** Hearing Rasika's words, Agni
saw Prabhu with [his own] eyes.
The fiercely blazing, boundless heat [of his]
he put out at once.[^408-14]

**20.** Seeing [this], all the people deemed a wonder
the manifestation [of the power] of Rasika.
All the people of the village fell at [his] feet
[and] became Rasika's servants.

**21.** To Rasika's greatness there is no limit —
listen, all people!
Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].[^408-15]

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eighth lahari, called "The Manifestation of His Own Glory at Muktapur on the Way to Nilachala."*

[^408-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("অষ্টম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2). "Panchali metre" (*chanda pā̃cālī*) — tripadi; the stanza is set in four lines in the edition and translated likewise (Pashchima, lahari 6, note 1). There is no ghosha and no mangala-shloka; the stanzas are numbered as in the edition. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীশ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে নীলাচল-যাত্রাপথে মুক্তাপুরে নিজ-মহিমা-প্রকাশ-নাম অষ্টম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*nīlācala-yātrāpathe muktāpure nija-mahimā-prakāśa*). Lahari 8 — stanzas 1–21; 17–21 and the colophon are, the next portion. The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^408-2]: "Whose vow is to purify the world" — *bhubanapābana-bānā*: *bānā* — "vow, mark, garb" (Dakshina, lahari 9, note 2, where it is understood as "garb"; Uttara, lahari 3, note 20); cf. 16. "Mercy to suffering people" — *duḥkhita jane karuṇā*; the same line ends 16.

[^408-3]: "The message from the brahmanas' lips" — of the two brahmanas sent by the king (lahari 7, 46, 52–59). "Set out on the journey" — *yātrā kaila*. "Singers and men of letters" — *saṅgīta-sāhitya*, literally "[all there was of] music [and] letters": understood as people versed in song and poetry. "Companions" — *anucara*.

[^408-4]: "Countless" (3) — *apramita*. "Halts" — *utare*. "Sida" (4) — *sidā*, uncooked provisions offered to a guest (Pashchima, lahari 2). "Of every kind" — *nānāmate*.

[^408-5]: "The elders" — *gurujana*: venerable persons, those senior in standing. "As befits [each]" — *yathāyogya-rūpe*. "Distribute" — *diẏe*.

[^408-6]: The eight siddhis — mystic perfections (the power to become smallest, lightest and so on; Bhag. 11.15); the nine treasures (*naba nidhi*) — the treasures of Kubera. The author's praise: according to the Bhagavata (11.14.14), a pure devotee does not desire siddhis; here they themselves follow Rasika like servants. "Splendour — as befits" — *baibhaba yathābidhi*.

[^408-7]: Muktapur (*mukutāpura*; in the colophon *muktāpura*) is not identified; on the way from Gopivallabhapur to Puri, before Dhamnagar and Jajpur. "Headman" — *pradhāna*, the village headman. "A wicked villain" — *duṣṭa durajana*.

[^408-8]: "A thousand" — *sahasra*. "Wise man" — *sudhī*, "wise": apparently ironical, of the headman; the sense is approximate.

[^408-9]: "In jest" (11) — *kautuke*. "Have enjoyed" — *bhoga kailā*. "For what purpose did you build houses" — *ki kāryye ghara tulilā*. "Mahajanas" (12) — *mahājana*, venerable Vaishnavas of Rasika's retinue.

[^408-10]: "North wind" (13) — *uttarā pabana*. "Has brought ruin" (14) — *kailā nipāte*. On how anger at or contempt for Rasika turns into calamity — cf. lahari 5 (Raja Ramachandra Dhal) and lahari 3; on the author's attitude to Rasika — lahari 7, note 9.

[^408-11]: "Stronghold of refuge" (15) — *śaraṇa-pañjara*, literally "cage (enclosure) of refuge." "Vow to crush the proud" (16) — *sagarbba-dalana-bānā* (note 2). "Disregarded" — *helana karilu*. The villagers' speech, Rasika's words to the fire and the extinguishing of the blaze are in 17–21.

[^408-12]: "Rasikendra-mani" — *rasikendra-maṇi*, "the jewel among rasikas." "With nectarean eyes" — *amṛtanaẏane*. "In a faltering voice" — *gada gada bhāse*: *gadgada* is speech choked by overflowing feeling, one of the signs of prema.

[^408-13]: Rasika addresses the fire. *brahmā haridāsa* — clear in the 1941 edition, the sense is unclear: apparently an address to Agni, the deity of fire, called "Brahma" (in the Vedic hymns Agni is the brahmana priest of the sacrifice) and "servant of Hari" (the demigods serve the Lord); another understanding is possible. "Do not destroy" — *nā kara bināśa*. "The living beings" — *jībe*.

[^408-14]: Agni (*agni*) is the deity of fire. "Saw Prabhu with [his own] eyes" — *dekhila prabhu naẏane*: the fire, as a living being, beheld Rasika. "Put out" — *nibhāila*; the subject is apparently Agni (it could also be understood as "[Prabhu] put out"). On how the author exalts Rasika, see lahari 7, note 9.

[^408-15]: "The manifestation [of the power]" (20) — *parakāśa*. "There is no limit" (21) — *dite nāhi sīmā*, literally "a limit cannot be set." The author's signature is given in the standard formula (README § 4); here it is in tripadi metre and reads differently: *śyāmānanda-pada, sakala sampada, rasamaẏera nandane* — "Shyamananda's feet are all the wealth of the son of Rasamaya" (cf. Purva, lahari 5, note 14). Lahari 8 comprises stanzas 1–21.


## Lahari 9. The Description of the Sinking of the Boat in the Midst of the Vaitarani River and of the Rescue from It of the Devotees and the Book Srimad-Bhagavatam

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika travels to Nilachala with great devotees, amid cries of "Hari!", singing, flutes and vinas; thousands of people gather to see him, many become his disciples, and all Utkala takes exclusive shelter in Krishna; at Dhamnagar Rasika leaves his palanquin and goes on foot; at Jajpur he bathes in the Vaitarani at the Ashvamedha ghat, sees Varahanatha, holds kirtan, dances and gives gifts to the brahmanas; the next day, on the flooded river, the wind and waves capsize the boat carrying two or three hundred people, but where a twenty-cubit pole finds no bottom the water becomes knee-deep for all, and Rasika turns the boat over; people on the banks lament the drowned, while others say that in Rasika's boat no one will perish; boats sent out pick everyone up; the manuscript of the Bhagavata is missing, the brahmana Radhamadhava finds it in the river, but neither he nor dozens of people can lift it out of the water, while Rasika lifts it into the boat with his hand, lighter than a flower; the author asks the learned not to hold against him faults in the order of the narrative*

*The ninth lahari.*

*Raga Shri.*[^409-1]
*Ghosha: "Rama, glory [to You]! Govinda, Rama, glory [to You]!"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of [his] beloved!
Be merciful, so that I may compose [his] glory.[^409-2]

**2.** At this time Rasikendra goes from road to road;
with him are great, great, exalted bhagavatas.

**3.** Along the road they go, again and again making the sound of Hari's name;
some sing, some play the flute [and] the vina.[^409-3]

**4.** Thousands upon thousands of people come to see;
with cries of "Hari!" they come from all sides.

**5.** Seeing Rasika's form, all in joy
gaze upon [his] lotus feet.

**6.** Seeing [his] form, the men and women were enchanted;
hearing Rasika's words, they gladden their ears.

**7.** Like bees, people surrounded [him] to see;
no one's heart consents to leave [him] and go.

**8.** How sweet [his] words, how sweet his converse!
He won everyone over by the radiance of his glance.[^409-4]

**9.** Many became [his] disciples as he went along the road;
becoming devoted to Krishna alone, they worship Krishna with pure hearts.

**10.** Seeing Rasika, all gave their minds to Krishna;
the land of Utkala took exclusive shelter.[^409-5]

**11.** Prabhu entered Dhamnagar;
from that place he gave up the palanquin.[^409-6]

**12.** On foot goes Rasika-shekhara;
at last he arrived at the town of Jajpur.

**13.** Bathing in the Sri Vaitarani — at the Ashvamedha ghat;
on its bank he saw Varahanatha.[^409-7]

**14.** That day he held kirtan at that place;
the son of Achyuta danced much.

**15.** Hundreds upon hundreds of streams of tears flow from [his] eyes;
seeing [this], the men and women were amazed.

**16.** Prabhu gave many goods to the brahmanas;
from there, the next day, he set out.

**17.** He entered the river at Jajpur;
the river was especially full from the flood.[^409-8]

**18.** Seeing the waves, the men and women tremble;
a boat came up and stopped close by.

**19.** Two or three hundred people sit [in it] at once;
Rasika-shekhara went and sat in the boat.

**20.** Remembering Krishna, taking his close ones with him,
ten or twenty mahantas joyfully went and sat [in it].[^409-9]

**21.** Steering the boat, the helmsman took [it] some distance;
from the force of the wind the boat pitches to and fro.

**22.** In the strong wind wave upon wave rises;
the boat, having gone [a little], came to the middle of the river.

**23.** The helmsman in great terror could not control [it];
the boat pitches to and fro without end, beyond measure.

**24.** In distress they remember Krishna:
"In this danger protect [us], son of Achyuta!

**25.** Apart from you there is no other protector;
in this terrible peril, Prabhu, save [us]!"

**26.** Calling out, Prabhu says to all:
"Do not fear; remember Krishna."

**27.** Even as he spoke, the boat capsized;
all fell and remained inside the boat.

**28.** Some people fell outside the boat —
Rasikendra-chudamani with his close ones.

**29.** The river is a bottomless sea; in its very middle
the men and women fell into the water.[^409-10]

**30.** In the boundless sea the water became knee-deep;
all the people stood up in the river.

**31.** Standing on firm ground, Prabhu quickly seized the boat,
lifted [and] turned the boat over — the men and women rise up.[^409-11]

**32.** Frantic with fear, all quickly rose;
all joyfully sing Rasika's qualities:

**33.** "Blessed, blessed is Rasikendra, the ocean of compassion!
We were sinking in the water in the middle of the river.

**34.** In the midst of the bottomless sea [the water] became thigh-deep!
Blessed is Rasikendra-chandra, the ocean of mercy!

**35.** Through such an impassable [place] you carried all of us across:
in the bottomless water of the sea we stood.[^409-12]

**36.** To deliver [the people of] the terrible [age of] Kali — Rasika the avatara!
In this terrible water he carried all of us across.[^409-13]

**37.** Prabhu, the breaker of fear, the friend of suffering people,
whose vow is to be a fortress of refuge, the ocean of mercy!"[^409-14]

**38.** Thus all the men and women offer praise;
Rasika's ingenuity cannot be understood at all.

**39.** Seeing the boat sinking, all the people on both banks
roll on the ground [and] weep — they cannot be held back.[^409-15]

**40.** All say: "Not one will survive now!
They have sunk in the middle of the river — protect [them], Narayana!

**41.** With huge waves the river devours both banks;
great is the roar of the waves under the blows of the wind.

**42.** In such waves hundreds of thousands (?) have sunk —
for nothing all the living beings have drowned [and] perished."[^409-16]

**43.** Some say: "In the boat in which Rasika travels
not one will perish — by his mercy.

**44.** He who holds to his name in the hour of great danger
is not touched by misfortune: he crosses over with ease.

**45.** Tiger, bear, elephant, lion, rhinoceros — flee;
when Rasika is remembered, none comes near.[^409-17]

**46.** That very Prabhu himself travels in the boat with them.
Have no fear at all," [they] said to everyone.

**47.** Fathomless is the glory of Rasikendra-chudamani:
he himself was born from a part of Narayana.[^409-18]

**48.** Whose vow is to deliver the fallen, the life of all,
Prabhu, the crusher of the pashandis, the son of Achyuta!

**49.** All the sadhus began to offer praise;
all [together] sent out two or four boats.

**50.** [The boatmen] saw all the people standing in the middle of the river;
all, taking the boats, came up [to them].

**51.** They lower a bamboo pole of twenty cubits — they find no bottom;
in that very place Rasika-shekhara is standing.[^409-19]

**52.** Two or three hundred people, all the sadhus —
all are standing in water up to the thigh.

**53.** Seeing [this], all the boatmen were amazed;
they lifted all into the boats, taking [them] by the hand.

**54.** Carefully they lifted out everyone's belongings;
they saw that no one had the Sri Bhagavata.[^409-20]

**55.** Amazed, Prabhu asks everyone;
the brahmana Radhamadhava leapt into the water.[^409-21]

**56.** He swam a good distance in the strong current;
suddenly the chest came into his hand.

**57.** Diving, he brought up the box within the water;
not a single drop of water had touched the book.[^409-22]

**58.** Seeing that the book was not [there], Prabhu grew anxious;
Prabhu himself wants to leap into the water.

**59.** Hearing Prabhu's words, all the companions —
ten or twenty — quickly leapt into the water in the middle [of the river].

**60.** From afar Sri Radhamadhava called:
"Quickly bring the boat here, all of you!

**61.** Though I have found the book, I cannot swim [with it]."
At that moment the helmsman arrives with the boat.

**62.** Ten or twenty companions gathered there;
they lift the book from the water — it will not rise at all.

**63.** All the people who were sitting in the boat
seized [it] together [and] pulled.

**64.** However much strength each of them had,
they could not lift [it] — the book floats away.

**65.** Amazed, all say to Rasika:
"Hundreds upon hundreds of people set to lifting the book,

**66.** [yet] we cannot raise [it] from the water even by a finger's breadth;
the water roars in the wind, the boat is being carried away."[^409-23]

**67.** Hearing, Prabhu in distress says to the helmsman:
"Hold the boat in the current — where the book is floating."[^409-24]

**68.** Quickly the helmsman brought the boat beside the book;
Prabhu, coming close, saw the book floating in the water.

**69.** Stretching out his hand from the boat, he takes hold of the book;
quickly he lifted the book into the boat.

**70.** That which hundreds upon hundreds of people could not lift
rose into Prabhu's hand lighter than a flower.[^409-25]

**71.** Seeing [this], all the companions are amazed;
by Sri Krishna's mercy this was resolved.

**72.** The pastimes are a boundless sea: who can know [them]?
[I tell] the little that is revealed to me by Rasika's mercy.

**73.** May the learned sadhus not take to heart
any faults in the order [of the narrative], and may they listen with love.[^409-26]

**74.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the ninth lahari, called "The Description of the Sinking of the Boat in the Midst of the Vaitarani River and of the Rescue from It of the Devotees and the Book Srimad-Bhagavatam."*[^409-27]

[^409-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("নবম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Shri (*śrī*; Purva, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Purva, lahari 1, and Dakshina, lahari 1, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "বৈতরণী-নদীমধ্যে নৌকাডুবি এবং তাহা হইতে ভক্তগণ ও শ্রীমদ্ভাগবত-গ্রন্থ-উদ্ধার-বর্ণন" (*baitaraṇī-nadīmadhye naukāḍubi ebaṃ tāhā haite bhaktagaṇa o śrīmadbhāgabata-grantha-uddhāra-barṇana*).

[^409-2]: "The life of [his] beloved" — *śyāmānanda-ballabhajībana*: understood as "Shyamananda, the life of [his] beloved [disciple]," i.e. Rasika (cf. lahari 8, 1: "the life of Rasika"); "the life of the beloved [devotees]" is also possible. The second line recurs at the beginning of many laharis; "compose [his] glory" — *yaśaḥ … racana*.

[^409-3]: "Exalted bhagavatas" (2) — *parama bhāgabata*, great devotees. "From road to road" — *pathe pathe*. "Making the sound of Hari's name" (3) — *haridhbani kari'*; likewise in 4. The vina is a stringed instrument.

[^409-4]: "By the radiance of his glance" — *cāhani prakāśa*.

[^409-5]: "Devoted to Krishna alone" (9) — *ananya*. "The land of Utkala" (10) — *utkalabhubana*: Orissa. "Exclusive shelter" — *ananyaśaraṇa*: shelter in Krishna alone.

[^409-6]: Dhamnagar (*dhāmanagara*) is a place in Orissa (now Bhadrak district), on the way from Medinipur to Puri, north of Jajpur. "Palanquin" — *sukapāla*. From here Rasika goes on foot (12; cf. lahari 10, 3–4).

[^409-7]: Jajpur (*jājapura*; Yajapura) is an ancient town and tirtha on the Vaitarani river in Orissa. Vaitarani — *boitaraṇī*, a sacred river of Orissa. The Ashvamedha ghat (*aśbamedhaghāṭa*) is a ghat on the Vaitarani at Jajpur; according to tradition Brahma performed ashvamedha sacrifices there (the Dashashvamedha ghat). Varahanatha (*barāhanātha*) is the Deity of Lord Varaha at Jajpur, on the bank of the Vaitarani.

[^409-8]: "The river at Jajpur" — *jājapura nadī*: the Vaitarani (colophon). "Flood" — *banyā*. "Came up and stopped close by" (18) — *nikaṭe haila upasana*: *upasana* — "came near, arrived" (Uttara, lahari 4, note 3); likewise in 22, 50.

[^409-9]: "His close ones" — *ātmagaṇa*. "Ten or twenty" — *daśabiśa*: "a score or so." Mahantas (*mohānta*) are senior Vaishnavas, heads of communities. "The helmsman" (21, 23, 61, 67–68) — *kāṇḍārī*; "the boatmen" (53) — *kāṇḍāriẏā*. "From the force of the wind" (21) — *pabanera bhaẏe*, literally "from fear of the wind." "Pitches to and fro" — *ṭalamala kare*.

[^409-10]: "A bottomless sea" — *agādha samudra*: so the author calls the flooded river; likewise in 30, 34–35.

[^409-11]: "Remained inside the boat" (27) — apparently under the capsized boat: Rasika, lifting it (31), frees them. "The water became knee-deep" (30) — *eka hā̃ṭu*, literally "one knee"; in 34, 52 — "thigh-deep" (*eka uru*). "Standing on firm ground" (31) — *sthale*: on the riverbed, which had become firm ground. "Lifted [and] turned over" — *tuliẏā phelila*.

[^409-12]: "We stood" — *ubhā* (the editor glosses it "উভা—দণ্ডায়মান," "standing"; likewise in 50).

[^409-13]: "Rasika the avatara" — *rasika-abatāra*: so those who were saved glorify Rasika. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding Rasikananda is not an avatara of the Lord but an eternal associate and dear devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda; *abatāra* here is in the broad sense of "one who has descended [into the world]" (Purva, lahari 6, note 11). On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "Carried across" — *pāra kaila*: both across the river and, by implication, across [the ocean of] Kali; cf. 44.

[^409-14]: "The breaker of fear" — *ātaṅkabhañjana*. "Whose vow is to be a fortress of refuge" — *śaraṇa-pañjara-bānā* (lahari 8, notes 2, 11).

[^409-15]: "The boat sinking" — *nāẏa ḍubā*: from the banks they saw the boat capsize. "They cannot be held back" — *nā yāẏa dharaṇa*.

[^409-16]: *lākhāni* — clear in the 1941 edition, the sense is unclear; understood tentatively from *lākh*, "a hundred thousand" (an exaggeration of the people on the bank); another meaning is possible. "For nothing" — *akāraṇe*. "Perished" — *marila*: so the people on the bank think; in fact no one perished (43, 52).

[^409-17]: "Travels" (43) — *bijaẏe*, said respectfully of a procession. "With ease" (44) — *hele*. "Rhinoceros" (45) — *gaṇḍā*; "flee" — *bhāga*: understood as *bhāg*, "flight"; the sense is approximate. "None comes near" — *nāhi āse lāga*. Verse 46 is understood as the continuation of the speech of "some" from 43.

[^409-18]: "Born from a part of Narayana" — *nārāẏaṇa-aṃśe janma*: the author's rapturous praise; see note 13 (Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11).

[^409-19]: "Whose vow is to deliver the fallen" (48) — *patitatāraṇa-bānā*. "Pashandis" — *pāṣaṇḍa*, unbelievers. "Sent out" (49) — the subject is "all [the sadhus]," apparently from the bank. "A bamboo pole of twenty cubits" (51) — *kuṛi hāta bā̃śa*: a bamboo pole for sounding the depth; "they find no bottom" — *nāi pāẏa sthala*.

[^409-20]: "The Sri Bhagavata" — the manuscript of the Srimad-Bhagavatam (in the colophon *śrīmadbhāgabata-grantha*) that Rasika was carrying with him; on Rasika's love for the Bhagavata, see Purva, lahari 8.

[^409-21]: The brahmana Radhamadhava (*dbija rādhāmādhaba*) is one of Rasika's companions; a Radhamadhava is also named in the list of Rasika's disciples (Pashchima, lahari 14, 147) — possibly the same person. The second line of 55 is apparently the answer to Prabhu's question: it was the brahmana Radhamadhava who leapt into the water [to search for the book].

[^409-22]: "The chest" (56) — *sinduka*; "the box" (57) — *peṛi*: the box in which the manuscript lay. "Brought up the box within the water" — *ḍubiẏā ānila peṛi jalera bhitara*: understood to mean that he raised the box from the depths but could not get out with it (60–61). "Seeing that the book was not [there]" (58) — in the boat.

[^409-23]: "It will not rise at all" (62) — *nā uṭhe sarbbathā*. "Seized [it] … [and] pulled" (63) — *ākarṣiẏā … dharila*. "Set to" (65) — *lāge*. "Even by a finger's breadth" (66) — *aṅguṣṭheka*, literally "by one thumb['s breadth]." "The boat is being carried away" — *palāila tarī*, literally "the boat ran away."

[^409-24]: "In the current" — *khare*: the editor glosses it "খর—স্রোত," "current." The line can also be understood as "hold the boat [against] the current where the book is floating."

[^409-25]: "Lighter than a flower" — *phula haite uśbāsa*: the editor glosses it "উশ্বাস—হালকা," "light."

[^409-26]: "This was resolved" (71) — *tāhā haila samādhāna*. "Is revealed" (72) — *sphure*. "Faults in the order [of the narrative]" (73) — *anukrama-doṣa*: the author asks not to be faulted if events are not told in sequence. "The learned sadhus" — *supaṇḍita sādhujana*.

[^409-27]: The colophon in the 1941 edition.


## Lahari 10. The Immovable Chariot of Sri Sri Jagannathadeva in Nilachala Set in Motion by the Touch of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika crosses the river without the loss of a single thing and, refusing to sit in a palanquin, goes on foot so fast that his companions cannot keep up, though his tender feet have cracked and are bleeding; on the day of the festival he arrives at Tulasi-chaura; the three chariots of Jagannatha come to a halt at Baligandi, and neither hundreds of thousands of pilgrims, nor the king with his ministers, nor elephants and horses can move them; Jagannatha bids Mudiratha tell the king that the chariot will move only when His dear devotee Murari comes; the gajapati meets Rasika and falls at his feet; the crowds leave the chariots to see Rasika; he offers gifts to the chariots and dances in the sankirtana of Rasamaya's community with Tulasidasa, while the people call him a second Narayana; Rasika pushes the chariot with his head, and the chariots, set in motion, swiftly reach their place; the gajapati glorifies Rasika and gives him lodging and prasada; Rasika visits the tirthas and mathas of Nilachala, receives land from the king, lays out a flower garden and a matha, makes gifts to the brahmanas and residents, and promises to come to every Ratha-yatra*

*The tenth lahari.*

*Raga Shri.*[^410-1]
*Ghosha: "O Hari, this time be merciful to me:*
*I hope to obtain the shade of Your feet."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the deliverer of the world!
Be merciful, so that I may compose [his] glory.[^410-2]

**2.** At this time Rasikendra crossed the river;
no one lost a single thing any more.

**3.** Prabhu goes along the road on tender feet;
both feet have cracked, and blood falls again and again.

**4.** All said many [times]: "Sit in the palanquin," —
[but] Rasika-shekhara heeded no one's words.[^410-3]

**5.** Tearing cloth, he binds the joints of his toes;
as he walks, blood drips from his tender feet onto the road.

**6.** And still he goes on with the speed of the wind;
the followers [who are] with him all cannot keep up [with him].[^410-4]

**7.** On the day of the festival he arrived at Tulasi-chaura;
weary from the road, Prabhu bathes there.[^410-5]

**8.** Meanwhile, there, Jagannatha-raya mounted the chariot;
the three chariots halted at Baligandi.

**9.** From Baligandi the chariots move no further;
thousands upon thousands of kalapithyas [set to] pull [them].[^410-6]

**10.** And still the chariot does not move; it stayed there;
[then] all the pilgrims began to pull.

**11.** Hundreds of thousands of people pull, gripping the chariot ropes;
and still the chariot does not move; it stays [as if] sunk to the ground.

**12.** Growing angry, the king [himself] began to pull the chariot,
[and with him] the officials, the ministers, all the people who were with him.

**13.** Together with the brahmanas, everyone pulls;
whatever strength each had, he pulls with all his might.

**14.** Carters [and] ploughmen pulled by the hundreds;
elephants [and] horses pull — and still the chariot does not move.[^410-7]

**15.** Seeing [this], the maharaja was greatly astonished.
At this time the Lord gave a command to the Mudiratha:

**16.** "My dear one, My devotee Murari has come;
coming to Tulasi-chaura, he has entered [the town].

**17.** Rasika will come [and] see the chariot —
only then will the chariot move; do not exert yourselves [in vain].

**18.** Rasika-shekhara himself will pull the chariot —
then the chariot will go quickly; tell [this] to the best of kings."[^410-8]

**19.** Hearing the command, the Mudiratha told the king;
hearing [it], the king hurried to see Rasika.

**20.** Messengers, hurrying, say to Rasika:
"The king has come out to meet you, to take you [with him]."

**21.** Hearing [this], Prabhu set out with the speed of the wind;
at Atharanala the king saw [him].[^410-9]

**22.** Seeing [him], the king in reverence fell at [his] feet;
Rasikendra embraced [him] with joy in his heart.

**23.** In many ways the king, the gajapati, offered praise;
all came for darshan, holding one another's hands.

**24.** Hearing Rasika's name, all the pilgrims,
kings [and] subjects — all came for darshan.

**25.** There is no counting the people [who came] to see Rasika;
all the people came — [only] the three chariots remained.[^410-10]

**26.** Hari-dhvani, [cries of] "Glory, glory!", music of every kind;
one after another, all have darshan of Rasika.

**27.** Then Prabhu, coming to the chariots, had darshan;
he offered cloth [and] ornaments with the five jewels.

**28.** To each of the three chariots he gave its own load of gifts;
seeing the gifts, everyone was amazed.[^410-11]

**29.** Seeing the beautiful moon-like face, the son of Achyuta [weeps]:
hundreds and hundreds of streams flow from his two eyes.

**30.** His body, its hair standing on end, is like a kadamba bud;
the eight sattvika-bhavas appear on his holy body.

**31.** Rasamaya's party, together with Sri Tulasidasa,
began sankirtana in great joy.

**32.** Rasika-shekhara himself danced;
from the manifestation of mahabhava his holy body is overwhelmed.[^410-12]

**33.** How charming [his] body, how [lovely] the movement of his dance!
How, absorbed in ecstasy, he roams like an intoxicated elephant!

**34.** Hundreds and hundreds of garlands sway on Rasika's neck;
everyone, with one another, starts a play with prasada.[^410-13]

**35.** Seeing Rasika's form, everyone was enchanted;
leaving the chariots, all came and began to gaze [at him].

**36.** All say: "This Prabhu is a second Narayana:
his union with Jagannatha is without difference.[^410-14]

**37.** Because of him the chariot moved no further;
it is he who preached devotion to Krishna.

**38.** This man has freed everyone from ignorance,
has preached sankirtana in every home.

**39.** In Utkala he has awakened prema-bhakti;
at his command everyone serves the sadhus.

**40.** It is he who established the festival procession of the rasa,
by whose mercy all are intoxicated with love for Krishna.[^410-15]

**41.** We do not know how to tell his endless qualities;
with him Jagannatha Himself enjoys His pastimes."

**42.** All speak with one another about Rasika.
At this time a pratihari delivered a message:

**43.** "Because of you the chariot has stayed here;
now you yourself pull the chariot rope."[^410-16]

**44.** Hearing [this], Rasika rejoiced in great bliss;
placing his head against a pillar of the chariot, he pushes [it] from one side.[^410-17]

**45.** At Rasika's touch the chariot [sped] with the speed of the wind:
the three chariots arrived at the place Balinara.[^410-18]

**46.** Seeing Rasika's manifestation [of power], all were amazed;
all say: "Rasikendra is a partial incarnation."

**47.** The gajapati came to believe in every way:
he praised Rasika as the very form of Narayana.[^410-19]

**48.** He gave [him] lodging in his own palace, in a splendid place,
[and] with care gave many provisions.

**49.** Whatever is offered to Jagannatha —
all that prasada the king sends [him] with care.[^410-20]

**50.** For nine days he stayed at the place Balinara,
conversing with all the mahantas.

**51.** Ceaseless play in the sweetness of music [and] poetry:
the son of Achyuta is intoxicated with the sweetness of sankirtana.

**52.** All the pilgrims, the residents of the Kshetra, kings [and] subjects,
Vaishnavas, sannyasis, brahmanas, all people of merit,

**53.** the poor, the lowly, the suffering, scholars of the six darshanas —
all stay with Rasika day after day.

**54.** To all Rasikendra gives food [and] water;
in secret the hosts of the gods stay with Rasika.

**55.** Having satisfied everyone, Rasikendra
only then, afterwards, sits down [to eat] with his own people.[^410-21]

**56.** With Rasika it is always a festival of life;
many days he stayed joyfully in Nilachala.

**57.** In all the holy places there are in Nilachala
he bathes, going round [to them] night and day.

**58.** All the mathas of the mahantas that are there —
going round night and day, he visits them everywhere.[^410-22]

**59.** Asking the king for land on the southern side,
he made a flower garden [and] a matha with joy in his heart.

**60.** Every day there are garlands twelve cubits [long], three dhondas;
he appointed ten or fifteen servitors.

**61.** He established a bhoga — ten or twenty abadas;
assigning villages, he gave [them] to brahmanas.[^410-23]

**62.** He gave many gifts to all the brahmanas,
cloth [and] ornaments to the residents of the Kshetra.

**63.** Rasikendra satisfied everyone;
Prabhu took his leave with joy in his heart.

**64.** With everyone Rasikendra made a firm promise:
"Every year I will come and see the moon-like face.

**65.** At the time of the Ratha-yatra I will always come" —
so he settled with the king, the subjects [and] the sadhus.[^410-24]

**66.** Many pastimes he performed in the abode of Nilachala —
they cannot be described even by speaking with a hundred mouths.

**67.** By his mercy I have made known a little —
a little of the qualities, glory [and] fame of Rasikadeva.[^410-25]

**68.** Listen to the *Rasika-mangala*, all friends:
without delay you will attain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**69.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the tenth lahari, called "The Immovable Chariot of Sri Sri Jagannathadeva in Nilachala Set in Motion by the Touch of Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu."*[^410-26]

[^410-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("দশম-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Shri (*śrī*; Purva, lahari 5, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Uttara, lahari 2 (note 1) and lahari 5, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and the ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ প্রভুর স্পর্শে নীলাচলে শ্রীশ্রীজগন্নাথদেবের অচল রথ সচল হওন" (*śrīśrīrasikānanda prabhura sparśe nīlācale śrīśrījagannāthadebera acala ratha sacala haona*), literally "How the immovable chariot … became movable by the touch of …". 5–69 and the colophon are, the next portion. The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^410-2]: "The deliverer of the world" — *jagata-tāraṇa*. The second line is as in lahari 9, 1 (note 2).

[^410-3]: "No one lost a single thing any more" (2) — *kāro eka drabya naṣṭa nāhi gela āra*: after the rescue of the Bhagavata (lahari 9, 54–70). "Have cracked" (3) — *phāṭi'*. "Palanquin" (4) — *sukapāla* (lahari 9, note 6): Rasika gave it up at Dhamnagar (lahari 9, 11).

[^410-4]: "The joints of his toes" (5) — *aṅguli-sandhi*: Rasika's feet have cracked on the way and are bleeding. "Cannot keep up" (6) — *nāi pāẏa lāge*.

[^410-5]: Tulasi-chaura (*tulasī caurā*; also in 16) — apparently a place at the entrance to Puri; not identified (*caurā* — a raised platform with a Tulasi plant). "On the day of the festival" — *yātrā-dine*: on the day of the Ratha-yatra. "Weary from the road" — *pathaśrānte*.

[^410-6]: "Mounted the chariot" (8) — *rathe bije kaila*. Jagannatha-raya — Jagannatha. The three chariots — those of Jagannatha, Baladeva and Subhadra. Baligandi (*bāligaṇḍī*) — Balagandi, the place on the great road from the temple to the Gundicha where the chariots halt for offerings (CC, Madhya 13). "Kalapithyas" (9) — *kālāpiṭhyā*: apparently *kālābeṭhiā*, the hereditary servitors of Puri who pull the chariots; the interpretation is tentative.

[^410-7]: "Stays [as if] sunk to the ground" (11) — *rahe bhūme paṛi'*. "The officials, the ministers" (12) — *pātra mantrī*. "With all his might" (13) — *prāṇapaṇe*. "Carters [and] ploughmen" (14) — *gāṛibahā hāliẏā*: understood as cart drivers and ploughmen (with their bullocks?); the sense is approximate. Cf. CC, Madhya 14: when the chariot stopped, King Prataparudra had elephants harnessed, but even they could not move it.

[^410-8]: "The Lord" (15) — *prabhu*: here Jagannatha. The Mudiratha — lahari 7, note 13. "Murari" (16) — Rasika (Rasika-Murari). "Has entered [the town]" — *parabeśa hailā*. "Do not exert yourselves [in vain]" (17) — *nā kara yatana*.

[^410-9]: "Has come out to meet you" (20) — *pāchoṭī*. "To take" — *nibāre*. Atharanala (*āṭhāra nālā*, 21) — the bridge of eighteen arches at the entrance to Puri (CC, Madhya 5). "With the speed of the wind" — *pabanagamane*.

[^410-10]: "Holding one another's hands" (23) — *dhari' hātāhāti*; perhaps "jostling, hand to hand." "There is no counting" (25) — *samuccaẏa nāi*. 25b — *sarbbaloka āilā rahilā tina rathe*: understood to mean that all the people went off [to Rasika] and the chariots were left alone (cf. 35); it may also be understood as "all the people came [and] stayed at the three chariots."

[^410-11]: "Offered" (27) — *bheṭilena*. "With the five jewels" — *pañcaratne*: pancharatna, the five precious things — a customary offering of honour. "Its own load of gifts" (28) — *bhinna bhinna drabya bhāra*.

[^410-12]: "Moon-like face" (29) — *śrīcandrabadana*: the face of Jagannatha. The eight sattvika-bhavas (30) — lahari 6, note 26. "Rasamaya's party" (31) — *rasamaẏa goṣṭhī*: understood as the kirtan party of Rasamaya, the author's father; it may also be understood as "a party full of sweetness (rasa)." Sri Tulasidasa — perhaps the same "guru of sankirtana" whom Rasika revered from childhood (Purva, lahari 1, notes 34, 63). "Is overwhelmed" (32) — *jara jara*.

[^410-13]: "Roams" (33) — *bule*. "A play with prasada" (34) — *prasādera khelā*: apparently they toss prasada garlands and food to one another.

[^410-14]: "A second Narayana" (36) — *dbitīẏa nārāẏaṇa*; "his union with Jagannatha is without difference" — *abheda milana*; in 46 — "a partial incarnation" (*aṃśa-abatāra*), in 47 — "the very form of Narayana" (*nārāẏaṇa-sbarūpe*); in 54 — "the hosts of the gods" with Rasika. So speak the crowd and the king — rapturous praise. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Rasika is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation (Pashchima, lahari 2, note 28; lahari 7, note 36); the Lord Himself exalts His devotee. On the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "With him Jagannatha Himself enjoys His pastimes" (41) — cf. Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37.

[^410-15]: "Ignorance" (38) — *abidyā*. "The festival procession of the rasa" (40) — *rāsa mahotsaba-yātrā*: the rasa festival at Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, laharis 2–3).

[^410-16]: Pratihari (*pratihārī*, 42) — temple servitors of Jagannatha, guards and messengers. "The chariot rope" (43) — *rathadaṛī*.

[^410-17]: "Placing his head against a pillar of the chariot, he pushes" — *rathastambhe māthā diẏā ṭhele*. Cf. CC, Madhya 14: at Balagandi the chariot stopped, and Sri Chaitanya moved it by pushing it with His head.

[^410-18]: Balinara — not identified; apparently the place the chariots arrive at, the Gundicha, where Jagannatha stays for the nine days of the Ratha-yatra (CC, Madhya 14; cf. 50, "nine days"). The reading and sense are unclear.

[^410-19]: See note 14. "Came to believe" — *biśbāsa haila*.

[^410-20]: "In his own palace" (48) — *āpanā mandire*: understood as the king's palace. "Is offered" (49) — *upahāra haẏa*.

[^410-21]: "The residents of the Kshetra" (52) — *kṣetrabāsī*, the residents of Puri (Sri Kshetra). "Scholars of the six darshanas" (53) — *ṣaṛdarśane paṇḍita*: of the six philosophical schools. "In secret … the hosts of the gods" (54) — *gupate … debabṛnda* (note 14). "Sits down [to eat]" (55) — *boïsena*; "with his own people" — *ātmabṛnda*.

[^410-22]: "A festival of life" (56) — *jībana-mahotsaba*; it may also be understood as "all of life is a great festival." "Night and day" (58) — *niśi diśi*. "The mathas of the mahantas" — *mohāntera maṭha*. "Everywhere" — *sarbbathā*.

[^410-23]: "On the southern side" (59) — *dakṣiṇa pāraśe*; of what is not said (probably of the temple or the town). "A flower garden [and] a matha" — *phulatoṭā maṭha*; this matha of Rasika in Puri is not identified. "Three dhondas" (60) — *tina dhoṇḍā*: the word is unclear — perhaps "bunch, bundle" (?). "Ten or fifteen servitors" — *daśa pā̃ca sebāita*, i.e. "several." "Abadas" (61) — *ābaṛā*, Oriya *abaḍā*: cooked rice offered to Jagannatha (mahaprasada); "ten or twenty abadas" — apparently that many [pots] of daily offering. "Established" — *nirṇe* (= *nirṇaya*). "Assigning villages, he gave [them] to brahmanas" — apparently he granted villages to brahmanas for the upkeep of this service.

[^410-24]: "Took his leave" (63) — *bidāẏa karila*; it may also be understood as "sent [everyone] off [with gifts]." "Made a firm promise" (64) — *nirabandha kaila* (= *nirbandha*). "The moon-like face" — the face of Jagannatha (cf. 29). "Always" (65) — *sarbba dine*, "on all days." "So he settled" — *karila e nirṇe*.

[^410-25]: "By his mercy" (67) — by Rasika's mercy. "Fame" — *kīrtta*.

[^410-26]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ প্রভুর স্পর্শে নীলাচলে শ্রীশ্রীজগন্নাথদেবের অচল রথ সচল হওন-নাম দশম-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śrīśrīrasikānanda prabhura sparśe nīlācale śrīśrījagannāthadebera acala ratha sacala haona*). Lahari 10 ends (॥69॥ — the author's signature).


## Lahari 11. The Sending of Wild Elephants at the Request of Shah Shuja and the Giving of Hari-nama to Two Wild Tigers

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; for the sake of the festivals Rasika constantly travels with his companions, serving the guru, Krishna and the sadhus; kings and subjects vie with one another to invite him, everywhere the eight siddhis and the nine treasures are with him, and he floods every land with love for Krishna; wicked people tell the Padishah of the great mahanta of Orissa who gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants and with whom Jagannatha converses, and Shah Shuja sends a khoja with a thousand horses and elephants to Gopivallabhapur to demand a miracle: let Rasika by his command bring elephants out of the forest; the Hindu community is alarmed, but Rasika answers with a smile that he knows no tricks, his Master is Krishna, and let the khoja keep the yavanas away while the twelve-day festival lasts and make his preparations; the khoja builds an enclosure, and at night, at Rasika's command, the elephant Gopala Dasa leads fourteen forest elephants into it; the khoja falls at Rasika's feet and acknowledges him as Ishvara, the elephants are taken to the Padishah, and the yavanas acknowledge Rasika as Narayana; in Varahabhumi the companions, losing their way at night, enter a dense forest where two tigers block the path; Rasika steps forward and gives them Hari-nama, and the tigers, bowing, lead everyone out of the forest to a village; people gather to see this, and Rasika bids his companions keep his manifestations secret; the author glorifies Rasika, who gave prema-bhakti to all of Utkala*

*The eleventh lahari.*

*Raga Narayani-gauda.*[^411-1]
*Ghosha: "My Krishna, treasury of virtues,*
*refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of compassion,
whose wealth [and] life is Rasikendra-chudamani!

**2.** For the sake of the festivals Sri Rasikendra-chandra
always wanders over the earth; with him is a host of Krishna's devotees.[^411-2]

**3.** He constantly serves the guru, Krishna and the sadhus;
in great bliss he always goes from town to town.

**4.** Kings [and] subjects, vying with one another [to] serve the sadhus,
invite Rasika and take [him to their homes].[^411-3]

**5.** Sending messengers ten or twenty days ahead
[and] watching for where Prabhu will arrive,

**6.** with their whole families they go joyfully for darshan;
falling at [his] feet, they bring [him], begging him to come.[^411-4]

**7.** He fulfils the desires of all;
Prabhu wanders in [all] four directions for the sake of living beings.

**8.** Whatever music [and] poetry there is on earth —
all of it always abides with Rasika.

**9.** Wherever Rasikendra-mani stays,
the eight siddhis [and] the nine treasures are present of themselves.

**10.** One who has not even a ser of rice in his house —
as soon as [Rasika] arrives, the eight siddhis at once supply [everything].[^411-5]

**11.** In the bliss of sankirtana Sri Rasika-chudamani
always himself sings sankirtana [and] dances.

**12.** The eight sattvika [bhavas] appear on his holy body;
with the streams from his eyes [everything] around is drenched.

**13.** How [lovely] the movement of his dance [and] his poses, how [lovely] his gentle smile!
How [sweet] the speech of his holy mouth always is!

**14.** With a special glance he won over all the pilgrims;
he flooded every land, one after another, with love for Krishna.[^411-6]

**15.** At this time wicked people say to the Padishah:
"There is a very great mahanta in the land of Orissa.

**16.** He gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants;
Jagannatha speaks with him — [this is] certain."[^411-7]

**17.** Hearing [this], the Padishah says, looking at the khoja:
"Go and tell Rasika: let him catch elephants [and] give [them to us].

**18.** The forest elephants are his servants.
Ask humbly; do not speak harsh words."[^411-8]

**19.** Hearing [this], the evil-minded khoja quickly set out,
taking with him a thousand horses [and] elephants.

**20.** He arrived in the vicinity of Sri Gopivallabhapur
[and] sent eminent people to Prabhu.

**21.** They submitted to Sri Rasika:
"This is why Shah Shuja has sent me:

**22.** [so that] he may grant me this miracle —
by his command bring elephants out of the forest.

**23.** When ten or twenty elephants come at [his] command,
[we] will surely acknowledge him as Ishvara."[^411-9]

**24.** [This] reached the whole Hindu community there;
deeming [it] a very great misfortune, they all go [to Rasika].[^411-10]

**25.** All made it known at Rasika's feet;
with a gentle smile on his face he says to all:

**26.** "I know nothing of tricks [and] shows;
with my whole being, my Master is Lord Krishna.[^411-11]

**27.** When Lord Krishna shows me mercy,
then the matter will be accomplished — tell the khoja.

**28.** The twelve-day great festival every year
I celebrate with great joy in Sri Gopivallabhapur.

**29.** As long as I am celebrating the festival here,
let not a single one of the yavanas come.

**30.** Tell him: staying at a distance, let him make his preparations;
Krishna will give the elephants if [he] takes pains."[^411-12]

**31.** All went and told [this] to the evil-minded khoja;
hearing it, he joyfully made many obeisances.[^411-13]

**32.** On [all] four sides he laid the foundation of a wall;
inside he carefully placed bananas, rice and so on.

**33.** He left there only one entrance with gate-leaves;
and he put his faith in Rasika's words.

**34.** At this time [Rasika] began the festival;
that [very] elephant, Gopala Dasa, came and entered.[^411-14]

**35.** At night he bowed down to Rasika;
before the elephant Rasika-shekhara spoke:

**36.** "Listen, listen, dear one, maddened best of elephants!
The king of the yavanas has sent servants.

**37.** He has wished to see my miracle:
[that] ten or twenty elephants be brought [and] given [to him] before his eyes.

**38.** At my command, dear one, do one task:
bring ten or twenty elephants [and] put [them] into the enclosure.

**39.** You yourself stay behind, do not go in through the entrance;
show me this very miracle."[^411-15]

**40.** Receiving the command, the maddened Gopala Dasa quickly went;
in the forest he entered among the elephants.

**41.** The king of elephants, leading the elephants along with him,
brings them inside the enclosure.

**42.** At the entrance he himself turned back [and] went off into the forest;
fourteen elephants went into the enclosure.[^411-16]

**43.** The servants closed the gate-leaves of the entrance;
seeing [this], that evil-minded yavana was amazed.

**44.** Seeing Rasika's greatness, he quickly came;
falling down like a rod, the khoja falls at [his] feet.

**45.** In many ways he offered praise before Rasika;
he firmly acknowledged [him] as Ishvara.

**46.** He quickly told everything to the Padishah;
[he] brought the elephants [and] gave [them] to him before his eyes.

**47.** Seeing all these signs, the yavanas
from that time acknowledged him as Narayana in person.[^411-17]

**48.** See, then: at Rasika's command
the forest elephants come to Rasika.[^411-18]

**49.** In the bliss of Krishna Rasika-shekhara wanders;
constantly, absorbed in Krishna, [his] eyes are full of tears.

**50.** From land to land he travels with a happy heart,
overwhelmed by sankirtana, in the happiness of supreme bliss.

**51.** To Varahabhumi Rasikendra once
journeyed, the Prabhu, taking his own people with him.

**52.** His companions are full of [the arts of] music and poetry;
the Prabhu, Achyuta's son, rides in a palanquin.[^411-19]

**53.** At this time, losing their way, they entered a forest;
the night is dark, clouds cover the sky.

**54.** Leaving the road, all wander from forest to forest;
all went on and entered an impenetrable thicket.

**55.** At this time two tigers blocked the way;
in fear all said to Rasika:

**56.** "Two very fearsome, ferocious tigers
have blocked [the way] ahead — the wicked ones do not let us pass."[^411-20]

**57.** Putting everyone behind him, the Prabhu went ahead;
going up to the tigers, he began to speak:

**58.** "Listen, listen, you two tigers!
Both of you, give up wicked deeds, give your minds to Krishna.

**59.** From past sins you were born in a wicked race;
if you do not worship Krishna, you will gain toil birth after birth.

**60.** Worship Krishna's lotus feet with firm resolve;
do not trouble any of the sadhus."[^411-21]

**61.** Hearing Rasika's words, the two tigers
both fell at [his] feet with tearful eyes.

**62.** Placing his hand on [their] heads, he gave the Hari-nama into [their] ears;
hearing the Name, in great bliss they fell at [his] feet.

**63.** Again and again — circumambulation, again — obeisance;
by seeing Rasika they gained divine knowledge.

**64.** Seeing [all] wandering from forest to forest, the two tigers,
clearing the way, go ahead — the two brothers.

**65.** All walk behind, the two in front;
crossing the forest, they came near a village.[^411-22]

**66.** Morning came; in the village everyone saw [them] —
hundreds of thousands of people come to see the tigers.[^411-23]

**67.** Rasika gave a command to the two tigers:
"Go, dear ones, go [and] worship Krishna with care."

**68.** Receiving the command, the two bow down;
circumambulating [him], both went off into the forest.

**69.** All the people saw Rasika's manifestation [of power];
all came, together with [the whole] town, for darshan.

**70.** Such is the greatness of Rasikendra-chudamani:
in the forest country he showed mercy to all the people.

**71.** Rasika gave a command to all his companions:
"All of you, keep all these manifestations secret."

**72.** And all the other manifestations he made in the same way —
receiving the command, the companions kept [them] secret.[^411-24]

**73.** Inviolable is the word of Sri Rasika-chudamani;
his commands are carried out by the best of gods and men.

**74.** He whose commands are carried out by tiger, bear, elephant, serpent,
whose commands are carried out in heaven by Indra, the great king!

**75.** Hearing of [his] greatness, all became stirred;
children [and] the old — all come [and] receive darshan.[^411-25]

**76.** In all lands the Prabhu gave prema-bhakti;
the poor, the lowly, down to the chandalas, he delivered.

**77.** The utter fools who lived in the forest country —
all became Vaishnavas by the touch of [his] feet.

**78.** Not even with a hundred mouths can [all] his qualities be told;
he flooded the land of Utkala with love for Krishna.

**79.** By his mercy I have made known a little
of the qualities, glory [and] fame of Shyamananda [and] Rasika.[^411-26]

**80.** [His] pastimes are a boundless sea, known in the world;
all of you, listen to the Rasika-mangala, giving [it your] heart.

**81.** All the pastimes he performed in the circle of the earth,
all the manifestations he made in waves of bliss —

**82.** even speaking with a hundred mouths, they cannot be described;
the Prabhu is an ocean of qualities, a treasury of compassion.

**83.** In brief I have composed [a song] of [his] fair glory;
listen with joy, people of the three worlds.

**84.** Good people [and] scholars, do not hold [my] faults [against me];
setting faults aside, all of you listen with joy.[^411-27]

**85.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eleventh lahari, called "The Sending of Wild Elephants at the Request of Shah Shuja and the Giving of Hari-nama to Two Wild Tigers."*[^411-28]

[^411-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("একাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. The raga in the 1941 edition is *nārānī gauṛā*, i.e. Narayani-gauda (Purva, lahari 7, note 1; lahari 10, note 1); the ghosha (refrain) is the same as there and in Uttara, lahari 1, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে সাহা সুজার অনুরোধে বন্যহস্তী প্রেরণ ও বন্যব্যাঘ্রদ্বয়কে হরিনাম-প্রদান-নাম একাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*sāhā sujāra anurodhe banyahastī preraṇa o banyabyāghradbaẏake harināma-pradāna*). The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^411-2]: "Rasikendra-chudamani" (1) — "the crest-jewel of Rasikendras," Rasika. "Whose wealth [and] life" — *yā̃ra dhana prāṇa*. "For the sake of the festivals" (2) — *mahotsaba-kāraṇe*. "A host of Krishna's devotees" — *kārṣṇabṛnda*; *kārṣṇa* — "a devotee of Krishna," as in Purva, lahari 1, note 66.

[^411-3]: "Serves the guru, Krishna and the sadhus" (3) — *guru-kṛṣṇa-sādhusebā*. "Vying with one another" (4) — *bādābādi haiẏā*. The editor's footnote gives the variant *sādhusaba* ("all the sadhus") for *sādhusebā*.

[^411-4]: "Ten or twenty days ahead" (5) — *daśa biśa dina ha'te*: in advance. "Will arrive" — *bije … āise*: *bije* — respectful for an arrival. "With their whole families" (6) — *sabaṃśe*. "Begging him to come" — *bije karāiẏā*.

[^411-5]: The eight siddhis and the nine treasures (9) — lahari 8, note 6. "Ser" (10) — *sera*, a measure of weight (about a kilogram). "As soon as [he] arrives" — *bije mātra*. "Supply" — *milāẏa*.

[^411-6]: The eight sattvika-bhavas (12) — lahari 6, note 26. "Poses" (13) — *bhaṅgi*. "With a special glance" (14) — *cāhani biśeṣe*. "Won over" — *baśa kaila*.

[^411-7]: The Padishah (*pātasāha*) — here Shah Shuja (21; note 9). "Wicked people say to the Padishah" (15) — *pātasāha kahe duṣṭagaṇe*: understood as the wicked people speaking to the Padishah (cf. 17). Mahanta — Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37. "Gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants" (16) — cf. the elephant Gopala Dasa (Pashchima, lahari 8, note 34; Uttara, lahari 7, 30–37). "Jagannatha speaks with him" — *jagannātha kathā tāhe kahe*: cf. Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37. "Certain" — *paramāṇa*.

[^411-8]: Khoja (*khojā*, Persian *khwāja*) — a eunuch official in the Padishah's service. "Let him catch … give" (17) — *dhari deuna* (respectful imperative). "Harsh words" (18) — *kubacana*.

[^411-9]: "Taking with him" (19) — *kariẏā saṃhati*. "Eminent people" (20) — *baṛa baṛa loka*. Shah Shuja — the son of Shah Jahan, governor (subahdar) of Bengal in 1639–1660; the author calls him Padishah. In 21b–23 the khoja speaks (through those he sent). "Miracle" (22) — *kerāmata* (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 41). "Will acknowledge him as Ishvara" (23) — *niścaẏa īśbara bali' āniba tā̃hāẏa*: *āniba*, literally "we will bring"; understood as "we will accept [him as] Ishvara (God)"; possibly a misprint for *jāniba*, "we will know".

[^411-10]: "The Hindu community" (24) — *hindugoṣṭhī*. "Reached" — *paśila*, literally "entered." "Deeming" — *bhāni'*.

[^411-11]: "Tricks [and] shows" (26) — *cāṭaka nāṭaka*. "With my whole being" — *sarbbātmabhābete*. "My Master is Lord Krishna" — *mora kṛṣṇa prabhu sbāmī*.

[^411-12]: "The twelve-day great festival" (28) — *duẏādaśa mahotsaba*, literally "twelve festivals" or "a festival of twelve [days]": the festival at Gopivallabhapur (lahari 6, note 1). "Of the yavanas" (29) — *yabanera gaṇe*: Muslims. "Let him make his preparations" (30) — *karuna udyama*; "takes pains" — *karile yatana*. Next the khoja builds an enclosure for the elephants.

[^411-13]: "Told [this]" (31) — Rasika's answer (26–30) was conveyed to the khoja by the eminent men he had sent (20–21). "Many obeisances" — *bahuta praṇāme*. "Laid the foundation of a wall" (32) — *prācīrera karilā pattane*. "Rice" — *dhānya*, unhusked rice. "Only one entrance with gate-leaves" (33) — *eka dbāra kapāṭa mātra rākhila tā̃'ẏa*. "And he put his faith" — *biśbāsa kaila āra*.

[^411-14]: "[Rasika] began the festival" (34) — the twelve-day festival at Gopivallabhapur (28–29, note 12); the subject is not named. The elephant Gopala Dasa — Pashchima, lahari 8, note 34; Pashchima, lahari 10; Uttara, lahari 7, 30–37. "Bowed down" (35) — *paraṇāma kailā*: the elephant bowed down.

[^411-15]: "Dear one" (36, 38) — *bāpu*, an affectionate address. "Maddened" — *matta*: the usual epithet of an elephant in rut. "The king of the yavanas" — *yabanarājana*: the Padishah (Shah Shuja; note 9). "Miracle" (37, 39) — *kerāmati* (note 9). "Enclosure" (38, 41, 42) — *kā̃thi*: the stockade built by the khoja (32–33). "Do not go in through the entrance" (39) — *nā paśibe dbāre*.

[^411-16]: "In the forest" (40) — *'raṇyete*. "Turned back" (42) — *bāhuṛi*.
