[^411-17]: "Falling down like a rod" (44) — *daṇḍabat haiẏā*. "Acknowledged [him] as Ishvara" (45) — *īśbara baliẏā se jānila* (cf. 23, note 9). "Narayana in person" (47) — *sākṣāta nārāẏaṇa*: so the yavanas acknowledge Rasika — enthusiastic praise; see lahari 10, note 14 (Rasika is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^411-18]: "At … command" — *ājñā paramāṇe*.

[^411-19]: "Wanders" (49) — *biharaẏa*. "Absorbed in Krishna" — *kṛṣṇābeśe*. Varahabhumi (*barāhabhūmi*, 51) — apparently Barabhum (Varahabhum), a forest country north-west of Medinipur (now Purulia district, West Bengal). "Once" — *kata dine*, lit. "after some time." "Journeyed" — *bije kaila*. "Full of [the arts of] music and poetry" (52) — *saṅgītasāhitye pūrṇa* (cf. 8). "Rides in a palanquin" — *sukapāle bije* (lahari 9, note 6).

[^411-20]: "Wander" (54) — *bhrami bule*. "Impenetrable thicket" — *gahana-kānana*. "Blocked" (55, 56) — *āgulila*. "Ferocious" (56) — *durācāra*.

[^411-21]: "Both" (58) — *dõhe*. "In a wicked race" (59) — *duṣṭa kule*. "Toil" — *śrama*, lit. "hard labour, exhaustion." "With firm resolve" (60) — *dṛṛhabhābe*. "Do not trouble" — *nā karibe udbege*.

[^411-22]: "Placing his hand on [their] heads" (62) — *muṇḍe hasta diẏā*. 63 — in the 1941 edition ॥ ৬৩ ॥. "Divine knowledge" — *dibyajñāna*. "Seeing [all] wandering" (64) — *bane bane bhramaṇa dekhiẏā*: understood as the tigers seeing the travellers wandering. "Clearing the way" — *patha karāiẏā*. "The two brothers" — *dui bhāi*: of the tigers. "Came near a village" (65) — *haila grāme upasana* (= *upasanna*).

[^411-23]: "Morning" — *bihāna* (the editor glosses "বিহান—সকাল," "morning"). "Hundreds of thousands" — *lakṣa lakṣa*: hyperbole.

[^411-24]: "Dear ones" (67) — *bāpu* (note 15). "Manifestation [of power]" (69, 71, 72) — *prakāśa*. "Together with [the whole] town" (69) — *nagara sahite*. "Keep secret" (71) — *kara saṅgopane*.

[^411-25]: "Inviolable" (73) — *alaṅghya*. "The best of gods and men" — *suranaradebamaṇi*, lit. "the jewels [among] suras, men [and] devas." 73–74 — the author's enthusiastic praise; see note 17. "Serpent" (74) — *nāga*. "Became stirred" (75) — *uccāṭana*.

[^411-26]: "Down to the chandalas" (76) — *ācaṇḍāla*. "Utter fools" (77) — *gaṇḍamūrkha*. "Forest country" — *banabhūmi* (cf. 70: *banabhūma*). "By his mercy" (79) — *tā̃'ra anugrahe*: apparently by Rasika's mercy (cf. lahari 10, 67). "Of the qualities, glory [and] fame of Shyamananda [and] Rasika" — *śyāmānanda rasikera guṇa yaśaḥ kīrtta*; it may also be understood as "of Rasika, [the disciple] of Shyamananda."

[^411-27]: "A boundless sea" (80) — *apāra-samudra-līlā*. "In waves of bliss" (81) — *ānanda-kallole*. "A treasury of compassion" (82) — *karuṇānidhāna*. "Of [his] fair glory" (83) — *suyaśaḥ*. "Do not hold [my] faults [against me]" (84) — *doṣa nā laibe*; "setting faults aside" — *doṣa parihari'*. Cf. lahari 9, 73.

[^411-28]: The colophon is; the title as in the heading of the lahari. On Shah Shuja — note 9.


## Lahari 12. The Deliverance of the Lord of the Kols

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; year after year Rasika travels through every land and floods gods and men with love for Krishna; on the way to Nagpur, going through the forest, he and his companions come into the domain of the cruel lord of the Kols, who with a huge host of Kols slays brahmanas, sannyasis, kings and subjects; scouts tell the lord that a wealthy rajaguru is coming with loads of silk and jewels, and he orders the roads blocked, the travellers surrounded with seven rings, and all of them killed at night and their goods taken; Rasika seats his companions around his palanquin and bids them chant the Hari-nama; at night four invisible great beings come to the lord, beat him and bid him fall at Rasika's feet and accept initiation into the Hari-nama; bleeding, he tells this to his kin, comes to Rasika with his whole clan and falls at his feet; Rasika embraces him, he gains divine knowledge and offers praise; Rasika initiates his clan into the Hari-nama, and all sing kirtan and dance; the lord feasts Rasika for several days, gives him gifts and escorts him through the forest; the forest tribes who sacrificed brahmanas to their goddess give up their wicked deeds, build temples and install Deities; Rasika enters Nagpur, and thousands become his disciples*

*The twelfth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^412-1]
*Ghosha: "[My] life is Radhanatha, O, [my] soul is Gopinatha."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of the world,
whose feet's servant is Achyuta's son!

**2.** Thus, in [all his] array, Rasikendra year after year
travels through every land at his own pleasure.

**3.** Nothing has remained [undone] in the deliverance of living beings:
he has flooded gods and men with love for Krishna.[^412-2]

**4.** At this time he went for some days to Nagpur;
I shall tell of it — listen eagerly.

**5.** He goes through the midst of the forest with his companions;
unexpectedly he arrived in the land of a villain.[^412-3]

**6.** The lord of the Kols is very wicked [and] evil;
he slays brahmanas, sannyasis, kings [and] subjects.

**7.** Twenty kahans of Kols go about with him;
whomever he finds there he kills with great delight.

**8.** At his name the forest country trembles;
before him there is no escape for anyone.[^412-4]

**9.** Rasikendra arrived in his domain;
before him the scouts said:

**10.** "With him are hundreds upon hundreds of sadhus, loads of all kinds of goods;
silk, silk cloth, bhot — with him, load upon load.

**11.** He is a great rajaguru in Orissa;
all kinds of jewels, diamonds and gems go with him."

**12.** With these words the scouts persuaded the villain;
hearing it, the villain joyfully says to his own men:[^412-5]

**13.** "All of you, block the roads and the crossings and hold him;
at night I will take all the goods [and] slaughter [them].

**14.** Detain them all quickly,
so that not one of them manages to flee."

**15.** Receiving the order, hundreds upon hundreds of men went in;
surrounding [the travellers] with seven rings, all kept awake.[^412-6]

**16.** Rasikendra heard the whole account;
joyfully he spoke to his companions:

**17.** "All of you, sit down around me;
do not go anywhere, remember Krishna."

**18.** Taking their seats, all sit on [all] four sides;
terror seized all, a great anxiety.

**19.** All say: "Today we have all lost our lives!
In the land of this asura there is no escape for anyone."

**20.** In the Prabhu's heart some unease arose;
he told everyone: "Chant the Hari-nama."[^412-7]

**21.** In the middle, in the palanquin, the Prabhu himself sat,
[and all] around on [all] four sides — like the stars surrounding the moon.

**22.** Again and again they sound the mantra of the Hari-nama;
hearing [this], the men and women were distraught:

**23.** "That Prabhu whose commands are carried out by tigers [and] elephants —
that Prabhu the villain will come and bind!

**24.** That Prabhu whose commands are carried out by gods, asuras [and] men —
that Prabhu has come and fallen into the power of an asura!"[^412-8]

**25.** Women, the old, children [and] youths were distraught;
they remember Krishna, anxious at heart.

**26.** Seated, all joyfully chant the Hari-nama;
a watch of the night passed — [they] did not drink [even] water.[^412-9]

**27.** In his settlement the wicked lord was sitting;
unexpectedly four great beings entered.

**28.** Seizing the villain by the hair, they beat [him] —
with all the punishments there are in the Creator's creation.[^412-10]

**29.** His life rose to his throat; he cries out in terror;
he sees no one — no one is with him.

**30.** He only hears words with his own ears:
"You [meant to] kill Rasika-shekhara!

**31.** [Him,] in fear of whom gods [and] asuras tremble,
whom the people of the three worlds serve, ever [remaining] with him;

**32.** the Prabhu who gave bhakti — love for Krishna,
who expounded bhakti hidden in the Vedas;

**33.** whose glory is renowned among the people of the three worlds,
the giver of prema-bhakti to the poor [and] lowly, down to the chandalas —

**34.** at the feet of such a Prabhu you have committed an offence!
Boundless are [his] beauty [and his] qualities, fathomless his greatness.[^412-11]

**35.** Now, evil one, go [and] fall at [his] feet;
for that reason we have spared your life.

**36.** At the Prabhu's place, all of you become servants of Krishna;
taking initiation into the Hari-nama, become [his] followers."

**37.** As soon as he heard these words with his own ears,
[he was] beaten with all [the punishments] the Creator made.

**38.** Falling to the ground, the wicked evil one cries out;
blood flows ceaselessly over his body [and] from his mouth.[^412-12]

**39.** Kinsmen, subjects and others, wives [and] sons
came and surrounded [him], all amazed at heart.

**40.** He has no strength to speak — he speaks by signs of the hand:
"I do not see [them], yet they beat [and] beat, taking my life."[^412-13]

**41.** Regaining consciousness for a moment, he says to all:
"Many punishments [they] inflicted [on me]; my life burns with pain.

**42.** All that they said I heard with my own ears:
Rasika-Murari Dasa is a second Narayana."[^412-14]

**43.** And all the rest about [his] greatness he told his household:
[that] the three worlds serve Rasika's feet.

**44.** "At such feet I committed an offence;
come, all, let us fall at the Prabhu's lotus feet.

**45.** Not knowing, I committed an offence at those feet —
[the feet] of Rasika-Murari Dasa, the second Narayana."

**46.** Thinking thus, the wicked one went to Rasika;
coming with his whole clan, he fell at [his] feet.

**47.** All around burn ten or twenty torches;
in the bliss of prema [Rasika] is seated, full of attachment to Krishna.

**48.** At that time all say to Rasika:
"The lord of the village has come [and] fallen at [your] feet."

**49.** That greatly fortunate one prostrated himself many times;
[Rasika], rising, embraced him with attachment to Krishna.[^412-15]

**50.** By Rasika's touch divine knowledge came to him;
clasping [his] feet, that fortunate one weeps:

**51.** "Not knowing, in my foolishness I committed an offence;
I am a great sinner, you are a fathomless [ocean] of mercy.

**52.** You, Prabhu, are a sure refuge, the possessor of all virtues;
boundless [are your] beauty [and] virtues, you are an ocean of compassion.

**53.** With my whole clan I have entered the shelter of your feet;
granting devotion to Krishna, Prabhu, protect [us].

**54.** You are the lord of the three worlds, the friend of all;
you are the soul of all people, an ocean of mercy."[^412-16]

**55.** With many [words] the lord of the kingdom offered praise;
hearing the praise, Shyamapati was pleased.[^412-17]

**56.** Granting the Hari-nama, [Rasika] made him a disciple with his whole clan;
all, joyful, danced in the kirtan.

**57.** For five or seven days [the lord] kept [him], falling at [his] feet,
feeding [him] with the nectar of six tastes and more.

**58.** He took leave of the Prabhu, offering many gifts,
[and], going [with him] with his whole clan, led [him] across the forest.[^412-18]

**59.** Thus hundreds of thousands of wicked ones, by the touch of [his] feet,
giving up their wicked deeds, float in the bliss of prema.

**60.** All the low-born, as many as there are in the forest land,
who killed brahmanas for the worship of their chosen goddess —

**61.** the ignorance of all went away by the sight of Rasika;
all people serve the guru, Krishna, the sadhus [and] the brahmanas.

**62.** All built temples, [installed] Sri-murtis and the like;
all began to dance in the sweetness of sankirtana.

**63.** All the forest land sways in love for Krishna;
all became firmly settled [in this, that] Krishna is their own Lord.[^412-19]

**64.** Rasika-shekhara entered Nagpur;
thousands upon thousands became [his] disciples [and] followers.

**65.** King [and] subjects — all were won over by love for Krishna;
day after day [he] held sankirtana in every house.

**66.** All became intoxicated with the sweetness of sankirtana;
all float in the sweetness of prema, finding no end [to it].

**67.** All the pastimes he performed on the circle of the earth,
all the manifestations he showed with delight —

**68.** if one speaks [of them], not even a small part of their account is told.
Listen to the "Rasika-mangala," all friends.

**69.** Without delay will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna
whoever hears this with faith.[^412-20]

**70.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the twelfth lahari, called "The Deliverance of the Lord of the Kols."*[^412-21]

[^412-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("দ্বাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2). The ghosha in the 1941 edition — *jībana rādhānātha / he parāṇa gopīnātha* — is the same as in Pashchima, lahari 2 (note 1) and Uttara, lahari 7 (note 1), and its translation is repeated: Radhanatha ("the Lord of Radha") and Gopinatha ("the Lord of the gopis") are names of Krishna. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥ (§ 7 does not apply). The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে কোলাধিপতির উদ্ধার-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*kolādhipatira uddhāra*), lit. "The Deliverance (Rescue) of the Lord of the Kols." The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^412-2]: "The life of the world" (1) — *jagatajībana*. "In [all his] array" (2) — *hena sāje*: with companions, music and festivals, as described in lahari 11. "At his own pleasure" — *icchāsukhe*. "Nothing has remained [undone]" (3) — *abaśeṣa nāi kichu*.

[^412-3]: Nagpur (4) — apparently Chota Nagpur, the forest plateau west of Medinipur (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 29). "For some days" — *kata dina*. "Eagerly" — *kutūhale*. "In the land of a villain" (5) — *khaṇṭera bhubane*: the editor glosses "খণ্ট—দুষ্ট," "wicked."

[^412-4]: The Kols (*kola*; the editor glosses "কোল—জাতি," "a people, a tribe") — the forest tribes of Chota Nagpur and the neighbouring lands (Munda, Ho and others). "The lord of the Kols" (6) — *kolā adhipati*; his name is not given. "Brahmanas, sannyasis" — *dbijanyāsī*. "Twenty kahans" (7) — *biṃśati kāhana*: a kahan is a count of 1280 (16 pans of 80), i.e. about twenty-five thousand — apparently hyperbole: "a countless host." "With great delight" — *mahāraṅge*. "Trembles" (8) — *kampamān*.

[^412-5]: "In his domain" (9) — *tā'ra nijasthāne*: in the domain of the lord of the Kols. "Scouts" — *dūtagaṇa*. "Silk, silk cloth, bhot" (10) — *pāṭa paṭṭāmbara bhoṭa*: *bhoṭa* — woollen cloth or blankets from Bhot (Tibet, Bhutan). "Load upon load" — *bhāre bhāra*. "Rajaguru" (11) — *rājaguru*, preceptor of kings. "Persuaded" (12) — *bujhāila*.

[^412-6]: "Block the roads and the crossings" (13) — *patha ghāṭa rundhe*; 13 — in the 1941 edition ॥ ১৩ ॥. "Slaughter" — *kariba saṃhāre*. "Manages to flee" (14) — *palā'bāra tare*. "With seven rings" (15) — *sātapurā*: the editor glosses "সাতপুরা—সাতবেড়া," "seven cordons." "Went in" — *prabeśilā*.

[^412-7]: "Sit down" (17) — *karaha āsana*. "Asura" (19) — the lord of the Kols. "Some unease" (20) — *kichu saṅkoca*, lit. "some constraint": understood as concern for his companions.

[^412-8]: "Like the stars surrounding the moon" (21) — *candra beṛi' … yena tārāgaṇe*. "The men and women" (22) — *naranārīgaṇa*: apparently Rasika's companions (cf. 25). 23–24 are understood as their sorrowful words; they may also be taken as the author's. "Fallen into the power of an asura" (24) — *ṭhekila … asuragocara*. The praise of Rasika, whose commands beasts, gods and men obey, is the author's enthusiastic praise (lahari 11, 73–74 and notes 17, 25 there; lahari 10, note 14); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.

[^412-9]: "Women" (25) — *strīri*. "A watch of the night" (26) — *praharek*: a prahara is about three hours. "Did not drink [even] water" — *nāhi jala pāna*.

[^412-10]: "In his settlement" (27) — *nigame*: *nigama* — "town, market settlement"; understood as the lord's seat. "Four great beings" — *cāri mahāmati*, lit. "four of great mind": beings who are invisible (29); the author does not name them. Cf. lahari 10, 54: "in secret the hosts of the gods stay with Rasika." "With all the punishments there are in the Creator's creation" (28) — *yata daṇḍa āchaẏe bidhātāra sṛjana*; likewise 37: *bidhātā sṛjana yata*.

[^412-11]: "His life rose to his throat" (29) — *kaṇṭhagata haila prāṇa*. "You [meant to] kill" (30) — *karibi nidhane*, lit. "you will kill." 31–34 are the words of the invisible beings: enthusiastic praise of Rasika; see note 8. "Ever [remaining] with him" (31) — *saṅge nirantara*. "Hidden in the Vedas" (32) — *bedagopya*. "Down to the chandalas" (33) — *ācaṇḍāla*. "Offence" (34) — *aparādha*: an offence against a Vaishnava.

[^412-12]: "For that reason we have spared your life" (35) — *se kāraṇe tomāra rākhinu nija prāṇe*. "Servants of Krishna" (36) — *kṛṣṇera kiṅkara*. "Initiation into the Hari-nama" — *harināma dīkṣā*. "Followers" — *anucara*. "Blood" (38) — *rudhira*.

[^412-13]: "Wives" (39) — *stīri*. "By signs of the hand" (40) — *hāta ṭhāri*. "I do not see [them]" — the beaters are invisible (29; note 10). "Punishments" (41) — *daṇḍa* (cf. 28, 37). "My life burns" — *prāṇa dahe*.

[^412-14]: "Rasika-Murari Dasa" (42, 45) — *rasikamurāri dāsa*: Rasika; *dāsa* is part of the name ("servant") or "servant [of Krishna]." "A second Narayana" — *dbitī nārāẏaṇa*: so the invisible ones said (30–36), and the lord of the Kols repeats it; cf. lahari 10, 36 and note 14 there; lahari 13, 3, 19. Rapturous praise; see note 8. "His household" (43) — *parijane*. "Let us fall" (44) — *paṛimu*.

[^412-15]: "Torches" (47) — *deuṭī*. "The lord of the village" (48) — *grāma-adhipati*: the lord of the Kols (6); in 55, "the lord of the kingdom" (*rājya-adhipati*). "That greatly fortunate one" (49) — *sei mahābhāge*. "Prostrated himself" — *daṇḍabata kailā*. "Embraced" — *kola dila*.

[^412-16]: "In my foolishness" (51) — *mūṛhapaṇe*. "A sure refuge" (52) — *śaraṇapañjara*, literally "a sheltering cage." "Have entered the shelter" (53) — *paśinu śaraṇa*. The lord's praise (52–54: "lord of the three worlds," "the soul of all people") is the rapturous praise of a convert; see note 8.

[^412-17]: "The lord of the kingdom" (55) — *rājya-adhipati*, the same lord of the Kols. Shyamapati — "the lord (husband) of Shyama": apparently Rasika as the husband of Shyamadasi (Dakshina, lahari 1); the epithet is unusual in the poem.

[^412-18]: "Kept [him]" (57) — *rākhe*. "The nectar of six tastes" — *ṣaṛarasa amṛtādi*. "Took leave" (58) — *bidāẏa kailā*. "Led [him] across the forest" — *araṇya karilā pāra*, literally "brought across the forest".

[^412-19]: "The low-born" (60) — *antyajāti*. "Their chosen goddess" — *iṣṭadebī*: apparently a local goddess of the forest tribes; "killed brahmanas" — *brāhmaṇahiṃsana*: according to the author, for her worship (cf. 6: the lord of the Kols kills brahmanas). "Ignorance" (61) — *abidyā*. "Built temples, [installed] Sri-murtis" (62) — *debālaẏa śrīmūrttyādi … karilā*. "Sways" (63) — *ḍhalāḍhali*. "Became firmly settled" — *dārḍhya karila*.

[^412-20]: Nagpur (64) — Chota Nagpur (note 3). "Were won over" (65) — *baśa haila*. "Finding no end [to it]" (66) — *nāhi pāẏa ora*. "Manifestations" (67) — *parakāśa*. "A small part of their account" (68) — *kichu bibaraṇa*. "With faith" (69) — *śraddhā kari'*.

[^412-21]: The colophon is: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে কোলাধিপতির উদ্ধার-নাম দ্বাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*kolādhipatira uddhāra*). Lahari 12 ends (॥70॥ — the author's signature).


## Lahari 13. The Ending of the Drought in Shekharabhumi

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika comes to Shekharabhumi, and the king, honouring him as a second Narayana, begs for help: for three years there has been no rain, and for want of water the subjects are leaving for other villages; Rasika bids him hold a great festival and gather the sadhus; during the sankirtana and the feasting of the sadhus he commands King Indra to send rain, and clouds cover the sky over Shekhara: a downpour fills the ponds and reservoirs, and in the month of Magha the rivers flood; the king recognizes Rasika as a second Narayana; the author glorifies Rasika, who never stays at home even for a moment but travels to deliver living beings, weeps with love for Krishna, speaks of Krishna to the pandits and spreads sankirtana and prema-bhakti in every land of Utkala*

*The thirteenth lahari.*

*Raga Varadi.*[^413-1]
*Ghosha: "O treasury of mercy, O compassionate Shyama!*
*Turn Your attention to the fallen, afflicted people."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy,
whose beloved follower is Rasikendra-chandra!

**2.** From there the Prabhu went to Shekharabhumi;
arriving, the Prabhu stayed at the king's palace.[^413-2]

**3.** The king with his whole clan rejoiced;
he honoured Rasika as a second Narayana.[^413-3]

**4.** Falling at [his] feet, the king makes a plea:
"For three years no rain has fallen here.

**5.** What offence has been committed against the sadhus?
What have the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus resolved [against us]?

**6.** That is why no rain falls in this village;
for want of water the king [and] subjects are exhausted.

**7.** Great dread has seized all the subjects;
for want of water all are leaving [the village] for other villages.[^413-4]

**8.** This is [my] plea, Prabhu, at your feet:
command King Indra [that] he send rain."[^413-5]

**9.** Hearing the king's words, Rasikendra says:
"Hold a great festival, gather the sadhus in crowds.

**10.** When the festival begins, rain will come."
Receiving the command, [the king] began the supreme sacrifice.[^413-6]

**11.** Day and night they began the sankirtana;
with care they honoured the guru, Krishna, the sadhus [and] the brahmanas.

**12.** The sadhus partake of food of six tastes;
on every side all remember Krishna.[^413-7]

**13.** Rasikendra commanded King Indra:
"Send abundant rain on all four sides of the village."

**14.** By [that] command, suddenly the clouds,
encircling the bounds of Shekhara, covered the sky.

**15.** A terrible downpour fell [through all] the fourth prahara;
ponds, reservoirs [and] embankment tanks quickly filled.

**16.** In the month of Magha the rivers, canals and other [waters] flooded;
the clouds, vying with one another, sent much rain.[^413-8]

**17.** Such is the command of Rasikendra-chandra:
gods, asuras, men [and] beasts carry [it] out with all their might.

**18.** All were amazed, seeing [this] manifestation;
all Rasika's servants rejoiced.[^413-9]

**19.** The king honoured [his] feet in many ways;
he knew Rasikendra to be a second Narayana:

**20.** "To deliver living beings the Prabhu has taken birth;
by great fortune I have seen this treasure — [his] feet."[^413-10]

**21.** Thus Rasikendra in every land, land after land,
in [all] four directions made devotion to Krishna manifest.

**22.** Not for a moment does he stay in his own house;
for the deliverance of living beings he wanders.

**23.** In every land he spread sankirtana;
granting prema-bhakti for Krishna, he delivered [people].

**24.** Rasikendra constantly weeps with love for Krishna;
in hundreds of streams [tears] flow from Rasika's eyes.

**25.** Over his whole body — pulaka, his speech is always faltering;
the people of the three worlds are enchanted, seeing [his] form.

**26.** The eight sattvika-bhavas are always manifest;
in love for Krishna he constantly delights in [its] play.[^413-11]

**27.** In whatever direction the Prabhu goes, all [go] in that direction;
all the dharmas always move with Rasika.

**28.** Rasikendra speaks of Krishna to all people;
surrounding [him] on every side, crowds of pandits listen.

**29.** Hearing the speech of [his] holy mouth, all are overwhelmed;
no one is able to answer [him].

**30.** Hearing the words of the holy mouth, like nectar —
hearing that sweet speech, [all] find solace of heart.[^413-12]

**31.** Weeping and weeping, he tells of Krishna;
hearing [it], the pandits roll on the ground.

**32.** He delivered the three worlds, granting prema-bhakti;
in love for Krishna he always wanders, roaming [everywhere].

**33.** To whatever land the Prabhu Rasika-shekhara comes,
all [there] gain countless treasures, intoxicated with joy.

**34.** No one lets [him] go, [all] hold [him] back with care;
when the Prabhu leaves that place, all are dying with weeping.

**35.** Thus all the lands constantly think
of Rasika's feet, in remembrance [and] meditation.

**36.** Thus he delivered the earth —
the son of Achyuta, [possessed] of boundless beauty [and] virtues.[^413-13]

**37.** He spread an unheard-of devotion to Krishna;
for all, Krishna alone [became] the refuge.

**38.** All people became filled with prema-bhakti for Krishna;
the evil desires of all people were destroyed.[^413-14]

**39.** Glory, glory to Rasika-shekhara, the jewel of virtues,
by the touch of whose feet the earth rejoices!

**40.** He performed many pastimes in the land of Utkala —
they cannot be described, even if one describes with a hundred mouths.

**41.** By his grace I have told a little;
all listen to the "Rasika-mangala" with attention.

**42.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the thirteenth lahari, called "The Ending of the Drought in Shekharabhumi."*[^413-15]

[^413-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Varadi (*barāṛī*; Purva, lahari 8, note 2); the ghosha is the same as in Pashchima, lahari 9 (note 1), and its translation is repeated: *kṛpānidhi he daẏāra śyāma / patita durgati jane kara abadhāna*. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে শেখরভূমিতে অনাবৃষ্টি-নিবারণ-নাম ত্রয়োদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śekharabhūmite anābṛṣṭi-nibāraṇa*).

[^413-2]: "Rasikendra-chandra" (1) — "the moon of Rasikendras," Rasika. "Beloved follower" — *priẏa anucara*. "From there" (2) — from Nagpur (lahari 12, 64). Shekharabhumi (*śekharabhūmi*; in 14, "Shekhara") — apparently Shikharbhum, the domain of the Shikhara rajas (Panchakot, in the present Purulia district, West Bengal); the identification is tentative, and the king is not named. "Stayed" — *utarilā*; "at the palace" — *bāṛīte*, "at the house."

[^413-3]: "As a second Narayana" (3) — *dbitī nārāẏaṇa sama*; likewise in 19; in 20 the king says: "To deliver living beings the Prabhu has taken birth." This is rapturous praise: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasika is a devotee, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation (lahari 10, note 14; lahari 12, notes 8, 14); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "With his whole clan" — *sagoṣṭhī sahite*.

[^413-4]: "Three years" (4) — *tina sambatsara*. "Against the sadhus" (5) — *sādhujana-sthāne*: the king thinks the drought is the result of an offence against sadhus. "Resolved" — *kibā karilena mane*, literally "what have [they] set in mind." "Exhausted" (6) — *bikala*. "Leaving [the village]" (7) — *chāṛi'*.

[^413-5]: "King Indra" (8, 13) — *indrarāja*: Indra, the king of heaven, who commands the rain. Indra and the other demigods are servants of the Lord; that Indra carries out Rasika's command (13–17; cf. lahari 11, 74) is the author's way of glorifying the power of a devotee (note 3; lahari 12, note 8). "Send rain" — *kare bariṣaṇe*.

[^413-6]: "In crowds" (9) — *bṛnda bṛnda*. "The supreme sacrifice" (10) — *parameṣṭi*: understood as *parama iṣṭi*, "supreme sacrifice (worship)," i.e. the festival itself (11–12); *parameṣṭhī* is also a name of Brahma, which does not fit here. The reading and sense are unclear. The subject is not named — apparently the king.

[^413-7]: "Food of six tastes" (12) — *ṣaṛarasa* (cf. lahari 12, 57). "Partake" — *bhojana kariẏā*. "Remember" — *saṅaraṇa*.

[^413-8]: "Suddenly" (14) — *ācambite*. "The bounds of Shekhara" — *śekharera sīmā* (note 2). "The fourth prahara" (15) — *caturtha prahara*: a prahara is about three hours; possibly "[all] four praharas," i.e. a whole day. "Reservoirs" — *taṛāga*; "embankment tanks" — *bānda* (*bā̃dh*, a pond or reservoir with an embankment). Magha (16) — January–February, the dry season. "Canals" — *khāla*. "Vying with one another" — *bādābādi* (lahari 11, note 3).

[^413-9]: "With all their might" (17) — *prāṇapaṇe*. "Manifestation" (18) — *parakāśa*.

[^413-10]: "In many ways" (19) — *bahurūpe*. "This treasure — [his] feet" (20) — *e caraṇadhana*. On "has taken birth" — note 3.

[^413-11]: "Not for a moment" (22) — *eka tila*, literally "not for a sesame seed." "In his own house" — *āpana mandire*. Pulaka (25) — the hairs standing on end in ecstasy. "Faltering speech" — *gada gada bāṇī*. The eight sattvika-bhavas (26) — lahari 6, note 26. "Delights in [its] play" — *karena bilāsa*.

[^413-12]: "All the dharmas" (27) — *sarbba dharma*: understood as "all virtues [and] righteousness." "Overwhelmed" (29) — *jara jara* (lahari 10, note 12). "Find solace of heart" (30) — *juṛāẏa parāṇa*, literally "the life is cooled (soothed)."

[^413-13]: "Roll on the ground" (31) — *loṭāẏa dharaṇī*. "Countless treasures" (33) — *koṭī nidhi*, literally "ten million treasures." "With care" (34) — *yatna kari'*. "Are dying with weeping" — *mare sabe jhuri*: figuratively, they pine with grief. "Think" (35) — *bhābe*; "in remembrance [and] meditation" — *smaraṇe dhiẏāne*. "The son of Achyuta" (36) — *acyuta-kumāra*, Rasika.

[^413-14]: "Unheard-of" (37) — *asambhaba*, literally "impossible." "Krishna alone [became] the refuge" — *ananyaśaraṇa kṛṣṇe*. "Evil desires" (38) — *durbbāsanā*.

[^413-15]: The colophon is (note 1). Lahari 13 ends (॥42॥ — the author's signature); below a rule, lahari 14 begins.


## Lahari 14. The Receiving by Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu, in a Dream, of the Command of Sri Sri Bhagavan to Depart to Krishna's Abode, at Bhograi

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika visits Kendubilva, the place of Jayadeva, Vishnupur and Ambuya, goes round the holy places on both banks of the Ganga and every year goes to Nilachala for the Ratha-yatra; in every land he spreads the talk of Krishna, service to the guru, Krishna, the sadhus and the brahmanas, and kirtan, and on the road Sri Chaitanya travelled he performs worship; his daily and nightly routine is described by dandas; every year he celebrates twelve festivals, and all Utkala takes refuge in Krishna; one day in seclusion Rasika reflects that Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates have disappeared, and Shyamananda and the mahantas too have departed, and resolves to return to his own abode, to Krishna in Vrindavana; he reveals this to those close to him and tells two of them — Gopijanavallabha and Tulasi — that at Bhograi after sankirtana, as he was pondering a book with closed eyes, the youthful Shyama with a flute appeared to him and bade him depart, and when he hesitated, angrily repeated the command three times; they fall to the ground, and Rasika, embracing them, says that he will always remain with them*

*The fourteenth lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^414-1]
*Ghosha: "It remains to proclaim the qualities of the moon Gauranga."*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy,
whose own servant from birth is the son of Achyuta![^414-2]

**2.** At that time Rasikendra [passed] through Kendubilva;
seeing the place of Jayadeva, he became absorbed in bhava.

**3.** Viewing Vishnupur with delight for some days,
Rasika came to Ambuya to bathe in the Ganga.[^414-3]

**4.** He wanders, visiting the holy places on both banks of the Ganga;
he sees Sri Chaitanya-chand [and] Nityananda-raya.

**5.** All the holy places of the mahantas that were on both banks
Rasika-shekhara viewed with joy in his heart.[^414-4]

**6.** From there Rasikendra came in haste [to Nilachala];
every year he sees Jagannatha on the chariot.

**7.** Every year, going to the abode of Nilachala,
the son of Achyuta performs many pastimes.

**8.** Every year he made festival pilgrimages;
for twelve months [of the year] he always wanders, renowned in the world.[^414-5]

**9.** In every land he joyfully spread the talk of Krishna,
service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus, the "Bhagavata" [and] the "Gita."

**10.** Service to the brahmanas, service to the sadhus, the spreading of kirtan —
in every land he widely spread this dharma.

**11.** Love for Krishna, the sixty-four [limbs] of bhakti and the rest
Rasika-Murari makes manifest in every land.[^414-6]

**12.** Not for one day does he know anything other than Krishna;
night and day Rasika always meditates on Krishna.

**13.** In the houses of all [his] disciples, [their] disciples' disciples [and] brothers
Rasikendra always dances in sankirtana.[^414-7]

**14.** [On the road] by which Sri Chaitanya-chandra went to Jagannatha and back —
on that road Rasikendra performs worship in many ways.[^414-8]

**15.** Somewhere he worships, somewhere he rolls [on the ground],
somewhere in sankirtana tears flow.[^414-9]

**16.** Service to Krishna, worship of Krishna, sankirtana of Krishna;
ceaselessly he listens to talks about Krishna.

**17.** In the morning — darshan of the mangala-arati;
for two dandas Prabhu meets with the Vaishnavas.[^414-10]

**18.** Then for four dandas he reads stotras, [scriptures] and so on;
bathing, worship of the Deity, remembrance and so on — four dandas.

**19.** Then two dandas — meditation in great absorption in bhava;
then four dandas — immersed in the rasa of the *Bhagavata*.

**20.** Then for two dandas he has the sadhus fed;
then for six dandas he hears the Puranas.

**21.** Then six dandas — with his circle, in the rasa of song:
Jayadeva's *Gita-govinda* and other works, in endless variety.[^414-11]

**22.** Thus he spends the day in the rasa of Krishna;
as evening comes, Prabhu beholds the arati.

**23.** For two dandas of the night he converses with the Vaishnavas;
eight dandas of the night — the delight of kirtan.

**24.** Then six dandas of the night — a gathering for music:
various instruments, various songs, wondrous tales.

**25.** From various lands skilled people come and stay [with him];
joyfully Prabhu listens to the singing of all.[^414-12]

**26.** Two dandas at night — the feeding of the sadhus;
together with the sadhus he joyfully eats.

**27.** Then for six dandas of the night he reads the *Bhagavata*,
sitting on his asana in seclusion, entirely alone.

**28.** Then for six dandas of the night he chants the Hari-nama;
resting in yoga-nidra, he ever meditates on Krishna.[^414-13]

**29.** Day and night, in every moment when there is leisure —
ceaselessly the Hari-nama, with eyes full of tears.

**30.** Always he chants the Hari-nama, holding the knots in his hand;
on roads and at landings he wanders, chanting the Hari-nama.[^414-14]

**31.** Day and night there is no rest [for him], not for a moment;
apart from Krishna, Rasika knows nothing.

**32.** Ceaselessly his mind is intoxicated with the rasa of sankirtana;
ceaselessly he explains to all the truth about Krishna.

**33.** Ceaselessly he travels for the sake of living beings;
freeing all from ignorance, he bestowed prema [on them].

**34.** He destroyed the evil desires of all people;
all people became intoxicated with prema-bhakti for Krishna.

**35.** To all the wicked, as many as there were in the whole world,
he proclaimed prema-bhakti in their hearts.

**36.** The moon of Rasikendras, whose vow is to destroy adharma,
establishes dharma with joy in his heart,

**37.** as Krishna, descending age after age,
establishes the sadhus, destroying the wicked.[^414-15]

**38.** Such a mahashaya, the crown jewel of Rasikendras,
destroying their sins, made everyone a sadhu.[^414-16]

**39.** Many lilas he performed in the world;
he distributed love for Krishna in every single home.

**40.** The mantra of Krishna, the tantra of Krishna, initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna and so on,
the essence [and] meaning of the Vedas and shastras that are well known —

**41.** with the consent of all the shastras, drawing out [their] essence,
he preached exclusive bhakti for Krishna.

**42.** All the bhakti that the scriptures have described for the good of living beings —
all that bhakti the son of Achyuta revealed.[^414-17]

**43.** Nothing more remained [to be done] in accomplishing bhakti;
the whole world became filled with love for Krishna.

**44.** The forest land of Utkala overflowed [with prema];
all understood: all [else] is false, Krishna is the true Lord.

**45.** Twelve festivals every year
Rasika-shekhara celebrated in great bliss.[^414-18]

**46.** All the kings and subjects there are in Orissa —
disciples, disciples of disciples [and] servants [of his] in every home.

**47.** Day and night they hold festivals everywhere;
with all their might they serve guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus.

**48.** Nothing remained with which to gladden [the world further]:
all in the land of Utkala had taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna].[^414-19]

**49.** One day Rasika-mahashaya, sitting in seclusion,
reflected in his heart:

**50.** by the word of all the sadhus [he] came to Bharata;
dispelling ignorance, [he] made all people sadhus.[^414-20]

**51.** [He] sees: the whole world has taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna];
in the hearts of children, the old [and] the young — the preaching [of] Krishna.[^414-21]

**52.** Women, men, and even the low-born [and] the Pukkashas,
Hunas, Pulindas and others, mlecchas, yavanas, rakshasas,

**53.** brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras and others, as many [as there are] —
all, having taken exclusive shelter, are intoxicated with love for Krishna.[^414-22]

**54.** Apart from the jubilant clamour [of the name] of Krishna, nothing else is heard;
the whole world floats in the bliss of love for Krishna.

**55.** "I do not know what the terrible [age of] Kali will do at some time;
apart from this happiness, I see nothing else with my eyes."[^414-23]

**56.** Service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus, festivals [and] processions
for sixty-two years [he] performed — renowned in the world.

**57.** Having come to earth, [he] took the shelter of Krishna;
in the bliss of love for Krishna he passed the time.[^414-24]

**58.** "Chaitanya Gosani, Nityananda, Advaita and others —
all have disappeared, [and with Them] Their associates, intimates, those who took refuge [in Them] and others.[^414-25]

**59.** Now [both] Shyamananda Prabhu [and] the host of mahantas —
before my eyes they have all departed.

**60.** Now, I understand, the terrible [age of] Kali will manifest:
all the sadhus have left [their] pastimes on earth.[^414-26]

**61.** I too shall go to my own place;
I shall go [and] see with my eyes Sri Nandanandana —

**62.** the Lord of Sri Radhika's life, Bhagavan Himself;
Krishna together with the maidens of Vraja I shall see with my eyes:

**63.** in Vrindavana, on the bank of the Yamuna, in the forest groves,
at the foot of the wish-fulfilling tree, Krishna on a throne of jewels —

**64.** bent in three places, graceful, Shyama, all-enchanting,
the youthful adolescent — between Radha and Chandravali.

**65.** Throng after throng the maidens of Vraja serve [Him] always;
the land [there] is chintamani, [that] abode cannot be described.[^414-27]

**66.** In such an abode I shall enjoy pastimes with Krishna;
I shall leave this body — this earthly dwelling — this very day."[^414-28]

**67.** Thus in seclusion [he] ponders all this in his mind;
the son of Achyuta disclosed [it] to those close to him.[^414-29]

**68.** Hearing this, all [felt as if] struck on the head by a thunderbolt;
rolling on the ground, they weep before Prabhu.[^414-30]

**69.** Prabhu says: "Gopijanavallabha [and] Tulasi!
More than life I love you all.[^414-31]

**70.** Birth after birth you all are dear to me;
many pastimes [you have] performed [with me] in the land of Utkala.

**71.** Whatever plans there were in my mind —
without your company I carry [them] out no longer.[^414-32]

**72.** Therefore I tell one thing to you two:
today, sitting in seclusion, I was pondering a book.

**73.** After the sankirtana, in that place, at Bhograi,
pondering the book, [I] was sitting with closed eyes.[^414-33]

**74.** A form [the colour] of a fresh cloud, a youthful adolescent,
in His hand an enchanting flute, beautiful to behold.

**75.** Coming before me, He spoke a word:
'The command [is given]: Rasikendra, depart!'[^414-34]

**76.** Absorbed in the taste of pondering the book, I delayed;
then, growing angry, He spoke a word:

**77.** 'You do not heed the command, Rasika-mahashaya!
To Krishna's abode, to your own place, set out!'[^414-35]

**78.** Commanding thus, He vanished,
and I, as if in a dream-trance, seemed to part with life.

**79.** This command was given to me at the end of the night:
again and again, three times He commanded insistently."[^414-36]

**80.** Hearing these words, both fell to the ground;
smiling, the jewel of Rasikendras speaks the truth [to them].

**81.** Embracing [them], Prabhu says: "Listen, you two:
I am always with you."[^414-37]

**82.** Nothing can be described of Rasika's life:
having descended, he purified the earth.

**83.** He delivered the three worlds by the mercy of [his] feet —
Rasikendra-raya, whose vow is to be a sheltering enclosure.[^414-38]

**84.** [His] pastimes are a boundless ocean, they cannot be described;
in brief I have described [them] by the mercy of his feet.

**85.** Listen to the "Rasika-mangala," all you sadhus:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of loving devotion to Krishna.[^414-39]

**86.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Receiving by Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu, in a Dream, of the Command of Sri Sri Bhagavan to Depart to Krishna's Abode, at Bhograi."*[^414-40]

[^414-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Karuna-shri (*karuṇāśrī*; Purva, lahari 1, note 8; Dakshina, lahari 1, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Purva, lahari 2 (note 1), and its translation is repeated: *gaurāṅga-cā̃dera guṇa rahilā ghoṣite*. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে ভোগরাইতে কৃষ্ণধামে গমনে শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ প্রভু প্রতি স্বপ্নাবেশে শ্রীশ্রীভগবদাদেশ-প্রাপ্তি-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*bhogarāite kṛṣṇadhāme gamane śrīśrīrasikānanda prabhu prati sbapnābeśe śrīśrībhagabadādeśa-prāpti*); "to depart to Krishna's abode" — *kṛṣṇadhāme gamane*, literally "concerning going to Krishna's abode"; "in a dream" — *sbapnābeśe*, "in a dream vision"; "at Bhograi" — apparently where Rasika received the command. Bhograi — a locality in the present Balasore district (Orissa), near the mouth of the Suvarnarekha. The summary line covers the whole lahari.

[^414-2]: "The son of Achyuta" (1) — *acyuta-kuṅara* (*kũar*, "prince, son"), Rasika. "Own servant from birth" — *nija bhṛtya janma*; it can also be understood as "whose own servant is the one born [as] the son of Achyuta."

[^414-3]: Kendubilva (*kendubilba*, 2) — Kenduli on the Ajay river (Birbhum district), the birthplace of Jayadeva, the author of the "Gita-govinda." "Became absorbed in bhava" — *bhābābeśa haiẏā*. Vishnupur (3) — Bishnupur (Bankura district), the capital of Mallabhum, the kingdom of Vira Hambira, a disciple of Shrinivasa Acharya. "With delight" — *kautuke*. Ambuya (*āmbuẏā*) — Ambika (Kalna) and its surroundings (Purva, lahari 2, note 8). "Came" — *bije kailā*.

[^414-4]: "Holy places" (4, 5) — *pāṭa* (shripat): places connected with Mahaprabhu's associates and their descendants. "He sees Sri Chaitanya-chand [and] Nityananda-raya" — apparently the darshan of the Deities of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda (cf. Ambika — Purva, lahari 2, note 8). The mahantas (5) — Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37.

[^414-5]: "Came in haste" (6) — *āilā tbarite*: apparently to Nilachala (Puri; 7). "On the chariot" — at the Ratha-yatra (lahari 10). "Festival pilgrimages" (8) — *mahotsaba-yātrā*. "Renowned in the world" — *jagata-bikhyātā*: it may also refer to the festivals ("renowned in the world").

[^414-6]: "Joyfully spread" (9) — *pramoda karila*. The "Bhagavata" [and] the "Gita" — the "Srimad-Bhagavatam" and the "Bhagavad-gita" (their reading and exposition). "The sixty-four [limbs] of bhakti" (11) — *catuḥṣaṣṭi bhakti*: the 64 limbs (angas) of sadhana-bhakti (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 25).

[^414-7]: "Not for one day" (12) — *ekadina … nāhi*. "Disciples' disciples" (13) — *anuśiṣya*. "Brothers" — *bhāi*: brothers in faith or brothers by birth. "In the houses" — *mandire*.

[^414-8]: *jagannātha gatāgate śrīcaitanya-candra / bahurūpe se pathe pūjena rasikendra*: understood to mean that on the road by which Sri Chaitanya went to Puri to Jagannatha and back (through Remuna, Jajpur and other places; CC, Madhya 5, 16), Rasika performs worship in many ways — apparently at the places of Mahaprabhu's pastimes. It can also be understood as "on that road Rasikendra worships Sri Chaitanya-chandra in many ways."

[^414-9]: "Rolls [on the ground]" — *gaṛi bule*. "Tears flow" — *bahe aśrujale*.

[^414-10]: 17–28 give Rasika's daily and nightly routine. A danda (*daṇḍa*) is 24 minutes, 1/60 of a day and night. By day: 2 (17) + 4 + 4 (18) + 2 + 4 (19) + 2 + 6 (20) + 6 (21) = 30 dandas; by night: 2 + 8 (23) + 6 (24) + 2 (26) + 6 (27) + 6 (28) = 30 dandas; together exactly 60 dandas, a full day and night. "Darshan of the mangala-arati" (17) — *maṅgala-ārati daraśana*: the morning arati to the Deity. "Meets with the Vaishnavas" — *baiṣṇaba-milana*.

[^414-11]: "Stotras, [scriptures] and so on" (18) — *staba pāṭha-ādi*, lit. "stotras, reading and so on." "Worship of the Deity" — *debārccanā*. "Remembrance" — *smaraṇa*: remembrance of Krishna's lilas. "In great absorption in bhava" (19) — *mahā-bhābābeśe*. "Has the sadhus fed" (20) — *sādhu karāẏa bhojana*. "With his circle" (21) — *goṣṭhī*. "Jayadeva's *Gita-govinda* and other works" — *jaẏadeba ādi grantha*, lit. "Jayadeva and other books": the songs of the *Gita-govinda*. "In endless variety" — *aśeṣa biśeṣe*.

[^414-12]: "Spends" (22) — *gũẏāi*. "As evening comes" — *sandhyā parabeśe*: the evening arati. "Converses with the Vaishnavas" (23) — *baiṣṇaba-sambhāṣa*. "The delight of kirtan" — *kīrttana-bilāsa*. "A gathering for music" (24) — *saṅgīta-milana*. "Wondrous tales" — *adbhuta kathana*. "Skilled people" (25) — *guṇī jana*: musicians and singers.

[^414-13]: "Joyfully" (26) — *kutuhale*. "In seclusion" (27) — *nigame* (Purva, lahari 16, note 21); likewise in 49. "Entirely alone" — *ekeśbara mātra*. "Resting in yoga-nidra" (28) — *yoganidrā abalambe*: the routine leaves no time for ordinary sleep; the author apparently means that Rasika's sleep is meditation on Krishna.

[^414-14]: "Holding the knots in his hand" (30) — *granthi dhari' kare*: apparently counting the names on a cord with knots (*granthi*, "knot"). "On roads and at landings" — *pathe ghāṭe*: everywhere.

[^414-15]: "The truth about Krishna" (32) — *kṛṣṇatattba*. "Freeing all from ignorance" (33) — *abidyā chāṛiẏā sabā*, lit. "making all give up ignorance (avidya)." "Evil desires" (34) — *durbbāsanā*. "In their hearts" (35) — *sabā hṛde*, "in the hearts of all". "Whose vow is to destroy adharma" (36) — *adharmmadhbaṃsana-bānā*; *bānā* — "vow, sign" (Dakshina, lahari 15, note 26). 36–37 echo *Bhagavad-gita* 4.7–8 (*paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām / dharma-saṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge*). The comparison of Rasika with the descending Krishna is the author's enthusiastic praise (on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11); and Rasika's "destruction of the wicked" is their transformation: the wicked become sadhus (35, 38); cf. the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai by Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda (CB, Madhya 13).

[^414-16]: "Mahashaya" — *mahāśaẏa*. "The crown jewel of Rasikendras" — *rasikendracūṛāmaṇi*.

[^414-17]: "The essence [and] meaning of the Vedas and shastras that are well known" (40) — *bedaśāstra-tattba artha ye āche prasiddhi*. "With the consent of all the shastras" (41) — *sarbbaśāstra sanmati*; "drawing out the essence" — *sāroddhāra*. "Exclusive bhakti" — *ananya bhakti*. "For the good of living beings" (42) — *prāṇihite*.

[^414-18]: "Overflowed [with prema]" (44) — *ḍhalaḍhala hailā*, lit. "swayed, brimmed over." "The forest land of Utkala" — *utkala banabhūmi*. "Twelve festivals" (45) — *duẏādaśa mahotsaba*: twelve festivals or a twelve-day festival.

[^414-19]: "In Orissa" (46) — *uṛiṣyā bhitare*. "Disciples of disciples" — *anuśiṣya*. "With all their might" (47) — *prāṇapaṇe*. "Nothing remained with which to gladden [the world further]" (48) — *abaśeṣa nāhi kichu pramoda karite*: *pramoda* — "joy, rejoicing" (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 26; cf. 9 and note 6: *pramoda karila*, "joyfully spread"); the sense is apparently that nothing and nowhere remained to which [bhakti] could still be joyfully spread (cf. 43). "Had taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna]" — *ananya-śaraṇa*.

[^414-20]: With 49 begin Rasika's reflections: the world is full of love for Krishna, the Lord's associates and Shyamananda have already departed — it is time for him, too, to go to his own abode. 50 is in the third person (*āilā*, *kailā*), so no quotation marks are used here. "By the word of all the sadhus" — *sādhu sabāra bacane*: understood as "by the word (command) of all the sadhus"; it may also be read as a general statement: "a sadhu comes to Bharata — by the word of all — and, dispelling ignorance, makes everyone a sadhu," i.e. about the purpose of sadhus. Bharata — *bhārata*, India, the earthly world.

[^414-21]: Continuation of lahari 14. begins with the complete couplet ॥51॥; no couplet carries over from. 51 continues Rasika's reflections (49–50, note 20). "[He] sees" — *dekhi'*, lit. "seeing." "Has taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna]" — *ananyaśaraṇa* (note 19). "The preaching [of] Krishna" — *kṛṣṇa paracāra*.

[^414-22]: 52–53 echo *Bhagavatam* 2.4.18 (*kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pukkaśā ... śudhyanti*): by taking shelter of the Lord even the lowest are purified. "Women" — *strīri*. "The low-born" — *antyaja*; the Pukkashas (*pukkaśa*) — a tribe counted among the lowest; Hunas and Pulindas — tribes; mlecchas — barbarians outside the Vedic order; yavanas — foreigners, here apparently Muslims; "rakshasas" (*rākṣasa*) — apparently cruel, savage people. "Intoxicated" — *matta*.

[^414-23]: "The jubilant clamour [of the name] of Krishna" (54) — *kṛṣṇakolāhala*. "Floats" — *bhāse*. 55 is in the first person (*nā jāni*, *nā dekhi*): here Rasika's words to himself begin; 56–57 are again in the third person (*kaila*, *karilā*), the author's words, so the quotation marks close after 55 and open again at 58 (*ibe bujhi*, "now, I understand"; *āmio*, "I too"), running to 66. "The terrible [age of] Kali" — *ghora kali*. "At some time" — *kakhane*. "This happiness" — *ei sukha*: the world full of love for Krishna (51–54).

[^414-24]: "Festivals [and] processions" (56) — *mahotsaba-yātrā*. "Sixty-two years" — *bāṣaṭṭi batsara*: the length of Rasikananda's life (1590–1652); in lahari 15, 37 — "sixty-two years and four months." "Renowned in the world" — *jagata bikhyātā*. "Having come to earth" (57) — *bhūmigata haiẏā*, lit. "having fallen to the ground," i.e. from his very birth. "Passed the time" — *kāla karilā haraṇa*.

[^414-25]: "Have disappeared" (58) — *gupta hailā*: the departure of the Lord and His associates is a disappearance from the manifest lila. "Their associates, intimates, those who took refuge [in Them]" — *sāṅgopāṅgāśraya*: *sāṅgopāṅga*, lit. "with limbs and sub-limbs," i.e. with the closest associates and their followers; *āśraya* — those who took refuge [in Them]; the same expression is in lahari 16, 5.

[^414-26]: "The host of mahantas" (59) — *mohāntera gaṇa*. "Before my eyes" — *dekhite dekhite*, lit. "while [I] was watching," i.e. one after another and quickly. On Shyamananda's departure — Pashchima, lahari 13. "Have departed" — *karilā gamana*. "Pastimes on earth" (60) — *pṛthibī-bilāsa*.

[^414-27]: "My own place" (61) — *āpanā sthāne*: the eternal abode (cf. 77: *nijasthāne*). Nandanandana — "the son of Nanda," Krishna. "The Lord of Sri Radhika's life" (62) — *śrīrādhikā-prāṇapati*; "Bhagavan Himself" — *sbaẏaṃ bhagabān*. "The maidens of Vraja" — *brajāṅganā*. "On the bank of the Yamuna, in the forest groves" (63) — *yamunā pulina kuñjabane*. "Bent in three places" (64) — *tribhaṅga*. Chandravali — the leader of the group of gopis rivalling Radha; pre-eminence among the gopis belongs to Radha (cf. 62). "Throng after throng" (65) — *yūtha yūtha*: a yutha is a group of gopis under a leader. "The land is chintamani" — *bhūmi cintāmaṇi*: the land of Vrindavana is made of wish-fulfilling chintamani stones; cf. *Brahma-samhita* 5.56 (*bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayī*), which also names the wish-fulfilling trees (63).

[^414-28]: "I shall enjoy pastimes" (66) — *kariba bilāsa*. "I shall leave this body" — *chāṛiba e deha* (so in the text). "This earthly dwelling" — *pṛthibīnibāsa*: understood as in apposition to "body"; it can also be read "I shall leave ... my life on earth." In the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding the departure of an associate of the Lord is not an end under the rule of karma but a passage into the eternal (unmanifest) lila. "This very day" — *āji*.

[^414-29]: "In seclusion" (67) — *nigame* (note 13). "To those close to him" — *ātmagaṇe*. The son of Achyuta is Rasika.

[^414-30]: "Struck on the head by a thunderbolt" (68) — *muṇḍe haila bajrāghāta*. "Rolling" — *luṭhiẏā*. "Before Prabhu" — *prabhura sākṣāta*.

[^414-31]: "Gopijanavallabha [and] Tulasi" (69) — *gopījanaballabhatulasī*, a single compound; understood as two names (cf. 72, 80, 81: "you two," "both"). Gopijanavallabha is possibly the author himself, Gopijana-vallabha Dasa, the son of Rasamaya; Tulasi is apparently Thakura Tulasi (Tulasidasa), the kirtan singer (Uttara, lahari 2, note 15; Purva, lahari 1, note 34). "More than life" — *prāṇa haite*.

[^414-32]: "Birth after birth" (70) — *janme janme*. "Many pastimes [you have] performed [with me]" — *aneka karilā khelā*: *karilā* is taken as a second-person form; it can also be read "[I] performed." "In the land of Utkala" — *utkala-bhubana*. "Plans" (71) — *bicāra*. "Without your company I carry [them] out no longer" — *tomā sabā saṅga binā nā kariẏe āra*: i.e. he does nothing without sharing it with them — and therefore discloses the command to them.

[^414-33]: "One thing" (72) — *eka kathā*. "Pondering a book" — *puṃthi cintā kari*: apparently a sacred book he was reading (which one is not said). "After the sankirtana" (73) — *saṃkīrttana upānte*. "In that place, at Bhograi" — *se bhogarāi sthāne* (note 1). "[I] was sitting" — *baise*, lit. "sits" (third person): Rasika speaks of himself as of another. "With closed eyes" — *mudritanaẏane*.

[^414-34]: "[The colour] of a fresh cloud" (74) — *nabaghanaśyāma*; "a youthful adolescent" — *nabīna kiśora*: Krishna (the colophon speaks of "the command of Sri Sri Bhagavan"). "Flute" — *bā̃śī*. "The command [is given]" (75) — *ājñā hailā*.

[^414-35]: "I delayed" (76) — *karilũ helana*, lit. "I neglected, disregarded." "You do not heed the command" (77) — *ājñā nāhi māna*. "Mahashaya" — *mahāśaẏa*. "Set out" — *karaha bijaẏa*: of a ceremonial departure (lahari 2, note 28).

[^414-36]: "He vanished" (78) — *haila antarddhāna*. "As if in a dream-trance, seemed to part with life" — *yena sbapnābeśe tejinu parāṇa*: i.e. from the shock he as it were lost consciousness; hence the colophon's "in a dream" (*sbapnābeśe*). "At the end of the night" (79) — *niśi śeṣe*: apparently the vision came in the night after the sankirtana (72–73); "today" (72) — on the same day. "Three times He commanded" — *tina ājñā karila*, lit. "gave three commands"; "insistently" — *biśeṣe*.

[^414-37]: "Both" (80) — *dõhā*. "Smiling" — *hāsiẏā*. "The truth" — *tattba*. "The jewel of Rasikendras" — *rasikendramaṇi*. "Embracing [them]" (81) — *kole kari'*, "taking into his arms." "Always" — *anukṣaṇa*, "every moment": a promise to remain with those close to him even after his departure.

[^414-38]: From 82 — the author's words. "Of Rasika's life" — *rasika-caritra*. "Having descended" — *abatīrṇa haiẏā*: the author's enthusiastic praise (on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11; cf. note 15). "He delivered the three worlds" (83) — *uddhārila tina loka*. "Whose vow is to be a sheltering enclosure" — *śaraṇapañjarabānā*: *śaraṇa-pañjara* — "a cage (enclosure) of refuge," i.e. a sure protection for those who take shelter; *bānā* — "vow, sign" (note 15). Raya — *rāẏa*, an honorific, "lord."

[^414-39]: "A boundless ocean" (84) — *apāra samudra*. "In brief" — *saṃkṣepe*. "By the mercy of his feet" — *tā̃ra caraṇakṛpāẏa*. "Without delay" (85) — *abilambe*. "The treasure of loving devotion to Krishna" — *kṛṣṇapremabhaktidhana*.

[^414-40]: The author's signature (86) and the colophon are; the title is as in note 1 (*sbapnābeśe*, "in a dream"). Below is a rule.


## Lahari 15. The Telling to the Disciples of the Departure to Goloka, and the Command to Build the Samadhi at Gopala's Place in Remuna

*A song in glory of Shyamananda; in seclusion Rasika discloses to those close to him that the command to depart has definitely been given him and that he will not remain in the terrible Kali, when the yavanas will grow strong and people abandon righteousness; he recounts his life: eighteen years of secret bhajan from birth, initiation from Shyamananda and nineteen years and seven months of wandering with him, and after Shyamananda's departure twenty-four years and nine months of service by his command, the yearly festivals and twelve-day aradhanas in Govindapur, Shyamasundarpur, Kusharada and Gopivallabhapur — sixty-two years and four months in all; only his wish for a month-long festival, another pilgrimage to Vrindavana and the feeding of Vaishnavas on the Ganga has gone unfulfilled; he asks that his samadhi be made in Remuna, at the place of Gopala, who stole kshira for Madhavendra Puri; those close to him weep in dread, and Rasika consoles them; ill omens appear — earthquakes, a rain of blood, strife — all beings grieve, and the author promises to tell of Rasika's disappearance*

*The fifteenth lahari.*

*Raga Karuna-shri.*[^415-1]
*Ghosha: "Having placed a treasure in [my] hands, O Creator,*
*why have you deprived [me of it]?"*

**1.** Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the life of Rasika,
who delivered the whole circle of the earth![^415-2]

**2.** At this time Rasikendra, sitting in seclusion,
tells those close to him all that is in his heart:

**3.** "The command has definitely been given me to depart;
no longer shall I remain in this terrible [age of] Kali.[^415-3]

**4.** The great Kali will manifest on earth,
the yavanas will grow strong in the land of Bharata.

**5.** All people will abandon righteous conduct;
all such conduct I shall see no more.[^415-4]

**6.** When I came from Gopivallabhapur,
I petitioned before Govinda:

**7.** 'In the manifest [world] I have served You all these days;
now, showing mercy, take [me] to [Your] own abode.'[^415-5]

**8.** Having come to earth, [I] performed bhajan of Krishna:
for eighteen years [I] performed bhajan in secret.[^415-6]

**9.** Ceaselessly streams of tears flow from my eyes;
in the mood of separation from Krishna I wander from forest to forest.

**10.** Living at home, [I] gave no thought to home,
intoxicated with the rasa of love for Krishna, pondering [Him] on and on.

**11.** [I] served the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus in secret;
apart from Krishna, I see nothing else with my eyes.[^415-7]

**12.** [I] cared nothing for bed, food or sleep;
for eighteen years [I] performed bhajan of Krishna.

**13.** At this time Shyamananda came:
the tantra, the mantra of Krishna [and] initiation he gave [me] in the ear.[^415-8]

**14.** In the bliss of love for Krishna [he] flooded the three worlds;
for twenty years [I] wandered together [with him].

**15.** [I] gladdened kings [and] subjects in land after land;
[I] made all lands brim over with love for Krishna.

**16.** Ceaselessly, in the bliss of Krishna, in the ocean of prema,
all enjoyed pastimes with Shyamananda.[^415-9]

**17.** Night and day [I] knew nothing but Krishna;
[I] preached service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus.

**18.** Service to the ashvattha, the tulasi, the dhatri, to the guru [and] the brahmanas,
Sri Harivasara and the rest, service to the Vrajavasis.[^415-10]

**19.** All bhakti, all dharma that there is according to the shastras —
[I] accomplished it all together with Shyamananda.

**20.** [I] spread sankirtana in all lands,
wandering with Shyamananda from land to land.

**21.** Thus for nineteen years and seven months
[I] manifested Krishna's pastimes on earth.[^415-11]

**22.** Then Prabhu departed to his own abode;
knowing [me] to be a servant, he entrusted the service to me.

**23.** For twenty-four years and nine months [I] bore the burden of service:
by Shyamananda's command [I] accepted [it].[^415-12]

**24.** All righteous conduct, all the burden of service [I carried out];
the treasure of loving devotion to Krishna [I] preached.

**25.** In all lands [I] gave prema-bhakti to every house;
in the homes of all [I] performed the pastime of sankirtana.

**26.** In all houses, in every one, [I] arranged service to the sadhus;
sixteenfold service to the guru, Krishna, the sadhus [and] the brahmanas.[^415-13]

**27.** Processions, festival days, great festivals — year after year;
service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus — every year.

**28.** The guru [and] the paratpara-[guru], and Chaitanya Gosani,
Advaita and the other mahajanas, and the godbrothers —

**29.** the aradhana of all [of them] every year
[I] celebrated with great festivals, in joy [and] delight.[^415-14]

**30.** Two [festivals] of twelve [days] [I] held in Govindapur,
three [festivals] of twelve [days] in Shyamasundarpur,

**31.** one [festival] of twelve [days] [I] held in the village of Kusharada:
these six [festivals] of twelve [days] [I] held in various places.

**32.** In Sri Gopivallabhapur — nineteen [festivals] of twelve [days]:
for nineteen years [I] tasted the rasa of Krishna's bliss.[^415-15]

**33.** The sixty-four limbs of bhakti [I] practised always;
all brimmed over with love for Krishna.

**34.** [By] the eighteen Puranas, the Sri Bhagavata and the rest
[I] revealed the bhajan of Krishna as prescribed.

**35.** Thus exclusive bhajan of Sri Krishna,
love for Krishna [I] revealed in the land of Bharata.[^415-16]

**36.** For twenty-four years and nine months in this way
[I] revealed the bhajan of Krishna, one thing after another.

**37.** Thus for sixty-two years and four months
[I] manifested the lila of the bhajan of Krishna.

**38.** In supreme bliss [I] passed the days;
[I] filled the whole world with love for Krishna.[^415-17]

**39.** [I] saw with my eyes [the world] brimming over with love for Krishna;
may I with these eyes look [on nothing else] any more.

**40.** Thus for sixty-two years [I] played;
now I shall go [and] see Krishna's own pastimes.[^415-18]

**41.** The command of Krishna has been given me: 'Come to [your] own abode.'
This is what I have told you in secret.

**42.** Birth after birth you all are those close to me;
therefore I have told [you] everything in detail.

**43.** Certainly I shall go to Krishna;
[only] one regret has remained in my mind.[^415-19]

**44.** [As] in the seventh wave of the *Shyamananda-rasarnava* —
a month-long great festival with the feeding of sweets, in joy;

**45.** to see the abode of Vrindavana once more;
the feeding of Vaishnavas at a temple on the bank of the Ganga —

**46.** this wish of mine has not been fulfilled.
The command to depart has been given — who will break it?[^415-20]

**47.** The command of Prabhu I never break:
certainly I shall go to Krishna.

**48.** For one who is born, the body certainly disappears;
birth after birth Bhagavan performs this lila.[^415-21]

**49.** From my heart I have told all this to you;
fulfil one request of mine with care.

**50.** To Nilachala, to the bank of the Ganga, to the abode of Vrindavana
I cannot set out quickly.

**51.** Now I am well — I say [this] to all;
[but] it is unknown [when] — be sure to perform [the rite] for the body.[^415-22]

**52.** Listen to my words, all you who are close to me:
make my samadhi at Gopala's place.[^415-23]

**53.** Chaitanya Gosani gave the command with [His own] mouth;
Gopala is my very own: this I know directly.[^415-24]

**54.** Madhavendra Puri and all the mahajanas
worshipped the feet of that Gopala in Remuna.

**55.** He is greatly subject to His devotees: stealing kshira,
He brought [it] and with love gave [it] to Madhavendra Puri.

**56.** Since then, calling [Him] Gopala Kshirachora,
all people serve [Him], seeing [His] manifestation.[^415-25]

**57.** My samadhi all will see in that place:
to all [of you] I have told the truth, sitting in seclusion."[^415-26]

**58.** Hearing this, all those close to him, in great dismay,
roll on the ground and weep, their eyes full of tears.[^415-27]

**59.** All the companions wept much;
he consoles everyone with sweet words.

**60.** "Do not take anything to heart, all you companions" —
embracing everyone by the neck, he weeps again and again.[^415-28]

**61.** Thus, having experienced the human lila,
he wished to conceal [it].[^415-29]

**62.** Earthquakes, a rain of blood, quarrels and strife
appeared in every home all over the earth.

**63.** Unfortunate the earth has now become:
Rasikendra has resolved to go to Goloka.[^415-30]

**64.** The earth wept much in secret —
all the various living beings, unmoving and moving.[^415-31]

**65.** The creatures of the waters and the forests all grew sorrowful;
in separation from Rasika grief arose in all.

**66.** Fear seized all the men and women;
all say: "Rasikendra will depart."

**67.** Thus, removing the burden of the earth's sorrow,
he spread the name of Krishna in the world.[^415-32]

**68.** Now I shall make known the account of [his] disappearance;
listen, everyone, to the *Rasika-mangala* with attention.[^415-33]

**69.** Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

*Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the fifteenth lahari, called "The Telling to the Disciples of the Departure to Goloka, and the Command to Build the Samadhi at Gopala's Place in Remuna."*[^415-34]

[^415-1]: The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("পঞ্চদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 15 begins. Raga Karuna-shri (*karuṇāśrī*; lahari 14, note 1). Ghosha: *hāte nidhi diẏā bidhi / ki lāgilā bañcilā*; "Creator" — *bidhi* (Vidhi, Brahma, the arbiter of fate); the treasure is apparently Rasika, whom the world is to lose. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে শিষ্যগণ প্রতি গোলোক-গমন-কথন ও রেমুণাতে গোপাল-স্থানে সমাধিনির্ম্মাণ-করণে আদেশ-প্রদান-নাম পঞ্চদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (*śiṣyagaṇa prati goloka-gamana-kathana o remuṇāte gopāla-sthāne samādhinirmmāṇa-karaṇe ādeśa-pradāna*), lit. "the telling to the disciples of the going to Goloka and the giving of the command for the building of the samadhi at Gopala's place in Remuna." 58–69 and the colophon are.

[^415-2]: "The life of Rasika" (1) — *rasikera prāṇa*. "Who delivered the whole circle of the earth" — *sarbba abanimaṇḍala kaila paritrāṇa*. "In seclusion" (2) — *nigame* (lahari 14, note 13). "Those close to him" — *ātmagaṇe*.

[^415-3]: From 3 to 57 is Rasika's speech to those close to him. In it Rasika speaks of himself now in the first person (3, 5–7, 9 *bhrami*, 11 *nā dekhi*, 22 *more*, 39–57), now with third-person verbs (8, 10, 12, 14–21, 23–38: *kaila*, *bhajila*, *sādhila*), as of another (cf. lahari 14, 73, note 33); in the EN the subject is supplied as "[I]." "Has definitely been given" — *niścaya hailā ājñā*. "The terrible [age of] Kali" — *ghora kali* (lahari 14, 55, 60).

[^415-4]: "The great Kali" (4) — *mahākali*. Yavanas — foreigners, here apparently Muslims (lahari 14, note 22). "Righteous conduct" (5) — *dharmmabyabahāra*. "All such conduct I shall see no more" — *e sakala ācaraṇa nā dekhiba āra*: apparently he does not wish to witness the decline (4–5a); it can also be read "I shall see no more such (righteous) conduct."

[^415-5]: "When I came from Gopivallabhapur" (6) — *yakhana āsi' gopīballabhapura haite*. "Before Govinda" — *gobinda-sākṣāte*: apparently before the Deity of Govinda; where is not said (possibly in Govindapur, cf. 30). "In the manifest [world]" (7) — *prakaṭe*: in the manifest lila. "All these days" — *etadina*. "To [Your] own abode" — *nijadhāme*.

[^415-6]: "Having come to earth" (8) — *bhūmigata haiẏā*: from birth (lahari 14, 57, note 24). "Eighteen years" — *aṣṭādaśa batsara*; likewise 12 (*āṭhāra*): from birth to initiation from Shyamananda (13). The reckoning of years in 8–40: 18 years (8, 12) + 19 years 7 months with Shyamananda (21; in 14, "twenty years," a round number) + 24 years 9 months after his departure (23, 36) = 62 years 4 months (37; 40 and lahari 14, 56 — "sixty-two years"). This agrees with the years of Rasikananda's life (1590–1652). "In secret" — *saṅgopane*; likewise 11.

[^415-7]: "Flow" (9) — *galaẏe*. "In the mood of separation from Krishna" — *kṛṣṇera biraha bhābe*. "I wander from forest to forest" — *bhrami bane bane*. "Gave no thought to home" (10) — *gṛhajñāna nā karila cite*, lit. "kept no thought of home in mind." "Pondering [Him] on and on" — *bhābite bhābite*.

[^415-8]: "Cared nothing" (12) — *nā kaila ādara*. "Came" (13) — *karila gamane*. "The tantra, the mantra of Krishna [and] initiation he gave [me] in the ear" — *kṛṣṇa tantra mantra dīkṣā karāila karṇe*: initiation in which the guru speaks the mantra into the disciple's ear. On Rasika's meeting with Shyamananda and his initiation — the Purva-vibhaga; cf. the *Bhakti-ratnakara*, taranga 15.

[^415-9]: "Flooded the three worlds" (14) — *bhāsāilā tribhubana*, lit. "made [them] float." "Twenty years" — *biṃśati batsara* (note 6). "Wandered together [with him]" — *kaila saṅge biharaṇa*. "Gladdened" (15) — *pramoda karila* (lahari 14, note 19). "Made ... brim over" — *ḍhalaḍhala kaila* (lahari 14, note 18). "All" (16) — *sabe*: all [the companions]. "Enjoyed pastimes" — *karila bihāre*.

[^415-10]: "Night and day" (17) — *niśi diśi*. Ashvattha, tulasi, dhatri (18) — sacred plants that are worshipped (Purva, lahari 6). Sri Harivasara (*śrīharibāsara*) — "the day of Hari," Ekadashi, the fast in honour of the Lord. "Service to the Vrajavasis" — *brajabāsī sebā*: service to the residents of Vraja.

[^415-11]: "According to the shastras" (19) — *śāstramate*. "Accomplished" — *sādhila*. "Nineteen years and seven months" (21) — *uniśa batsara sāta māsa* (note 6). "Krishna's pastimes" — *kṛṣṇakhelā*.

[^415-12]: "Prabhu departed to his own abode" (22) — *prabhu bijaẏa karila nijadhāme*: Shyamananda's departure (Pashchima, lahari 13). "Knowing [me] to be a servant" — *bhṛtya jāni'*. "Twenty-four years and nine months" (23) — *cabbiśa bachara naẏa māsa*; likewise 36 (note 6). "The burden of service" — *sebābhāra*. "Accepted" — *karila aṅgīkāra*.

[^415-13]: "All righteous conduct" (24) — *yata dharmma ācaraṇa*. "In the homes of all" (25) — *sabāra mandire*: *mandira* — "house" or "temple." "Sixteenfold service" (26) — *ṣaṛ-daśa sebā*: apparently worship with sixteen offerings (*ṣoḍaśa-upacāra*; Purva, lahari 8, note 23).

[^415-14]: "Processions, festival days, great festivals" (27) — *yātrā parbba mahotsaba*. The edition's footnote to 27 gives the variant *ārādhanā yātrā kaila*. "The guru [and] the paratpara-[guru]" (28) — *guru parātpara*: understood as the guru and the senior gurus of the succession (*parama-guru*, *parātpara-guru*); it can also be read "the guru, highest of the high." "Mahajanas" — *mahājana*. "Godbrothers" — *guru bhāi*. "Aradhana" (29) — *ārādhanā*: yearly worship on memorial days (Uttara, lahari 2). "In joy [and] delight" — *ānanda kutuhale*.

[^415-15]: "[Festival] of twelve [days]" (30–32) — *duẏādaśa*, *dbādaśa*: the yearly twelve-day aradhana of Shyamananda (lahari 5, notes 28–29; lahari 14, note 18). Here: two in Govindapur, three in Shyamasundarpur, one in Kusharada, six in all (31), and nineteen in Gopivallabhapur (32); in lahari 5, 49–51 — "five in three villages" and "twenty" in Gopivallabhapur. The total in both places is twenty-five, i.e. one festival a year for the almost twenty-five years after Shyamananda's departure (23). "Tasted the rasa of Krishna's bliss" (32) — *kaila kṛṣṇānandarasa*.

[^415-16]: "The sixty-four limbs of bhakti" (33) — *catuḥṣaṣṭi bhakti-aṅga*: the sixty-four practices of bhakti (*Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu* 1.2; CC, Madhya 22). "All brimmed over" — *ḍhalāḍhali hailā sabāẏa*. "As prescribed" (34) — *yathābidhi*. "Exclusive bhajan" (35) — *ananya ... bhajana*. "In the land of Bharata" — *bhāratabhubana*.

[^415-17]: "One thing after another" (36) — *eke eke*. "Sixty-two years and four months" (37) — *bāṣaṭṭi batsara cāri māsa*. "The lila of the bhajan" — *bhajanalīlā*. "Passed the days" (38) — *dina karila haraṇa*.

[^415-18]: "Saw" (39) — *dekhila* (third person). "May I with these eyes look [on nothing else] any more" — *e naẏane āra yena nā kari darśane*: having seen the world full of love for Krishna, he wishes to see nothing else (cf. lahari 14, 55). "Played" (40) — *kaila khelā*. "Krishna's own pastimes" — *kṛṣṇera nija līlā*: Krishna's eternal pastimes in His abode.

[^415-19]: "Come to [your] own abode" (41) — *esa nijadhāme* (cf. lahari 14, 75–77). "You" — *tomāre*, singular: apparently addressed to one of those close to him (cf. lahari 14, 72: "to you two"); in 42 again "you all." "Those close to me" (42) — *ātmagaṇa*. "Regret" (43) — *saṃśaya*, lit. "doubt," here an unfulfilled wish (44–46).

[^415-20]: *Shyamananda-rasarnava* (44) — *śyāmānanda rasārṇaba*, lit. "the ocean of Shyamananda's rasa": apparently the biography *Sri Shyamananda-rasarnava*, which the edition's preface ascribes to Krishnadasa, the author of the *Shyamananda-prakasha*; the "seventh wave" (*saptama-taraṅga*) is its chapter; its contents have not been checked. It can also be read figuratively: "in the seventh wave of the ocean of Shyamananda's rasa." The sense of 44 is apparently that Rasika wished to hold a month-long festival with the feeding of sweets, as described there. "In joy" — *raṅge*. "Once more" (45) — *āra bāra*. "The feeding of Vaishnavas at a temple on the bank of the Ganga" — *gaṅgātīre debālaẏe baiṣṇaba bhojana*. "Has not been fulfilled" (46) — *nā haila sāṅga*. "Who will break it?" — *ke karibe bhaṅga*.

[^415-21]: "Prabhu" (47) — here the Lord who gave the command. "For one who is born, the body certainly disappears" (48) — *janmile abaśya haẏa deha antarddhāna*: *antarddhāna* — "vanishing, disappearance." "Bhagavan performs this lila" — apparently the Lord, descending age after age, Himself displays birth and departure as lila (cf. *Bhagavad-gita* 4.6–9), and His associates come and go with Him. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the appearance and disappearance of the Lord and His pure devotees are not a compelled birth and end of the body under the rule of karma but their lila.

[^415-22]: "From my heart" (49) — *marame*. "Request" — *nibedana*. 50 — *śīghrate nā pāri tathā karite praẏāṇa*: apparently Rasika will not have time to go to the holy places (Nilachala, the Ganga, Vrindavana) where Vaishnavas wish to leave the body, and therefore asks for a samadhi in Remuna (52). "Now I am well" (51) — *ekṣaṇe āchiẏe bhāla*. "It is unknown [when]" — *nā jāniẏe*. "Be sure to perform [the rite] for the body" — *abaśya karaẏe deha-karmme*: *deha-karma* is understood as the funeral rite; the sense is approximate.

[^415-23]: "Samadhi" (52) — *samādhi*: a tomb, the place where a Vaishnava's body is laid to rest (the bodies of saintly Vaishnavas are usually not cremated but interred). "At Gopala's place" — *gopālera sthāne*: in Remuna (54; colophon). The edition's footnote gives the variant *gopīnātha*: the Deity of Remuna is known as Kshirachora Gopinatha (CC, Madhya 4); Rasikananda's samadhi is in Remuna, at the temple of Kshirachora Gopinatha.

[^415-24]: "Gave the command with [His own] mouth" (53) — *ājñā karilena mukhe*. "Gopala is my very own" — *nije gopāla āmāra*: the sense is unclear; understood as Rasika's words: Gopala is his own Lord; it can also be read as Sri Chaitanya's words ("Gopala is My very own"). What command Sri Chaitanya gave, and to whom, is not said (Rasika was born after Sri Chaitanya's disappearance). "Directly" — *pratyakṣe*.

[^415-25]: "Mahajanas" (54) — *mahājana*. Madhavendra Puri and Sri Chaitanya visited Remuna (CC, Madhya 4; Madhya 16). "Subject to His devotees" (55) — *bhaktabaśa*. According to CC, Madhya 4, Gopinatha hid for Madhavendra Puri a pot of kshira (sweet thickened milk) offered to Him, and in a dream told the pujari to give it to Puri; since then He has been called Kshirachora, "the thief of kshira." 55b — *dilena āniẏā preme mādhabendra purī*: understood with *mādhabendra purī* as the recipient; it can also be read "Madhavendra Puri brought [it] and with love gave [it]," but according to the CC it was the pujari who brought the kshira to Puri. Gopala Kshirachora — *kṣīracorā gopāla* (56). "[His] manifestation" — *prakāśa*: His manifest mercy (or the Deity Himself).

[^415-26]: "The truth" (57) — *tattba*. "In seclusion" — *nigame*. Here Rasika's speech ends; ends with the complete ॥57॥ and begins with ॥58॥ — no couplet carries over. The continuation of lahari 15 (58–69, the author's signature and the colophon) is (the next portion).

[^415-27]: Continuation of lahari 15. ends with the complete ॥57॥ begins with the complete ॥58॥ — no couplet runs over. "In great dismay" — *mahātrāse*, lit. "in great fear." "Roll on the ground" — *bhūmite loṭāñā*.

[^415-28]: "Do not take anything to heart" — *kichu mane nā karibe*, lit. "keep nothing in mind": apparently "do not grieve [over my departure]." "Again and again" — *ghane ghane*.

[^415-29]: "Having experienced the human lila" — *mānuṣika līlā anubhaba*; the line may also be read "thus [ended] the manifestation of the human lila." "Conceal" — *saṅgopana karibāre*: to hide [the lila] from the world's eyes, i.e. to depart. "He wished" — *haila anurāga*, lit. "an inclination arose."

[^415-30]: 62–63 — ill omens before Rasika's departure; cf. the omens Yudhishthira sees when Krishna leaves the earth (*Bhagavata Purana* 1.14). "Unfortunate" — *hatabhāgī*. "Now" — *etadine*, lit. "by this day." Goloka is Krishna's highest abode. "Has resolved" — *mane kaila*.
